`CLAUDE.md`:

```md
# ida-ttd

An IDA Pro 9.5 plugin (C++, Windows x64) that turns a time-travel recording into
an IDA debugger session: step forwards and backwards, jump to any position, and
run whole-recording queries (calls, coverage, memory accesses, syscalls, memory
map, self-modifying code, strings, buffers, forks). Two kinds of recording:

- **Microsoft TTD** (`.run`), read through the TTD Replay SDK
  (NuGet `Microsoft.TimeTravelDebugging.Apis`, version pinned in
  `msbuild/Directory.Build.props`).
- **Sogen** (`.sogttd`), read through Sogen's trace reader
  (github.com/momo5502/sogen, `src/windows-ttd`). Sogen can also *replay* a
  recording in its emulator, which is what forking uses.

IDA 9.5 only: 9.5 raised the debugger interface version (IDD 32), so a build
against one version's SDK does not load in the other.

README.md is the user-facing description, and the page plugins.hex-rays.com
shows (the package carries it). Hex-Rays asks for an overview, installation
and usage, and credits; keep those sections, and keep it in step with
features. `docs/` holds design notes: `docs/scripting.md` (the `ida_ttd`
Python module, then the `ttd("...")` commands it wraps; one page since
docs/python.md was merged into it) and `docs/licensing.md` (what each binary
contains and the terms it ships under) are current, while
`modular-backends.md` is historical and may be out of date.

Local notes stay out of git: `docs/sogen-ttd-requests*.md` (requests to the
Sogen side and its answers; ignored, and removed from the history on
2026-11-16), `docs/code-review*.md`, `docs/how-the-analyses-work.md`,
`TODO.txt`. Never add them.

**Local setup** (where things live on this machine and on the test machine,
reference material, test recordings) is in `CLAUDE.local.md`, which is
git-ignored. Read it if it exists; keep machine-specific paths out of this file.

## Architecture

```
IDA  <->  plugin (ida-ttd.dll)  <->  ITraceBackend  <->  backend DLL (C ABI)
                                      core/backend.h       src/abi/ida_ttd_backend.h
```

- **`src/abi/ida_ttd_backend.h`**: the versioned C interface every backend DLL
  exports (`ittd_*` types, count-then-fill queries, `ITTD_CAP_*` capability
  bits). Backends are found in `$IDAUSR\ida-ttd\backends\` (user-installed),
  then `plugins\ida-ttd-backends\` and `plugins\ida-ttd\ida-ttd-backends\`
  (`load_backend_modules`).
- **`src/core/`**: `ITraceBackend` / `ITraceCursor` (`backend.h`), the
  backend-neutral `Position` (`position.h`; shown as `HI:LO` hex), `BackendModule`
  (adapts a DLL to `ITraceBackend`) and `abi_export` (the reverse: wraps a C++
  `ITraceBackend` as the C ABI, used by the MS backend).
- **`src/backend-msttd/`**: the only code that sees the TTD Replay SDK. It does
  not link `ida.lib` (`msttd_ida_shim.cpp` supplies the few kernel functions
  `qstring` needs), so `ittd-probe` can run it outside IDA. Whole-recording
  queries are replays with engine callbacks/watchpoints (`msttd_sweep`).
  Syscalls come from `KernelCall` gaps (`msttd_syscalls`); the memory map is built
  from those syscalls (`msttd_memmap`); strings, buffers and self-modifying code
  come from two write-watchpoint replays (`msttd_scans`).
- **`src/backend-sogen/`**: implements the C ABI directly against Sogen's
  reader and emulator, split by what each part does (`sogen_state.h`, the
  shared types; `sogen_session`, `sogen_memory`, `sogen_nav`, `sogen_queries`,
  `sogen_emulator`, `sogen_fork`, `sogen_scans`; `sogen_backend.cpp`, the
  table and the export). Not in the solution (see Building).
- **`src/common/`**: shared helpers. `write_scans.h` is header-only and
  standard-library-only on purpose: the string and buffer scanners, shared by
  both backends (the Sogen backend builds without the rest of the plugin).
  They implement `docs/scan-rules.md`, Sogen's rules written down as
  behavior, and were written from that document, not ported: Sogen is
  GPL-2.0-only and the rest of ida-ttd is `Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only`
  (dual, so the plugin can ship with the GPL backend; `docs/licensing.md`).
  Never copy code from Sogen into anything outside `src/backend-sogen/`;
  change a rule in the document, then the code. `src/backend-sogen/` is
  GPL-2.0-only (an SPDX header on every file), so code shared with the Sogen backend must not
  pull in more of the plugin. The package ships `ida-ttd-sogen.dll` with
  its licenses folder (`scripts/sogen_dist.py`), and its source goes on
  the release; the Sogen commit it is built from is `msbuild/sogen.pin`.
- **`src/common/apimeta/`** + **`data/*.bin`**: the Win32/phnt API metadata
  indexes and their loader, ported from ttd-capa-cpp (same author, Apache-2.0;
  keep them close to the original). `debugger/apidecode` decodes a call's
  arguments from them; the build copies `data/` to `ida-ttd-data/` beside the
  plugin, which is where the plugin looks.
- **`src/debugger/`**: the IDA debugger over one backend. `TraceManager` owns
  the session (cursor, pending movement requests, event queue to IDA);
  `ModuleRegistry` (modules, exports, PDBs, function bounds), `MemoryReader`
  (recording first, then the on-disk image, then placeholder zeros),
  `SegmentLayout` (what `ev_get_memory_info` reports).
- **`src/analysis/`**: whole-recording analyses, each a backend query run behind
  a cancellable wait box (`query_runner`), writing results to the database
  where relevant (netnode stores; `trace_store` stamps which recording they came
  from).
- **`src/ui/`**: choosers (one per listing), action handlers (`ui.h` declares
  them and the `actions::` ids), pseudocode painting (`decompiler.cpp`), SVG
  icons (`icons.hh`, Material Symbols / codicons). The graph window, the
  memory heatmap and the call tree are PySide6 windows in
  `scripts/ida_ttd_graph.py`, `ida_ttd_heatmap.py` and `ida_ttd_calltree.py`,
  run through IDAPython (`run_python_window` in `graph_view.h`, which
  reloads a module whose file changed).
- **`src/plugin/`**: the `plugmod_t`, split by what it does: `plugin.cpp`
  (construction and teardown), `plugin_actions.cpp` (the action table,
  `build_action_table`: label, handler, shortcut, tooltip, icon, menu group,
  submenu: adding a command is a handler + one row; the toolbar),
  `plugin_menu.cpp` (the TTD menu), `plugin_session.cpp` (starting and
  switching sessions), `plugin_events.cpp` (IDA's notifications, context
  menus in `ui_finish_populating_widget_popup`) and `plugin_stopviews.cpp`
  (the after-stop work, `do_after_stop`, run from a timer after IDA's own
  stop handling). `script_api.cpp` is the `ttd("cmd args")` IDC function and
  its dispatch; the commands live in `script_session`, `script_analysis`,
  `script_ui`, `script_fork` and `script_drv` (each file's own table of
  rows), on `script_args.h` and `script_json.h`. IDAPython is called through
  `common/python_eval.h`.
- **`scripts/ida_ttd.py`**: the Python API (`Session`, `Recording`, `call`).
  The build copies it to `ida-ttd-python/` beside the plugin, and the plugin
  puts that folder on IDAPython's `sys.path` when it loads.
- **Settings**: declared in `ida-plugin.json` (`settings`, every one with a
  default and `"prompt": false`, so HCLI asks nothing at install; keep it
  that way), read through the `ida-settings` package by
  `scripts/ida_ttd_settings.py` and handed to C++ once per plugin load
  (`plugin/settings.h`, whose defaults must match the JSON). Without
  `ida-settings` the defaults apply. TTD > Settings... opens the IDA
  Settings Editor.
- **`scripts/ida_ttd_qt.py`**: the few Qt changes the SDK has no call for
  (a toolbar button's width, a submenu's icon, whether the theme is dark),
  called from C++ through IDAPython. Put such code here, not in C strings.
- **`scripts/ida_ttd_runtime.py`**: TTD > Backends > Install the TTD runtime
  (WinDbg), and Install the Sogen backend (from a file the user picks, into
  `$IDAUSR\ida-ttd\backends\`). The TTD menu is rebuilt whole
  (`Plugin::rebuild_ttd_menu`) whenever its contents change: session items,
  then the replay-start items, then Backends, which every database has. Copies `amd64\ttd` out of an installed WinDbg, or shows WinDbg's
  license and downloads its x64 package from Microsoft (HTTP range reads of
  the bundle), into `$IDAUSR\ida-ttd\windbg\`, where the MS
  backend looks. Copied beside `ida_ttd.py`. Everything below
  `install_runtime()` runs without IDA, for testing.
- **`src/loader/`**: `ttd-loader.dll`, so File > Open accepts a recording.
- **`src/setup/`**: `ida-ttd-loader-setup.dll`, a `PLUGIN_FIX` component of the
  HCLI package that copies the bundled `ttd-loader.dll` into
  `$IDAUSR\loaders\` as IDA starts (HCLI installs only into
  `plugins\ida-ttd\`, and IDA finds loaders only in `loaders\`). It stays
  loaded in the GUI to show TTD > Backends while no database is open (the
  main plugin, and its menu, load only with a database).
- **`scripts/package.py`**: builds `dist\ida-ttd.zip`, the HCLI package (an
  `ida-ttd/` suite folder, with the setup component and its generated
  `ida-plugin.json`). The release workflow runs it, then `hcli plugin lint`.
- **`src/tools/ittd_probe.c`**: drives any backend DLL through the ABI outside
  IDA and checks its promises.

`src/` is the include root: includes always name the folder
(`#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"`).

## Building

Visual Studio 2022+ with the C++ desktop workload; the TTD Replay SDK is
restored with `nuget install msbuild\packages.config -OutputDirectory packages`.

```
msbuild msbuild\ida-ttd.vcxproj      -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
msbuild msbuild\backend-msttd.vcxproj -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
msbuild msbuild\ittd-probe.vcxproj   -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
msbuild msbuild\ttd-loader.vcxproj   -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
msbuild msbuild\ida-ttd-loader-setup.vcxproj -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64
python scripts\package.py
```

Output goes to `build\Release\` (backends in `build\Release\backends\`). New
source files: add them to the `.vcxproj` (CRLF files), then run
`python msbuild/gen_filters.py`.

The **Sogen backend** needs a Sogen source tree and a CMake build of it
(`docs/building-the-sogen-backend.md`). Build it with `-t:Rebuild`: MSBuild does
not relink when Sogen's libraries change. Don't build in a Sogen checkout someone
is working in: use a snapshot (`git archive` + a CMake configure with
`-DFETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED=ON`) and pass
`-p:SogenRoot=<snapshot> -p:SogenBuild=<build>`.

**Releasing.** Pushing a tag `vX.Y.Z` runs `.github/workflows/release.yml`:
it checks the tag against `ida-plugin.json`'s `version` (bump that first),
builds everything including the Sogen backend at `msbuild/sogen.pin`, runs
`hcli plugin lint` on the zip and attaches `ida-ttd.zip`, `ttd-loader.dll`
and `ida-ttd-sogen-source.zip` to the release. Hex-Rays' plugin repository
indexes public GitHub repositories' releases daily; there is no submission.

## Testing

1. **Backend changes: `ittd-probe`, locally, no IDA.**
   `build\Release\ittd-probe.exe build\Release\backends\ida-ttd-msttd.dll <trace.run>`
   (or `ida-ttd-sogen.dll` with a `.sogttd`). The probe ends with
   "N check(s) failed".
   Environment switches: `ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY=<hives dir>` enables the scan
   and fork sections; `ITTD_PROBE_SCAN_DUMP=<prefix>` writes every recovered
   string/buffer to TSV for diffing before/after a change;
   `ITTD_PROBE_MAP_DUMP=1` dumps the memory map; `ITTD_PROBE_FIND=<text>` searches
   recovered strings.
2. **Plugin/UI changes: in IDA through the `ida` MCP**, which may run on a
   different machine than the source. The user installs builds by hand:
   tell them which DLLs changed with their sha256, then verify the installed
   hashes from inside IDA before testing. Drive the plugin with
   `idc.eval_idc('ttd("cmd")')` (JSON back; `ttd("help")` lists commands);
   `scripts/selftest.py` is the end-to-end suite (`run()`: 28 checks on
   either kind of recording; `run_sogen()`: the Sogen-only ones). Release
   the MCP lease (`close_database`) when done, or the DLLs stay locked.
   - The automatic passes after a stop (coverage, conditional moves,
     indirect calls) run from UI timers, which a headless worker never
     fires: test them on a GUI database, returning from `execute_python`
     between the movement and the check.
   - `ida_hexrays.decompile()` can hand back a decompilation cached before
     the database changed; check pseudocode with `DECOMP_NO_CACHE` (after
     `clear_cached_cfuncs()`) or in an open view.

There is no unit-test suite; correctness is checked against known recordings
(e.g. the sample program stores 0x2222222222222222 over 0x1111111111111111) and
by comparing MS and Sogen recordings of the same program.

## Pitfalls

- **HCLI replaces `plugins\ida-ttd\` on every upgrade.** Nothing the user adds
  (the TTD runtime DLLs, a Sogen backend, its `registry\` folder) may be
  expected to live there. They go in `$IDAUSR\ida-ttd\` (`windbg\`,
  `backends\`, `registry\`; `user_data_dir()` in `core/backend_module.h`),
  outside `plugins\` since none of them is a plugin. The old
  `plugins\ida-ttd-backends\` is still searched.
  `hcli plugin lint` exits 0 even on errors; read its output.
- **Never ship or fetch Microsoft's TTD runtime any other way.** Its terms
  forbid redistribution, and the standalone TTD package's terms forbid
  commercial use; WinDbg's do not. So it comes from WinDbg only, on the
  user's machine, after they accept WinDbg's license. A DLL in an installed
  package's folder (`WindowsApps`) cannot be loaded from IDA (access denied),
  only read, so it is copied out.
- **Never poll IDA's windows from a thread inside the IDA process** (e.g. an
  `EnumWindows` loop on a Python thread): it deadlocked the user's IDA.
- **Never call `ida_dbg.set_debugger_options(0)`** to read the options: it
  replaces them, and there is no getter.
- Debugger segments (the system DLLs of an MS recording) and anything painted on
  them vanish when the session ends; database-backed state must not assume they
  persist.
- IDA moves its views to the instruction pointer after a stop, so anything that
  positions a view after a travel must run from `do_after_stop`, not inline.
- Wait boxes only appear after a grace period while the UI pumps; long
  synchronous work (e.g. loading a PDB) looks like a hang instead.
- From 9.5, Hex-Rays prints an instruction's repeatable comment in the
  pseudocode itself, wherever its own map of instructions to statements puts
  it. The indirect-call notes are repeatable comments, so `decompiler.cpp`
  appends a note only where the function's text does not already show it
  (`notes_already_shown`). Other decompiler plugins read those comments too:
  hrtng's automatic renaming named a variable after a note.
- Shell edits: don't pass code containing backslashes (`\n` in C strings,
  Windows paths) through bash heredocs; they get mangled. Use the Edit/Write
  tools or a script file. Working copies are CRLF (`core.autocrlf=true`), and
  `sed -i` in Git Bash writes a file back as LF: check `git ls-files --eol`
  after one.

## Conventions

- **Code style**: IDA SDK style: 4-space indent, `if ( x )` with inner spaces,
  braces on their own lines, `m_` members, `qstring`/`qvector` in plugin code
  and `std::` in backends. Comments explain *why* in full sentences, and are
  dense; match the surrounding file.
- **American English everywhere**: code, comments, identifiers, user-facing
  text, docs, commit messages and the wiki (color, gray, behavior, license,
  analyze, initialize, center, labeled). Third-party text quoted verbatim
  (license texts, Sogen's messages) stays as written.
- **User-facing text** (menus, tooltips, messages, README) is plain and
  specific; the README is kept in step with features.
- **Git**: work directly on `main` (the user prefers few branches). Commit with a
  short imperative subject and a prose body explaining the change. GitHub
  is the `github` remote (`git push github main`); push only when the user
  asks. The history was rewritten on 2026-11-16 (the request documents
  removed), so clones and forks from before then do not share it.
  `TODO.txt` (the user's feature/bug list with a dated Done section) stays
  untracked; update it when finishing an item.

```

`README.md`:

```md
> [!Warning]
> Claude was used to write this project's code. I performed testing for my own use cases, but
> you may run into issues. If you do, feel free to open an issue on this repository!

# ida-ttd

ida-ttd is an IDA Pro plugin that turns a time travel debugging (TTD) recording into an IDA
debugger session: step forwards and backwards, jump to any point, and ask questions about the
whole recording. It reads [Microsoft TTD](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/debuggercmds/time-travel-debugging-overview)
recordings (`.run`) and recordings from a [custom fork of Sogen](https://github.com/TTD-Club/sogen)
(`.sogttd`).

The [wiki](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki) has the full instructions.

<img width="2559" height="1233" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8275042f-1d4b-4a64-ac2e-d9e1e9197508" />

## Overview

- Reverse navigation: step, step over, step out, continue and run to cursor, backwards too
- Bookmarks and a timeline of thread and module events
- Every call to a function or pattern (`kernel32!Virtual*`), with decoded arguments and return values
- Every read, write or execute of an address range
- Where a value came from, traced back through the instructions that set it
- Syscalls, handles, the memory map and its timeline, a memory heatmap
- Recovered strings and buffers, self-modifying code
- Indirect calls resolved, and executed code highlighted in the disassembly and the decompiler
- A Python API

Sogen recordings can also be **forked**: change registers or memory at any point and record what
the program does next, then compare the two runs. See
[Sogen TTD Features](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki/Sogen-TTD-Features).

## Installation

Requires IDA Pro 9.5 on Windows x64.

```
hcli plugin install ida-ttd
```

Or extract `ida-ttd.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/releases)
into `%APPDATA%\Hex-Rays\IDA Pro\plugins\`. Restart IDA once, so `File > Open` recognizes
recordings.

Microsoft recordings need the TTD runtime first:
[Installation](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki#installation). To build the plugin
yourself, see [Building from Source](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki/Building-from-Source).

## Usage examples

Each feature is described on
[Features and Usage](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki/Features-and-Usage).

**Open a recording.** `File > Open` a `.run` or `.sogttd` file; the original binary is not
needed. The TTD toolbar adds the backward controls, and the queries are on the **TTD** menu.

**Find what wrote a buffer.** Right-click the address and choose **Find memory accesses**
(`Ctrl+Shift+M`). Double-click a write to travel there, then press `Ctrl+Shift+W` on the stored
register to see where its value came from.

**Find every call to an API.** Press `Ctrl+Shift+F` and enter `kernel32!CreateFileW`.
Double-click a call to travel to it.

**Find unpacked code.** Open `TTD > Memory > Memory map`: executable memory outside every loaded
module is colored. Double-click its "Allocated at" position to travel to the allocation.

**Script it** ([Scripting](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki/Scripting)):

```python
import ida_ttd
s = ida_ttd.Session()
s.start()                                   # replay this database's recording
s.step(back=True)                           # one instruction backwards
for c in s.calls_to("kernel32!CreateFileW"):
    print(c["pos"], c["args"], c["ret"])
s.origin("rax")                             # where rax's value came from
```

All keyboard shortcuts: [Shortcuts](https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/wiki/Features-and-Usage#shortcuts).

## Future Work/Ideas
- Function/memory query language
- Linux support for Sogen recordings (MS recordings will never work unless there's official support from Microsoft)

`docs/building-the-sogen-backend.md`:

```md
# Building and testing the Sogen backend

`ida-ttd-sogen.dll` reads Sogen time-travel traces (`.sogttd`) for ida-ttd. It
is a separate DLL behind the C ABI in `src/abi/ida_ttd_backend.h`, and it links
Sogen's trace reader and `cpu_view`, and for forks and the replay scans
Sogen's replay, recorder and Windows emulator, all GPL-2.0-only. The DLL it
produces is therefore a GPL-2.0 binary
([modular-backends.md](modular-backends.md) §3). It is not part of
`ida-ttd.slnx`, so building ida-ttd never needs Sogen. Releases build it from
the commit in `msbuild/sogen.pin` (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) and ship
it in the plugin package; `scripts/sogen_dist.py` writes the licenses that go
beside it and the source archive that goes on the release
([licensing.md](licensing.md)). A local build goes in the package the same
way: run `sogen_dist.py` after building, then `package.py`.

The core does not load backends yet (that is phase 4 of the plan). Until it
does, the backend is exercised with `ittd-probe`, which is in the solution.

## 1. Build Sogen's reader and view

From a Visual Studio x64 developer prompt, against a Sogen checkout on
`ttd/next` (`%SOGEN%`) and a build directory of your choosing
(`%SOGEN_BUILD%`):

Use `ttd/next` at `86158936` or later. Before `ada569b0`, reading a page of
memory walked every recorded access to it -- tens to hundreds of
milliseconds on a hot code page -- and IDA reads whole modules after their
symbols load; since, a page comes from the checkpoint and the writes since,
in tens of microseconds. `86158936` walks those writes backward, so a busy
heap page is quick too, keeps four decoded checkpoints, and reads memory
committed but never written as zero rather than unknown. The backend reports ITTD_CAP_CHEAP_READS only for recordings
with checkpoint memory, so an older recording still opens, more slowly.

To update an existing build after pulling Sogen, reconfigure with
`-DFETCHCONTENT_FULLY_DISCONNECTED=ON` -- otherwise CMake tries to update the
dependencies it fetched, which can fail on long paths -- and build the same
target again.

```bat
cmake -S %SOGEN% -B %SOGEN_BUILD% -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo ^
      -DSOGEN_BUILD_STATIC=ON -DSOGEN_BUILD_TOOLS=OFF -DSOGEN_ENABLE_PYTHON_BINDINGS=OFF ^
      -DSOGEN_ENABLE_RUST_CODE=OFF -DSOGEN_DISABLE_FEX=ON -DSOGEN_ENABLE_SDL3=OFF ^
      -DSOGEN_ENABLE_LTO=OFF -DSOGEN_ENABLE_SCCACHE=OFF
cmake --build %SOGEN_BUILD% --target windows-ttd windows-ttd-view
```

That builds about 260 objects into 22 static libraries under
`%SOGEN_BUILD%\artifacts`: the reader and view, plus the replay and recorder
(`windows-ttd`), the Windows emulator and what it links (mbedTLS, the
disassembler, the process manager). No SDL, FEX or Rust. The backend imports
nothing beyond the CRT, Winsock, crypt32 and bcrypt -- in particular not the
Windows Hypervisor Platform -- and is about 15 MB.

Until 2026-10-13 the backend needed only `windows-ttd-view`; a build of just
that target no longer links. After updating Sogen, rebuilding only
`windows-ttd-view` does link, against the old `windows-ttd.lib` and
`windows-emulator.lib`, and the result reads every register as zero: always
build `windows-ttd`.

Since 2026-10-14 the backend needs `ttd/next` at `9fa4e1a3` or later, for
`cpu_views_at` (registers at many positions, each register snapshot interval
replayed once for all of them) and `cpu_view::read_register`.

Since 2026-11-09 it is built from TTD-Club/sogen `main` at `253c9488`
(`msbuild/sogen.pin`), and needs it or later:

- **Use a fresh build directory.** Unicorn is now built for x86 and AArch64
  (`UNICORN_ARCH "x86;aarch64"`, a cache value): an older build directory
  keeps `x86`, and the backend then fails to link `uc_init_aarch64`. The
  backend links `aarch64-softmmu.lib` and `iphlpapi.lib` as well.
- `windows_emulator::emu()` is the architecture-neutral `guest_machine`
  now; the backend reaches registers through `x64_emu()`.
- The trace format is version 9. Version 8 recordings (Sogen before
  2026-11-07) still open and answer every query, but cannot be forked: their
  checkpoints hold the old emulator state, and the replay stops with
  "Reading from serialized buffer mismatches written data!".
- `emulator_settings::disable_logging` is no longer read; the backend
  silences the logger itself (and forwards it when asked, `ittd_fork_settings::log`).
- Pass `-DSOGEN_ENABLE_SCCACHE=OFF` to build without sccache even where it
  is installed.

Since 2026-11-11 the pin is `f848464d` (`ttd/next`; `main` is still at
`253c9488`). Nothing in the build changes; what does:

- `emulator_settings::relative_time_start`: where a relative-time run's
  system time starts. `record_program` sets it from
  `ittd_record_request::start_time`. The emulator's saved state carries it,
  so replays and forks start at the recording's own date and need nothing
  set. A program sees the start plus Sogen's simulated uptime (about 44
  minutes), not the start itself.
- That saved state grew without a trace format change: v9 recordings made
  before `f848464d` still open and answer every query, but **do not fork**
  ("Reading from serialized buffer mismatches written data!").
- A message to a port Sogen does not emulate is reported once per
  connection through `on_generic_access` ("Rejecting message to unknown
  port"). The backend passes that one, and "Opening unsupported device", to
  the emulator log (`sogen_log`), and none of the other generic accesses.
- A checkpoint holding a file open in a folder deleted later now restores
  (the folders are recreated too).
- `create-root.bat` copies each collected DLL's `SystemResources\<dll>.mun`.
  WinINet's start-up fails without `wininet.dll.mun`, so an emulation root
  made before this needs it copied in, or the root made again.

Since 2026-11-12 the pin is `154088cc` (`ttd/next`, also `main`). The build
options and libraries are the same; Unicorn comes from TTD-Club's fork
(`ttd` branch, for `UC_CTL_HOOK_NO_SYNC`), so make a fresh snapshot. What
changes:

- **The network is recorded.** A recording keeps every answer the host
  network gave (`network_inputs`), and a replay takes the answers from it
  instead of asking the host, so scans and the probe's replays of a
  live-network recording need no network and see the same traffic. Older
  recordings replay with the backend's offline network, as before.
- That replay stops at the first question the log has no answer for. A fork
  asks new ones as soon as its run differs, so `fork_open` puts the network
  back on (`network_tap::go_live`) after the seek: offline, or the real one
  with `ITTD_NET_LIVE`. Sockets open at the fork position were the
  recording's, and answer as a connection the host reset.
- A pending request on a host socket waits for the host, for up to 10 s of
  real time, without guest time passing (`socket_factory::wait_for_sockets`);
  the backend's switchable factory passes that on.
- The relative clock runs at 100 MHz instead of 1 kHz, so a guest timeout
  lasts about as long as in real time. WinINet's connect and receive
  timeouts no longer expire before any real work is done.
- Trace format version 10: checkpoints after the first hold only the pages
  changed since their base. Versions 7 to 9 still open; recordings made
  before `154088cc` do not fork on it (the saved state gained the network
  input position).
- `keep_kernel_lock_between_instructions`, which the backend turns on: one
  vCPU keeps the kernel lock between instructions instead of taking it for
  each. Nothing the backend runs inside a hook waits for another thread.
- The WinINet fixes from round 9 (the Schannel names, the ALPC reply view,
  a reproducible TLS handshake that checkpoints can hold).

Since 2026-11-13 the pin is `0908dc17` (`ttd/next`, also `main`), for
`fe87f8d9`: Unicorn gave a RAM block mapped after a bigger one the offset of
the bigger one's first page, so a store into a page the register view had
mapped looked like a change to the running instruction's code, and the view
ran a `rep stos` iteration twice (TTD-Club/sogen#100). Only `deps/unicorn`
changed (TTD-Club/unicorn#2). The trace format and saved state are the
same, so `154088cc` recordings still fork.

- **The cache values matter.** `backend-sogen.vcxproj` compiles Sogen's headers
  with the defines this configuration produces (`SOGEN_BUILD_STATIC=1`,
  `SOGEN_ENABLE_RUST_CODE=0`, ...). A different configuration needs the same
  change there.
- **Sogen must be the top-level CMake project.** Its build uses
  `CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR` throughout, so it cannot be pulled in with
  `add_subdirectory`; that is why the backend links the built libraries rather
  than building Sogen itself.
- **Do not point this at a checkout someone is working in.** Building writes
  nothing into the source tree, but a tree in the middle of an edit may not
  build. A clean checkout of a commit (`git archive`, plus the `deps`
  submodules) is what this was tested with.

## 2. Build the backend and the probe

`-t:Rebuild` because MSBuild does not notice when Sogen's libraries change --
neither by name nor by full path -- and would keep a backend linked against
the old reader. It is one source file.

```bat
msbuild msbuild\backend-sogen.vcxproj -t:Rebuild -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64 ^
        -p:SogenRoot=%SOGEN% -p:SogenBuild=%SOGEN_BUILD%
msbuild ida-ttd.slnx -p:Configuration=Release -p:Platform=x64 -m:1
```

The backend lands in `build\Release\backends\ida-ttd-sogen.dll`. It goes in
`ida-ttd\backends\` under the IDA user directory (**TTD > Backends > Install
the Sogen backend...** puts it there): not the plugin's `plugins\ida-ttd\`,
which HCLI replaces on upgrade, and not under `plugins\`, since it is not a
plugin.

## 3. Probe a trace

```bat
build\Release\ittd-probe.exe build\Release\backends\ida-ttd-sogen.dll trace.sogttd [EXPORT]
```

`ittd-probe` loads any backend through the ABI and prints what it reports. It
also checks the promises the ABI makes about positions, because getting those
wrong is silent in the UI:

- **Accesses:** at an access's position, RIP is the instruction that did it.
- **Calls:** at `pos` RIP is the call site, at `entry_pos` the target, and at
  `ret_pos` it is just past the site.
- **Steps and runs:** a step moves one position, and running backward to an
  address lands on its last execution.
- **Batch registers:** `regs_at`, given positions in reverse order, agrees with
  the cursor.

- **Syscalls:** in position order and named, and RIP at a sampled syscall's
  position is a `syscall` instruction.
- **Self-modifying code:** RIP at a hit's write position is the writer, and at
  its first-run position the written instruction.

With `ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY` naming a folder of registry hives, it also
replays: a fork in the middle of the recording with a changed register,
recorded into `ITTD_PROBE_FORK_OUT` (default `fork.sogttd`) and opened again
(it starts at the fork's position, with the parent's RIP and the changed
register), a second fork with the recording settings (writes and executes
only, a shorter checkpoint interval, the log callback; `ITTD_PROBE_NET=1`
opens the network past the position, `ITTD_PROBE_FORK_AT` and
`ITTD_PROBE_FORK_MAX` move it and set its length), and the string and buffer
scans (a sampled string is in memory at or just after its position: the scan
gives the step after the completing write, as Sogen's scanner does, and a
string that lived one step is gone a step later). It also checks that a
recording made against the host is not replayed without
`ITTD_FORK_ALLOW_HOST`. The reference traces were all recorded against the
host, so these runs re-run their file operations on the machine running the
probe.

`ITTD_PROBE_RECORD=<exe>` first records that program from its start into the
TRACE path (`record_program`, against the host with the hives in
`ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY`, or in `ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ROOT`;
`ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ARGS`, `ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_MAX`, `ITTD_PROBE_NET`,
`ITTD_PROBE_LOG=1` to print the emulator's log), then probes the result.
`ITTD_PROBE_PEEK=ADDR,POS` lists what touched 32 bytes at ADDR in the 200
steps before POS and shows them around it.

It exits 0 when every check passes. It is written in C, which also keeps the
ABI header honest about being C.

## 4. Registry hives for replay

Forks and the replay scans run the program again in Sogen's emulator, which
reads the registry the recording ran against: `HARDWARE`, `NTUSER.DAT`,
`SOFTWARE` and `SYSTEM`, and `SAM` and `SECURITY` when they were there
(Sogen's `grab-registry.bat` captures them; an emulation root's `registry`
folder has them).

**Recordings that carry their hives** (Sogen since `8a9fb161`, 2026-10-21)
hold the parts of the hive files the run read, and replay with no hive files
at all (`replay_env` reports `registry_carried`). The backend still loads the
recording's own hive files when they are found, so a fork that reads further
than the recording did can go on; without them, such a fork fails saying it
needs them.

**Older recordings** need the very files the recorder was given: the
manifest holds a fingerprint of them (`registry`), and a new capture of the
same machine gives other bytes. The backend checks a folder against it
(`check_registry`, Sogen's `registry_fingerprint`) and refuses other hives
unless `ITTD_FORK_ANY_REGISTRY` is given.

Where the hives are looked for depends on how the recording was made:

- **In an emulation root:** Sogen loads `<root>\registry` and ignores any
  other folder, so the plugin asks for the root itself when it is elsewhere on
  this machine (`ittd_fork_settings::emulation_root`; `root=DIR` in scripts).
- **Against the host:** the plugin looks, in order, in the folder last chosen,
  a `registry` folder beside the recording, and `ida-ttd\registry\` under the
  IDA user directory, and uses the first that holds the recording's own hives
  (`an.registry` lists them). Given no folder (`ittd-probe` without
  `ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY`), the backend looks in a `registry` folder next
  to `ida-ttd-sogen.dll`.

A recording made against the host also replays only on a Windows build like
the one it ran on: what the program loads or reads after the first checkpoint
(further DLLs, NLS files, fonts) comes from this machine. The manifest's
`system_dlls` (ntdll, kernel32, kernelbase) stands in for that; `replay_env`
says when it differs, and the Registry hives dialog says so. Record in an
emulation root when a recording has to travel.

`SAM` and `SECURITY`, with `SYSTEM`, hold the recording machine's local
password hashes. Sogen no longer requires them, and a recording that carries
its hives holds only their 340-byte headers unless the program opened them;
delete them from a root you mean to share.

## Results

Run on 2026-11-12 against `154088cc`, and again 2026-11-13 against `0908dc17` (same results), Release, on the `ttd-traces`
recordings made that day with Sogen's analyzer (host mode, test-sample with
the network live and `--root-mode rw`): 0 checks failed. The 2026-11-11
recordings fail only their forks, as expected.

| Check | ttd-step-sample (5.9M) | test-sample (31.4M) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| syscalls | 571, all named | 5,437, all named |
| self-modifying code | 11 hits, 0.7 s | 1 hit, 3.4 s |
| fork in the middle, open | 353 ms | 409 ms |
| strings (8+ characters) | 27,840, 1.5 s | 122,592, 8.8 s |
| buffers | 509 | 908 |
| checkpoint intervals verified | 11 of 11 | 62 of 62 |

**Network.** A program that resolves `example.com` and connects was
recorded with `record_program` and the network on. The lookup and the
connect succeed, and the probe's replays of it (scans included) ran with no
network. Forked from position 1,000 to the end with the network on, the
fork resolves and connects again. Forked offline, it gets 11001 (host not
found) and runs to the end. An offline recording forked with the network on
resolves and connects.

**Register views.** At `154088cc`, test-sample recorded with
`record_program` (offline, default root mode) failed one probe check:
`regs_at` had no registers at 16,481,686, where Sogen's register view ran a
`rep stos` iteration twice (TTD-Club/sogen#100). At `0908dc17` that
recording, Sogen's own recording of it and a fresh one all pass, and the
table's numbers are unchanged.

Run on 2026-11-11 against `f848464d`, Release, on the `ttd-traces`
recordings made that day with Sogen's analyzer (host mode, test-sample with
the network live) and on a program recorded with `record_program`: 0 checks
failed. The 2026-11-09 recordings fail only their forks, as expected.

| Check | ttd-step-sample (5.9M) | test-sample (31.5M) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| syscalls | 577, all named | 5,493, all named |
| self-modifying code | 11 hits, 0.6 s | 1 hit, 3.2 s |
| fork in the middle, open | 360 ms | 464 ms |
| strings (8+ characters) | 27,804, 1.6 s | 122,571, 9.0 s |
| buffers | 515 | 936 |
| checkpoint intervals verified | 11 of 11 | 61 of 63 |

test-sample's two failing intervals are around 20,000,000. Before it, a
replay cannot map a file the program has just created (forks from
19,975,579 to 20,000,000 fail). After it, the state at 20,500,000 differs
slightly, and forks still work. The 2026-11-09 recording gave 35
self-modifying hits: Windows updated the system DLLs in between, and a host
recording runs on this machine's DLLs.

**Start time.** A program printing `GetSystemTime` and `QueryInterruptTime`
around `Sleep(60000)`, recorded with `start_time` at the current time, saw
2026-11-11 18:44:58 and then 18:46:10. Without it, it saw 1970-01-01 00:43:53
and 00:45:05. The interrupt time moved 72 s in both.

Run on 2026-11-09 against TTD-Club/sogen `253c9488`, Release, on recordings
made with the backend's own `record_program` (`ITTD_PROBE_RECORD`, offline,
against the host, hives from the emulation root's `registry`). All checks
pass; the 2026-10-21 v8 recording gives the same strings, buffers and
self-modifying code as before, byte for byte, and only its fork fails.

| Check | ttd-step-sample (6.0M) | test-sample (30.8M, offline) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| record from the start | 1.6 s | 9.3 s |
| syscalls | 578, all named | 5,156, all named |
| self-modifying code | 11 hits, 0.6 s | 1 hit, 3.3 s |
| fork in the middle, open | 380 ms | 551 ms |
| strings (8+ characters) | 28,076, 1.6 s | 122,137, 9.1 s |
| buffers | 520 | 926 |

test-sample's reference recording was made with `--network live --root-mode
rw`; offline it takes other paths (fewer syscalls, one self-modifying hit).

**Network access.** A program that resolves `example.com` and connects:
recorded offline, the lookup fails (11001); a fork of that recording from
near its start with `ITTD_NET_LIVE` resolves and connects, and so does a new
recording with it. The replay to the fork's position stays offline.

**`bench.sogttd`** (recorded 2026-10-08, before register snapshots): queries
work, but every register read fails, because `cpu_view` needs snapshots. A trace
that old can be searched but not debugged. The backend reports the reason
through `last_error`, and the core should say so rather than show empty
registers.

## What it does not do yet

Stepping is complete: step over and step out in both directions walk the
thread's instructions back to the call that entered a frame, and pair it
with its `ret` through `calls_to`.

| | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `module_functions` | Sogen records no `.pdata`; the core reads it from the file on disk |
| `prepare` | Nothing to prepare: a seek is a `cpu_view`, with no keyframes |

`docs/licensing.md`:

```md
# Licensing: what ships, under what terms

Settled 2026-10-22, against Sogen `8a9fb161` and TTD Replay SDK 0.9.5;
checked again 2026-11-09 for Sogen `253c9488` (the PDB still holds no
minidump_cpp or flatbuffers code; the DLL now also contains Unicorn's AArch64
target, under Unicorn's same terms; the new `deps/libadrenotools`, BSD-2-Clause,
is Android-only and in the source archive only), 2026-11-11 for
`f848464d` (eight source files changed, no dependency), and 2026-11-12 for
`154088cc` (no new dependency; Unicorn now comes from TTD-Club's fork,
which changes 28 lines and keeps Unicorn's license files and terms; the
PDB check below still finds only `minidump_cpp` and no flatbuffers), and
2026-11-13 for `0908dc17` (a 9-line change to that Unicorn fork, nothing
else). Not legal advice; where a
point is a reading rather than a fact, it says so.

**In short:** ida-ttd is `Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only`, at the recipient's
choice. The plugin package ships both backends: the Microsoft one under the
same dual license, the Sogen one under GPL-2.0-only with its license, notices
and source. Everything can be used commercially.

## Why dual

The Sogen backend is GPL-2.0-only: it links Sogen (GPL-2.0-only) and Unicorn
(GPL-2.0, with QEMU code from many contributors). The plugin loads it into the
same process and calls it, and one reading of the GPL makes the two a single
combined work, which then has to be GPL-2.0-compatible as a whole. The FSF
holds Apache-2.0 incompatible with GPL-2.0. So the plugin is offered under
GPL-2.0-only as well: taken that way, plugin and backend combine under one
license, whichever reading is right. Anyone not shipping the Sogen backend can
keep taking ida-ttd under Apache-2.0, exactly as before.

An exception from Sogen's author would not have been enough: it could cover
Sogen, but not Unicorn, whose copyright is not his.

## What is in each binary, and its terms

| Binary | Terms | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ida-ttd.dll`, `ttd-loader.dll`, the setup DLL | Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only | ida-ttd's code; IDA SDK headers and import libraries (MIT); the API metadata loader `src/common/apimeta` (Apache-2.0, ttd-capa-cpp); Codicons (CC BY 4.0) and Material Symbols (Apache-2.0) icons |
| `ida-ttd-msttd.dll` | Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only | ida-ttd's code; the TTD Replay SDK's headers and import libraries (NuGet `Microsoft.TimeTravelDebugging.Apis`, MIT) |
| `ida-ttd-sogen.dll` | GPL-2.0-only | below |
| `ida-ttd-data/*.bin` | MIT | built from win32metadata/win32json and phnt |

The apimeta loader and the icons stay under their own licenses by choice. The
loader is the same author's code, so his own distribution of it alongside the
GPL backend cannot breach his own terms. The icons are embedded images. They
are not GPL-compatible in the FSF's reading, but they're not program code
either.

The TTD **runtime** (`TTDReplay.dll`, `TTDReplayCPU.dll`) is not in the
package and must never be. WinDbg's license forbids redistributing it but
not commercial use; the standalone TTD package's license forbids both. It is
copied from the user's own WinDbg, or downloaded from Microsoft as WinDbg
after the user accepts WinDbg's license (`scripts/ida_ttd_runtime.py`).

### ida-ttd-sogen.dll

It imports only the MSVC runtime and Windows, and does not link the IDA SDK
or the rest of ida-ttd; it meets the plugin at `src/abi/ida_ttd_backend.h`
(CC0). What it links, from the link inputs and the symbols in its PDB:

| Component | License | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sogen (windows-ttd, emulator, ...) | GPL-2.0-only | makes the DLL GPL-2.0-only |
| Unicorn, with QEMU/TCG/softfloat | GPL-2.0 (QEMU parts GPL-2.0-or-later, BSD, MIT) | |
| Capstone (x86) | BSD-3-Clause, LLVM parts NCSA | |

Two of Sogen's dependencies would be problems and are **not** in the DLL:
**minidump_cpp** (no license at all) and **flatbuffers** (Apache-2.0). The
linker drops both. A search of the PDB finds no `minidump` or `flatbuffers`
symbol: `minidump_cpp` appears only as an include path in compiler command
lines. The same search finds Unicorn, Mbed TLS and zstd. **Check again whenever
the pin in `msbuild/sogen.pin` moves**:

```
grep -a -o -i "minidump[A-Za-z_:]*" ida-ttd-sogen.pdb | sort -u    # only minidump_cpp
grep -a -o -i "flatbuffers[A-Za-z_:]*" ida-ttd-sogen.pdb | sort -u # nothing
```

If either shows real symbols, the DLL cannot ship until it is gone.

## What shipping it takes (all automated)

GPL-2.0 sections 1 and 3: the license text, the notices, and the complete
corresponding source go with the binary.

- **License and notices:** `scripts/sogen_dist.py` writes
  `ida-ttd-backends/ida-ttd-sogen-licenses/`: the GPL text as `COPYING.txt`,
  each component's own license file, and a `README.txt` that says what the
  DLL contains and where its source is. `scripts/package.py` refuses to
  package the DLL without that folder.
- **Source:** `sogen_dist.py` also writes `ida-ttd-sogen-source.zip`:
  - the Sogen tree at the pin, its submodules included;
  - ida-ttd at the commit being built.

  The release workflow attaches it to the same release as the package (source
  offered "from the same place", section 3). minidump_cpp and
  sogen-linux-files state no license, so they are left out of it. The README
  names their repositories and commits; none of their code is in the DLL.
- **Build:** the release workflow builds Sogen at `msbuild/sogen.pin`, then
  the backend, and packages with `--require-sogen`.

## Using it at work

GPL-2.0 puts no restriction on use, commercial or otherwise. Its obligations
fall only on whoever distributes the binary. Anyone who passes the package on
has the same obligations the project does, which the steps above meet. The
TTD runtime comes from WinDbg on the user's machine, under WinDbg's license,
which allows commercial use.

- `docs/modular-backends.md` section 3 calls the IDA SDK proprietary. The SDK
  headers and import libraries are MIT now (`ida-sdk/LICENSE`). IDA itself is
  still proprietary. Nothing changes: no backend links either.
