`msbuild/common.props`:

```props
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<!--
  Everything ida-ttd.vcxproj and ttd-loader.vcxproj build the same way. Each
  imports this once, after Microsoft.Cpp.props.

  A project varies the build by setting these before the import:

    ExtraPreprocessorDefines   e.g. __LOADER__;LOADER_COMPILE
    ExtraIncludeDirectories    e.g. $(IdaSdkDir)\ldr
    ExtraLinkDependencies      e.g. delayimp.lib
    ExtraDelayLoadDLLs         e.g. TTDReplay.dll
    UseTTDReplaySdk            true for the Microsoft backend only
    LinkIdaKernel              false for a backend DLL, which runs without IDA
-->
<Project>
  <!-- TTD Replay SDK: adds the SDK include dir and the x64 import-lib dir. -->
  <Import Project="$(TTDReplaySdkProps)" Condition="'$(UseTTDReplaySdk)' == 'true' And Exists('$(TTDReplaySdkProps)')" />

  <!-- The import above has to be conditional (MSBuild evaluates imports before
       any target could restore the package), so say plainly what is missing
       rather than letting the compile fail on <TTD/IReplayEngine.h>. -->
  <Target Name="RequireTTDReplaySdk" BeforeTargets="PrepareForBuild">
    <Error Condition="'$(UseTTDReplaySdk)' == 'true' And !Exists('$(TTDReplaySdkProps)')"
           Text="The TTD Replay SDK is not restored: $(TTDReplaySdkProps) does not exist. Run &quot;nuget install msbuild\packages.config -OutputDirectory packages&quot; from the repository root." />
  </Target>

  <PropertyGroup>
    <OutDir>$(RepoRoot)build\$(Configuration)\</OutDir>
    <!-- Both projects compile some of the same sources, so each needs its own
         object directory. Kept under build\ so one .gitignore rule covers it. -->
    <IntDir>$(RepoRoot)build\obj\$(ProjectName)\$(Configuration)\</IntDir>
  </PropertyGroup>

  <ItemDefinitionGroup>
    <ClCompile>
      <WarningLevel>Level3</WarningLevel>
      <SDLCheck>true</SDLCheck>
      <ConformanceMode>true</ConformanceMode>
      <LanguageStandard>stdcpp20</LanguageStandard>
      <PrecompiledHeader>NotUsing</PrecompiledHeader>
      <!-- src\ is the single include root: every local include is written from
           it ("debugger/trace_manager.h"), so a header's home is visible at the
           include site and two folders can hold like-named files. -->
      <AdditionalIncludeDirectories>$(SrcDir);$(IdaSdkDir)\include;$(ExtraIncludeDirectories);%(AdditionalIncludeDirectories)</AdditionalIncludeDirectories>
      <!-- NDEBUG in both configurations, not _DEBUG: both keep the RELEASE CRT
           (RuntimeLibrary below) because that is what IDA itself uses. _DEBUG
           would make the MSVC headers reference debug-CRT-only symbols
           (_CrtDbgReport, _calloc_dbg, msvcprtd.lib) that the release CRT does
           not export -> LNK2001/LNK1120. -->
      <PreprocessorDefinitions>NDEBUG;__NT__;__EA64__;__X64__;_CRT_SECURE_NO_WARNINGS;_SILENCE_ALL_CXX20_DEPRECATION_WARNINGS;WIN32;_WINDOWS;_USRDLL;$(ExtraPreprocessorDefines);%(PreprocessorDefinitions)</PreprocessorDefinitions>
      <!-- Match IDA's CRT: the dynamic release runtime, in Debug too. -->
      <RuntimeLibrary>MultiThreadedDLL</RuntimeLibrary>
    </ClCompile>
    <Link>
      <SubSystem>Windows</SubSystem>
      <GenerateDebugInformation>true</GenerateDebugInformation>
      <EnableUAC>false</EnableUAC>
      <AdditionalLibraryDirectories>$(IdaSdkDir)\lib\x64_win_64;%(AdditionalLibraryDirectories)</AdditionalLibraryDirectories>
      <AdditionalDependencies Condition="'$(LinkIdaKernel)' != 'false'">ida.lib;%(AdditionalDependencies)</AdditionalDependencies>
      <AdditionalDependencies Condition="'$(UseTTDReplaySdk)' == 'true'">TTDReplay.lib;%(AdditionalDependencies)</AdditionalDependencies>
      <AdditionalDependencies>$(ExtraLinkDependencies);%(AdditionalDependencies)</AdditionalDependencies>
      <DelayLoadDLLs>$(ExtraDelayLoadDLLs);%(DelayLoadDLLs)</DelayLoadDLLs>
    </Link>
  </ItemDefinitionGroup>

  <ItemDefinitionGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)'=='Debug'">
    <ClCompile>
      <!-- Stated rather than inherited: this is an unoptimised build with full
           debug info, not a debug-CRT build, so the usual Debug defaults that
           follow from UseDebugLibraries do not all apply here. -->
      <Optimization>Disabled</Optimization>
    </ClCompile>
  </ItemDefinitionGroup>

  <ItemDefinitionGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)'=='Release'">
    <ClCompile>
      <FunctionLevelLinking>true</FunctionLevelLinking>
      <IntrinsicFunctions>true</IntrinsicFunctions>
    </ClCompile>
    <Link>
      <EnableCOMDATFolding>true</EnableCOMDATFolding>
      <OptimizeReferences>true</OptimizeReferences>
    </Link>
  </ItemDefinitionGroup>
</Project>
```

`msbuild/gen_filters.py`:

```py
"""Generate .vcxproj.filters mirroring the src/ folder tree, from the project's
own item lists, so the two can never drift."""
import pathlib, re, uuid, hashlib

HEADER_EXT = {".h", ".hh", ".hpp", ".inl"}


def stable_guid(name):
    h = hashlib.md5(("ida-ttd:" + name).encode()).hexdigest()
    return "{%s}" % str(uuid.UUID(h)).upper()


def gen(proj_path):
    proj = pathlib.Path(proj_path)
    text = proj.read_text()
    items = re.findall(r'<(ClInclude|ClCompile) Include="\$\(SrcDir\)\\([^"]+)" />', text)

    folders = []
    rows = []
    for tag, rel in items:
        rel = rel.replace("/", "\\")
        folder = "\\".join(rel.split("\\")[:-1])
        if folder and folder not in folders:
            folders.append(folder)
        rows.append((tag, rel, folder))

    # Every intermediate folder needs its own <Filter> entry.
    all_folders = []
    for f in folders:
        parts = f.split("\\")
        for i in range(1, len(parts) + 1):
            p = "\\".join(parts[:i])
            if p not in all_folders:
                all_folders.append(p)
    all_folders.sort()

    out = ['<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>',
           '<Project ToolsVersion="4.0" xmlns="http://schemas.microsoft.com/developer/msbuild/2003">',
           '  <!-- Generated to mirror the src/ tree; see msbuild/gen_filters.py. -->',
           '  <ItemGroup>']
    for f in all_folders:
        out.append('    <Filter Include="%s">' % f)
        out.append('      <UniqueIdentifier>%s</UniqueIdentifier>' % stable_guid(f))
        out.append('    </Filter>')
    out.append('  </ItemGroup>')

    for tag in ("ClInclude", "ClCompile"):
        group = [r for r in rows if r[0] == tag]
        if not group:
            continue
        out.append('  <ItemGroup>')
        for _, rel, folder in group:
            out.append('    <%s Include="$(SrcDir)\\%s">' % (tag, rel))
            out.append('      <Filter>%s</Filter>' % folder)
            out.append('    </%s>' % tag)
        out.append('  </ItemGroup>')

    out.append('  <ItemGroup>')
    out.append('    <None Include="packages.config" />')
    out.append('  </ItemGroup>')
    out.append('</Project>')
    dest = proj.with_suffix(".vcxproj.filters")
    dest.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    print("wrote", dest, len(rows), "items")


gen("msbuild/ida-ttd.vcxproj")
gen("msbuild/ttd-loader.vcxproj")
gen("msbuild/backend-msttd.vcxproj")
gen("msbuild/ida-ttd-loader-setup.vcxproj")

```

`scripts/ida_ttd.py`:

```py
"""Drive the ida-ttd plugin from Python inside IDA.

Installed in ida-ttd-python/ beside the plugin DLL, which the plugin puts on
sys.path when it loads. In the IDAPython console, a script, or an MCP
server's Python:

    import ida_ttd
    s = ida_ttd.Session()                # the TTD debugger session in this IDA
    s.start()                            # replay the recording this database is for
    s.position, hex(s.pc)
    s.step(); s.step(back=True)
    s.goto("1A:2F")
    s.regs()["rax"]
    s.read(s.reg("rsp"), 0x40)           # bytes
    for c in s.syscalls(): print(c["name"], hex(c["result"]))
    s.origin("rax")                      # where the value in rax came from
    s.origin(0x1234, 8)                  # ... or the 8 bytes at 0x1234
    s.handles(); s.memory_map(); s.calls_to("kernel32!CreateFileW")

    r = ida_ttd.Recording(r"C:\\traces\\run.sogttd")   # a recording, no debugger
    r.seek("first"); r.step(); r.regs(); r.read(0x401000, 16)

Underneath is one IDC function, ttd("command args..."), which answers in
JSON. call() sends a command and returns the answer as a dict; the classes
turn answers into Python values (addresses and numbers as ints, bytes as
bytes). Positions stay strings in the recording's own syntax
("Sequence:Steps" for Microsoft TTD, a step count for Sogen) and are passed
back unchanged. A failure raises TtdError with the plugin's reason.
call("help") lists every command; docs/scripting.md describes them.

It works the same in the GUI, in idat, and in an idalib worker. Without the
plugin loaded, exec() this file's source and call ensure_loaded().
"""

import json

import ida_expr
import ida_idaapi
import ida_loader


class TtdError(RuntimeError):
    """The plugin answered {"ok": false, "error": ...}."""


def _quote(arg):
    s = str(arg)
    if not s or any(c in s for c in ' \t"'):
        if '"' in s:
            raise ValueError("arguments cannot contain double quotes: %r" % s)
        return '"%s"' % s
    return s


def _arg(v):
    """A command argument: ints go as hex, the plugin's number syntax."""
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "1" if v else "0"
    if isinstance(v, int):
        return "%X" % v
    return v


def loaded():
    """Whether the plugin's ttd() function exists in this IDA."""
    rv = ida_expr.idc_value_t()
    return ida_expr.eval_idc_expr(rv, ida_idaapi.BADADDR, 'ttd("help")') is None


def ensure_loaded(plugin="ida-ttd"):
    """Load the plugin if this IDA has not (an idalib worker may not load
    plugins on its own). 'plugin' is a name in IDA's plugins directory or a
    full path to the DLL."""
    if loaded():
        return True
    ida_loader.load_plugin(plugin)
    return loaded()


def raw(line):
    """Send one command line and return the parsed answer, failed or not."""
    rv = ida_expr.idc_value_t()
    # json.dumps writes a valid IDC string literal for anything a command
    # line contains: quotes and backslashes are escaped the same way.
    err = ida_expr.eval_idc_expr(rv, ida_idaapi.BADADDR,
                                 "ttd(%s)" % json.dumps(line, ensure_ascii=False))
    if err is not None:
        raise TtdError("ttd() is not available (%s); is the plugin loaded? "
                       "Try ensure_loaded()." % err)
    return json.loads(rv.c_str())


def call(command, *args):
    """Run a command; return its answer, or raise TtdError."""
    line = " ".join([command] + [_quote(_arg(a)) for a in args])
    answer = raw(line)
    if not answer.get("ok"):
        raise TtdError("%s: %s" % (command, answer.get("error", "failed")))
    return answer


def h(value):
    """An answer's "0x..." string as an int."""
    return int(value, 16)


def py(value):
    """An answer with its numbers as ints, recursively. The plugin writes a
    number as a "0x..." string and lists its key in the object's "_hex", so
    only those are converted: text that happens to read "0x41" (a string the
    program wrote, a name) stays text. "_hex" itself is dropped."""
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        hexed = set(value.get("_hex", ()))
        out = {}
        for k, v in value.items():
            if k == "_hex":
                continue
            if k in hexed:
                out[k] = [int(x, 16) for x in v] if isinstance(v, list) else int(v, 16)
            else:
                out[k] = py(v)
        return out
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [py(v) for v in value]
    return value


def _bytes(text):
    """The plugin's hex dump ("??" for unknown bytes, read as 0) as bytes."""
    return bytes(0 if text[i:i + 2] == "??" else int(text[i:i + 2], 16)
                 for i in range(0, len(text) - 1, 2))


def _kinds(kinds):
    """Access kinds as the plugin takes them: any of "r", "w", "x"."""
    k = kinds.lower()
    if not k or any(c not in "rwx" for c in k):
        raise ValueError("access kinds are the letters r, w and x: %r" % kinds)
    return k


def _record_options(net, checkpoint_interval, access, elevated, log):
    """The recording options as an.fork / an.record words; None keeps the
    Sogen setting."""
    words = []
    if net is not None:
        words.append("net" if net else "nonet")
    if checkpoint_interval is not None:
        words.append("ckpt=%X" % checkpoint_interval)
    if access is not None:
        words.append("access=" + _kinds(access))
    if elevated:
        words.append("elevated")
    if log:
        words.append("log")
    return words


def record(program, path, max_instructions=0, args=None, cwd=None, registry=None,
           root=None, host=False, net=None, checkpoint_interval=None, access=None,
           elevated=False, log=False, place=None, replace=False, start=None):
    """Run 'program' from its start in Sogen's emulator and record it into
    'path' (TTD > Backends > Record a program with Sogen), with no recording
    open. Without 'root' (an emulation root) it runs against this machine's
    files, which needs host=True; 'registry' is the hives folder (default:
    the first known one). net, checkpoint_interval, access ("rwx") default to
    the Sogen settings. With a root, 'place' (a guest folder such as
    "C:\\ida-ttd") copies a program from outside the root into it first;
    replace=True overwrites a different file already there. 'start' is
    "now", "1970" or a UTC "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS", the date the program
    starts at (default: the sogen_start_now setting). Returns
    {"instructions", "cancelled", "path", "network", "program", "placed"}."""
    words = [program, path]
    if max_instructions:
        words.append(max_instructions)
    for key, value in (("args", args), ("cwd", cwd), ("registry", registry), ("root", root),
                       ("place", place), ("start", start)):
        if value:
            words.append("%s=%s" % (key, value))
    if host:
        words.append("host")
    if replace:
        words.append("replace")
    words += _record_options(net, checkpoint_interval, access, elevated, log)
    return py(call("an.record", *words))


class Session(object):
    """The TTD debugger session in this IDA: the recording this database was
    opened from, replayed through IDA's debugger. Movements wait for the stop;
    the analyses are the TTD menu's, without their windows."""

    # ---- state and movement ----------------------------------------------
    def start(self, timeout=120):
        """Start the replay and wait for the first stop. Fails when a
        debugging session is already running."""
        return py(call("start", "timeout=%X" % timeout))

    def stop(self):
        """End the session."""
        return py(call("stop"))

    def state(self):
        return py(call("state"))

    @property
    def position(self):
        """Where the replay is, in the recording's own position syntax."""
        return call("state").get("pos")

    @property
    def pc(self):
        return h(call("state")["pc"])

    # Each movement waits for the stop, 'timeout' seconds at most (the
    # answer then has "timed_out", and the replay is still moving).
    def _move(self, what, back, timeout, *args):
        words = list(args) + (["back"] if back else [])
        if timeout is not None:
            words.append("timeout=%X" % timeout)
        return py(call(what, *words))

    def step(self, back=False, timeout=None):
        return self._move("step", back, timeout)

    def step_over(self, back=False, timeout=None):
        return self._move("over", back, timeout)

    def step_out(self, back=False, timeout=None):
        return self._move("out", back, timeout)

    def run(self, back=False, timeout=None):
        """To the next breakpoint, or the edge of the recording."""
        return self._move("run", back, timeout)

    def run_to(self, ea, back=False, timeout=None):
        return self._move("runto", back, timeout, ea)

    def goto(self, position, timeout=None):
        # A position is passed as written: Sogen's are decimal step counts.
        words = [str(position)] + ([] if timeout is None else ["timeout=%X" % timeout])
        return py(call("goto", *words))

    # ---- what is there -----------------------------------------------------
    def regs(self):
        """The registers IDA shows, by lower-case name."""
        return py(call("regs")["regs"])

    def reg(self, name):
        return self.regs()[name.lower()]

    def read(self, ea, size=0x40):
        """Memory as IDA reads it at the current position."""
        return _bytes(call("read", ea, size)["bytes"])

    def segments(self, limit=400):
        return py(call("segments", limit)["segments"])

    # ---- whole-recording questions -----------------------------------------
    def syscalls(self, limit=100000):
        """Every syscall: position, thread, number, name, result, arguments."""
        return py(call("an.syscalls", limit)["syscalls"])

    def calls_to(self, target, limit=10000):
        """Every call to a function (an address, or "module!Glob*") with its
        arguments and return value."""
        return py(call("an.trace", target, limit)["calls"])

    def accesses(self, lo, hi=None, kinds="rw", limit=10000):
        """Every read, write or execute ("r", "w", "x") of [lo, hi)."""
        hi = lo + 1 if hi is None else hi
        return py(call("an.search", lo, hi, _kinds(kinds), limit)["accesses"])

    def origin(self, what, size=8, at=None, through=True):
        """Where a value came from: what is a register name ("rax", "xmm0") or
        an address (with 'size' bytes), as of the current position, or of
        'at' (a position) when given. The chain of hops back to where the
        value was made, the first hop first. It goes through computations
        made from a single value; through=False stops at every computation."""
        tail = (["from=" + at] if at else []) + ([] if through else ["stop"])
        if isinstance(what, str):
            return py(call("an.origin", what, *tail)["chain"])
        return py(call("an.origin", "mem", what, size, *tail)["chain"])

    def origin_graph(self, what, size=8, at=None, max_nodes=60):
        """Every chain at once, as the value origin graph draws it: at each
        instruction that combined several values, each value it read is
        followed (address registers and rsp are not). 'nodes' are hops as
        origin() gives them, [0] the value asked about; each of 'edges' goes
        'from' the hop that used a value 'to' the hop that set it ('input':
        one of several the instruction read). 'truncated' when max_nodes cut
        it short."""
        tail = (["from=" + at] if at else []) + ["max=%x" % max_nodes]
        if isinstance(what, str):
            return py(call("an.origingraph", what, *tail))
        return py(call("an.origingraph", "mem", what, size, *tail))

    def show_origin_graph(self, what, size=8, at=None):
        """Open the value origin graph window for a value, as the TTD menu
        does, without asking for it."""
        tail = ["from=" + at] if at else []
        if isinstance(what, str):
            return call("ui.origingraph", what, *tail)
        return call("ui.origingraph", "mem", what, size, *tail)

    def inputs(self, at=None):
        """The values the instruction about to run at 'at' (default: the
        current position) read: each has 'what', 'value', 'address' (true for
        a register that only formed an address), and 'reg', or 'addr' and
        'size'. Pass a hop's 'by_pos' to continue a chain that ended at a
        computation, then origin(..., at=that by_pos) on the input."""
        r = call("an.inputs", at) if at else call("an.inputs")
        return py(r["inputs"])

    def handles(self, limit=100000):
        """The handles the program opened and closed."""
        return py(call("an.handles", limit)["handles"])

    def memory_map(self, limit=100000):
        """The regions at the current position: base, size, protection, type, use."""
        return py(call("an.regions", limit)["regions"])

    def self_modifying(self, limit=100000):
        return py(call("an.selfmod", limit)["hits"])

    def strings(self, min_length=8, limit=100000):
        return py(call("an.strings", min_length, limit)["strings"])

    def buffers(self, limit=100000):
        return py(call("an.buffers", limit)["buffers"])

    def call_tree(self, limit=100000):
        """The calls the function at the current position made in this run of it."""
        return py(call("an.calltree", limit)["calls"])

    def heat(self):
        """The memory heatmap's counts: per page, per slice of time,
        [slice, reads, writes, executes]."""
        call("an.heat")
        return call("ui.heat")["heat"]


class Recording(object):
    """A recording opened through its backend, without the debugger: a cursor
    to move and read at, and the backend's queries. One at a time; close() it,
    or use it as a context manager."""

    # The handle of the recording drv.* drives now: opening another closes
    # this one in the plugin, so an older object must refuse to go on.
    _current = None

    def __init__(self, path, backend=None):
        args = [path] + ([backend] if backend else [])
        self.info = py(call("drv.open", *args))
        self._handle = self.info.get("handle")
        Recording._current = self._handle

    def _call(self, command, *args):
        if self._handle is None or Recording._current != self._handle:
            raise TtdError("%s: this Recording was closed, or another one was opened "
                           "since (one at a time)" % command)
        return call(command, *args)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        self.close()

    def close(self):
        """Close it; closing one already closed, or superseded, does nothing."""
        if self._handle is not None and Recording._current == self._handle:
            call("drv.close")
            Recording._current = None
        self._handle = None

    # ---- the cursor --------------------------------------------------------
    def where(self):
        """The cursor: position, thread, pc, sp."""
        return py(self._call("drv.pos"))

    @property
    def position(self):
        return self._call("drv.pos")["pos"]

    def seek(self, position):
        """A position, or "first" / "last"."""
        return py(self._call("drv.seek", str(position)))

    def step(self, back=False):
        return py(self._call("drv.step", *(["back"] if back else [])))

    def step_over(self, back=False):
        return py(self._call("drv.over", *(["back"] if back else [])))

    def step_out(self, back=False):
        return py(self._call("drv.out", *(["back"] if back else [])))

    def run(self, back=False):
        """To a breakpoint set with breakpoints(), or the edge."""
        return py(self._call("drv.run", *(["back"] if back else [])))

    def run_to(self, ea, back=False):
        return py(self._call("drv.runto", ea, *(["back"] if back else [])))

    def breakpoints(self, *bps):
        """Replace the breakpoints: addresses, or (ea, size, "rwx") tuples."""
        args = []
        for b in bps:
            if isinstance(b, tuple):
                args.append("%X:%X:%s" % (b[0], b[1], _kinds(b[2])))
            else:
                args.append(_arg(b))
        return py(self._call("drv.bp", *args))

    def regs(self):
        return py(self._call("drv.regs")["regs"])

    def read(self, ea, size=0x40):
        """Memory at the cursor; bytes the recording does not have read as 0."""
        return _bytes(self._call("drv.read", ea, size)["bytes"])

    def instructions(self, n=16):
        return py(self._call("drv.insns", n)["instructions"])

    # ---- the recording -------------------------------------------------------
    def modules(self):
        return py(self._call("drv.modules")["modules"])

    def threads(self, live=False):
        return py(self._call("drv.threads", *(["live"] if live else []))["threads"])

    def timeline(self, limit=10000):
        return py(self._call("drv.timeline", limit)["events"])

    def accesses(self, lo, hi=None, kinds="rw", limit=10000):
        hi = lo + 1 if hi is None else hi
        return py(self._call("drv.accesses", lo, hi, _kinds(kinds), limit)["accesses"])

    def calls_to(self, ea, limit=10000):
        return py(self._call("drv.calls", ea, limit)["calls"])

    def syscalls(self, limit=100000):
        return py(self._call("drv.syscalls", limit)["syscalls"])

    def exceptions(self):
        return py(self._call("drv.exceptions")["exceptions"])

    def memory_changes(self, limit=100000):
        return py(self._call("drv.map", limit)["changes"])
```

`scripts/ida_ttd_calltree.py`:

```py
"""The call tree window, drawn with PySide6.

A real tree control (columns, expand arrows, theme colors) is a Qt widget,
and Hex-Rays steer plugins away from Qt in C++ (it ties the binary to IDA's
exact Qt build) towards PySide6 in IDAPython. The plugin builds the tree; this
draws it, fetching it with ttd("ui.calltree") and travelling with
ttd("ui.travel POS"), the same commands a test uses. Without IDAPython,
src/ui/ui_calltree.cpp falls back to a text view.

The plugin calls show() through ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module("ida_ttd_calltree").
"""
import json
import ida_kernwin
import idc
from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets


def ttd(cmd):
    # cmd becomes an IDC string literal: escape what would end it early.
    cmd = cmd.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
    return json.loads(idc.eval_idc('ttd("%s")' % cmd))


# The open windows' forms, by kind or title. Kept across importlib.reload
# (ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module), which runs this file again in the same
# namespace: a window opened before a reinstall is still found and reused.
try:
    _forms
except NameError:
    _forms = {}


def show():
    """Open the call tree the plugin built last, replacing an open one of
    the same function."""

    data = ttd("ui.calltree")
    if not data.get("ok"):
        raise RuntimeError(data.get("error", "no call tree"))
    tree = data["tree"]

    POS_ROLE = QtCore.Qt.UserRole
    SITE_ROLE = QtCore.Qt.UserRole + 1
    TARGET_ROLE = QtCore.Qt.UserRole + 2
    COLUMNS = ["Call", "Position", "Called from", "Returns at", "Calls"]

    class CallTreeForm(ida_kernwin.PluginForm):
        def OnCreate(self, form):
            self.parent = self.FormToPyQtWidget(form)
            self.view = QtWidgets.QTreeWidget()
            self.view.setColumnCount(len(COLUMNS))
            self.view.setHeaderLabels(COLUMNS)
            self.view.setUniformRowHeights(True)
            # Alternate rows a shade off the background: IDA's dark theme
            # leaves AlternateBase near white, under light text.
            pal = self.view.palette()
            base = pal.color(QtGui.QPalette.Base)
            alt = base.lighter(118) if base.lightness() < 128 else base.darker(104)
            pal.setColor(QtGui.QPalette.AlternateBase, alt)
            self.view.setPalette(pal)
            self.view.setAlternatingRowColors(True)
            self.view.setSelectionMode(QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView.SingleSelection)
            self.view.setContextMenuPolicy(QtCore.Qt.CustomContextMenu)
            self.view.customContextMenuRequested.connect(self.menu)
            self.view.itemActivated.connect(lambda item, col: self.travel(item))

            self.filter = QtWidgets.QLineEdit()
            self.filter.setPlaceholderText("Filter by function name")
            self.filter.setClearButtonEnabled(True)
            self.filter.textChanged.connect(self.apply_filter)

            self.status = QtWidgets.QLabel()
            self.status.setTextInteractionFlags(QtCore.Qt.TextSelectableByMouse)

            layout = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout()
            layout.setContentsMargins(2, 2, 2, 2)
            layout.addWidget(self.filter)
            layout.addWidget(self.view)
            layout.addWidget(self.status)
            self.parent.setLayout(layout)
            self.populate()

        def populate(self):
            rows = tree["rows"]
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(False)
            root = QtWidgets.QTreeWidgetItem([tree["name"], tree["from"], "", tree["to"], str(len(rows))])
            font = root.font(0)
            font.setBold(True)
            root.setFont(0, font)
            root.setData(0, POS_ROLE, tree["from"])
            root.setData(0, TARGET_ROLE, tree["root"])
            self.view.addTopLevelItem(root)
            # Rows are in call order, each one level deeper than its caller,
            # so a row's parent is the nearest row above it one level up.
            stack = [root]
            items = [root]
            depths = [0]
            for r in rows:
                depth = r["depth"] + 1
                del stack[depth:]
                parent = stack[-1]
                name = r["name"] + ("  (jump)" if r.get("jump") else "")
                item = QtWidgets.QTreeWidgetItem(parent, [name, r["pos"], r["from"], r["ret"], ""])
                item.setData(0, POS_ROLE, r["pos"])
                item.setData(0, SITE_ROLE, r["site"])
                item.setData(0, TARGET_ROLE, r["target"])
                if r.get("jump"):
                    f = item.font(0)
                    f.setItalic(True)
                    item.setFont(0, f)
                stack.append(item)
                items.append(item)
                depths.append(len(stack) - 1)
            self.count_below(items, depths)
            if len(rows) <= 300:
                self.view.expandAll()
            else:
                self.view.expandToDepth(0)
            for c in range(1, len(COLUMNS)):
                self.view.resizeColumnToContents(c)
            self.view.setColumnWidth(0, max(self.view.columnWidth(0), 360))
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(True)
            self.view.setCurrentItem(root)
            note = "%d call(s) from %s to %s, thread %s" % (len(rows), tree["from"], tree["to"], tree["tid"])
            if tree.get("from_cursor"):
                note += "; the function's entry was not found, so this starts at the cursor"
            if tree.get("truncated"):
                note += "; cut short"
            self.status.setText(note + ".  Double-click or Enter to go there.")

        def count_below(self, items, depths):
            # Subtree sizes from the items in tree order (what follows an item
            # at greater depth is below it). Walked from the end so a child's
            # size is known when its parent skips over it; no recursion, which
            # a deep tree would take past Python's limit.
            below = [0] * len(items)
            for i in range(len(items) - 1, -1, -1):
                end = i + 1
                while end < len(items) and depths[end] > depths[i]:
                    end += 1 + below[end]
                below[i] = end - i - 1
                if i != 0 and below[i]:
                    items[i].setText(4, str(below[i]))

        def travel(self, item):
            pos = item.data(0, POS_ROLE)
            if pos:
                # With the tree's recording, so a tree left open across a
                # switch to a fork does not travel into the fork.
                ttd("ui.travel %s %s" % (pos, tree.get("recording", "")))

        def menu(self, point):
            item = self.view.itemAt(point)
            if item is None:
                return
            m = QtWidgets.QMenu(self.view)
            m.addAction("Go to this call", lambda: self.travel(item))
            site = item.data(0, SITE_ROLE)
            target = item.data(0, TARGET_ROLE)
            if site:
                m.addAction("Show the call site", lambda: ida_kernwin.jumpto(int(site, 16)))
            if target:
                m.addAction("Show the function called", lambda: ida_kernwin.jumpto(int(target, 16)))
            m.addSeparator()
            m.addAction("Expand everything below", lambda: self.expand_below(item))
            m.addAction("Collapse everything", self.view.collapseAll)
            m.exec(self.view.viewport().mapToGlobal(point))

        def expand_below(self, item):
            # Iterative: a deep tree would pass Python's recursion limit, and
            # updates stay off until the whole subtree is open.
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(False)
            todo = [item]
            while todo:
                it = todo.pop()
                it.setExpanded(True)
                todo.extend(it.child(i) for i in range(it.childCount()))
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(True)

        def apply_filter(self, text):
            text = text.strip().lower()
            # Every item with its parent's index, parents first; then walked
            # from the end so children are settled first. A row stays when it
            # or something below it matches.
            order = []
            todo = [(self.view.topLevelItem(i), -1) for i in range(self.view.topLevelItemCount())]
            while todo:
                item, parent = todo.pop()
                order.append((item, parent))
                todo.extend((item.child(i), len(order) - 1) for i in range(item.childCount()))
            below = [False] * len(order)
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(False)
            for i in range(len(order) - 1, -1, -1):
                item, parent = order[i]
                keep = below[i] or not text or text in item.text(0).lower()
                item.setHidden(not keep)
                if text and below[i]:
                    item.setExpanded(True)
                if keep and parent >= 0:
                    below[parent] = True
            self.view.setUpdatesEnabled(True)

        def OnClose(self, form):
            _forms.pop(title, None)

    title = "TTD call tree: " + tree["name"]
    old = ida_kernwin.find_widget(title)
    if old is not None:
        ida_kernwin.close_widget(old, 0)
    form = CallTreeForm()
    _forms[title] = form
    form.Show(title, options=ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_DP_TAB | ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_RESTORE)


```

`scripts/ida_ttd_graph.py`:

```py
"""The plugin's graph window, drawn with PySide6.

One window per kind of graph ("forks", "origin"). The plugin builds the model
(src/ui/graph_view.cpp) and this draws it: ttd("ui.graph KIND") hands over the
nodes and edges, ttd("ui.graphact KIND NODE ACTION") runs a node's action. It
is drawn as IDA draws its own graphs: plain boxes with a shadow, text in the
disassembly font and colors (the node's kind as a comment), right-angled
edges, in a top-down tree. Colors are read from IDA's theme, so light and
dark themes both work.

Mouse and keys as in IDA's graphs: drag to pan, wheel to scroll, Ctrl+wheel
to zoom; F (or Home) fits the graph, Ctrl+0 shows it at 100%.

The plugin calls show() through ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module("ida_ttd_graph").
"""
import json
import re
import ida_kernwin
import idc
from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets


def ttd(cmd):
    # cmd becomes an IDC string literal: escape what would end it early.
    cmd = cmd.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
    return json.loads(idc.eval_idc('ttd("%s")' % cmd))


# The open windows' forms, by kind or title. Kept across importlib.reload
# (ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module), which runs this file again in the same
# namespace: a window opened before a reinstall is still found and reused.
try:
    _forms
except NameError:
    _forms = {}


def show(kind, first):
    """Open the graph of 'kind', or redraw its open window with the model
    the plugin holds now ('first': also bring the window to the front)."""
    forms = _forms

    def fetch():
        r = ttd("ui.graph " + kind)
        if not r.get("ok"):
            raise RuntimeError(r.get("error", "no graph"))
        return r["graph"]

    def mix(a, b, t):
        return QtGui.QColor(int(a.red() + (b.red() - a.red()) * t),
                            int(a.green() + (b.green() - a.green()) * t),
                            int(a.blue() + (b.blue() - a.blue()) * t))

    # IDA's theme colors, read from a disassembly view (CustomIDAMemo).
    # Fallbacks: IDA's shipped light and dark values.
    LIGHT = {
        "line-bg-default": "#ffffff", "line-fg-insn": "#000080", "line-fg-default": "#000080",
        "line-fg-automatic-comment": "#808080", "line-fg-regular-comment": "#0000ff",
        "line-fg-numlit-in-insn": "#008000", "line-fg-register-name": "#000080",
        "line-fg-keyword": "#000080", "line-fg-punctuation": "#000080",
        "graph-bg-top": "#ffffff", "graph-bg-bottom": "#e0f8ff",
        "graph-node-shadow": "#000000", "graph-node-high1": "#ccffff",
        "graph-edge-normal": "#0000ff", "graph-node-frame-selected": "#aa5500",
    }
    DARK = {
        "line-bg-default": "#2d2d2d", "line-fg-insn": "#ffffff", "line-fg-default": "#aaaaaa",
        "line-fg-automatic-comment": "#808080", "line-fg-regular-comment": "#ffc5f3",
        "line-fg-numlit-in-insn": "#d25032", "line-fg-register-name": "#73adad",
        "line-fg-keyword": "#ababab", "line-fg-punctuation": "#c0c0c0",
        "graph-bg-top": "#b2b2b2", "graph-bg-bottom": "#b2b2b2",
        "graph-node-shadow": "#242424", "graph-node-high1": "#003900",
        "graph-edge-normal": "#0043cb", "graph-node-frame-selected": "#c68e00",
    }

    def theme_colors(dark):
        out = dict(DARK if dark else LIGHT)
        memo = None
        for w in QtWidgets.QApplication.allWidgets():
            if w.metaObject().className() == "CustomIDAMemo":
                memo = w
                break
        if memo is None:
            return out
        for key in list(out):
            for name in (key, key.replace("-", "_")):
                v = memo.property(name)
                if isinstance(v, QtGui.QColor) and v.isValid():
                    out[key] = v.name()
                    break
        return out

    class Theme(object):
        def __init__(self, widget):
            pal = widget.palette()
            self.dark = pal.color(QtGui.QPalette.Base).lightness() < 128
            c = dict((k, QtGui.QColor(v)) for k, v in theme_colors(self.dark).items())
            self.canvas_top = c["graph-bg-top"]
            self.canvas_bottom = c["graph-bg-bottom"]
            self.canvas = mix(self.canvas_top, self.canvas_bottom, 0.5)
            self.node = c["line-bg-default"]
            self.root = c["graph-node-high1"]
            self.text = c["line-fg-insn"]
            self.plain = c["line-fg-default"]
            self.comment = c["line-fg-automatic-comment"]
            self.number = c["line-fg-numlit-in-insn"]
            self.register = c["line-fg-register-name"]
            self.punct = c["line-fg-punctuation"]
            self.frame = mix(self.node, self.text, 0.55)
            self.shadow = c["graph-node-shadow"]
            self.edge = c["graph-edge-normal"]
            self.select = c["graph-node-frame-selected"]
            # Edge labels sit on the background, not in a node.
            ink = QtGui.QColor("#000000" if self.canvas.lightness() > 128 else "#ffffff")
            self.label = mix(ink, self.canvas, 0.3)

    PAD_X = 6
    PAD_Y = 4
    SHADOW = 4
    MAX_W = 520
    HGAP = 32
    VGAP = 48

    class Fonts(object):
        def __init__(self, widget):
            # The disassembly's font, else any fixed font.
            font = None
            for w in QtWidgets.QApplication.allWidgets():
                if w.metaObject().className() == "CustomIDAMemo":
                    font = QtGui.QFont(w.font())
                    break
            if font is None:
                font = QtGui.QFontDatabase.systemFont(QtGui.QFontDatabase.FixedFont)
            self.code = font
            self.fm = QtGui.QFontMetrics(font)
            self.line = self.fm.height()

    REGS = set(
        "rax rbx rcx rdx rsi rdi rbp rsp rip eax ebx ecx edx esi edi ebp esp eip "
        "ax bx cx dx si di bp sp al bl cl dl ah bh ch dh sil dil bpl spl".split()
        + ["r%d%s" % (i, s) for i in range(8, 16) for s in ("", "d", "w", "b")]
        + ["%smm%d" % (p, i) for p in "xyz" for i in range(32)])
    TOKEN = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*|0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+|[0-9][0-9A-Fa-f]*h?|\s+|.")
    NUMBER = re.compile(r"^(0x[0-9A-Fa-f]+|[0-9][0-9A-Fa-f]*h?)$")

    def insn_runs(theme, text):
        # Mnemonic, registers, numbers and punctuation, colored as IDA does.
        runs = []
        first = True
        for tok in TOKEN.findall(text):
            if tok.isspace():
                color = theme.text
            elif first:
                color = theme.text
                first = False
            elif tok.lower() in REGS:
                color = theme.register
            elif NUMBER.match(tok):
                color = theme.number
            elif tok.isalnum() or tok[0] == "_":
                color = theme.text
            else:
                color = theme.punct
            runs.append((tok, color))
        return runs

    class Card(QtWidgets.QGraphicsItem):
        def __init__(self, form, node):
            super().__init__()
            self.form = form
            self.node = node
            self.setFlag(QtWidgets.QGraphicsItem.ItemIsSelectable, True)
            if node.get("tooltip"):
                self.setToolTip(node["tooltip"])
            self.measure()

        def measure(self):
            f = self.form.fonts
            n = self.node
            badge = n.get("badge") or ""
            # Title with its kind as a comment, the instruction, comment lines.
            self.rows = [("title", n["title"], badge)]
            if n.get("code"):
                self.rows.append(("code", n["code"], ""))
            for line in n.get("lines", []):
                self.rows.append(("comment", "; " + line, ""))
            want = 0
            for kind_, text, extra in self.rows:
                w = f.fm.horizontalAdvance(text)
                if extra:
                    w += f.fm.horizontalAdvance("  ; " + extra)
                want = max(want, w)
            self.w = int(min(want + 2 * PAD_X, MAX_W))
            self.h = int(len(self.rows) * f.line + 2 * PAD_Y)

        def boundingRect(self):
            return QtCore.QRectF(-2, -2, self.w + SHADOW + 4, self.h + SHADOW + 4)

        def paint(self, painter, option, widget=None):
            t = self.form.theme
            f = self.form.fonts
            n = self.node
            rect = QtCore.QRectF(0, 0, self.w, self.h)
            painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing, False)
            painter.setPen(QtCore.Qt.NoPen)
            painter.setBrush(t.shadow)
            painter.drawRect(rect.translated(SHADOW, SHADOW))
            painter.setBrush(t.root if n.get("emphasis") else t.node)
            if self.isSelected():
                pen = QtGui.QPen(t.select, 2)
            else:
                pen = QtGui.QPen(t.frame, 1)
            if n.get("dashed"):
                pen.setStyle(QtCore.Qt.DashLine)
            pen.setJoinStyle(QtCore.Qt.MiterJoin)
            painter.setPen(pen)
            painter.drawRect(rect)

            painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.TextAntialiasing, True)
            painter.setFont(f.code)
            limit = self.w - 2 * PAD_X
            y = PAD_Y
            for kind_, text, extra in self.rows:
                x = PAD_X
                base = y + f.fm.ascent()
                if kind_ == "code":
                    runs = insn_runs(t, text)
                elif kind_ == "comment":
                    runs = [(text, t.comment)]
                else:
                    runs = [(text, t.text)]
                    if extra:
                        runs.append(("  ; " + extra, t.comment))
                for tok, color in runs:
                    room = limit - (x - PAD_X)
                    if room <= 0:
                        break
                    w = f.fm.horizontalAdvance(tok)
                    if w > room:
                        tok = f.fm.elidedText(tok, QtCore.Qt.ElideRight, int(room))
                        w = room
                    painter.setPen(color)
                    painter.drawText(QtCore.QPointF(x, base), tok)
                    x += w
                y += f.line

        def mouseDoubleClickEvent(self, e):
            self.form.act(self.node, None)

        def contextMenuEvent(self, e):
            self.scene().clearSelection()
            self.setSelected(True)
            m = QtWidgets.QMenu()
            for label, action in self.node.get("menu", []):
                if not label:
                    m.addSeparator()
                else:
                    m.addAction(label, lambda a=action: self.form.act(self.node, a))
            if not m.isEmpty():
                m.exec(e.screenPos())

    class Edge(QtWidgets.QGraphicsItem):
        # Right-angled, as IDA routes edges. An edge to a node on its own row
        # or above goes round the right side.
        def __init__(self, form, a, b, edge, up, port):
            super().__init__()
            self.form = form
            self.edge = edge
            self.setZValue(-1)
            p0 = a.pos() + QtCore.QPointF(a.w / 2 + port, a.h)
            p1 = b.pos() + QtCore.QPointF(b.w / 2, 0)
            if p1.y() - p0.y() >= 2 * 8:
                mid = p1.y() - VGAP / 2
                pts = [p0, QtCore.QPointF(p0.x(), mid), QtCore.QPointF(p1.x(), mid), p1]
            else:
                side = max(a.pos().x() + a.w, b.pos().x() + b.w) + HGAP / 2
                pts = [p0, QtCore.QPointF(p0.x(), p0.y() + 12), QtCore.QPointF(side, p0.y() + 12),
                       QtCore.QPointF(side, p1.y() - 12), QtCore.QPointF(p1.x(), p1.y() - 12), p1]
            self.pts = pts
            self.poly = QtGui.QPolygonF(pts)
            # The arrowhead, where the flow arrives.
            self.tip = pts[0] if up else pts[-1]
            self.tip_dir = -1 if up else 1
            # Beside the line into the target, which no other edge shares.
            self.label = edge.get("label") or ""
            self.label_at = QtCore.QPointF(p1.x() + 5, (pts[-2].y() + p1.y()) / 2)

        def boundingRect(self):
            return self.poly.boundingRect().adjusted(-80, -14, 80, 14)

        def paint(self, painter, option, widget=None):
            t = self.form.theme
            f = self.form.fonts
            painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing, False)
            pen = QtGui.QPen(t.edge, 1)
            if self.edge.get("dashed"):
                pen.setStyle(QtCore.Qt.DashLine)
            painter.setPen(pen)
            painter.drawPolyline(self.poly)
            painter.setRenderHint(QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing, True)
            d = self.tip_dir
            tip = self.tip
            head = QtGui.QPolygonF([tip, tip + QtCore.QPointF(-4, -8 * d), tip + QtCore.QPointF(4, -8 * d)])
            painter.setPen(QtCore.Qt.NoPen)
            painter.setBrush(t.edge)
            painter.drawPolygon(head)
            if self.label:
                painter.setFont(f.code)
                painter.setPen(t.label)
                painter.drawText(QtCore.QPointF(self.label_at.x(), self.label_at.y() + f.fm.ascent() / 2 - 1),
                                 self.label)

    class View(QtWidgets.QGraphicsView):
        def __init__(self, form):
            super().__init__()
            self.form = form
            # Scoped enum names: IDA's PyQt5 shim warns on '|' and '&' over
            # the unscoped ones (QtGui.QPainter.Antialiasing).
            self.setRenderHints(QtGui.QPainter.RenderHint.Antialiasing
                                | QtGui.QPainter.RenderHint.TextAntialiasing)
            self.setDragMode(QtWidgets.QGraphicsView.ScrollHandDrag)
            self.setTransformationAnchor(QtWidgets.QGraphicsView.AnchorUnderMouse)
            self.setViewportUpdateMode(QtWidgets.QGraphicsView.SmartViewportUpdate)
            self.setFrameShape(QtWidgets.QFrame.NoFrame)

        def wheelEvent(self, e):
            if e.modifiers() & QtCore.Qt.KeyboardModifier.ControlModifier:
                self.zoom(1.15 if e.angleDelta().y() > 0 else 1 / 1.15)
                e.accept()
            else:
                super().wheelEvent(e)

        def zoom(self, k):
            s = self.transform().m11() * k
            if 0.1 <= s <= 3.0:
                self.scale(k, k)

        def keyPressEvent(self, e):
            k = e.key()
            if k in (QtCore.Qt.Key_F, QtCore.Qt.Key_Home):
                self.form.fit()
            elif k == QtCore.Qt.Key_0 and e.modifiers() & QtCore.Qt.KeyboardModifier.ControlModifier:
                self.resetTransform()
            elif k in (QtCore.Qt.Key_Plus, QtCore.Qt.Key_Equal):
                self.zoom(1.15)
            elif k == QtCore.Qt.Key_Minus:
                self.zoom(1 / 1.15)
            elif k in (QtCore.Qt.Key_Return, QtCore.Qt.Key_Enter):
                sel = [i for i in self.scene().selectedItems() if isinstance(i, Card)]
                if sel:
                    self.form.act(sel[0].node, None)
            else:
                super().keyPressEvent(e)

        def drawBackground(self, painter, rect):
            # IDA's graph background: a gradient down the visible area.
            t = getattr(self.form, "theme", None)
            if t is None:
                return super().drawBackground(painter, rect)
            vr = self.mapToScene(self.viewport().rect()).boundingRect()
            g = QtGui.QLinearGradient(vr.topLeft(), vr.bottomLeft())
            g.setColorAt(0, t.canvas_top)
            g.setColorAt(1, t.canvas_bottom)
            painter.fillRect(rect, g)

        def contextMenuEvent(self, e):
            if self.itemAt(e.pos()) is not None:
                return super().contextMenuEvent(e)
            m = QtWidgets.QMenu(self)
            m.addAction("Fit the graph (F)", self.form.fit)
            m.addAction("Actual size (Ctrl+0)", self.resetTransform)
            m.addSeparator()
            m.addAction("Copy as an image", self.form.copy_image)
            m.exec(e.globalPos())

    def layout(cards, edges):
        # A top-down tree: each node goes under the first node, breadth first
        # from the roots, with an edge to it; children in edge order. Other
        # edges are drawn but do not affect the layout.
        n = len(cards)
        kids = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        has_parent = [False] * n
        for e in edges:
            if 0 <= e["src"] < n and 0 <= e["dst"] < n:
                has_parent[e["dst"]] = True
        roots = [i for i in range(n) if not has_parent[i]] or ([0] if n else [])
        placed = [False] * n
        depth = [0] * n
        order = []
        queue = list(roots)
        for r in roots:
            placed[r] = True
        out = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for e in edges:
            if 0 <= e["src"] < n and 0 <= e["dst"] < n:
                out[e["src"]].append(e["dst"])
        while queue:
            v = queue.pop(0)
            order.append(v)
            for c in out[v]:
                if not placed[c]:
                    placed[c] = True
                    depth[c] = depth[v] + 1
                    kids[v].append(c)
                    queue.append(c)
        for i in range(n):
            if not placed[i]:
                roots.append(i)
                placed[i] = True

        rows = {}
        for i in range(n):
            rows[depth[i]] = max(rows.get(depth[i], 0), cards[i].h)
        tops = {}
        y = 0
        for d in sorted(rows):
            tops[d] = y
            y += rows[d] + VGAP

        width = [0] * n

        def measure(v):
            s = sum(measure(c) for c in kids[v]) + HGAP * max(len(kids[v]) - 1, 0)
            width[v] = max(cards[v].w, s)
            return width[v]

        def place(v, left):
            span = sum(width[c] for c in kids[v]) + HGAP * max(len(kids[v]) - 1, 0)
            x = left + (width[v] - span) / 2
            for c in kids[v]:
                place(c, x)
                x += width[c] + HGAP
            if kids[v]:
                a = cards[kids[v][0]]
                b = cards[kids[v][-1]]
                center = (a.pos().x() + a.w / 2 + b.pos().x() + b.w / 2) / 2
            else:
                center = left + width[v] / 2
            cards[v].setPos(center - cards[v].w / 2, tops[depth[v]])

        left = 0
        for r in roots:
            measure(r)
            place(r, left)
            left += width[r] + HGAP * 2

    class GraphForm(ida_kernwin.PluginForm):
        def __init__(self, graph):
            super().__init__()
            self.graph = graph

        def OnCreate(self, form):
            self.parent = self.FormToPyQtWidget(form)
            self.view = View(self)
            self.scene = QtWidgets.QGraphicsScene(self.view)
            self.view.setScene(self.scene)
            self.status = QtWidgets.QLabel()
            self.status.setWordWrap(True)
            self.status.setTextInteractionFlags(QtCore.Qt.TextSelectableByMouse)
            box = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout()
            box.setContentsMargins(0, 0, 0, 0)
            box.setSpacing(0)
            self.status.setContentsMargins(8, 4, 8, 4)
            box.addWidget(self.view)
            box.addWidget(self.status)
            self.parent.setLayout(box)
            self.load(self.graph, True)

        def load(self, graph, first=False):
            self.graph = graph
            self.theme = Theme(self.view)
            self.fonts = Fonts(self.view)
            self.scene.clear()
            cards = []
            for node in graph["nodes"]:
                c = Card(self, node)
                self.scene.addItem(c)
                cards.append(c)
            layout(cards, graph["edges"])
            up = bool(graph.get("arrows_up"))
            # Edges leaving a card spread across its bottom, ordered by the
            # cards they reach, rather than all leaving from one point.
            leaving = {}
            for e in graph["edges"]:
                if 0 <= e["src"] < len(cards) and 0 <= e["dst"] < len(cards):
                    leaving.setdefault(e["src"], []).append(e)
            for src, out in leaving.items():
                a = cards[src]
                out.sort(key=lambda e: cards[e["dst"]].pos().x())
                spread = min(a.w * 0.5, 24 * (len(out) - 1))
                for k, e in enumerate(out):
                    port = 0 if len(out) == 1 else -spread / 2 + spread * k / (len(out) - 1)
                    self.scene.addItem(Edge(self, a, cards[e["dst"]], e, up, port))
            r = self.scene.itemsBoundingRect().adjusted(-40, -40, 40, 40)
            self.scene.setSceneRect(r)
            self.status.setText(graph.get("status") or "")
            if first:
                QtCore.QTimer.singleShot(0, self.fit_or_actual)

        def fit_or_actual(self):
            # Actual size when it fits, else the whole graph; either way,
            # scrolled to the top, where it starts.
            r = self.scene.sceneRect()
            vp = self.view.viewport().rect()
            self.view.resetTransform()
            if r.width() > vp.width() or r.height() > vp.height():
                k = min(vp.width() / r.width(), vp.height() / r.height())
                k = max(k, 0.45)
                self.view.scale(k, k)
            self.view.centerOn(r.center().x(), r.top() + self.view.viewport().height() / 2 / self.view.transform().m11())

        def fit(self):
            self.view.fitInView(self.scene.sceneRect(), QtCore.Qt.KeepAspectRatio)
            if self.view.transform().m11() > 1.0:
                self.view.resetTransform()

        def copy_image(self):
            r = self.scene.sceneRect()
            img = QtGui.QImage(int(r.width()), int(r.height()), QtGui.QImage.Format_ARGB32)
            img.fill(self.theme.canvas)
            p = QtGui.QPainter(img)
            self.scene.render(p, QtCore.QRectF(img.rect()), r)
            p.end()
            QtWidgets.QApplication.clipboard().setImage(img)

        def act(self, node, action):
            if action is None:
                menu = [a for l, a in node.get("menu", []) if l]
                if not menu:
                    return
                action = menu[0]
            # Deferred out of this item's own event: the action may redraw
            # the graph, which deletes the item.
            def run():
                r = ttd("ui.graphact %s %x %s" % (kind, node["id"], action))
                if not r.get("ok"):
                    ida_kernwin.warning(r.get("error", "That did not work."))
            QtCore.QTimer.singleShot(0, run)

        def OnClose(self, form):
            if forms.get(kind) is self:
                forms.pop(kind, None)

    graph = fetch()
    form = forms.get(kind)
    if form is not None and ida_kernwin.find_widget(graph["title"]) is not None:
        # Skipped if the window closed meanwhile, deleting what load() draws on.
        QtCore.QTimer.singleShot(0, lambda: form.load(graph) if forms.get(kind) is form else None)
        if first:
            ida_kernwin.activate_widget(ida_kernwin.find_widget(graph["title"]), True)
        return
    form = GraphForm(graph)
    forms[kind] = form
    form.Show(graph["title"], options=ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_DP_TAB | ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_RESTORE)

```

`scripts/ida_ttd_heatmap.py`:

```py
"""The memory heatmap window, drawn with PySide6.

One row per page the recording touched, in address order; one column per
slice of time. A cell's color is the page's access count in that slice, on a
log scale; in "All", writes are red, reads green and executes blue, so a mix
blends. The plugin counts (ttd("ui.heat")); a double-click travels to the
slice and shows the page in the hex view (ttd("ui.showbytes POS EA")).

Drag across the columns, or type a start and end position, to zoom. Each
zoom recounts that span alone (ttd("ui.heatzoom FROM TO")), so it keeps the
full number of slices; Back and Whole recording zoom out. A vertical line
marks the debugger's slice (ttd("ui.heatnow"), polled by a QTimer on the UI
thread, never from another thread).

The plugin calls show() through ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module("ida_ttd_heatmap").
"""
import json
import math
import re
import ida_kernwin
import idc
from PySide6 import QtCore, QtGui, QtWidgets


def ttd(cmd):
    # cmd becomes an IDC string literal: escape what would end it early.
    cmd = cmd.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
    return json.loads(idc.eval_idc('ttd("%s")' % cmd))


# The open windows' forms, by kind or title. Kept across importlib.reload
# (ida_ttd_qt.fresh_module), which runs this file again in the same
# namespace: a window opened before a reinstall is still found and reused.
try:
    _forms
except NameError:
    _forms = {}


def show():
    """Open the heatmap of the counts the plugin holds, replacing an open one."""

    # What a typed span end may look like: Microsoft's Sequence:Steps in hex,
    # Sogen's decimal instruction number, or "end". The backend parses it
    # properly; this only keeps spaces and other words out of the command.
    POSITION_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9A-Fa-f]+(?::[0-9A-Fa-f]+)?|end")

    data = ttd("ui.heat")
    if not data.get("ok"):
        raise RuntimeError(data.get("error", "no heatmap"))

    # The counts shown. A zoom replaces them whole, so everything reads them
    # from here instead of keeping a copy.
    H = {}

    def load(heat):
        H["shift"] = heat["page_shift"]
        H["slices"] = heat["slices"]
        H["starts"] = heat["starts"]
        H["end"] = heat.get("end", "")
        H["whole"] = heat.get("whole", True)
        H["can_zoom"] = heat.get("can_zoom", False)
        H["pages"] = heat["pages"]

    load(data["heat"])

    def slice_end(s):
        # Where slice s ends: the next one's start, or the span's end.
        return H["starts"][s + 1] if s + 1 < H["slices"] else H["end"]

    MODES = ["All (writes red, reads green, executes blue)", "Reads", "Writes", "Executes"]
    ROW = 6
    GUTTER = 250

    def ramp(t):
        # Dark violet -> red -> orange -> pale yellow, for one kind of access.
        stops = [(0.0, (40, 10, 70)), (0.35, (170, 30, 80)), (0.7, (245, 130, 30)), (1.0, (255, 245, 170))]
        for (a, ca), (b, cb) in zip(stops, stops[1:]):
            if t <= b:
                f = (t - a) / (b - a) if b > a else 0.0
                return tuple(int(ca[i] + (cb[i] - ca[i]) * f) for i in range(3))
        return stops[-1][1]

    class Canvas(QtWidgets.QWidget):
        def __init__(self, owner):
            super().__init__()
            self.owner = owner
            self.mode = 0
            self.rows = H["pages"]
            self.runs = []
            self.image = None
            # [first slice, last slice] while a span is being dragged out.
            self.drag = None
            # The slice the current position is in, or -1.
            self.now = -1
            self.setMouseTracking(True)

        def set_rows(self, rows, mode):
            self.rows = rows
            self.mode = mode
            self.image = None
            # Runs of neighbouring pages of one module: [first row, end row).
            self.runs = []
            for y, r in enumerate(rows):
                if (y == 0 or r["page"] != rows[y - 1]["page"] + 1
                        or r["label"] != rows[y - 1]["label"]):
                    self.runs.append([y, y + 1])
                else:
                    self.runs[-1][1] = y + 1
            self.setMinimumHeight(max(len(rows) * ROW, 50))
            self.updateGeometry()
            self.update()

        def build_image(self):
            n = max(len(self.rows), 1)
            img = QtGui.QImage(H["slices"], n, QtGui.QImage.Format_RGB32)
            img.fill(self.palette().color(QtGui.QPalette.Base))
            mx = [1, 1, 1]
            for r in self.rows:
                for c in r["cells"]:
                    for k in range(3):
                        if c[1 + k] > mx[k]:
                            mx[k] = c[1 + k]
            lm = [math.log1p(m) for m in mx]
            for y, r in enumerate(self.rows):
                for s, rd, wr, ex in r["cells"]:
                    if self.mode == 0:
                        g = rd and int(60 + 195 * math.log1p(rd) / lm[0])
                        red = wr and int(60 + 195 * math.log1p(wr) / lm[1])
                        b = ex and int(60 + 195 * math.log1p(ex) / lm[2])
                        col = QtGui.QColor(red, g, b)
                    else:
                        v = (rd, wr, ex)[self.mode - 1]
                        if not v:
                            continue
                        col = QtGui.QColor(*ramp(math.log1p(v) / lm[self.mode - 1]))
                    img.setPixelColor(s, y, col)
            self.image = img

        def slice_at(self, x):
            w = max(self.width() - GUTTER, 1)
            s = int((x - GUTTER) * H["slices"] // w)
            return min(max(s, 0), H["slices"] - 1)

        def cell_at(self, pos):
            y = int(pos.y() // ROW)
            if y < 0 or y >= len(self.rows) or pos.x() < GUTTER:
                return None, None
            return y, self.slice_at(pos.x())

        def paintEvent(self, ev):
            p = QtGui.QPainter(self)
            if self.image is None:
                self.build_image()
            w = max(self.width() - GUTTER, 1)
            # Only the rows in view: the image can be thousands of rows tall.
            top = max(int(ev.rect().top() // ROW), 0)
            bottom = min(int(ev.rect().bottom() // ROW) + 1, len(self.rows))
            if bottom > top:
                src = QtCore.QRect(0, top, H["slices"], bottom - top)
                dst = QtCore.QRect(GUTTER, top * ROW, w, (bottom - top) * ROW)
                p.drawImage(dst, self.image, src)
            # A rule above each run of neighbouring pages, labeled inside when
            # the run is tall enough (a label never crosses the next rule);
            # shorter runs are named by the tooltip.
            fg = self.palette().color(QtGui.QPalette.Text)
            rule = self.palette().color(QtGui.QPalette.Mid)
            font = p.font()
            font.setPointSizeF(max(font.pointSizeF() - 1.5, 6.0))
            p.setFont(font)
            text_h = QtGui.QFontMetrics(font).height()
            for first, end in self.runs:
                if end <= top or first >= bottom:
                    continue
                y0 = first * ROW
                h = (end - first) * ROW
                if first > 0:
                    p.setPen(rule)
                    p.drawLine(0, y0, self.width(), y0)
                if h >= text_h + 2:
                    r = self.rows[first]
                    p.setPen(fg)
                    p.drawText(QtCore.QRect(4, y0 + 1, GUTTER - 8, h - 1),
                               QtCore.Qt.AlignLeft | QtCore.Qt.AlignTop | QtCore.Qt.TextSingleLine,
                               "0x%X  %s" % (r["page"] << H["shift"], r["label"]))
            # The debugger's slice: a line down its middle, dark-edged to show
            # on any cell color.
            if 0 <= self.now < H["slices"]:
                x = GUTTER + (2 * self.now + 1) * w // (2 * H["slices"])
                y0, y1 = ev.rect().top(), ev.rect().bottom()
                p.setPen(QtGui.QPen(QtGui.QColor(0, 0, 0), 3))
                p.drawLine(x, y0, x, y1)
                p.setPen(QtGui.QPen(QtGui.QColor(255, 255, 255), 1))
                p.drawLine(x, y0, x, y1)
            # The span being dragged out, over every row in view.
            if self.drag is not None:
                a, b = sorted(self.drag)
                x0 = GUTTER + a * w // H["slices"]
                x1 = GUTTER + (b + 1) * w // H["slices"]
                hl = QtGui.QColor(self.palette().color(QtGui.QPalette.Highlight))
                hl.setAlpha(70)
                p.fillRect(QtCore.QRect(x0, ev.rect().top(), max(x1 - x0, 1), ev.rect().height()), hl)
            p.end()

        def resizeEvent(self, ev):
            self.update()

        def mousePressEvent(self, ev):
            if (ev.button() == QtCore.Qt.LeftButton and H["can_zoom"]
                    and ev.position().x() >= GUTTER):
                s = self.slice_at(ev.position().x())
                self.drag = [s, s]

        def mouseReleaseEvent(self, ev):
            if self.drag is None:
                return
            a, b = sorted(self.drag)
            self.drag = None
            self.update()
            # A click is not a span: a double-click's press and release also
            # land here before it travels.
            if b > a:
                self.owner.zoom(H["starts"][a], slice_end(b))

        def mouseMoveEvent(self, ev):
            if self.drag is not None:
                s = self.slice_at(ev.position().x())
                if s != self.drag[1]:
                    self.drag[1] = s
                    self.update()
                a, b = sorted(self.drag)
                QtWidgets.QToolTip.showText(ev.globalPosition().toPoint(),
                                            "Zoom to %s .. %s" % (H["starts"][a], slice_end(b)), self)
                return
            y, s = self.cell_at(ev.position())
            if y is None:
                QtWidgets.QToolTip.hideText()
                return
            r = self.rows[y]
            counts = [0, 0, 0]
            for c in r["cells"]:
                if c[0] == s:
                    counts = c[1:]
                    break
            tip = "0x%X%s\nslice %d of %d, %s .. %s\n%d reads, %d writes, %d executes\nDouble-click: go there%s" % (
                r["page"] << H["shift"], ("  (" + r["label"] + ")") if r["label"] else "",
                s + 1, H["slices"], H["starts"][s], slice_end(s), counts[0], counts[1], counts[2],
                "\nDrag across the columns: zoom in" if H["can_zoom"] else "")
            QtWidgets.QToolTip.showText(ev.globalPosition().toPoint(), tip, self)

        def mouseDoubleClickEvent(self, ev):
            self.drag = None
            y, s = self.cell_at(ev.position())
            if y is None:
                return
            r = self.rows[y]
            # The first slice from here on that touched the page, else this one.
            target = s
            for c in r["cells"]:
                if c[0] >= s:
                    target = c[0]
                    break
            if H["starts"][target]:
                ttd("ui.showbytes %s %X" % (H["starts"][target], r["page"] << H["shift"]))

    class HeatmapForm(ida_kernwin.PluginForm):
        def OnCreate(self, form):
            self.parent = self.FormToPyQtWidget(form)
            # Spans zoomed out of, most recent last, for Back.
            self.history = []
            self.mode = QtWidgets.QComboBox()
            self.mode.addItems(MODES)
            self.mode.currentIndexChanged.connect(self.refresh)
            self.filter = QtWidgets.QLineEdit()
            self.filter.setPlaceholderText("Filter by module or address")
            self.filter.setClearButtonEnabled(True)
            self.filter.textChanged.connect(self.refresh)
            self.status = QtWidgets.QLabel()
            bar = QtWidgets.QHBoxLayout()
            bar.addWidget(self.mode)
            bar.addWidget(self.filter, 1)
            bar.addWidget(self.status)

            # The span: typed, or dragged out on the columns.
            self.span_from = QtWidgets.QLineEdit()
            self.span_to = QtWidgets.QLineEdit()
            for e in (self.span_from, self.span_to):
                e.setPlaceholderText("position")
                e.returnPressed.connect(self.apply_span)
            self.apply_btn = QtWidgets.QPushButton("Zoom")
            self.apply_btn.clicked.connect(self.apply_span)
            self.back_btn = QtWidgets.QPushButton("Back")
            self.back_btn.clicked.connect(self.back)
            self.whole_btn = QtWidgets.QPushButton("Whole recording")
            self.whole_btn.clicked.connect(self.whole)
            span = QtWidgets.QHBoxLayout()
            span.addWidget(QtWidgets.QLabel("Span"))
            span.addWidget(self.span_from, 1)
            span.addWidget(QtWidgets.QLabel("to"))
            span.addWidget(self.span_to, 1)
            span.addWidget(self.apply_btn)
            span.addWidget(self.back_btn)
            span.addWidget(self.whole_btn)

            self.canvas = Canvas(self)
            scroll = QtWidgets.QScrollArea()
            scroll.setWidgetResizable(True)
            scroll.setWidget(self.canvas)
            layout = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout()
            layout.setContentsMargins(2, 2, 2, 2)
            layout.addLayout(bar)
            layout.addLayout(span)
            layout.addWidget(scroll, 1)
            self.parent.setLayout(layout)
            self.show_span()
            self.refresh()
            self.timer = QtCore.QTimer(self.parent)
            self.timer.timeout.connect(self.poll_now)
            self.timer.start(500)
            self.poll_now()

        def poll_now(self):
            try:
                r = ttd("ui.heatnow")
            except Exception:
                return
            if not r.get("ok") or r.get("busy"):
                return              # moving, or no session: keep the last mark
            s = r.get("slice", -1)
            if s != self.canvas.now:
                self.canvas.now = s
                self.canvas.update()

        def show_span(self):
            self.span_from.setText(H["starts"][0] if H["starts"] else "")
            self.span_to.setText(H["end"])
            zoomable = H["can_zoom"]
            for w in (self.span_from, self.span_to, self.apply_btn):
                w.setEnabled(zoomable)
                w.setToolTip("" if zoomable else
                             "This recording's backend can only count the whole recording.")
            self.back_btn.setEnabled(zoomable and bool(self.history))
            self.whole_btn.setEnabled(zoomable and not H["whole"])

        def recount(self, cmd):
            # A fresh count, behind the plugin's wait box. On failure the
            # counts shown are kept.
            r = ttd(cmd)
            if not r.get("ok"):
                ida_kernwin.warning("The heatmap could not be counted over that span: %s"
                                    % r.get("error", "unknown error"))
                return False
            load(r["heat"])
            self.show_span()
            self.refresh()
            self.poll_now()
            return True

        def zoom(self, first, last):
            if not first or not last:
                return
            here = (H["starts"][0], H["end"], H["whole"])
            if self.recount("ui.heatzoom %s %s" % (first, last)):
                self.history.append(here)
                self.show_span()

        def apply_span(self):
            first = self.span_from.text().strip()
            last = self.span_to.text().strip()
            if not first or not last:
                return
            for text in (first, last):
                if not POSITION_RE.fullmatch(text):
                    ida_kernwin.warning("'%s' is not a position." % text)
                    return
            self.zoom(first, last)

        def back(self):
            if not self.history:
                return
            first, last, whole = self.history.pop()
            if not self.recount("ui.heatzoom" if whole else "ui.heatzoom %s %s" % (first, last)):
                self.history.append((first, last, whole))
            self.show_span()

        def whole(self):
            here = (H["starts"][0], H["end"], H["whole"])
            if self.recount("ui.heatzoom"):
                self.history.append(here)
                self.show_span()

        def refresh(self, *args):
            text = self.filter.text().strip().lower()
            mode = self.mode.currentIndex()
            pages = H["pages"]
            rows = pages
            if text:
                rows = [r for r in pages if text in r["label"].lower() or text in ("%x" % (r["page"] << H["shift"]))]
            if mode != 0:
                rows = [r for r in rows if any(c[mode] for c in r["cells"])]
            self.canvas.set_rows(rows, mode)
            self.status.setText("%d of %d pages, %d slices of %s" % (
                len(rows), len(pages), H["slices"], "the recording" if H["whole"] else "this span"))

        def OnClose(self, form):
            self.timer.stop()
            _forms.pop(title, None)

    title = "TTD memory heatmap"
    old = ida_kernwin.find_widget(title)
    if old is not None:
        ida_kernwin.close_widget(old, 0)
    form = HeatmapForm()
    _forms[title] = form
    form.Show(title, options=ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_DP_TAB | ida_kernwin.PluginForm.WOPN_RESTORE)
```
