`scripts/ida_ttd_qt.py`:

```py
"""Qt touches the plugin cannot make from C++.

IDA's SDK has no call for a toolbar button's width or a submenu's icon, and
reaching IDA's Qt from C++ means building against its exact Qt version. The
plugin calls these through IDAPython's PySide instead. Each is a no-op
without Qt (an idalib worker).
"""

try:
    from PySide6 import QtGui, QtWidgets
    import shiboken6
except ImportError:
    QtWidgets = None

_pos_button = None


def _widgets():
    app = QtWidgets.QApplication.instance() if QtWidgets is not None else None
    return app.allWidgets() if app is not None else []


def pin_position_width(tooltip, sample):
    """Give the toolbar's position button a fixed minimum width, wide enough
    for 'sample' (the recording's last position) with every digit as wide as
    the widest, so the toolbar does not shift as the position changes. The
    button is found by its tooltip once, then kept."""
    global _pos_button
    if QtWidgets is None:
        return
    b = _pos_button
    if b is None or not shiboken6.isValid(b):
        b = None
        for w in _widgets():
            a = w.defaultAction() if isinstance(w, QtWidgets.QToolButton) else None
            if a is not None and a.toolTip() == tooltip:
                b = w
                break
        _pos_button = b
        if b is None:
            return
    fm = b.fontMetrics()
    digit = max(fm.horizontalAdvance(c) for c in "0123456789ABCDEF")
    want = fm.horizontalAdvance("Position ") + 16 + sum(
        digit if c.isalnum() else fm.horizontalAdvance(c) for c in sample)
    if b.minimumWidth() != want:
        b.setMinimumWidth(want)


def set_submenu_icon(menu, label, svg):
    """Set the icon of submenu 'label' of menu 'menu' (create_menu takes none)."""
    if QtWidgets is None:
        return
    pix = QtGui.QPixmap()
    pix.loadFromData(svg.encode(), "SVG")
    for m in _widgets():
        if not isinstance(m, QtWidgets.QMenu) or not shiboken6.isValid(m) \
                or m.title().replace("&", "") != menu:
            continue
        for a in m.actions():
            sub = a.menu()
            if sub is not None and shiboken6.isValid(sub) and a.text().replace("&", "") == label:
                a.setIcon(QtGui.QIcon(pix))


def chooser_current_column(title):
    """The column of the current cell in the chooser titled 'title', -1 when
    unknown. A double-click makes the clicked cell current before IDA calls
    the chooser's enter(), which is told the row only."""
    if QtWidgets is None:
        return -1
    import ida_kernwin
    tw = ida_kernwin.find_widget(title)
    if tw is None:
        return -1
    w = ida_kernwin.PluginForm.TWidgetToPySideWidget(tw)
    if w is None:
        return -1
    for v in w.findChildren(QtWidgets.QAbstractItemView):
        if shiboken6.isValid(v) and v.currentIndex().isValid():
            return v.currentIndex().column()
    return -1


def theme_is_dark():
    """1 when IDA's theme is dark (Qt's palette), 0 when light or unknown."""
    app = QtWidgets.QApplication.instance() if QtWidgets is not None else None
    return int(app is not None and app.palette().base().color().lightness() < 128)


def fresh_module(name):
    """The module 'name' (one of the windows: ida_ttd_graph, ida_ttd_heatmap,
    ida_ttd_calltree), imported, and reloaded when its file changed since:
    a reinstall while IDA runs then shows the installed window code, as
    when the plugin ran it from a string on every call, without compiling
    it again on every show and refresh. The modules keep their open windows
    across a reload."""
    import importlib
    import os
    import sys

    def stamp(m):
        try:
            st = os.stat(m.__file__)
            return (st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size)
        except (OSError, TypeError, AttributeError):
            return None

    mod = sys.modules.get(name)
    if mod is None:
        mod = importlib.import_module(name)
    elif stamp(mod) != getattr(mod, "_ida_ttd_stamp", None):
        mod = importlib.reload(mod)
    mod._ida_ttd_stamp = stamp(mod)
    return mod


# The window a recording runs behind (run_query in query_runner.cpp): what
# is running, for how long, Sogen's log as it comes, and Pause and Stop.
# IDA's wait box shows a few lines of text and offers only Cancel, which for
# a recording means "stop and keep what ran". The plugin drives the window
# from its wait loop: recording_window_update() ten times a second, which
# also runs Qt's events, since the plugin's loop is all that runs while the
# recording does.
_rec = None


def _main_window():
    app = QtWidgets.QApplication.instance()
    for w in app.topLevelWidgets() if app is not None else []:
        if isinstance(w, QtWidgets.QMainWindow):
            return w
    return None


def recording_window_open(title, what, can_pause):
    """Show the window. 1 when it is up, 0 without Qt."""
    global _rec
    if QtWidgets is None or QtWidgets.QApplication.instance() is None:
        return 0
    from PySide6 import QtCore
    recording_window_close()

    class RecordingWindow(QtWidgets.QDialog):
        def __init__(self):
            super().__init__(_main_window())
            self.request = ""
            self.paused = False
            self.stopping = False
            self.setWindowTitle(title)
            self.setWindowModality(QtCore.Qt.ApplicationModal)
            self.setWindowFlag(QtCore.Qt.WindowContextHelpButtonHint, False)
            lay = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout(self)
            self.what = QtWidgets.QLabel(what)
            self.status = QtWidgets.QLabel("Starting...")
            lay.addWidget(self.what)
            lay.addWidget(self.status)
            lay.addWidget(QtWidgets.QLabel("Sogen's log"))
            self.log = QtWidgets.QPlainTextEdit()
            self.log.setReadOnly(True)
            self.log.setLineWrapMode(QtWidgets.QPlainTextEdit.NoWrap)
            self.log.setMaximumBlockCount(20000)
            self.log.setFont(QtGui.QFontDatabase.systemFont(QtGui.QFontDatabase.FixedFont))
            self.log.setPlaceholderText("Nothing logged yet.")
            lay.addWidget(self.log, 1)
            row = QtWidgets.QHBoxLayout()
            row.addStretch(1)
            self.pause = None
            if can_pause:
                self.pause = QtWidgets.QPushButton("&Pause")
                self.pause.setToolTip("Hold the program where it is; Resume carries on")
                self.pause.clicked.connect(self._pause)
                row.addWidget(self.pause)
            self.stop = QtWidgets.QPushButton("&Stop recording")
            self.stop.setToolTip("End the recording here and keep what ran")
            self.stop.clicked.connect(self._stop)
            row.addWidget(self.stop)
            lay.addLayout(row)
            self.resize(780, 380)

        def _pause(self):
            if self.stopping:
                return
            self.paused = not self.paused
            self.request = "pause" if self.paused else "resume"
            self.pause.setText("&Resume" if self.paused else "&Pause")

        def _stop(self):
            if self.stopping:
                return
            self.stopping = True
            self.request = "stop"
            self.stop.setEnabled(False)
            if self.pause is not None:
                self.pause.setEnabled(False)

        # Escape and the close box stop the recording, as Cancel did; the
        # window itself goes only when the plugin closes it.
        def reject(self):
            self._stop()

        def closeEvent(self, e):
            e.ignore()
            self._stop()

    _rec = RecordingWindow()
    _rec.show()
    QtWidgets.QApplication.processEvents()
    return 1


def recording_window_update(status, lines):
    """Show 'status', append 'lines' (newline-separated, may be empty) to the
    log, run Qt's events, and return what was asked since the last call:
    "stop", "pause", "resume", "" for nothing, or "gone" when the window is
    not there."""
    w = _rec
    if w is None or not shiboken6.isValid(w):
        return "gone"
    if status and w.status.text() != status:
        w.status.setText(status)
    if lines:
        bar = w.log.verticalScrollBar()
        follow = bar.value() >= bar.maximum() - 2
        w.log.appendPlainText(lines)
        if follow:
            bar.setValue(bar.maximum())
    QtWidgets.QApplication.processEvents()
    r, w.request = w.request, ""
    return r


def recording_window_close():
    global _rec
    w, _rec = _rec, None
    if w is not None and shiboken6.isValid(w):
        w.hide()
        w.deleteLater()
```

`scripts/ida_ttd_runtime.py`:

```py
"""Install the TTD replay runtime that Microsoft recordings need.

The Microsoft TTD backend replays a .run through TTDReplay.dll and
TTDReplayCPU.dll. Only Microsoft may distribute them, so ida-ttd cannot ship
them. They come with WinDbg, whose terms allow any use, commercial included
(the standalone TTD package's terms do not, so it is not used). This module
does what installing WinDbg by hand would: download WinDbg from Microsoft,
show Microsoft's license, and only after the user accepts it unpack the x64
package into

    $IDAUSR/ida-ttd/windbg/

where the backend looks for amd64/ttd/TTDReplay.dll. That folder is outside
the plugin's package folder, so upgrades leave it alone. (Earlier versions
used $IDAUSR/plugins/ida-ttd-backends/windbg/; the backend still looks there,
and install_runtime() moves it.) With WinDbg already installed (Microsoft
Store, winget, Microsoft's installer), nothing is downloaded: its amd64/ttd
folder is copied instead, since Windows will not load DLLs from an installed
package's folder into IDA.

WinDbg is published as one bundle (about 1.2 GB) with an uncompressed package
per architecture. Only the x64 package (about 400 MB) is downloaded, through
HTTP range requests: the bundle's zip directory, then the license inside the
x64 package, then that package.

In IDA: TTD > Backends > Install the TTD runtime (WinDbg)..., or
install_runtime(). The functions it calls to find, download, unpack and copy
WinDbg use no IDA module, so they can be tested outside IDA.

The same menu installs another build of the Sogen backend: install_sogen(),
at the end of this module.
"""

import ctypes
import datetime
import io
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import threading
import time
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
import zipfile

APPINSTALLER_URL = "https://aka.ms/windbg/download"
X64_PACKAGE = "windbg_win-x64.msix"
WINDBG_FAMILY = "Microsoft.WinDbg_8wekyb3d8bbwe"
RUNTIME_FILES = ("TTDReplay.dll", "TTDReplayCPU.dll")
TTD_SUBDIR = os.path.join("amd64", "ttd")
MARKER = "ida-ttd-install.json"


class InstallError(RuntimeError):
    """A step of the install failed; the message says which, for the user."""


class Cancelled(Exception):
    pass


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Where a runtime already is

def has_runtime(root):
    """Whether 'root' is a WinDbg folder holding the replay runtime."""
    ttd = os.path.join(root, TTD_SUBDIR)
    return all(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(ttd, f)) for f in RUNTIME_FILES)


def installed_windbg():
    """(folder, version) of WinDbg installed as a Windows package for this
    user, if it holds the runtime, else None. Windows refuses to load a DLL
    from a package folder into a process outside the package (reading is
    allowed), so the runtime is copied out."""
    try:
        k32 = ctypes.WinDLL("kernel32")
        count = ctypes.c_uint32(0)
        buflen = ctypes.c_uint32(0)
        # The first call only sizes the buffers (ERROR_INSUFFICIENT_BUFFER).
        rc = k32.GetPackagesByPackageFamily(WINDBG_FAMILY, ctypes.byref(count), None,
                                            ctypes.byref(buflen), None)
        if rc not in (0, 122) or count.value == 0:
            return None
        names = (ctypes.c_wchar_p * count.value)()
        buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(buflen.value)
        if k32.GetPackagesByPackageFamily(WINDBG_FAMILY, ctypes.byref(count), names,
                                          ctypes.byref(buflen), buf) != 0:
            return None
        for name in names[:count.value]:
            plen = ctypes.c_uint32(0)
            k32.GetPackagePathByFullName(name, ctypes.byref(plen), None)
            path = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(plen.value or 1)
            if k32.GetPackagePathByFullName(name, ctypes.byref(plen), path) == 0 \
               and has_runtime(path.value):
                # A full name is Name_Version_Architecture_ResourceId_PublisherId.
                parts = name.split("_")
                return path.value, parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else "?"
    except (OSError, AttributeError):
        pass
    return None


def read_marker(target):
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(target, MARKER), encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reading Microsoft's package over HTTP

def _check_microsoft(url):
    """Refuse anything but Microsoft over HTTPS, checked after redirects."""
    u = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url)
    host = (u.hostname or "").lower()
    if u.scheme != "https" or not (host == "microsoft.com" or host.endswith(".microsoft.com")):
        raise InstallError("refusing to download from %s: not a Microsoft HTTPS address" % url)


def _open(url, headers=None, timeout=60):
    r = urllib.request.urlopen(urllib.request.Request(url, headers=headers or {}), timeout=timeout)
    _check_microsoft(r.geturl())
    return r


def resolve_latest():
    """(version, bundle URL) of the current WinDbg, from the App Installer
    file Microsoft's download link points to."""
    with _open(APPINSTALLER_URL) as r:
        root = ET.fromstring(r.read(1 << 20))
    for el in root.iter():
        if el.tag.rsplit("}", 1)[-1] == "MainBundle":
            url, version = el.get("Uri"), el.get("Version")
            if url and version:
                _check_microsoft(url)
                return version, url
    raise InstallError("Microsoft's WinDbg download page did not name a package")


class _HttpFile(io.RawIOBase):
    """A remote file read through range requests, enough for zipfile."""

    def __init__(self, url, base=0, size=None):
        self.url, self.base, self.pos = url, base, 0
        if size is None:
            req = urllib.request.Request(url, method="HEAD")
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
                _check_microsoft(r.geturl())
                self.url = r.geturl()
                size = int(r.headers["Content-Length"])
        self.size = size

    def readable(self):
        return True

    def seekable(self):
        return True

    def tell(self):
        return self.pos

    def seek(self, off, whence=0):
        self.pos = {0: off, 1: self.pos + off, 2: self.size + off}[whence]
        return self.pos

    def readinto(self, b):
        n = min(len(b), self.size - self.pos)
        if n <= 0:
            return 0
        start = self.base + self.pos
        with _open(self.url, {"Range": "bytes=%d-%d" % (start, start + n - 1)}) as r:
            if r.status != 206:
                raise InstallError("Microsoft's server does not allow partial downloads")
            data = r.read(n)
        b[:len(data)] = data
        self.pos += len(data)
        return len(data)


def _member_offset(f, info):
    """Where a zip member's data starts: after its local header."""
    f.seek(info.header_offset)
    h = f.read(30)
    if h[:4] != b"PK\x03\x04":
        raise InstallError("the WinDbg package is not laid out as expected")
    return info.header_offset + 30 + int.from_bytes(h[26:28], "little") \
        + int.from_bytes(h[28:30], "little")


class Release(object):
    """One WinDbg release: its version, its license, and where in the bundle
    the x64 package is."""

    def __init__(self, version, url):
        self.version, self.url = version, url
        raw = _HttpFile(url)
        self.url = raw.url
        f = io.BufferedReader(raw, buffer_size=1 << 16)
        try:
            info = zipfile.ZipFile(f).getinfo(X64_PACKAGE)
        except (KeyError, zipfile.BadZipFile):
            raise InstallError("the WinDbg bundle has no %s" % X64_PACKAGE)
        if info.compress_type != zipfile.ZIP_STORED:
            raise InstallError("the WinDbg bundle stores its x64 package compressed")
        self.offset = _member_offset(f, info)
        self.size = info.file_size
        self.crc = info.CRC

    def license_text(self):
        inner = io.BufferedReader(_HttpFile(self.url, self.offset, self.size), buffer_size=1 << 16)
        try:
            rtf = zipfile.ZipFile(inner).read("eula.rtf")
        except (KeyError, zipfile.BadZipFile):
            raise InstallError("the WinDbg package has no license file (eula.rtf)")
        return rtf_to_text(rtf)


def latest_release():
    return Release(*resolve_latest())


def download(release, dest, progress=None, chunk=1 << 20):
    """Download the x64 package to 'dest'. progress(done, total) is called
    as it goes; Cancelled is raised once 'progress' returns False."""
    done = 0
    crc = 0
    end = release.offset + release.size - 1
    with _open(release.url, {"Range": "bytes=%d-%d" % (release.offset, end)}, timeout=120) as r, \
         open(dest, "wb") as out:
        if r.status != 206:
            raise InstallError("Microsoft's server does not allow partial downloads")
        while done < release.size:
            data = r.read(min(chunk, release.size - done))
            if not data:
                raise InstallError("the download stopped after %d of %d bytes" % (done, release.size))
            out.write(data)
            crc = zipfile.crc32(data, crc)
            done += len(data)
            if progress is not None and progress(done, release.size) is False:
                raise Cancelled()
    # The bundle's directory holds the package's CRC; a mismatch is a broken
    # download.
    if crc != release.crc:
        raise InstallError("the download is damaged (checksum mismatch); try again")


# Package metadata, not WinDbg's files.
_PACKAGE_META = ("[Content_Types].xml",)


def _kept(name):
    """Whether a package member (its unquoted, '/'-separated name) is
    unpacked: anything under amd64/ttd, and the license beside it."""
    ttd = TTD_SUBDIR.replace(os.sep, "/").lower() + "/"
    n = name.replace("\\", "/").lower()
    return n.startswith(ttd) or n == "eula.rtf"


def unpack(package, target, version, progress=None):
    """Unpack a downloaded package into 'target', replacing what is there.
    It is unpacked beside it and renamed into place, so a failure leaves the
    old install (or none), never half of one."""
    staging = target + ".new"
    shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
    os.makedirs(staging)
    root = os.path.realpath(staging)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(package) as z:
        # Only what copy_installed takes from an installed WinDbg: the TTD
        # runtime and the license. The rest of the package is the whole
        # debugger (hundreds of MB) and most of the unpacking time.
        members = [m for m in z.infolist() if not m.is_dir() and m.filename not in _PACKAGE_META
                   and _kept(urllib.parse.unquote(m.filename))]
        for i, m in enumerate(members):
            # Package part names are percent-encoded ("Third%20Party...").
            name = urllib.parse.unquote(m.filename).replace("/", os.sep)
            path = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(staging, name))
            if os.path.commonpath([root, path]) != root:
                raise InstallError("the package holds a file outside its folder: %s" % m.filename)
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
            with z.open(m) as src, open(path, "wb") as dst:
                shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, 1 << 20)
            if progress is not None and progress(i + 1, len(members)) is False:
                raise Cancelled()
    _finish(staging, target, version, APPINSTALLER_URL,
            "Microsoft Software License Terms - WinDbg, accepted in IDA before download")


def copy_installed(source, target, version):
    """Copy the TTD runtime (amd64/ttd) and the license out of an installed
    WinDbg into 'target', replacing what is there."""
    staging = target + ".new"
    shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.copytree(os.path.join(source, TTD_SUBDIR), os.path.join(staging, TTD_SUBDIR))
    if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(source, "eula.rtf")):
        shutil.copy2(os.path.join(source, "eula.rtf"), staging)
    _finish(staging, target, version, source,
            "Microsoft Software License Terms - WinDbg, as installed with WinDbg")


def _finish(staging, target, version, source, license_note):
    """Stamp a complete 'staging' folder and rename it to 'target'."""
    if not has_runtime(staging):
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
        raise InstallError("WinDbg %s does not contain %s" % (version, " or ".join(RUNTIME_FILES)))
    with open(os.path.join(staging, MARKER), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({
            "version": version,
            "source": source,
            "installed": datetime.datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
            "license": license_note,
        }, f, indent=2)

    old = target + ".old"
    if os.path.exists(old):
        if os.path.exists(target):
            shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)
            if os.path.exists(old):
                # Not all of it could go (a DLL in it is still loaded by an
                # IDA): moved aside under a name of its own, or the rename
                # of the target onto it below would fail and every later
                # install would say the runtime is in use.
                aside = "%s.%d" % (old, int(time.time()))
                try:
                    os.rename(old, aside)
                except OSError:
                    pass
        else:
            # An earlier install stopped between its two renames: the old
            # folder is the only working copy, so it is put back rather
            # than deleted.
            try:
                os.rename(old, target)
            except OSError as e:
                shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
                raise InstallError("Could not restore %s from %s (%s). Close every IDA that has "
                                   "a Microsoft recording open, then try again." % (target, old, e))
    moved = False
    if os.path.exists(target):
        try:
            os.rename(target, old)
            moved = True
        except OSError:
            shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
            raise InstallError("%s is in use. Close every IDA that has a Microsoft recording "
                               "open, then try again." % target)
    try:
        os.rename(staging, target)
    except OSError as e:
        # Put the previous runtime back, so a failed upgrade leaves it working.
        if moved:
            try:
                os.rename(old, target)
            except OSError:
                pass
        shutil.rmtree(staging, ignore_errors=True)
        raise InstallError("Could not move the new runtime into %s (%s); the previous one "
                           "was kept." % (target, e))
    shutil.rmtree(old, ignore_errors=True)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# RTF to text, enough for a license file

_RTF_TOKEN = re.compile(r"\\([a-z]{1,32})(-?\d{1,10})? ?|\\'([0-9a-f]{2})|\\([^a-z])|([{}])|[\r\n]+|(.)",
                        re.I | re.S)

# Groups that hold formatting tables or metadata, never text.
_RTF_SKIP = {
    "fonttbl", "colortbl", "stylesheet", "info", "pict", "header", "footer",
    "headerl", "headerr", "headerf", "footerl", "footerr", "footerf",
    "listtable", "listoverridetable", "rsidtbl", "generator", "xmlnstbl",
    "themedata", "colorschememapping", "latentstyles", "datastore",
    "pgdsctbl", "filetbl", "revtbl", "object", "fldinst", "mmathPr",
}
_RTF_CHARS = {
    "par": "\n", "line": "\n", "sect": "\n\n", "page": "\n\n", "tab": "\t",
    "cell": "\t", "row": "\n", "emdash": "\u2014", "endash": "\u2013",
    "lquote": "\u2018", "rquote": "\u2019", "ldblquote": "\u201c",
    "rdblquote": "\u201d", "bullet": "\u2022", "emspace": " ", "enspace": " ",
}


def rtf_to_text(rtf):
    if isinstance(rtf, bytes):
        rtf = rtf.decode("latin-1")
    stack = []
    skip = False         # inside a group that holds no text
    ucskip = 1           # characters after \uN that stand in for it
    pending = 0          # of those, still to drop
    out = []
    for word, arg, hexc, sym, brace, char in (m.groups() for m in _RTF_TOKEN.finditer(rtf)):
        if brace:
            pending = 0
            if brace == "{":
                stack.append((skip, ucskip))
            elif stack:
                skip, ucskip = stack.pop()
        elif sym:
            pending = 0
            if sym == "*":
                skip = True
            elif sym in "\\{}":
                if not skip:
                    out.append(sym)
            elif sym == "~":
                if not skip:
                    out.append("\u00a0")
            elif sym in "\r\n":
                if not skip:
                    out.append("\n")
        elif word:
            pending = 0
            w = word.lower()
            if w in _RTF_SKIP:
                skip = True
            elif skip:
                pass
            elif w == "uc":
                ucskip = int(arg or 1)
            elif w == "u":
                # \u takes a signed 16-bit number; a missing or out-of-range
                # one (a damaged file) becomes U+FFFD rather than an error.
                c = int(arg) if arg else None
                if c is not None and c < 0:
                    c += 0x10000
                if c is None or not 0 <= c <= 0x10FFFF or 0xD800 <= c <= 0xDFFF:
                    c = 0xFFFD
                out.append(chr(c))
                pending = ucskip
            elif w in _RTF_CHARS:
                out.append(_RTF_CHARS[w])
        elif hexc:
            if pending:
                pending -= 1
            elif not skip:
                out.append(bytes([int(hexc, 16)]).decode("cp1252", "replace"))
        elif char:
            if pending:
                pending -= 1
            elif not skip:
                out.append(char)
    text = "".join(out)
    text = re.sub(r"[ \t]+\n", "\n", text)
    return re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", text).strip() + "\n"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# In IDA

def user_data_dir(*parts):
    """$IDAUSR/ida-ttd: what the user adds after installing
    (src/core/backend_module.h, user_data_dir). Not the package folder,
    which HCLI replaces on every upgrade, and not under plugins/, since none
    of it is a plugin."""
    import ida_diskio
    return os.path.join(ida_diskio.get_user_idadir(), "ida-ttd", *parts)


def legacy_dir(*parts):
    """$IDAUSR/plugins/ida-ttd-backends: where earlier versions installed
    the runtime and the Sogen backend. Still searched, so nothing breaks."""
    import ida_diskio
    return os.path.join(ida_diskio.get_user_idadir(), "plugins", "ida-ttd-backends", *parts)


def default_target():
    return user_data_dir("windbg")


def adopt_folder(old, new):
    """Move folder 'old' to 'new' when only the old one exists. False when
    it cannot (a DLL in it is loaded, say); the old copy then stays where it
    is found anyway."""
    if os.path.exists(new) or not os.path.isdir(old):
        return False
    try:
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(new), exist_ok=True)
        os.replace(old, new)
        return True
    except OSError:
        return False


def _in_background(title, work, status):
    """Run work(cancel) on a worker thread behind a cancellable wait box.
    The thread does only network and file work; every IDA call stays on the
    main thread. status() is the wait box's current text."""
    import ida_kernwin
    result = {}
    cancel = threading.Event()

    def run():
        try:
            result["value"] = work(cancel)
        except BaseException as e:      # handed to the main thread below
            result["error"] = e

    t = threading.Thread(target=run, name="ida-ttd runtime install", daemon=True)
    ida_kernwin.show_wait_box(title)
    try:
        t.start()
        shown = None
        while t.is_alive():
            t.join(0.15)
            if ida_kernwin.user_cancelled():
                cancel.set()
            text = status()
            if text and text != shown:
                ida_kernwin.replace_wait_box(text)
                shown = text
    finally:
        ida_kernwin.hide_wait_box()
    if "error" in result:
        raise result["error"]
    return result.get("value")


def _ask_license(release, target, text):
    """Show WinDbg's license; True only if the user accepts it."""
    intro = ("ida-ttd needs Microsoft's TTD replay runtime (TTDReplay.dll) to open "
             "Microsoft TTD recordings. It comes with WinDbg, and Microsoft does not allow "
             "anyone else to distribute it, so ida-ttd cannot include it.\n\n"
             "This will download WinDbg %s (%d MB) from Microsoft and unpack it into\n%s\n\n"
             "WinDbg is Microsoft's software, licensed to you by Microsoft under the terms "
             "below. Accept installs it; Decline installs nothing."
             % (release.version, (release.size + (1 << 19)) >> 20, target))
    try:
        from PySide6 import QtWidgets
    except ImportError:
        QtWidgets = None
    if QtWidgets is None:
        import ida_kernwin
        path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(target), "WinDbg-license.txt")
        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write(text)
        os.startfile(path)
        return ida_kernwin.ask_buttons("Accept", "Decline", "", 0,
                                       "%s\n\nThe license is open in a text editor (%s)."
                                       % (intro, path)) == 1

    return _license_dialog(QtWidgets, intro, text).exec() == QtWidgets.QDialog.Accepted


def _license_dialog(QtWidgets, intro, text):
    dlg = QtWidgets.QDialog(QtWidgets.QApplication.activeWindow())
    dlg.setWindowTitle("Install the TTD runtime: WinDbg license")
    lay = QtWidgets.QVBoxLayout(dlg)
    head = QtWidgets.QLabel(intro)
    head.setWordWrap(True)
    lay.addWidget(head)
    body = QtWidgets.QPlainTextEdit()
    body.setReadOnly(True)
    # The license puts a tab after each clause number ("1.\tINSTALLATION");
    # Qt's default tab stop is eight characters wide.
    body.setTabStopDistance(3 * body.fontMetrics().horizontalAdvance("0"))
    body.setPlainText(text)
    lay.addWidget(body, 1)
    buttons = QtWidgets.QDialogButtonBox()
    accept = buttons.addButton("Accept", QtWidgets.QDialogButtonBox.AcceptRole)
    decline = buttons.addButton("Decline", QtWidgets.QDialogButtonBox.RejectRole)
    decline.setDefault(True)
    accept.setAutoDefault(False)
    buttons.accepted.connect(dlg.accept)
    buttons.rejected.connect(dlg.reject)
    lay.addWidget(buttons)
    dlg.resize(760, 640)
    return dlg


def install_runtime(target=None):
    """TTD > Backends > Install the TTD runtime (WinDbg)...: find, or else
    install, WinDbg's TTD runtime. Returns the folder holding it, or None."""
    import ida_kernwin
    if target is None:
        target = default_target()
        # Move an earlier version's runtime here, so the version checks below
        # see it.
        if adopt_folder(legacy_dir("windbg"), target):
            ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] Moved the TTD runtime from %s to %s.\n" % (legacy_dir("windbg"), target))

    mine = read_marker(target) if has_runtime(target) else None
    found = installed_windbg()
    if found:
        source, version = found
        if mine is not None and mine.get("version") == version:
            ida_kernwin.info("ida-ttd already has the TTD runtime of WinDbg %s, the version "
                             "installed on this computer:\n%s" % (version, target))
            return target
        if ida_kernwin.ask_yn(ida_kernwin.ASKBTN_YES,
                              "WinDbg %s is installed on this computer.\n\n"
                              "Copy its TTD runtime for ida-ttd? Windows does not let other "
                              "programs load it from where WinDbg is installed, so ida-ttd keeps "
                              "a copy in\n%s\n\nRun this again after WinDbg updates to copy the "
                              "new version." % (version, target)) != ida_kernwin.ASKBTN_YES:
            return None
        try:
            os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
            copy_installed(source, target, version)
        except Exception as e:
            shutil.rmtree(target + ".new", ignore_errors=True)
            ida_kernwin.warning("Copying the TTD runtime from WinDbg failed: %s" % e)
            return None
        return _installed(version, target)

    state = {"text": "Asking Microsoft for the current WinDbg..."}
    try:
        release = _in_background("HIDECANCEL\n" + state["text"],
                                 lambda cancel: latest_release(), lambda: state["text"])
    except Exception as e:
        ida_kernwin.warning("Could not reach Microsoft's WinDbg download: %s" % e)
        return None

    if mine is not None:
        if mine.get("version") == release.version:
            ida_kernwin.info("WinDbg %s, the current version, is already installed for ida-ttd:\n%s"
                             % (release.version, target))
            return target
        if ida_kernwin.ask_yn(ida_kernwin.ASKBTN_YES,
                              "WinDbg %s is installed for ida-ttd; %s is available.\n\nUpdate it?"
                              % (mine.get("version", "?"), release.version)) != ida_kernwin.ASKBTN_YES:
            return target

    try:
        text = _in_background("HIDECANCEL\nReading the WinDbg license...",
                              lambda cancel: release.license_text(), lambda: None)
    except Exception as e:
        ida_kernwin.warning("Could not read the WinDbg license: %s" % e)
        return None
    if not _ask_license(release, target, text):
        ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] The WinDbg license was declined; nothing was installed.\n")
        return None

    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(target), exist_ok=True)
    package = target + ".msix.part"
    total_mb = release.size >> 20

    def work(cancel):
        def dl(done, total):
            state["text"] = "Downloading WinDbg %s from Microsoft: %d of %d MB" % (
                release.version, done >> 20, total_mb)
            return not cancel.is_set()

        def up(done, total):
            state["text"] = "Unpacking WinDbg: %d of %d files" % (done, total)
            return not cancel.is_set()
        try:
            download(release, package, dl)
            state["text"] = "Unpacking WinDbg..."
            unpack(package, target, release.version, up)
        finally:
            try:
                os.remove(package)
            except OSError:
                pass

    state["text"] = "Downloading WinDbg %s from Microsoft..." % release.version
    try:
        _in_background(state["text"], work, lambda: state["text"])
    except Cancelled:
        shutil.rmtree(target + ".new", ignore_errors=True)
        ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] The WinDbg install was cancelled; nothing was installed.\n")
        return None
    except Exception as e:
        shutil.rmtree(target + ".new", ignore_errors=True)
        ida_kernwin.warning("Installing WinDbg failed: %s" % e)
        return None

    return _installed(release.version, target)


def _installed(version, target):
    import ida_kernwin
    ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] Installed the TTD runtime of WinDbg %s in %s; Microsoft TTD "
                    "recordings can be replayed now.\n" % (version, target))
    ida_kernwin.info("The TTD runtime of WinDbg %s is installed in\n%s\n\nMicrosoft TTD recordings "
                     "can be replayed now: start the debugger (Debugger > Start process) to begin."
                     % (version, target))
    return target


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The Sogen backend
#
# The package ships ida-ttd-sogen.dll. This installs another build of it
# into $IDAUSR/ida-ttd/backends/, which upgrades leave alone and which
# ida-ttd searches first, so it takes the packaged one's place. The source
# is a file the user picks: the DLL, or a zip holding it (its license and
# notice files are kept beside it). The functions up to install_sogen() use
# no IDA module.

SOGEN_DLL = "ida-ttd-sogen.dll"
SOGEN_LICENSES = "ida-ttd-sogen-licenses"
# The one symbol every backend exports (src/abi/ida_ttd_backend.h).
BACKEND_ENTRY = b"ida_ttd_backend\0"


def sogen_target():
    return user_data_dir("backends")


def retire_sogen(folder):
    """Take the backend out of 'folder' (where an earlier version installed
    it), so IDA does not load that copy too. A loaded DLL cannot be deleted
    but can be renamed; .old files are removed on a later run. True when
    there was one."""
    final = os.path.join(folder, SOGEN_DLL)
    if not os.path.isdir(folder):
        return False
    for old in os.listdir(folder):
        if old.startswith(SOGEN_DLL + ".old"):
            try:
                os.remove(os.path.join(folder, old))
            except OSError:
                pass                    # still loaded by an IDA somewhere
    if not os.path.exists(final):
        return False
    n = 0
    while os.path.exists("%s.old%d" % (final, n)):
        n += 1
    os.rename(final, "%s.old%d" % (final, n))
    shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(folder, SOGEN_LICENSES), ignore_errors=True)
    return True


def _check_backend(data, where):
    if data[:2] != b"MZ" or BACKEND_ENTRY not in data:
        raise InstallError("%s is not an ida-ttd backend DLL" % where)


def stage_sogen(source, target):
    """Put the backend from 'source' (the DLL, or a zip holding it) into
    target/ida-ttd-sogen.dll.new, and any license or notice files the zip
    has into target/ida-ttd-sogen-licenses.new/. Returns the staged DLL."""
    os.makedirs(target, exist_ok=True)
    staged = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_DLL + ".new")
    lic_dir = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_LICENSES + ".new")
    shutil.rmtree(lic_dir, ignore_errors=True)
    if zipfile.is_zipfile(source):
        with zipfile.ZipFile(source) as z:
            names = [n for n in z.namelist() if not n.endswith("/")]
            dlls = [n for n in names if os.path.basename(n).lower() == SOGEN_DLL]
            if not dlls:
                raise InstallError("%s holds no %s" % (os.path.basename(source), SOGEN_DLL))
            data = z.read(dlls[0])
            _check_backend(data, dlls[0])
            folder = os.path.dirname(dlls[0])
            for n in names:
                base = os.path.basename(n)
                if os.path.dirname(n) == folder and re.match(r"(?i)(license|copying|notice|third-party)", base):
                    os.makedirs(lic_dir, exist_ok=True)
                    with open(os.path.join(lic_dir, base), "wb") as f:
                        f.write(z.read(n))
    else:
        with open(source, "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        _check_backend(data, os.path.basename(source))
    with open(staged, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)
    return staged


def place_sogen(staged, target):
    """Move the staged backend (and its licenses) into place. A loaded
    backend cannot be overwritten but can be renamed, so it is moved aside
    and removed on the next run. True when one was replaced (IDA needs a
    restart to use the new one)."""
    final = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_DLL)
    for old in os.listdir(target):
        if old.startswith(SOGEN_DLL + ".old"):
            try:
                os.remove(os.path.join(target, old))
            except OSError:
                pass                    # still loaded by an IDA somewhere
    replaced = os.path.exists(final)
    if replaced:
        try:
            os.replace(staged, final)
        except PermissionError:
            n = 0
            while os.path.exists("%s.old%d" % (final, n)):
                n += 1
            os.rename(final, "%s.old%d" % (final, n))
            os.replace(staged, final)
    else:
        os.replace(staged, final)
    lic_new = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_LICENSES + ".new")
    if os.path.isdir(lic_new):
        lic = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_LICENSES)
        shutil.rmtree(lic, ignore_errors=True)
        os.replace(lic_new, lic)
    return replaced


def install_sogen(source=None, target=None):
    """TTD > Backends > Install the Sogen backend...: install
    ida-ttd-sogen.dll from a file. Returns where it went, or None."""
    import ida_kernwin
    legacy = legacy_dir() if target is None else None
    target = target or sogen_target()
    if source is None:
        source = ida_kernwin.ask_file(0, "ida-ttd-sogen.dll;*.zip",
                                      "Choose the Sogen backend (ida-ttd-sogen.dll, or a zip holding it)")
        if not source:
            return None
    try:
        staged = stage_sogen(source, target)
        replaced = place_sogen(staged, target)
    except Exception as e:
        try:
            os.remove(os.path.join(target, SOGEN_DLL + ".new"))
        except OSError:
            pass
        shutil.rmtree(os.path.join(target, SOGEN_LICENSES + ".new"), ignore_errors=True)
        ida_kernwin.warning("Installing the Sogen backend failed: %s" % e)
        return None
    # The new backend is in place from here on, so a failure tidying up
    # after an earlier version is reported, not taken for a failed install.
    leftover = None
    if legacy is not None:
        try:
            # An earlier version's copy would still load if this one failed
            # to, and be the version nobody expects.
            if retire_sogen(legacy):
                replaced = True
            # Its registry hives sat beside it; the plugin now looks in
            # ida-ttd/registry.
            adopt_folder(os.path.join(legacy, "registry"), user_data_dir("registry"))
        except Exception as e:
            leftover = "Could not move the earlier copy out of %s (%s). Delete %s there by hand, " \
                       "or IDA may load that one too." % (legacy, e, SOGEN_DLL)
    final = os.path.join(target, SOGEN_DLL)
    ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] Installed the Sogen backend in %s; restart IDA to load it.\n" % final)
    if leftover:
        ida_kernwin.msg("[ida-ttd] %s\n" % leftover)
    ida_kernwin.info("The Sogen backend is installed in\n%s\n\nRestart IDA to use it%s: "
                     "backends are loaded when IDA starts. Then Sogen recordings (.sogttd) "
                     "open like Microsoft ones, and the Forks menu appears for them.%s"
                     % (final, " (it replaces the one loaded now)" if replaced else "",
                        "\n\nWarning: " + leftover if leftover else ""))
    return final

```

`scripts/ida_ttd_settings.py`:

```py
"""ida-ttd's settings, read through ida-settings for the plugin.

The settings are declared in ida-plugin.json (every one with a default and
"prompt": false, so installing asks nothing). Their values live in IDA's
ida-config.json, where `hcli plugin config ida-ttd set KEY VALUE` and the IDA
Settings Editor plugin put them. ida-settings is the library that reads them,
and it is Python, so the plugin (C++) asks this module: dump() hands back
every value as text, and the plugin keeps its own defaults for anything
missing, which is all of them when ida-settings is not installed.

Copied beside ida_ttd.py (ida-ttd-python/), which the plugin puts on sys.path.
"""

PLUGIN = "ida-ttd"

EDITOR_FUNC = "ida_settings_show_plugin_settings"


def _settings():
    try:
        import ida_settings
    except Exception:                   # not installed, or broken: defaults
        return None
    return ida_settings.PluginSettings(PLUGIN)


def available():
    return _settings() is not None


def dump(keys):
    """'key=value' lines for each of the space-separated 'keys' that has a
    value (booleans as true/false), and '!key=reason' for one whose stored
    value could not be read. Empty without ida-settings."""
    s = _settings()
    if s is None:
        return ""
    out = []
    for key in keys.split():
        try:
            v = s.get_setting(key)
        except KeyError:
            continue
        except Exception as e:          # an invalid stored value, say
            # hcli finds plugins by their folder in $IDAUSR/plugins; a copy
            # loaded from anywhere else has no settings, only defaults.
            if type(e).__name__ == "PluginNotInstalledError":
                return ""
            out.append("!%s=%s" % (key, str(e).replace("\n", " ")))
            continue
        if isinstance(v, bool):
            v = "true" if v else "false"
        out.append("%s=%s" % (key, str(v).replace("\n", " ")))
    return "\n".join(out)


def show_editor():
    """TTD > Settings...: the IDA Settings Editor on ida-ttd's settings, or how
    to change them without it."""
    import ida_expr
    import ida_kernwin
    import idc
    if ida_expr.find_idc_func(EDITOR_FUNC) == EDITOR_FUNC:
        idc.eval_idc('%s("%s")' % (EDITOR_FUNC, PLUGIN))
        return
    have = available()
    ida_kernwin.info(
        "ida-ttd's settings are edited in the IDA Settings Editor, which is not installed.\n\n"
        "Install it with:\n    hcli plugin install ida-settings-editor\n\n"
        "Or set a value from the command line:\n    hcli plugin config ida-ttd set KEY VALUE\n"
        "    hcli plugin config ida-ttd list\n\n"
        "Changes apply from the next stop of the replay.%s"
        % ("" if have else
           "\n\nThe ida-settings Python package is not installed either, so ida-ttd uses its "
           "defaults. Installing ida-ttd with hcli installs it."))

```

`scripts/package.py`:

```py
"""Build the plugin package (ida-ttd.zip) from a build folder.

    python scripts/package.py [--build build/Release] [--out dist]

The zip is what HCLI installs into $IDAUSR/plugins/ida-ttd/ and what the
plugin repository indexes. Everything is under one top-level ida-ttd/ folder,
which HCLI requires of a suite (a plugin with components); inside it, the
layout is the installed layout:

    ida-plugin.json                 the suite root (components: below)
    ida-ttd.dll                     the plugin
    ida-ttd-backends/               the backends: Microsoft TTD (Apache-2.0
        ida-ttd-msttd.dll           OR GPL-2.0-only, like the plugin) and,
        ida-ttd-sogen.dll           when the build has it, Sogen (GPL-2.0-only),
        ida-ttd-sogen-licenses/     with its license, notices and where its
                                    source is (scripts/sogen_dist.py)
    ida-ttd-data/                   API metadata, found beside ida-ttd.dll
    ida-ttd-python/                 the ida_ttd module, found beside ida-ttd.dll
    LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, README.md
    ida-ttd-loader-setup/           a component: a PLUGIN_FIX plugin that
        ida-plugin.json             copies ttd-loader.dll into $IDAUSR/loaders/
        ida-ttd-loader-setup.dll    as IDA starts, since HCLI can install
        ttd-loader.dll              nothing outside the plugin folder

The Sogen backend is optional here (--require-sogen makes it not): a build
without it packages the rest. It never goes in without its licenses folder.

The component's ida-plugin.json is written here from the root one, so its
version, authors and URLs cannot drift from the suite's. The zip is built with
zipfile rather than Compress-Archive so entry names always use '/' and the JSON
carries no byte-order mark: HCLI reads both strictly.
"""
import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import zipfile

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SETUP = "ida-ttd-loader-setup"


def component_manifest(root):
    plugin = root["plugin"]
    keep = ("version", "license", "platforms", "idaVersions", "urls", "authors", "maintainers")
    meta = {k: plugin[k] for k in keep if k in plugin}
    meta.update({
        "name": SETUP,
        "entryPoint": SETUP,
        "description": "Installs the ida-ttd trace loader into IDA's loaders folder, "
                       "so File > Open recognizes recordings.",
        "categories": ["file-parsers-and-loaders"],
        "keywords": ["ttd", "loader"],
    })
    return {
        "$schema": root.get("$schema", "https://hcli.docs.hex-rays.com/schemas/ida-plugin.json"),
        "IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion": root["IDAMetadataDescriptorVersion"],
        "plugin": meta,
    }


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", default=str(REPO / "build" / "Release"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / "dist"))
    ap.add_argument("--require-sogen", action="store_true",
                    help="fail when the build has no Sogen backend")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    build = pathlib.Path(args.build)
    out = pathlib.Path(args.out)

    root = json.loads((REPO / "ida-plugin.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if SETUP not in root["plugin"].get("components", []):
        raise SystemExit("ida-plugin.json does not declare the %s component" % SETUP)

    # (path in the zip, file on disk); missing files fail here, before the
    # zip exists, rather than producing a package without them.
    files = [
        ("ida-plugin.json", REPO / "ida-plugin.json"),
        ("ida-ttd.dll", build / "ida-ttd.dll"),
        ("ida-ttd-backends/ida-ttd-msttd.dll", build / "backends" / "ida-ttd-msttd.dll"),
        ("LICENSE", REPO / "LICENSE"),
        ("THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt", REPO / "THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt"),
        ("README.md", REPO / "README.md"),
        (SETUP + "/" + SETUP + ".dll", build / (SETUP + ".dll")),
        (SETUP + "/ttd-loader.dll", build / "ttd-loader.dll"),
    ]
    sogen = build / "backends" / "ida-ttd-sogen.dll"
    licenses = build / "backends" / "ida-ttd-sogen-licenses"
    if sogen.is_file():
        found = sorted(p for p in licenses.glob("*") if p.is_file())
        if not any(p.name == "COPYING.txt" for p in found):
            raise SystemExit("%s has no licenses beside it (%s): run scripts/sogen_dist.py"
                             % (sogen, licenses))
        # Written for this build, not left from an older one: its README
        # names the Sogen commit, which must be the pin, and it is not older
        # than the DLL (sogen_dist.py runs after the build).
        readme = licenses / "README.txt"
        pin = ""
        for line in (REPO / "msbuild" / "sogen.pin").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
            if line.strip().startswith("commit="):
                pin = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
        text = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if readme.is_file() else ""
        if not pin or pin not in text:
            raise SystemExit("%s does not name the pinned Sogen commit %s: run scripts/sogen_dist.py again"
                             % (readme, pin or "(none in msbuild/sogen.pin)"))
        if readme.stat().st_mtime < sogen.stat().st_mtime:
            raise SystemExit("%s is older than %s: run scripts/sogen_dist.py again" % (licenses, sogen))
        files.append(("ida-ttd-backends/ida-ttd-sogen.dll", sogen))
        files += [("ida-ttd-backends/ida-ttd-sogen-licenses/" + p.name, p) for p in found]
    elif args.require_sogen:
        raise SystemExit("no Sogen backend in the build (%s)" % sogen)
    # What the build copies into each folder (msbuild/ida-ttd.vcxproj:
    # CopyApiMetadata and the Python copy step), named rather than globbed,
    # so a stray file is not shipped and a missing one fails below.
    expected = {
        "ida-ttd-data": sorted(p.name for p in (REPO / "data").glob("*.bin")),
        "ida-ttd-python": ["ida_ttd.py", "ida_ttd_runtime.py", "ida_ttd_settings.py", "ida_ttd_qt.py",
                           "ida_ttd_graph.py", "ida_ttd_heatmap.py", "ida_ttd_calltree.py"],
    }
    for folder, names in expected.items():
        if not names:
            raise SystemExit("nothing to ship in %s" % folder)
        files += [(folder + "/" + n, build / folder / n) for n in names]
        extra = sorted(p.name for p in (build / folder).glob("*") if p.name not in names)
        if extra:
            print("warning: not packaged, not something the build puts in %s: %s"
                  % (build / folder, ", ".join(extra)))
    missing = [str(src) for _, src in files if not src.is_file()]
    if missing:
        raise SystemExit("missing from the build:\n  " + "\n  ".join(missing))

    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest = out / "ida-ttd.zip"
    with zipfile.ZipFile(dest, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for name, src in files:
            z.write(src, "ida-ttd/" + name)
        z.writestr("ida-ttd/" + SETUP + "/ida-plugin.json",
                   json.dumps(component_manifest(root), indent=2) + "\n")
    print("wrote %s (%d files)" % (dest, len(files) + 1))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

`scripts/selftest.py`:

```py
"""End-to-end self-test of ida-ttd, run inside IDA (GUI or an idalib worker).

Drives a real debugger session over the reference sample (the program in the
ttd-traces folder that stores 0x2222222222222222 over 0x1111111111111111 in a
global) and checks every movement and analysis against what it is known to
do. The same checks hold for Microsoft and Sogen recordings of it.

The addresses are found in the database, not hard-coded, because recordings
of more than one build exist: the store is the instruction that writes the
register loaded with the constant, main is the function holding it, and so
on (sample_addresses).

Open the trace (File > Open, or the MCP's open_database), then:

    exec(open(r"...\\scripts\\selftest.py").read())
    run()

Each line of the result is "ok" or "FAIL" with the check's name.

The checks go through ida_ttd.py, the Python API scripts use: the movements
through Session, a recording without the debugger through Recording, and
every other command through ida_ttd.raw() and py(), so the API's quoting
and its number conversion are tested with the plugin.

On a Sogen recording, run_sogen() also checks the Sogen-only commands
(syscalls, self-modifying code, and, when the recording carries its registry
hives or a folder of them is given, recovered strings and a fork); see its
docstring.
"""
import os
import time

import ida_bytes
import ida_funcs
import ida_nalt
import ida_segment
import idautils
import idc

import ida_ttd


def T(cmd):
    """One command line, answered as ida_ttd's classes see it: failures are
    returned (ok false), not raised, and numbers are ints."""
    return ida_ttd.py(ida_ttd.raw(cmd))


def sample_addresses():
    """The sample's landmarks in this database, as a dict:

    store      the instruction that writes 0x2222222222222222 over the global
    next       the instruction after it
    glob       the global
    main       the function holding the store
    call       the last call in main before the store; after_call follows it
    crt_call   the CRT's call of main; crt_next and crt_next2 follow it
    text       (start, end) of .text
    """
    text = ida_segment.get_segm_by_name(".text")
    data = ida_bytes.get_bytes(text.start_ea, text.end_ea - text.start_ea) or b""
    # mov reg, 2222222222222222h: REX.W (48, or 49 for r8-r15), B8+r, imm64.
    i = data.find(bytes.fromhex("22" * 8))
    if i < 2:
        raise RuntimeError("the constant 0x2222222222222222 is not in .text: not the reference sample")
    load = text.start_ea + i - 2
    reg = idc.print_operand(load, 0)
    store = load
    while True:
        store = idc.next_head(store, text.end_ea)
        if store == idc.BADADDR:
            raise RuntimeError("no store of %s after %X" % (reg, load))
        if idc.print_insn_mnem(store) == "mov" and idc.print_operand(store, 1) == reg \
                and idc.get_operand_type(store, 0) == idc.o_mem:
            break
    glob = idc.get_operand_value(store, 0)
    main = ida_funcs.get_func(store).start_ea
    call = store
    while True:
        call = idc.prev_head(call, main)
        if call == idc.BADADDR:
            raise RuntimeError("no call in main before the store")
        if idc.print_insn_mnem(call) == "call":
            break
    crt = [x for x in idautils.CodeRefsTo(main, 0) if idc.print_insn_mnem(x) == "call"]
    if len(crt) != 1:
        raise RuntimeError("main is called from %d places, not one" % len(crt))
    crt_next = idc.next_head(crt[0], text.end_ea)
    return {
        "store": store, "next": idc.next_head(store, text.end_ea), "glob": glob, "main": main,
        "call": call, "after_call": idc.next_head(call, text.end_ea),
        "crt_call": crt[0], "crt_next": crt_next, "crt_next2": idc.next_head(crt_next, text.end_ea),
        "text": (text.start_ea, text.end_ea),
    }


def run():
    A = sample_addresses()
    B = ida_nalt.get_imagebase()
    G = A["glob"]
    res, fails = [], []

    def chk(name, cond, detail=""):
        res.append(("ok  " if cond else "FAIL") + " " + name + (" " + str(detail) if detail != "" else ""))
        if not cond:
            fails.append(name)

    def pc(r):
        return r.get("pc")

    # The movements through the Python API's Session.
    S = ida_ttd.Session()
    t0 = time.time()
    r = S.start(timeout=0xB4)
    chk("start", r.get("ok") and r.get("process_state") == -1, r.get("pos"))
    r = S.run_to(A["store"])
    chk("runto the store", pc(r) == A["store"], r.get("pos"))
    chk("old value before it", S.read(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("11" * 8))
    r = S.step()
    chk("step", pc(r) == A["next"] and S.pc == A["next"])
    chk("new value after it", S.read(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("22" * 8))
    r = S.step(back=True)
    chk("step back", pc(r) == A["store"])
    chk("registers as ints", isinstance(S.reg("rip" if inf_64() else "eip"), int))

    r = S.run_to(A["call"], back=True)
    chk("runto backwards", pc(r) == A["call"])
    call_pos = r.get("pos")
    r = S.step_over()
    chk("step over a call", pc(r) == A["after_call"])
    r = S.step_over(back=True)
    chk("step back over the call", pc(r) == A["call"] and r.get("pos") == call_pos, (r.get("pos"), r.get("pc")))

    S.run_to(A["store"])
    r = S.step_out(timeout=0x3C)
    chk("step out of main", pc(r) == A["crt_next"], r.get("pc"))
    r = S.step()
    chk("step after it", pc(r) == A["crt_next2"], r.get("pc"))
    # The CRT's entry tail-jumps to the function that called main, so the call
    # that entered its frame is the system's call of the entry point.
    r = S.step_out(back=True)
    lp = pc(r) or 0
    image_end = max(idc.get_segm_end(s) for s in idautils.Segments() if B <= s < B + 0x100000)
    chk("step out backwards lands on a call outside the image",
        not (B <= lp < image_end) and idc.print_insn_mnem(lp) == "call", r.get("pc"))
    r = S.run_to(A["main"])
    chk("runto main", pc(r) == A["main"])
    r = S.step_out(back=True)
    chk("step out backwards from main's entry lands on the call", pc(r) == A["crt_call"], r.get("pc"))

    # A typo in a movement is refused, not read as some other movement.
    r = T("runto %X bakc" % A["main"])
    chk("an unknown word is refused", not r.get("ok") and "bakc" in r.get("error", ""), r.get("error"))

    # A write breakpoint on the global, as a user sets one: it stops on the
    # store itself, running forward from main and backward from past it.
    import ida_dbg
    import ida_idd
    T("runto %X" % A["main"])
    chk("write breakpoint accepted", ida_dbg.add_bpt(G, 8, ida_idd.BPT_WRITE))
    r = T("run")
    chk("write breakpoint stops on the store", pc(r) == A["store"], r.get("pc"))
    T("step")
    T("step")
    r = T("run back")
    chk("... and running back into it too", pc(r) == A["store"], r.get("pc"))
    ida_dbg.del_bpt(G)

    lo, hi = A["text"]
    a = T("an.search %X %X rw" % (G, G + 8))
    chk("memory search: one write, one read", a.get("count") == 2 and a["accesses"][0]["kind"] == "Write")
    a = T("an.coverage %X %X" % (lo, hi))
    chk("coverage", a.get("executed", 0) > 600, a.get("executed"))
    # 24 in the first build of the sample, 25 in the second.
    a = T("an.callsites %X %X" % (lo, hi))
    chk("indirect call sites", a.get("sites", 0) >= 24, a.get("sites"))
    a = T("an.trace %X 5" % A["main"])
    # The return value reads "(int)0x0" when main has no type in the database
    # and "(__int64)0" once IDA has guessed one (decompiling it does): compare
    # the number, not the text.
    ret = a["calls"][0]["ret"] if a.get("count") == 1 else ""
    chk("trace main: argc 1, returns 0",
        a.get("count") == 1 and a["calls"][0]["args"][0] == "0x1" and int(ret.rpartition(")")[2], 0) == 0, ret)
    a = T("an.memmap 4")
    chk("memory map", a.get("changes", 0) > 50, a.get("changes"))

    # The recording again without the debugger, through Recording; a second
    # one supersedes the first, which must then refuse to go on.
    trace = T("state").get("trace", "")
    if trace:
        first = ida_ttd.Recording(trace)
        first.seek("first")
        p0 = first.position
        first.step()
        chk("a Recording moves", first.position != p0, (p0, first.position))
        second = ida_ttd.Recording(trace)
        try:
            first.position
            chk("an older Recording refuses after a newer one opens", False)
        except ida_ttd.TtdError:
            chk("an older Recording refuses after a newer one opens", True)
        second.close()
        first.close()

    r = T("state")
    chk("still responsive", r.get("session") and r.get("process_state") == -1)
    r = T("stop")
    chk("stop", r.get("process_state") == 0, r.get("process_state"))
    res.append("%.1f s, %d failed" % (time.time() - t0, len(fails)))
    return res


def inf_64():
    import ida_ida
    return ida_ida.inf_is_64bit()


def run_sogen(registry=None, host=False, fork_path=None):
    """The Sogen-only commands, on a Sogen recording of the same sample.

    registry: a folder of registry hives (SYSTEM, SOFTWARE, ...) for the checks
    that replay the program (recovered strings, forks). Not needed when the
    recording carries its own hives (an.registry's registry_carried); with
    neither, those checks are skipped. host: allow replaying a recording made
    against the host, which reruns the program's file and network operations
    on this machine (the reference recordings were made that way). fork_path:
    where the fork goes (default: next to the database, named for this run;
    the forks this test makes are deleted at the end unless fork_path is
    given).
    """
    A = sample_addresses()
    res, fails = [], []

    def chk(name, cond, detail=""):
        res.append(("ok  " if cond else "FAIL") + " " + name + (" " + str(detail) if detail != "" else ""))
        if not cond:
            fails.append(name)

    t0 = time.time()
    r = T("start B4")
    chk("start", r.get("ok") and r.get("process_state") == -1, r.get("pos"))

    s = T("an.syscalls 5")
    chk("syscalls listed and named", s.get("ok") and s.get("count", 0) > 0 and s["syscalls"][0]["name"] != "",
        (s.get("count"), s.get("error")))
    chk("syscall arguments read", s.get("ok") and bool(s.get("syscalls")) and "args" in s["syscalls"][0],
        s.get("error"))

    m = T("an.selfmod 5")
    chk("self-modifying code search runs", m.get("ok"), (m.get("count"), m.get("error")))

    carried = bool(T("an.registry").get("registry_carried"))
    if registry or carried:
        extra = (' registry="%s"' % registry if registry else "") + (" host" if host else "")
        if not registry:
            res.append("note: using the hives the recording carries")
        st = T("an.strings 8 5" + extra)
        chk("strings recovered by a replay", st.get("ok") and st.get("count", 0) > 0,
            (st.get("count"), st.get("error")))
        T("runto %X" % A["main"])
        # A name of its own per run, so an earlier run's forks (an.forget
        # leaves the files) are never overwritten.
        path = fork_path or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(idc.get_idb_path()),
                                         "selftest-fork-%s.sogttd" % time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S"))
        f = T('an.fork "%s" 4E20 rax=1%s' % (path, extra))
        chk("a fork records", f.get("ok") and f.get("instructions") == 0x4E20 and os.path.exists(path),
            (f.get("instructions"), f.get("error")))
        # The fork as the GUI makes it: fork here, change a register and the
        # global through IDA's own debugger calls, record.
        import ida_dbg
        G = A["glob"]
        T("runto %X" % A["store"])
        T("an.forkhere")
        ok_reg = ida_dbg.set_reg_val("RAX", 0x1234)
        ok_mem = ida_dbg.write_dbg_memory(G, bytes.fromhex("33" * 8)) == 8
        d = T("an.forkdraft")
        chk("fork here takes IDA's register and memory writes",
            ok_reg and ok_mem and len(d.get("regs", [])) == 1 and len(d.get("memory", [])) == 1, d)
        chk("... and shows them there",
            ida_dbg.get_reg_val("RAX") == 0x1234 and idc.read_dbg_memory(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("33" * 8))
        T("step")
        moved = idc.read_dbg_memory(G, 8)
        chk("elsewhere the recording is read-only",
            moved == bytes.fromhex("22" * 8) and ida_dbg.write_dbg_memory(G, bytes.fromhex("44")) != 1, moved)
        T("step back")
        chk("back at the fork the changes show again", idc.read_dbg_memory(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("33" * 8))
        path2 = path.replace(".sogttd", "-draft.sogttd")
        f = T('an.forkrecord "%s" 4E20%s' % (path2, extra))
        chk("the fork records with its changes",
            f.get("ok") and f.get("regs") == 1 and f.get("writes") == 1 and os.path.exists(path2),
            (f.get("instructions"), f.get("error")))
        T("an.forkdiscard")
        chk("discarding it shows the recording again", idc.read_dbg_memory(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("11" * 8))

        # The Fork manager's list, and switching the replay to the fork and
        # back, in this database.
        forks = T("an.forks").get("forks", [])
        mine = [x for x in forks if os.path.normcase(x["path"]) == os.path.normcase(path2)]
        chk("the fork is in the fork list, with its parent and change",
            len(mine) == 1 and mine[0]["changes"] == "rax=0x1234, 8 bytes at 0x%X" % G, mine)
        parent = mine[0]["parent"] if mine else ""
        sw = T('switch "%s"' % path2)
        chk("switching replays the fork in this database",
            sw.get("ok") and os.path.normcase(sw.get("trace", "")) == os.path.normcase(path2)
            and sw.get("pc") == A["store"]
            and ida_dbg.get_reg_val("RAX") == 0x1234 and idc.read_dbg_memory(G, 8) == bytes.fromhex("33" * 8),
            (sw.get("trace"), sw.get("pc"), sw.get("error")))
        sw = T('switch "%s"' % parent)
        chk("... and back to the recording", sw.get("ok") and os.path.normcase(sw.get("trace", "")) == os.path.normcase(parent),
            (sw.get("trace"), sw.get("error")))
        for x in (path, path2):
            T('an.forget "%s"' % x)
            if not fork_path:
                try:
                    os.remove(x)
                except OSError:
                    pass
    else:
        res.append("skip strings and fork: the recording carries no registry hives and no folder was given")

    r = T("stop")
    chk("stop", r.get("process_state") == 0, r.get("process_state"))
    res.append("%.1f s, %d failed" % (time.time() - t0, len(fails)))
    return res

```

`scripts/sogen_dist.py`:

```py
"""Get the Sogen backend ready to ship: its licenses, and its source.

    python scripts/sogen_dist.py --sogen <Sogen tree> [--git <Sogen checkout>]
                                 [--build build/Release] [--out dist] [--no-source]
                                 [--allow-dirty]

ida-ttd-sogen.dll is GPL-2.0-only (it links Sogen and Unicorn), so it goes out
with the GPL text, the notices of what it contains, and its complete source
(docs/licensing.md). This writes:

    <build>/backends/ida-ttd-sogen-licenses/
        COPYING.txt             the GPL-2.0 text, which the DLL is under
        README.txt              what the DLL contains, and where its source is
        <component>-<file>      each component's own license or notice
    <out>/ida-ttd-sogen-source.zip
        sogen/                  the Sogen tree it was built from, deps included
        ida-ttd/                ida-ttd at the commit being built (the backend's
                                source, the shared header, the build files)

scripts/package.py puts the DLL and the licenses folder in the plugin package;
the release workflow attaches the source archive to the same release.

Two of Sogen's submodules state no license at all, so they are left out of the
archive and named instead: minidump_cpp (its headers are on the include path,
but none of its code is in the DLL; docs/licensing.md says how that is checked)
and sogen-linux-files (test data). Sogen's build fetches both as submodules.

--sogen is the tree that was built (a checkout with its submodules, or a
snapshot of one). --git is a Sogen git checkout to read the submodule commits
from, when --sogen is a snapshot without .git; it is only read.
"""
import argparse
import io
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import tarfile
import zipfile

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
LICENSES = "ida-ttd-sogen-licenses"
SOURCE_ZIP = "ida-ttd-sogen-source.zip"
EXCLUDED = ("minidump_cpp", "sogen-linux-files")

# What the DLL contains, by the symbols in its PDB (docs/licensing.md), and
# the files in each component's tree that carry its terms.
NOTICES = [
    ("Sogen", "", ["LICENSE"]),
    ("unicorn", "deps/unicorn", ["COPYING", "COPYING.LGPL2", "COPYING_GLIB"]),
    ("capstone", "deps/capstone", ["LICENSES/LICENSE.TXT", "LICENSES/LICENSE_BSD_3_CLAUSE.txt",
                                    "LICENSES/LICENSE_LLVM.TXT"]),
    ("mbedtls", "deps/mbedtls", ["LICENSE"]),
    ("zstd", "deps/zstd", ["LICENSE", "COPYING"]),
    ("base64", "deps/base64", ["LICENSE"]),
    ("reflect", "deps/reflect", ["reflect"]),      # MIT, in the header itself
    ("Vulkan-Headers", "deps/Vulkan-Headers", ["LICENSE.md"]),
]


def read_pin():
    pin = {}
    for line in (REPO / "msbuild" / "sogen.pin").read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
            k, v = line.split("=", 1)
            pin[k.strip()] = v.strip()
    return pin


def submodule_commits(git, commit):
    """{name: commit} of Sogen's deps/ at 'commit', or {} without git."""
    if git is None or not (git / ".git").exists():
        return {}
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(git), "ls-tree", commit, "deps/"],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0:
        return {}
    found = {}
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        meta, path = line.split("\t", 1)
        mode, kind, sha = meta.split()
        if kind == "commit":
            found[path[len("deps/"):]] = sha
    return found


def tree_mismatches(sogen, git, commit, subdir="src/windows-ttd"):
    """Files under 'subdir' of the tree at 'sogen' that differ from Sogen at
    'commit' (in the git checkout 'git'), as a list of paths; None when there
    is no checkout to compare with.

    The README says the source is Sogen at the pinned commit, and the source
    archive is whatever tree --sogen names: a snapshot of another commit
    would ship source that does not match its own README (GPL source
    correspondence). The backend is built from src/windows-ttd, so that is
    what is compared, by git blob hash, which needs no .git in the snapshot.
    """
    import hashlib
    if git is None or not (git / ".git").exists():
        return None
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(git), "ls-tree", "-r", commit, "--", subdir],
                         capture_output=True, text=True)
    if out.returncode != 0:
        return None
    want = {}
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        meta, path = line.split("\t", 1)
        mode, kind, sha = meta.split()
        if kind == "blob" and mode != "120000":     # symlinks do not extract on Windows
            want[path] = sha
    bad = []
    for path, sha in want.items():
        f = sogen / path
        if not f.is_file():
            bad.append(path + " (missing)")
            continue
        data = f.read_bytes()
        # As stored, or as git archive writes it with core.autocrlf (CRLF
        # line ends): both are the committed file.
        ok = False
        for d in (data, data.replace(b"\r\n", b"\n")):
            if hashlib.sha1(b"blob %d\0" % len(d) + d).hexdigest() == sha:
                ok = True
                break
        if not ok:
            bad.append(path)
    return bad


def submodule_urls(sogen):
    urls, path = {}, None
    gm = sogen / ".gitmodules"
    if not gm.is_file():
        return urls
    for line in gm.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
        line = line.strip()
        if line.startswith("path"):
            path = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
        elif line.startswith("url") and path:
            urls[path[len("deps/"):]] = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip()
    return urls


def ida_ttd_commit():
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    return out.stdout.strip() if out.returncode == 0 else "unknown"


def readme(pin, commits, urls):
    lines = [
        "ida-ttd-sogen.dll: the Sogen backend of ida-ttd",
        "",
        "This DLL is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 2 only",
        "(COPYING.txt). It contains:",
        "",
        "  - ida-ttd's Sogen backend (src/backend-sogen/, GPL-2.0-only)",
        "    and its string and buffer scanners (src/common/write_scans.h, taken here",
        "    under GPL-2.0-only)",
        "  - Sogen, GPL-2.0-only (Sogen-LICENSE)",
        "  - Unicorn, with parts of QEMU, GPL-2.0 (unicorn-*)",
        "  - Capstone, BSD-3-Clause, with LLVM parts under the NCSA license (capstone-*)",
        "  - Mbed TLS, Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-or-later, here under the GPL (mbedtls-LICENSE)",
        "  - zstd, BSD OR GPL-2.0 (zstd-*)",
        "  - base64 and reflect, MIT (base64-LICENSE, reflect-reflect)",
        "  - Vulkan-Headers, Apache-2.0 OR MIT (Vulkan-Headers-LICENSE.md)",
        "",
        "Source",
        "",
        "The complete source it was built from is %s, attached to" % SOURCE_ZIP,
        "the same ida-ttd release as this package (https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd/releases).",
        "",
        "  Sogen    %s at %s" % (pin["repository"], pin["commit"]),
        "  ida-ttd  https://github.com/HullaBrian/ida-ttd at %s" % ida_ttd_commit(),
        "",
        "Built with docs/building-the-sogen-backend.md and .github/workflows/release.yml",
        "of that ida-ttd commit. Two Sogen submodules state no license and are not in",
        "the archive; none of their code is in this DLL. Sogen's build expects them:",
        "",
    ]
    for name in EXCLUDED:
        lines.append("  deps/%-18s %s at %s" % (name, urls.get(name, "?"), commits.get(name, "the commit Sogen records")))
    if commits:
        lines += ["", "Every submodule, at the commits Sogen %s records:" % pin["commit"][:8], ""]
        for name in sorted(commits):
            lines.append("  deps/%-18s %s" % (name, commits[name]))
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"


def write_licenses(sogen, dest, pin, commits, urls):
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for old in dest.iterdir():
        if old.is_dir() and not old.is_symlink():
            shutil.rmtree(old)
        else:
            old.unlink()
    (dest / "COPYING.txt").write_bytes((REPO / "LICENSES" / "GPL-2.0-only.txt").read_bytes())
    for component, folder, names in NOTICES:
        for name in names:
            src = sogen / folder / name
            if not src.is_file():
                raise SystemExit("missing %s: is %s a full Sogen tree?" % (src, sogen))
            (dest / ("%s-%s" % (component, pathlib.PurePath(name).name))).write_bytes(src.read_bytes())
    (dest / "README.txt").write_text(readme(pin, commits, urls), encoding="utf-8", newline="\r\n")


def uncommitted_changes():
    """Tracked files under src/ or msbuild/ that differ from HEAD. The
    archive is HEAD, so with any of these the DLL may not be built from the
    source that ships with it. Untracked files (TODO.txt, scratch) do not
    count: git archive leaves them out, and the build does not use them."""
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO), "status", "--porcelain", "--untracked-files=no",
                          "--", "src", "msbuild"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    return [line for line in out.stdout.splitlines() if line.strip()]


def write_source(sogen, out):
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    skip = {"deps/" + n for n in EXCLUDED}
    with zipfile.ZipFile(out, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED, compresslevel=6) as z:
        n = 0
        for p in sorted(sogen.rglob("*")):
            rel = p.relative_to(sogen).as_posix()
            first = rel.split("/", 1)[0]
            if first in (".git", "build") or any(rel == s or rel.startswith(s + "/") for s in skip):
                continue
            if "/.git/" in "/" + rel + "/" or not p.is_file() or p.is_symlink():
                continue
            z.write(p, "sogen/" + rel)
            n += 1
        # ida-ttd at HEAD, as git has it (no build output, no local files).
        arch = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(REPO), "archive", "--format=tar", "HEAD"],
                              capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=io.BytesIO(arch)) as t:
            for m in t.getmembers():
                if m.isfile():
                    z.writestr("ida-ttd/" + m.name, t.extractfile(m).read())
                    n += 1
    return n


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--sogen", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--git")
    ap.add_argument("--build", default=str(REPO / "build" / "Release"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", default=str(REPO / "dist"))
    ap.add_argument("--no-source", action="store_true")
    ap.add_argument("--allow-dirty", action="store_true",
                    help="write the source archive even though src/ or msbuild/ has uncommitted changes")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    if not args.no_source and not args.allow_dirty:
        dirty = uncommitted_changes()
        if dirty:
            raise SystemExit("src/ or msbuild/ has uncommitted changes, so the source archive "
                             "(ida-ttd at HEAD) may not match the DLL:\n  %s\n"
                             "Commit them and rebuild, or pass --allow-dirty (or --no-source)."
                             % "\n  ".join(dirty))
    sogen = pathlib.Path(args.sogen)
    pin = read_pin()
    git = pathlib.Path(args.git) if args.git else sogen
    bad = tree_mismatches(sogen, git, pin["commit"])
    if bad is None:
```
