`src/analysis/origin.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "analysis/origin.h"
#include "analysis/query_runner.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"
#include "ui/names.h"

#include <intel.hpp>

namespace idattd
{
    namespace
    {
        const char *const GP_NAMES[ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT] =
        {
            "rax", "rcx", "rdx", "rbx", "rsp", "rbp", "rsi", "rdi",
            "r8", "r9", "r10", "r11", "r12", "r13", "r14", "r15", "rip",
        };

        // How far back a register's last change is sought. The backend's own
        // search replays the thread forward (seconds per few million steps);
        // stepping back one at a time, without one, costs a millisecond or
        // more per step.
        const uint64_t kRegisterLookBack = 4000000;
        const uint64_t kStepLookBack     = 200000;
        // Syscalls checked for having written memory, latest first.
        const size_t   kSyscallsChecked  = 300;

        // IDA's x86 register number to ITTD_REG_* / ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 + n;
        // -1 for those not followed (segment, flags, x87, ...).
        int ittd_reg_of(int r)
        {
            if ( r >= R_ax && r <= R_r15 )
                return r - R_ax;
            if ( r >= R_al && r <= R_bl )
                return r - R_al;
            if ( r >= R_ah && r <= R_bh )
                return r - R_ah;
            if ( r >= R_spl && r <= R_dil )
                return ITTD_REG_RSP + (r - R_spl);
            if ( r >= R_xmm0 && r <= R_xmm15 )
                return int(ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0) + (r - R_xmm0);
            if ( r >= R_ymm0 && r <= R_ymm15 )
                return int(ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0) + (r - R_ymm0);
            return -1;
        }

        bool same_target(const OriginTarget &a, const OriginTarget &b)
        {
            return a.is_reg == b.is_reg && (a.is_reg ? a.reg == b.reg : a.addr == b.addr && a.size == b.size);
        }

        bytevec_t read_value(ITraceCursor *cur, const OriginTarget &t, uint32_t tid)
        {
            bytevec_t v;
            if ( t.is_reg )
            {
                // Nothing between the general registers and xmm0, or past
                // the last xmm.
                const uint32_t nxmm = (uint32_t)std::extent_v<decltype(ittd_regs::xmm)>;
                if ( t.reg >= ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 + nxmm || (t.reg >= ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT && t.reg < ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0) )
                    return v;
                ittd_regs r{};
                bool ok = cur->thread_id() == tid ? cur->read_registers(&r) : cur->read_thread_registers(tid, &r);
                if ( !ok )
                    return v;
                if ( t.reg >= ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 )
                    v.append(r.xmm[t.reg - ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0], 16);
                else
                    v.append(&r.gp[t.reg], 8);
                return v;
            }
            v.resize(t.size);
            std::vector<uint8_t> known;
            cur->read_memory(t.addr, v.begin(), v.size(), &known);
            return v;
        }

        // What one hop's backend phase found (worker thread, no IDA calls).
        struct Search
        {
            bool        found = false;      // an instruction of the program set it
            Position    pos;
            ea_t        pc = BADADDR;
            uint32_t    tid = 0;
            bool        stepped = false;    // searched by stepping back (no backend search)
            uint64_t    looked = 0;         // how far, when not found
            // The system wrote it after the program last did (memory).
            bool        system = false;
            Position    sys_pos;
            qstring     sys_name;
            std::vector<Access> reads;      // what the setting instruction read
        };

        // The reads the instruction at 'pc' made in the one step at 'pos'.
        void reads_at(ITraceBackend *b, Position pos, ea_t pc, std::vector<Access> *out, ProgressSink *sink)
        {
            // All of user space; the one-step range is what narrows it.
            const ea_t hi = b->info().is64 ? (ea_t)0x800000000000ull : (ea_t)0x100000000ull;
            PositionRange one{ pos, b->position_add(pos, 1) };
            std::vector<Access> v;
            b->query_accesses(0, hi, ACCESS_READ, one, &v, sink);
            for ( const Access &a : v )
                if ( a.pc == pc )
                    out->push_back(a);
        }

        void find_reads(ITraceBackend *b, Search *s, ProgressSink *sink)
        {
            if ( s->found )
                reads_at(b, s->pos, s->pc, &s->reads, sink);
        }

        void search_register(ITraceBackend *b, const OriginTarget &t, Position at, uint32_t tid,
                             Search *s, ProgressSink *sink)
        {
            Position where;
            bool found = false;
            if ( b->query_register_change(at, tid, t.reg, kRegisterLookBack, &where, &found, sink) )
            {
                s->looked = kRegisterLookBack;
                if ( found )
                {
                    CursorPtr cur = b->make_cursor();
                    if ( cur && cur->seek(where) )
                    {
                        s->found = true;
                        s->pos   = where;
                        s->pc    = cur->program_counter();
                        s->tid   = cur->thread_id();
                    }
                }
                return;
            }

            // No search of the backend's own: step back on the thread.
            s->stepped = true;
            CursorPtr cur = b->make_cursor();
            if ( !cur || !cur->seek(at) )
                return;
            std::unique_ptr<INavigator> nav = b->make_navigator(cur.get());
            if ( !nav )
                return;
            const bytevec_t v0 = read_value(cur.get(), t, tid);
            for ( uint64_t i = 0; i < kStepLookBack; i++ )
            {
                if ( (i & 255) == 0 && sink != nullptr )
                {
                    if ( sink->cancelled() )
                        return;
                    sink->report(uint32_t(i * 100 / kStepLookBack));
                }
                if ( nav->step(false) != StopReason::Stepped )
                    break;
                s->looked = i + 1;
                if ( read_value(cur.get(), t, tid) != v0 )
                {
                    s->found = true;
                    s->pos   = cur->position();
                    s->pc    = cur->program_counter();
                    s->tid   = cur->thread_id();
                    return;
                }
            }
        }

        // The syscalls, listed at most once per trace_value_origin: on
        // Microsoft TTD a listing replays the whole recording.
        struct SyscallCache
        {
            bool                      listed = false;
            std::vector<SyscallEvent> calls;
        };

        // Memory is set by the program's last write to it, or by the system
        // afterwards, which may not be reported as a write (Microsoft TTD
        // reports a syscall filling a buffer as other access kinds). So when
        // the value after the program's write differs from the one asked
        // about, or the program never wrote it, the syscalls since are checked,
        // latest first.
        void search_memory(ITraceBackend *b, const OriginTarget &t, Position at, const bytevec_t &value,
                           SyscallCache *sc_cache, Search *s, ProgressSink *sink)
        {
            CursorPtr cur = b->make_cursor();
            if ( !cur || !cur->seek(at) )
                return;
            {
                std::unique_ptr<INavigator> nav = b->make_navigator(cur.get());
                if ( !nav )
                    return;
                Breakpoint bp;
                bp.addr  = t.addr;
                bp.size  = t.size;
                bp.kinds = ACCESS_WRITE;
                nav->set_breakpoints({ bp });
                nav->set_progress(sink);
                StopReason r = nav->run(false);
                nav->set_progress(nullptr);
                if ( r == StopReason::Breakpoint )
                {
                    s->found = true;
                    s->pos   = cur->position();
                    s->pc    = cur->program_counter();
                    s->tid   = cur->thread_id();
                }
            }
            if ( sink != nullptr && sink->cancelled() )
                return;

            // The value just after that write, on its thread.
            if ( s->found )
            {
                CursorPtr c2 = b->make_cursor();
                if ( c2 && c2->seek(s->pos) )
                {
                    std::unique_ptr<INavigator> n2 = b->make_navigator(c2.get());
                    if ( n2 && n2->step(true) == StopReason::Stepped && read_value(c2.get(), t, 0) == value )
                        return;
                }
            }

            if ( !b->capabilities().syscalls )
                return;
            if ( !sc_cache->listed )
            {
                // Start clean: never append to a listing left part-done.
                sc_cache->calls.clear();
                b->query_syscalls(&sc_cache->calls, sink);
                sc_cache->listed = !(sink != nullptr && sink->cancelled());
            }
            const std::vector<SyscallEvent> &calls = sc_cache->calls;
            // The candidates, newest first: syscalls before 'at' and after the
            // program's own write.
            std::vector<const SyscallEvent *> cand;
            for ( auto it = calls.rbegin(); it != calls.rend() && cand.size() < kSyscallsChecked; ++it )
            {
                if ( !(it->pos < at) )
                    continue;
                if ( s->found && !(s->pos < it->pos) )
                    break;
                cand.push_back(&*it);
            }
            if ( cand.empty() || t.is_reg || t.size == 0 )
                return;
            // The value at each syscall and one position after it, in one
            // batched read: a cursor, a seek and a step per candidate was
            // about 600 seeks a hop on Microsoft TTD (17 ms each), and a
            // graph repeats it per node. Memory is the process's, so "one
            // position after" is after the syscall whichever thread runs
            // next (the handle listing reads out parameters the same way).
            std::vector<MemAt> reads;
            reads.reserve(cand.size() * 2);
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < cand.size(); i++ )
                for ( int side = 0; side < 2; side++ )
                {
                    MemAt m;
                    m.pos    = side == 0 ? cand[i]->pos : b->position_add(cand[i]->pos, 1);
                    m.addr   = t.addr;
                    m.size   = t.size;
                    m.offset = reads.size() * t.size;
                    reads.push_back(m);
                }
            std::vector<uint8_t> data, known;
            const QueryResult rq = b->read_memory_at(reads, &data, &known, sink);
            if ( rq.cancelled || !rq.ran || data.size() < reads.size() * t.size )
                return;
            auto value_in = [&](size_t r) -> bytevec_t
            {
                bytevec_t v;
                const size_t off = r * t.size;
                for ( size_t j = 0; j < t.size; j++ )
                    if ( known[off + j] == ITTD_KNOWN_NO )
                        return bytevec_t();
                v.append(data.data() + off, t.size);
                return v;
            };
            // On Microsoft TTD a syscall's write to memory surfaces only where
            // the program later reads it, so "one position after" still shows
            // the old value. Where the backend can find that write
            // (query_out_values, as for handles), it is asked about every
            // candidate whose value did not visibly change.
            std::vector<std::optional<uint64_t>> surfaced;
            if ( t.size <= 8 && value.size() == t.size )
            {
                std::vector<OutSlot> slots;
                std::vector<size_t>  slot_of;
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < cand.size(); i++ )
                {
                    const bytevec_t before = value_in(2 * i), after = value_in(2 * i + 1);
                    if ( before.empty() || before != after )
                        continue;
                    OutSlot o;
                    o.call  = cand[i]->pos;
                    o.addr  = t.addr;
                    o.tid   = cand[i]->tid;
                    o.width = t.size;
                    memcpy(&o.before, before.begin(), t.size);
                    slots.push_back(o);
                    slot_of.push_back(i);
                }
                std::vector<std::optional<uint64_t>> vals;
                if ( !slots.empty() && b->query_out_values(slots, &vals, sink) )
                {
                    surfaced.assign(cand.size(), std::nullopt);
                    for ( size_t j = 0; j < slot_of.size() && j < vals.size(); j++ )
                        surfaced[slot_of[j]] = vals[j];
                }
            }
            uint64_t want_u = 0;
            if ( value.size() <= 8 )
                memcpy(&want_u, value.begin(), value.size());
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < cand.size(); i++ )
            {
                const bytevec_t before = value_in(2 * i), after = value_in(2 * i + 1);
                const bool by_search = i < surfaced.size() && surfaced[i].has_value()
                                    && *surfaced[i] == want_u && !before.empty()
                                    && memcmp(before.begin(), &want_u, before.size()) != 0;
                if ( !by_search && (after.empty() || after != value || before == after) )
                    continue;
                // Only the match needs a cursor: for its instruction.
                ea_t sys_pc = BADADDR;
                CursorPtr c = b->make_cursor();
                if ( c && c->seek(cand[i]->pos) )
                    sys_pc = c->program_counter();
                s->system   = true;
                s->sys_pos  = cand[i]->pos;
                s->sys_name = cand[i]->name.empty() ? qstring("a syscall") : cand[i]->name;
                s->found    = true;
                s->pos      = cand[i]->pos;
                s->pc       = sys_pc;
                s->tid      = cand[i]->tid;
                return;
            }
        }

        bool is_copy(uint16 itype)
        {
            switch ( itype )
            {
                case NN_mov: case NN_movzx: case NN_movsx: case NN_movsxd:
                case NN_movd: case NN_movq: case NN_movdqa: case NN_movdqu:
                case NN_movups: case NN_movaps: case NN_movupd: case NN_movapd:
                case NN_movss: case NN_movsd: case NN_lddqu:
                case NN_vmovd: case NN_vmovq: case NN_vmovdqa: case NN_vmovdqu:
                case NN_vmovups: case NN_vmovaps: case NN_vmovupd: case NN_vmovapd:
                case NN_vmovdqu8: case NN_vmovdqu16: case NN_vmovdqu32: case NN_vmovdqu64:
                case NN_vmovdqa32: case NN_vmovdqa64:
                    return true;
                default:
                    return false;
            }
        }

        bool is_memory(const op_t &op)
        {
            return op.type == o_mem || op.type == o_displ || op.type == o_phrase;
        }

        // The recorded read of the instruction's memory operand: one of
        // 'want_size' bytes when there is one, else the first.
        const Access *pick_read(const Search &s, size_t want_size)
        {
            const Access *any = nullptr;
            for ( const Access &a : s.reads )
            {
                if ( want_size != 0 && a.size == want_size )
                    return &a;
                if ( any == nullptr )
                    any = &a;
            }
            return any;
        }

        // From the instruction that set the value, what to follow next: for a
        // copy, fills 'next' and returns true; otherwise sets the kind and
        // note and returns false. 'made_here' is set when the instruction
        // computed the value into its destination (not a side-effect
        // register), so its inputs are what the value was made of.
        bool next_source(const OriginHop &hop, const Search &s, OriginHop *out, OriginTarget *next,
                         bool *made_here)
        {
            *made_here = false;
            insn_t ins;
            if ( decode_insn(&ins, s.pc) <= 0 )
            {
                out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                out->note = "the instruction could not be decoded here";
                return false;
            }
            if ( ins.itype == NN_syscall || ins.itype == NN_sysenter )
            {
                out->kind = OriginKind::System;
                out->note = hop.what.is_reg ? "the result of a syscall" : "written by the system during a syscall";
                return false;
            }

            // A register a copy changes as a side effect (rsp under push and
            // pop, rsi/rdi/rcx under string moves) was computed, not copied.
            if ( hop.what.is_reg )
            {
                const int want = int(hop.what.reg);
                auto names = [&](const op_t &op) { return op.type == o_reg && ittd_reg_of(op.reg) == want; };
                bool dest = true;
                switch ( ins.itype )
                {
                    case NN_push: case NN_movs: case NN_stos:
                        dest = false;
                        break;
                    case NN_lods:
                        dest = want == ITTD_REG_RAX;
                        break;
                    case NN_xchg:
                        dest = names(ins.ops[0]) || names(ins.ops[1]);
                        break;
                    case NN_pop:
                        dest = names(ins.ops[0]);
                        break;
                    default:
                        if ( is_copy(ins.itype) )
                            dest = names(ins.ops[0]);
                        break;
                }
                if ( !dest )
                {
                    out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                    out->note = "changed as a side effect of this instruction";
                    return false;
                }
                // A write to the low 8 or 16 bits (mov al, ...; mov ah, bl)
                // keeps the rest of the register as it was, so the source is
                // where only part of the value came from: following it would
                // report the whole value as copied from a byte. A 32-bit
                // write zero-extends, and movzx/movsx extend, so those copy
                // the whole register.
                const op_t &d0 = ins.ops[0];
                if ( d0.type == o_reg && ittd_reg_of(d0.reg) == want
                  && get_dtype_size(d0.dtype) < 4
                  && ins.itype != NN_movzx && ins.itype != NN_movsx && ins.itype != NN_movsxd )
                {
                    out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                    out->note.sprnt("only its low %u bits were written here; the rest kept an earlier value",
                                    (unsigned)(8 * get_dtype_size(d0.dtype)));
                    return false;
                }
            }

            const op_t *src = nullptr;
            bool from_read = false;           // the source is what it read
            int  stos_size = 0;
            switch ( ins.itype )
            {
                case NN_push:
                    src = &ins.ops[0];
                    break;
                case NN_pop:
                case NN_movs:
                case NN_lods:
                    from_read = true;
                    break;
                case NN_stos:
                    stos_size = (int)get_dtype_size(ins.ops[0].dtype);
                    break;
                case NN_xchg:
                {
                    // The operand that is not the value's destination.
                    const op_t &a = ins.ops[0], &b = ins.ops[1];
                    bool a_is_dest = hop.what.is_reg
                                   ? a.type == o_reg && ittd_reg_of(a.reg) == int(hop.what.reg)
                                   : is_memory(a);
                    src = a_is_dest ? &b : &a;
                    break;
                }
                default:
                    if ( is_copy(ins.itype) )
                        src = &ins.ops[1];
                    break;
            }

            if ( stos_size != 0 )
            {
                next->is_reg = true;
                next->reg    = ITTD_REG_RAX;
                out->kind = OriginKind::Copied;
                out->note = "stored from rax";
                return true;
            }
            // xor or sub of a register with itself: zero, whatever it held.
            if ( src == nullptr && !from_read
              && ins.ops[0].type == o_reg && ins.ops[1].type == o_reg && ins.ops[0].reg == ins.ops[1].reg )
            {
                switch ( ins.itype )
                {
                    case NN_xor: case NN_sub: case NN_pxor: case NN_xorps: case NN_xorpd:
                        out->kind = OriginKind::Constant;
                        out->note = "zeroed: a register combined with itself";
                        return false;
                    default:
                        break;
                }
            }
            if ( src == nullptr && !from_read )
            {
                out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                out->note = "computed by this instruction";
                *made_here = true;
                return false;
            }
            if ( src != nullptr && src->type == o_imm )
            {
                out->kind = OriginKind::Constant;
                out->note.sprnt("the constant 0x%llX in the code", (unsigned long long)src->value);
                return false;
            }
            if ( src != nullptr && src->type == o_reg )
            {
                int r = ittd_reg_of(src->reg);
                if ( r < 0 )
                {
                    out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                    out->note = "copied from a register this does not follow";
                    return false;
                }
                next->is_reg = true;
                next->reg    = (uint32_t)r;
                out->kind = OriginKind::Copied;
                out->note.sprnt("copied from %s", origin_target_text(*next).c_str());
                return true;
            }
            // From memory: the recorded read gives the address.
            size_t want = src != nullptr ? get_dtype_size(src->dtype) : 0;
            const Access *rd = pick_read(s, want);
            if ( rd == nullptr )
            {
                out->kind = OriginKind::Computed;
                out->note = "copied from memory, but the recording has no read for it";
                return false;
            }
            next->is_reg = false;
            next->addr   = rd->addr;
            next->size   = rd->size != 0 ? rd->size : 8;
            out->kind = OriginKind::Copied;
            out->note.sprnt("copied from %s", origin_target_text(*next).c_str());
            return true;
        }
    }

    qstring origin_value_text(const bytevec_t &v)
    {
        qstring s;
        if ( v.empty() )
            return "?";
        if ( v.size() <= 8 )
        {
            uint64_t x = 0;
            memcpy(&x, v.begin(), v.size());
            s.sprnt("0x%llX", (unsigned long long)x);
            return s;
        }
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < v.size(); i++ )
            s.cat_sprnt("%02X", v[i]);
        return s;
    }

    qstring origin_target_text(const OriginTarget &t)
    {
        qstring s;
        if ( t.is_reg )
        {
            if ( t.reg >= ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 )
                s.sprnt("xmm%u", t.reg - ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0);
            else if ( t.reg < ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT )
                s = GP_NAMES[t.reg];
            return s;
        }
        s.sprnt("[0x%llX], %u byte%s", (unsigned long long)t.addr, t.size, t.size == 1 ? "" : "s");
        return s;
    }

    bool parse_register(const char *name, uint32_t *reg)
    {
        qstring n(name);
        n.trim2();
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < n.length(); i++ )
            n[i] = qtolower(n[i]);
        for ( uint32_t i = 0; i < ITTD_REG_RIP; i++ )
            if ( n == GP_NAMES[i] )
                return *reg = i, true;
        // 32-, 16- and 8-bit names of the first eight map to the 64-bit one.
        static const char *const NARROW[][4] =
        {
            { "eax", "ax", "al", "ah" }, { "ecx", "cx", "cl", "ch" },
            { "edx", "dx", "dl", "dh" }, { "ebx", "bx", "bl", "bh" },
            { "esp", "sp", "spl", "" }, { "ebp", "bp", "bpl", "" },
            { "esi", "si", "sil", "" }, { "edi", "di", "dil", "" },
        };
        for ( uint32_t i = 0; i < 8; i++ )
            for ( const char *alias : NARROW[i] )
                if ( *alias != '\0' && n == alias )
                    return *reg = i, true;
        // r8d, r8w, r8b and the like map to their 64-bit register.
        if ( n.length() >= 2 && n[0] == 'r' && qisdigit(n[1]) )
        {
            char *end = nullptr;
            unsigned long k = strtoul(n.c_str() + 1, &end, 10);
            if ( end != n.c_str() + 1 && k >= 8 && k <= 15
              && (*end == '\0' || ((*end == 'd' || *end == 'w' || *end == 'b') && end[1] == '\0')) )
                return *reg = (uint32_t)k, true;
        }
        if ( (n.length() == 4 || n.length() == 5) && (n.substr(0, 3) == "xmm" || n.substr(0, 3) == "ymm")
          && qisdigit(n[3]) )
        {
            char *end = nullptr;
            unsigned long k = strtoul(n.c_str() + 3, &end, 10);
            if ( *end == '\0' && k < 16 )
                return *reg = ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 + (uint32_t)k, true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    const char *origin_kind_name(OriginKind k)
    {
        switch ( k )
        {
            case OriginKind::Copied:    return "copied";
            case OriginKind::Computed:  return "computed";
            case OriginKind::Constant:  return "constant";
            case OriginKind::System:    return "system";
            case OriginKind::Unchanged: return "unchanged";
            case OriginKind::Cancelled: return "cancelled";
            default:                    return "failed";
        }
    }

    // origin_inputs, also reporting whether the user cancelled the search for
    // the memory read (which leaves 'out' missing that input).
    static bool collect_inputs(TraceManager *mgr, Position at, std::vector<OriginInput> *out,
                               bool *cancelled);

    // How many values (not address registers) the instruction at 'at' read;
    // 'only' gets the first.
    static int value_inputs(TraceManager *mgr, Position at, OriginTarget *only, bool *cancelled)
    {
        std::vector<OriginInput> inputs;
        if ( !collect_inputs(mgr, at, &inputs, cancelled) || *cancelled )
            return 0;
        int n = 0;
        for ( const OriginInput &in : inputs )
            if ( !in.address && n++ == 0 )
                *only = in.what;
        return n;
    }

    // 'syscalls' holds the recording's syscall list once something asked for
    // it; a caller tracing several values passes one cache to all of them, so
    // the list (a full replay) is made at most once.
    static bool trace_from(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position start, uint32_t start_tid,
                           size_t max_hops, bool through_computations, std::vector<OriginHop> *out,
                           SyscallCache &syscalls)
    {
        ITraceBackend *b = mgr->backend();
        OriginTarget target = what;
        Position     at     = start;
        uint32_t     tid    = start_tid;
        for ( size_t hop_no = 0; hop_no < max_hops; hop_no++ )
        {
            OriginHop hop;
            hop.what = target;
            hop.at   = at;
            hop.tid  = tid;
            {
                CursorPtr cur = b->make_cursor();
                if ( !cur || !cur->seek(at) )
                    return !out->empty();
                hop.value = read_value(cur.get(), target, tid);
            }

            Search s;
            qstring what_text;
            what_text.sprnt("Finding where %s came from", origin_target_text(target).c_str());
            QueryResult qr = run_query(what_text.c_str(), [&](ProgressSink *sink)
            {
                if ( target.is_reg )
                    search_register(b, target, at, tid, &s, sink);
                else
                    search_memory(b, target, at, hop.value, &syscalls, &s, sink);
                if ( !s.system )
                    find_reads(b, &s, sink);
                QueryResult r;
                r.ran = true;
                r.cancelled = sink != nullptr && sink->cancelled();
                return r;
            });
            if ( qr.cancelled )
            {
                hop.kind = OriginKind::Cancelled;
                out->push_back(hop);
                return true;
            }

            if ( !s.found )
            {
                hop.kind = OriginKind::Unchanged;
                if ( !target.is_reg )
                {
                    qstring mod = mgr->modules().name_at(target.addr);
                    hop.note = mod.empty()
                             ? qstring("nothing in the recording wrote it: it held this value from the start")
                             : qstring("nothing in the recording wrote it: part of ") + mod + "'s image";
                }
                else if ( s.stepped && s.looked >= kStepLookBack )
                    hop.note.sprnt("not changed in the last %llu instructions of this thread",
                                   (unsigned long long)s.looked);
                else if ( !s.stepped && s.looked != 0 )
                    hop.note = "not changed since the thread began, or within the last few million of its instructions";
                else
                    hop.note = "not changed since the thread began";
                out->push_back(hop);
                return true;
            }

            hop.by_pos = s.pos;
            hop.by_pc  = s.pc;
            hop.by_tid = s.tid;
            qstring line;
            if ( generate_disasm_line(&line, s.pc, GENDSM_REMOVE_TAGS | GENDSM_FORCE_CODE) )
            {
                line.trim2();
                hop.insn = line;
            }
            if ( s.system )
            {
                hop.kind = OriginKind::System;
                hop.note.sprnt("written by the system during %s", s.sys_name.c_str());
                out->push_back(hop);
                return true;
            }

            OriginTarget next;
            bool made_here = false;
            bool more = next_source(hop, s, &hop, &next, &made_here);
            // A computation from a single value (lea rax, [rdi+0Dh]; inc rdi;
            // add [mem], 2) is followed through it as if copied. Not through
            // rsp: a stack address's history is just the frames that moved it.
            if ( !more && made_here )
            {
                OriginTarget only;
                bool cancelled = false;
                const int n = through_computations ? value_inputs(mgr, s.pos, &only, &cancelled) : -1;
                if ( cancelled )
                {
                    hop.kind = OriginKind::Cancelled;
                    out->push_back(hop);
                    return true;
                }
                if ( n == 1 && only.is_reg && only.reg == ITTD_REG_RSP )
                {
                    hop.note = "computed from rsp: a stack address";
                }
                else if ( n == 1 )
                {
                    hop.note.sprnt("computed from %s", origin_target_text(only).c_str());
                    next = only;
                    more = true;
                }
                hop.combined = n >= 2 || n < 0;
            }
            out->push_back(hop);
            if ( !more )
                return true;
            // The next hop asks about the source just before the copy ran.
            // Stop rather than follow the same target at the same position.
            if ( same_target(next, target) && s.pos == at )
                return true;
            target = next;
            at     = s.pos;
            tid    = s.tid;
        }
        return true;
    }

    // A session to trace in, on a recording whose backend can list the reads
    // each hop is found from (reads_at).
    static bool session_ready(TraceManager *mgr)
    {
        return mgr != nullptr && mgr->is_active() && mgr->backend() != nullptr && mgr->cursor() != nullptr
            && mgr->backend()->capabilities().access_queries;
    }

    bool trace_value_origin(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, size_t max_hops,
                            std::vector<OriginHop> *out, bool through_computations)
    {
        out->clear();
        if ( !session_ready(mgr) )
            return false;
        SyscallCache syscalls;
        return trace_from(mgr, what, mgr->current_position(), mgr->cursor()->thread_id(), max_hops,
                          through_computations, out, syscalls);
    }

    // trace_value_origin at a position, with the caller's syscall cache.
    static bool trace_origin_at(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position at, size_t max_hops,
                                std::vector<OriginHop> *out, bool through_computations,
                                SyscallCache &syscalls)
    {
        out->clear();
        if ( !session_ready(mgr) )
            return false;
        CursorPtr cur = mgr->backend()->make_cursor();
        if ( !cur || !cur->seek(at) )
            return false;
        return trace_from(mgr, what, at, cur->thread_id(), max_hops, through_computations, out, syscalls);
    }

    bool trace_value_origin(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position at, size_t max_hops,
                            std::vector<OriginHop> *out, bool through_computations)
    {
        SyscallCache syscalls;
        return trace_origin_at(mgr, what, at, max_hops, out, through_computations, syscalls);
    }

    bool build_origin_graph(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position at, size_t max_nodes,
                            OriginGraph *out)
    {
        *out = OriginGraph();
        if ( !session_ready(mgr) )
            return false;

        struct Work
        {
            OriginTarget what;
            Position     at;
            int          from = -1;     // the node whose instruction read it
        };
        std::deque<Work> work;
        work.push_back(Work{ what, at, -1 });
        std::map<qstring, int> seen;    // "rax@3A:46", in effect -> node
        auto key = [](const OriginHop &h)
        {
            return origin_target_text(h.what) + qstring().sprnt("@%llX:%llX", h.at.hi, h.at.lo);
        };

        // One syscall list for every value the graph follows.
        SyscallCache syscalls;
        while ( !work.empty() )
        {
            if ( out->nodes.size() >= max_nodes )
            {
                out->truncated = true;
                break;
            }
            Work w = work.front();
            work.pop_front();
            std::vector<OriginHop> hops;
            if ( !trace_origin_at(mgr, w.what, w.at, max_nodes - out->nodes.size(), &hops, true, syscalls)
              || hops.empty() )
                continue;
            int prev = w.from;
            bool input = w.from >= 0;
            for ( OriginHop &h : hops )
            {
                if ( h.kind == OriginKind::Cancelled )
                {
                    out->cancelled = true;
                    return true;
                }
                const int idx = (int)out->nodes.size();
                auto [it, fresh] = seen.emplace(key(h), idx);
                if ( !fresh )
                {
                    if ( prev >= 0 )
                        out->edges.push_back(OriginGraph::Edge{ prev, it->second, input });
                    prev = -1;
                    break;
                }
                if ( prev >= 0 )
                    out->edges.push_back(OriginGraph::Edge{ prev, idx, input });
                out->nodes.push_back(std::move(h));
                prev  = idx;
                input = false;
            }
            if ( prev < 0 )
                continue;
            const OriginHop &end = out->nodes[prev];
            if ( !end.combined || !end.by_pos.is_valid() )
                continue;
            std::vector<OriginInput> inputs;
            bool cancelled = false;
            collect_inputs(mgr, end.by_pos, &inputs, &cancelled);
            if ( cancelled )
            {
                out->cancelled = true;
                return true;
            }
            for ( const OriginInput &in : inputs )
            {
                if ( in.address || (in.what.is_reg && in.what.reg == ITTD_REG_RSP) )
                    continue;
                work.push_back(Work{ in.what, end.by_pos, prev });
            }
        }
        if ( !work.empty() )
            out->truncated = true;
        return true;
    }

    bool origin_inputs(TraceManager *mgr, Position at, std::vector<OriginInput> *out)
    {
        bool cancelled = false;
        return collect_inputs(mgr, at, out, &cancelled);
    }

    static bool collect_inputs(TraceManager *mgr, Position at, std::vector<OriginInput> *out,
                               bool *cancelled)
    {
        out->clear();
        *cancelled = false;
        if ( !session_ready(mgr) )
            return false;
        ITraceBackend *b = mgr->backend();
        CursorPtr cur = b->make_cursor();
        if ( !cur || !cur->seek(at) )
            return true;
        const ea_t     pc  = cur->program_counter();
        const uint32_t tid = cur->thread_id();
        insn_t ins;
        if ( decode_insn(&ins, pc) <= 0 || ins.itype == NN_syscall || ins.itype == NN_sysenter )
            return true;

        // Operands first, then address-only registers: a pointer is rarely the
        // value being chased.
        std::vector<OriginTarget> operands, addresses;
        auto has = [](const std::vector<OriginTarget> &v, const OriginTarget &t)
        {
            for ( const OriginTarget &x : v )
                if ( same_target(x, t) )
                    return true;
            return false;
        };
        auto add_reg = [&](int ida_reg, bool address)
        {
            const int r = ittd_reg_of(ida_reg);
            if ( r < 0 )
                return;
            OriginTarget t;
            t.reg = (uint32_t)r;
            if ( has(operands, t) || has(addresses, t) )
                return;
            (address ? addresses : operands).push_back(t);
        };

        const uint32 feature = ins.get_canon_feature(PH);
        const bool   lea     = ins.itype == NN_lea;
        bool   reads_memory = false;
        size_t memory_size  = 0;
        for ( int n = 0; n < UA_MAXOP && ins.ops[n].type != o_void; n++ )
        {
            const op_t &op = ins.ops[n];
            if ( op.type == o_reg )
            {
                if ( has_cf_use(feature, n) )
                    add_reg(op.reg, false);
                continue;
            }
            if ( !is_memory(op) )
                continue;
            if ( !lea && has_cf_use(feature, n) )
            {
                reads_memory = true;
                memory_size  = get_dtype_size(op.dtype);
            }
            // o_mem has no base: its phrase is not a register.
            if ( op.type != o_mem )
            {
                const int base = x86_base_reg(ins, op);
                if ( base != R_none )
                    add_reg(base, !lea);
            }
            const int index = x86_index_reg(ins, op);
            if ( index != R_none )
                add_reg(index, !lea);
        }
        // Implicit inputs the operands do not show.
        switch ( ins.itype )
        {
            case NN_mul: case NN_div: case NN_idiv:
                add_reg(R_ax, false);
                if ( ins.itype != NN_mul )
                    add_reg(R_dx, false);
                break;
            case NN_imul:
                if ( ins.ops[1].type == o_void )
                    add_reg(R_ax, false);
                break;
            case NN_cbw: case NN_cwde: case NN_cdqe: case NN_cwd: case NN_cdq: case NN_cqo:
                add_reg(R_ax, false);
                break;
            default:
                break;
        }

        // Memory comes from the recorded read; the operand's address is not
        // computed here.
        if ( reads_memory )
        {
            Search s;
            QueryResult qr = run_query("Finding what the instruction read", [&](ProgressSink *sink)
            {
                reads_at(b, at, pc, &s.reads, sink);
                QueryResult r;
                r.ran = true;
                return r;
            });
            *cancelled = qr.cancelled;
            const Access *rd = qr.cancelled ? nullptr : pick_read(s, memory_size);
            if ( rd != nullptr )
            {
                OriginTarget t;
                t.is_reg = false;
                t.addr   = rd->addr;
                t.size   = rd->size != 0 ? rd->size : 8;
                operands.insert(operands.begin(), t);
            }
        }

        for ( int pass = 0; pass < 2; pass++ )
            for ( const OriginTarget &t : pass == 0 ? operands : addresses )
            {
                OriginInput in;
                in.what    = t;
                in.value   = read_value(cur.get(), t, tid);
                in.address = pass == 1;
                out->push_back(in);
            }
        return true;
    }
}
```

`src/analysis/origin.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/position.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class TraceManager;

    // Where a value came from: the current rax, or the bytes at an address.
    //
    // Each hop finds the instruction that last set a register or wrote memory
    // before a position. When it only moved the value (mov, push or pop, a
    // string move, an SSE load or store), the next hop asks the same of its
    // source as it stood just before. The chain ends at a computation, at the
    // system (a syscall's result, or memory it wrote), at a constant in the
    // code, or where nothing in the recording changed the value.
    //
    // A computation from one value (lea rax, [rdi+0Dh]; inc rdi) is followed
    // through that value. One from several ends the chain; each value it read
    // (origin_inputs) starts a chain of its own, from just before it ran.

    // A register or a range of memory, as of some position.
    struct OriginTarget
    {
        bool     is_reg = true;
        uint32_t reg  = 0;              // ITTD_REG_*, or ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 + n
        ea_t     addr = BADADDR;        // memory
        uint32_t size = 8;
    };
    qstring origin_target_text(const OriginTarget &t);   // "rax", "xmm0", "[0x1234], 8 bytes"
    // A value read back: "0x1234" up to 8 bytes, hex bytes above.
    qstring origin_value_text(const bytevec_t &v);
    // "rax", "eax" (as rax), "xmm3", "r12"; false for anything else.
    bool parse_register(const char *name, uint32_t *reg);

    enum class OriginKind
    {
        Copied,         // moved from somewhere else: the next hop follows it
        Computed,       // an instruction made the value: the chain ends there
        Constant,       // an immediate in the code
        System,         // a syscall's result, or memory the system wrote
        Unchanged,      // nothing in the searched span changed it
        Failed,
        Cancelled,
    };
    const char *origin_kind_name(OriginKind k);

    struct OriginHop
    {
        OriginTarget what;
        Position     at;                // the value asked about is as of here
        uint32_t     tid = 0;
        bytevec_t    value;             // its bytes there

        OriginKind   kind = OriginKind::Failed;
        Position     by_pos;            // the instruction that set it, before it ran
        ea_t         by_pc = BADADDR;
        uint32_t     by_tid = 0;
        qstring      insn;              // that instruction's disassembly
        qstring      note;              // in words: "copied from rsi", "written by NtReadFile"
        // The instruction combined several values: the chain ends here and
        // continues from origin_inputs(by_pos).
        bool         combined = false;
    };

    // Follow 'what' back from the playhead, at most 'max_hops' hops, each
    // search behind a cancellable wait box. False when there is no session.
    // 'through_computations' false stops at every computation, even of a
    // single value.
    bool trace_value_origin(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, size_t max_hops,
                            std::vector<OriginHop> *out, bool through_computations = true);
    // The same from 'at' instead of the playhead, on the thread running there.
    bool trace_value_origin(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position at, size_t max_hops,
                            std::vector<OriginHop> *out, bool through_computations = true);

    // A value an instruction read, as it stood just before the instruction ran.
    struct OriginInput
    {
        OriginTarget what;
        bytevec_t    value;
        bool         address = false;   // a register that only formed an address
    };
    // What the instruction about to run at 'at' read: its operand registers
    // and memory (including implicit ones of mul, div, cdq, ...), then the
    // registers that formed an address (for lea, its operands). Memory is the
    // read the recording has. Empty for a syscall, an instruction that reads
    // nothing, or one that cannot be decoded. False when there is no session.
    bool origin_inputs(TraceManager *mgr, Position at, std::vector<OriginInput> *out);

    // Every chain at once, breadth first up to 'max_nodes' hops: from 'what'
    // as of 'at', and from each value read by an instruction that combined
    // several (address-only registers and the stack pointer left out). The
    // same register or memory at the same position is one node.
    struct OriginGraph
    {
        std::vector<OriginHop> nodes;   // [0] is the value asked about
        struct Edge
        {
            int  from = -1;             // the hop that used the value...
            int  to   = -1;             // ...and the hop that set it
            bool input = false;         // one of several the instruction read
        };
        std::vector<Edge> edges;
        bool truncated = false;         // inputs left unfollowed at the limit
        bool cancelled = false;
    };
    bool build_origin_graph(TraceManager *mgr, const OriginTarget &what, Position at, size_t max_nodes,
                            OriginGraph *out);
}
```

`src/analysis/query_runner.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "analysis/query_runner.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"
#include "core/diag.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"
#include "ui/query_view.h"

#include <psapi.h>     // K32EnumProcessModules: kernel32, no psapi.lib

namespace idattd
{
    // How often the main thread looks at the worker and repaints the wait box.
    static const int POLL_MS = 100;

    namespace
    {
        // Python's GIL, released while run_query sleeps. A script that runs a
        // query (ttd() from IDAPython, an MCP server's Python) holds it on this
        // thread for the whole call, so anything else needing Python waited
        // for the UI to run Python code (a click): a sub-second query once took
        // 108 minutes. Looked up at run time, since IDA without IDAPython has
        // no python3*.dll.
        class PythonGil
        {
        public:
            PythonGil()
            {
                // Grown until every module fits: IDA with its plugins and Qt
                // loads hundreds, and Python may come late.
                std::vector<HMODULE> mods(512);
                DWORD need = 0;
                for ( ;; )
                {
                    const DWORD have = DWORD(mods.size() * sizeof(HMODULE));
                    if ( !K32EnumProcessModules(GetCurrentProcess(), mods.data(), have, &need) )
                        return;
                    if ( need <= have )
                        break;
                    mods.resize(need / sizeof(HMODULE) + 32);
                }
                size_t n = need / sizeof(HMODULE);
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < n && m_save == nullptr; i++ )
                {
                    char name[MAX_PATH];
                    if ( K32GetModuleBaseNameA(GetCurrentProcess(), mods[i], name, sizeof(name)) == 0
                      || _strnicmp(name, "python3", 7) != 0 )
                        continue;
                    auto ready   = (int (*)())GetProcAddress(mods[i], "Py_IsInitialized");
                    auto held    = (int (*)())GetProcAddress(mods[i], "PyGILState_Check");
                    auto save    = (void *(*)())GetProcAddress(mods[i], "PyEval_SaveThread");
                    auto restore = (void (*)(void *))GetProcAddress(mods[i], "PyEval_RestoreThread");
                    if ( ready != nullptr && held != nullptr && save != nullptr && restore != nullptr )
                    {
                        m_ready   = ready;
                        m_held    = held;
                        m_save    = save;
                        m_restore = restore;
                    }
                }
            }

            // The thread state to give back to resume(), or nullptr when
            // this thread did not hold the GIL.
            void *release() const
            {
                if ( m_save == nullptr || m_ready() == 0 || m_held() == 0 )
                    return nullptr;
                return m_save();
            }
            void resume(void *state) const
            {
                if ( state != nullptr )
                    m_restore(state);
            }

        private:
            int   (*m_ready)()          = nullptr;
            int   (*m_held)()           = nullptr;
            void *(*m_save)()           = nullptr;
            void  (*m_restore)(void *)  = nullptr;
        };

        // The reported percentage and the main thread's Cancel, as atomics:
        // safe from any thread.
        class AtomicSink : public ProgressSink
        {
        public:
            void report(uint32_t percent) override { m_pct.store(percent, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
            bool cancelled() override
            {
                // Paused: the thread asking (the emulator's, which asks
                // between two checkpoint intervals) waits here until Resume
                // or a stop, so the program stands still. It runs no IDA
                // code, so holding it blocks nothing on the main thread.
                if ( m_pause.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) )
                {
                    m_holding.fetch_add(1);
                    while ( m_pause.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) && !m_cancel.load(std::memory_order_relaxed) )
                        std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(20));
                    m_holding.fetch_sub(1);
                }
                return m_cancel.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
            }

            uint32_t percent() const { return m_pct.load(std::memory_order_relaxed); }
            void     cancel() { m_cancel.store(true, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
            void     pause(bool on) { m_pause.store(on, std::memory_order_relaxed); }
            // A thread is held by the pause (it has taken effect).
            bool     holding() const { return m_holding.load() > 0; }

        private:
            std::atomic<uint32_t> m_pct{ 0 };
            std::atomic<bool>     m_cancel{ false };
            std::atomic<bool>     m_pause{ false };
            std::atomic<int>      m_holding{ 0 };
        };
    }

    // Main-thread state only: run_query and movements both run there.
    static bool g_queryRunning = false;
    static bool g_traceMoving  = false;
    // The running query's sink and completion flag, for stop_running_query.
    // They live on run_query's stack and are set only while it waits.
    static AtomicSink        *g_runningSink = nullptr;
    static std::atomic<bool> *g_runningDone = nullptr;
    static bool               g_runningStopped = false;

    static const PythonGil &python_gil()
    {
        static const PythonGil gil;
        return gil;
    }

    void set_trace_moving(bool moving)
    {
        g_traceMoving = moving;
    }

    bool query_in_progress()
    {
        return g_queryRunning;
    }

    QueryResult run_query(const char *what, const std::function<QueryResult(ProgressSink *)> &query,
                          bool cancellable, const QueryShow *show)
    {
        DiagTimer diag_timer("query", qstring(what));

        // The wait loop below pumps the UI and releases the GIL, so a UI
        // action, a script's ttd() call or an execute_sync request can start
        // another query (or one can start during a movement's wait box) while
        // the backend is busy. A backend is not built to be driven by two
        // replays at once, so the nested one is refused without calling it,
        // reported as not run and cancelled so callers keep nothing from it.
        if ( g_queryRunning || g_traceMoving )
        {
            msg("[ida-ttd] %s: not started, %s.\n", what,
                g_queryRunning ? "another trace query is running"
                               : "a movement through the recording is in progress");
            QueryResult refused;
            refused.cancelled = true;
            return refused;
        }
        const PythonGil &gil = python_gil();
        AtomicSink sink;
        QueryResult result;
        std::atomic<bool> done{ false };

        // Declared after the sink and flag it publishes, so it is destroyed
        // (and stops publishing them) first.
        struct RunningFlag
        {
            RunningFlag(AtomicSink *s, std::atomic<bool> *d)
            {
                g_queryRunning   = true;
                g_runningSink    = s;
                g_runningDone    = d;
                g_runningStopped = false;
            }
            ~RunningFlag()
            {
                g_queryRunning = false;
                g_runningSink  = nullptr;
                g_runningDone  = nullptr;
            }
        } running(&sink, &done);

        std::thread worker([&]()
        {
            // 'done' is set on every exit path, or the main thread would spin
            // forever behind the wait box.
            try
            {
                result = query(&sink);
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
                result = QueryResult{};
            }
            done.store(true, std::memory_order_release);
        });

        // The wait box, or the recording window (ui/query_view.h), and what
        // the user asks of it, passed to the worker through the sink.
        QueryProgressView view(what, cancellable, show);
        bool cancelled = false;
        while ( !done.load(std::memory_order_acquire) )
        {
            switch ( view.poll(sink.percent(), sink.holding()) )
            {
                case QueryProgressView::ASK_STOP:
                    cancelled = true;
                    sink.cancel();
                    break;
                case QueryProgressView::ASK_PAUSE:
                    sink.pause(true);
                    break;
                case QueryProgressView::ASK_RESUME:
                    sink.pause(false);
                    break;
                default:
                    break;
            }
            flush_backend_log();
            void *py = gil.release();
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(POLL_MS));
            gil.resume(py);
        }
        worker.join();
        flush_backend_log();
        view.close();
        // Stopped because the session ended under it: whatever the worker
        // got is from a backend that is gone, so callers must keep nothing.
        if ( g_runningStopped )
        {
            result.ran           = false;
            result.session_ended = true;
            cancelled            = true;
        }
        if ( cancelled )
            result.cancelled = true;
        return result;
    }

    void stop_running_query()
    {
        if ( !g_queryRunning || g_runningSink == nullptr || g_runningDone == nullptr )
            return;
        // This runs nested inside run_query's wait loop (the session ended
        // from a UI action, a script or an execute_sync request it pumped).
        // The worker never calls IDA or Python, so blocking the main thread
        // until it returns cannot deadlock; a query that cannot stop
        // part-way (preparing the recording) is simply waited for.
        msg("[ida-ttd] the session is ending: stopping the running trace query.\n");
        g_runningStopped = true;
        g_runningSink->cancel();
        const PythonGil &gil = python_gil();
        while ( !g_runningDone->load(std::memory_order_acquire) )
        {
            flush_backend_log();
            void *py = gil.release();
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(10));
            gil.resume(py);
        }
    }

    // Visible top-level windows of the calling thread. Called only on the main
    // thread for its own windows; asking about another thread's would send
    // cross-thread messages.
    static int visible_thread_windows()
    {
        int n = 0;
        EnumThreadWindows(GetCurrentThreadId(), [](HWND h, LPARAM p) -> BOOL
        {
            if ( IsWindowVisible(h) )
                ++*reinterpret_cast<int *>(p);
            return TRUE;
        }, reinterpret_cast<LPARAM>(&n));
        return n;
    }

    void show_wait_box_now(const char *text)
    {
        const int before = visible_thread_windows();
        show_wait_box("%s", text);
        const ULONGLONG until = GetTickCount64() + 2000;
        while ( visible_thread_windows() <= before && GetTickCount64() < until )
        {
            user_cancelled();       // runs the message loop
            std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(15));
        }
        repaint_wait_box();
    }

    void repaint_wait_box()
    {
        for ( int i = 0; i < 3; i++ )
            user_cancelled();
    }

    bool prepare_backend(ITraceBackend *backend)
    {
        if ( backend == nullptr )
            return false;
        if ( backend->prepared() )
            return true;
        bool ok = false;
        run_query("Preparing the recording", [&](ProgressSink *p)
        {
            ok = backend->prepare(p);
            QueryResult r;
            r.ran = true;
            return r;
        }, false);
        return ok;
    }

    WaitBoxSink::WaitBoxSink(const char *what) : m_what(what)
    {
        show_wait_box("%s (Cancel to stop)...", m_what.c_str());
    }

    WaitBoxSink::~WaitBoxSink()
    {
        hide_wait_box();
    }

    void WaitBoxSink::report(uint32_t percent)
    {
        if ( percent != m_shown )
        {
            replace_wait_box("%s (Cancel to stop)... %u%%", m_what.c_str(), percent);
            m_shown = percent;
        }
    }

    bool WaitBoxSink::cancelled()
    {
        return user_cancelled();
    }

    qstring query_error(TraceManager *mgr, ITraceBackend *backend, const QueryResult &qr,
                        const char *ended, const char *fallback)
    {
        if ( qr.session_ended || mgr == nullptr || !mgr->is_active() || backend == nullptr )
            return qstring(ended);
        qstring why = !qr.error.empty() ? qr.error : backend->last_error();
        if ( why.empty() )
            why = fallback;
        return why;
    }
}
```

`src/analysis/query_runner.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class TraceManager;

    // Run a whole-trace query behind a cancellable wait box.
    //
    // 'query' runs on a worker thread (a query can take minutes, and on the
    // main thread it would block repaints and Cancel). The main thread owns
    // the wait box, shows the percentage reported through the ProgressSink
    // and passes Cancel back through it. The sink only touches atomics, so a
    // backend may call it from any thread, including the engine's replay
    // threads. The query itself must not call IDA.
    //
    // 'what' is the wait-box line without punctuation or percentage, e.g.
    // "Measuring execution coverage".
    //
    // 'cancellable' false hides Cancel, for work that cannot stop part-way
    // (building Microsoft's memory index).
    //
    // One query at a time: the wait loop pumps the UI, so another query can
    // be asked for while one runs, or while a movement's wait box is up. Such
    // a query is refused without calling the backend (a message says why) and
    // comes back with 'ran' false and 'cancelled' true.
    //
    // 'show', when given, adds lines under that one while the work runs.
    // What is shown, and how, is ui/query_view.h's.
    // With log lines, and IDAPython's Qt to show it, a recording window
    // takes the wait box's place: the whole log in a scrolling box, the
    // running time, and Stop (ending the work as Cancel would) and Pause
    // buttons instead of Cancel.
    struct QueryShow
    {
        bool        elapsed   = false;   // "Running for 1 min 05 s"
        size_t      log_lines = 0;       // the emulator log's last lines (emulator_log_tail)
        const char *title     = nullptr; // the window's title; nullptr: 'what'
        // Pause holds the thread that asks whether to cancel until Resume,
        // which for a recording is the emulator's, between two checkpoint
        // intervals.
        bool        pausable  = false;
    };
    QueryResult run_query(const char *what, const std::function<QueryResult(ProgressSink *)> &query,
                          bool cancellable = true, const QueryShow *show = nullptr);

    // Why a query on 'backend' did not run: the reason the query captured as
    // it failed (QueryResult::error), else the backend's last error. The
    // session can end during it (the wait box pumps the UI) and close the
    // backend, whose last error is then not this query's and must not be
    // read: 'ended' is said instead. Never empty: 'fallback' when the backend
    // gave no reason.
    qstring query_error(TraceManager *mgr, ITraceBackend *backend, const QueryResult &qr,
                        const char *ended, const char *fallback);

    // A query is running (run_query is waiting for it).
    bool query_in_progress();
    // Cancel the running query, if any, and block until its worker returns:
    // for the session's end, which can run nested inside run_query's wait
    // loop and must not close the backend under the worker. That run_query
    // then reports the query as not run and cancelled.
    void stop_running_query();
    // TraceManager marks a movement through the recording, during which
    // run_query refuses to start.
    void set_trace_moving(bool moving);

    // One stage of a multi-call query: the stage's 0..100 maps onto [lo, hi]
    // of the whole, so the bar does not restart per call. Cancel passes
    // straight through.
    class StageSink : public ProgressSink
    {
    public:
        StageSink(ProgressSink *outer, uint32_t lo, uint32_t hi)
            : m_outer(outer), m_lo(lo), m_hi(hi) {}
        void report(uint32_t percent) override
        {
            if ( m_outer != nullptr )
                m_outer->report(m_lo + (m_hi - m_lo) * std::min<uint32_t>(percent, 100) / 100);
        }
        bool cancelled() override { return m_outer != nullptr && m_outer->cancelled(); }

    private:
        ProgressSink *m_outer;
        uint32_t      m_lo;
        uint32_t      m_hi;
    };

    // show_wait_box() for work that then blocks the UI thread without pumping
    // it (applying a PDB). IDA shows a wait box only after a grace delay and
    // while its message loop runs, so this pumps until the box is on screen
    // (two seconds at most). 'text' is show_wait_box's, prefixes included.
    void show_wait_box_now(const char *text);
    // Let a box already shown repaint after replace_wait_box().
    void repaint_wait_box();

    // Prepare the open recording (ITraceBackend::prepare) behind a wait box,
    // unless it already is. True when it is prepared afterwards.
    bool prepare_backend(ITraceBackend *backend);

    // A sink for work on the main thread (a movement), which can show IDA's
    // wait box itself. The box appears only after IDA's grace delay; Cancel
    // is user_cancelled().
    class WaitBoxSink : public ProgressSink
    {
    public:
        explicit WaitBoxSink(const char *what);
        ~WaitBoxSink() override;
        void report(uint32_t percent) override;
        bool cancelled() override;

    private:
        qstring  m_what;
        uint32_t m_shown = 101;
    };
}
```

`src/analysis/replay_scans.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "analysis/replay_scans.h"
#include "analysis/query_runner.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"
#include "plugin/settings.h"

namespace idattd
{
    static const char SCAN_REGKEY[] = "ida-ttd";

    qstring saved_registry_dir()
    {
        qstring s;
        reg_read_string(&s, "ForkRegistryDir", SCAN_REGKEY);
        return s;
    }

    void save_registry_dir(const char *dir)
    {
        reg_write_string("ForkRegistryDir", dir != nullptr ? dir : "", SCAN_REGKEY);
    }

    static void add_candidate(qstrvec_t *v, qstring dir)
    {
        while ( dir.length() > 3 && (dir.last() == '\\' || dir.last() == '/') )
            dir.remove_last();
        if ( dir.empty() )
            return;
        for ( const qstring &d : *v )
            if ( stricmp(d.c_str(), dir.c_str()) == 0 )
                return;
        v->push_back(dir);
    }

    // Per recording, for this session only: a root belongs to the machine
    // viewing the recording, and rarely moves.
    static std::map<qstring, qstring> g_roots;

    qstring chosen_emulation_root(TraceManager *mgr)
    {
        if ( mgr == nullptr )
            return qstring();
        auto it = g_roots.find(mgr->trace_path());
        return it != g_roots.end() ? it->second : qstring();
    }

    void choose_emulation_root(TraceManager *mgr, const char *dir)
    {
        if ( mgr != nullptr )
            g_roots[mgr->trace_path()] = dir != nullptr ? dir : "";
    }

    static bool get_env(TraceManager *mgr, ReplayEnv *env)
    {
        return mgr != nullptr && mgr->backend() != nullptr && mgr->backend()->replay_env(env);
    }

    qstrvec_t registry_candidates(TraceManager *mgr)
    {
        qstrvec_t v;
        ReplayEnv env;
        if ( get_env(mgr, &env) && !env.host )
        {
            qstring root = chosen_emulation_root(mgr);
            if ( root.empty() )
            {
                add_candidate(&v, env.registry_hint);
            }
            else
            {
                root.append("\\registry");
                add_candidate(&v, root);
            }
            return v;
        }
        add_candidate(&v, saved_registry_dir());
        if ( mgr != nullptr )
        {
            qstring beside = mgr->trace_path();
            ssize_t slash = beside.rfind('\\');
            if ( slash >= 0 )
            {
                beside.resize((size_t)slash);
                beside.append("\\registry");
                add_candidate(&v, beside);
            }
        }
        add_candidate(&v, settings().registry_folder);     // the registry_folder setting
        add_candidate(&v, user_data_dir("registry"));
        return v;
    }

    qstring find_registry_dir(TraceManager *mgr)
    {
        ITraceBackend *b = mgr != nullptr ? mgr->backend() : nullptr;
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return saved_registry_dir();
        ReplayEnv env;
        const bool known = get_env(mgr, &env);
        if ( known && !env.host )
            return qstring();
        qstring unverified, mismatch;
        for ( const qstring &dir : registry_candidates(mgr) )
        {
            switch ( b->check_registry(dir.c_str(), nullptr) )
            {
                case HiveCheck::Match:
                    return dir;
                case HiveCheck::Unverified:
                    if ( unverified.empty() )
                        unverified = dir;
                    break;
                case HiveCheck::Mismatch:
                    if ( mismatch.empty() )
                        mismatch = dir;
                    break;
                case HiveCheck::Missing:
                    break;
            }
        }
        // A recording carrying its hives replays without files; only its own
        // hives would add anything (a fork reading further than it did).
        if ( known && env.registry_carried )
            return qstring();
        return !unverified.empty() ? unverified : mismatch;
    }

    static ITraceBackend *scanning_backend(TraceManager *mgr, qstring *error)
    {
        if ( mgr == nullptr || !mgr->is_active() || mgr->backend() == nullptr )
        {
            *error = "no recording is being replayed";
            return nullptr;
        }
        if ( !mgr->backend()->capabilities().replay_scans )
        {
            *error = "this recording's backend cannot replay it with a scanner";
            return nullptr;
        }
        return mgr->backend();
    }

    // Why a replay did not run (query_error).
    static qstring replay_error(TraceManager *mgr, ITraceBackend *backend, const QueryResult &qr)
    {
        return query_error(mgr, backend, qr, "the replay session ended during the replay",
                           "the replay did not run");
    }

    bool recover_strings(TraceManager *mgr, const ReplaySettings &settings, uint32_t min_length,
                         std::vector<StringHit> *out, bool *cancelled, qstring *error)
    {
        out->clear();
        *cancelled = false;
        error->clear();
        ITraceBackend *backend = scanning_backend(mgr, error);
        if ( backend == nullptr )
            return false;
        QueryResult qr = run_query("Replaying the recording to recover its strings", [&](ProgressSink *p)
        {
            return backend->query_strings(settings, min_length, out, p);
        });
        *cancelled = qr.cancelled;
        if ( !qr.ran )
            *error = replay_error(mgr, backend, qr);
        return qr.ran;
    }

    bool recover_buffers(TraceManager *mgr, const ReplaySettings &settings,
                         std::vector<BufferHit> *out, bool *cancelled, qstring *error)
    {
        out->clear();
        *cancelled = false;
        error->clear();
        ITraceBackend *backend = scanning_backend(mgr, error);
        if ( backend == nullptr )
            return false;
        QueryResult qr = run_query("Replaying the recording to recover the buffers it filled", [&](ProgressSink *p)
        {
            return backend->query_buffers(settings, out, p);
        });
        *cancelled = qr.cancelled;
        if ( !qr.ran )
            *error = replay_error(mgr, backend, qr);
        return qr.ran;
    }
}
```

`src/analysis/replay_scans.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class TraceManager;

    // Recovering what the program had in memory by replaying the whole
    // recording with a scanner (capabilities().replay_scans: Sogen re-executes
    // it, Microsoft TTD replays it with write watchpoints). Each costs a full
    // replay behind a cancellable wait box; the backend keeps the answer for
    // the session.
    //
    // False when it did not run; 'error' says why when the backend does.

    bool recover_strings(TraceManager *mgr, const ReplaySettings &settings, uint32_t min_length,
                         std::vector<StringHit> *out, bool *cancelled, qstring *error);

    bool recover_buffers(TraceManager *mgr, const ReplaySettings &settings,
                         std::vector<BufferHit> *out, bool *cancelled, qstring *error);

    // The folder of registry hives the user last chose (shared by forks and
    // the scans); empty when none.
    qstring saved_registry_dir();
    void    save_registry_dir(const char *dir);

    // The emulation root for replaying a recording made in one: the folder
    // the user chose for this recording this session, or empty for the one
    // the recording names.
    qstring chosen_emulation_root(TraceManager *mgr);
    void    choose_emulation_root(TraceManager *mgr, const char *dir);

    // Where the open recording's hives may be, best first, without
    // duplicates. Made in an emulation root: only that root's registry
    // folder, which a replay loads. Made against the host: the folder the user
    // chose, a registry folder beside the recording (how one is shared with
    // its hives), the registry_folder setting, and $IDAUSR\ida-ttd\registry.
    qstrvec_t registry_candidates(TraceManager *mgr);

    // The registry folder to give a replay of the open recording: the first
    // candidate holding the recording's own hives. Otherwise, unless the
    // recording carries what it read of them, the first holding hives it
    // cannot vouch for, else the first holding other hives (the replay then
    // refuses, saying so); else empty. Always empty for a recording made in
    // an emulation root, whose replay loads the root's own. Checking reads
    // the hives, once per folder.
    qstring find_registry_dir(TraceManager *mgr);
}
```
