`src/backend-msttd/msttd_ida_shim.cpp`:

```cpp
// The IDA kernel functions the Microsoft backend reaches without meaning to.
//
// The backend uses the core's types (qstring, ea_t), whose inline code in
// pro.h calls into ida.dll for memory and formatting. A backend DLL must run
// without IDA (the probe loads it into a plain process), so it does not link
// ida.lib; these stand in, with the same contracts over the C runtime.
//
// Only what the link asks for is here. A new unresolved external from ida.dll
// means the backend started using something of IDA's it should not.

#include "common/pch.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>

idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qalloc(size_t size)
{
    return malloc(size != 0 ? size : 1);
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qrealloc(void *alloc, size_t newsize)
{
    return realloc(alloc, newsize != 0 ? newsize : 1);
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE void ida_export qfree(void *alloc)
{
    free(alloc);
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qcalloc(size_t nitems, size_t itemsize)
{
    return calloc(nitems != 0 ? nitems : 1, itemsize != 0 ? itemsize : 1);
}

// IDA declares the *_or_throw functions as not throwing, so an exception
// from here would end in std::terminate anyway; say why first.
[[noreturn]] static void out_of_memory()
{
    OutputDebugStringA("[ida-ttd] the Microsoft backend ran out of memory\n");
    abort();
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qalloc_or_throw(size_t size)
{
    void *p = qalloc(size);
    if ( p == nullptr )
        out_of_memory();
    return p;
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qrealloc_or_throw(void *ptr, size_t size)
{
    void *p = qrealloc(ptr, size);
    if ( p == nullptr )
        out_of_memory();
    return p;
}

// qvector<T> is { T *array; size_t n; size_t alloc; }. This grows its array
// to at least 'cnt' elements (reallocating 'old', or fresh when it is null),
// records the new capacity and returns the array. Growing by half again keeps
// push_back amortised, as IDA's does.
idaman THREAD_SAFE void *ida_export qvector_reserve(void *vec, void *old, size_t cnt, size_t elsize)
{
    struct layout { void *array; size_t n; size_t alloc; };
    layout *v = static_cast<layout *>(vec);
    size_t want = v->alloc + v->alloc / 2;
    if ( want < cnt )
        want = cnt;
    if ( want < 4 )
        want = 4;
    // A count whose byte size wraps would allocate a small block and let the
    // caller write past it; no allocation can satisfy it anyway.
    if ( elsize != 0 && want > SIZE_MAX / elsize )
    {
        if ( cnt > SIZE_MAX / elsize )
            out_of_memory();
        want = cnt;     // the half-again growth overflowed, the request did not
    }
    void *p =old != nullptr ? qrealloc_or_throw(old, want * elsize) : qalloc_or_throw(want * elsize);
    v->alloc = want;
    return p;
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE AS_PRINTF(3, 0) int ida_export qvsnprintf(char *buffer, size_t n, const char *format, va_list va)
{
    if ( buffer == nullptr || n == 0 )
        return vsnprintf(nullptr, 0, format, va);
    int r = vsnprintf(buffer, n, format, va);
    buffer[n - 1] = '\0';
    return r;
}

idaman THREAD_SAFE AS_PRINTF(3, 4) int ida_export qsnprintf(char *buffer, size_t n, const char *format, ...)
{
    va_list va;
    va_start(va, format);
    int r = qvsnprintf(buffer, n, format, va);
    va_end(va);
    return r;
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_memmap.cpp`:

```cpp
// The Microsoft backend's memory map, reconstructed from the syscalls that
// shape the address space, because the Replay SDK reports no protections and
// no region list. The syscalls come from the recording's kernel transitions
// (msttd_syscalls.h), so memory a program maps with its own syscalls is
// included. analysis/memmap.cpp holds the backend-independent model, fold,
// persistence and listing, and asks query_mapping_changes for the changes.
//
// Callbacks write plain memory only; Cancel and progress go through the
// ProgressSink, so nothing here touches IDA's UI.

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_syscalls.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_host.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_guest.h"
#include "common/symbols.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    // The syscalls that shape a process's address space, described as data.
    //
    // Every parameter of all five is a handle, a pointer or a ULONG, which is
    // what lets one uniform stack layout serve the x86 side: no parameter is
    // wider than a slot, so no argument after it is shifted.
    namespace
    {
        struct WatchDesc
        {
            const char *name;
            uint8_t     kind;
            size_t      nargs;
            int         iProc;    // ProcessHandle argument
            int         iBase;    // BaseAddress argument
            int         iSize;    // RegionSize argument, -1 when there is none
            int         iExtra;   // Protect, or FreeType, -1 when there is none
            bool        basePtr;  // BaseAddress is PVOID* rather than PVOID
            bool        deferred; // out-params the KERNEL writes, not the caller
        };

        // NtAllocateVirtualMemory(HANDLE, PVOID* Base, ULONG_PTR, PSIZE_T Size, ULONG, ULONG Protect)
        // NtProtectVirtualMemory (HANDLE, PVOID* Base, PSIZE_T Size, ULONG NewProtect, PULONG)
        // NtFreeVirtualMemory    (HANDLE, PVOID* Base, PSIZE_T Size, ULONG FreeType)
        // NtMapViewOfSection     (HANDLE Section, HANDLE Process, PVOID* Base, ULONG_PTR,
        //                         SIZE_T, PLARGE_INTEGER, PSIZE_T ViewSize, SECTION_INHERIT,
        //                         ULONG, ULONG Win32Protect)
        // NtUnmapViewOfSection   (HANDLE Process, PVOID Base)
        // NtAllocateVirtualMemoryEx(HANDLE, PVOID* Base, PSIZE_T Size, ULONG, ULONG Protect, ...)
        // NtMapViewOfSectionEx   (HANDLE Section, HANDLE Process, PVOID* Base, PLARGE_INTEGER,
        //                         PSIZE_T ViewSize, ULONG, ULONG Protect, ...)
        // NtUnmapViewOfSectionEx (HANDLE Process, PVOID Base, ULONG)
        //
        // The indexes are the syscall's own arguments, as the kernel takes them.
        //
        // 'deferred' marks those whose out-params the kernel fills in. A free's
        // are written by the caller before the call, so they are recorded and
        // need no recovery. Map's process handle is its second argument.
        static const WatchDesc kWatches[] =
        {
            { "NtAllocateVirtualMemory", ITTD_MAP_ALLOC,     6, 0, 1,  3,  5, true,  true  },
            { "NtProtectVirtualMemory",  ITTD_MAP_PROTECT,   5, 0, 1,  2,  3, true,  true  },
            { "NtFreeVirtualMemory",     ITTD_MAP_FREE,      4, 0, 1,  2,  3, true,  false },
            { "NtMapViewOfSection",      ITTD_MAP_MAPVIEW,  10, 1, 2,  6,  9, true,  true  },
            { "NtUnmapViewOfSection",    ITTD_MAP_UNMAPVIEW, 2, 0, 1, -1, -1, false, false },
            { "NtAllocateVirtualMemoryEx", ITTD_MAP_ALLOC,   7, 0, 1,  2,  4, true,  true  },
            { "NtMapViewOfSectionEx",    ITTD_MAP_MAPVIEW,   9, 1, 2,  4,  6, true,  true  },
            { "NtUnmapViewOfSectionEx",  ITTD_MAP_UNMAPVIEW, 3, 0, 1, -1, -1, false, false },
        };

        static const uint64_t PAGE = 0x1000;

        // These syscalls round the request to pages before writing it back, so
        // a value that is not page-granular did not come from the kernel. That,
        // not "non-zero", is the acceptance test: an aggressive query cannot
        // tell the kernel's write from the caller's own earlier store (only the
        // latter is recorded), and accepting the request would silently report
        // a region short by the kernel's rounding.
        static bool page_granular(uint64_t v) { return v != 0 && (v % PAGE) == 0; }
        static uint64_t page_floor(uint64_t v)   { return v - (v % PAGE); }
        static uint64_t page_ceiling(uint64_t v)
        {
            uint64_t r = v % PAGE;
            return r == 0 ? v : v + (PAGE - r);
        }

        // A pseudo-handle of -1 is NtCurrentProcess. Anything else names another
        // process, and the call changed that map rather than ours.
        static bool is_current_process(uint64_t h, bool is64)
        {
            uint64_t self = is64 ? 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull : 0xFFFFFFFFull;
            return h == self || h == 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFull;
        }

        // One captured call, before its out-params were resolved.
        struct Rec
        {
            const WatchDesc *d = nullptr;
            bool     is64 = false;
            uint32_t tid = 0;                // UniqueId, for SetPositionOnThread
            uint32_t os_tid = 0;             // the OS id, which is what the core reports
            ea_t     pc = BADADDR;
            ea_t     api = BADADDR;
            TtdPosition retPos;
            TtdPosition callPos;
            ea_t     chain[ITTD_CHAIN_MAX] = { 0 };
            uint8_t  chain_n = 0;
            uint64_t pBase = 0, pSize = 0;   // addresses of the out-param slots
            uint64_t base = 0, size = 0;     // resolved values
            uint32_t extra = 0;              // protection, or free type
            bool     baseOk = false, sizeOk = false;
            bool     otherProcess = false;
        };

        // An out-param not readable yet, retried as the replay rolls forward:
        // the value becomes visible once the guest reads it back.
        struct Retry
        {
            uint64_t addr = 0;
            uint32_t tid = 0;
            uint32_t width = 8;
            size_t   rec = 0;
            bool     isBase = true;
            int      attempts = 0;
            bool     live = false;
        };

        struct SweepState
        {
            std::vector<Rec> recs;

            std::vector<Retry> retries;
            std::map<uint32_t, std::vector<size_t>> byThread;
            size_t outstanding = 0;

            bool truncated = false;
        };

        // Hard cap: a recording that allocates in a loop can produce millions,
        // and a bad_alloc in a noexcept callback terminates the process.
        static const size_t kMaxRecs = 200000;     // the memory map's own storage cap
    }

    static bool read_ptr_policy(ICursorView const *c, uint64_t addr, uint32_t width,
                                QueryMemoryPolicy pol, uint64_t *out)
    {
        uint64_t tmp = 0;
        MemoryBuffer mb = c->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ addr },
                                               BufferView{ &tmp, width }, pol);
        if ( mb.Memory.Size != width )
            return false;
        *out = tmp;
        return true;
    }

    // Last resort for one out-param: replay the thread forward a bounded number
    // of steps with a Read watchpoint on the slot and take the value the guest
    // reads back, the only recorded trace of the kernel's write. 'cur' is the
    // caller's, reused across slots (a cursor per slot is not free, and there
    // can be hundreds of thousands); it is left with nothing armed. It must
    // not be one used for policy reads: a replayed cursor answers thread-locally.
    static bool recover_by_readback(ICursorView *cur, const TtdPosition &from,
                                    uint32_t tid, uint64_t addr, uint32_t width,
                                    uint64_t *out)
    {
        uint64_t found = 0;
        bool     got   = false;

        auto on_read = [&](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &,
                           IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
        {
            uint64_t v = 0;
            if ( msttd_read_word(t, addr, width, &v) && page_granular(v) )
            {
                found = v;
                got   = true;
                return true;        // accept the hit: this ends the replay
            }
            return false;
        };

        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ addr };
        wp.Size       = width;
        wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Read;
        // Confined to the calling thread, which is the one that reads the
        // out-param, so the step budget is not spent elsewhere.
        wp.ThreadId   = (UniqueThreadId)tid;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(cur, ReplayFlags::ReplayOnlyCurrentThread | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially,
                           EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            arm.watch(wp);
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_read);
            cur->SetPositionOnThread((UniqueThreadId)tid, from);
            cur->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, (StepCount)0x2000);
        }

        if ( got )
            *out = found;
        return got;
    }

    // What syscalls wrote through out parameters (ReplayAPI.md, "the
    // kernel-write gap"). The kernel's write is not recorded where it
    // happened; the value first appears at a DataMismatch or NewData on the
    // slot, or where the program reads it. Each slot is watched on its thread
    // from the call, for a bounded number of steps. A program write first
    // means the kernel's value never surfaced: unknown, not the stale one.
    // Each slot costs a seek, so they are shared between cursors
    // (msttd_parallel).
    bool MsTtdBackend::query_out_values(const std::vector<OutSlot> &slots,
                                        std::vector<std::optional<uint64_t>> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return false;
        out->assign(slots.size(), std::nullopt);
        // The slots in call order, so each worker's stretch is close together.
        std::vector<size_t> order(slots.size());
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < order.size(); i++ )
            order[i] = i;
        std::stable_sort(order.begin(), order.end(),
                         [&](size_t a, size_t b) { return slots[a].call < slots[b].call; });
        std::atomic<bool> made{ false };
        const bool complete = msttd_parallel(slots.size(), 8, progress,
            [&](size_t begin, size_t end, std::atomic<size_t> &done, const std::atomic<bool> &stop)
        {
            UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
            if ( !cur )
                return;
            made = true;

            for ( size_t n = begin; n < end && !stop.load(); n++, done++ )
            {
                const size_t i = order[n];
                const OutSlot &sl = slots[i];
                if ( sl.addr == 0 || (sl.width != 4 && sl.width != 8) )
                    continue;
                // The thread that made the call, not another that had its id.
                const uint32_t utid = unique_thread_id(sl.tid, sl.call);
                if ( utid == 0 )
                    continue;
                bool        got = false;
                uint64_t    value = 0;
                TtdPosition wrote = TtdPosition::Invalid;
                auto on_hit = [&](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
                {
                    const TtdPosition p = t->GetPosition();
                    // A write of the program's own, and nothing of the kernel's at
                    // the same position: the kernel's value is gone.
                    if ( wrote.IsValid() && !(p == wrote) )
                        return true;
                    uint64_t v = 0;
                    const bool ok = msttd_read_word(t, sl.addr, sl.width, &v);
                    switch ( w.AccessType )
                    {
                        case DataAccessType::DataMismatch:
                        case DataAccessType::NewData:
                        case DataAccessType::Read:
                            if ( ok )
                            {
                                value = v;
                                got = true;
                            }
                            return true;
                        case DataAccessType::Write:
                        case DataAccessType::Overwrite:
                            wrote = p;
                            return false;
                        default:
                            return false;
                    }
                };
                MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
                wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)sl.addr };
                wp.Size       = sl.width;
                wp.AccessMask = (DataAccessMask)((uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Read | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Write
                                               | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Overwrite | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::DataMismatch
                                               | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::NewData);
                wp.ThreadId   = (UniqueThreadId)utid;
                {
                    ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplayOnlyCurrentThread
                                            | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially,
                                   EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
                    arm.watch(wp);
                    arm.on_watchpoint(on_hit);
                    cur->SetPositionOnThread((UniqueThreadId)utid, from_core(sl.call));
                    cur->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, (StepCount)0x4000);
                }
                if ( got )
                    (*out)[i] = value;
            }
        });
        // Cancelled, no answer is given: the slots not reached would read
        // as searched and not found. The callers check their own Cancel
        // before they fall back to anything.
        if ( !complete )
            return false;
        return slots.empty() || made.load();
    }

    // What the census replay settled for the map (see SyscallCensus).
    struct MemmapRecords
    {
        std::vector<Rec> recs;
        bool truncated = false;
    };

    std::shared_ptr<const MemmapRecords> empty_memmap_records()
    {
        return std::make_shared<MemmapRecords>();
    }

    namespace
    {
        // The census callbacks that settle each memory syscall. Everything
        // here runs on the replay thread, noexcept.
        class MemmapHooksImpl : public MemmapHooks
        {
        public:
            MemmapHooksImpl(const MsTtdBackend *backend, std::map<uint32_t, const WatchDesc *> by_number)
                : m_is64(backend->is64()), m_byNumber(std::move(by_number)) {}

            void arm(KernelCallOptions *opts) override
            {
                // One replay with the call/return callback, which both the
                // chains and the settling need.
                opts->args_wanted = [this](uint32_t n) { return desc_of(n) != nullptr; };
                opts->chains      = true;
                opts->on_syscall  = [this](const KernelCall &k, IThreadView const *t) noexcept { on_syscall(k, t); };
                opts->on_call_ret = [this](IThreadView const *t, uint32_t utid, bool is_return, uint64_t target) noexcept
                {
                    on_call_ret(t, utid, is_return, target);
                };
            }

            std::shared_ptr<const MemmapRecords> finish() override
            {
                auto r = std::make_shared<MemmapRecords>();
                r->recs      = std::move(m_st.recs);
                r->truncated = m_st.truncated;
                m_st = SweepState{};
                m_outNow.clear();
                return r;
            }

        private:
            const WatchDesc *desc_of(uint32_t n) const
            {
                auto it = m_byNumber.find(n);
                return it != m_byNumber.end() ? it->second : nullptr;
            }

            void retire(size_t idx) noexcept
            {
                if ( !m_st.retries[idx].live )
                    return;
                m_st.retries[idx].live = false;
                if ( m_st.outstanding != 0 )
                    m_st.outstanding--;
            }

            void add_retry(uint64_t addr, uint32_t tid, uint32_t width, size_t rec, bool isBase) noexcept
            {
                try
                {
                    // A wrapper reuses one stack local for every call, so an
                    // older retry on this slot would pick up a newer call's
                    // value. Retire it: a missing region is a gap, a wrong
                    // one silently displaces a real region.
                    auto it = m_st.byThread.find(tid);
                    if ( it != m_st.byThread.end() )
                    {
                        for ( size_t i : it->second )
                            if ( m_st.retries[i].live && m_st.retries[i].addr == addr )
                                retire(i);
                    }
                    Retry retry;
                    retry.addr     = addr;
                    retry.tid      = tid;
                    retry.width    = width;
                    retry.rec      = rec;
                    retry.isBase   = isBase;
                    retry.attempts = 256;
                    retry.live     = true;
                    m_st.retries.push_back(retry);
                    m_st.byThread[tid].push_back(m_st.retries.size() - 1);
                    m_st.outstanding++;
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    m_st.truncated = true;
                }
            }

            // A kernel-written out-param is often not recorded when the
            // syscall returns, only once the program reads it back, so each
            // later call and return on the same thread looks again.
            void poll_retries(IThreadView const *t, uint32_t tid) noexcept
            {
                if ( m_st.outstanding == 0 )
                    return;
                auto it = m_st.byThread.find(tid);
                if ( it == m_st.byThread.end() )
                    return;
                for ( size_t i : it->second )
                {
                    Retry &retry = m_st.retries[i];
                    if ( !retry.live )
                        continue;
                    uint64_t v = 0;
                    if ( msttd_read_word(t, retry.addr, retry.width, &v) && page_granular(v) )
                    {
                        Rec &rec = m_st.recs[retry.rec];
                        if ( retry.isBase ) { rec.base = v; rec.baseOk = true; }
                        else                { rec.size = v; rec.sizeOk = true; }
                        retire(i);
                    }
                    else if ( --retry.attempts <= 0 )
                    {
                        // Past a few hundred callbacks the slot may belong to
                        // something else entirely. Hand it to the slower routes.
                        retire(i);
                    }
                }
                // Drop the settled ones: this runs on every call and return,
                // and would otherwise walk all of a thread's past retries
                // each time.
                std::vector<size_t> &mine = it->second;
                mine.erase(std::remove_if(mine.begin(), mine.end(),
                                          [this](size_t i) { return !m_st.retries[i].live; }),
                           mine.end());
            }

            void on_syscall(const KernelCall &k, IThreadView const *) noexcept
            {
                try
                {
                    if ( desc_of(k.number) != nullptr )
                        m_outNow[k.utid].push_back(k);
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    m_st.truncated = true;
                }
            }

            void settle(const KernelCall &k, IThreadView const *t) noexcept
            {
                try
                {
                    const WatchDesc *d = desc_of(k.number);
                    if ( d == nullptr )
                        return;
                    // NTSTATUS: anything negative failed, and a failed call
                    // changed nothing.
                    if ( (int32_t)(uint32_t)t->GetBasicReturnValue() < 0 )
                        return;
                    if ( m_st.recs.size() >= kMaxRecs )
                    {
                        m_st.truncated = true;
                        return;
                    }
                    const bool is64 = m_is64;
                    const uint32_t width = is64 ? 8 : 4;
                    const uint64_t mask = is64 ? ~0ull : 0xFFFFFFFFull;

                    Rec rec;
                    rec.d       = d;
                    rec.is64    = is64;
                    rec.tid     = k.utid;
                    rec.os_tid  = k.tid;
                    rec.pc      = k.chain_n != 0 ? k.chain[0] : k.pc;
                    rec.api     = k.stub != BADADDR ? k.stub : k.pc;
                    rec.retPos  = t->GetPosition();
                    rec.callPos = k.pos;
                    rec.chain_n = k.chain_n;
                    for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < k.chain_n; i++ )
                        rec.chain[i] = k.chain[i];
                    rec.extra = d->iExtra >= 0 ? (uint32_t)k.args[d->iExtra] : 0;
                    rec.otherProcess = !is_current_process(k.args[d->iProc] & mask, is64);

                    if ( !d->basePtr )
                    {
                        // The address is the argument itself (an unmap).
                        rec.base   = k.args[d->iBase] & mask;
                        rec.baseOk = rec.base != 0;
                        rec.sizeOk = true;                 // there is no size
                        m_st.recs.push_back(rec);
                        return;
                    }

                    rec.pBase = k.args[d->iBase] & mask;
                    rec.pSize = d->iSize >= 0 ? k.args[d->iSize] & mask : 0;

                    if ( rec.pBase != 0 && msttd_read_word(t, rec.pBase, width, &rec.base) )
                        rec.baseOk = !d->deferred || page_granular(rec.base);
                    if ( rec.pSize == 0 )
                        rec.sizeOk = true;                 // a free may pass none
                    else if ( msttd_read_word(t, rec.pSize, width, &rec.size) )
                        rec.sizeOk = !d->deferred || page_granular(rec.size);

                    // A free's out-params were written by the caller, so what
                    // was just read is recorded and final. Only kernel-written
                    // ones need chasing.
                    m_st.recs.push_back(rec);
                    size_t idx = m_st.recs.size() - 1;
                    if ( d->deferred )
                    {
                        if ( !m_st.recs[idx].baseOk && rec.pBase != 0 )
                            add_retry(rec.pBase, k.utid, width, idx, true);
                        if ( !m_st.recs[idx].sizeOk && rec.pSize != 0 )
                            add_retry(rec.pSize, k.utid, width, idx, false);
                    }
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    m_st.truncated = true;
                }
            }

            // The memory syscalls still out, per thread, innermost last
            // (m_outNow). Each is settled at the return from the call that
            // made it (the stub's return to its caller), where the result is
            // still in rax and the out-params are as the caller first sees
            // them.
            void on_call_ret(IThreadView const *t, uint32_t utid, bool is_return, uint64_t target) noexcept
            {
                poll_retries(t, utid);
                if ( !is_return )
                    return;
                auto it = m_outNow.find(utid);
                if ( it == m_outNow.end() || it->second.empty() )
                    return;
                // The innermost call this return leaves. An unwind can leave
                // several frames at once; syscalls in the frames above it
                // never came back the usual way.
                std::vector<KernelCall> &v = it->second;
                for ( size_t i = v.size(); i-- > 0; )
                {
                    if ( v[i].frame_ret != target )
                        continue;
                    settle(v[i], t);
                    v.resize(i);
                    return;
                }
            }

            const bool m_is64;
            const std::map<uint32_t, const WatchDesc *> m_byNumber;
            SweepState m_st;
            std::map<uint32_t, std::vector<KernelCall>> m_outNow;
        };
    }

    std::unique_ptr<MemmapHooks> make_memmap_hooks(const MsTtdBackend *backend, const SyscallTable &table)
    {
        // By number, not by watching ntdll's exports: a program that makes
        // its own syscalls never calls the export.
        std::map<uint32_t, const WatchDesc *> by_number;
        for ( const WatchDesc &d : kWatches )
            for ( uint32_t n : table.numbers_of(d.name) )
                by_number.emplace(n, &d);
        if ( by_number.empty() )
            return nullptr;
        return std::make_unique<MemmapHooksImpl>(backend, std::move(by_number));
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_mapping_changes(std::vector<ittd_mapping_change> *out,
                                                    std::vector<qstring> *files,
                                                    ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        qnotused(files);        // the syscalls do not say which file a view maps
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        const std::vector<ModuleInfo> all_modules = modules();

        // ---- the syscalls, with their chains ---------------------------------
        //
        // From the census the syscall listing shares (msttd_syscalls.cpp):
        // whichever of the two runs first replays the recording, and the
        // other starts from what it kept.
        QueryResult kr;
        std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> census = syscall_census(true, progress, &kr);
        if ( census != nullptr && census->memmap == nullptr )
        {
            msttd_log("[ida-ttd] memory map: could not find ntdll's memory syscalls in this "
                "recording (its export table was never read during recording).\n");
            set_error("could not find ntdll's memory syscalls in this recording "
                      "(its export table was never read during recording)");
            return r;
        }
        if ( census == nullptr || !kr.ran )
            return r;
        SweepState st;
        // A copy: the census is shared, and the passes below fill in the
        // records' values.
        st.recs      = census->memmap->recs;
        st.truncated = kr.truncated || census->memmap->truncated;
        const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> mods = module_ranges(all_modules);

        // Cancelling the replay or the resolve pass leaves a partial map; the
        // caller is told so it is not saved as complete.
        bool stopped = kr.cancelled;

        // ---- whatever the in-replay retry did not catch ----------------------
        size_t snapped = 0, dropped = 0;
        std::atomic<size_t> viaPolicy{ 0 }, viaReplay{ 0 };
        {
            // The records whose kernel values the replay did not catch, each
            // needing a seek and maybe a replay of its own (17 ms and up on
            // Microsoft TTD): independent, so spread over worker cursors.
            std::vector<size_t> todo;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < st.recs.size(); i++ )
            {
                const Rec &rc = st.recs[i];
                if ( !((rc.baseOk && rc.sizeOk) || rc.d == nullptr || !rc.d->deferred) )
                    todo.push_back(i);
            }
            const bool complete = stopped || todo.empty() || msttd_parallel(todo.size(), 8, progress,
                [&](size_t begin, size_t end, std::atomic<size_t> &done, const std::atomic<bool> &stop)
            {
                UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
                UniqueCursor readback;      // recover_by_readback's, kept apart from 'cur'
                if ( !cur )
                    return;
                for ( size_t k = begin; k < end && !stop.load(); k++, done++ )
                {
                    Rec &rc = st.recs[todo[k]];
                    uint32_t width = rc.is64 ? 8 : 4;
                    cur->SetPosition(rc.retPos);

                    // InFragmentAggressive searches the whole fragment, including
                    // future steps where the caller's read-back usually is;
                    // GloballyAggressive widens that at lower confidence. Both are
                    // accepted only when page-granular (see page_granular).
                    static const QueryMemoryPolicy pols[] =
                    {
                        QueryMemoryPolicy::InFragmentAggressive,
                        QueryMemoryPolicy::GloballyAggressive,
                    };
                    for ( QueryMemoryPolicy pol : pols )
                    {
                        uint64_t v = 0;
                        if ( !rc.baseOk && rc.pBase != 0
                          && read_ptr_policy(cur.get(), rc.pBase, width, pol, &v)
                          && page_granular(v) )
                        {
                            rc.base = v; rc.baseOk = true; viaPolicy++;
                        }
                        if ( !rc.sizeOk && rc.pSize != 0
                          && read_ptr_policy(cur.get(), rc.pSize, width, pol, &v)
                          && page_granular(v) )
                        {
                            rc.size = v; rc.sizeOk = true; viaPolicy++;
                        }
                        if ( rc.baseOk && rc.sizeOk )
                            break;
                    }

                    if ( (rc.baseOk || rc.pBase == 0) && (rc.sizeOk || rc.pSize == 0) )
                        continue;
                    if ( !readback )
                        readback = new_engine_cursor();
                    if ( !readback )
                        continue;
                    if ( !rc.baseOk && rc.pBase != 0
                      && recover_by_readback(readback.get(), rc.retPos, rc.tid, rc.pBase, width, &rc.base) )
                    {
                        rc.baseOk = true; viaReplay++;
                    }
                    if ( !rc.sizeOk && rc.pSize != 0
                      && recover_by_readback(readback.get(), rc.retPos, rc.tid, rc.pSize, width, &rc.size) )
                    {
                        rc.sizeOk = true; viaReplay++;
                    }
                }
            });
            if ( !complete )
                stopped = true;
        }

        // ---- the records as changes -----------------------------------------
        auto in_module = [&mods](ea_t lo, ea_t hi)
        {
            for ( const auto &m : mods )
                if ( lo < m.second && m.first < hi )
                    return true;
            return false;
        };

        out->reserve(out->size() + st.recs.size());
        size_t before = out->size();
        for ( Rec &rc : st.recs )
        {
            if ( rc.d == nullptr )
                continue;
            bool exact = true;

            if ( !rc.baseOk || (rc.d->iSize >= 0 && rc.d->deferred && !rc.sizeOk) )
            {
                // Give up only when nothing was readable: no base means no
                // region, no size means nothing to bound it.
                if ( rc.base == 0 || (rc.d->iSize >= 0 && rc.size == 0 && rc.d->deferred) )
                {
                    dropped++;
                    continue;
                }
                // What survived is the caller's request; the kernel's answer is
                // that request snapped to pages (base down, end up). A floor,
                // never an overstatement.
                uint64_t nb = page_floor(rc.base);
                rc.size = page_ceiling(rc.size + (rc.base - nb));
                rc.base = nb;
                exact = false;
                snapped++;
            }
            else if ( !rc.d->deferred && rc.d->iSize >= 0 && rc.size != 0 )
            {
                // A free's base and size are the caller's request, which the
                // kernel rounds out to whole pages (base down, end up) before
                // acting on it: that rounding is the region it freed, and
                // still exact. Size 0 (the whole region) is left as it is.
                uint64_t nb = page_floor(rc.base);
                rc.size = page_ceiling(rc.size + (rc.base - nb));
                rc.base = nb;
            }

            ittd_mapping_change c{};
            Position p  = to_core(rc.retPos);
            Position cp = to_core(rc.callPos);
            c.pos      = ittd_position{ p.hi, p.lo };
            c.call_pos = ittd_position{ cp.hi, cp.lo };
            c.api      = rc.api == BADADDR ? ITTD_BADADDR : (uint64_t)rc.api;
            c.chain_n  = rc.chain_n;
            for ( uint8_t k = 0; k < rc.chain_n; k++ )
                c.chain[k] = (uint64_t)rc.chain[k];
            // No chain: the call came from a frame opened before the recording
            // began. The calling instruction is still known (the listing shows
            // it as the caller), so it becomes a one-frame chain.
            if ( c.chain_n == 0 && rc.pc != BADADDR )
            {
                c.chain[0] = (uint64_t)rc.pc;
                c.chain_n  = 1;
            }
            c.tid      = rc.os_tid;
            c.kind     = rc.d->kind;
            c.base     = rc.base;
            c.size     = rc.size;
            c.protect  = rc.extra;
            c.flags    = (exact ? ITTD_MAP_F_EXACT : 0)
                       | (rc.otherProcess ? ITTD_MAP_F_OTHER_PROCESS : 0);
            bool inmod = c.size != 0 ? in_module((ea_t)c.base, (ea_t)(c.base + c.size))
                                     : in_module((ea_t)c.base, (ea_t)c.base + 1);
            if ( inmod )
                c.flags |= ITTD_MAP_F_IN_MODULE;
            // The calling instruction, which the listing shows, rides in
            // chain[0]: it is the innermost frame of the chain.
            out->push_back(c);
        }

        // In position order, as the ABI requires: calls were recorded as they
        // returned, which interleaved threads can leave out of order.
        std::stable_sort(out->begin() + (ptrdiff_t)before, out->end(),
                         [](const ittd_mapping_change &a, const ittd_mapping_change &b)
        {
            return a.pos.hi != b.pos.hi ? a.pos.hi < b.pos.hi : a.pos.lo < b.pos.lo;
        });

        msttd_log("[ida-ttd] memory map: %d change(s) from %d call(s); %d out-param(s) "
            "needed a re-query, %d a replay, %d region(s) fell back to the "
            "caller's request, %d call(s) unresolved.\n",
            (int)(out->size() - before), (int)st.recs.size(),
            (int)viaPolicy, (int)viaReplay, (int)snapped, (int)dropped);
        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = stopped;
        r.truncated = st.truncated;
        return r;
    }
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_navigator.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_navigator.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_host.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    static DataAccessMask access_mask_of(uint8_t kinds)
    {
        DataAccessMask m = DataAccessMask::None;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_READ )  m = m | DataAccessMask::Read;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_WRITE ) m = m | DataAccessMask::Write;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_EXEC )  m = m | DataAccessMask::Execute;
        return m == DataAccessMask::None ? DataAccessMask::Execute : m;
    }

    MsTtdNavigator::MsTtdNavigator(MsTtdBackend *backend, MsTtdCursor *cursor)
        : m_backend(backend), m_cursor(cursor)
    {
        record_hits();
    }

    MsTtdNavigator::~MsTtdNavigator()
    {
        // The watchpoints live on the cursor, which outlives this navigator.
        for ( const MemoryWatchpointData &wp : m_userWatchpoints )
            cur()->RemoveMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
        cur()->SetMemoryWatchpointCallback(nullptr, 0);
        cur()->SetEventMask(EventMask::None);
    }

    void MsTtdNavigator::restore_event_mask()
    {
        cur()->SetEventMask(m_userWatchpoints.empty() ? EventMask::None : EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
    }

    bool MsTtdNavigator::set_breakpoints(const std::vector<Breakpoint> &bpts, std::vector<bool> *accepted)
    {
        for ( const MemoryWatchpointData &wp : m_userWatchpoints )
            cur()->RemoveMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
        m_userWatchpoints.clear();
        if ( accepted != nullptr )
            accepted->assign(bpts.size(), false);

        bool all = true;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < bpts.size(); i++ )
        {
            DataAccessMask mask = access_mask_of(bpts[i].kinds);
            MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
            wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)bpts[i].addr };
            wp.Size       = mask == DataAccessMask::Execute ? 1 : (bpts[i].size > 0 ? bpts[i].size : 1);
            wp.AccessMask = mask;
            // Report the truth: a watchpoint the engine refuses never fires,
            // and claiming it was set would leave IDA showing an active
            // breakpoint that silently does nothing.
            if ( cur()->AddMemoryWatchpoint(wp) )
            {
                m_userWatchpoints.insert(wp);
                if ( accepted != nullptr )
                    (*accepted)[i] = true;
            }
            else
            {
                all = false;
                msttd_log("[ida-ttd] could not set a TTD watchpoint for the breakpoint at 0x%llX.\n",
                    (uint64_t)bpts[i].addr);
            }
        }
        restore_event_mask();
        return all;
    }

    qstring MsTtdNavigator::take_notice()
    {
        qstring n;
        n.swap(m_notice);
        return n;
    }

    bool MsTtdNavigator::data_breakpoints_armed() const
    {
        for ( const MemoryWatchpointData &wp : m_userWatchpoints )
            if ( wp.AccessMask != DataAccessMask::Execute )
                return true;
        return false;
    }

    static bool is_data_access(DataAccessType t)
    {
        return t == DataAccessType::Read || t == DataAccessType::Write || t == DataAccessType::Overwrite;
    }

    // The context is the navigator's m_lastHitData. A plain function, because
    // the SDK keeps a pointer to the callable it is given, not a copy.
    static bool __fastcall record_hit(uintptr_t context, ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w,
                                      IThreadView const *)
    {
        *reinterpret_cast<bool *>(context) = is_data_access(w.AccessType);
        return true;
    }

    void MsTtdNavigator::record_hits()
    {
        cur()->SetMemoryWatchpointCallback(&record_hit, reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(&m_lastHitData));
    }

    // Did the instruction just before the playhead make a watched data access?
    // A backward run cannot say (the engine would report it at the playhead
    // itself, which it skips), so replay that one instruction forward and
    // see. When it did, stop on it.
    bool MsTtdNavigator::data_hit_just_before()
    {
        if ( !data_breakpoints_armed() )
            return false;
        const TtdPosition here = cur()->GetPosition();
        cur()->ReplayBackward(TtdPosition::Min, StepCount{ 1 });
        const TtdPosition before = cur()->GetPosition();
        if ( !(before < here) )
        {
            cur()->SetPosition(here);
            return false;
        }
        m_lastHitData = false;
        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, StepCount{ 1 });
        bool hit = r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint && m_lastHitData;
        cur()->SetPosition(hit ? before : here);
        return hit;
    }

    bool MsTtdNavigator::step_past_own_access()
    {
        if ( !data_breakpoints_armed() )
            return false;
        const TtdPosition here = cur()->GetPosition();
        m_lastHitData = false;
        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, StepCount{ 1 });
        if ( r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint && m_lastHitData )
        {
            m_lastHitData = false;
            return true;
        }
        cur()->SetPosition(here);
        m_lastHitData = false;
        return false;
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::settle(EventType sr, bool forward, ea_t target)
    {
        // First and unconditionally: a run that reached either end leaves the
        // cursor on the limit sentinel, not a recorded position.
        m_cursor->clamp_to_trace();

        // A breakpoint stop is not a trace edge.
        if ( sr == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint )
        {
            // An execute breakpoint or the movement's own target stops on the
            // instruction. A data breakpoint stops just after the access, so
            // step back onto the instruction that made it.
            ea_t pc = (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter();
            if ( pc != target && m_lastHitData )
                cur()->ReplayBackward(TtdPosition::Min, StepCount{ 1 });
            m_lastHitData = false;
            return StopReason::Breakpoint;
        }
        IReplayEngine *e = m_backend->engine();
        TtdPosition p = cur()->GetPosition();
        if ( forward && !(p < e->GetLastPosition()) )
            return StopReason::TraceBoundary;
        if ( !forward && !(e->GetFirstPosition() < p) )
            return StopReason::TraceBoundary;
        return StopReason::Stepped;
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::step(bool forward)
    {
        EventType sr = navigate_steps(forward, StepCount{ 1 });
        // The access is the stepped instruction's own: the step completed.
        if ( sr == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint && m_lastHitData )
        {
            m_lastHitData = false;
            sr = EventType::Position;
        }
        return settle(sr, forward);
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::run(bool forward)
    {
        if ( !forward && data_hit_just_before() )
            return StopReason::Breakpoint;
        if ( forward )
            step_past_own_access();
        return settle(navigate_steps(forward, StepCount::Max), forward);
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::step_over(bool forward)
    {
        // IDA has no RESMOD_BACKOVER: "step over backwards" arrives as
        // ev_set_backwards plus RESMOD_OVER, and is a real backward step-over.
        EventType sr = forward ? navigate_over(false) : navigate_over_backward();
        return settle(sr, forward);
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::step_out(bool forward)
    {
        // Likewise: backward step-out is the frame walk, not one step.
        EventType sr = forward ? navigate_over(true) : navigate_out_backward();
        return settle(sr, forward);
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::run_to(ea_t addr, bool forward)
    {
        if ( !forward && data_hit_just_before() )
            return StopReason::Breakpoint;
        if ( forward && step_past_own_access()
          && (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter() == addr )
            return StopReason::Stepped;
        EventType sr = forward ? navigate_forward_to(addr) : navigate_backward_to(addr);
        StopReason r = settle(sr, forward, addr);
        // The target is a temporary watchpoint, so reaching it reads as a
        // watchpoint stop; it is the movement completing, unless a user
        // breakpoint somewhere else stopped it first.
        if ( r == StopReason::Breakpoint && (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter() == addr )
            return StopReason::Stepped;
        return r;
    }

    StopReason MsTtdNavigator::seek_to(Position p)
    {
        return m_cursor->seek(p) ? StopReason::Stepped : StopReason::Failed;
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // The strategies
    //=======================================================================
    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_steps(bool forward, StepCount steps)
    {
        // A bounded step must start from a recorded position: one step
        // backward from the end-of-trace sentinel runs to the start instead.
        if ( steps != StepCount::Max )
            m_cursor->clamp_to_trace();
        const TtdPosition before = cur()->GetPosition();

        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = forward
            ? cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, steps)
            : cur()->ReplayBackward(TtdPosition::Min, steps);

        // An execute breakpoint on the instruction the replay starts from
        // fires before it runs, so the movement stopped where it was. A step
        // or a run from there must still execute it, as in a debugger that
        // steps over the breakpoint it is stopped on. IDA sets one there
        // itself when stepping from pseudocode, and the step then reported a
        // breakpoint without moving, which IDA's statement stepping could
        // answer by running on to the end of the recording.
        if ( r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint && !m_lastHitData
          && cur()->GetPosition() == before )
        {
            r = forward
              ? cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, steps)
              : cur()->ReplayBackward(TtdPosition::Min, steps);
        }

        // A bounded backward step that lands on the first position jumped to
        // the start instead of stepping; say so.
        if ( !forward && steps != StepCount::Max )
        {
            const TtdPosition after = cur()->GetPosition();
            const TtdPosition first = m_backend->engine()->GetFirstPosition();
            if ( first.IsValid() && after <= first && before.Sequence != first.Sequence )
            {
                msttd_log("[ida-ttd] backward step from %llX:%llX landed at the start of "
                    "the trace (%llX:%llX) instead of stepping.\n",
                    (uint64_t)before.Sequence, (uint64_t)before.Steps,
                    (uint64_t)after.Sequence, (uint64_t)after.Steps);
            }
        }
        return r.StopReason;
    }

    bool MsTtdNavigator::add_temp_exec_watchpoint(ea_t addr, MemoryWatchpointData &wp)
    {
        wp = MemoryWatchpointData{};
        wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)addr };
        wp.Size       = 1;
        wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Execute;
        // An identical user breakpoint is the same watchpoint to the engine;
        // removing "ours" afterwards would delete the user's.
        if ( m_userWatchpoints.find(wp) != m_userWatchpoints.end() )
            return false;
        return cur()->AddMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
    }

    void MsTtdNavigator::drop_temp_exec_watchpoint(const MemoryWatchpointData &wp, bool owned)
    {
        if ( owned )
            cur()->RemoveMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
    }

    // Run forward to 'addr' on a specific thread and frame, honoring breakpoints.
    MsTtdNavigator::RunStop MsTtdNavigator::run_to_addr_guarded(ea_t addr, uint64_t min_sp, uint32_t utid)
    {
        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        bool owned = add_temp_exec_watchpoint(addr, wp);

        // The callback is shared by all watchpoints on the cursor: accept the
        // step target only on the right thread and frame, but always stop on
        // any other (user) breakpoint. When the user has a breakpoint on the
        // target itself (not owned), the watchpoint is the user's: a hit on
        // another thread or in a deeper frame is that breakpoint, and stops.
        // Which of the two stopped the replay is told by 'reached', not by
        // where it stopped, since both stop at 'addr'.
        bool reached = false;
        auto stop_cb = [this, addr, min_sp, utid, owned, &reached](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w,
                                                                   IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
        {
            if ( (uint64_t)w.Address == (uint64_t)addr && w.AccessType != DataAccessType::Read
              && w.AccessType != DataAccessType::Write && w.AccessType != DataAccessType::Overwrite )
            {
                m_lastHitData = false;
                if ( (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId == utid && (uint64_t)t->GetStackPointer() >= min_sp )
                {
                    reached = true;
                    return true;
                }
                return !owned;
            }
            m_lastHitData = is_data_access(w.AccessType);
            return true; // user breakpoint
        };
        cur()->SetMemoryWatchpointCallback(stop_cb);
        cur()->SetEventMask(EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);

        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayForward();

        drop_temp_exec_watchpoint(wp, owned);
        record_hits();
        restore_event_mask();

        if ( r.StopReason != EventType::MemoryWatchpoint )
            return RunStop::TraceBoundary;
        return reached ? RunStop::Reached : RunStop::Breakpoint;
    }

    // Run backward to 'addr': a temporary Execute watchpoint and one backward
    // replay, which the engine answers by seeking straight to the previous
    // execution (no backward single-step loop).
    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_backward_to(ea_t addr)
    {
        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        bool owned = add_temp_exec_watchpoint(addr, wp);
        cur()->SetEventMask(EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayBackward();
        drop_temp_exec_watchpoint(wp, owned);
        restore_event_mask();
        return r.StopReason;
    }

    // Run forward to 'addr' the same way. If the cursor is already on 'addr',
    // step once first, so the run reaches the next occurrence.
    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_forward_to(ea_t addr)
    {
        if ( (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter() == addr )
            cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, StepCount{ 1 });
        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        bool owned = add_temp_exec_watchpoint(addr, wp);
        cur()->SetEventMask(EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayForward();
        drop_temp_exec_watchpoint(wp, owned);
        restore_event_mask();
        return r.StopReason;
    }

    // Forward step-out without stepping: find the call that entered the frame
    // and run to its return address, accepting the hit only on this thread
    // with the stack back where it was at the call (a recursive call's return
    // to the same address happens deeper). One frame search and one replay,
    // where the step loop can take a hundred thousand single steps. 'origin'
    // is where the movement began, to go back to when the frame never
    // returns. Called part-way through a step-out, never on its first
    // instruction, so any data access from here on is a stop.
    bool MsTtdNavigator::step_out_by_entry(EventType *result, const TtdPosition &origin)
    {
        const uint64_t    start_sp  = (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer();
        const uint32_t    utid      = (uint32_t)cur()->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;

        MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry fe;
        bool cancelled = false;
        if ( !find_frame_entry_position(fe, cancelled) )
        {
            if ( !cancelled )
                return false;
            *result = EventType::Position;          // stay where it started
            return true;
        }

        // The stack pointer at the call itself, before its push: the callback
        // that found the call may report it either side of the push. Inside
        // the callee the stack is lower, or the call found is not this
        // frame's, and the step loop decides instead.
        ICursorView *fc = frame_cursor();
        if ( fc == nullptr || fe.ret_addr == 0 )
            return false;
        fc->SetPosition(fe.pos);
        if ( (uint32_t)fc->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId != utid )
            return false;
        const uint64_t call_sp = (uint64_t)fc->GetStackPointer();
        if ( call_sp <= start_sp )
            return false;
        const ea_t ret = (ea_t)fe.ret_addr;

        switch ( run_to_addr_guarded(ret, call_sp, utid) )
        {
            case RunStop::Reached:
                *result = EventType::Position;
                break;
            case RunStop::Breakpoint:
                *result = EventType::MemoryWatchpoint;
                break;
            case RunStop::TraceBoundary:
                // The recording ended before the frame unwound, which is no
                // answer to "step out": stay where it started.
                cur()->SetPosition(origin);
                m_notice = "This frame does not return anywhere in the "
                           "recording, so there is nothing to step out to.\n\n"
                           "The position has been left where it was.";
                *result = EventType::Position;
                break;
        }
        return true;
    }

    // Forward step-over and step-out on the playhead: step over a call by
    // running to the return site; step out by repeating until the frame is
    // unwound. Single instructions are stepped directly.
    //
    // A step-out first single-steps a short budget: most frames end within
    // it, sooner than the frame search and seek of step_out_by_entry (tens
    // to hundreds of milliseconds) would. A frame still running after it is
    // left by the entering call's return, and the loop goes on only when that
    // call cannot be found.
    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_over(bool step_out)
    {
        TtdPosition start_pos = cur()->GetPosition();
        uint64_t    start_sp  = (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer();
        uint32_t    utid      = (uint32_t)cur()->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;
        bool hit_bpt  = false;
        bool boundary = false;      // ran out of recording rather than unwinding

        // Both can run long: stepping over a call that never returns replays
        // to the end of the trace, and step-out repeats until the frame
        // unwinds. The core's progress sink keeps Cancel working between
        // iterations.
        const int CAP = 100000;                 // backstop against a pathological frame
        const int kQuickSteps = 64;             // step-out's budget before the frame search
        int iters = 0;
        for ( ;; )
        {
            if ( cancelled() )
                break;
            if ( ++iters > CAP )
            {
                msttd_log("[ida-ttd] step out: giving up after %d iterations without unwinding the frame.\n", CAP);
                break;
            }

            ea_t      pc = (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter();
            X86Branch br = branch_here();
            int  len     = br.len;
            bool is_call = br.is_call;
            bool is_ret  = br.is_ret;

            if ( is_call )
            {
                // Guard on this call's stack pointer, not the frame's: at a
                // nested call the stack is below start_sp, so guarding on it
                // would reject the very return being waited for.
                uint64_t call_sp = (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer();
                // The call's own push is not a stop (step_past_own_access).
                if ( iters == 1 )
                    step_past_own_access();
                RunStop oc = run_to_addr_guarded((ea_t)((uint64_t)pc + len), call_sp, utid);
                if ( oc == RunStop::Breakpoint ) { hit_bpt = true; break; }
                if ( oc == RunStop::TraceBoundary ) { boundary = true; break; }
            }
            else
            {
                ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayForward(TtdPosition::Max, StepCount{ 1 });
                // On the first instruction an access is its own, not a stop;
                // later in a step-out it is one.
                bool own = iters == 1 && m_lastHitData;
                if ( r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint && !own ) { hit_bpt = true; break; }
                m_lastHitData = false;
                if ( r.StopReason == EventType::Position
                  || r.StopReason == EventType::Process
                  || r.StopReason == EventType::Error )
                {
                    boundary = true;
                    break;
                }
            }

            if ( !step_out )
                break;                                  // step-over: a single iteration
            // Step-out: done once a RET takes the stack above where it
            // started. The rise alone is not enough; an epilogue's 'add rsp'
            // does that a few instructions before the RET.
            if ( is_ret && (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer() > start_sp )
                break;
            if ( iters == kQuickSteps )
            {
                EventType ev;
                if ( step_out_by_entry(&ev, start_pos) )
                    return ev;
            }
        }

        // The recording ended before the frame unwound, which is no answer to
        // "step out": stay where it started.
        if ( step_out && boundary && (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer() <= start_sp )
        {
            cur()->SetPosition(start_pos);
            m_notice = "This frame does not return anywhere in the "
                       "recording, so there is nothing to step out to.\n\n"
                       "The position has been left where it was.";
        }
        return hit_bpt ? EventType::MemoryWatchpoint : EventType::Position;
    }

    ICursorView *MsTtdNavigator::frame_cursor()
    {
        if ( !m_frameCursor )
        {
            m_frameCursor = m_backend->new_engine_cursor();
            if ( m_frameCursor )
                m_frameCursor->SetReplayFlags(ReplayFlags::ReplayAllSegmentsWithoutFiltering
                                            | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially);
        }
        return m_frameCursor.get();
    }

    // Find the CALL that entered the playhead's frame, so the caller can seek
    // straight to it or run to its return (MsTtdBackend::find_frame_entry).
    bool MsTtdNavigator::find_frame_entry_position(MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry &out, bool &cancelled)
    {
        cancelled = false;
        out       = MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry{};
        if ( frame_cursor() == nullptr )
            return false;

        // Look-back schedule: a slice of the current sequence, then all of
        // it, then ever more whole sequences. Capped, or a frame entered near
        // the start of a long recording would mean replaying all of it.
        // Sequence ids advance unevenly, hence widening well past 64.
        using Kind = MsTtdBackend::FrameWindowKind;
        static const MsTtdBackend::FrameWindow kWindows[] = {
            { Kind::InSequence, 4096  }, { Kind::InSequence, 65536 },
            { Kind::Sequences,  1     }, { Kind::Sequences,  4     }, { Kind::Sequences, 16    },
            { Kind::Sequences,  64    }, { Kind::Sequences,  256   }, { Kind::Sequences, 1024  },
            { Kind::Sequences,  4096  }, { Kind::Sequences,  16384 },
        };
        MsTtdBackend::FrameSearch fs = m_backend->find_frame_entry(
            m_frameCursor.get(), cur()->GetPosition(), (uint32_t)cur()->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId,
            (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer(), kWindows, qnumber(kWindows), m_progress, true, &out);
        cancelled = fs == MsTtdBackend::FrameSearch::Cancelled;
        return fs == MsTtdBackend::FrameSearch::Found;
    }

    X86Branch MsTtdNavigator::branch_here()
    {
        uint8_t b[16] = { 0 };
        ea_t pc = (ea_t)(uint64_t)cur()->GetProgramCounter();
        MemoryBuffer mb = cur()->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)pc }, BufferView{ b, sizeof(b) },
                                                   QueryMemoryPolicy::GloballyAggressive);
        // A 32-bit thread of a 64-bit process (WoW64) runs with CS 0x23.
        bool is64 = m_backend->is64();
        if ( is64 )
        {
            CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT ctx = cur()->GetCrossPlatformContext();
            if ( ctx.Amd64Context.SegCs == 0x23 )
                is64 = false;
        }
        return x86_branch(b, (size_t)mb.Memory.Size, is64);
    }

    EventType MsTtdNavigator::rewind_to(const TtdPosition &p)
    {
        // One engine call, not a step loop. User breakpoints stay armed, so a
        // hit between here and 'p' stops the run there.
        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayBackward(p);
        return r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint ? EventType::MemoryWatchpoint
                                                            : EventType::Position;
    }

    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_out_backward()
    {
        MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry entry;
        bool cancelled = false;
        if ( !find_frame_entry_position(entry, cancelled) )
        {
            if ( !cancelled )
                m_notice = "Could not find the call that entered this frame.\n\n"
                           "It happened further back than the search window "
                           "reaches, or this thread is in its outermost frame.";
            return EventType::Position;     // leave the cursor where it is
        }
        return rewind_to(entry.pos);
    }

    // Backward step-over: one backward step; if that landed on the tail of a
    // callee that had just returned (same thread, deeper frame), rewind on out
    // of it to the CALL that entered it.
    EventType MsTtdNavigator::navigate_over_backward()
    {
        const uint64_t start_sp = (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer();
        const uint32_t utid     = (uint32_t)cur()->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;

        ICursorView::ReplayResult r = cur()->ReplayBackward(TtdPosition::Min, StepCount{ 1 });
        const bool hit_bpt = r.StopReason == EventType::MemoryWatchpoint;

        // A lower stack pointer alone is not enough (stepping back over a
        // 'pop' does that too): a returning callee is identified by landing on
        // its RET with the stack lower, on the same thread.
        bool deeper = false;
        if ( !hit_bpt
          && (uint32_t)cur()->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId == utid
          && (uint64_t)cur()->GetStackPointer() < start_sp )
        {
            deeper = branch_here().is_ret;
        }

        if ( deeper )
        {
            // If the entering call cannot be found, stay on the RET: the step
            // already moved, and a popup would be noise for "step back one".
            MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry entry;
            bool cancelled = false;
            if ( find_frame_entry_position(entry, cancelled) )
                return rewind_to(entry.pos);
        }
        return hit_bpt ? EventType::MemoryWatchpoint : EventType::Position;
    }
}
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_navigator.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_x86.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Movement through a Microsoft recording. Stepping is a strategy, not a
    // primitive (a backward step-over steps back, notices it landed in a
    // callee that just returned, and rewinds out of it), and each strategy
    // takes the engine's cheapest route: one replay with a watchpoint armed
    // rather than a step loop.
    //
    // It moves the cursor it was made over and keeps the breakpoints as
    // engine watchpoints on that cursor.
    class MsTtdNavigator : public INavigator
    {
    public:
        MsTtdNavigator(MsTtdBackend *backend, MsTtdCursor *cursor);
        ~MsTtdNavigator() override;

        StopReason step(bool forward) override;
        StopReason step_over(bool forward) override;
        StopReason step_out(bool forward) override;
        StopReason run(bool forward) override;
        StopReason run_to(ea_t addr, bool forward) override;
        StopReason seek_to(Position p) override;

        bool set_breakpoints(const std::vector<Breakpoint> &bpts,
                             std::vector<bool> *accepted) override;
        qstring take_notice() override;
        void set_progress(ProgressSink *progress) override { m_progress = progress; }

    private:
        using EventType = TTD::Replay::EventType;

        enum class RunStop
        {
            Reached,        // execution came back to the address asked for
            Breakpoint,     // a user breakpoint stopped it first
            TraceBoundary,  // the recording ended first
        };

        TTD::Replay::ICursorView *cur() const { return m_cursor->exec(); }

        EventType navigate_steps(bool forward, TTD::Replay::StepCount steps);
        EventType navigate_over(bool step_out);
        EventType navigate_over_backward();
        EventType navigate_out_backward();
        EventType navigate_backward_to(ea_t addr);
        EventType navigate_forward_to(ea_t addr);
        EventType rewind_to(const TTD::Replay::Position &p);
        bool      find_frame_entry_position(MsTtdBackend::FrameEntry &out, bool &cancelled);
        // Forward step-out by the entering call: false when it cannot be
        // found, for the step loop to go on.
        bool      step_out_by_entry(EventType *result, const TTD::Replay::Position &origin);
        TTD::Replay::ICursorView *frame_cursor();
        RunStop   run_to_addr_guarded(ea_t addr, uint64_t min_sp, uint32_t utid);
        // The call or return at the playhead, decoded from recorded memory.
        X86Branch branch_here();
        bool      cancelled() const { return m_progress != nullptr && m_progress->cancelled(); }
        bool      add_temp_exec_watchpoint(ea_t addr, TTD::Replay::MemoryWatchpointData &wp);
        void      drop_temp_exec_watchpoint(const TTD::Replay::MemoryWatchpointData &wp, bool owned);
        void      restore_event_mask();

        // The movement's engine result as a stop reason, after clamping onto a
        // real position: a run that reached either end leaves the cursor on
        // the limit sentinel, and everything after it works from there.
        StopReason settle(EventType sr, bool forward, ea_t target = BADADDR);

        // Data breakpoints. The engine reports a data watchpoint just after
        // the instruction that made the access, in either direction, and a
        // backward run never reports the instruction right before where it
        // started; the ABI's stop is at that instruction.
        bool data_breakpoints_armed() const;
        bool data_hit_just_before();
        // A movement does not stop on an access made by the instruction it
        // starts on (the last stop left it there; stopping again would never
        // move). Executes that instruction when it makes such an access;
        // true when it did.
        bool step_past_own_access();
        // Records, for every watchpoint that stops a replay, whether it was a
        // data access: the program counter alone cannot say, since an execute
        // breakpoint on any byte of an instruction stops on its first.
        void record_hits();

        MsTtdBackend *m_backend;
        MsTtdCursor  *m_cursor;
        TTD::Replay::UniqueCursor m_frameCursor;   // see frame_cursor()
        std::set<TTD::Replay::MemoryWatchpointData> m_userWatchpoints;
        qstring m_notice;
        ProgressSink *m_progress = nullptr;
        bool          m_lastHitData = false;   // see record_hits()
    };
}
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_position.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_pch.h"
#include "core/position.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Inside namespace idattd an unqualified Position is the core's, so
    // engine-side code that means the Microsoft one says TtdPosition.
    using TtdPosition = TTD::Replay::Position;

    // Microsoft TTD positions in and out of the core's representation.
    //
    // The core's Position is two opaque 64-bit words, so the conversion is
    // nearly the identity: a TTD position is a (sequence, steps) pair. Only
    // the three sentinels differ in bit pattern and are translated by name.
    //
    //   core none()  <-> Position::Invalid  = { TTD::SequenceId::Invalid, 0 }
    //   core begin() <-> Position::Min      = { 0, 0 }
    //   core end()   <-> Position::Max      = { SequenceId::Max, StepCount::Max }
    //
    // The round trip is lossless because SequenceId::Invalid is UINT64_MAX:
    // no real position has that sequence, so the core's two high sentinels
    // (which do) cannot collide with one. Position::Min {0, 0} is both the
    // first position and begin(), the same place either way.
    //
    // to_core tests Position::Max before IsValid(): Max's sequence is
    // UINT64_MAX - 1 today, and testing the named constant first stays
    // correct if a future SDK changes that.

    inline Position to_core(const TTD::Replay::Position &p)
    {
        if ( p == TTD::Replay::Position::Max )
            return Position::end();
        if ( !p.IsValid() )
            return Position::none();
        return Position{ (uint64_t)p.Sequence, (uint64_t)p.Steps };
    }

    inline TTD::Replay::Position from_core(const Position &p)
    {
        if ( p == Position::none() )
            return TTD::Replay::Position::Invalid;
        if ( p == Position::begin() )
            return TTD::Replay::Position::Min;
        if ( p == Position::end() )
            return TTD::Replay::Position::Max;
        return TTD::Replay::Position{ (TTD::SequenceId)p.hi,
                                      (TTD::Replay::StepCount)p.lo };
    }
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_queries.cpp`:

```cpp
// The Microsoft backend's whole-trace queries, each a replay with a
// watchpoint or the call/return callback armed. The analyses that ask them
// (memsearch, coverage, callsites, tracer) only present the answer.
//
// Every callback runs on the engine's replay thread and is noexcept: it
// writes plain memory only, caps what it keeps and guards its growth, so an
// allocation failure stops collecting instead of terminating IDA.

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    static TtdPosition range_first(PositionRange when)
    {
        return when.first == Position::begin() ? TtdPosition::Min : from_core(when.first);
    }

    static TtdPosition range_last(PositionRange when)
    {
        return when.last == Position::end() ? TtdPosition::Max : from_core(when.last);
    }

    // The position of the next instruction on the same thread: between two
    // sequence points the steps are one thread's, so it is one step on. Wrong
    // only when 'p' is the last instruction before a sequence point (the next
    // one is then in a later sequence), which a call or return rarely is;
    // exactness would cost a seek per call, and there can be millions.
    static Position next_on_thread(const TtdPosition &p)
    {
        TtdPosition n = p;
        n.Steps = (StepCount)((uint64_t)p.Steps + 1);
        return to_core(n);
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // Accesses to a range
    //=======================================================================

    // A busy loop over a watched range can produce millions of hits; past
    // this many the answer is "touched constantly".
    static const size_t kMaxHits = 200000;

    // Only the three access types the watchpoint asks for. CodeFetch and
    // Overwrite are not asked for (see query_accesses); the rest describe how
    // the recording stored a value rather than what the program did.
    static uint8_t kind_of(DataAccessType t)
    {
        switch ( t )
        {
            case DataAccessType::Read:    return ACCESS_READ;
            case DataAccessType::Write:   return ACCESS_WRITE;
            case DataAccessType::Execute: return ACCESS_EXEC;
            default:                      return 0;
        }
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_accesses(ea_t lo, ea_t hi, uint8_t kinds, PositionRange when,
                                             std::vector<Access> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr || lo >= hi || kinds == 0 )
            return r;
        UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return r;

        std::vector<Access> hits;
        bool hit_cap = false;
        auto on_hit = [&hits, &hit_cap, kinds](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w,
                                               IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
        {
            uint8_t k = kind_of(w.AccessType);
            if ( k == 0 || (k & kinds) == 0 )
                return false;
            if ( hits.size() >= kMaxHits )
            {
                hit_cap = true;
                return false;
            }
            try
            {
                Access a;
                a.pos  = to_core(t->GetPosition());
                a.tid  = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().Id;
                a.pc   = (ea_t)(uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
                a.addr = (ea_t)(uint64_t)w.Address;
                a.size = (uint32_t)w.Size;
                a.kind = k;
                hits.push_back(a);
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
            }
            return false;       // collecting them, not stopping on them
        };

        // Segment filtering stays on: a watchpoint is maskable, so the engine
        // skips the parts of the recording that never touch the range.
        // Read, Write and Execute only, as query_executed and the scans ask.
        // Execute is exact, one hit per executed instruction; CodeFetch is
        // the engine's lossy coverage aggregate (hits vary run to run, may
        // repeat or cover many executions at once). Overwrite is the
        // pre-write companion of every Write, so asking for it would report
        // each store twice and halve what kMaxHits holds.
        DataAccessMask am = DataAccessMask::None;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_READ )
            am |= DataAccessMask::Read;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_WRITE )
            am |= DataAccessMask::Write;
        if ( kinds & ACCESS_EXEC )
            am |= DataAccessMask::Execute;
        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)lo };
        wp.Size       = (uint64_t)(hi - lo);
        wp.AccessMask = am;
        bool complete;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            arm.watch(wp);
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_hit);
            complete = arm.sweep(range_first(when), range_last(when), progress);
        }

        // A timeline must not depend on how the engine scheduled the work, and
        // sorting on the whole tuple groups duplicates for the pass below.
        auto key = [](const Access &a) { return std::tie(a.pos, a.addr, a.kind, a.size, a.tid); };
        std::sort(hits.begin(), hits.end(), [&key](const Access &a, const Access &b) { return key(a) < key(b); });
        // Exact duplicates are dropped all the same, which costs nothing
        // after the sort and keeps the list clean whatever the engine reports.
        hits.erase(std::unique(hits.begin(), hits.end(),
                               [&key](const Access &a, const Access &b) { return key(a) == key(b); }),
                   hits.end());
        out->insert(out->end(), hits.begin(), hits.end());

        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        r.truncated = hit_cap;
        return r;
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // Executed addresses
    //=======================================================================
    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_executed(const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &ranges,
```
