```cpp
                                             std::vector<ea_t> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;

        // Sorted, merged spans, so the callback's lookup is a binary search.
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> spans;
        for ( const auto &x : ranges )
            if ( x.first < x.second )
                spans.push_back(x);
        std::sort(spans.begin(), spans.end());
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> merged;
        for ( const auto &x : spans )
        {
            if ( !merged.empty() && x.first <= merged.back().second )
                merged.back().second = std::max(merged.back().second, x.second);
            else
                merged.push_back(x);
        }
        if ( merged.empty() )
            return r;

        // One bit per byte of scope, so the scope is capped: a caller passing
        // a whole address space would otherwise ask for terabytes of bitmap.
        // The core's coverage command already stops at 512 MiB.
        static const uint64_t kMaxScopeBytes = 1ull << 30;
        uint64_t total = 0;
        for ( const auto &x : merged )
            total += (uint64_t)(x.second - x.first);
        if ( total > kMaxScopeBytes )
        {
            set_error("the coverage scope spans %llu MiB, more than the %llu MiB "
                      "this backend maps at once", total >> 20, kMaxScopeBytes >> 20);
            return r;
        }

        UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return r;

        // One bit per byte of scope: compact where a set of millions of
        // addresses is not.
        struct Bin
        {
            ea_t lo = 0, hi = 0;
            std::vector<uint8_t> bits;
        };
        std::vector<Bin> bins;
        try
        {
            bins.resize(merged.size());
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < merged.size(); i++ )
            {
                bins[i].lo = merged[i].first;
                bins[i].hi = merged[i].second;
                bins[i].bits.assign((size_t)(((uint64_t)(merged[i].second - merged[i].first) + 7) / 8), 0);
            }
        }
        catch ( const std::bad_alloc & )
        {
            set_error("not enough memory for a coverage map of %llu MiB", total >> 23);
            return r;
        }

        // Cached last hit: consecutive instructions almost always land in the
        // same span, so the search is only paid at module changes.
        Bin *cache = nullptr;
        auto on_exec = [&bins, &cache](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w,
                                       IThreadView const *) noexcept -> bool
        {
            uint64_t a = (uint64_t)w.Address;
            Bin     *b = cache;
            if ( b == nullptr || a < (uint64_t)b->lo || a >= (uint64_t)b->hi )
            {
                size_t lo = 0, hi = bins.size();
                while ( lo < hi )
                {
                    size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
                    if ( a < (uint64_t)bins[mid].lo )
                        hi = mid;
                    else
                        lo = mid + 1;
                }
                if ( lo == 0 )
                    return false;
                b = &bins[lo - 1];
                if ( a >= (uint64_t)b->hi )
                    return false;
                cache = b;
            }
            uint64_t off = a - (uint64_t)b->lo;
            b->bits[(size_t)(off >> 3)] |= (uint8_t)(1u << (off & 7));
            // Counting executions, not stopping on them: accepting would end
            // the replay at the first instruction that ran.
            return false;
        };

        // Segment filtering stays on: a narrow scope lets the engine skip the
        // parts of the recording that never touch it.
        bool complete;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            for ( const auto &x : merged )
            {
                MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
                wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)x.first };
                wp.Size       = (uint64_t)(x.second - x.first);
                wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Execute;
                arm.watch(wp);
            }
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_exec);
            complete = arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, progress);
        }

        for ( const Bin &b : bins )
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < b.bits.size(); i++ )
                if ( b.bits[i] != 0 )
                    for ( int k = 0; k < 8; k++ )
                        if ( b.bits[i] & (1u << k) )
                            out->push_back(b.lo + (ea_t)(i * 8 + k));

        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        return r;
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // Where calls from a range went
    //=======================================================================
    static const size_t kMaxTargetsPerSite = 16;
    static const size_t kMaxSites          = 20000;

    // Every call made from inside 'ranges', with each target it reached. The
    // engine says where a call went, not whether it was indirect (this
    // backend does not decode the instruction), so direct calls are reported
    // too and the caller keeps the indirect ones. Indirect jumps are not
    // reported.
    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_indirect_targets(const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &ranges,
                                                     bool jumps,
                                                     std::map<ea_t, std::vector<IndirectTarget>> *out,
                                                     ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        qnotused(jumps);
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> spans;
        for ( const auto &x : ranges )
            if ( x.first < x.second )
                spans.push_back(x);
        std::sort(spans.begin(), spans.end());
        if ( spans.empty() )
            return r;
        UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return r;

        struct Seen
        {
            uint64_t hits = 0;
            Position first;
        };
        std::map<ea_t, std::map<ea_t, Seen>> seen;
        bool hit_cap = false;

        auto in_scope = [&spans](ea_t a) noexcept -> bool
        {
            size_t lo = 0, hi = spans.size();
            while ( lo < hi )
            {
                size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
                if ( a < spans[mid].first )
                    hi = mid;
                else
                    lo = mid + 1;
            }
            return lo != 0 && a < spans[lo - 1].second;
        };

        auto on_call_ret = [&](GuestAddress target, GuestAddress fall_through, IThreadView const *t) noexcept
        {
            if ( (uint64_t)fall_through == 0 )
                return;                         // a return, not a call
            // The callback fires on the call instruction, so the thread's
            // program counter is the call site.
            ea_t site = (ea_t)(uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
            if ( !in_scope(site) )
                return;
            try
            {
                auto it = seen.find(site);
                if ( it == seen.end() )
                {
                    if ( seen.size() >= kMaxSites )
                    {
                        hit_cap = true;
                        return;
                    }
                    it = seen.emplace(site, std::map<ea_t, Seen>()).first;
                }
                // A site that reaches a great many targets is a dispatcher, and
                // listing hundreds of them helps nobody. Keep the first few.
                ea_t tgt = (ea_t)(uint64_t)target;
                auto tt = it->second.find(tgt);
                if ( tt == it->second.end() )
                {
                    if ( it->second.size() >= kMaxTargetsPerSite )
                        return;
                    tt = it->second.emplace(tgt, Seen{ 0, to_core(t->GetPosition()) }).first;
                }
                tt->second.hits++;
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
            }
        };

        // A call/return callback is not a maskable event, so there is nothing
        // for segment filtering to work with.
        bool complete;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplayAllSegmentsWithoutFiltering
                                    | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially);
            arm.on_call_return(on_call_ret);
            complete = arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, progress);
        }

        for ( const auto &[site, targets] : seen )
            for ( const auto &[tgt, s] : targets )
            {
                IndirectTarget it;
                it.target  = tgt;
                it.hits    = s.hits;
                it.first   = s.first;
                it.is_call = true;
                (*out)[site].push_back(it);
            }

        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        r.truncated = hit_cap;
        return r;
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // Calls to functions
    //=======================================================================
    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_calls(const std::vector<ea_t> &targets, PositionRange when,
                                          std::vector<CallEvent> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        UniqueCursor sweep = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !sweep )
            return r;

        const std::set<ea_t> wanted(targets.begin(), targets.end());
        struct Rec
        {
            CallEvent ev;
            uint64_t  retAddr;
        };
        std::vector<Rec> recs;
        std::map<uint32_t, std::vector<size_t>> inflight;   // per-thread call stack

        // A broad pattern over a long trace produces tens of millions of hits.
        static const size_t kMaxRecords = 2000000;
        bool truncated = false;

        auto on_call_ret = [&](GuestAddress instr, GuestAddress fall_through, IThreadView const *t) noexcept
        {
            uint32_t tid = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().Id;
            if ( (uint64_t)fall_through != 0 )
            {
                // CALL: instr == callee.
                ea_t callee = (ea_t)(uint64_t)instr;
                if ( !wanted.empty() && wanted.find(callee) == wanted.end() )
                    return;
                if ( recs.size() >= kMaxRecords )
                {
                    truncated = true;
                    return;
                }
                Rec rec{};
                // The callback fires at the call instruction: the ABI's 'pos',
                // where arguments are read with the call-site stack layout.
                rec.ev.pos       = to_core(t->GetPosition());
                rec.ev.entry_pos = next_on_thread(t->GetPosition());
                rec.ev.ret_pos   = Position::none();
                rec.ev.tid       = tid;
                rec.ev.site      = (ea_t)(uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
                rec.ev.target    = callee;
                rec.ev.is_call   = true;
                rec.retAddr      = (uint64_t)fall_through;
                // The record first: an index pushed before a push_back that
                // throws would point one past the end, and the next RET on
                // this thread would write through it.
                try
                {
                    recs.push_back(rec);
                    try
                    {
                        inflight[tid].push_back(recs.size() - 1);
                    }
                    catch ( ... )
                    {
                        recs.pop_back();
                        throw;
                    }
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    truncated = true;
                }
            }
            else
            {
                // RET: instr == the address returned to. Pair it with the most
                // recent in-flight call on this thread expecting it, and drop
                // the calls above it, which left without returning (an
                // exception, longjmp or tail jump) and would block every outer
                // call from pairing.
                auto it = inflight.find(tid);
                if ( it != inflight.end() )
                {
                    std::vector<size_t> &stack = it->second;
                    for ( size_t k = stack.size(); k-- > 0; )
                    {
                        size_t idx = stack[k];
                        if ( (uint64_t)instr != recs[idx].retAddr )
                            continue;
                        // The callback fires at the ret; ret_pos is just
                        // after it, back at the return address.
                        recs[idx].ev.ret_pos = next_on_thread(t->GetPosition());
                        stack.resize(k);
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
        };

        bool complete;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(sweep.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplayAllSegmentsWithoutFiltering
                                      | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially);
            arm.on_call_return(on_call_ret);
            complete = arm.sweep(range_first(when), range_last(when), progress);
        }

        out->reserve(out->size() + recs.size());
        for ( const Rec &rec : recs )
            out->push_back(rec.ev);
        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        r.truncated = truncated;
        return r;
    }
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_scans.cpp`:

```cpp
// The Microsoft backend's replay scans: self-modifying code, strings and
// buffers, which Sogen gets from hooks on its emulator and this backend from
// the engine's memory watchpoints.
//
// One write watchpoint can cover the whole address space, and at its callback
// memory already holds the written value. So:
//
//   1. A replay with that watchpoint finds every range the program wrote.
//   2. A second replay watches the writes again plus the execution of only
//      those ranges, so never-written code costs nothing. Each write feeds
//      all three scanners; each execution is matched against earlier writes.
//
// System writes (a syscall filling a buffer, the loader mapping an image)
// arrive as other access types and are left out, as Sogen leaves them out.
// All three answers come from the same two replays and are kept, so the
// second one asked for is free.
//
// The scanners (common/write_scans.h) implement docs/scan-rules.md and are
// shared with the Sogen backend, so lists read the same from either kind of
// recording. Every callback is noexcept and guards its growth.

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_host.h"
#include "common/write_scans.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    namespace
    {
        // ---- limits -------------------------------------------------------
        const size_t   kMaxStrings       = 500000;
        const size_t   kMaxSelfMod       = 100000;
        const size_t   kMaxWriteNodes    = 4000000;        // the last-write map
        const size_t   kMaxExecRanges    = 4096;           // execute watchpoints
        const uint32_t kStringMinimum    = 4;              // kept; callers ask for more
        const uint64_t kStringWindowMax  = 64 * 1024;

        using scans::kStringContext;

        // Sogen measures "the same burst of writing" as 250,000 instructions;
        // the engine's callbacks count writes, about a fifth as many.
        const uint64_t kNearbyWrites = 50000;

        using StringScan = scans::StringScan<TtdPosition>;
        using BufferScan = scans::BufferScan<TtdPosition>;

        // ---- the last write to every byte ---------------------------------
        //
        // [start, end) -> the write that last stored it, as non-overlapping
        // spans: a write splits whatever it lands on.
        class LastWrites
        {
        public:
            struct Write
            {
                uint64_t    end;
                TtdPosition pos;
                uint64_t    ip;
            };
            bool truncated = false;

            void assign(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, const TtdPosition &pos, uint64_t ip)
            {
                if ( lo >= hi )
                    return;
                auto it = m_map.lower_bound(lo);
                // The same span written again (a stack slot, a loop's
                // variable), which is most writes: updated in place rather
                // than erased and allocated again. The spans do not overlap,
                // so nothing before it reaches past 'lo'.
                if ( it != m_map.end() && it->first == lo && it->second.end == hi )
                {
                    it->second.pos = pos;
                    it->second.ip  = ip;
                    return;
                }
                if ( it != m_map.begin() )
                {
                    auto prev = std::prev(it);
                    if ( prev->second.end > lo )
                    {
                        Write tail = prev->second;
                        prev->second.end = lo;
                        if ( tail.end > hi )
                            m_map.emplace(hi, tail);
                    }
                }
                while ( it != m_map.end() && it->first < hi )
                {
                    if ( it->second.end > hi )
                    {
                        Write tail = it->second;
                        it = m_map.erase(it);
                        m_map.emplace(hi, tail);
                        break;
                    }
                    it = m_map.erase(it);
                }
                if ( m_map.size() >= kMaxWriteNodes )
                {
                    truncated = true;
                    return;
                }
                m_map.emplace(lo, Write{ hi, pos, ip });
            }

            // The latest write to any byte of [lo, hi); nullptr when none.
            const Write *latest(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi) const
            {
                const Write *best = nullptr;
                auto it = m_map.upper_bound(lo);
                if ( it != m_map.begin() )
                    --it;
                for ( ; it != m_map.end() && it->first < hi; ++it )
                    if ( it->second.end > lo && (best == nullptr || best->pos < it->second.pos) )
                        best = &it->second;
                return best;
            }

        private:
            std::map<uint64_t, Write> m_map;
        };

        // The ranges a replay saw written, merged.
        using Ranges = std::map<uint64_t, uint64_t>;   // start -> end

        void add_range(Ranges &r, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, uint64_t gap)
        {
            auto it = r.upper_bound(lo);
            if ( it != r.begin() )
            {
                auto prev = std::prev(it);
                if ( prev->second + gap >= lo )
                {
                    lo = prev->first;
                    hi = std::max(hi, prev->second);
                    it = r.erase(prev);
                }
            }
            while ( it != r.end() && it->first <= hi + gap )
            {
                hi = std::max(hi, it->second);
                it = r.erase(it);
            }
            r.emplace(lo, hi);
        }

        // Merge until there are few enough to watch, never across a module's
        // edge: a range that reached into code nobody wrote would call back on
        // every instruction run there.
        std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> watch_ranges(const Ranges &written,
                                                                 const std::vector<ModuleInfo> &mods,
                                                                 bool *capped)
        {
            auto module_of = [&mods](uint64_t a) -> size_t
            {
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < mods.size(); i++ )
                    if ( mods[i].base <= a && a < mods[i].base + mods[i].size )
                        return i;
                return (size_t)-1;
            };
            std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> v(written.begin(), written.end());
            for ( uint64_t gap = 0x1000; v.size() > kMaxExecRanges && gap <= 0x100000; gap *= 4 )
            {
                std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> m;
                for ( const auto &r : v )
                {
                    if ( !m.empty() && r.first - m.back().second <= gap
                      && module_of(m.back().second - 1) == module_of(r.first) )
                        m.back().second = std::max(m.back().second, r.second);
                    else
                        m.push_back(r);
                }
                v.swap(m);
            }
            *capped = v.size() > kMaxExecRanges;
            if ( *capped )
                v.resize(kMaxExecRanges);
            return v;
        }
    }

    // What the two replays found, kept for the backend's lifetime.
    struct MsTtdScanResults
    {
        StringScan               strings{ kStringMinimum, kMaxStrings };
        std::vector<BufferHit>   buffers;
        std::vector<SelfModHit>  selfmod;
        bool                     truncated = false;
    };

    MsTtdBackend::ScanResultsPtr::~ScanResultsPtr() { delete p; }

    void MsTtdBackend::ScanResultsPtr::reset()
    {
        delete p;
        p = nullptr;
    }

    namespace
    {
        // ---- 1: where the program writes ------------------------------------
        // False when stopped.
        bool scan_written(ICursorView *cur, uint64_t space, ProgressSink *progress, Ranges *written, bool *capped)
        {
            auto on_write = [&](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *) noexcept -> bool
            {
                if ( w.AccessType != DataAccessType::Write )
                    return false;
                try
                {
                    add_range(*written, (uint64_t)w.Address, (uint64_t)w.Address + w.Size, 16);
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    *capped = true;
                }
                return false;
            };
            MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
            wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ 0 };
            wp.Size       = space;
            wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Write;
            ArmedSweep arm(cur, ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            arm.watch(wp);
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_write);
            return arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, progress);
        }

        // ---- 2: the writes again, and what ran of them ------------------------
        //
        // Each write feeds the buffer scan, the string windows and, when it
        // lands in code watched for execution, the last-write map; each
        // execution is matched against that map. The callback is all of it,
        // on the replay thread.
        class WriteReplay
        {
        public:
            WriteReplay(const std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> &exec, StringScan &strings)
                : m_exec(exec), m_strings(strings), m_buffers(kNearbyWrites) {}

            bool on_hit(ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t) noexcept
            {
                try
                {
                    if ( w.AccessType == DataAccessType::Execute )
                        executed(w, t);
                    else if ( w.AccessType == DataAccessType::Write && w.Size != 0 )
                        wrote(w, t);
                }
                catch ( ... )
                {
                    truncated = true;
                }
                return false;
            }

            // The bursts still open at the end, read where the recording
            // ends ('cur' is positioned there).
            void finish_windows(ICursorView *cur)
            {
                for ( auto &[tid, win] : m_windows )
                {
                    if ( !win.live )
                        continue;
                    win.live = false;
                    uint8_t tail[2] = { 0xFF, 0xFF };
                    cur->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ win.hi }, BufferView{ tail, 2 },
                                           QueryMemoryPolicy::GloballyAggressive);
                    win.bytes.push_back(tail[0]);
                    win.bytes.push_back(tail[1]);
                    m_strings.inspect(win.base, win.bytes, win.pos);
                }
            }

            BufferScan &buffers() { return m_buffers; }
            const std::map<uint64_t, SelfModHit> &selfmod() const { return m_selfmod; }
            bool last_truncated() const { return m_last.truncated; }

            bool truncated = false;

        private:
            // Strings are scanned one burst of writing at a time, per thread:
            // the bytes a thread writes forwards through memory, plus what
            // was just before them. A copy is kept as written, so a later
            // overwrite does not change what is scanned.
            struct Window
            {
                uint64_t             base = 0;          // bytes[0] is here
                uint64_t             lo = 0, hi = 0;    // what was written
                std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;
                TtdPosition          pos;
                bool                 live = false;
            };

            static bool read(IThreadView const *t, uint64_t a, size_t n, uint8_t *out)
            {
                MemoryBuffer mb = t->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ a }, BufferView{ out, n });
                return mb.Memory.Size == n;
            }

            void flush(Window &w, IThreadView const *t)
            {
                if ( !w.live )
                    return;
                w.live = false;
                // The terminator after the last byte, as memory has it now.
                uint8_t tail[2] = { 0xFF, 0xFF };
                if ( t != nullptr )
                    read(t, w.hi, 2, tail);
                w.bytes.push_back(tail[0]);
                w.bytes.push_back(tail[1]);
                m_strings.inspect(w.base, w.bytes, w.pos);
            }

            // Whether [lo, hi) touches code watched for execution. Only those
            // bytes are ever asked about (an execution is matched against
            // its own bytes), so only those writes go in the last-write map.
            // The ranges were made from these same writes, so while they are
            // not capped every write lands in one (measured: none left out
            // on either test recording); past the cap, the writes to what is
            // not watched stay out of the map instead of filling it. The
            // writes of one stretch of code mostly land in one range, which
            // is cached.
            bool watched_for_exec(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi)
            {
                if ( m_lastExec != nullptr && m_lastExec->first < hi && lo < m_lastExec->second )
                    return true;
                auto it = std::upper_bound(m_exec.begin(), m_exec.end(), lo,
                                           [](uint64_t v, const std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> &r) { return v < r.first; });
                if ( it != m_exec.begin() && std::prev(it)->second > lo )
                {
                    m_lastExec = &*std::prev(it);
                    return true;
                }
                if ( it != m_exec.end() && it->first < hi )
                {
                    m_lastExec = &*it;
                    return true;
                }
                return false;
            }

            void executed(ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t)
            {
                const uint64_t a = (uint64_t)w.Address;
                const size_t n = w.Size != 0 ? (size_t)w.Size : 1;
                m_buffers.executed(a, n);
                auto hit = m_selfmod.find(a);
                if ( hit != m_selfmod.end() )
                {
                    hit->second.executions++;
                    return;
                }
                // The write that made it is the one that wrote its first
                // byte, the opcode, as Sogen has it; then any of its others.
                const LastWrites::Write *lw = m_last.latest(a, a + 1);
                if ( lw == nullptr )
                    lw = m_last.latest(a, a + n);
                if ( lw == nullptr )
                    return;
                if ( m_selfmod.size() >= kMaxSelfMod )
                {
                    truncated = true;
                    return;
                }
                SelfModHit h;
                h.address     = (ea_t)a;
                h.size        = n;
                h.write_pos   = to_core(lw->pos);
                h.write_ip    = (ea_t)lw->ip;
                h.execute_pos = to_core(t->GetPosition());
                h.executions  = 1;
                m_selfmod.emplace(a, h);
            }

            void wrote(ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t)
            {
                const uint64_t a = (uint64_t)w.Address;
                const size_t n = (size_t)std::min<uint64_t>(w.Size, 4096);
                uint8_t stack[64];
                uint8_t *bytes = stack;
                if ( n > sizeof(stack) )
                {
                    if ( m_largeWrite.size() < n )
                        m_largeWrite.resize(n);
                    bytes = m_largeWrite.data();
                }
                if ( !read(t, a, n, bytes) )
                    return;
                const TtdPosition pos = t->GetPosition();
                const uint64_t    ip  = (uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
                ++m_clock;
                if ( watched_for_exec(a, a + n) )
                    m_last.assign(a, a + n, pos, ip);
                m_buffers.ingest(a, bytes, n, m_clock, pos, ip);

                // Threads write in bursts, so the window lookup is cached.
                const uint32_t utid = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;
                if ( m_lastWin == nullptr || utid != m_lastUtid )
                {
                    m_lastWin  = &m_windows[utid];
                    m_lastUtid = utid;
                }
                Window &win = *m_lastWin;
                if ( win.live && a >= win.hi && a <= win.hi + 16 && a + n - win.lo <= kStringWindowMax )
                {
                    // Onwards from the last write: the gap, then these bytes.
                    size_t gap = size_t(a - win.hi);
                    size_t at  = win.bytes.size();
                    win.bytes.resize(at + gap + n);
                    if ( gap != 0 && !read(t, win.hi, gap, win.bytes.data() + at) )
                        memset(win.bytes.data() + at, 0xFF, gap);
                    memcpy(win.bytes.data() + at + gap, bytes, n);
                    win.hi  = a + n;
                    win.pos = pos;
                    return;
                }
                flush(win, t);
                // What was there just before, which a string written in
                // pieces may have begun with.
                const uint64_t before = std::min<uint64_t>(a, kStringContext);
                win.base = a - before;
                win.lo   = a;
                win.hi   = a + n;
                win.pos  = pos;
                win.bytes.assign(size_t(before), 0xFF);
                if ( before != 0 && !read(t, win.base, size_t(before), win.bytes.data()) )
                {
                    // Partly unreadable: take the part next to the write.
                    for ( uint64_t k = 0; k < before; k += 16 )
                    {
                        uint64_t chunk = std::min<uint64_t>(16, before - k);
                        read(t, a - before + k, size_t(chunk), win.bytes.data() + k);
                    }
                }
                win.bytes.insert(win.bytes.end(), bytes, bytes + n);
                win.live = true;
            }

            const std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> &m_exec;
            const std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t> *m_lastExec = nullptr;
            StringScan                     &m_strings;
            BufferScan                      m_buffers;
            LastWrites                      m_last;
            std::map<uint64_t, SelfModHit>  m_selfmod;
            std::map<uint32_t, Window>      m_windows;
            Window                         *m_lastWin  = nullptr;   // std::map nodes stay put
            uint32_t                        m_lastUtid = 0;
            uint64_t                        m_clock    = 0;
            // A write too long for the callback's stack buffer is read into
            // this, which keeps its capacity from one such write to the next.
            std::vector<uint8_t>            m_largeWrite;
        };

        // ---- 3: the text the modules brought with them ----------------------
        //
        // What was in memory from the start (Sogen scans its initial memory):
        // each image, at its load position. False when cancelled.
        bool scan_module_strings(ICursorView *cur, const std::vector<ModuleInfo> &mods, StringScan &strings,
                                 ProgressSink *progress)
        {
            std::vector<uint8_t> bytes;      // one buffer for every chunk
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < mods.size(); i++ )
            {
                if ( progress != nullptr )
                {
                    if ( progress->cancelled() )
                        return false;
                    progress->report(uint32_t(i * 100 / std::max<size_t>(mods.size(), 1)));
                }
                const ModuleInfo &m = mods[i];
                cur->SetPosition(from_core(m.loaded));
                const TtdPosition at = cur->GetPosition();
                const uint64_t chunk = 0x10000;
                for ( uint64_t off = 0; off < m.size; off += chunk )
                {
                    const uint64_t b = off > kStringContext ? off - kStringContext : 0;
                    const uint64_t e = std::min<uint64_t>(m.size, off + chunk + kStringContext);
                    bytes.assign(size_t(e - b), 0);
                    MemoryBuffer mb = cur->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ m.base + b },
                                                             BufferView{ bytes.data(), bytes.size() },
                                                             QueryMemoryPolicy::GloballyAggressive);
                    if ( mb.Memory.Size == 0 )
                        continue;
                    bytes.resize(size_t(mb.Memory.Size));
                    strings.inspect(m.base + b, bytes, at);
                }
            }
            return true;
        }
    }

    bool MsTtdBackend::run_scans(ProgressSink *progress, QueryResult *qr)
    {
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_scansMtx);
            if ( m_scans.p != nullptr )
                return true;
        }
        // A second query asking while the first replays waits for its answer
        // (the strings and the buffers are often asked for together).
        auto ready = [this]
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_scansMtx);
            return m_scans.p != nullptr;
        };
        switch ( m_scansRun.enter(progress, ready) )
        {
            case SharedRun::Turn::Ready:
                return true;
            case SharedRun::Turn::Cancelled:
                qr->cancelled = true;
                return false;
            case SharedRun::Turn::Run:
                break;
        }
        SharedRun::Runner runner(m_scansRun, progress);
        const uint64_t space = user_space_end();

        UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return false;
        Ranges written;
        bool   capped = false;
        {
            ScaledProgress stage(&runner, 0, 30);
            if ( !scan_written(cur.get(), space, &stage, &written, &capped) )
            {
                qr->cancelled = true;
                return false;
            }
        }
        const std::vector<ModuleInfo> mods = modules();
        bool exec_capped = false;
        const std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> exec = watch_ranges(written, mods, &exec_capped);

        std::unique_ptr<MsTtdScanResults> res(new MsTtdScanResults);
        WriteReplay pass(exec, res->strings);
        // A fresh cursor for the second replay, as for the first.
        cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return false;
        {
            auto on_hit = [&pass](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
            {
                return pass.on_hit(w, t);
            };
            ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
            wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ 0 };
            wp.Size       = space;
            wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Write;
            arm.watch(wp);
            for ( const auto &[lo, hi] : exec )
            {
                MemoryWatchpointData x{};
                x.Address    = GuestAddress{ lo };
                x.Size       = hi - lo;
                x.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Execute;
                arm.watch(x);
            }
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_hit);
            ScaledProgress stage(&runner, 30, 60);
            if ( !arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, &stage) )
            {
                qr->cancelled = true;
                return false;
            }
        }
        cur->SetPosition(TtdPosition::Max);
        pass.finish_windows(cur.get());

        {
            ScaledProgress stage(&runner, 90, 10);
            if ( !scan_module_strings(cur.get(), mods, res->strings, &stage) )
            {
                qr->cancelled = true;
                return false;
            }
        }

        BufferScan &buffers = pass.buffers();
        buffers.finish();
        res->buffers.reserve(buffers.results.size());
        for ( const scans::FoundBuffer<TtdPosition> &f : buffers.results )
        {
            BufferHit h;
            h.address   = (ea_t)f.address;
            h.size      = f.size;
            h.first_pos = to_core(f.first);
            h.last_pos  = to_core(f.last);
            h.writer_ip = (ea_t)f.writer_ip;
            h.writes    = f.writes;
            h.kind      = f.kind.c_str();
            h.preview   = f.preview.c_str();
            res->buffers.push_back(std::move(h));
        }
        res->selfmod.reserve(pass.selfmod().size());
        for ( const auto &[a, h] : pass.selfmod() )
            res->selfmod.push_back(h);
        res->truncated = capped || exec_capped || pass.truncated || buffers.truncated || pass.last_truncated()
                      || res->strings.truncated;
        msttd_log("[ida-ttd] write scan: %d range(s) written, %d watched for execution%s; %d self-modifying "
                  "instruction(s), %d buffer(s).\n", (int)written.size(), (int)exec.size(),
                  exec_capped ? " (capped)" : "", (int)res->selfmod.size(), (int)res->buffers.size());
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_scansMtx);
        if ( m_scans.p == nullptr )
            m_scans.p = res.release();
        return true;
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_self_modifying(std::vector<SelfModHit> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        // Ran only once the scans exist: a failed run (no cursor, say) must
        // not read as a complete, empty answer that a caller would save. A
        // cancelled one did run, and says so (cancelled, not unsupported).
        if ( !run_scans(progress, &r) )
        {
            r.ran = r.cancelled;
            return r;
        }
        r.ran = true;
        const MsTtdScanResults *s = m_scans.p;
        out->insert(out->end(), s->selfmod.begin(), s->selfmod.end());
        r.truncated = s->truncated;
        return r;
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_strings(const ReplaySettings &, uint32_t min_length,
                                            std::vector<StringHit> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        // Ran only once the scans exist: a failed run (no cursor, say) must
        // not read as a complete, empty answer that a caller would save. A
        // cancelled one did run, and says so (cancelled, not unsupported).
        if ( !run_scans(progress, &r) )
        {
            r.ran = r.cancelled;
            return r;
        }
        r.ran = true;
        const uint32_t want = std::max(min_length, kStringMinimum);
        const MsTtdScanResults *s = m_scans.p;
        s->strings.for_each([&](uint64_t address, const StringScan::Entry &e)
        {
            if ( e.value.size() < want )
                return;
            StringHit h;
            h.address = (ea_t)address;
            h.pos     = to_core(e.pos);
            h.wide    = e.wide;
            h.length  = (uint32_t)e.value.size();
            h.text    = e.value.c_str();
            out->push_back(std::move(h));
        });
        r.truncated = s->truncated;
        return r;
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_buffers(const ReplaySettings &, std::vector<BufferHit> *out,
                                            ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        // Ran only once the scans exist: a failed run (no cursor, say) must
        // not read as a complete, empty answer that a caller would save. A
        // cancelled one did run, and says so (cancelled, not unsupported).
        if ( !run_scans(progress, &r) )
        {
            r.ran = r.cancelled;
            return r;
        }
        r.ran = true;
        const MsTtdScanResults *s = m_scans.p;
        out->insert(out->end(), s->buffers.begin(), s->buffers.end());
        r.truncated = s->truncated;
        return r;
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // The memory heatmap
    //=======================================================================
    // One replay with a read/write/execute watchpoint over the whole address
    // space, each access counted against its page and time slice. Time is
    // sliced by sequence number, the engine's clock, which advances with
    // every thread switch.
    //
    // A window (the heatmap zoomed in) replays only its own stretch, so
    // zooming in is cheaper than the first count.

    // The window's ends on the engine's clock, the open ends taken as the
    // recording's.
    static void heat_window(TTD::Replay::IReplayEngineView *engine, PositionRange when,
                            TtdPosition *first, TtdPosition *last)
    {
        *first = when.first == Position::begin() ? engine->GetFirstPosition() : from_core(when.first);
        *last  = when.last  == Position::end()   ? engine->GetLastPosition()  : from_core(when.last);
        if ( *first < engine->GetFirstPosition() )
            *first = engine->GetFirstPosition();
        if ( engine->GetLastPosition() < *last )
            *last = engine->GetLastPosition();
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_access_heat(uint32_t page_shift, uint32_t slices,
                                                std::vector<HeatCell> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        return query_access_heat_window(page_shift, slices, PositionRange{}, out, progress);
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_access_heat_window(uint32_t page_shift, uint32_t slices,
                                                       PositionRange when, std::vector<HeatCell> *out,
                                                       ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr || slices == 0 || slices > 4096 || page_shift < 8 || page_shift > 30 )
            return r;
        TtdPosition first, last;
        heat_window(m_engine.get(), when, &first, &last);
        if ( last < first )
            return r;
        UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !cur )
            return r;
        r.ran = true;
        const uint64_t s0   = (uint64_t)first.Sequence;
        const uint64_t s1   = (uint64_t)last.Sequence;
        const uint64_t span = std::max<uint64_t>(s1 - s0 + 1, 1);
        const uint64_t space = user_space_end();

        std::unordered_map<uint64_t, HeatCell> cells;
        bool capped = false;
        auto on_hit = [&](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
        {
            const DataAccessType k = w.AccessType;
            if ( k != DataAccessType::Read && k != DataAccessType::Write && k != DataAccessType::Execute )
                return false;
            const uint64_t seq   = (uint64_t)t->GetPosition().Sequence;
            if ( seq < s0 || seq > s1 )
                return false;           // the sweep's edges, outside the window
            uint64_t       slice = (seq - s0) * slices / span;
            if ( slice >= slices )
                slice = slices - 1;
            const uint64_t page = (uint64_t)w.Address >> page_shift;
            try
            {
                HeatCell &c = cells[(page << 12) | slice];
                c.page  = page;
                c.slice = (uint32_t)slice;
                if ( k == DataAccessType::Read )
                    c.reads++;
                else if ( k == DataAccessType::Write )
                    c.writes++;
                else
                    c.executes++;
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
                capped = true;
            }
            return false;
        };
        MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
        wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ 0 };
        wp.Size       = space;
        wp.AccessMask = (DataAccessMask)((uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Read | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Write
                                       | (uint8_t)DataAccessMask::Execute);
        const bool whole = when.whole_trace();
        bool complete;
        {
            ArmedSweep arm(cur.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
            arm.watch(wp);
            arm.on_watchpoint(on_hit);
            complete = arm.sweep(whole ? TtdPosition::Min : first, whole ? TtdPosition::Max : last, progress);
        }
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        r.truncated = capped;
        const size_t before = out->size();
        out->reserve(before + cells.size());
        for ( const auto &[key, c] : cells )
            out->push_back(c);
        std::sort(out->begin() + (ptrdiff_t)before, out->end(), [](const HeatCell &a, const HeatCell &b)
        {
            return a.page != b.page ? a.page < b.page : a.slice < b.slice;
        });
        return r;
    }

    Position MsTtdBackend::heat_slice_position(uint32_t slices, uint32_t slice)
    {
        return heat_window_slice_position(slices, slice, PositionRange{});
    }

    Position MsTtdBackend::heat_window_slice_position(uint32_t slices, uint32_t slice, PositionRange when)
    {
        if ( !m_engine || slices == 0 )
            return Position::none();
        TtdPosition first, last;
        heat_window(m_engine.get(), when, &first, &last);
        const uint64_t s0   = (uint64_t)first.Sequence;
        const uint64_t span = std::max<uint64_t>((uint64_t)last.Sequence - s0 + 1, 1);
        TtdPosition p;
        p.Sequence = (SequenceId)(s0 + std::min<uint64_t>(slice, slices) * span / slices);
        p.Steps    = StepCount::Zero;
        if ( !(first < p) )
            p = first;
        return to_core(p);
    }
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h"

#include <condition_variable>

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    static const int POLL_MS = 50;

    bool msttd_sweep(ICursorView *cursor, TTD::Replay::Position first, TTD::Replay::Position last,
                     ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        if ( cursor == nullptr )
            return false;

        // Filtering is the caller's choice (a maskable watchpoint lets the
        // engine skip segments, a call/return callback does not), so only the
        // sequential bit is added.
        cursor->SetReplayFlags(cursor->GetReplayFlags() | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially);

        // A percentage over sequence numbers, the only monotonic measure the
        // progress callback gives. It runs on the engine's threads, so it only
        // stores a number.
        const uint64_t from = first.IsValid() && first != TTD::Replay::Position::Min ? (uint64_t)first.Sequence : 0;
        // 'last' may be Position::Max; the cursor clamps a seek to the trace's
        // real end, which is the number a percentage needs. A real position
        // already says it: the seek (about 17 ms) is only for Max, since
        // callers such as query_register_change run many short sweeps.
        uint64_t to = 0;
        if ( last.IsValid() && last != TTD::Replay::Position::Max )
        {
            to = (uint64_t)last.Sequence;
        }
        else
        {
            cursor->SetPosition(last);
            to = (uint64_t)cursor->GetPosition().Sequence;
        }
        std::atomic<uint32_t> pct{ 0 };
        auto on_progress = [&pct, from, to](TTD::Replay::Position const &p) noexcept
        {
            uint64_t seq = (uint64_t)p.Sequence;
            if ( to > from )
                pct.store((uint32_t)(seq >= to ? 100 : seq <= from ? 0 : (seq - from) * 100 / (to - from)),
                          std::memory_order_relaxed);
        };
        cursor->SetReplayProgressCallback(on_progress);
        cursor->SetPosition(first);

        std::mutex              mu;
        std::condition_variable cv;
        bool                    done = false;
        std::thread worker([cursor, last, &mu, &cv, &done]()
        {
            try { cursor->ReplayForward(last); } catch ( ... ) {}
            {
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mu);
                done = true;
            }
            cv.notify_one();
        });

        // Woken as soon as the replay ends, not at the next poll: callers such
        // as query_register_change run many short sweeps in a row, and a fixed
        // sleep would cost each one a whole interval.
        bool stopped = false;
        uint32_t shown = 101;
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mu);
        while ( !done )
        {
            lock.unlock();
            if ( !stopped && progress != nullptr && progress->cancelled() )
            {
                stopped = true;
                cursor->InterruptReplay();
            }
            uint32_t now = pct.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
            if ( progress != nullptr && now != shown )
            {
                progress->report(now);
                shown = now;
            }
            lock.lock();
            cv.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(POLL_MS), [&done] { return done; });
        }
        lock.unlock();
        worker.join();
        cursor->SetReplayProgressCallback(nullptr, 0);
        return !stopped;
    }

    ArmedSweep::ArmedSweep(ICursorView *cursor, ReplayFlags flags)
        : m_cursor(cursor), m_oldEvents(cursor->GetEventMask())
    {
        m_cursor->SetReplayFlags(flags);
    }

    ArmedSweep::ArmedSweep(ICursorView *cursor, ReplayFlags flags, EventMask events)
        : ArmedSweep(cursor, flags)
    {
        m_cursor->SetEventMask(events);
        m_events = true;
    }

    bool ArmedSweep::watch(const MemoryWatchpointData &wp)
    {
        if ( !m_cursor->AddMemoryWatchpoint(wp) )
            return false;
        try
        {
            m_watched.push_back(wp);
        }
        catch ( ... )
        {
            // Not removable later, so not left behind either.
            m_cursor->RemoveMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    void ArmedSweep::disarm()
    {
        if ( !m_armed )
            return;
        m_armed = false;
        if ( m_watchCb )
            m_cursor->SetMemoryWatchpointCallback(nullptr, 0);
        if ( m_callRetCb )
            m_cursor->SetCallReturnCallback(nullptr, 0);
        if ( m_gapCb )
            m_cursor->SetGapEventCallback(nullptr, 0);
        for ( const MemoryWatchpointData &wp : m_watched )
            m_cursor->RemoveMemoryWatchpoint(wp);
        m_watched.clear();
        if ( m_events )
            m_cursor->SetEventMask(m_oldEvents);
    }

    SharedRun::Turn SharedRun::enter(ProgressSink *progress, const std::function<bool()> &ready)
    {
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(m_mu);
        for ( ;; )
        {
            if ( ready() )
                return Turn::Ready;
            if ( !m_running )
            {
                m_running = true;
                m_pct.store(0, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                return Turn::Run;
            }
            // The caller's sink is not called with the lock held: it calls
            // into the core, which the runner may be calling too. Each turn
            // of the loop looks at 'ready' and 'm_running' again under the
            // lock, so a runner that finishes meanwhile is not missed.
            lock.unlock();
            if ( progress != nullptr )
            {
                if ( progress->cancelled() )
                    return Turn::Cancelled;
                progress->report(m_pct.load(std::memory_order_relaxed));
            }
            lock.lock();
            if ( m_running )
                m_cv.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(POLL_MS));
        }
    }

    void SharedRun::leave()
    {
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_mu);
            m_running = false;
        }
        m_cv.notify_all();
    }

    // More workers than this gain little (measured: 16 workers on a 24-thread
    // machine cut 41 s of seeks and reads to 3 s) and each cursor holds its
    // own cache.
    static const size_t kMaxWorkers = 16;

    bool msttd_parallel(size_t items, size_t min_per_worker, ProgressSink *progress, const ParallelWork &work)
    {
        if ( items == 0 )
            return true;
        size_t workers = std::max<size_t>(1, std::thread::hardware_concurrency());
        workers = std::min(workers, kMaxWorkers);
        workers = std::min(workers, std::max<size_t>(1, items / std::max<size_t>(1, min_per_worker)));

        std::atomic<size_t> done{ 0 };
        std::atomic<size_t> finished{ 0 };
        std::atomic<bool>   stop{ false };
        std::mutex              mu;
        std::condition_variable cv;
        std::vector<std::thread> pool;
        pool.reserve(workers);
        for ( size_t w = 0; w < workers; w++ )
        {
            const size_t begin = items * w / workers, end = items * (w + 1) / workers;
            pool.emplace_back([&, begin, end]()
            {
                try { work(begin, end, done, stop); } catch ( ... ) {}
                {
                    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(mu);
                    finished++;
                }
                cv.notify_one();
            });
        }
        bool stopped = false;
        std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(mu);
        while ( finished.load() < workers )
        {
            lock.unlock();
            if ( progress != nullptr )
            {
                if ( !stopped && progress->cancelled() )
                {
                    stopped = true;
                    stop = true;
                }
                progress->report(uint32_t(std::min(done.load(), items) * 100 / items));
            }
            lock.lock();
            cv.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(POLL_MS), [&] { return finished.load() >= workers; });
        }
        lock.unlock();
        for ( std::thread &t : pool )
            t.join();
        return !stopped;
    }
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

#include <condition_variable>

namespace idattd
{
    // Replay a Microsoft recording from 'first' to 'last' on 'cursor' for a
    // query, with progress and Cancel through 'progress' (nothing of IDA's).
    //
    // The caller owns the cursor and what the sweep looks for (watchpoints,
    // event mask, callbacks), set before and detached after. This adds what
    // every sweep needs: sequential replay (callbacks write unsynchronized
    // state, and the engine's default dispatches them from several threads),
    // a worker thread, the percentage, and InterruptReplay on Cancel.
    //
    // The progress callback is installed here; the caller must not set one.
    // Returns true when the replay ran to the end, false when it was stopped.
    bool msttd_sweep(TTD::Replay::ICursorView *cursor, TTD::Replay::Position first,
                     TTD::Replay::Position last, ProgressSink *progress);

    // What one replay arms on a cursor (its flags, event mask, watchpoints
    // and callbacks), taken off again when this goes out of scope or at
    // disarm(). The engine keeps a pointer to each callable, not a copy, so
    // a callback left set when its lambda dies is called through a dangling
    // pointer by the next replay on that cursor; declaring the lambdas
    // before this object makes the order right by construction. The event
    // mask is put back as it was, so a cursor reused for one slot after
    // another (query_out_values) keeps its own. Replays run through sweep()
    // (msttd_sweep), or straight on cursor() when no progress is wanted.
    class ArmedSweep
    {
    public:
        // A call/return callback needs no event: that sweep leaves the mask
        // alone.
        ArmedSweep(TTD::Replay::ICursorView *cursor, TTD::Replay::ReplayFlags flags);
        ArmedSweep(TTD::Replay::ICursorView *cursor, TTD::Replay::ReplayFlags flags,
                   TTD::Replay::EventMask events);
        ~ArmedSweep() { disarm(); }
        ArmedSweep(const ArmedSweep &) = delete;
        ArmedSweep &operator=(const ArmedSweep &) = delete;

        // Removed again at disarm().
        bool watch(const TTD::Replay::MemoryWatchpointData &wp);

        template <typename F> void on_watchpoint(F &f)
        {
            m_cursor->SetMemoryWatchpointCallback(f);
            m_watchCb = true;
        }
        template <typename F> void on_call_return(F &f)
        {
            m_cursor->SetCallReturnCallback(f);
            m_callRetCb = true;
        }
        template <typename F> void on_gap(F &f, TTD::Replay::GapKindMask kinds, TTD::Replay::GapEventMask events)
        {
            m_cursor->SetGapKindMask(kinds);
            m_cursor->SetGapEventMask(events);
            m_cursor->SetGapEventCallback(f);
            m_gapCb = true;
        }

        bool sweep(TTD::Replay::Position first, TTD::Replay::Position last, ProgressSink *progress)
        {
            return msttd_sweep(m_cursor, first, last, progress);
        }
        TTD::Replay::ICursorView *cursor() const { return m_cursor; }

        // Everything off, now rather than at the end of the scope: before the
        // cursor is used for something else.
        void disarm();

    private:
        TTD::Replay::ICursorView *m_cursor;
        TTD::Replay::EventMask    m_oldEvents;
        std::vector<TTD::Replay::MemoryWatchpointData> m_watched;
        bool m_watchCb   = false;
        bool m_callRetCb = false;
        bool m_gapCb     = false;
        bool m_events    = false;   // the mask was set, and is put back
        bool m_armed     = true;
    };

    // One whole-recording replay whose answer is kept (the syscall census,
    // the write scans), shared between callers that ask at the same time:
    // the first runs it and the others wait for its answer instead of each
    // replaying the whole recording too. A waiter still polls its own
    // Cancel, and sees the runner's percentage. When the runner gives up
    // (cancelled, or failed), the next waiter runs its own.
    class SharedRun
    {
    public:
        enum class Turn
        {
            Run,        // the caller runs it, wrapping its progress in a Runner
            Ready,      // the answer is kept: take it
            Cancelled,  // the caller's own Cancel, while it waited
        };
        // 'ready' says whether the answer is kept. It is asked with this
        // object's lock held, so it takes no lock that a runner holds while
        // it calls back in here.
        Turn enter(ProgressSink *progress, const std::function<bool()> &ready);

        // The runner's side, from enter() returning Run until it goes out of
        // scope, which lets the waiters look again: the runner keeps its
        // answer first. Its progress is passed on and shown to the waiters.
        class Runner : public ProgressSink
        {
        public:
            Runner(SharedRun &run, ProgressSink *progress) : m_run(run), m_to(progress) {}
            ~Runner() { m_run.leave(); }
            Runner(const Runner &) = delete;
            Runner &operator=(const Runner &) = delete;
            void report(uint32_t pct) override
            {
                m_run.m_pct.store(pct, std::memory_order_relaxed);
                if ( m_to != nullptr )
                    m_to->report(pct);
            }
            bool cancelled() override { return m_to != nullptr && m_to->cancelled(); }
        private:
            SharedRun    &m_run;
            ProgressSink *m_to;
        };

    private:
        void leave();

        std::mutex              m_mu;
        std::condition_variable m_cv;
        bool                    m_running = false;
        std::atomic<uint32_t>   m_pct{ 0 };
    };

    // Independent work on 'items' things that each need the engine at a
    // position of their own (a seek costs about 15 ms however near, so a
    // query that visits thousands of positions spends minutes seeking). The
    // engine serves separate cursors concurrently, so the items are shared
    // out in contiguous stretches between worker threads, each making its
    // own cursors: work(begin, end, done, stop) does [begin, end), adds one
    // to 'done' per item and returns early once 'stop' is set. At least
    // 'min_per_worker' items a worker, since a cursor costs something to
    // make. Progress and Cancel through 'progress' from the calling thread.
    // An exception from 'work' ends that worker only. Returns false when
    // cancelled.
    using ParallelWork = std::function<void(size_t begin, size_t end, std::atomic<size_t> &done,
                                            const std::atomic<bool> &stop)>;
    bool msttd_parallel(size_t items, size_t min_per_worker, ProgressSink *progress, const ParallelWork &work);

    // One stage of a query made of several (replays, a scan of the modules),
    // reported as its share of one percentage: 'span' percent from 'from'.
    class ScaledProgress : public ProgressSink
    {
    public:
        ScaledProgress(ProgressSink *to, uint32_t from, uint32_t span) : m_to(to), m_from(from), m_span(span) {}
        void report(uint32_t pct) override
        {
            if ( m_to != nullptr )
                m_to->report(m_from + pct * m_span / 100);
        }
        bool cancelled() override { return m_to != nullptr && m_to->cancelled(); }
    private:
        ProgressSink *m_to;
        uint32_t      m_from, m_span;
    };
}

```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_syscalls.cpp`:

```cpp
// The Microsoft backend's syscalls (see msttd_syscalls.h): the listing, and
// the census the memory map is reconstructed from.
//
// Every callback runs on the engine's replay thread and is noexcept: it
// writes plain memory only, caps what it keeps and guards its growth, so an
// allocation failure stops collecting instead of terminating IDA.

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_syscalls.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_sweep.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_host.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_guest.h"
#include "common/guest_pe.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    // A program that makes syscalls in a loop can make millions. Past this
    // many the listing and the map are cut short (and say so).
    static const size_t kMaxKernelCalls = 1000000;

    // One frame of the per-thread shadow call stack, which gives a syscall
    // the chain of calls that led to it.
    struct ShadowFrame
    {
        uint64_t ret_addr;  // where this call will return to
        uint64_t sp;        // the stack pointer when it was made
        ea_t     site;      // the instruction that made it
    };
    // A call depth past this is pathological, and an unbounded vector grown
    // inside a noexcept callback is the shape of bug that takes the whole
    // process down with no message.
    static const size_t kMaxDepth = 256;

    std::vector<uint32_t> SyscallTable::numbers_of(const char *name) const
    {
        std::vector<uint32_t> out;
        for ( const auto &[n, s] : names )
            if ( s == name )
                out.push_back(n);
        return out;
    }

    // How far into a stub its syscall instruction can be: past the number,
    // a check of whether to syscall or int 2e, and the branch.
    static const ea_t kStubSpan = 0x40;

    ea_t SyscallTable::stub_of(uint32_t n, ea_t pc) const
    {
        auto [lo, hi] = stubs.equal_range(n);
        for ( auto it = lo; it != hi; ++it )
            if ( it->second <= pc && pc < it->second + kStubSpan )
                return it->second;
        return BADADDR;
    }

    // The number a stub loads, or false when it does not start like one.
    // x64: mov r10, rcx; mov eax, imm32. x86: mov eax, imm32. A stub that
    // starts with an indirect jmp was hooked when the export table was
    // read; the hook's target is decoded instead, once.
    static bool decode_stub(const GuestRead &rd, uint64_t at, bool is64, uint32_t *ssn, bool hop = true)
    {
        uint8_t b[16];
        if ( !pe_read(rd, at, b, sizeof(b)) )
            return false;
        if ( is64 && b[0] == 0x4C && b[1] == 0x8B && b[2] == 0xD1 && b[3] == 0xB8 )
        {
            memcpy(ssn, b + 4, 4);
            return true;
        }
        if ( !is64 && b[0] == 0xB8 )
        {
            memcpy(ssn, b + 1, 4);
            return true;
        }
        if ( hop && b[0] == 0xFF && b[1] == 0x25 )
        {
            int32_t disp;
            memcpy(&disp, b + 2, 4);
            uint64_t slot = is64 ? at + 6 + (int64_t)disp : (uint64_t)(uint32_t)disp;
            uint64_t target = 0;
            if ( pe_read(rd, slot, &target, is64 ? 8 : 4) )
                return decode_stub(rd, target, is64, ssn, false);
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Every complete syscall stub in a module's image, by number. x64:
    // mov r10, rcx; mov eax, n; ... syscall at +0x12. x86: mov eax, n;
    // mov edx, Wow64Transition; call edx (one stub has a call $+5 between).
    static size_t scan_stubs(ICursorView *c, const ModuleInfo &ml, bool is64,
                             std::multimap<uint32_t, ea_t> *out)
    {
        std::vector<uint8_t> img(size_t(ml.size), 0);
        const uint64_t chunk = 0x10000;
        for ( uint64_t off = 0; off < ml.size; off += chunk )
        {
            size_t n = size_t(std::min<uint64_t>(chunk, ml.size - off));
            c->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ ml.base + off }, BufferView{ img.data() + off, n },
                                 QueryMemoryPolicy::GloballyAggressive);
        }
        size_t found = 0;
        auto imm = [&img](size_t at) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, img.data() + at, 4); return v; };
        for ( size_t i = 0; i + 0x20 < img.size(); i++ )
        {
            if ( is64 )
            {
                if ( img[i] == 0x4C && img[i + 1] == 0x8B && img[i + 2] == 0xD1 && img[i + 3] == 0xB8
                  && img[i + 0x12] == 0x0F && img[i + 0x13] == 0x05 )
                {
                    out->emplace(imm(i + 4) & 0xFFFF, ml.base + i);
                    found++;
                }
                continue;
            }
            if ( img[i] != 0xB8 )
                continue;
            size_t j = i + 5;
            if ( img[j] == 0xE8 && imm(j + 1) == 0 )
                j += 5;
            if ( img[j] == 0xBA && img[j + 5] == 0xFF && img[j + 6] == 0xD2 )
            {
                out->emplace(imm(i + 1) & 0xFFFF, ml.base + i);
                found++;
            }
        }
        return found;
    }

    bool build_syscall_table(const MsTtdBackend *backend, SyscallTable *out)
    {
        out->names.clear();
        out->stubs.clear();
        UniqueCursor sym = backend->new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !sym )
            return false;
        // Every ntdll the recording loaded (a WoW64 recording has a 32-bit
        // and a 64-bit one under the same name), and win32u, whose stubs are
        // win32k's: NtUser*, NtGdi*, numbered from 0x1000.
        for ( const ModuleInfo &ml : backend->modules() )
        {
            if ( _stricmp(ml.name.c_str(), "ntdll.dll") != 0 && _stricmp(ml.name.c_str(), "win32u.dll") != 0 )
                continue;
            // Exports can only be read where the module is mapped.
            sym->SetPosition(from_core(ml.loaded));
            GuestRead rd = msttd_read_plain(sym.get());
            GuestPeInfo pe;
            bool is64 = read_guest_pe_info(rd, ml.base, &pe) ? pe.is64 : backend->is64();
            // The names, from the exports. A 32-bit stub's number carries
            // WoW64's argument-conversion index in the high word, which is
            // not part of the syscall's number.
            std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, std::string>> exports;
            read_guest_exports(rd, ml.base, is64, &exports);
            std::multimap<uint32_t, ea_t> by_export;
            for ( const auto &[ea, name] : exports )
            {
                if ( name.size() < 3 || name[0] != 'N' || name[1] != 't' )
                    continue;
                uint32_t n = 0;
                if ( !decode_stub(rd, ea, is64, &n) )
                    continue;
                out->names.emplace(n & 0xFFFF, name);
                by_export.emplace(n & 0xFFFF, ea);
            }
            // The stubs themselves, from the image: a process can point
            // its exports elsewhere (thunks in a private region), and
            // then every syscall would look like one the program made
            // itself. Some numbers have two stubs.
            size_t found = scan_stubs(sym.get(), ml, is64, &out->stubs);
            if ( found == 0 )
                out->stubs.insert(by_export.begin(), by_export.end());
        }
        return !out->names.empty();
    }

    // The syscall at a KernelCall gap: its number, and where it returns to.
    // 'ctx' is the thread's context there.
    static void read_kernel_call(IThreadView const *t, const CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT &ctx, bool is64,
                                 KernelCall *k) noexcept
    {
        k->pc = (ea_t)(uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
        k->sp = (uint64_t)t->GetStackPointer();
        if ( is64 )
        {
            k->number = (uint32_t)ctx.Amd64Context.Rax;
            // syscall (0F 05) and its relatives are two bytes; the kernel
            // comes back to the next instruction.
            uint8_t ins[2] = { 0, 0 };
            MemoryBuffer mb = t->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ (uint64_t)k->pc }, BufferView{ ins, 2 });
            if ( mb.Memory.Size == 2
              && ((ins[0] == 0x0F && (ins[1] == 0x05 || ins[1] == 0x34)) || (ins[0] == 0xCD && ins[1] == 0x2E)) )
                k->ret_pc = (uint64_t)k->pc + 2;
            return;
        }
        // The high word is WoW64's; the number is the low one, the same
        // numbering as x64's.
        k->number = (uint32_t)ctx.X86Nt5Context.Eax & 0xFFFF;
        // The gap is at WoW64's transition, which the stub called: the word
        // on top of the stack is the return into the stub, which is where
        // the kernel's answer comes back.
        uint64_t ret = 0;
        if ( msttd_read_word(t, k->sp, 4, &ret) )
            k->ret_pc = ret;
    }

    // Its arguments as the kernel takes them, after read_kernel_call.
    static void read_kernel_call_args(IThreadView const *t, const CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT &ctx, bool is64,
                                      KernelCall *k) noexcept
    {
        if ( is64 )
        {
            // The stub moved rcx to r10 (syscall overwrites rcx with the
            // return address). Arguments 5 and on are where the stub's caller
            // put them, past the return address and the shadow space; the
            // stub has not touched the stack.
            const AMD64_CONTEXT &c = ctx.Amd64Context;
            const uint64_t regs[4] = { c.R10, c.Rdx, c.R8, c.R9 };
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < 4; i++ )
                k->args[i] = regs[i];
            uint64_t slots[kKernelCallArgs - 4] = { 0 };
            t->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ k->sp + 0x28 }, BufferView{ slots, sizeof(slots) });
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < kKernelCallArgs - 4; i++ )
                k->args[4 + i] = slots[i];
            return;
        }
        // Argument n is at [esp+8+4n], past the return into the stub and the
        // stub's own return address.
        uint32_t slots[kKernelCallArgs] = { 0 };
        t->QueryMemoryBuffer(GuestAddress{ k->sp + 8 }, BufferView{ slots, sizeof(slots) });
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < kKernelCallArgs; i++ )
            k->args[i] = slots[i];
    }

    std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> module_ranges(const std::vector<ModuleInfo> &mods)
    {
        std::map<ea_t, ea_t> m;
        for ( const ModuleInfo &mi : mods )
            m.emplace(mi.base, mi.base + (ea_t)mi.size);
        return std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>>(m.begin(), m.end());
    }

    QueryResult collect_kernel_calls(const MsTtdBackend *backend, const SyscallTable &table,
                                     const KernelCallOptions &opts,
                                     std::vector<KernelCall> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        const bool chains = opts.chains;
        QueryResult r;
        UniqueCursor census = backend->new_engine_cursor();
        if ( !census || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        const bool is64 = backend->is64();

        // Which module an address belongs to, from a table built before the
        // replay: the callback runs on the replay worker, so nothing it reads
        // may be built lazily.
        const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> mods = module_ranges(backend->modules());
        auto module_of = [&mods](ea_t ea) noexcept -> size_t
        {
            size_t lo = 0, hi = mods.size();
            while ( lo < hi )
            {
                size_t mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2;
                if ( mods[mid].first <= ea )
                    lo = mid + 1;
                else
                    hi = mid;
            }
            if ( lo == 0 )
                return (size_t)-1;
            --lo;
            return ea < mods[lo].second ? lo : (size_t)-1;
        };
        // The program's own module, whose frames a chain keeps all of.
        size_t mainMod = (size_t)-2;
        for ( const ModuleInfo &mi : backend->modules() )
            if ( _stricmp(mi.name.c_str(), backend->info().main_module.c_str()) == 0 )
            {
                mainMod = module_of(mi.base);
                break;
            }

        std::vector<KernelCall> calls;
        bool truncated = false;

        // ---- the census: every transition into the kernel -------------------
        //
        // The shadow call stacks, when chains are wanted: every call pushes a
        // frame and every matching return pops it. The lookup is cached: it
        // runs on every call, and threads execute in bursts.
        //
        // The same callback takes each syscall's result. A thread makes one
        // syscall at a time, so its latest is the one waiting to come back
        // ('pending', an index into 'calls'), and the kernel comes back to
        // the instruction after the syscall (x86: the return into the stub).
        // In a stub that instruction is the stub's ret, so the callback
        // fires on it before it runs, with the result still in rax: what an
        // execute watchpoint there reads, without a replay of its own.
        struct ThreadShadow
        {
            std::vector<ShadowFrame> frames;
            size_t                   pending = SIZE_MAX;
        };
        std::map<uint32_t, ThreadShadow> shadow;
        uint32_t      lastTid    = 0xFFFFFFFF;
        ThreadShadow *lastShadow = nullptr;
        auto shadow_for = [&](uint32_t tid) -> ThreadShadow *
        {
            if ( tid != lastTid || lastShadow == nullptr )
            {
                lastShadow = &shadow[tid];
                lastTid    = tid;
            }
            return lastShadow;
        };

        auto on_call_ret = [&](GuestAddress instr, GuestAddress fall_through, IThreadView const *t) noexcept
        {
            try
            {
                const uint32_t utid = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;
                ThreadShadow *ts = shadow_for(utid);
                std::vector<ShadowFrame> *sh = &ts->frames;
                if ( ts->pending != SIZE_MAX && (uint64_t)fall_through == 0 )
                {
                    KernelCall &k = calls[ts->pending];
                    if ( (uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter() == k.ret_pc )
                    {
                        const CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT ctx = t->GetCrossPlatformContext();
                        k.result   = is64 ? (uint64_t)ctx.Amd64Context.Rax : (uint64_t)ctx.X86Nt5Context.Eax;
                        k.returned = true;
                        ts->pending = SIZE_MAX;
                    }
                }
                if ( (uint64_t)fall_through != 0 )
                {
                    // A call. Whichever instruction the position sits on, the
                    // site is in the caller: the program counter when it is
                    // not the callee itself, else the instruction after the
                    // call.
                    ea_t tgt  = (ea_t)(uint64_t)instr;
                    ea_t pc   = (ea_t)(uint64_t)t->GetProgramCounter();
                    ea_t site = pc != tgt ? pc : (ea_t)(uint64_t)fall_through;
                    // Frames the stack has already left behind (a call that
                    // never returned, an unwind, a tail jump) are below the
                    // stack pointer: the stack grows down.
                    uint64_t sp = (uint64_t)t->GetStackPointer();
                    while ( !sh->empty() && sh->back().sp < sp )
                        sh->pop_back();
                    // At the cap, slide rather than stop: the frames worth
```
