```cpp
                    // having are the innermost ones.
                    if ( sh->size() >= kMaxDepth )
                        sh->erase(sh->begin());
                    sh->push_back(ShadowFrame{ (uint64_t)fall_through, sp, site });
                    if ( opts.on_call_ret )
                        opts.on_call_ret(t, utid, false, (uint64_t)instr);
                    return;
                }
                // A return: unwind to the frame that expected it, dropping
                // anything above (an exception or longjmp leaves several
                // frames at once).
                for ( size_t k = sh->size(); k-- > 0; )
                {
                    if ( sh->at(k).ret_addr == (uint64_t)instr )
                    {
                        sh->resize(k);
                        break;
                    }
                }
                if ( opts.on_call_ret )
                    opts.on_call_ret(t, utid, true, (uint64_t)instr);
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
                truncated = true;
            }
        };

        auto on_gap = [&](GapKind, GapEventType type, IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
        {
            if ( type != GapEventType::KernelCall )
                return false;
            if ( calls.size() >= kMaxKernelCalls )
            {
                truncated = true;
                return false;
            }
            try
            {
                KernelCall k;
                k.pos  = t->GetPosition();
                k.utid = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;
                k.tid  = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().Id;
                // The number first; the arguments only for the calls the
                // caller wants them for. One context fetch serves all three.
                const CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT ctx = t->GetCrossPlatformContext();
                read_kernel_call(t, ctx, is64, &k);
                ittd_regs regs;
                regs_from_context(ctx, is64, &regs);
                memcpy(k.gp, regs.gp, sizeof(k.gp));
                k.rflags = regs.rflags;
                k.name = table.name_of(k.number);
                // x86: the gap is at the transition, outside every module;
                // the stub is where it returns to.
                k.stub = table.stub_of(k.number, is64 ? k.pc : (ea_t)k.ret_pc);
                if ( !opts.args_wanted || opts.args_wanted(k.number) )
                {
                    read_kernel_call_args(t, ctx, is64, &k);
                    if ( chains )
                    {
                        // From the call into the stub (or the syscall itself,
                        // when the program made its own), then one frame per
                        // library module crossed: the innermost in each, the
                        // code that called onward. In the program's own
                        // module and in code outside every module, every
                        // frame: the innermost there is often a helper (its
                        // malloc) that every allocation goes through, and
                        // only the frames beyond it tell the callers apart.
                        const std::vector<ShadowFrame> *sh = &shadow_for(k.utid)->frames;
                        if ( !sh->empty() )
                            k.frame_ret = sh->back().ret_addr;
                        size_t lastMod = (size_t)-2;    // distinct from "none"
                        if ( k.stub == BADADDR )
                        {
                            k.chain[k.chain_n++] = k.pc;
                            lastMod = module_of(k.pc);
                        }
                        for ( size_t i = sh->size(); i-- > 0 && k.chain_n < ITTD_CHAIN_MAX; )
                        {
                            ea_t   s  = sh->at(i).site;
                            // The stub's own call into WoW64's transition.
                            if ( k.stub != BADADDR && k.stub <= s && s < k.stub + kStubSpan )
                                continue;
                            size_t mi = module_of(s);
                            const bool own = mi == mainMod || mi == (size_t)-1;
                            if ( k.chain_n != 0 && mi == lastMod && !own )
                                continue;
                            k.chain[k.chain_n++] = s;
                            lastMod = mi;
                        }
                    }
                }
                calls.push_back(k);
                // A call still pending never came back (the thread ended in
                // it): this one is the thread's now.
                if ( chains )
                    shadow_for(k.utid)->pending = k.ret_pc != 0 ? calls.size() - 1 : SIZE_MAX;
                if ( opts.on_syscall )
                    opts.on_syscall(calls.back(), t);
            }
            catch ( ... )
            {
                truncated = true;
            }
            return false;       // collecting them, not stopping on them
        };

        bool complete;
        {
            // No filtering: a call/return callback gives the engine nothing
            // to filter on, and every stretch of a recording ends in kernel
            // calls.
            ArmedSweep arm(census.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplayAllSegmentsWithoutFiltering
                                       | ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::Gap);
            arm.on_gap(on_gap, GapKindMask::All, GapEventMask::KernelCall);
            if ( chains )
                arm.on_call_return(on_call_ret);
            complete = arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, progress);
        }
        census.reset();
        shadow.clear();

        std::stable_sort(calls.begin(), calls.end(),
                         [](const KernelCall &a, const KernelCall &b) { return a.pos < b.pos; });

        msttd_log("[ida-ttd] syscalls: %d in the recording, %d named%s.\n",
                  (int)calls.size(),
                  (int)std::count_if(calls.begin(), calls.end(), [](const KernelCall &c) { return c.name != nullptr; }),
                  truncated ? " (cut short)" : "");
        *out = std::move(calls);
        r.ran       = true;
        r.cancelled = !complete;
        r.truncated = truncated;
        return r;
    }

    // ---- the returns the census could not see --------------------------------
    //
    // An execute watchpoint on every instruction the kernel returns to that
    // the census left open (to_watch: code making its own syscalls, and on
    // x86 every syscall the census did not see come back). A thread makes
    // one syscall at a time, so a return belongs to that thread's latest
    // call before it; every call is kept in that order, the settled ones
    // included, so a later return is never taken for an earlier call's.
    // 'calls' is in position order. False when stopped.
    static bool collect_kernel_returns(const MsTtdBackend *backend, std::vector<CensusSyscall> *callsp,
                                       ProgressSink *progress, bool *truncatedp)
    {
        std::vector<CensusSyscall> &calls = *callsp;
        const bool is64 = backend->is64();
        bool truncated = false;
        bool complete = true;
        std::map<uint32_t, std::vector<size_t>> per_thread;
        std::set<uint64_t> ret_pcs;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < calls.size(); i++ )
        {
            per_thread[calls[i].utid].push_back(i);
            if ( calls[i].to_watch )
                ret_pcs.insert(calls[i].ret_pc);
        }
        if ( !ret_pcs.empty() )
        {
            UniqueCursor ret = backend->new_engine_cursor();
            if ( ret )
            {
                std::map<uint32_t, size_t> next;   // per thread: its first call not settled
                auto on_exec = [&](ICursorView::MemoryWatchpointResult const &w, IThreadView const *t) noexcept -> bool
                {
                    try
                    {
                        uint32_t utid = (uint32_t)t->GetThreadInfo().UniqueId;
                        auto pt = per_thread.find(utid);
                        if ( pt == per_thread.end() )
                            return false;
                        const std::vector<size_t> &mine = pt->second;
                        size_t &k = next[utid];
                        TtdPosition here = t->GetPosition();
                        // A call whose return was never seen (the thread
                        // ended in it) is settled by the next one starting.
                        while ( k + 1 < mine.size() && calls[mine[k + 1]].pos < here )
                            k++;
                        if ( k >= mine.size() )
                            return false;
                        CensusSyscall &c = calls[mine[k]];
                        if ( !c.to_watch || c.returned || !(c.pos < here) || c.ret_pc != (uint64_t)w.Address )
                            return false;
                        CROSS_PLATFORM_CONTEXT ctx = t->GetCrossPlatformContext();
                        c.result   = is64 ? (uint64_t)ctx.Amd64Context.Rax : (uint64_t)ctx.X86Nt5Context.Eax;
                        c.returned = true;
                        k++;
                    }
                    catch ( ... )
                    {
                        truncated = true;
                    }
                    return false;
                };
                ArmedSweep arm(ret.get(), ReplayFlags::ReplaySegmentsSequentially, EventMask::MemoryWatchpoint);
                for ( uint64_t a : ret_pcs )
                {
                    MemoryWatchpointData wp{};
                    wp.Address    = GuestAddress{ a };
                    wp.Size       = 1;
                    wp.AccessMask = DataAccessMask::Execute;
                    arm.watch(wp);
                }
                arm.on_watchpoint(on_exec);
                complete = arm.sweep(TtdPosition::Min, TtdPosition::Max, progress);
            }
        }
        *truncatedp = truncated;
        return complete;
    }

    // The registers of the first syscalls in the census, so the listing's
    // argument column costs no seek per row. Capped: it is a convenience.
    static const size_t kMaxCachedRegs = 250000;

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::registers_at(const std::vector<Position> &positions,
                                           std::vector<ittd_regs> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        r.ran = true;
        out->assign(positions.size(), ittd_regs{});

        // The census's registers first; what it does not have (past its cap,
        // or not a syscall) is read below. The census is immutable, so its
        // registers are read without a lock however many queries ask at once.
        const std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> census = cached_census();
        const std::vector<CensusRegs> *known = census != nullptr && census->regs != nullptr
                                             ? census->regs.get() : nullptr;
        std::vector<size_t> missing;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < positions.size(); i++ )
        {
            const TtdPosition p = from_core(positions[i]);
            if ( known != nullptr )
            {
                auto it = std::lower_bound(known->begin(), known->end(), p,
                                           [](const CensusRegs &a, const TtdPosition &b) { return a.pos < b; });
                if ( it != known->end() && it->pos == p )
                {
                    ittd_regs &o = (*out)[i];
                    memcpy(o.gp, it->gp, sizeof(o.gp));
                    o.rflags = it->rflags;
                    o.have   = ITTD_REGS_GP;
                    continue;
                }
            }
            missing.push_back(i);
        }
        if ( missing.empty() )
            return r;

        // A seek each, about 17 ms: a million syscalls past the cache was
        // hours on one cursor. Spread over worker cursors like
        // read_memory_at, in position order so neighbours share a worker.
        std::sort(missing.begin(), missing.end(), [&](size_t a, size_t b)
        {
            return positions[a] < positions[b];
        });
        const bool complete = msttd_parallel(missing.size(), 16, progress,
            [&](size_t begin, size_t end, std::atomic<size_t> &done, const std::atomic<bool> &stop)
        {
            UniqueCursor cur = new_engine_cursor();
            if ( !cur )
                return;
            for ( size_t k = begin; k < end && !stop.load(); k++, done++ )
            {
                const size_t i = missing[k];
                cur->SetPosition(from_core(positions[i]));
                regs_from_context(cur->GetCrossPlatformContext(), m_info.is64, &(*out)[i]);
            }
        });
        if ( !complete )
            r.cancelled = true;
        return r;
    }

    std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> MsTtdBackend::cached_census()
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_censusMtx);
        return m_census;
    }

    std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> MsTtdBackend::syscall_census(bool need_memmap, ProgressSink *progress,
                                                                      QueryResult *qr)
    {
        *qr = QueryResult{};
        auto from_cache = [this, qr]() -> std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus>
        {
            std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> c = cached_census();
            if ( c != nullptr )
            {
                qr->ran       = true;
                qr->truncated = c->truncated;
            }
            return c;
        };
        if ( std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> c = from_cache() )
            return c;
        // The listing and the map are often asked for together, and the
        // second would otherwise replay the whole recording again.
        switch ( m_censusRun.enter(progress, [this] { return cached_census() != nullptr; }) )
        {
            case SharedRun::Turn::Ready:
                return from_cache();
            case SharedRun::Turn::Cancelled:
            {
                // Cancelled while waiting: an empty census, which both
                // callers present as the partial answer a cancelled census
                // gives.
                auto none = std::make_shared<SyscallCensus>();
                none->table  = std::make_shared<SyscallTable>();
                none->memmap = empty_memmap_records();
                qr->ran       = true;
                qr->cancelled = true;
                return none;
            }
            case SharedRun::Turn::Run:
                break;
        }
        SharedRun::Runner runner(m_censusRun, progress);

        auto table = std::make_shared<SyscallTable>();
        const bool named = build_syscall_table(this, table.get());
        std::unique_ptr<MemmapHooks> mm = make_memmap_hooks(this, *table);
        if ( need_memmap && mm == nullptr )
        {
            // The map has nothing to look for; a replay now would serve only
            // a listing nobody asked for.
            auto none = std::make_shared<SyscallCensus>();
            none->table = table;
            return none;
        }
        if ( !named )
            msttd_log("[ida-ttd] syscalls: no ntdll stubs were readable in this recording, so they "
                      "are listed by number only.\n");

        KernelCallOptions opts;
        opts.args_wanted = [](uint32_t) { return false; };
        if ( mm != nullptr )
            mm->arm(&opts);
        std::vector<KernelCall> calls;
        QueryResult kr = collect_kernel_calls(this, *table, opts, &calls, &runner);
        if ( !kr.ran )
            return nullptr;

        auto c = std::make_shared<SyscallCensus>();
        c->table     = table;
        c->truncated = kr.truncated;
        if ( mm != nullptr )
            c->memmap = mm->finish();
        // Which returns the census settles for good. With the call/return
        // callback (chains) it saw every return made by a ret. A stub's
        // syscall is followed by its ret on x64, so one the census did not
        // see come back never did. Code making its own syscalls may come
        // back to anything, and on x86 the return into the stub has not been
        // measured against the watchpoints, so those are left to the return
        // pass, which watches the instruction itself.
        const bool settled = opts.chains && m_info.is64;
        bool to_watch = false;
        c->calls.reserve(calls.size());
        for ( const KernelCall &k : calls )
        {
            CensusSyscall s;
            s.pos      = k.pos;
            s.ret_pc   = k.ret_pc;
            s.name     = k.name;
            s.utid     = k.utid;
            s.tid      = k.tid;
            s.number   = k.number;
            s.result   = k.result;
            s.returned = k.returned;
            s.to_watch = !k.returned && k.ret_pc != 0 && (!settled || k.stub == BADADDR);
            to_watch  |= s.to_watch;
            c->calls.push_back(s);
        }
        c->results = !kr.cancelled && !to_watch;
        auto regs = std::make_shared<std::vector<CensusRegs>>();
        regs->reserve(std::min(calls.size(), kMaxCachedRegs));
        for ( const KernelCall &k : calls )
        {
            if ( regs->size() >= kMaxCachedRegs )
                break;
            CensusRegs cr;
            cr.pos = k.pos;
            memcpy(cr.gp, k.gp, sizeof(cr.gp));
            cr.rflags = k.rflags;
            regs->push_back(cr);
        }
        c->regs = std::move(regs);
        *qr = kr;
        if ( !kr.cancelled )
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_censusMtx);
            m_census = c;
        }
        return c;
    }

    QueryResult MsTtdBackend::query_syscalls(std::vector<SyscallEvent> *out, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        QueryResult r;
        if ( !m_engine || out == nullptr )
            return r;
        // The census takes most of the results, and is most of the time; the
        // return pass watches a few addresses, which the engine filters on.
        std::shared_ptr<const SyscallCensus> c = cached_census();
        const bool fresh = c == nullptr;
        if ( fresh )
        {
            ScaledProgress first(progress, 0, 90);
            c = syscall_census(false, &first, &r);
            if ( c == nullptr || !r.ran )
                return r;
        }
        else
        {
            r.ran       = true;
            r.truncated = c->truncated;
        }
        const std::vector<CensusSyscall> *calls = &c->calls;
        std::vector<CensusSyscall> with_results;
        if ( !c->results && !r.cancelled )
        {
            with_results = c->calls;
            ScaledProgress second(progress, fresh ? 90 : 0, fresh ? 10 : 100);
            bool trunc = false;
            const bool complete = collect_kernel_returns(this, &with_results, &second, &trunc);
            r.cancelled = !complete;
            r.truncated = r.truncated || trunc;
            calls = &with_results;
            if ( complete )
            {
                // Kept in place of the census without results, unless another
                // query replaced or dropped that one meanwhile.
                auto done = std::make_shared<SyscallCensus>();
                done->table             = c->table;
                done->regs              = c->regs;
                done->truncated         = c->truncated;
                done->memmap            = c->memmap;
                done->results           = true;
                done->results_truncated = trunc;
                done->calls             = std::move(with_results);
                calls = &done->calls;
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_censusMtx);
                if ( m_census == c )
                    m_census = done;
                c = std::move(done);
            }
        }
        else if ( c->results )
        {
            r.truncated = r.truncated || c->results_truncated;
        }

        size_t returned = 0;
        for ( const CensusSyscall &s : *calls )
            returned += s.returned ? 1 : 0;
        msttd_log("[ida-ttd] syscalls: %d listed, %d with a result%s.\n",
                  (int)calls->size(), (int)returned, r.truncated ? " (cut short)" : "");
        out->reserve(out->size() + calls->size());
        for ( const CensusSyscall &s : *calls )
        {
            SyscallEvent e;
            e.pos    = to_core(s.pos);
            e.result = s.result;
            e.number = s.number;
            e.tid    = s.tid;
            if ( s.name != nullptr )
                e.name = s.name;
            out->push_back(std::move(e));
        }
        return r;
    }
}
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_syscalls.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class MsTtdBackend;

    // The syscalls of a Microsoft recording.
    //
    // The recording does not list them, but the engine reports every kernel
    // transition as a KernelCall gap on the syscall instruction. That catches
    // syscalls made anywhere (an ntdll stub or the program's own code), which
    // watching ntdll's exports cannot. The number is in rax (eax) there; the
    // name comes from the recorded ntdll's stubs, each of which starts by
    // loading its number.

    static const size_t kKernelCallArgs = 12;

    struct KernelCall
    {
        TTD::Replay::Position pos;          // at the syscall instruction
        uint32_t  utid      = 0;            // UniqueId, for SetPositionOnThread
        uint32_t  tid       = 0;            // the OS thread id
        ea_t      pc        = BADADDR;      // the syscall instruction
        uint64_t  ret_pc    = 0;            // where the kernel returns to; 0 unknown
        uint64_t  sp        = 0;
        uint32_t  number    = 0;
        // The general registers going in (ITTD_REG_*), so a listing of
        // syscalls shows their arguments without seeking to each one.
        uint64_t  gp[ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT] = { 0 };
        uint64_t  rflags    = 0;
        const char *name    = nullptr;      // in the SyscallTable; nullptr unknown
        ea_t      stub      = BADADDR;      // the ntdll/win32u stub it was made from, if one
        uint64_t  args[kKernelCallArgs] = { 0 };    // as the kernel takes them
        // With chains: innermost first, one frame per module crossed. It
        // starts at the call into the stub, or at the syscall itself when
        // the program made its own.
        ea_t      chain[ITTD_CHAIN_MAX] = { 0 };
        uint8_t   chain_n   = 0;
        // With chains: where the innermost open call returns to (for a
        // stub's syscall, back into the stub's caller).
        uint64_t  frame_ret = 0;
        // With chains: rax (eax) where the kernel came back, when the census
        // saw it (see collect_kernel_calls).
        uint64_t  result    = 0;
        bool      returned  = false;
    };

    // Syscall number -> Nt* name, from the stubs of every ntdll in the
    // recording.
    struct SyscallTable
    {
        std::map<uint32_t, std::string> names;
        std::multimap<uint32_t, ea_t>   stubs;  // number -> each stub that makes it
        const char *name_of(uint32_t n) const
        {
            auto it = names.find(n);
            return it != names.end() ? it->second.c_str() : nullptr;
        }
        // Every number 'name' is made with (WoW64: a 32-bit one as well).
        std::vector<uint32_t> numbers_of(const char *name) const;
        // The stub syscall 'n' made at 'pc' belongs to; BADADDR when it was
        // made from anywhere else.
        ea_t stub_of(uint32_t n, ea_t pc) const;
    };

    bool build_syscall_table(const MsTtdBackend *backend, SyscallTable *out);

    // Every module as [lo, hi), sorted by base, one per distinct base.
    std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> module_ranges(const std::vector<ModuleInfo> &mods);

    struct KernelCallOptions
    {
        // Which numbers get their arguments read (and, with chains, their
        // chain). Empty: every one.
        std::function<bool(uint32_t)> args_wanted;
        // The call chain that led to each syscall, which costs a call/return
        // callback on every call in the recording. The same callback sees
        // each syscall come back (KernelCall::result).
        bool chains = false;
        // With chains: told of every call and return the recording makes, on
        // the replay thread, after the shadow stack has taken it. 'target'
        // is the callee, or the address returned to.
        std::function<void(TTD::Replay::IThreadView const *, uint32_t utid, bool is_return,
                           uint64_t target)> on_call_ret;
        // Told of each syscall as the census reads it, on the replay thread.
        std::function<void(const KernelCall &, TTD::Replay::IThreadView const *)> on_syscall;
    };

    // Every syscall in the recording, in position order: one replay.
    QueryResult collect_kernel_calls(const MsTtdBackend *backend, const SyscallTable &table,
                                     const KernelCallOptions &opts,
                                     std::vector<KernelCall> *out, ProgressSink *progress);

    // One syscall as the census keeps it between queries: what the listing
    // shows and what the return pass needs. The registers are kept apart
    // (SyscallCensus::regs) and the arguments not at all, so a census at the
    // cap of a million syscalls stays near 60 MB.
    struct CensusSyscall
    {
        TTD::Replay::Position pos;          // at the syscall instruction
        uint64_t    ret_pc   = 0;           // where the kernel returns to; 0 unknown
        uint64_t    result   = 0;           // from the census, or the return pass
        const char *name     = nullptr;     // in the census's SyscallTable; nullptr unknown
        uint32_t    utid     = 0;
        uint32_t    tid      = 0;
        uint32_t    number   = 0;
        bool        returned = false;       // seen coming back
        // Left to the return pass: the census cannot tell whether it came
        // back (see syscall_census).
        bool        to_watch = false;
    };

    // The general registers going into one syscall, so the listing's
    // argument column costs no seek per row.
    struct CensusRegs
    {
        TTD::Replay::Position pos;
        uint64_t gp[ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT];
        uint64_t rflags;
    };

    // What the memory map keeps from the census replay (msttd_memmap.cpp).
    struct MemmapRecords;

    // The syscall census, kept by the backend so the listing and the memory
    // map share one replay, whichever is asked first: the map's call/return
    // callback costs little next to the replay itself, so the census always
    // collects the map's records too. Immutable once cached; a return pass
    // that completes caches a copy with the results.
    struct SyscallCensus
    {
        std::shared_ptr<const SyscallTable> table;     // the names point into it
        std::vector<CensusSyscall> calls;              // in position order
        // The first syscalls' registers, in position order (shared by the
        // copy a return pass makes). Capped: they are a convenience, and
        // registers_at seeks for the rest.
        std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<CensusRegs>> regs;
        bool truncated = false;                        // the census was cut short
        // Every result is known: the census took them all, or the return
        // pass ran to the end.
        bool results   = false;
        bool results_truncated = false;
        // Null when the recording names none of the memory syscalls.
        std::shared_ptr<const MemmapRecords> memmap;
    };

    // Records with nothing in them, for a census given up while waiting for
    // another (msttd_memmap.cpp).
    std::shared_ptr<const MemmapRecords> empty_memmap_records();

    // The memory map's part of the census (msttd_memmap.cpp): callbacks that
    // settle each memory syscall as the replay passes its return.
    class MemmapHooks
    {
    public:
        virtual ~MemmapHooks() = default;
        // Sets the options the map needs; the hooks must outlive the replay.
        virtual void arm(KernelCallOptions *opts) = 0;
        // What the replay settled, taken once it has ended.
        virtual std::shared_ptr<const MemmapRecords> finish() = 0;
    };
    // Null when 'table' names none of the memory syscalls.
    std::unique_ptr<MemmapHooks> make_memmap_hooks(const MsTtdBackend *backend, const SyscallTable &table);
}
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_trace_open.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_trace_open.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_backend.h"
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_host.h"

using namespace TTD;
using namespace TTD::Replay;

namespace idattd
{
    void __fastcall MsttdErrorReporting::VPrintError(char const *pFmt, va_list argList)
    {
        char buf[2048];
        vsnprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), pFmt, argList);
        msttd_log("[ida-ttd] TTD: %s\n", buf);
        if ( owner != nullptr )
            owner->set_error("TTD: %s", buf);
    }

    // TTD invokes this from its own indexing worker threads, with the sink as
    // its context. A sink takes calls from any thread; this only passes the
    // percentage on.
    static void __stdcall index_progress(void const *ctx, IndexBuildProgressType const *d) noexcept
    {
        ProgressSink *sink = (ProgressSink *)ctx;
        if ( sink != nullptr && d != nullptr && d->KeyframeCount > 0 )
            sink->report((uint32_t)((uint64_t)d->KeyframesProcessed * 100 / d->KeyframeCount));
    }

    bool build_trace_index(IReplayEngine *engine, ProgressSink *progress)
    {
        if ( engine == nullptr )
            return false;
        if ( engine->GetIndexStatus() == IndexStatus::IndexFileLoaded )
            return true;

        IndexStatus st = IndexStatus::IndexFileNotPresent;
        try { st = engine->BuildIndex(index_progress, progress, IndexBuildFlags::None); }
        catch ( ... ) {}

        // IndexFileUnloadable is normal here: the engine still builds and uses
        // an in-memory index; this status describes only the on-disk .idx file.
        if ( st != IndexStatus::IndexFileLoaded )
            msttd_log("[ida-ttd] TTD index build finished with status %d (in-memory index still usable).\n", (int)st);
        return true;
    }
}
```

```h
#pragma once

#include "backend-msttd/msttd_pch.h"
#include "common/strings.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // What opening a TTD trace needs besides the engine itself: somewhere for
    // its diagnostics to go, and the memory index.

    class MsTtdBackend;

    // Error sink so the TTD engine's diagnostics reach the host's log, and
    // become the backend's last error: the engine says why it failed here
    // and nowhere else.
    class MsttdErrorReporting : public TTD::ErrorReporting
    {
    public:
        void __fastcall VPrintError(char const *pFmt, va_list argList) override;

        const MsTtdBackend *owner = nullptr;
    };

    // Build the trace's memory index if it has none; without one, memory reads
    // are severely limited.
    //
    // BuildIndex is synchronous and can take minutes, so the core runs this on
    // a worker thread behind a wait box. The percentage reaches 'progress'
    // (may be null) from TTD's own indexing threads. The build cannot be
    // interrupted: the progress callback returns void and there is no
    // cancellation flag.
    //
    // Returns true when the trace has a usable index. IndexFileUnloadable still
    // counts: the engine keeps an in-memory index, and GetIndexStatus()
    // describes only the on-disk .idx file.
    bool build_trace_index(TTD::Replay::IReplayEngine *engine, ProgressSink *progress);
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_x86.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "backend-msttd/msttd_x86.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Bytes the ModRM operand takes after the ModRM byte itself (SIB and
    // displacement), or -1 when 'n' runs out first.
    static int modrm_tail(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, size_t at, bool addr16)
    {
        if ( at >= n )
            return -1;
        uint8_t modrm = b[at];
        uint8_t mod = modrm >> 6, rm = modrm & 7;
        if ( mod == 3 )
            return 0;
        if ( addr16 )
        {
            if ( mod == 0 )
                return rm == 6 ? 2 : 0;
            return mod == 1 ? 1 : 2;
        }
        int extra = 0;
        if ( rm == 4 )
        {
            if ( at + 1 >= n )
                return -1;
            extra = 1;
            uint8_t base = b[at + 1] & 7;
            if ( mod == 0 && base == 5 )
                return extra + 4;
        }
        if ( mod == 0 )
            return extra + (rm == 5 ? 4 : 0);    // rm 5: disp32, RIP-relative in 64-bit
        return extra + (mod == 1 ? 1 : 4);
    }

    X86Branch x86_branch(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, bool is64)
    {
        X86Branch r;
        size_t i = 0;
        bool addr16 = false;
        for ( ; i < n && i < 15; i++ )
        {
            uint8_t p = b[i];
            if ( p == 0x67 )
                addr16 = !is64;
            else if ( !(p == 0x66 || p == 0xF2 || p == 0xF3 || p == 0xF0 || p == 0x2E || p == 0x3E
                     || p == 0x26 || p == 0x36 || p == 0x64 || p == 0x65) )
                break;
        }
        if ( is64 && i < n && (b[i] & 0xF0) == 0x40 )
            i++;                                    // REX
        if ( i >= n )
            return r;

        uint8_t op = b[i];
        if ( op == 0xC3 || op == 0xC2 || op == 0xCB || op == 0xCA )
        {
            r.is_ret = true;
            return r;
        }
        if ( op == 0xE8 )
        {
            r.is_call = true;
            r.len     = (int)i + 5;
            return r;
        }
        if ( op == 0x9A && !is64 )
        {
            r.is_call = true;
            r.len     = (int)i + 7;                 // ptr16:32
            return r;
        }
        if ( op == 0xFF && i + 1 < n )
        {
            uint8_t reg = (b[i + 1] >> 3) & 7;
            if ( reg != 2 && reg != 3 )
                return r;
            int tail = modrm_tail(b, n, i + 1, addr16);
            if ( tail < 0 )
                return r;
            r.is_call = true;
            r.len     = (int)i + 2 + tail;
        }
        return r;
    }
}
```

`src/backend-msttd/msttd_x86.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>

namespace idattd
{
    // Just enough x86 decoding for the navigator: is the instruction a call
    // (and how long, since its return address is just past it) or a return.
    // A backend has no IDA decoder, and these questions need only the opcode,
    // ModRM, SIB and displacement.
    struct X86Branch
    {
        bool is_call = false;   // E8, FF /2, FF /3, 9A
        bool is_ret  = false;   // C3, C2 iw, CB, CA iw
        int  len     = 0;       // the call's length; 0 when it is not one
    };

    // 'b' holds up to 'n' bytes starting at the instruction; 'is64' is the
    // code's mode (64-bit, or 32-bit including WoW64 code).
    X86Branch x86_branch(const uint8_t *b, size_t n, bool is64);
}
```
