```cpp
                      ittd_buffer_hit *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count,
                      int *out_truncated, const ittd_progress *progress)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->scans.mtx);
            if ( recorded_scans(b) )
            {
                bool cut = false;
                const std::vector<ittd_buffer_hit> &v = recorded_buffers(b, progress, &cut);
                b->scan_note.clear();
                set_scan_truncated(out_truncated, v.size(), cap, buf != nullptr, cut);
                return fill(v, buf, cap, out_count, [](const ittd_buffer_hit &h) { return h; });
            }
            const std::string key = scan_key(settings);
            auto found = b->scans.buffers.find(key);
            if ( found == b->scans.buffers.end() )
            {
                std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> t = open_forward_trace(b->path);
                bool strict = false;
                auto emu = replay_emulator(*t, settings, &strict);
                std::optional<ttd::buffer_scanner> scanner;
                // What each scanner put away at a restore found, then the
                // last one's.
                std::vector<ttd::recovered_buffer> found_before;
                // A scanner checks every write against the recording and, at
                // the end, that none is missing. One put away at a divergence
                // fails both checks by definition; its results are kept
                // (finish hands them out before it throws).
                auto put_away = [&](bool diverged)
                {
                    if ( !scanner )
                        return;
                    try
                    {
                        scanner->finish();
                    }
                    catch ( const std::runtime_error & )
                    {
                        if ( !diverged )
                            throw;
                    }
                    found_before.insert(found_before.end(), scanner->results().begin(), scanner->results().end());
                    scanner.reset();
                };
                b->scans.notes[key] = replay_scan(*emu, *t, [&]() { scanner.emplace(*emu, *t); },
                                                 [&]() { put_away(true); }, [&]() { scanner.emplace(*emu, *t); },
                                                 strict, progress);
                // The last scanner ran to the end unless the last divergence
                // had no checkpoint after it.
                put_away(!b->scans.notes[key].empty());
                std::vector<ittd_buffer_hit> v;
                for ( const ttd::recovered_buffer &r : found_before )
                    v.push_back(buffer_hit(r.address, r.size, r.first_step, r.last_step, r.writer_ip, r.writes,
                                           r.kind, r.preview));
                found = b->scans.buffers.emplace(key, std::move(v)).first;
            }
            b->scan_note.set(b->scans.notes[key]);
            set_truncated(out_truncated, found->second.size(), cap, buf != nullptr);
            return fill(found->second, buf, cap, out_count, [](const ittd_buffer_hit &h) { return h; });
        });
    }
}

```

`src/backend-sogen/sogen_session.cpp`:

```cpp
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only
//
// ida-ttd's Sogen backend: the recording as a whole (identity, open,
// info, positions, threads, modules, the timeline, symbols, the replay
// environment) and the cursors.
// See sogen_state.h.

#include "backend-sogen/sogen_state.h"

namespace idattd::sogen
{
    text_slot g_module_error;       // last_error(NULL)

    uint64_t fold_id(const std::string &id)
    {
        // At most 33 ASCII characters: 32 hex digits, or "h" and 32 hex digits
        // for traces older than the stored id. Any 64 of the bits will do;
        // this takes the first 16 digits.
        size_t start = !id.empty() && id[0] == 'h' ? 1 : 0;
        uint64_t v = 0;
        for ( size_t i = start; i < id.size() && i < start + 16; i++ )
        {
            char c = id[i];
            uint64_t d = c >= '0' && c <= '9' ? c - '0'
                       : c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' ? c - 'a' + 10
                       : c >= 'A' && c <= 'F' ? c - 'A' + 10 : 0;
            v = v << 4 | d;
        }
        return v;
    }

    // Every thread with the span it ran over, in the order they first ran.
    std::vector<thread_span> thread_spans(const ttd::trace &t)
    {
        std::map<uint32_t, thread_span> by_tid;
        const auto &sw = t.threads().switches;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < sw.size(); i++ )
        {
            thread_span &s = by_tid[sw[i].thread_id];
            s.tid = sw[i].thread_id;
            s.first_step = std::min(s.first_step, sw[i].step);
            uint64_t end = i + 1 < sw.size() ? sw[i + 1].step : last_position(t) + 1;
            s.end_step = std::max(s.end_step, end);
            s.running_at_end = i + 1 == sw.size();
        }
        std::vector<thread_span> v;
        v.reserve(by_tid.size());
        for ( auto &[tid, s] : by_tid )
            v.push_back(s);
        std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](const thread_span &a, const thread_span &b)
                  { return a.first_step < b.first_step; });
        return v;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ identity

    const char *id() { return "sogen"; }
    const char *display_name() { return "Sogen"; }
    const char *file_filter() { return "Sogen TTD trace (*.sogttd)"; }

    int can_open(const char *path)
    {
        // Any version: an unsupported one should reach open() and say why,
        // rather than fall through to "IDA does not know this file".
        try
        {
            return path != nullptr && ttd::is_trace_file(utf8_path(path)) ? 1 : 0;
        }
        catch ( ... )
        {
            return 0;
        }
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ session

    ittd_backend *open(const char *path)
    {
        if ( path == nullptr )
        {
            g_module_error.set("no path");
            return nullptr;
        }
        backend_t *opened = nullptr;
        guarded(g_module_error, [&]()
        {
            auto b = std::make_unique<backend_t>();
            b->path  = utf8_path(path);
            b->trace = open_trace(b->path);
            b->trace->set_checkpoint_cache_size(kCheckpointsPerReader);
            b->spans = thread_spans(*b->trace);
            if ( b->trace->has_memory_regions() )
            {
                constexpr uint32_t kMmioKind = 5;
                for ( const ttd::memory_region &r : b->trace->memory_regions().regions )
                    if ( r.kind == kMmioKind && r.size != 0 )
                        b->mmio.emplace_back(r.address, r.address + r.size);
                b->regions.build(b->trace->memory_regions().regions);
            }
            opened = b.release();
            return ITTD_OK;
        });
        return reinterpret_cast<ittd_backend *>(opened);
    }

    void close(ittd_backend *b)
    {
        delete B(b);
    }

    // Both copy the text, which can throw (out of memory); nothing may cross
    // the C ABI, so a failed copy reads as no message.
    const char *last_error(ittd_backend *b)
    {
        try
        {
            return b == nullptr ? g_module_error.get() : B(b)->error.get();
        }
        catch ( ... )
        {
            return "";
        }
    }

    const char *scan_notice(ittd_backend *b)
    {
        try
        {
            return b == nullptr ? "" : B(b)->scan_note.get();
        }
        catch ( ... )
        {
            return "";
        }
    }

    int info(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_trace_info *out)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            const ttd::trace &t = *b->trace;
            *out = ittd_trace_info{};
            const ttd::module_entry *m = main_module(t);
            out->is64 = is64(t) ? 1 : 0;
            out->capabilities = ITTD_CAP_ACCESS_QUERIES | ITTD_CAP_CALL_QUERIES
                              | ITTD_CAP_RECORDED_EXPORTS
                              | ITTD_CAP_REVERSE_STEP | ITTD_CAP_BATCH_REGS;
            if ( t.has_syscalls() )
                out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_SYSCALLS;
            // Only offered when the recording holds the events the query
            // needs. A chunked recording names its event kinds in its
            // header; an older one would need a walk over every event to
            // find out (access_mask), too slow here, so self-modifying code
            // stays offered and answers with an error that says what is
            // missing, while exceptions, which need chunked data, are not.
            const uint64_t X  = (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::execute;
            const uint64_t W  = (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::write;
            const uint64_t HW = (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::host_write;
            if ( t.has_access_data() )
            {
                const uint64_t mask = b->trace->access_mask();
                if ( (mask & (W | X)) == (W | X) )
                    out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_SELF_MODIFYING;
                if ( (mask & (X | HW)) == (X | HW) )
                    out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_EXCEPTIONS;
            }
            else
            {
                out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_SELF_MODIFYING;
            }
            // Any recording can be replayed to a position; fork_open finds
            // out whether the replay holds on this machine.
            out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_FORK | ITTD_CAP_REPLAY_SCANS;
            // The memory map with protections (section 17), in traces
            // recorded since Sogen kept it. Older ones only say that a range
            // was mapped or unmapped, which is not enough to draw a map.
            if ( t.has_memory_regions() )
                out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_MAPPING_CHANGES;
            // With checkpoint memory, memory_at starts from the checkpoint and
            // applies the writes since (ttd/next ada569b0): tens of
            // microseconds a page once the checkpoint is decoded. Without it,
            // a page read walks every access to the page.
            if ( t.has_checkpoint_memory() )
                out->capabilities |= ITTD_CAP_CHEAP_READS;
            out->fingerprint = fold_id(t.id());
            out->first = at(first_position(t));
            out->last  = at(last_position(t));
            copy_str(out->main_module, sizeof(out->main_module), m != nullptr ? m->name : std::string());
            copy_str(out->backend_name, sizeof(out->backend_name), "Sogen");
            return ITTD_OK;
        });
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ positions

    int format_position(ittd_backend *, ittd_position p, char *buf, size_t buf_size)
    {
        if ( buf == nullptr || buf_size == 0 )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        if ( same(p, NONE) )
            std::snprintf(buf, buf_size, "-");
        else if ( same(p, END) )
            std::snprintf(buf, buf_size, "end");
        else
            std::snprintf(buf, buf_size, "%llu", (unsigned long long)p.lo);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    int parse_position(ittd_backend *, const char *text, ittd_position *out)
    {
        if ( text == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        while ( *text == ' ' || *text == '\t' )
            text++;
        if ( *text == '\0' )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        // What format_position prints for END reads back as END.
        if ( std::strncmp(text, "end", 3) == 0 )
        {
            const char *rest = text + 3;
            while ( *rest == ' ' || *rest == '\t' )
                rest++;
            if ( *rest == '\0' )
            {
                *out = END;
                return ITTD_OK;
            }
        }
        // strtoull accepts a sign and wraps "-1" round to UINT64_MAX.
        if ( *text < '0' || *text > '9' )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        char *end = nullptr;
        unsigned long long v = std::strtoull(text, &end, 10);
        while ( end != nullptr && (*end == ' ' || *end == '\t') )
            end++;
        if ( end == nullptr || *end != '\0' )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        *out = at(v);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    const char *position_syntax(ittd_backend *) { return "Instruction number, in decimal"; }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ cursors

    ittd_cursor *cursor_open(ittd_backend *hb)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return nullptr;
        cursor_t *opened = nullptr;
        guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            auto c = std::make_unique<cursor_t>();
            c->owner    = b;
            c->trace    = open_trace(b->path);
            c->trace->set_checkpoint_cache_size(kCheckpointsPerReader);
            c->position = first_position(*c->trace);
            opened = c.release();
            return ITTD_OK;
        });
        return reinterpret_cast<ittd_cursor *>(opened);
    }

    void cursor_close(ittd_cursor *c)
    {
        delete C(c);
    }

    int cursor_position(ittd_cursor *hc, ittd_position *out)
    {
        cursor_t *c = C(hc);
        if ( c == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        *out = at(c->position);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    void move(cursor_t *c, uint64_t position)
    {
        if ( position != c->position )
        {
            c->position = position;
            c->view.reset();
        }
    }

    int cursor_seek(ittd_cursor *hc, ittd_position p)
    {
        cursor_t *c = C(hc);
        if ( c == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        uint64_t pos = 0;
        if ( !resolve(*c->trace, p, &pos) )
            return ITTD_E_NO_POSITION;
        move(c, pos);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    int cursor_thread(ittd_cursor *hc, uint32_t *out)
    {
        cursor_t *c = C(hc);
        if ( c == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        *out = thread_after(*c->trace, c->position);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    // Through cpu_view::read_register, which decodes the saved register state
    // on one CPU per thread; view.cpu() would build an emulator per view.
    void read_regs(const ttd::cpu_view &view, ittd_regs *out)
    {
        *out = ittd_regs{};
        for ( int i = 0; i < ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT; i++ )
            out->gp[i] = view.read_register(kGp[i]);
        out->rflags  = view.read_register(x86_register::rflags);
        out->fs_base = view.read_register(x86_register::fs_base);
        out->gs_base = view.read_register(x86_register::gs_base);
        for ( int i = 0; i < ITTD_SEG_COUNT; i++ )
            out->seg[i] = (uint16_t)view.read_register(kSeg[i]);
        for ( int i = 0; i < 16; i++ )
            view.read_register((x86_register)((int)x86_register::xmm0 + i), out->xmm[i], 16);
        out->have = ITTD_REGS_GP | ITTD_REGS_SEG | ITTD_REGS_XMM;
    }

    int cursor_regs(ittd_cursor *hc, ittd_regs *out)
    {
        cursor_t *c = C(hc);
        if ( c == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(c->owner->error, [&]()
        {
            if ( !c->view )
                c->view = std::make_unique<ttd::cpu_view>(*c->trace, c->position);
            read_regs(*c->view, out);
            return ITTD_OK;
        });
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ threads

    ittd_thread to_thread(const ttd::trace &t, const thread_span &s)
    {
        ittd_thread th{};
        th.tid     = s.tid;
        th.created = before_step(s.first_step);
        // Sogen records when a thread last ran, not when it exited; the thread
        // running at the end is taken to be alive.
        th.exited  = s.running_at_end ? NONE : at(s.end_step - 1);
        auto name = t.threads().names.find(s.tid);
        copy_str(th.name, sizeof(th.name), name != t.threads().names.end() ? name->second : std::string());
        if ( const ttd::thread_stack *st = t.thread_stack_of(s.tid) )
        {
            th.teb         = st->teb;
            th.teb32       = st->teb32;
            th.stack_base  = st->stack_base;
            th.stack_limit = st->stack_limit;
        }
        return th;
    }

    int threads(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_thread *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            const ttd::trace &t = *b->trace;
            return fill(b->spans, buf, cap, out_count,
                        [&](const thread_span &s) { return to_thread(t, s); });
        });
    }

    int cursor_threads(ittd_cursor *hc, ittd_thread *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count)
    {
        cursor_t *c = C(hc);
        if ( c == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(c->owner->error, [&]()
        {
            const ttd::trace &t = *c->trace;
            std::vector<thread_span> live;
            for ( const thread_span &s : c->owner->spans )
                if ( s.first_step <= c->position + 1 && (s.running_at_end || c->position < s.end_step) )
                    live.push_back(s);
            return fill(live, buf, cap, out_count,
                        [&](const thread_span &s) { return to_thread(t, s); });
        });
    }

    int position_add(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_position p, int64_t delta, ittd_position *out)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        uint64_t pos = 0;
        if ( !resolve(*b->trace, p, &pos) )
            return ITTD_E_NO_POSITION;
        uint64_t lo = first_position(*b->trace), hi = last_position(*b->trace);
        if ( delta < 0 )
        {
            // In unsigned arithmetic: -delta overflows for INT64_MIN.
            const uint64_t back = 0ull - (uint64_t)delta;
            pos = pos - lo > back ? pos - back : lo;
        }
        else
            pos = hi - pos > (uint64_t)delta ? pos + (uint64_t)delta : hi;
        *out = at(pos);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ enumeration

    int modules(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_module *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            return fill(b->trace->modules(), buf, cap, out_count, [](const ttd::module_entry &m)
            {
                ittd_module out{};
                out.base     = m.base;
                out.size     = m.size;
                out.loaded   = at(m.load_step);
                out.unloaded = m.unload_step ? at(*m.unload_step) : NONE;
                out.machine  = m.machine;
                copy_str(out.name, sizeof(out.name), base_name(m.name.empty() ? m.path : m.name));
                copy_str(out.path, sizeof(out.path), m.path);
                return out;
            });
        });
    }

    int timeline(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_trace_event *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            ttd::trace &t = *b->trace;
            std::vector<ittd_trace_event> v;
            auto add = [&](ittd_position pos, uint32_t kind, uint32_t tid, const std::string &text)
            {
                ittd_trace_event e{};
                e.pos  = pos;
                e.kind = kind;
                e.tid  = tid;
                copy_str(e.text, sizeof(e.text), text);
                v.push_back(e);
            };
            for ( const ttd::module_entry &m : t.modules() )
            {
                std::string name = base_name(m.name.empty() ? m.path : m.name);
                add(at(m.load_step), ITTD_EV_MODULE_LOAD, 0, "Loaded " + name);
                if ( m.unload_step )
                    add(at(*m.unload_step), ITTD_EV_MODULE_UNLOAD, 0, "Unloaded " + name);
            }
            for ( const thread_span &s : b->spans )
            {
                char text[64];
                std::snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "Thread %u first runs", s.tid);
                add(before_step(s.first_step), ITTD_EV_THREAD_START, s.tid, text);
            }
            // Only where info() offers exceptions: trace::exceptions() throws
            // for a recording without the events it needs (an older,
            // unchunked one), which would lose the modules and threads too.
            const uint64_t xhw = (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::execute | (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::host_write;
            const bool has_exceptions = t.has_access_data() && (t.access_mask() & xhw) == xhw;
            std::vector<ttd::exception_event> exceptions;
            if ( has_exceptions )
            {
                try
                {
                    exceptions = t.exceptions();
                }
                catch ( const std::exception & )
                {
                    exceptions.clear();
                }
            }
            for ( const ttd::exception_event &e : exceptions )
            {
                char text[96];
                std::snprintf(text, sizeof(text), "Exception 0x%08X at 0x%llX",
                              e.code, (unsigned long long)e.address);
                add(before_step(e.step), ITTD_EV_EXCEPTION, e.thread_id, text);
            }
            std::stable_sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](const ittd_trace_event &a, const ittd_trace_event &b)
                             { return a.pos.hi != b.pos.hi ? a.pos.hi < b.pos.hi : a.pos.lo < b.pos.lo; });
            return fill(v, buf, cap, out_count, [](const ittd_trace_event &e) { return e; });
        });
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ symbols

    int module_symbols(ittd_backend *hb, uint64_t base, ittd_symbol *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            std::vector<ittd_symbol> v;
            for ( const ttd::module_entry &m : b->trace->modules() )
            {
                if ( m.base != base || m.exports == nullptr )
                    continue;
                for ( const ttd::module_export &e : *m.exports )
                {
                    // A forwarder's RVA points at the forwarder string, not
                    // code; the name belongs to the module it forwards to.
                    if ( !e.forwarder.empty() || e.name.empty() || e.name[0] == '#' )
                        continue;
                    ittd_symbol s{};
                    s.ea        = m.base + e.rva;
                    s.is_export = 1;
                    copy_str(s.name, sizeof(s.name), e.name);
                    v.push_back(s);
                }
                break;
            }
            return fill(v, buf, cap, out_count, [](const ittd_symbol &s) { return s; });
        });
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ the replay environment

    int replay_env(ittd_backend *hb, ittd_replay_env *out)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr || out == nullptr || out->size < sizeof(ittd_replay_env) )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
            const ttd::trace &t = *b->trace;
            const uint32_t size = out->size;
            std::memset(out, 0, size);
            out->size = size;
            const std::string root = manifest_value(t, "emulation_root");
            out->host = root.empty() ? 1 : 0;
            out->registry_known = manifest_value(t, "registry").empty() ? 0 : 1;
            out->registry_carried = t.has_registry_hives() ? 1 : 0;
            if ( const std::string dlls = manifest_value(t, "system_dlls"); !dlls.empty() )
            {
                const std::string here = system_dll_fingerprint(root);
                out->system_dlls = here.empty() ? ITTD_DLLS_UNKNOWN
                                 : here == dlls ? ITTD_DLLS_SAME : ITTD_DLLS_DIFFER;
            }
            copy_str(out->emulation_root, sizeof(out->emulation_root), root);
            // Where a replay in the root loads its hives from (whatever
            // registry_dir says), and where create-root.bat puts them.
            if ( !root.empty() )
                copy_str(out->registry_hint, sizeof(out->registry_hint),
                         path_utf8(utf8_path(root.c_str()) / "registry"));
            copy_str(out->windows_version, sizeof(out->windows_version), manifest_value(t, "windows_version"));
            return ITTD_OK;
        });
    }

    int check_registry(ittd_backend *hb, const char *dir)
    {
        backend_t *b = B(hb);
        if ( b == nullptr || dir == nullptr || *dir == '\0' )
            return ITTD_E_BAD_ARG;
        return guarded(b->error, [&]()
        {
            std::string recorded;
            {
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(b->mtx);
                recorded = manifest_value(*b->trace, "registry");
            }
            std::string why;
            const int rc = check_hives(recorded, utf8_path(dir), &why);
            if ( rc < 0 )
                throw coded_error(rc, why);
            return rc;
        });
    }
}

```

`src/backend-sogen/sogen_state.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-2.0-only
//
// ida-ttd's backend for Sogen time-travel traces (.sogttd): what its files
// share.
//
// ida-ttd-sogen.dll is loaded by the ida-ttd core through the C ABI in
// abi/ida_ttd_backend.h. It reads a recording through Sogen's trace reader
// and cpu_view, and replays one in Sogen's emulator (forks, replay scans,
// recording a program). Of ida-ttd it uses only the ABI header,
// common/local_path.h and common/write_scans.h, and it never sees an IDA
// type.
//
// Sogen is GPL-2.0-only, so ida-ttd-sogen.dll is a GPL-2.0 binary, and these
// files, which are only ever built into it, are GPL-2.0-only too
// (LICENSES/GPL-2.0-only.txt). The rest of ida-ttd is Apache-2.0 OR
// GPL-2.0-only (docs/licensing.md): nothing of Sogen's, and nothing here that
// pulls in more of the plugin, may cross that line.
//
// The files:
//
//  - sogen_state.h      the handles, the readers, and the helpers all share
//  - sogen_session.cpp  identity, open and info, positions, cursors, threads,
//                       modules, the timeline, symbols, the replay environment
//  - sogen_memory.cpp   the page cache and cursor_read_memory
//  - sogen_insn.h       what an executed instruction is (call, ret)
//  - sogen_nav.cpp      stepping, running, the entering call of a frame
//  - sogen_queries.cpp  the whole-recording queries, the heatmap, regs_at
//  - sogen_emulator.cpp registry hives, fork settings, the log relay, the
//                       network gate, and the emulators everything replays in
//  - sogen_fork.cpp     forks, writing a recording, record_program
//  - sogen_scans.cpp    replay scans, scans of the recorded writes,
//                       read_memory_at
//  - sogen_backend.cpp  the ABI table and the export
//
// Only the emulator, fork and scans files include Sogen's emulator.
//
// Conventions used throughout:
//
//  - Positions. Sogen position N is the state after instruction N, which is
//    the state before instruction N + 1: the ABI's meaning. A cursor position
//    is therefore a Sogen position with hi = 0. An event's step is the
//    1-based number of the instruction that did it, so its ABI position is
//    step - 1 (the state just before it).
//  - No exception leaves an entry point. Bodies run through guarded(), which
//    maps operation_cancelled to ITTD_E_CANCELLED and anything else to
//    ITTD_E_FAILED with the reason in last_error.
//  - One sogen::ttd::trace per handle and per cursor, plus one for the long
//    queries (query_reader). A trace is not thread-safe (one ifstream,
//    mutable caches, a lazily built CPU), and opening another costs about
//    25 ms, so none is shared.
//  - Everything is in namespace idattd::sogen, where "sogen::" would name
//    that namespace: Sogen's own is "::sogen::", and "ttd::" is its
//    ::sogen::ttd.

#pragma once

#include <abi/ida_ttd_backend.h>
#include <common/local_path.h>

#include <ttd_trace.hpp>
#include <ttd_view.hpp>

#include <algorithm>
#include <atomic>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <exception>
#include <filesystem>
#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <memory>
#include <mutex>
#include <optional>
#include <span>
#include <stdexcept>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

// Sogen's emulator, which only the files that run one include.
namespace sogen
{
    class windows_emulator;
    struct application_settings;
    struct emulator_settings;
}

namespace idattd::sogen
{
    namespace ttd = ::sogen::ttd;
    using ::sogen::x86_register;

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ handles

    // A message the core reads back through last_error or scan_notice.
    //
    // Written by whichever thread failed (a query on the core's worker, a
    // cursor call on IDA's main thread) and often read by another, so the
    // text is only touched under the mutex. The reader gets a copy in a
    // thread_local buffer, which stays valid until that thread asks again,
    // whatever other threads write meanwhile: the ABI's "valid until the next
    // call on the same handle".
    class text_slot
    {
      public:
        void set(std::string text)
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_mtx);
            m_text = std::move(text);
        }

        void clear() { set(std::string()); }

        const char *get() const
        {
            thread_local std::string copy;
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(m_mtx);
            copy = m_text;
            return copy.c_str();
        }

      private:
        mutable std::mutex m_mtx;
        std::string m_text;
    };

    // One page as memory_at showed it, and the positions it holds for.
    //
    // memory_at walks the page's recorded accesses until every byte is
    // accounted for, which on a hot code page (ntdll's, executed millions of
    // times) costs tens of milliseconds. IDA reads a module's code page by
    // page after every stop, so uncached reads froze it for minutes. A page
    // only changes at a write to it or a change to its mapping, so one read
    // answers every position in between.
    struct cached_page
    {
        uint64_t from = 0, to = 0;      // positions [from, to] it holds for
        uint64_t used = 0;              // for eviction
        std::vector<uint8_t> bytes, known;
        // For an MMIO page, the offsets 'known' marks, in order. A read of
        // KUSER_SHARED_DATA shows a few hundred of its bytes, and a miss
        // fills its unknown bytes from every other version of the page
        // cached (read_page), which grow with every stop: by these, a miss
        // costs what the versions know, not a page per version.
        std::vector<uint16_t> known_at;
    };

    struct page_cache
    {
        std::mutex mtx;
        std::unordered_map<uint64_t, std::vector<cached_page>> pages;   // by page base
        size_t   count = 0;
        uint64_t clock = 0;
    };

    // The memory regions section as an interval index over addresses, built
    // once at open. Every uncached page read asks which entries touch its
    // page (stable_span, mmio_page_near), and a walk of the whole table per
    // miss grew with every change the program made to its memory. A static
    // interval tree laid over the entries sorted by start: the middle entry
    // of each subrange keeps the highest end within the subrange.
    class region_index
    {
      public:
        void build(const std::vector<ttd::memory_region> &regions)
        {
            m_items.clear();
            m_items.reserve(regions.size());
            for ( const ttd::memory_region &r : regions )
                m_items.push_back({ r.address, r.address + r.size, r.step });
            std::sort(m_items.begin(), m_items.end(), [](const item &a, const item &b) { return a.lo < b.lo; });
            m_max.assign(m_items.size(), 0);
            build_max(0, m_items.size());
        }

        // fn(step) for every entry touching [lo, hi): starting below hi and
        // ending above lo. That counts an empty entry strictly inside the
        // range, as the table walk this replaces did.
        template <typename F>
        void for_each(uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, F &&fn) const
        {
            visit(0, m_items.size(), lo, hi, fn);
        }

      private:
        struct item
        {
            uint64_t lo, hi, step;
        };
        std::vector<item>     m_items;
        std::vector<uint64_t> m_max;    // by the middle index of each subrange

        uint64_t build_max(size_t b, size_t e)
        {
            if ( b >= e )
                return 0;
            const size_t m = b + (e - b) / 2;
            const uint64_t v = std::max({ m_items[m].hi, build_max(b, m), build_max(m + 1, e) });
            m_max[m] = v;
            return v;
        }

        template <typename F>
        void visit(size_t b, size_t e, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, F &fn) const
        {
            if ( b >= e )
                return;
            const size_t m = b + (e - b) / 2;
            if ( m_max[m] <= lo )
                return;                     // nothing in this subrange ends above lo
            visit(b, m, lo, hi, fn);
            if ( m_items[m].lo >= hi )
                return;                     // this entry and all to its right start too high
            if ( m_items[m].hi > lo )
                fn(m_items[m].step);
            visit(m + 1, e, lo, hi, fn);
        }
    };

    // One query's answer, kept from its count call to its fill.
    //
    // count-then-fill asks every question twice, and a query that computes
    // its answer from scratch (a walk over the event stream, a replay) did
    // all its work twice. The answer is kept under the arguments it was
    // asked with ('key'), so a different question is never answered from
    // it, and dropped once filled, or straight away when it is empty (the
    // core skips the fill of an empty answer), as abi_export keeps the
    // Microsoft backend's. A failure or a cancel keeps nothing.
    template <typename T>
    struct kept_answer
    {
        std::mutex mtx;
        std::string key;
        std::shared_ptr<const std::vector<T>> data;
        int served = 0;
    };

    // The parts of a recovered string a listing needs. An ittd_string_hit
    // is about 288 bytes, mostly a fixed text buffer, and the cached scans
    // hold every string of the recording for the backend's life (135k on a
    // test recording: 39 MB); this keeps the text at its own length.
    struct kept_string
    {
        uint64_t      address = 0;
        ittd_position pos{};
        uint32_t      length = 0;       // as the listing counts it
        bool          wide = false;
        std::string   text;
    };

    // A thread and the span it ran over, from the switch table.
    struct thread_span
    {
        uint32_t tid = 0;
        uint64_t first_step = UINT64_MAX;
        uint64_t end_step = 0;          // one past the last step it ran
        bool     running_at_end = false;
    };

    // The results of the scans, kept for the backend's life: each is a full
    // pass, and count-then-fill asks twice. Their own mutex keeps a scan
    // from holding up the other queries; the self-modifying code query's
    // pass takes it too.
    struct scan_cache
    {
        std::mutex mtx;
        // Keyed by what the replay ran with (scan_key), and for strings also
        // the minimum length, so a strict run is never answered by a lenient one.
        std::map<std::string, std::vector<kept_string>> strings;
        std::map<std::string, std::vector<ittd_buffer_hit>> buffers;
        // Whether a cached scan stopped keeping results at a scanner's own
        // limit, by the same keys, so a later fill still reports it.
        std::map<std::string, bool> strings_truncated, buffers_truncated;
        // What each cached scan skipped (scan_notice), by the same keys.
        std::map<std::string, std::string> notes;
        // query_access_heat's answers, by page shift and slice count.
        std::map<std::string, std::vector<ittd_heat_cell>> heat;
    };

    struct backend_t
    {
        std::filesystem::path path;
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> trace;   // for the short whole-trace calls
        std::mutex mtx;                      // guards 'trace'
        text_slot error;
        // The reader the long queries run on (query_reader), opened on first
        // use. Its own mutex means a query that takes seconds never holds
        // 'mtx', which the module and thread lists asked for at every stop
        // need.
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> query_trace;
        std::mutex query_mtx;                // guards 'query_trace'
        page_cache pages;                    // shared by this backend's cursors
        // Every thread's span, computed once at open: the switch table is
        // fixed, and the thread list is asked for at every stop.
        std::vector<thread_span> spans;
        scan_cache scans;
        // query_executed's answer, kept between its count and fill calls,
        // and the ranges it was for.
        std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> executed_ranges;
        std::vector<uint64_t> executed;
        bool executed_valid = false;
        // Address ranges recorded as MMIO at any time (region kind 5), whose
        // pages are cached only between accesses: memory_at reads them from
        // their accesses, so they change at reads too, not only at writes.
        std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, uint64_t>> mmio;
        // The memory regions section by address, for the page reads; fixed
        // after open, so read without a lock.
        region_index regions;
        // The answers of the queries that compute theirs from scratch, each
        // kept from its count call to its fill (kept_answer).
        kept_answer<ittd_access>      accesses_answer;
        kept_answer<ittd_call>        calls_answer;
        kept_answer<ittd_call_target> indirect_answer;
        kept_answer<ittd_exception>   exceptions_answer;
        kept_answer<ittd_selfmod>     selfmod_answer;
        // The last scan's notice (scan_notice).
        text_slot scan_note;
    };

    struct cursor_t
    {
        backend_t *owner = nullptr;
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> trace;   // this cursor's own reader
        uint64_t position = 0;
        std::vector<ittd_breakpoint> breakpoints;
        // The CPU at 'position', built on first use and dropped on every move.
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::cpu_view> view;
        // Cancel for the movements that walk (nav_set_progress); the core
        // keeps it valid until it clears it.
        const ittd_progress *progress = nullptr;
    };

    // Opens the real network once 'live' is set, and keeps the loopback-only
    // one until then: a fork reaches its position offline (the recording's
    // results stand in for what the network answered), then runs on with
    // the real one. Sockets made before the switch stay on the loopback
    // network, so a poll may hold both kinds; each goes to its own factory.
    struct net_gate
    {
        std::atomic<bool> live{false};
    };

    // A recording replayed to a position and held there (fork_open).
    struct fork_t
    {
        backend_t *owner = nullptr;
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> trace;               // its own reader: seek needs one
        std::unique_ptr<::sogen::windows_emulator> emu;
        uint64_t position = 0;
        bool     recorded = false;                       // fork_record runs once
        // From fork_open's settings, for fork_record (which has none).
        uint64_t access_kinds = ttd::all_access_kinds;
        uint64_t checkpoint_interval = 0;                // 0: Sogen's default
        // Set when the settings asked for the network: opened once the
        // replay has reached the position.
        std::shared_ptr<net_gate> net;
    };

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ helpers

    constexpr ittd_position NONE  = { UINT64_MAX, UINT64_MAX };
    constexpr ittd_position BEGIN = { 0, 0 };
    constexpr ittd_position END   = { UINT64_MAX, UINT64_MAX - 1 };

    inline bool same(ittd_position a, ittd_position b) { return a.hi == b.hi && a.lo == b.lo; }

    inline ittd_position at(uint64_t position) { return { 0, position }; }

    // The ABI position of the instruction whose step is 'step': just before it.
    inline ittd_position before_step(uint64_t step)
    {
        if ( step == UINT64_MAX || step == 0 )
            return NONE;
        return at(step - 1);
    }

    inline uint64_t first_position(const ttd::trace &t) { return t.start_position(); }
    inline uint64_t last_position(const ttd::trace &t)  { return t.metadata().instruction_count; }

    // Resolve the sentinels; false for NONE or a position outside the trace.
    inline bool resolve(const ttd::trace &t, ittd_position p, uint64_t *out)
    {
        if ( same(p, BEGIN) ) { *out = first_position(t); return true; }
        if ( same(p, END) )   { *out = last_position(t);  return true; }
        if ( same(p, NONE) || p.hi != 0 )
            return false;
        if ( p.lo < first_position(t) || p.lo > last_position(t) )
            return false;
        *out = p.lo;
        return true;
    }

    // An ABI position range as the inclusive range of event steps inside it.
    // Position a is just before step a + 1, and position b just after step b, so
    // the events between the two are steps a + 1 .. b.
    inline void step_range(const ttd::trace &t, ittd_position_range when, uint64_t *lo, uint64_t *hi)
    {
        uint64_t a = first_position(t), b = last_position(t);
        resolve(t, when.first, &a);
        resolve(t, when.last, &b);
        *lo = a + 1;
        *hi = b;
    }

    // How much of 'src' a field of 'cap' bytes holds with its terminator, cut
    // on a character boundary, never inside a UTF-8 sequence.
    inline size_t fitted_length(const std::string &src, size_t cap)
    {
        size_t n = std::min(src.size(), cap - 1);
        while ( n > 0 && n < src.size() && (static_cast<unsigned char>(src[n]) & 0xC0) == 0x80 )
            n--;
        return n;
    }

    inline void copy_str(char *dst, size_t cap, const std::string &src)
    {
        const size_t n = fitted_length(src, cap);
        std::memcpy(dst, src.data(), n);
        dst[n] = '\0';
    }

    inline std::string base_name(const std::string &path)
    {
        size_t slash = path.find_last_of("/\\");
        return slash == std::string::npos ? path : path.substr(slash + 1);
    }

    // The thread that runs the instruction after 'position'. cpu_view shows
    // its registers there, since a snapshot taken at a thread switch already
    // holds the incoming thread.
    inline uint32_t thread_after(const ttd::trace &t, uint64_t position)
    {
        if ( auto tid = t.thread_at(position + 1) )
            return *tid;
        if ( auto tid = t.thread_at(position) )
            return *tid;
        return 0;
    }

    // An ittd_progress as Sogen's operation_control. Both of Sogen's callbacks
    // run on the calling thread, which the ABI's sink allows.
    inline ttd::operation_control control(const ittd_progress *p)
    {
        ttd::operation_control c;
        if ( p == nullptr )
            return c;
        if ( p->cancelled != nullptr )
            c.interrupted = [p]() { return p->cancelled(p->ud) != 0; };
        if ( p->report != nullptr )
            c.progress = [p](uint64_t done, uint64_t total)
            {
                p->report(p->ud, total == 0 ? 0 : (uint32_t)std::min<uint64_t>(1000, done * 1000 / total));
            };
        return c;
    }

    // A failure the caller can act on, with its own ITTD_E_* code.
    struct coded_error : std::runtime_error
    {
        int code;
        coded_error(int c, const std::string &what) : std::runtime_error(what), code(c) {}
    };

    // Run 'body', mapping exceptions onto status codes and 'err'.
    template <typename F>
    inline int guarded(text_slot &err, F &&body)
    {
        try
        {
            return body();
        }
        catch ( const ttd::operation_cancelled & )
        {
            err.set("canceled");
            return ITTD_E_CANCELLED;
        }
        catch ( const coded_error &e )
        {
            err.set(e.what());
            return e.code;
        }
        catch ( const std::exception &e )
        {
            err.set(e.what());
            return ITTD_E_FAILED;
        }
        catch ( ... )
        {
            err.set("unknown error");
            return ITTD_E_FAILED;
        }
    }

    // The count-then-fill convention: write what fits, report the full count.
    template <typename T, typename Range, typename Conv>
    inline int fill(const Range &src, T *buf, size_t cap, size_t *out_count, Conv conv)
    {
        if ( out_count != nullptr )
            *out_count = src.size();
        if ( buf != nullptr )
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < src.size() && i < cap; i++ )
                buf[i] = conv(src[i]);
        return ITTD_OK;
    }

    // The ittd_access kind of a Sogen event. A host write (a syscall writing
    // guest memory) counts as a write for "who wrote this".
    inline uint32_t access_kind_of(ttd::access_kind k)
    {
        switch ( k )
        {
            case ttd::access_kind::read:       return ITTD_ACCESS_READ;
            case ttd::access_kind::write:
            case ttd::access_kind::host_write: return ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE;
            case ttd::access_kind::execute:    return ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC;
        }
        return 0;
    }

    inline uint64_t sogen_mask(uint32_t kinds)
    {
        uint64_t m = 0;
        if ( kinds & ITTD_ACCESS_READ )  m |= (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::read;
        if ( kinds & ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE ) m |= (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::write
                                            | (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::host_write;
        if ( kinds & ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC )  m |= (uint64_t)ttd::access_kind::execute;
        return m;
    }

    // The ABI's strings are UTF-8; a path built from char would be read in the
    // ANSI code page instead.
    inline std::filesystem::path utf8_path(const char *s)
    {
        return std::filesystem::path(std::u8string(reinterpret_cast<const char8_t *>(s)));
    }

    // Decoded checkpoints each reader keeps (Sogen's default is four). Each is
    // about the size of the program's committed memory, and every cursor has
    // a reader: with four, a session on a large recording passed half a
    // gigabyte. Two cover moving between a call and its return.
    constexpr size_t kCheckpointsPerReader = 2;

    inline std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> open_trace(const std::filesystem::path &path)
    {
        auto version = ttd::trace_file_version(path);
        if ( !version )
            throw std::runtime_error("not a Sogen trace");
        if ( !ttd::is_supported_trace_version(*version) )
        {
            char msg[160];
            std::snprintf(msg, sizeof(msg),
                          "Sogen trace format v%u; this backend reads v%u to v%u",
                          *version, ttd::oldest_trace_version, ttd::newest_trace_version);
            throw std::runtime_error(msg);
        }
        return std::make_unique<ttd::trace>(path);
    }

    // A reader for one pass that only moves forward (a scan, the heatmap, a
    // replay): it never returns to a checkpoint it has left, so keeping more
    // than the one decoded checkpoint would only hold memory.
    inline std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> open_forward_trace(const std::filesystem::path &path)
    {
        std::unique_ptr<ttd::trace> t = open_trace(path);
        t->set_checkpoint_cache_size(1);
        return t;
    }

    // The backend's reader for one long query, held for the query's whole run.
    //
    // Calls, accesses, regs_at, exceptions and the like run for seconds on
    // the core's worker thread. On the shared reader under 'mtx' they blocked
    // every main-thread call that takes it (the module and thread lists at
    // every stop, the timeline), so IDA hung behind its own wait box. They
    // use this reader under 'query_mtx' instead. It is opened once and kept:
    // a count query's second call then finds the chunks the first decoded
    // still cached, and a reader (with its decoded checkpoints) is too large
    // to keep several. Long queries therefore run one at a time.
    class query_reader
    {
      public:
        explicit query_reader(backend_t *b) : m_lock(b->query_mtx)
        {
            if ( b->query_trace == nullptr )
            {
                b->query_trace = open_trace(b->path);
                b->query_trace->set_checkpoint_cache_size(kCheckpointsPerReader);
            }
            m_trace = b->query_trace.get();
        }

        ttd::trace &trace() const { return *m_trace; }

      private:
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> m_lock;
        ttd::trace *m_trace = nullptr;
    };

    inline const ttd::module_entry *main_module(const ttd::trace &t)
    {
        // The program is the first .exe mapped, not the first module: Sogen
        // maps some system DLLs (win32u) before the executable.
        auto mods = t.modules();
        for ( const ttd::module_entry &m : mods )
        {
            std::string n = base_name(m.name.empty() ? m.path : m.name);
            if ( n.size() > 4 && _stricmp(n.c_str() + n.size() - 4, ".exe") == 0 )
                return &m;
        }
        return mods.empty() ? nullptr : &mods.front();
    }

    // Whether the program is 64-bit: anything but an i386 main module.
    inline bool is64(const ttd::trace &t)
    {
        const ttd::module_entry *m = main_module(t);
        return m == nullptr || m->machine != 0x14c;
    }

    // The general-purpose registers in ittd_regs.gp order.
    const x86_register kGp[ITTD_REG_GP_COUNT] = {
        x86_register::rax, x86_register::rcx, x86_register::rdx, x86_register::rbx,
        x86_register::rsp, x86_register::rbp, x86_register::rsi, x86_register::rdi,
        x86_register::r8,  x86_register::r9,  x86_register::r10, x86_register::r11,
        x86_register::r12, x86_register::r13, x86_register::r14, x86_register::r15,
        x86_register::rip,
    };

    // The segment selectors in ittd_regs.seg order.
    const x86_register kSeg[ITTD_SEG_COUNT] = {
        x86_register::cs, x86_register::ss, x86_register::ds,
        x86_register::es, x86_register::fs, x86_register::gs,
    };

    inline backend_t *B(ittd_backend *b) { return reinterpret_cast<backend_t *>(b); }
    inline cursor_t  *C(ittd_cursor *c)  { return reinterpret_cast<cursor_t *>(c); }

    constexpr uint64_t kPage = 0x1000;

    inline void set_truncated(int *out_truncated, size_t have, size_t cap, bool buf_given)

            *out_truncated = buf_given && have > cap ? 1 : 0;
    }
```

`src/common/apimeta/builtinsigs.cpp`:

```cpp
// Ported from ttd-capa-cpp (ttd/src/builtinsigs.cpp), Apache-2.0, by the same author.
// Kept close to the original so changes there can be carried over.
#include "builtinsigs.hpp"

namespace idattd::win32meta {
    namespace {

        constexpr uint8_t kIn = AttrIn;
        constexpr uint8_t kOut = AttrOut;
        constexpr uint8_t kInOut = AttrIn | AttrOut;
        constexpr uint8_t kInOpt = AttrIn | AttrOptional;

        // Every parameter below is pointer-sized or smaller, so the x86 footprint is
        // 4 in all but the one 64-bit case, which is why BuiltinParam defaults it.
        constexpr uint16_t kPtr = 8;

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 1. win32u: the win32k syscall stubs phnt's ntuser.h does not declare
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        //
        // Only the ones whose prototypes are not in doubt. NtUserCreateWindowEx and
        // NtUserRegisterClassExWOW are deliberately absent: they take a dozen-odd
        // parameters whose order is documented only by reimplementations, they
        // accounted for eight calls in the trace that motivated this, and a wrong
        // arity would misattribute every argument after the mistake.

        // SHORT NtUserGetAsyncKeyState(int Key)
        //
        // 576,705 calls in one desktop trace: the inner syscall of the
        // GetAsyncKeyState polling loop, and the largest single source of
        // invented arguments in the report.
        constexpr BuiltinParam kNtUserGetAsyncKeyState[] = {
            { "Key", "int", ArgKind::Integer, kIn, 4 },
        };

        // ULONG NtUserGetAtomName(ATOM Atom, PUNICODE_STRING AtomName)
        constexpr BuiltinParam kNtUserGetAtomName[] = {
            { "Atom",     "ATOM",             ArgKind::Integer,           kIn,  2 },
            { "AtomName", "UNICODE_STRING*",  ArgKind::CountedWideString, kOut, 16 },
        };

        // UINT NtUserRegisterWindowMessage(PUNICODE_STRING MessageName)
        constexpr BuiltinParam kNtUserRegisterWindowMessage[] = {
            { "MessageName", "UNICODE_STRING*", ArgKind::CountedWideString, kIn, 16 },
        };

        // BOOL NtUserUnregisterClass(PUNICODE_STRING ClassName, HINSTANCE Instance,
        //                            PVOID ClassMenuName)
        constexpr BuiltinParam kNtUserUnregisterClass[] = {
            { "ClassName",     "UNICODE_STRING*", ArgKind::CountedWideString, kIn,  16 },
            { "Instance",      "HINSTANCE",       ArgKind::Handle,            kIn,  kPtr },
            { "ClassMenuName", "PVOID",           ArgKind::Pointer,           kOut, 0 },
        };

        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // 2. the C runtime, exported by ntdll, msvcrt and ucrtbase
        // -------------------------------------------------------------------
        //
        // Standard C. ucrtbase additionally exports `_o_`-prefixed forwarders with
        // identical signatures, listed at the bottom against the same tables.
        //
        // These are worth signing not because a rule matches on strlen, but because
        // an unsignatured call reports four argument registers and any of them that
        // happens to point at text is rendered as a string. memset alone was 60,650
        // calls; that is 60,650 chances to invent a string feature.

        // Dest is left an opaque pointer on purpose. Capturing it would add a few
        // hundred bytes of hex to every one of 60,000 calls to say what Value and
        // Count already say, and the same content is captured once from Src on the
        // copies, where it is actual evidence.
        constexpr BuiltinParam kMemset[] = {
            { "Dest",  "void*",  ArgKind::Pointer, kIn, 0 },
            { "Value", "int",    ArgKind::Integer, kIn, 4 },
            { "Count", "size_t", ArgKind::Integer, kIn, 8 },
        };

        constexpr BuiltinParam kMemcpy[] = {
            { "Dest",  "void*",       ArgKind::Pointer,    kIn, 0 },
            { "Src",   "const void*", ArgKind::ByteBuffer, kIn, 1, 4, AuxKind::BytesFromParam, 2 },
            { "Count", "size_t",      ArgKind::Integer,    kIn, 8 },
        };

        constexpr BuiltinParam kMemcmp[] = {
            { "Buf1",  "const void*", ArgKind::ByteBuffer, kIn, 1, 4, AuxKind::BytesFromParam, 2 },
            { "Buf2",  "const void*", ArgKind::ByteBuffer, kIn, 1, 4, AuxKind::BytesFromParam, 2 },
            { "Count", "size_t",      ArgKind::Integer,    kIn, 8 },
        };

        constexpr BuiltinParam kStrOne[] = {
            { "Str", "const char*", ArgKind::AnsiString, kIn, 1 },
        };
        constexpr BuiltinParam kWcsOne[] = {
            { "Str", "const wchar_t*", ArgKind::WideString, kIn, 2 },
        };
        constexpr BuiltinParam kStrTwo[] = {
            { "Str1", "const char*", ArgKind::AnsiString, kIn, 1 },
            { "Str2", "const char*", ArgKind::AnsiString, kIn, 1 },
        };
        constexpr BuiltinParam kWcsTwo[] = {
            { "Str1", "const wchar_t*", ArgKind::WideString, kIn, 2 },
            { "Str2", "const wchar_t*", ArgKind::WideString, kIn, 2 },
        };
        constexpr BuiltinParam kStrTwoCount[] = {
```

`src/common/apimeta/builtinsigs.hpp`:

```hpp
// Ported from ttd-capa-cpp (ttd/src/builtinsigs.hpp), Apache-2.0, by the same author.
// Kept close to the original so changes there can be carried over.
#ifndef BUILTINSIGS_HPP
#define BUILTINSIGS_HPP

// The three small hand-written tables, and why each one has to be hand-written.
//
// Most signatures are generated: win32json for the documented Win32 surface
// (build-win32-index.py) and phnt for the native one (build-phnt-index.py). What
// no public source covers is:
//
//   1. win32u: the win32k syscall stubs. phnt's ntuser.h has 292 of them but not
//      NtUserGetAsyncKeyState, by far the most-called unsignatured function in a
//      desktop trace. Syscall-table projects publish names, not prototypes.
//
//   2. The C runtime (memset, strlen, malloc and friends), exported by ntdll,
//      msvcrt and ucrtbase. Standard C, and no metadata describes it.
//
//   3. The flag-enum overlay. phnt types every flag argument as a bare ULONG
//      (NtProtectVirtualMemory's NewProtection is not PAGE_PROTECTION_FLAGS).
//      win32json holds those enum tables, so this names one per function and
//      parameter. It is a judgement about meaning, so it cannot be generated.
//
// Keep all three short. A wrong prototype is worse than none: it turns "unknown"
// into a confident-looking value, the failure this subsystem exists to avoid.

#include <cstdint>
#include <span>

#include "win32meta.hpp"

namespace idattd::win32meta {

    // One parameter of a hand-written signature. Deliberately not ParamSig: the slot
    // is implied by position, and there is no enum index because the overlay below
    // names its enums instead of numbering them.
    struct BuiltinParam {
        const char* name = "";
        const char* type = "";
        ArgKind kind = ArgKind::Unknown;
        uint8_t attrs = 0;
        uint16_t pointeeSize = 0;
        uint8_t x86Footprint = 4;
        AuxKind auxKind = AuxKind::None;
        int32_t auxValue = 0;
    };

    struct BuiltinFunc {
        const char* name = "";
        const char* dll = "";
        const BuiltinParam* params = nullptr;
        uint8_t paramCount = 0;
    };

    // Names a win32json enum table for one parameter of one function.
    struct EnumOverlay {
        const char* function = "";
        const char* parameter = "";
        const char* enumName = "";
    };

    // Both tables are static storage, so their strings outlive any index.
    std::span<const BuiltinFunc> builtinSignatures();
    std::span<const EnumOverlay> builtinEnumOverlays();

}  // namespace idattd::win32meta

#endif

```

`src/common/apimeta/win32meta.cpp`:

```cpp
// Ported from ttd-capa-cpp (ttd/src/win32meta.cpp), Apache-2.0, by the same author.
// Kept close to the original so changes there can be carried over.
#include "win32meta.hpp"
#include "builtinsigs.hpp"

#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#include <windows.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cstring>
#include <fstream>

namespace idattd::win32meta {
    namespace {
        constexpr char kMagic[8] = { 'W', '3', '2', 'I', 'D', 'X', '0', '1' };
        constexpr uint32_t kFormatVersion = 1;

        // Record sizes must match the struct.pack formats in tools/build-win32-index.py.
        constexpr size_t kHeaderSize = 32;
        constexpr size_t kFuncRecSize = 16;
        constexpr size_t kParamRecSize = 24;
        constexpr size_t kEnumRecSize = 16;
        constexpr size_t kEnumValRecSize = 16;

        template <typename T>
        T readAt(const uint8_t* p, size_t off) {
            T v{};
            std::memcpy(&v, p + off, sizeof(T));
            return v;
        }

        int popcount64(uint64_t v) {
            int n = 0;
            while (v) {
                v &= v - 1;
                ++n;
            }
            return n;
        }
    }  // namespace

    bool Index::parseBlob(const std::filesystem::path& path, std::vector<Staged>& out,
                          bool withEnums, std::string& error) {
        std::ifstream f(path, std::ios::binary);
        if (!f) {
            error = "cannot open index";
            return false;
        }
        std::vector<uint8_t> blob((std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(f)), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        if (blob.size() < kHeaderSize || std::memcmp(blob.data(), kMagic, sizeof(kMagic)) != 0) {
            error = "not a win32 index file (bad magic)";
            return false;
        }

        const uint8_t* p = blob.data();
        uint32_t version = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 8);
        if (version != kFormatVersion) {
            error = "index format version " + std::to_string(version) +
                    ", expected " + std::to_string(kFormatVersion) + " (regenerate with tools/build-win32-index.py)";
            return false;
        }

        uint32_t funcCount = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 12);
        uint32_t paramCount = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 16);
        uint32_t enumCount = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 20);
        uint32_t enumValCount = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 24);
        uint32_t strtabSize = readAt<uint32_t>(p, 28);

        size_t funcOff = kHeaderSize;
        size_t paramOff = funcOff + static_cast<size_t>(funcCount) * kFuncRecSize;
        size_t enumOff = paramOff + static_cast<size_t>(paramCount) * kParamRecSize;
        size_t enumValOff = enumOff + static_cast<size_t>(enumCount) * kEnumRecSize;
        size_t strOff = enumValOff + static_cast<size_t>(enumValCount) * kEnumValRecSize;
        if (strOff + strtabSize != blob.size()) {
            error = "index is truncated or corrupt";
            return false;
        }
        // Every string offset is dereferenced without a bounds check below, so the
        // pool must be NUL-terminated for that to be safe.
        if (strtabSize == 0 || blob[blob.size() - 1] != 0) {
            error = "index string pool is not NUL-terminated";
            return false;
        }

        // The strings stay borrowed from here for the life of the index.
        blobs_.push_back(std::move(blob));
        p = blobs_.back().data();
        const char* strtab = reinterpret_cast<const char*>(p + strOff);
        auto str = [&](uint32_t off) -> const char* {
            return off < strtabSize ? strtab + off : "";
        };

        // Enum tables are appended, so a later source's indices are shifted past
        // those already loaded. Only the primary has any today; the offset keeps
        // a second table-bearing source correct.
        uint32_t enumBase = static_cast<uint32_t>(enums_.size());
        if (withEnums && enumCount != 0) {
            uint32_t valueBase = static_cast<uint32_t>(enumValues_.size());
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < enumValCount; ++i) {
                size_t o = enumValOff + static_cast<size_t>(i) * kEnumValRecSize;
                EnumValue ev;
                ev.name = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o));
                ev.value = readAt<int64_t>(p, o + 8);
                enumValues_.push_back(ev);
            }
            for (uint32_t i = 0; i < enumCount; ++i) {
                size_t o = enumOff + static_cast<size_t>(i) * kEnumRecSize;
                EnumTable et;
                et.name = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o));
                et.valueOffset = valueBase + readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 4);
                et.valueCount = readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 8);
                et.isFlags = p[o + 12] != 0;
                et.width = p[o + 13];
                if (static_cast<size_t>(et.valueOffset) + et.valueCount > enumValues_.size()) {
                    et.valueOffset = 0;
                    et.valueCount = 0;
                }
                enums_.push_back(et);
            }
        }

        std::vector<ParamSig> params(paramCount);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < paramCount; ++i) {
            size_t o = paramOff + static_cast<size_t>(i) * kParamRecSize;
            ParamSig& ps = params[i];
            ps.name = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o));
            ps.type = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 4));
            ps.kind = static_cast<ArgKind>(p[o + 8]);
            ps.attrs = p[o + 9];
            ps.slot = p[o + 10];
            ps.auxKind = static_cast<AuxKind>(p[o + 11]);
            ps.auxValue = readAt<int32_t>(p, o + 12);
            ps.enumIndex = readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 16);
            ps.pointeeSize = readAt<uint16_t>(p, o + 20);
            ps.x86Footprint = p[o + 22];
            if (ps.enumIndex != 0xFFFFFFFFu) {
                ps.enumIndex = withEnums && ps.enumIndex < enumCount
                    ? enumBase + ps.enumIndex
                    : 0xFFFFFFFFu;
            }
        }

        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < funcCount; ++i) {
            size_t o = funcOff + static_cast<size_t>(i) * kFuncRecSize;
            uint32_t firstParam = readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 8);
            uint8_t count = p[o + 12];
            if (static_cast<size_t>(firstParam) + count > params.size()) {
                error = "index parameter range out of bounds";
                return false;
            }
            Staged st;
            st.name = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o));
            st.dll = str(readAt<uint32_t>(p, o + 4));
            st.flags = p[o + 13];
            st.params.assign(params.begin() + firstParam, params.begin() + firstParam + count);
            out.push_back(std::move(st));
        }
        return true;
    }

    bool Index::load(const std::filesystem::path& path,
                     const std::vector<std::filesystem::path>& overlays,
                     std::string& error) {
        blobs_.clear();
        funcs_.clear();
        params_.clear();
        enums_.clear();
        enumValues_.clear();
        byName_.clear();

        std::vector<Staged> staged;
        if (!parseBlob(path, staged, /*withEnums=*/true, error)) {
            return false;
        }

        // Everything after the primary only fills gaps: an index built from real
        // metadata is richer than one recovered from headers or written by hand.
        // An entry the primary flagged unsupported is no answer, and is replaced.
        std::unordered_map<std::string_view, size_t> seen;
        seen.reserve(staged.size() * 2);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < staged.size(); ++i) {
            seen.emplace(std::string_view(staged[i].name), i);
        }

        auto absorb = [&](std::vector<Staged>& incoming) {
            for (Staged& st : incoming) {
                auto it = seen.find(std::string_view(st.name));
                if (it == seen.end()) {
                    seen.emplace(std::string_view(st.name), staged.size());
                    staged.push_back(std::move(st));
                } else if (staged[it->second].flags & FlagUnsupported) {
                    staged[it->second] = std::move(st);
                }
            }
        };

        for (const std::filesystem::path& overlay : overlays) {
            std::vector<Staged> extra;
            std::string overlayError;
            // An overlay is optional by design: a missing or unreadable one costs
            // coverage, not correctness, so it must not fail the whole load.
            if (!parseBlob(overlay, extra, /*withEnums=*/false, overlayError)) {
                // (the overlay is skipped)
                continue;
            }
            absorb(extra);
        }

        mergeBuiltins(staged);
        finalize(staged);
        path_ = path;
        return true;
    }

    void Index::finalize(std::vector<Staged>& staged) {
        size_t total = 0;
        for (const Staged& st : staged) {
            total += st.params.size();
        }
        // One contiguous array, built once. FuncSig::params points into it, so it
        // must never grow again; that is why every source is staged first.
        params_.reserve(total);
        funcs_.reserve(staged.size());
        byName_.reserve(staged.size() * 2);

        for (Staged& st : staged) {
            size_t first = params_.size();
            params_.insert(params_.end(), st.params.begin(), st.params.end());
            FuncSig fs;
            fs.name = st.name;
            fs.dll = st.dll;
            fs.paramCount = static_cast<uint8_t>(st.params.size());
            fs.flags = st.flags;
            fs.params = st.params.empty() ? nullptr : &params_[first];
            byName_[std::string_view(fs.name)] = static_cast<uint32_t>(funcs_.size());
            funcs_.push_back(fs);
        }
    }

    uint32_t Index::findEnum(const char* name) const {
        for (size_t i = 0; i < enums_.size(); ++i) {
            if (std::strcmp(enums_[i].name, name) == 0) {
                return static_cast<uint32_t>(i);
            }
        }
        return 0xFFFFFFFFu;  // the generator never referenced it; render the number
    }

    void Index::mergeBuiltins(std::vector<Staged>& staged) {
        std::unordered_map<std::string_view, size_t> byName;
        byName.reserve(staged.size() * 2);
        for (size_t i = 0; i < staged.size(); ++i) {
            byName.emplace(std::string_view(staged[i].name), i);
        }

        for (const BuiltinFunc& bf : builtinSignatures()) {
            auto it = byName.find(std::string_view(bf.name));
            if (it != byName.end() && !(staged[it->second].flags & FlagUnsupported)) {
                continue;  // a generated signature already covers it
            }
            Staged st;
            st.name = bf.name;
            st.dll = bf.dll;
            st.flags = 0;
            st.params.resize(bf.paramCount);
            for (uint8_t i = 0; i < bf.paramCount; ++i) {
                const BuiltinParam& src = bf.params[i];
                ParamSig& ps = st.params[i];
                ps.name = src.name;
                ps.type = src.type;
                ps.kind = src.kind;
                ps.attrs = src.attrs;
                ps.slot = i;  // none of these returns an aggregate needing a hidden pointer
                ps.auxKind = src.auxKind;
                ps.auxValue = src.auxValue;
                ps.pointeeSize = src.pointeeSize;
                ps.x86Footprint = src.x86Footprint;
                ps.enumIndex = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
            }
            if (it != byName.end()) {
                staged[it->second] = std::move(st);
            } else {
                byName.emplace(std::string_view(st.name), staged.size());
                staged.push_back(std::move(st));
            }
        }

        // The flag-enum overlay. phnt types every flag argument as a bare ULONG, so
        // the tables that name those bits live only in win32json's half of the index;
        // this is the one place the two sources are stitched together. Kept as a
        // hand-written list because it is a judgement about meaning, not a fact any
        // header states.
        for (const EnumOverlay& ov : builtinEnumOverlays()) {
            auto it = byName.find(std::string_view(ov.function));
            if (it == byName.end()) {
                continue;
            }
            uint32_t idx = findEnum(ov.enumName);
            if (idx == 0xFFFFFFFFu) {
                continue;  // win32json never referenced that enum; render the number
            }
            for (ParamSig& ps : staged[it->second].params) {
                if (std::strcmp(ps.name, ov.parameter) != 0) {
                    continue;
                }
                ps.enumIndex = idx;
                // A scalar the enum describes directly becomes an Enum; a pointer to
                // one keeps its pointer kind, and utils.cpp decodes the pointee.
                if (ps.kind == ArgKind::Integer) {
                    ps.kind = ArgKind::Enum;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    const FuncSig* Index::lookup(std::string_view api) const {
        auto it = byName_.find(api);
        return it == byName_.end() ? nullptr : &funcs_[it->second];
    }

    const char* Index::enumName(uint32_t enumIndex) const {
        return enumIndex < enums_.size() ? enums_[enumIndex].name : "";
    }

    std::vector<std::string> Index::decodeEnum(uint32_t enumIndex, uint64_t value) const {
        std::vector<std::string> out;
        if (enumIndex >= enums_.size()) {
            return out;
        }
        const EnumTable& et = enums_[enumIndex];
        // The captured value is a full 64-bit register; mask to the enum's real width
        // so sign-extension and upper garbage don't defeat the comparisons.
        uint64_t mask = et.width >= 8 ? ~0ull : ((1ull << (et.width * 8)) - 1);
        uint64_t v = value & mask;

        const EnumValue* vals = enumValues_.data() + et.valueOffset;
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < et.valueCount; ++i) {
            if ((static_cast<uint64_t>(vals[i].value) & mask) == v) {
                out.emplace_back(vals[i].name);
                return out;  // exact match wins, flags or not
            }
        }
        if (!et.isFlags || v == 0) {
            return out;
        }

        // Greedy decomposition: consume the widest matching bit groups first so
        // composites like GENERIC_WRITE beat their individual constituent bits.
        std::vector<uint32_t> order(et.valueCount);
        for (uint32_t i = 0; i < et.valueCount; ++i) {
            order[i] = i;
        }
        std::sort(order.begin(), order.end(), [&](uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
            return popcount64(static_cast<uint64_t>(vals[a].value) & mask) >
                   popcount64(static_cast<uint64_t>(vals[b].value) & mask);
        });

        uint64_t remaining = v;
        for (uint32_t i : order) {
            uint64_t bits = static_cast<uint64_t>(vals[i].value) & mask;
            if (bits != 0 && (remaining & bits) == bits) {
                out.emplace_back(vals[i].name);
                remaining &= ~bits;
            }
        }
        if (remaining != 0) {
            char buf[32];
            std::snprintf(buf, sizeof(buf), "0x%llx", static_cast<unsigned long long>(remaining));
            out.emplace_back(buf);
        }
        return out;
    }

    Index& index() {
        static Index instance;
        return instance;
    }

    namespace {
        std::filesystem::path executableDir() {
            // The directory of the module this code is in: the plugin.
            HMODULE self = nullptr;
            ::GetModuleHandleExW(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS
                                 | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                                 reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(&executableDir), &self);
            wchar_t buf[MAX_PATH * 4];
            DWORD n = ::GetModuleFileNameW(self, buf, static_cast<DWORD>(std::size(buf)));
            if (n == 0 || n >= std::size(buf)) {
                return {};
            }
            return std::filesystem::path(buf, buf + n).parent_path();
        }
    }  // namespace

    bool loadIndex(const std::filesystem::path& explicitPath, std::string& error) {
        std::vector<std::filesystem::path> candidates;
        if (!explicitPath.empty()) {
            candidates.push_back(explicitPath);
        } else {
            std::filesystem::path dir = executableDir();
            if (!dir.empty()) {
                candidates.push_back(dir / L"ida-ttd-data" / L"win32-index.bin");
                // running straight out of build\Release during development
                candidates.push_back(dir / L".." / L".." / L"data" / L"win32-index.bin");
            }
        }

        std::error_code ec;
        for (const auto& c : candidates) {
            if (!std::filesystem::exists(c, ec)) {
                continue;
            }
            // The native-API overlay lives beside the primary. It is optional: without
            // it every ntdll call goes back to being unsignatured, which is a loss of
            // coverage rather than a failure.
            std::vector<std::filesystem::path> overlays;
            std::filesystem::path phnt = c.parent_path() / L"phnt-index.bin";
            if (std::filesystem::exists(phnt, ec)) {
                overlays.push_back(phnt);
            }
            if (index().load(c, overlays, error)) {
                return true;
            }
            return false;  // found but unusable: surface the real reason
        }
        error = "win32-index.bin not found in plugins\\ida-ttd-data";
        return false;
    }

    const char* kindName(ArgKind kind) {
        switch (kind) {
            case ArgKind::Integer:         return "int";
            case ArgKind::Bool:            return "bool";
            case ArgKind::Handle:          return "handle";
            case ArgKind::Enum:            return "enum";
            case ArgKind::Float:           return "float";
            case ArgKind::Double:          return "double";
            case ArgKind::AnsiString:      return "str";
            case ArgKind::WideString:      return "wstr";
            case ArgKind::AnsiBuffer:      return "strbuf";
            case ArgKind::WideBuffer:      return "wstrbuf";
            case ArgKind::ByteBuffer:      return "buf";
            case ArgKind::PtrToInt:        return "int*";
            case ArgKind::StructPtr:       return "struct*";
            case ArgKind::FuncPtr:         return "fnptr";
            case ArgKind::Guid:            return "guid";
            case ArgKind::Pointer:         return "ptr";
            case ArgKind::PtrToAnsiString: return "str*";
            case ArgKind::PtrToWideString: return "wstr*";
            case ArgKind::CountedAnsiString: return "astr";
            case ArgKind::CountedWideString: return "ustr";
            case ArgKind::Unknown:
            default:                       return "unknown";
        }
    }
}  // namespace idattd::win32meta
```
