`src/common/apimeta/win32meta.hpp`:

```hpp
// Ported from ttd-capa-cpp (ttd/src/win32meta.hpp), Apache-2.0, by the same author.
// Kept close to the original so changes there can be carried over.
#ifndef WIN32META_HPP
#define WIN32META_HPP

// Loader for the pre-baked Win32 API metadata index (win32-index.bin) produced by
// tools/build-win32-index.py from the win32json submodule.
//
// The index answers one question per recorded call: given this export name, what
// are its parameters (count, names, types, direction, how to decode each)? That
// turns a blind 4-register grab into an exact capture.
//
// Lookup is keyed on the bare function name. Module is carried for display only:
// API sets mean the metadata's "CreateFileW -> KERNEL32.dll" shows up in a trace as
// KERNELBASE.dll!CreateFileW, so matching on module would lose most calls.
// See WIN32JSON-TTD-INTEGRATION-NOTES.md section 4.

#include <cstdint>
#include <filesystem>
#include <string>
#include <string_view>
#include <unordered_map>
#include <vector>

namespace idattd::win32meta {

    // How to decode one parameter. Values must match the K_* constants in
    // tools/build-win32-index.py.
    enum class ArgKind : uint8_t {
        Unknown = 0,
        Integer,           // plain scalar, never dereferenced
        Bool,
        Handle,            // opaque HANDLE/HKEY/HWND; pointer-sized but not a pointer
        Enum,              // scalar with a symbolic value table (see enumIndex)
        Float,             // 4-byte float, arrives in XMM<slot>
        Double,            // 8-byte float, arrives in XMM<slot>
        AnsiString,        // char*, NUL-terminated
        WideString,        // wchar_t*, NUL-terminated
        AnsiBuffer,        // char[], length from aux
        WideBuffer,        // wchar_t[], length from aux
        ByteBuffer,        // void*/byte[], length from aux
        PtrToInt,          // pointer to a pointeeSize-byte scalar
        StructPtr,         // pointer to a struct/union (not expanded in v1)
        FuncPtr,
        Guid,              // pointer to a 16-byte GUID
        Pointer,           // opaque pointer, contents unknown
        PtrToAnsiString,   // char**: out-param that receives an allocated string
        PtrToWideString,   // wchar_t**
        CountedAnsiString, // ANSI_STRING* / STRING*: {USHORT Length; USHORT Max; PSTR Buffer;}
        CountedWideString, // UNICODE_STRING*: the same shape with a PWSTR
    };

    // Bitmask of a parameter's direction/nullability attributes.
    enum ParamAttr : uint8_t {
        AttrIn = 0x01,
        AttrOut = 0x02,
        AttrOptional = 0x04,
        AttrConst = 0x08,
        AttrReserved = 0x10,
        AttrNotNulTerminated = 0x20,
        AttrNulNulTerminated = 0x40,
        AttrComOutPtr = 0x80,
    };

    // Where a buffer parameter's length comes from.
    enum class AuxKind : uint8_t {
        None = 0,
        BytesFromParam,   // auxValue is the index of a parameter holding a byte count
        CountFromParam,   // auxValue is the index of a parameter holding an element count
        CountConst,       // auxValue is the element count itself
    };

    enum FuncFlag : uint8_t {
        FlagHiddenRetPtr = 0x01,  // returns a large aggregate; RCX is the hidden return buffer
        FlagUnsupported = 0x02,   // at least one parameter could not be classified
        FlagSetLastError = 0x04,
    };

    struct ParamSig {
        const char* name = "";
        const char* type = "";
        ArgKind kind = ArgKind::Unknown;
        uint8_t attrs = 0;
        uint8_t slot = 0;          // positional ABI slot, already shifted for FlagHiddenRetPtr
        AuxKind auxKind = AuxKind::None;
        int32_t auxValue = 0;
        uint32_t enumIndex = 0xFFFFFFFFu;
        uint16_t pointeeSize = 0;  // bytes per pointee/element, 0 if unknown
        // Bytes this parameter occupies on a 32-bit argument stack, or 0 when the
        // builder could not say and abi.cpp has to infer one from the type. Only
        // build-phnt-index.py fills it in; win32json records x64 sizes, where a
        // pointer-sized scalar and a genuine 64-bit one are both 8.
        uint8_t x86Footprint = 0;

        bool isIn() const { return (attrs & AttrIn) != 0; }
        bool isOut() const { return (attrs & AttrOut) != 0; }
        bool isFloat() const { return kind == ArgKind::Float || kind == ArgKind::Double; }
        bool hasEnum() const { return enumIndex != 0xFFFFFFFFu; }
    };

    struct FuncSig {
        const char* name = "";
        const char* dll = "";
        const ParamSig* params = nullptr;
        uint8_t paramCount = 0;
        uint8_t flags = 0;

        bool unsupported() const { return (flags & FlagUnsupported) != 0; }
        bool hiddenRetPtr() const { return (flags & FlagHiddenRetPtr) != 0; }
    };

    // Loaded once at startup and read-only thereafter, so the replay sweep can hit
    // it from the call callback without synchronisation.
    class Index {
    public:
        // `overlays` are further blobs in the same format, merged *under* the primary
        // one: they fill gaps and replace entries the primary flagged unsupported,
        // and never displace a usable primary signature. They arrive together because
        // every FuncSig points into one contiguous parameter array, which is built
        // once all the sources are known.
        bool load(const std::filesystem::path& path,
                  const std::vector<std::filesystem::path>& overlays,
                  std::string& error);
        bool loaded() const { return !funcs_.empty(); }
        size_t functionCount() const { return funcs_.size(); }
        const std::filesystem::path& path() const { return path_; }

        // Bare export name, e.g. "CreateFileW". Returns nullptr when unknown, which
        // is the caller's cue to fall back to the heuristic capture.
        const FuncSig* lookup(std::string_view api) const;

        const char* enumName(uint32_t enumIndex) const;

        // Symbolic names for `value`: an exact match if one exists, otherwise a
        // greedy bit decomposition for flag enums. Empty when nothing matches.
        std::vector<std::string> decodeEnum(uint32_t enumIndex, uint64_t value) const;

    private:
        // One function on its way into the index, before the parameter arrays are
        // flattened into `params_`. Staging is what lets several sources be merged
        // without the FuncSig::params pointers moving under anyone.
        struct Staged {
            const char* name = "";
            const char* dll = "";
            uint8_t flags = 0;
            std::vector<ParamSig> params;
        };

        // Read one blob in the index format. Its string pool is kept alive in blobs_.
        bool parseBlob(const std::filesystem::path& path, std::vector<Staged>& out,
                       bool withEnums, std::string& error);

        // Fold the hand-written tables (builtinsigs.hpp) in: the win32u and CRT
        // signatures no generator can supply, and the flag-enum overlay that names a
        // win32json enum table for a native parameter phnt types as a bare ULONG.
        void mergeBuiltins(std::vector<Staged>& staged);

        // Flatten `staged` into params_/funcs_/byName_. Nothing may be added after.
        void finalize(std::vector<Staged>& staged);

        // Index of the enum table with this name, or 0xFFFFFFFF. The overlay needs it:
        // it names its enums, having no way to know the numbers the generator chose.
        uint32_t findEnum(const char* name) const;

        struct EnumTable {
            const char* name = "";
            uint32_t valueOffset = 0;
            uint32_t valueCount = 0;
            bool isFlags = false;
            uint8_t width = 4;
        };
        struct EnumValue {
            const char* name = "";
            int64_t value = 0;
        };

        // One entry per source blob. Every `const char*` in the index points into one
        // of these, so they have to outlive the tables built from them.
        std::vector<std::vector<uint8_t>> blobs_;
        std::vector<FuncSig> funcs_;
        std::vector<ParamSig> params_;
        std::vector<EnumTable> enums_;
        std::vector<EnumValue> enumValues_;
        std::unordered_map<std::string_view, uint32_t> byName_;
        std::filesystem::path path_;
    };

    // Process-wide instance; empty until loadIndex() succeeds.
    Index& index();

    // Try `explicitPath` if non-empty, else the conventional locations next to the
    // executable and in the source tree. The native-API overlay (phnt-index.bin) is
    // looked for beside whichever win32-index.bin is used, and is optional: without
    // it ntdll calls simply go back to being unsignatured. Returns false with `error`
    // set; the caller is expected to warn and continue in heuristic mode.
    bool loadIndex(const std::filesystem::path& explicitPath, std::string& error);

    const char* kindName(ArgKind kind);

}  // namespace idattd::win32meta

#endif
```

`src/common/dbstore.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/dbstore.h"

namespace idattd
{
    void BlobWriter::u32(uint32_t v)
    {
        for ( int i = 0; i < 4; i++ )
            m_b.push_back((uchar)((v >> (i * 8)) & 0xFF));
    }

    void BlobWriter::u64(uint64_t v)
    {
        for ( int i = 0; i < 8; i++ )
            m_b.push_back((uchar)((v >> (i * 8)) & 0xFF));
    }

    void BlobWriter::str(const qstring &s)
    {
        uint32_t n = (uint32_t)qmin(s.length(), (size_t)DB_MAX_STR);
        u32(n);
        for ( uint32_t i = 0; i < n; i++ )
            m_b.push_back((uchar)s[i]);
    }

    bool BlobReader::have(size_t k)
    {
        if ( !m_ok || m_off + k > m_n )
        {
            m_ok = false;
            return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    uint8_t BlobReader::u8()
    {
        if ( !have(1) )
            return 0;
        return m_p[m_off++];
    }

    uint32_t BlobReader::u32()
    {
        if ( !have(4) )
            return 0;
        uint32_t v = 0;
        for ( int i = 0; i < 4; i++ )
            v |= (uint32_t)m_p[m_off++] << (i * 8);
        return v;
    }

    uint64_t BlobReader::u64()
    {
        uint32_t lo = u32();
        uint32_t hi = u32();
        return (uint64_t)lo | ((uint64_t)hi << 32);
    }

    bool BlobReader::str(qstring *out)
    {
        uint32_t len = u32();
        if ( !m_ok || len > DB_MAX_STR || !have(len) )
        {
            m_ok = false;
            return false;
        }
        out->qclear();
        out->append((const char *)m_p + m_off, len);
        m_off += len;
        return true;
    }

    bool PluginNode::exists() const
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        return nn != BADNODE;
    }

    void PluginNode::put(uchar tag, uint32_t magic, uint32_t version,
                         const BlobWriter &w, uint64_t fingerprint)
    {
        netnode nn(m_name, 0, true);   // create on first write
        if ( w.size() == 0 )
        {
            nn.delblob(0, tag);
            return;
        }
        // Header first, so a reader can reject a blob before parsing it.
        BlobWriter hdr;
        hdr.u32(magic);
        hdr.u32(version);
        hdr.u64(fingerprint);

        std::vector<uchar> buf;
        buf.reserve(hdr.size() + w.size());
        buf.insert(buf.end(), hdr.data(), hdr.data() + hdr.size());
        buf.insert(buf.end(), w.data(), w.data() + w.size());
        nn.setblob(buf.data(), buf.size(), 0, tag);
    }

    bool PluginNode::get(uchar tag, uint32_t magic, uint32_t version,
                         uint64_t fingerprint, std::vector<uchar> *out) const
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        if ( nn == BADNODE || out == nullptr )
            return false;

        size_t sz = 0;
        void *raw = nn.getblob(nullptr, &sz, 0, tag);
        if ( raw == nullptr )
            return false;

        BlobReader r(raw, sz);
        bool ok = r.u32() == magic && r.u32() == version;
        uint64_t stamp = r.u64();
        // A fingerprint of 0 on either side means "not tied to a recording".
        if ( ok && fingerprint != 0 && stamp != 0 && stamp != fingerprint )
            ok = false;
        if ( ok && r.ok() )
        {
            const uchar *p = (const uchar *)raw;
            out->assign(p + DB_HEADER_SIZE, p + sz);
        }
        else
        {
            ok = false;
        }
        qfree(raw);
        return ok;
    }

    void PluginNode::erase(uchar tag)
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        if ( nn != BADNODE )
            nn.delblob(0, tag);
    }

    nodeidx_t PluginNode::alt(nodeidx_t idx, uchar tag) const
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        return nn == BADNODE ? 0 : nn.altval(idx, tag);
    }

    void PluginNode::set_alt(nodeidx_t idx, nodeidx_t value, uchar tag)
    {
        netnode nn(m_name, 0, true);
        nn.altset(idx, value, tag);
    }

    void PluginNode::del_alt(nodeidx_t idx, uchar tag)
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        if ( nn != BADNODE )
            nn.altdel(idx, tag);
    }

    // Reserved tag, kept away from the tags a feature chooses for itself.
    static const uchar DB_STAMP_TAG = 'Z';

    uint64_t PluginNode::trace_stamp() const
    {
        return (uint64_t)alt(0, DB_STAMP_TAG);
    }

    void PluginNode::set_trace_stamp(uint64_t fingerprint)
    {
        set_alt(0, (nodeidx_t)fingerprint, DB_STAMP_TAG);
    }

    void PluginNode::each_alt(uchar tag,
                              const std::function<void(nodeidx_t, nodeidx_t)> &fn) const
    {
        netnode nn(m_name);
        if ( nn == BADNODE )
            return;
        for ( nodeidx_t i = nn.altfirst(tag); i != BADNODE; i = nn.altnext(i, tag) )
            fn(i, nn.altval(i, tag));
    }
}

```

`src/common/dbstore.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Plugin data in the database (bookmarks, coverage, resolved call sites,
    // the memory map), with one shared encoding.
    //
    // Everything read back is untrusted: a blob can be stale, truncated, or
    // from another plugin version. The reader bounds-checks every field and
    // one failure abandons the whole parse.

    // Little-endian writer. Values are appended in the order the reader expects.
    class BlobWriter
    {
    public:
        void u8(uint8_t v)  { m_b.push_back(v); }
        void u32(uint32_t v);
        void u64(uint64_t v);
        // Length-prefixed, not NUL-terminated. Longer strings are truncated.
        void str(const qstring &s);

        const uchar *data() const { return m_b.begin(); }
        size_t       size() const { return m_b.size(); }

    private:
        bytevec_t m_b;
    };

    // Bounds-checked reader. Once ok() is false every further read returns zero
    // and the caller should discard whatever it has built.
    class BlobReader
    {
    public:
        BlobReader(const void *p, size_t n)
            : m_p((const uchar *)p), m_n(n) {}

        uint8_t  u8();
        uint32_t u32();
        uint64_t u64();
        bool     str(qstring *out);

        bool ok() const { return m_ok; }

    private:
        bool have(size_t k);

        const uchar *m_p = nullptr;
        size_t       m_n = 0;
        size_t       m_off = 0;
        bool         m_ok = true;
    };

    // Longest string any feature will write or believe.
    static const uint32_t DB_MAX_STR = 4096;

    // A plugin netnode, named "$ ..." so it cannot collide with a program byte
    // name.
    //
    // Blobs are stamped with the recording they came from, and reading one
    // back against another recording is refused: addresses and positions from
    // one execution mean nothing in another.
    class PluginNode
    {
    public:
        explicit PluginNode(const char *name) : m_name(name) {}

        // True when the node exists at all.
        bool exists() const;

        // Replace the blob under 'tag' with 'w', behind a header carrying
        // 'magic', 'version' and 'fingerprint'. A fingerprint of 0 means the
        // data does not depend on any one recording.
        void put(uchar tag, uint32_t magic, uint32_t version,
                 const BlobWriter &w, uint64_t fingerprint);
        // Read the blob under 'tag'. False when it is absent, when its header
        // does not match 'magic' and 'version', or when it was written against a
        // different recording. The caller owns nothing on failure.
        bool get(uchar tag, uint32_t magic, uint32_t version, uint64_t fingerprint,
                 std::vector<uchar> *out) const;

        void erase(uchar tag);

        // Plain scalar slots, for state small enough not to need a blob.
        nodeidx_t alt(nodeidx_t idx, uchar tag) const;
        void      set_alt(nodeidx_t idx, nodeidx_t value, uchar tag);
        void      del_alt(nodeidx_t idx, uchar tag);
        // Iterate the alt slots under 'tag', in index order.
        void      each_alt(uchar tag, const std::function<void(nodeidx_t idx, nodeidx_t val)> &fn) const;

        // Which recording this node's non-blob state came from (blobs carry
        // the header below instead); zero when unstamped. Callers stamp on
        // write and compare at session start.
        uint64_t trace_stamp() const;
        void     set_trace_stamp(uint64_t fingerprint);

    private:
        const char *m_name;
    };

    // Header every blob carries, written by put() and checked by get():
    //   u32 magic, u32 version, u64 trace fingerprint
    static const size_t DB_HEADER_SIZE = 16;
}
```

`src/common/guest_pe.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/guest_pe.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Read exactly 'size' bytes of guest memory; return false on a short read.
    bool pe_read(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t addr, void *buf, size_t size)
    {
        return c(addr, buf, size) == size;
    }

    // Read a NUL-terminated ASCII string from guest memory (bounded).
    std::string pe_read_cstr(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t addr, size_t maxlen)
    {
        std::string s;
        char chunk[64];
        while ( s.size() < maxlen )
        {
            size_t got = c(addr + s.size(), chunk, qmin(sizeof(chunk), maxlen - s.size()));
            if ( got == 0 )
                break;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < got; i++ )
            {
                if ( chunk[i] == '\0' )
                    return s;
                s.push_back(chunk[i]);
            }
        }
        return s;
    }

    // Locate a module's NT headers and their flavour. Shared by every reader here
    // so the DOS/NT walk and its e_lfanew guard exist once.
    static bool locate_nt_headers(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t base, uint64_t *nt_addr_out,
                                  bool *is64_out)
    {
        IMAGE_DOS_HEADER dos{};
        if ( !pe_read_val(c, base, &dos) || dos.e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE )
            return false;
        // e_lfanew is attacker-controlled (the image may be malware); a wild value
        // would send every following read somewhere unrelated.
        if ( dos.e_lfanew < 0 || (uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew > 0x10000000u )
            return false;

        uint64_t ntAddr = base + (uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew;
        uint32_t sig = 0;
        if ( !pe_read_val(c, ntAddr, &sig) || sig != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE )
            return false;

        // The optional header magic (after the signature and file header) says
        // whether the image is 32- or 64-bit; the recording machine's
        // architecture does not.
        uint16_t magic = 0;
        if ( !pe_read_val(c, ntAddr + 4 + sizeof(IMAGE_FILE_HEADER), &magic) )
            return false;
        if ( magic != IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC && magic != IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR32_MAGIC )
            return false;

        *nt_addr_out = ntAddr;
        *is64_out    = magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC;
        return true;
    }

    // Data directory 'index' (IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_*) of the module whose NT
    // header is at 'ntAddr'; false when absent. Entries past
    // NumberOfRvaAndSizes are not directories, whatever bytes sit there.
    static bool read_data_dir(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t ntAddr, bool is64, int index,
                              uint32_t *rva_out, uint32_t *size_out)
    {
        if ( is64 )
        {
            IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 nt{};
            if ( !pe_read_val(c, ntAddr, &nt) || nt.OptionalHeader.NumberOfRvaAndSizes <= (DWORD)index )
                return false;
            const IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY &dd = nt.OptionalHeader.DataDirectory[index];
            *rva_out  = dd.VirtualAddress;
            *size_out = dd.Size;
        }
        else
        {
            IMAGE_NT_HEADERS32 nt{};
            if ( !pe_read_val(c, ntAddr, &nt) || nt.OptionalHeader.NumberOfRvaAndSizes <= (DWORD)index )
                return false;
            const IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY &dd = nt.OptionalHeader.DataDirectory[index];
            *rva_out  = dd.VirtualAddress;
            *size_out = dd.Size;
        }
        return *rva_out != 0 && *size_out != 0;
    }

    bool read_guest_pe_info(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, GuestPeInfo *out)
    {
        if ( cursor == nullptr || out == nullptr || base == BADADDR )
            return false;
        *out = GuestPeInfo();

        uint64_t b = (uint64_t)base;
        uint64_t ntAddr = 0;
        bool     is64   = false;
        if ( !locate_nt_headers(cursor, b, &ntAddr, &is64) )
            return false;

        out->is64 = is64;

        // The section table follows the optional header, whose size comes from
        // the file header. It is not always sizeof(IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER); a
        // hand-built image would put the table a few bytes off.
        IMAGE_FILE_HEADER fh{};
        if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, ntAddr + 4, &fh) )
            return false;
        out->timestamp = fh.TimeDateStamp;
        uint16_t nsections = fh.NumberOfSections;
        uint64_t sectAddr  = ntAddr + 4 + sizeof(IMAGE_FILE_HEADER) + fh.SizeOfOptionalHeader;

        if ( is64 )
        {
            IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 nt{};
            if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, ntAddr, &nt) )
                return false;
            out->entry_rva       = nt.OptionalHeader.AddressOfEntryPoint;
            out->size_of_image   = nt.OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage;
            out->size_of_headers = nt.OptionalHeader.SizeOfHeaders;
            out->preferred_base  = nt.OptionalHeader.ImageBase;
            out->checksum        = nt.OptionalHeader.CheckSum;
        }
        else
        {
            IMAGE_NT_HEADERS32 nt{};
            if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, ntAddr, &nt) )
                return false;
            out->entry_rva       = nt.OptionalHeader.AddressOfEntryPoint;
            out->size_of_image   = nt.OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage;
            out->size_of_headers = nt.OptionalHeader.SizeOfHeaders;
            out->preferred_base  = nt.OptionalHeader.ImageBase;
            out->checksum        = nt.OptionalHeader.CheckSum;
        }

        // NumberOfSections is untrusted: 65535 would ask for a 2.5 MB read of a
        // module with three sections. The loader requires the section table
        // to lie within SizeOfHeaders, so that bounds it (Windows loads images
        // with more than the 96 sections the PE documentation names). An
        // image whose SizeOfHeaders leaves no room for the table still gets
        // the documented 96, in case the field alone is malformed.
        static const uint64_t kFallbackSections = 96;
        uint64_t tableOff = sectAddr - b;
        uint64_t fit = out->size_of_headers > tableOff
                     ? (out->size_of_headers - tableOff) / sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER)
                     : 0;
        if ( fit < kFallbackSections )
            fit = kFallbackSections;
        if ( nsections > fit )
            nsections = (uint16_t)fit;
        if ( nsections == 0 )
            return true;    // valid headers; a sectionless image is merely odd

        std::vector<IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER> hdrs(nsections);
        size_t mb = cursor(sectAddr, hdrs.data(), (size_t)nsections * sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER));
        size_t got = mb / sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER);

        out->sections.reserve(got);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < got; i++ )
        {
            const IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER &sh = hdrs[i];
            GuestPeSection s;
            memcpy(s.name, sh.Name, 8);
            s.name[8]         = '\0';
            s.va              = sh.VirtualAddress;
            s.vsize           = sh.Misc.VirtualSize;
            s.rawsize         = sh.SizeOfRawData;
            s.characteristics = sh.Characteristics;
            out->sections.push_back(s);
        }
        return true;
    }

    bool read_guest_pdb_info(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, GuestPdbInfo *out)
    {
        if ( cursor == nullptr || out == nullptr || base == BADADDR )
            return false;
        *out = GuestPdbInfo();

        uint64_t b = (uint64_t)base;
        uint64_t ntAddr = 0;
        bool     is64   = false;
        if ( !locate_nt_headers(cursor, b, &ntAddr, &is64) )
            return false;

        uint32_t dbgRva = 0, dbgSize = 0;
        if ( !read_data_dir(cursor, ntAddr, is64, IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_DEBUG, &dbgRva, &dbgSize) )
            return false;

        // Cap the entry count like the section table: the size field is
        // untrusted and a wild value would ask for an enormous read.
        static const uint32_t kMaxEntries = 64;
        uint32_t nentries = dbgSize / (uint32_t)sizeof(IMAGE_DEBUG_DIRECTORY);
        if ( nentries > kMaxEntries )
            nentries = kMaxEntries;

        for ( uint32_t i = 0; i < nentries; i++ )
        {
            IMAGE_DEBUG_DIRECTORY dd{};
            if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, b + dbgRva + i * sizeof(IMAGE_DEBUG_DIRECTORY), &dd) )
                return false;
            if ( dd.Type != IMAGE_DEBUG_TYPE_CODEVIEW || dd.AddressOfRawData == 0 )
                continue;

            // The CodeView record: "RSDS", a GUID, an age, then the PDB path as
            // the linker wrote it. Other formats give no symbol-server name.
            struct RsdsHeader
            {
                uint32_t signature;     // 'SDSR'
                GUID     guid;
                uint32_t age;
            } rs{};
            uint64_t cv = b + dd.AddressOfRawData;
            if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, cv, &rs) || rs.signature != 0x53445352 )
                continue;

            std::string path = pe_read_cstr(cursor, cv + sizeof(RsdsHeader), MAX_PATH);
            if ( path.empty() )
                continue;
            // The path is the build machine's; only the file name matters here.
            size_t slash = path.find_last_of("/" "\\");
            out->name = slash == std::string::npos ? path : path.substr(slash + 1);

            // Symbol-server key: the GUID in registry order without separators,
            // then the age in hex, both upper case.
            char sig[64];
            qsnprintf(sig, sizeof(sig),
                      "%08X%04X%04X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%X",
                      rs.guid.Data1, rs.guid.Data2, rs.guid.Data3,
                      rs.guid.Data4[0], rs.guid.Data4[1], rs.guid.Data4[2],
                      rs.guid.Data4[3], rs.guid.Data4[4], rs.guid.Data4[5],
                      rs.guid.Data4[6], rs.guid.Data4[7], rs.age);
            out->signature = sig;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Call 'visit(address, name)' for each named, non-forwarded export of the
    // module at 'base' until it returns false; returns how many were visited.
    //
    // The image's own optional header decides PE32 versus PE32+: a WoW64
    // recording has both a 32- and a 64-bit ntdll, and the caller's process
    // bitness cannot tell which one 'base' is.
    template <typename Visit>
    static size_t walk_exports(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, Visit visit)
    {
        if ( cursor == nullptr || base == BADADDR )
            return 0;

        uint64_t b = (uint64_t)base;
        uint64_t ntAddr = 0;
        bool     is64   = false;
        if ( !locate_nt_headers(cursor, b, &ntAddr, &is64) )
            return 0;

        uint32_t exportRva = 0, exportSize = 0;
        if ( !read_data_dir(cursor, ntAddr, is64, IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXPORT, &exportRva, &exportSize) )
            return 0;

        IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY exp{};
        if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, b + exportRva, &exp) )
            return 0;
        if ( exp.AddressOfNames == 0 || exp.AddressOfNameOrdinals == 0 || exp.AddressOfFunctions == 0 )
            return 0;

        // One read per parallel array rather than three reads per export:
        // ntdll alone exports ~2400 names and this runs for every module. The
        // counts are untrusted, so they are clamped before sizing buffers.
        static const uint32_t kMaxExports = 1u << 20;
        uint32_t nNames = exp.NumberOfNames < kMaxExports ? exp.NumberOfNames : kMaxExports;
        uint32_t nFuncs = exp.NumberOfFunctions < kMaxExports ? exp.NumberOfFunctions : kMaxExports;
        if ( nNames == 0 || nFuncs == 0 )
            return 0;

        std::vector<uint32_t> nameRvas(nNames);
        std::vector<uint16_t> ordinals(nNames);
        std::vector<uint32_t> funcRvas(nFuncs);

        size_t mbN = cursor(b + exp.AddressOfNames, nameRvas.data(), (size_t)nNames * sizeof(uint32_t));
        size_t mbO = cursor(b + exp.AddressOfNameOrdinals, ordinals.data(), (size_t)nNames * sizeof(uint16_t));
        size_t mbF = cursor(b + exp.AddressOfFunctions, funcRvas.data(), (size_t)nFuncs * sizeof(uint32_t));

        // An array may come back short (a recording holds only accessed
        // memory); use the prefix that resolved.
        size_t gotNames = mbN / sizeof(uint32_t);
        size_t gotOrds  = mbO / sizeof(uint16_t);
        size_t gotFuncs = mbF / sizeof(uint32_t);
        size_t usable   = gotNames < gotOrds ? gotNames : gotOrds;

        size_t visited = 0;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < usable; i++ )
        {
            uint16_t ordinal = ordinals[i];
            if ( (size_t)ordinal >= gotFuncs )
                continue;
            uint32_t funcRva = funcRvas[ordinal];
            if ( funcRva == 0 )
                continue;
            // A forwarder's "address" points at a string inside the export
            // directory; its target is in another module. Written as a
            // difference so a directory near 4 GB cannot wrap the bound.
            if ( funcRva >= exportRva && funcRva - exportRva < exportSize )
                continue;
            std::string name = pe_read_cstr(cursor, b + nameRvas[i]);
            if ( name.empty() )
                continue;
            visited++;
            if ( !visit((ea_t)(b + funcRva), std::move(name)) )
                break;
        }
        return visited;
    }

    size_t read_guest_exports(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64,
                              std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, std::string>> *out)
    {
        qnotused(is64);   // the image's own header is the authority (walk_exports)
        return walk_exports(cursor, base, [&](ea_t ea, std::string &&n)
        {
            if ( out != nullptr )
                out->emplace_back(ea, std::move(n));
            return true;
        });
    }
}
```

`src/common/guest_pe.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/guest_view.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // PE parsing from guest memory, for both the backends and the core. Nothing
    // here touches the IDA database; common/symbols applies the results.

    // Read exactly 'size' bytes of guest memory; false on a short read.
    bool pe_read(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t addr, void *buf, size_t size);
    template <typename T>
    bool pe_read_val(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t addr, T *out)
    {
        return pe_read(c, addr, out, sizeof(T));
    }
    // A NUL-terminated string of at most 'maxlen' bytes; empty when unreadable.
    std::string pe_read_cstr(const GuestRead &c, uint64_t addr, size_t maxlen = 512);

    // Every named, non-forwarded export of the module at 'base', as (address,
    // name). The cursor must be where the module is mapped. Returns the count.
    size_t read_guest_exports(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64,
                              std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, std::string>> *out);

    // ---- reading a module's PE headers straight out of the recording -------
    //
    // The loader and the memory-map sweep need a module's bitness, entry point
    // and section layout. The engine's Module record has only name, base, size,
    // checksum and timestamp, so these come from the image itself, read at a
    // position where the module is mapped.

    struct GuestPeSection
    {
        char     name[9] = { 0 };   // NUL-terminated copy of the 8-byte PE name
        uint32_t va = 0;            // RVA of the section
        uint32_t vsize = 0;         // virtual size (0 means "use rawsize")
        uint32_t rawsize = 0;       // size of the initialized data on disk
        uint32_t characteristics = 0;
    };

    struct GuestPeInfo
    {
        bool     is64 = false;      // from the optional header magic, not the host
        uint32_t entry_rva = 0;
        uint32_t size_of_image = 0;
        uint32_t size_of_headers = 0;
        uint64_t preferred_base = 0;
        uint32_t timestamp = 0;     // FileHeader.TimeDateStamp
        uint32_t checksum = 0;      // OptionalHeader.CheckSum
        std::vector<GuestPeSection> sections;
    };

    // Parse the PE headers of the module at 'base'. The cursor must be where
    // the module is loaded (its ModuleLoadedEvent position is reliable).
    //
    // Bitness comes from the optional header magic, not the engine's
    // SystemInfo, which describes the recording machine: a 32-bit program
    // recorded on x64 reports AMD64 there.
    bool read_guest_pe_info(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, GuestPeInfo *out);

    // Which PDB a module was built with, from the CodeView record in its debug
    // directory. The only authoritative answer when the local DLL is a
    // different build: its PDB would describe code the recording never ran.
    struct GuestPdbInfo
    {
        std::string name;           // e.g. "ntdll.pdb", as the linker wrote it
        std::string signature;      // GUID + age, the symbol server's directory
    };

    // Read the above for the module at 'base'; the cursor must be where it is
    // loaded. False when it is unreadable there or has no CodeView record.
    bool read_guest_pdb_info(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base,
                             GuestPdbInfo *out);
}
```

`src/common/json_str.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/json_str.h"

namespace idattd
{
    void json_str(qstring *out, const char *s)
    {
        // Through UTF-16, so bytes that are not UTF-8 (a guest's console
        // output in Sogen's log) come out as U+FFFD rather than as a bad
        // byte that fails the whole Python call.
        qwstring w;
        utf8_utf16(&w, s);
        out->append('"');
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < w.length(); i++ )
        {
            uint32_t c = (uint16_t)w[i];
            if ( c >= 0xD800 && c < 0xDC00 && i + 1 < w.length()
              && (uint16_t)w[i + 1] >= 0xDC00 && (uint16_t)w[i + 1] < 0xE000 )
            {
                // Outside the BMP: as UTF-8. JSON would take a surrogate pair
                // of escapes, but Python reads those as two lone surrogates.
                c = 0x10000 + ((c - 0xD800) << 10) + ((uint16_t)w[++i] - 0xDC00);
                out->append((char)(0xF0 | (c >> 18)));
                out->append((char)(0x80 | ((c >> 12) & 0x3F)));
                out->append((char)(0x80 | ((c >> 6) & 0x3F)));
                out->append((char)(0x80 | (c & 0x3F)));
            }
            else if ( c >= 0xD800 && c < 0xE000 )
            {
                out->append("\\ufffd");          // a lone surrogate Qt would refuse
            }
            else if ( c == '"' || c == '\\' )
            {
                out->append('\\');
                out->append((char)c);
            }
            else if ( c < 0x20 || c >= 0x7F )
            {
                out->cat_sprnt("\\u%04x", c);
            }
            else
            {
                out->append((char)c);
            }
        }
        out->append('"');
    }
}

```

`src/common/json_str.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Append UTF-8 's' as a quoted JSON string, which is also a Python
    // string literal: the one escaper for every model an IDAPython window
    // asks for (graphs, the call tree, the heatmap) and every string the
    // plugin passes to Python code it runs. Plain ASCII apart from
    // characters outside the BMP (as UTF-8); bytes that are not UTF-8 come
    // out as U+FFFD.
    void json_str(qstring *out, const char *s);
}
```

`src/common/local_path.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only
//
// Dual-licensed like write_scans.h: shared by the plugin and both backends,
// so it stays header-only and standard-library-only (plus <windows.h>).
//
// A recording names host paths (module files, Sogen's emulation root) that
// the plugin then opens. A crafted recording could name a UNC path, which
// makes Windows connect to that host over SMB or WebDAV and send the user's
// NTLM credentials, or a device path (\\.\pipe\...) that blocks the reader.
// Only paths on a local drive letter are opened.

#pragma once

#include <string>

#ifndef WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#define WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN
#endif
#ifndef NOMINMAX
#define NOMINMAX
#endif
#include <windows.h>

namespace idattd
{
    // A legacy DOS device name (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM0-9, LPT0-9), with or
    // without an extension: Win32 opens the device, whatever folder it is
    // in ("C:\x\CON.txt" is the console), and a read of the console waits
    // for keyboard input. Case-insensitive, trailing dots and blanks
    // ignored, as Win32 does.
    template <typename C>
    inline bool is_dos_device_name(const C *s, size_t n)
    {
        size_t stem = 0;
        while ( stem < n && s[stem] != C('.') )
            stem++;
        while ( stem > 0 && (s[stem - 1] == C(' ') || s[stem - 1] == C('.')) )
            stem--;
        auto up = [](C c) { return (c >= C('a') && c <= C('z')) ? C(c - C('a') + C('A')) : c; };
        auto is3 = [&](const char *w)
        {
            return up(s[0]) == C(w[0]) && up(s[1]) == C(w[1]) && up(s[2]) == C(w[2]);
        };
        if ( stem == 3 )
            return is3("CON") || is3("PRN") || is3("AUX") || is3("NUL");
        if ( stem == 4 && s[3] >= C('0') && s[3] <= C('9') )
            return is3("COM") || is3("LPT");
        return false;
    }

    // Any component of 'p' (separated by '\' or '/') is a DOS device name.
    template <typename C>
    inline bool has_dos_device_component(const C *p, size_t n)
    {
        size_t i = 0;
        while ( i < n )
        {
            size_t j = i;
            while ( j < n && p[j] != C('\\') && p[j] != C('/') )
                j++;
            if ( j > i && is_dos_device_name(p + i, j - i) )
                return true;
            i = j + 1;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // True when 'path' is an absolute path on a local (non-network) drive:
    // "X:\..." or "\\?\X:\...". UNC, device and relative paths are refused,
    // and so is a drive letter mapped to a network share, and a path naming
    // a DOS device (has_dos_device_component).
    inline bool is_local_drive_path(const std::wstring &path)
    {
        std::wstring p = path;
        for ( wchar_t &c : p )
            if ( c == L'/' )
                c = L'\\';
        if ( p.compare(0, 4, L"\\\\?\\") == 0 )
            p.erase(0, 4);
        if ( p.size() < 3 || p[1] != L':' || p[2] != L'\\' )
            return false;
        wchar_t d = p[0];
        if ( !((d >= L'A' && d <= L'Z') || (d >= L'a' && d <= L'z')) )
            return false;
        if ( has_dos_device_component(p.c_str() + 3, p.size() - 3) )
            return false;
        const wchar_t root[4] = { d, L':', L'\\', 0 };
        UINT type = GetDriveTypeW(root);
        return type == DRIVE_FIXED || type == DRIVE_REMOVABLE
            || type == DRIVE_CDROM || type == DRIVE_RAMDISK;
    }

    // UTF-8 overload.
    inline bool is_local_drive_path(const char *utf8)
    {
        if ( utf8 == nullptr || *utf8 == '\0' )
            return false;
        int n = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, utf8, -1, nullptr, 0);
        if ( n <= 0 )
            return false;
        std::wstring w((size_t)n - 1, L'\0');
        MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, utf8, -1, w.data(), n);
        return is_local_drive_path(w);
    }
}
```

`src/common/pdb_publics.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/pdb_publics.h"

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstring>
#include <memory>

namespace idattd
{
    namespace
    {
        // The MSF 7.00 container ("big MSF") and the streams the public
        // symbols need, per llvm.org/docs/PDB/ and Microsoft's microsoft-pdb:
        //
        //   superblock   magic, block size, ..., directory size, block map addr
        //   directory    stream count, every stream's size, every stream's blocks
        //   stream 3     DBI: names the symbol record stream, and its optional
        //                debug header names the section header stream (and an
        //                OMAP stream when the image was rearranged after linking)
        //   symbol records: S_PUB32 { flags, offset, segment, name }
        const char     kMagic[]      = "Microsoft C/C++ MSF 7.00\r\n\x1a" "DS\0\0";
        const size_t   kMagicSize    = 32;
        const uint32_t kDbiStream    = 3;
        const uint16_t kNilStream    = 0xFFFF;
        const uint16_t S_PUB32       = 0x110E;
        const uint32_t kPubCode      = 0x1;     // cvpsfCode
        const uint32_t kPubFunction  = 0x2;     // cvpsfFunction

        // Optional debug header slots (DbgHeaderType).
        const size_t   kDbgOmapFromSrc  = 4;
        const size_t   kDbgSectionHdr   = 5;

        // Allocation bounds against damaged or hostile files. The biggest
        // system PDBs are a few hundred MB, with streams well under the cap.
        const uint32_t kMaxStreams      = 1u << 20;
        const uint64_t kMaxStreamBytes  = 1ull << 30;

        uint16_t rd16(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] | (p[1] << 8)); }
        uint32_t rd32(const uint8_t *p)
        {
            return (uint32_t)p[0] | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 8) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 16)
                 | ((uint32_t)p[3] << 24);
        }

        struct FileCloser { void operator()(FILE *f) const { if ( f != nullptr ) fclose(f); } };

        class Msf
        {
        public:
            bool open(const wchar_t *path, std::string *error)
            {
                FILE *f = nullptr;
                if ( _wfopen_s(&f, path, L"rb") != 0 || f == nullptr )
                    return fail(error, "cannot open the file");
                m_file.reset(f);
                if ( _fseeki64(f, 0, SEEK_END) != 0 )
                    return fail(error, "cannot read the file");
                m_fileSize = (uint64_t)_ftelli64(f);

                uint8_t sb[kMagicSize + 24];
                if ( !read_at(0, sb, sizeof(sb)) || memcmp(sb, kMagic, kMagicSize) != 0 )
                    return fail(error, "not an MSF 7.00 PDB");
                m_blockSize      = rd32(sb + kMagicSize + 0);
                uint32_t nblocks = rd32(sb + kMagicSize + 8);
                uint32_t dirSize = rd32(sb + kMagicSize + 12);
                uint32_t mapAddr = rd32(sb + kMagicSize + 20);
                if ( m_blockSize != 512 && m_blockSize != 1024 && m_blockSize != 2048
                  && m_blockSize != 4096 && m_blockSize != 8192 && m_blockSize != 16384
                  && m_blockSize != 32768 )
                    return fail(error, "unexpected MSF block size");
                if ( (uint64_t)nblocks * m_blockSize > m_fileSize + m_blockSize )
                    return fail(error, "the file is shorter than its header says");
                m_nblocks = nblocks;
                if ( dirSize < 4 || dirSize > kMaxStreamBytes || !fits(dirSize) )
                    return fail(error, "bad stream directory size");
                if ( mapAddr >= m_nblocks )
                    return fail(error, "bad block map address");

                // The block map is one block listing the directory's blocks.
                uint32_t dirBlocks = blocks_for(dirSize);
                if ( (uint64_t)dirBlocks * 4 > m_blockSize )
                    return fail(error, "the stream directory does not fit its block map");
                std::vector<uint8_t> map((size_t)dirBlocks * 4);
                if ( !read_at((uint64_t)mapAddr * m_blockSize, map.data(), map.size()) )
                    return fail(error, "cannot read the stream directory's block map");
                std::vector<uint32_t> dirList(dirBlocks);
                for ( uint32_t i = 0; i < dirBlocks; i++ )
                    dirList[i] = rd32(&map[i * 4]);
                std::vector<uint8_t> dir;
                if ( !gather(dirList, dirSize, dir) )
                    return fail(error, "cannot read the stream directory");

                uint32_t nstreams = rd32(dir.data());
                if ( nstreams > kMaxStreams || 4 + (uint64_t)nstreams * 4 > dir.size() )
                    return fail(error, "bad stream count");
                m_sizes.resize(nstreams);
                m_blocks.resize(nstreams);
                size_t at = 4 + (size_t)nstreams * 4;
                for ( uint32_t s = 0; s < nstreams; s++ )
                {
                    uint32_t size = rd32(&dir[4 + (size_t)s * 4]);
                    if ( size == 0xFFFFFFFF )
                        size = 0;       // a deleted (nil) stream
                    if ( !fits(size) )
                        return fail(error, "a stream is larger than the file");
                    m_sizes[s] = size;
                    uint32_t n = blocks_for(size);
                    if ( at + (uint64_t)n * 4 > dir.size() )
                        return fail(error, "the stream directory ends early");
                    m_blocks[s].resize(n);
                    for ( uint32_t b = 0; b < n; b++ )
                        m_blocks[s][b] = rd32(&dir[at + (size_t)b * 4]);
                    at += (size_t)n * 4;
                }
                return true;
            }

            bool stream(uint32_t index, std::vector<uint8_t> &out) const
            {
                if ( index >= m_sizes.size() || m_sizes[index] > kMaxStreamBytes )
                    return false;
                return gather(m_blocks[index], m_sizes[index], out);
            }

        private:
            static bool fail(std::string *error, const char *why)
            {
                if ( error != nullptr )
                    *error = why;
                return false;
            }

            // A stream cannot hold more bytes than the file has blocks; checked
            // before any buffer is sized from an untrusted length.
            bool fits(uint32_t size) const
            {
                return (uint64_t)size <= (uint64_t)m_nblocks * m_blockSize;
            }

            uint32_t blocks_for(uint32_t size) const
            {
                return (uint32_t)(((uint64_t)size + m_blockSize - 1) / m_blockSize);
            }

            bool read_at(uint64_t off, void *buf, size_t size) const
            {
                if ( off > m_fileSize || size > m_fileSize - off )
                    return false;
                if ( _fseeki64(m_file.get(), (long long)off, SEEK_SET) != 0 )
                    return false;
                return fread(buf, 1, size, m_file.get()) == size;
            }

            bool gather(const std::vector<uint32_t> &blocks, uint32_t size,
                        std::vector<uint8_t> &out) const
            {
                // Every block index must name a block of the file, and the
                // list must be long enough for 'size', before allocating.
                if ( !fits(size) || (uint64_t)blocks.size() * m_blockSize < size )
                    return false;
                out.resize(size);
                size_t done = 0;
                for ( uint32_t b : blocks )
                {
                    if ( done >= size )
                        break;
                    if ( b >= m_nblocks )
                        return false;
                    size_t n = size - done < m_blockSize ? size - done : m_blockSize;
                    if ( !read_at((uint64_t)b * m_blockSize, out.data() + done, n) )
                        return false;
                    done += n;
                }
                return done == size;
            }

            std::unique_ptr<FILE, FileCloser>   m_file;
            uint64_t                            m_fileSize  = 0;
            uint32_t                            m_blockSize = 0;
            uint32_t                            m_nblocks   = 0;
            std::vector<uint32_t>               m_sizes;
            std::vector<std::vector<uint32_t>>  m_blocks;
        };
    }

    bool read_pdb_publics(const wchar_t *path, std::vector<PdbPublic> &out, std::string *error)
    {
        out.clear();
        Msf msf;
        if ( !msf.open(path, error) )
            return false;

        auto fail = [&](const char *why)
        {
            if ( error != nullptr )
                *error = why;
            return false;
        };

        // DBI header (64 bytes): the symbol record stream at 20, then the
        // substream sizes. The optional debug header is the last substream,
        // after the EC substream.
        std::vector<uint8_t> dbi;
        if ( !msf.stream(kDbiStream, dbi) || dbi.size() < 64 )
            return fail("no DBI stream");
        if ( (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[0]) != -1 )
            return fail("an old-format DBI stream");
        uint16_t symStream = rd16(&dbi[20]);
        int32_t  sizes[6]  =
        {
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[24]),    // module info
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[28]),    // section contributions
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[32]),    // section map
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[36]),    // source info
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[40]),    // type server map
            (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[52]),    // EC substream
        };
        int32_t dbgSize = (int32_t)rd32(&dbi[48]);
        uint64_t at = 64;
        for ( int32_t s : sizes )
        {
            if ( s < 0 )
                return fail("a damaged DBI stream");
            at += (uint64_t)s;
        }
        if ( dbgSize < 0 || at + (uint64_t)dbgSize > dbi.size() )
            return fail("a damaged DBI stream");
        auto dbg_stream = [&](size_t slot) -> uint16_t
        {
            if ( (slot + 1) * 2 > (size_t)dbgSize )
                return kNilStream;
            return rd16(&dbi[(size_t)at + slot * 2]);
        };

        // An OMAP image's public offsets use the pre-rearrangement layout;
        // these section headers would put every name in the wrong place.
        uint16_t omap = dbg_stream(kDbgOmapFromSrc);
        std::vector<uint8_t> omapBytes;
        if ( omap != kNilStream && msf.stream(omap, omapBytes) && !omapBytes.empty() )
            return fail("the image was rearranged after linking (OMAP)");

        // IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER is 40 bytes, VirtualAddress at 12. A public's
        // segment n is section n, counted from one.
        std::vector<uint8_t> sh;
        uint16_t shStream = dbg_stream(kDbgSectionHdr);
        if ( shStream == kNilStream || !msf.stream(shStream, sh) || sh.size() < 40 )
            return fail("no section headers");
        std::vector<uint32_t> sectionRva(sh.size() / 40);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < sectionRva.size(); i++ )
            sectionRva[i] = rd32(&sh[i * 40 + 12]);

        std::vector<uint8_t> sym;
        if ( symStream == kNilStream || !msf.stream(symStream, sym) )
            return fail("no symbol record stream");

        // Records: u16 length (not counting itself), u16 kind, then the body.
        for ( size_t p = 0; p + 4 <= sym.size(); )
        {
            uint16_t len  = rd16(&sym[p]);
            uint16_t kind = rd16(&sym[p + 2]);
            if ( len < 2 || p + 2 + len > sym.size() )
                break;          // the rest is damaged; keep what was read
            if ( kind == S_PUB32 && len >= 2 + 10 + 1 )
            {
                const uint8_t *b   = &sym[p + 4];
                uint32_t flags     = rd32(b);
                uint32_t offset    = rd32(b + 4);
                uint16_t segment   = rd16(b + 8);
                const char *name   = (const char *)(b + 10);
                size_t maxName     = (size_t)len - 2 - 10;
                size_t nameLen     = strnlen(name, maxName);
                if ( segment >= 1 && segment <= sectionRva.size() && nameLen > 0 )
                {
                    PdbPublic pub;
                    pub.rva  = sectionRva[segment - 1] + offset;
                    pub.code = (flags & (kPubCode | kPubFunction)) != 0;
                    pub.name.assign(name, nameLen);
                    out.push_back(std::move(pub));
                }
            }
            p += 2 + (size_t)len;
        }
        if ( out.empty() )
            return fail("no public symbols");
        return true;
    }
}
```

`src/common/pdb_publics.h`:

```h
#pragma once

// Reading a PDB's public symbols without IDA, on any thread.
//
// IDA's PDB plugin applies a PDB in full (types, prototypes, names) but runs
// on the main thread for seconds per system DLL, which makes a step hang.
// What a system DLL needs is its function names, and Microsoft's public PDBs
// are stripped to public symbols anyway. Those sit in one stream and take
// milliseconds to read, so they are read here off the main thread and only
// the naming is left to IDA.
//
// Standard library only, so a worker thread can call it while the main thread
// owns the database.

#include <cstdint>
#include <string>
#include <vector>

namespace idattd
{
    struct PdbPublic
    {
        uint32_t    rva = 0;        // relative to the module's image base
        bool        code = false;   // a function (cvpsfCode / cvpsfFunction)
        std::string name;           // as recorded: possibly decorated
    };

    // Every public symbol of the PDB at 'path' (wide, since the store is under
    // the user's profile), with section:offset turned into an RVA through the
    // PDB's own section headers. False, with a reason in 'error', when the file
    // is not an MSF 7 PDB, is damaged, or describes an image rearranged after
    // linking (OMAP); such a PDB has to go through IDA's PDB plugin.
    bool read_pdb_publics(const wchar_t *path, std::vector<PdbPublic> &out, std::string *error);
}
```

`src/common/python_eval.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/python_eval.h"
#include "common/json_str.h"

namespace idattd
{
    bool python_available(bool with_expr)
    {
        extlang_object_t py = find_extlang_by_name("Python");
        return py != nullptr && py->eval_snippet != nullptr
            && (!with_expr || py->eval_expr != nullptr);
    }

    bool eval_py(const char *code, qstring *err)
    {
        extlang_object_t py = find_extlang_by_name("Python");
        return py != nullptr && py->eval_snippet != nullptr
            && py->eval_snippet(code, err);
    }

    bool eval_py_expr(idc_value_t *rv, const char *expr, qstring *err)
    {
        extlang_object_t py = find_extlang_by_name("Python");
        return py != nullptr && py->eval_snippet != nullptr && py->eval_expr != nullptr
            && py->eval_expr(rv, BADADDR, expr, err);
    }

    bool call_py(const char *module, const char *fn,
                 std::initializer_list<const char *> args, qstring *err)
    {
        qstring code;
        code.sprnt("import %s\n%s.%s(", module, module, fn);
        bool first = true;
        for ( const char *a : args )
        {
            if ( !first )
                code.append(", ");
            first = false;
            json_str(&code, a);
        }
        code.append(")\n");
        return eval_py(code.c_str(), err);
    }
}
```

`src/common/python_eval.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include <expr.hpp>

#include <initializer_list>

namespace idattd
{
    // Running Python through IDAPython's extlang, which is how the plugin
    // reaches the Qt changes, the settings and the windows that live in
    // scripts/. Every caller used to look the extlang up and check its
    // members itself; these are that code, once.
    //
    // IDAPython can be missing (not installed, or not loaded yet in an idalib
    // worker), so each caller decides what that means: some stay silent,
    // some say so.

    // IDAPython is loaded and can run statements (and, with 'with_expr',
    // evaluate an expression too).
    bool python_available(bool with_expr = false);

    // Run 'code' as Python statements. False without IDAPython, with *err
    // left as it was, or when the code raised, with the message in *err.
    bool eval_py(const char *code, qstring *err);

    // Evaluate the Python expression 'expr' into *rv. False without
    // IDAPython (or without its expression evaluator), with *err left as it
    // was, or when the expression raised, with the message in *err.
    bool eval_py_expr(idc_value_t *rv, const char *expr, qstring *err);

    // import <module>; <module>.<fn>(args...), each argument passed as a
    // quoted string literal (json_str). As eval_py otherwise.
    bool call_py(const char *module, const char *fn,
                 std::initializer_list<const char *> args, qstring *err);
}
```

`src/common/strings.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/strings.h"

namespace idattd
{
    std::string to_utf8(const wchar_t *w, size_t len)
    {
        if ( w == nullptr || len == 0 )
            return std::string();
        int n = WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w, (int)len, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr);
        if ( n <= 0 )
            return std::string();
        std::string s((size_t)n, '\0');
        WideCharToMultiByte(CP_UTF8, 0, w, (int)len, s.data(), n, nullptr, nullptr);
        return s;
    }

    std::string to_utf8(const wchar_t *w)
    {
        return to_utf8(w, w != nullptr ? wcslen(w) : 0);
    }

    std::wstring to_wstring(const char *s)
    {
        if ( s == nullptr || *s == '\0' )
            return std::wstring();
        int n = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s, -1, nullptr, 0);
        if ( n <= 0 )
            return std::wstring();
        std::wstring w((size_t)n, L'\0');
        MultiByteToWideChar(CP_UTF8, 0, s, -1, w.data(), n);
        if ( !w.empty() && w.back() == L'\0' )
            w.pop_back();
        return w;
    }

    std::string base_name(const std::string &path)
    {
        size_t p = path.find_last_of("\\/");
        return p == std::string::npos ? path : path.substr(p + 1);
    }
}
```

`src/common/strings.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // String helpers shared by the core and the backends. The TTD engine uses
    // wide strings and IDA uses UTF-8.
    std::string  to_utf8(const wchar_t *w, size_t len);
    std::string  to_utf8(const wchar_t *w);
    std::wstring to_wstring(const char *s);
    // Everything after the last slash or backslash: how a module's full
    // recorded path is compared with the name the user or database knows.
    std::string  base_name(const std::string &path);
}
```

`src/common/symbols.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/symbols.h"
#include "common/local_path.h"
#include "common/strings.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Open a module file named by the recording. The path is the recording
    // machine's and the recording may be crafted, so only a local drive path
    // is opened (a UNC path would send the user's credentials to its host).
    // The path is UTF-8; the wide open keeps non-ASCII names working, which
    // the narrow (ANSI code page) open does not.
    static bool open_recorded_file(const char *path, std::ifstream &f, std::ios::openmode mode)
    {
        if ( !is_local_drive_path(path) )
            return false;
        std::wstring wpath = to_wstring(path);
        if ( wpath.empty() )
            return false;
        f.open(wpath.c_str(), mode);
        return f.is_open();
    }

    size_t apply_module_exports(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64)
    {
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, std::string>> exports;
        read_guest_exports(cursor, base, is64, &exports);
        size_t named = 0;
        for ( const auto &e : exports )
            if ( apply_export_name(e.first, e.second.c_str()) )
                named++;
        return named;
    }

    bool apply_export_name(ea_t va, const char *name)
    {
        if ( va == BADADDR || name == nullptr || name[0] == '\0' )
            return false;
        // ntdll exports every syscall stub twice, as NtXxx and ZwXxx, and the
        // sorted name table delivers Zw second; naively it would rename every
        // call site to ZwXxx. So the first real name keeps the address, except
        // that Zw gives way to the Nt spelling of the same stub. Dummy
        // sub_/loc_ names are always replaced.
        if ( has_user_name(get_flags(va)) )
        {
            qstring cur;
            if ( get_name(&cur, va) <= 0 )
                return false;
            size_t n = strlen(name);
            bool zw_to_nt = cur.length() == n
                         && n > 2
                         && strncmp(cur.c_str(), "Zw", 2) == 0
                         && strncmp(name, "Nt", 2) == 0
                         && strcmp(cur.c_str() + 2, name + 2) == 0;
            if ( !zw_to_nt )
                return false;
        }
        return set_name(va, name, SN_NOWARN | SN_FORCE | SN_NOCHECK);
    }

    size_t parse_pdata_functions(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64,
                                 std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        // The RUNTIME_FUNCTION table only exists for x64 (x86 SEH is different).
        if ( cursor == nullptr || base == BADADDR || !is64 )
            return 0;

        uint64_t b = (uint64_t)base;
        IMAGE_DOS_HEADER dos{};
        if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, b, &dos) || dos.e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE )
            return 0;

        // The same e_lfanew bound as guest_pe. The magic check matters too: a
        // PE32 image read as PE32+ puts the data directories 16 bytes off.
        if ( dos.e_lfanew < 0 || (uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew > 0x10000000u )
            return 0;
        IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 nt{};
        if ( !pe_read_val(cursor, b + (uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew, &nt) || nt.Signature != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE
          || nt.OptionalHeader.Magic != IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC
          || nt.OptionalHeader.NumberOfRvaAndSizes <= IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXCEPTION )
            return 0;

        const IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY &dd = nt.OptionalHeader.DataDirectory[IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXCEPTION];
        uint32_t rva  = dd.VirtualAddress;
        uint32_t size = dd.Size;
        if ( rva == 0 || size == 0 )
            return 0;

        // RUNTIME_FUNCTION = { uint32 BeginRva; uint32 EndRva; uint32 UnwindRva; }.
        struct RtFunc { uint32_t Begin, End, Unwind; };
        // 'size' is attacker-controlled (the image may be malware); cap it so
        // a corrupt directory cannot ask for a multi-gigabyte buffer.
        static const size_t kMaxFuncs = 1u << 22;   // 4M functions ~ 48 MB
        size_t maxEntries = size / sizeof(RtFunc);
        if ( maxEntries == 0 )
            return 0;
        if ( maxEntries > kMaxFuncs )
            maxEntries = kMaxFuncs;

        std::vector<RtFunc> buf(maxEntries);
        size_t mb = cursor(b + rva, buf.data(), maxEntries * sizeof(RtFunc));
        size_t got = mb / sizeof(RtFunc);

        out.reserve(got);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < got; i++ )
        {
            const RtFunc &rf = buf[i];
            if ( rf.Begin == 0 || rf.End <= rf.Begin )
                continue;
            out.emplace_back((ea_t)(b + rf.Begin), (ea_t)(b + rf.End));
        }
        std::sort(out.begin(), out.end());
        return out.size();
    }

    size_t parse_pdata_functions_from_file(const char *path, ea_t base, bool is64,
                                           uint32_t want_timestamp, uint32_t want_checksum,
                                           std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        if ( path == nullptr || *path == '\0' || base == BADADDR || !is64 )
            return 0;

        std::ifstream f;
        if ( !open_recorded_file(path, f, std::ios::binary) )
            return 0;

        IMAGE_DOS_HEADER dos{};
        f.read((char *)&dos, sizeof(dos));
        if ( !f || dos.e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE )
            return 0;

        // The same e_lfanew bound and directory-count check as the guest
        // reader above: entries past NumberOfRvaAndSizes are not directories.
        if ( dos.e_lfanew < 0 || (uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew > 0x10000000u )
            return 0;
        f.seekg((std::streamoff)(uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew, std::ios::beg);
        IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 nt{};
        f.read((char *)&nt, sizeof(nt));
        if ( !f || nt.Signature != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE
          || nt.OptionalHeader.Magic != IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC
          || nt.OptionalHeader.NumberOfRvaAndSizes <= IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXCEPTION )
            return 0;

        // The path is the recording machine's; a local file there with other
        // headers is a different build whose bounds would be silently wrong.
        if ( (want_timestamp != 0 && nt.FileHeader.TimeDateStamp != want_timestamp)
          || (want_checksum  != 0 && nt.OptionalHeader.CheckSum  != want_checksum) )
            return 0;

        const IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY &dd = nt.OptionalHeader.DataDirectory[IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_EXCEPTION];
        uint32_t rva  = dd.VirtualAddress;
        uint32_t size = dd.Size;
        if ( rva == 0 || size == 0 )
            return 0;

        // Map the .pdata RVA to a file offset via the section headers (which
        // follow the optional header).
        uint64_t secOff = (uint64_t)(uint32_t)dos.e_lfanew + 4
                        + sizeof(IMAGE_FILE_HEADER) + nt.FileHeader.SizeOfOptionalHeader;
        f.seekg((std::streamoff)secOff, std::ios::beg);

        uint64_t fileOff = 0;
        bool     found   = false;
        for ( uint16_t i = 0; i < nt.FileHeader.NumberOfSections; i++ )
        {
            IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER sec{};
            f.read((char *)&sec, sizeof(sec));
            if ( !f )
                break;
            uint32_t vsize = sec.Misc.VirtualSize != 0 ? sec.Misc.VirtualSize : sec.SizeOfRawData;
            // Differences, not sums: header fields near 4 GB must not wrap.
            if ( rva >= sec.VirtualAddress && rva - sec.VirtualAddress < vsize )
            {
                fileOff = sec.PointerToRawData + (uint64_t)(rva - sec.VirtualAddress);
                found   = true;
                break;
            }
        }
        if ( !found )
            return 0;

        struct RtFunc { uint32_t Begin, End, Unwind; };
        // 'size' is untrusted: bound it by a hard cap and by the file length.
        static const size_t kMaxFuncs = 1u << 22;
        size_t count = size / sizeof(RtFunc);
        if ( count == 0 )
            return 0;
        f.seekg(0, std::ios::end);
        uint64_t fileLen = (uint64_t)f.tellg();
        if ( fileOff >= fileLen )
            return 0;
        size_t avail = (size_t)((fileLen - fileOff) / sizeof(RtFunc));
        if ( count > avail )
            count = avail;
        if ( count > kMaxFuncs )
            count = kMaxFuncs;
        if ( count == 0 )
            return 0;

        std::vector<RtFunc> buf(count);
        f.seekg((std::streamoff)fileOff, std::ios::beg);
        f.read((char *)buf.data(), (std::streamsize)(count * sizeof(RtFunc)));
        size_t got = (size_t)f.gcount() / sizeof(RtFunc);

        uint64_t b = (uint64_t)base;
        out.reserve(got);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < got; i++ )
        {
            const RtFunc &rf = buf[i];
            if ( rf.Begin == 0 || rf.End <= rf.Begin )
                continue;
            out.emplace_back((ea_t)(b + rf.Begin), (ea_t)(b + rf.End));
        }
        std::sort(out.begin(), out.end());
        return out.size();
    }

    bool load_module_image(const char *path, ModuleImage &out)
    {
        out = ModuleImage{};
        if ( path == nullptr || *path == '\0' )
            return false;

        std::ifstream f;
        if ( !open_recorded_file(path, f, std::ios::binary | std::ios::ate) )
            return false;
        std::streamoff len = f.tellg();
        if ( len <= 0 )
            return false;
        // The path comes from the recording: it can name any local file (a
        // disk image, a dump). Read only what can be a module: a PE header
        // first, and nothing larger than any real DLL.
        const std::streamoff MAX_IMAGE_FILE = std::streamoff(1) << 30;     // 1 GiB
        if ( len > MAX_IMAGE_FILE || len < (std::streamoff)sizeof(IMAGE_DOS_HEADER) )
            return false;
        {
            char mz[2] = { 0, 0 };
            f.seekg(0, std::ios::beg);
            f.read(mz, 2);
            if ( f.gcount() != 2 || mz[0] != 'M' || mz[1] != 'Z' )
                return false;
        }
        out.file.resize((size_t)len);
        f.seekg(0, std::ios::beg);
        f.read((char *)out.file.data(), (std::streamsize)len);
        if ( (size_t)f.gcount() != out.file.size() )
            out.file.resize((size_t)f.gcount());

        const uint8_t *base = out.file.data();
        size_t         fsz  = out.file.size();
        if ( fsz < sizeof(IMAGE_DOS_HEADER) )
            return false;

        const IMAGE_DOS_HEADER *dos = (const IMAGE_DOS_HEADER *)base;
        if ( dos->e_magic != IMAGE_DOS_SIGNATURE )
            return false;

        if ( dos->e_lfanew < 0 )
            return false;
        uint32_t ntoff = (uint32_t)dos->e_lfanew;
        if ( (size_t)ntoff + sizeof(IMAGE_NT_HEADERS32) > fsz )
            return false;
        const IMAGE_NT_HEADERS32 *nt32 = (const IMAGE_NT_HEADERS32 *)(base + ntoff);
        if ( nt32->Signature != IMAGE_NT_SIGNATURE )
            return false;

        uint16_t nsec    = nt32->FileHeader.NumberOfSections;
        uint16_t optsz   = nt32->FileHeader.SizeOfOptionalHeader;
        out.timestamp    = nt32->FileHeader.TimeDateStamp;
        if ( nt32->OptionalHeader.Magic == IMAGE_NT_OPTIONAL_HDR64_MAGIC )
        {
            // IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 is larger than the 32-bit form checked above;
            // re-check so a truncated PE32+ file is not read past its end.
            if ( (size_t)ntoff + sizeof(IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64) > fsz )
                return false;
            const IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 *nt64 = (const IMAGE_NT_HEADERS64 *)(base + ntoff);
            out.sizeOfHeaders = nt64->OptionalHeader.SizeOfHeaders;
            out.checksum      = nt64->OptionalHeader.CheckSum;
            out.sizeOfImage   = nt64->OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage;
        }
        else
        {
            out.sizeOfHeaders = nt32->OptionalHeader.SizeOfHeaders;
            out.checksum      = nt32->OptionalHeader.CheckSum;
            out.sizeOfImage   = nt32->OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage;
        }

        size_t secOff = (size_t)ntoff + 4 + sizeof(IMAGE_FILE_HEADER) + optsz;
        if ( secOff + (size_t)nsec * sizeof(IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER) > fsz )
            return false;

        const IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER *secs = (const IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER *)(base + secOff);
        out.sections.reserve(nsec);
        for ( uint16_t i = 0; i < nsec; i++ )
        {
            ModuleImage::Section s{};
            s.va      = secs[i].VirtualAddress;
            s.vsize   = secs[i].Misc.VirtualSize != 0 ? secs[i].Misc.VirtualSize : secs[i].SizeOfRawData;
            s.raw     = secs[i].PointerToRawData;
            s.rawsize = secs[i].SizeOfRawData;
            out.sections.push_back(s);
        }
        out.ok = true;
        return true;
    }

    size_t read_module_image_rva(const ModuleImage &img, uint32_t rva, void *buf, size_t size)
    {
        if ( !img.ok || size == 0 )
            return 0;

        // The PE headers are mapped 1:1 from file offset 0.
        if ( rva < img.sizeOfHeaders )
        {
            size_t avail = img.sizeOfHeaders - rva;
            if ( (size_t)rva >= img.file.size() )
                return 0;
            size_t fileAvail = img.file.size() - rva;
            size_t run = size < avail ? size : avail;
            if ( run > fileAvail )
                run = fileAvail;
            memcpy(buf, img.file.data() + rva, run);
            return run;
        }

        // Otherwise locate the section whose virtual range contains rva.
        for ( const ModuleImage::Section &s : img.sections )
        {
            if ( rva < s.va || rva - s.va >= s.vsize )
                continue;
            uint32_t inSec = rva - s.va;
            if ( inSec >= s.rawsize )
                return 0;                       // zero-fill tail (.bss): leave it 0
            uint64_t fileOff = (uint64_t)s.raw + inSec;
            if ( (size_t)fileOff >= img.file.size() )
                return 0;
            size_t avail     = s.rawsize - inSec;            // contiguous raw bytes
            size_t fileAvail = img.file.size() - fileOff;
            size_t run = size < avail ? size : avail;
            if ( run > fileAvail )
                run = fileAvail;
            memcpy(buf, img.file.data() + fileOff, run);
            return run;
        }
        return 0;
    }
}
```

`src/common/symbols.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/guest_view.h"
#include "common/guest_pe.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Name every export of the module at 'base' from its export table in guest
    // memory. 'cursor' must be positioned where the module is loaded. Returns
    // the number of names applied.
    //
    // The offline symbol path: needs no symbol server. PDB names, when
    // available, are applied on top and add non-exported functions.
    size_t apply_module_exports(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64);

    // Name one exported address by the rule every name source follows: a real
    // name already there wins, except that a Zw syscall stub gives way to the
    // Nt spelling of the same stub. True when the name was applied.
    bool apply_export_name(ea_t va, const char *name);

    // The [start, end) range of every function of the module at 'base', from
    // its x64 exception directory (.pdata) in guest memory, sorted by start.
    // This recovers function bounds of stripped system DLLs without symbols,
    // as WinDbg does. Returns the count; 0 for x86, which has no such table.
    size_t parse_pdata_functions(const GuestRead &cursor, ea_t base, bool is64,
                                 std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out);

    // Same, from the module's on-disk PE file at 'path'. The more complete
    // source: TTD records only accessed memory, and .pdata is often never
    // touched. A non-zero 'want_timestamp' / 'want_checksum' (from the trace's
    // Module record) must match the file's NT headers, else the file is a
    // different build and its bounds would be wrong. Pass 0 for both to skip.
    size_t parse_pdata_functions_from_file(const char *path, ea_t base, bool is64,
                                           uint32_t want_timestamp, uint32_t want_checksum,
                                           std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out);

    // A module's on-disk PE image, cached to serve bytes the recording never
    // saw (code never executed or read). WinDbg fills those gaps from the file
    // too. Recorded memory always wins (it reflects self-modification); the
    // image only fills holes.
    struct ModuleImage
    {
        struct Section { uint32_t va, vsize, raw, rawsize; };
        std::vector<uint8_t> file;        // whole file contents
        std::vector<Section> sections;
        uint32_t             sizeOfHeaders = 0;
        // Identity of the file opened, from its NT headers. The trace records
        // the same values, so the caller can refuse a different build: the
        // path is the recording machine's and may name another file here.
        uint32_t             timestamp = 0;   // FileHeader.TimeDateStamp
        uint32_t             checksum  = 0;   // OptionalHeader.CheckSum
        uint32_t             sizeOfImage = 0; // OptionalHeader.SizeOfImage
        bool                 ok = false;  // false once tried and failed
    };

    // Read the module file at 'path' into 'out' and parse its section map.
    // Returns out.ok; false (not a crash) for a missing or non-PE file.
    bool load_module_image(const char *path, ModuleImage &out);

    // Copy up to 'size' image bytes starting at 'rva' into 'buf'. Returns the
    // length of one contiguous run (bounded by the containing section's raw
    // data, or the headers), or 0 when 'rva' has no file bytes (a zero-fill
    // tail), which the caller leaves zero as the loader would.
    size_t read_module_image_rva(const ModuleImage &img, uint32_t rva, void *buf, size_t size);
}
```
