`src/common/symsrv.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/symsrv.h"
#include "common/strings.h"
#include "common/local_path.h"

#include <condition_variable>
#include <winhttp.h>
#pragma comment(lib, "winhttp.lib")

namespace idattd
{
    // Where PDBs come from: Microsoft's server unless the symbol_server setting
    // names another (symsrv_configure). Set at plugin load, before any fetch,
    // and copied into each fetch so workers never read the global.
    struct Server
    {
        bool          enabled = true;
        qstring       url     = "https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols";
        std::wstring  host    = L"msdl.microsoft.com";
        INTERNET_PORT port    = INTERNET_DEFAULT_HTTPS_PORT;
        bool          secure  = true;
        std::wstring  root    = L"/download/symbols";
    };
    static Server g_server;
    // The conventional symbol-client user agent; some servers serve only it.
    static const wchar_t SYM_AGENT[] = L"Microsoft-Symbol-Server/10.0.0.0";

    // Timeouts in milliseconds: generous on receive (a PDB can be tens of MB),
    // tight on connect (an unreachable server is the case this file is for).
    static const int TMO_RESOLVE = 5000;
    static const int TMO_CONNECT = 5000;
    static const int TMO_SEND    = 15000;
    static const int TMO_RECEIVE = 60000;

    // Asking for dozens of PDBs at once made the server stop answering some
    // of them on a fresh machine (ntdll's among them). So a few at a time,
    // and an unanswered request is retried after a pause.
    static const size_t MAX_PARALLEL = 4;
    static const int    ATTEMPTS     = 3;
    static const int    RETRY_MS[]   = { 2000, 6000 };

    namespace
    {
        // A download thread and the flag it sets when it has finished, so
        // fetch_pdb can join it without blocking.
        struct Worker
        {
            std::thread                        thread;
            std::shared_ptr<std::atomic<bool>> done;
        };

        struct State
        {
            std::mutex               mtx;
            std::vector<Worker>      workers;
            std::vector<FetchResult> completed;
            std::set<qstring>        seen;      // identities being fetched now
            size_t                   pending = 0;
            size_t                   running = 0;   // downloads holding a slot
            std::condition_variable  cv;            // a slot freed, or abort
            std::atomic<bool>        abort{ false };
            // Requests a worker may be blocked in. Closing one from another
            // thread makes the blocked WinHTTP call fail at once; the abort
            // flag is only checked between reads.
            std::set<HINTERNET>      live;
        };

        State &state()
        {
            static State s;
            return s;
        }

        // Create every level of 'dir'. A failure at any level is harmless:
        // either it exists, or the file create that needs it fails and is
        // reported there.
        void make_dirs(const qstring &dir)
        {
            qstring cur;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < dir.length(); i++ )
            {
                cur.append(dir[i]);
                if ( dir[i] == '/' || dir[i] == '\\' || i + 1 == dir.length() )
                    qmkdir(cur.c_str(), 0755);
            }
        }

        // A closer for every HINTERNET, so no early return leaks one.
        struct Handle
        {
            HINTERNET h = nullptr;
            ~Handle() { if ( h != nullptr ) WinHttpCloseHandle(h); }
            operator HINTERNET() const { return h; }
        };

        // Download one PDB to 'dest' via a ".part" file renamed on success, so
        // an interrupted fetch never leaves a short file that looks complete.
        // '*again' says whether a retry is worthwhile (no answer, or busy),
        // as opposed to a PDB the server does not have.
        bool download(const Server &srv, const std::wstring &url_path, const qstring &dest,
                      qstring *err, bool *again)
        {
            *again = false;
            Handle session;
            session.h = WinHttpOpen(SYM_AGENT, WINHTTP_ACCESS_TYPE_AUTOMATIC_PROXY,
                                    WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_NAME, WINHTTP_NO_PROXY_BYPASS, 0);
            if ( session.h == nullptr )
            {
                *err = "could not open an HTTP session";
                return false;
            }
            WinHttpSetTimeouts(session.h, TMO_RESOLVE, TMO_CONNECT, TMO_SEND, TMO_RECEIVE);

            Handle conn;
            conn.h = WinHttpConnect(session.h, srv.host.c_str(), srv.port, 0);
            if ( conn.h == nullptr )
            {
                *err = "could not reach the symbol server";
                *again = true;
                return false;
            }

            Handle req;
            req.h = WinHttpOpenRequest(conn.h, L"GET", url_path.c_str(), nullptr,
                                       WINHTTP_NO_REFERER, WINHTTP_DEFAULT_ACCEPT_TYPES,
                                       srv.secure ? WINHTTP_FLAG_SECURE : 0);
            if ( req.h == nullptr )
            {
                *err = "could not build the request";
                return false;
            }

            // Register the request so symsrv_shutdown() can cancel it, and
            // unregister on the way out. If shutdown already closed the
            // handle, it must not be closed again here.
            {
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state().mtx);
                if ( state().abort.load() )
                {
                    *err = "canceled";
                    return false;
                }
                state().live.insert(req.h);
            }
            struct Unregister
            {
                Handle &req;
                ~Unregister()
                {
                    std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(state().mtx);
                    if ( state().live.erase(req.h) == 0 )
                        req.h = nullptr;
                }
            } unregister{ req };

            if ( !WinHttpSendRequest(req.h, WINHTTP_NO_ADDITIONAL_HEADERS, 0,
                                     WINHTTP_NO_REQUEST_DATA, 0, 0, 0)
              || !WinHttpReceiveResponse(req.h, nullptr) )
            {
                *err = "no response from the symbol server";
                *again = true;
                return false;
            }

            DWORD status = 0, len = sizeof(status);
            if ( !WinHttpQueryHeaders(req.h,
                                      WINHTTP_QUERY_STATUS_CODE | WINHTTP_QUERY_FLAG_NUMBER,
                                      WINHTTP_HEADER_NAME_BY_INDEX, &status, &len,
                                      WINHTTP_NO_HEADER_INDEX) )
            {
                *err = "no status from the symbol server";
                return false;
            }
            if ( status != 200 )
            {
                err->sprnt("the symbol server answered %d", (int)status);
                *again = status == 429 || status >= 500;
                return false;
            }

            qstring tmp = dest;
            tmp.append(".part");
            // qfopen, like the qrename/qunlink below, takes IDA's UTF-8 paths.
            FILE *f = qfopen(tmp.c_str(), "wb");
            if ( f == nullptr )
            {
                err->sprnt("could not write %s", tmp.c_str());
                return false;
            }

            // The body becomes the PDB that IDA's PDB plugin and the publics
            // reader open, so it is checked before it is renamed into the
            // store: an error page, a captive portal's answer or a hostile
            // server's endless body must not land there. Only uncompressed
            // PDBs are requested (no .pd_), so the MSF 7.00 magic must lead.
            static const char     kMsfMagic[] = "Microsoft C/C++ MSF 7.00\r\n\x1a" "DS\0\0";
            static const size_t   kMsfMagicSize = 32;
            static const uint64_t kMaxBody = 1ull << 30;   // far above any real PDB
            char     head[kMsfMagicSize] = { 0 };
            uint64_t total = 0;

            std::vector<char> buf(64 * 1024);
            bool ok = true;
            for ( ;; )
            {
                if ( state().abort.load() )
                {
                    *err = "canceled";
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                DWORD got = 0;
                if ( !WinHttpReadData(req.h, buf.data(), (DWORD)buf.size(), &got) )
                {
                    *err = "the download was interrupted";
                    *again = true;
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                if ( got == 0 )
                    break;                          // end of body
                if ( total < kMsfMagicSize )
                {
                    size_t n = (size_t)qmin((uint64_t)got, kMsfMagicSize - total);
                    memcpy(head + total, buf.data(), n);
                }
                total += got;
                if ( total > kMaxBody )
                {
                    *err = "the symbol server's answer is too large to be a PDB";
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
                if ( fwrite(buf.data(), 1, got, f) != got )
                {
                    *err = "could not write the downloaded file";
                    ok = false;
                    break;
                }
            }
            qfclose(f);

            if ( ok && (total < kMsfMagicSize || memcmp(head, kMsfMagic, kMsfMagicSize) != 0) )
            {
                *err = "the symbol server's answer is not a PDB";
                ok = false;
            }

            if ( !ok || qrename(tmp.c_str(), dest.c_str()) != 0 )
            {
                qunlink(tmp.c_str());
                if ( ok )
                    *err = "could not move the downloaded file into place";
                return false;
            }
            return true;
        }

        // Up to ATTEMPTS downloads, holding one MAX_PARALLEL slot throughout.
        // Pauses between attempts end early on shutdown.
        bool download_with_retries(const Server &srv, const std::wstring &url_path, const qstring &dest,
                                   qstring *err)
        {
            State &s = state();
            {
                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
                s.cv.wait(lock, [&] { return s.abort.load() || s.running < MAX_PARALLEL; });
                if ( s.abort.load() )
                {
                    *err = "canceled";
                    return false;
                }
                s.running++;
            }
            bool ok = false;
            for ( int attempt = 0; attempt < ATTEMPTS; attempt++ )
            {
                bool again = false;
                ok = download(srv, url_path, dest, err, &again);
                if ( ok || !again || attempt + 1 == ATTEMPTS )
                    break;
                std::unique_lock<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
                if ( s.cv.wait_for(lock, std::chrono::milliseconds(RETRY_MS[attempt]),
                                   [&] { return s.abort.load(); }) )
                    break;
            }
            {
                std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
                s.running--;
            }
            s.cv.notify_all();
            return ok;
        }
    }

    qstring symbol_store_dir()
    {
        // Under LOCALAPPDATA rather than temp: PDBs are expensive to fetch and
        // worth keeping across reboots. qgetenv, not getenv: IDA's file
        // functions take UTF-8, and getenv's ANSI text mangles a profile path
        // outside the code page.
        qstring dir;
        qstring local;
        if ( qgetenv("LOCALAPPDATA", &local) && !local.empty() )
            dir.sprnt("%s/ida-ttd/symbols", local.c_str());
        else
            dir = "ida-ttd-symbols";
        return dir;
    }

    // Name and signature become store directory and file names and URL path
    // segments, and the name comes from the recorded image (written by the
    // malware author, for a malware recording). Only the characters of real
    // PDB names and signatures are accepted: no separators, drive or stream
    // colons, URL metacharacters, "." or "..", and a bounded length.
    static bool safe_component(const char *s)
    {
        size_t n = strlen(s);
        if ( n == 0 || n > 128 || strcmp(s, ".") == 0 || strcmp(s, "..") == 0 )
            return false;
        // "nul.pdb" would name a device, not a file in the store.
        if ( is_dos_device_name(s, n) )
            return false;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < n; i++ )
        {
            unsigned char c = (unsigned char)s[i];
            bool alnum = (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z')
                      || (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z');
            if ( !(alnum || c == '.' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '+') )
                return false;
        }
        return true;
    }

    qstring symbol_store_path(const char *name, const char *signature)
    {
        qstring p;
        if ( name == nullptr || signature == nullptr
          || !safe_component(name) || !safe_component(signature) )
        {
            return p;
        }
        p.sprnt("%s/%s/%s/%s", symbol_store_dir().c_str(), name, signature, name);
        return p;
    }

    void symsrv_install_path()
    {
        qstring store = symbol_store_dir();
        qstring want;
        // With downloads off, the store alone, so IDA's PDB plugin does not
        // fetch either.
        if ( g_server.enabled )
            want.sprnt("srv*%s*%s", store.c_str(), g_server.url.c_str());
        else
            want.sprnt("srv*%s", store.c_str());

        // Keep the user's path after this one: their store may hold PDBs the
        // public server lacks.
        qstring existing;
        if ( qgetenv("_NT_SYMBOL_PATH", &existing) && !existing.empty() )
        {
            if ( existing.find(store) != qstring::npos )
                return;                     // already installed this session
            want.cat_sprnt(";%s", existing.c_str());
        }
        qsetenv("_NT_SYMBOL_PATH", want.c_str());
    }

    bool symsrv_configure(bool enabled, const char *url)
    {
        Server srv;
        srv.enabled = enabled;
        if ( url != nullptr && url[0] != '\0' && strcmp(url, srv.url.c_str()) != 0 )
        {
            // WinHttpCrackUrl returns pointers into its input, so the wide
            // copy must outlive the uses below.
            std::wstring wurl = to_wstring(url);
            URL_COMPONENTS uc = { sizeof(uc) };
            uc.dwHostNameLength = (DWORD)-1;
            uc.dwUrlPathLength  = (DWORD)-1;
            if ( !WinHttpCrackUrl(wurl.c_str(), 0, 0, &uc) || uc.dwHostNameLength == 0
              || (uc.nScheme != INTERNET_SCHEME_HTTPS && uc.nScheme != INTERNET_SCHEME_HTTP) )
            {
                g_server.enabled = enabled;
                return false;               // keep the server, honor the switch
            }
            srv.url    = url;
            srv.host   = std::wstring(uc.lpszHostName, uc.dwHostNameLength);
            srv.port   = uc.nPort;
            srv.secure = uc.nScheme == INTERNET_SCHEME_HTTPS;
            srv.root   = std::wstring(uc.lpszUrlPath, uc.dwUrlPathLength);
            while ( !srv.root.empty() && srv.root.back() == L'/' )
                srv.root.pop_back();
        }
        g_server = srv;
        return true;
    }

    qstring symsrv_server_url()
    {
        return g_server.url;
    }

    FetchState fetch_pdb(const char *name, const char *signature, ea_t base)
    {
        qstring dest = symbol_store_path(name, signature);
        if ( dest.empty() )
            return FetchState::Failed;
        if ( qfileexist(dest.c_str()) )
            return FetchState::Cached;
        if ( !g_server.enabled )
            return FetchState::Off;

        State &s = state();
        if ( s.abort.load() )
            return FetchState::Failed;

        qstring key;
        key.sprnt("%s/%s", name, signature);

        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
        if ( !s.seen.insert(key).second )
            return FetchState::Fetching;    // already being fetched; it reports when done

        // Join the workers that have finished, so a long session does not
        // keep one thread object per PDB until shutdown. A worker sets its
        // flag as the last thing it does under this lock, so one seen done
        // here has released the lock and only has to return: the join does
        // not wait on anything this thread holds.
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < s.workers.size(); )
        {
            if ( s.workers[i].done->load() )
            {
                if ( s.workers[i].thread.joinable() )
                    s.workers[i].thread.join();
                s.workers.erase(s.workers.begin() + i);
            }
            else
            {
                i++;
            }
        }

        // Create the directory here so all path handling stays on one thread.
        qstring dir;
        dir.sprnt("%s/%s/%s", symbol_store_dir().c_str(), name, signature);
        make_dirs(dir);

        std::wstring url;
        url.append(g_server.root);
        url.append(L"/");
        url.append(to_wstring(name));
        url.append(L"/");
        url.append(to_wstring(signature));
        url.append(L"/");
        url.append(to_wstring(name));

        qstring qname = name;
        s.pending++;
        auto done = std::make_shared<std::atomic<bool>>(false);
        Worker w;
        w.done   = done;
        w.thread = std::thread([srv = g_server, url, dest, qname, key, base, done]()
        {
            qstring err;
            bool ok = download_with_retries(srv, url, dest, &err);

            State &st = state();
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> l(st.mtx);
            // The key leaves the in-flight set either way: a failed identity
            // may be asked for again (the next stop in its module), and a
            // fetched one is found in the store (Cached) from now on.
            st.seen.erase(key);
            FetchResult r;
            r.base  = base;
            r.name  = qname;
            r.path  = ok ? dest : qstring();
            r.error = ok ? qstring() : err;
            st.completed.push_back(r);
            st.pending--;
            done->store(true);      // last, under the lock (see fetch_pdb)
        });
        s.workers.push_back(std::move(w));
        return FetchState::Fetching;
    }

    size_t symsrv_take_completed(std::vector<FetchResult> *out)
    {
        if ( out == nullptr )
            return 0;
        State &s = state();
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
        size_t n = s.completed.size();
        for ( const FetchResult &r : s.completed )
            out->push_back(r);
        s.completed.clear();
        return n;
    }

    size_t symsrv_pending()
    {
        State &s = state();
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
        return s.pending;
    }

    void symsrv_shutdown()
    {
        State &s = state();
        s.abort.store(true);
        s.cv.notify_all();      // workers waiting for a slot or between attempts

        // Close every request in flight (so no worker waits out a receive
        // timeout), and move the threads out under the lock, then join outside
        // it: a worker takes the same lock on its way out.
        std::vector<Worker> mine;
        {
            std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
            for ( HINTERNET h : s.live )
                WinHttpCloseHandle(h);
            s.live.clear();
            mine.swap(s.workers);
        }
        for ( Worker &w : mine )
            if ( w.thread.joinable() )
                w.thread.join();

        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(s.mtx);
        s.completed.clear();
        s.seen.clear();
        s.pending = 0;
        s.running = 0;
        s.abort.store(false);
    }
}
```

`src/common/symsrv.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Fetching PDBs from the symbol server on worker threads.
    //
    // IDA's PDB plugin downloads on the main thread, so a slow or unreachable
    // server freezes the UI. The download itself touches no IDA state, so it
    // runs here in the background, into a local store laid out like a symbol
    // server; the PDB plugin is then only asked for files already on disk.
    // No new data leaves the machine: the same identities went to the same
    // server before, from the main thread.

    // The local store, created on first use. Mirrors the symbol-server layout
    // (<store>/<name>/<signature>/<name>) so other tools can read it too.
    qstring symbol_store_dir();

    // Where a PDB with this identity belongs in the store; empty when the name
    // or signature is not a safe path component.
    qstring symbol_store_path(const char *name, const char *signature);

    // Put the store at the front of this process's _NT_SYMBOL_PATH so IDA's
    // PDB plugin looks there before the network. The user's own path is kept
    // after it. Call once per session.
    void symsrv_install_path();

    // Ask for a PDB. Returns immediately.
    //
    //   Cached   the file is already in the store; load it now
    //   Fetching a worker is downloading it (perhaps for an earlier request,
    //            whose 'base' the completion then carries);
    //            symsrv_take_completed() reports
    //   Failed   nothing to wait for (a bad identity, or shutting down; a
    //            failed fetch may be asked for again)
    //   Off      not in the store, and downloads are turned off
    //
    // A few downloads run at a time; one the server did not answer is retried
    // after a pause before it is reported as failed.
    enum class FetchState { Cached, Fetching, Failed, Off };
    FetchState fetch_pdb(const char *name, const char *signature, ea_t base);

    // The symbol_downloads and symbol_server settings, before any fetch (and
    // before symsrv_install_path). False when 'url' is not an HTTP(S) URL,
    // which keeps the server in use.
    bool symsrv_configure(bool enabled, const char *url);

    // The server PDBs come from, as a URL.
    qstring symsrv_server_url();

    // One finished download, taken off the completion queue.
    struct FetchResult
    {
        ea_t    base = BADADDR;     // the module it was wanted for
        qstring name;               // e.g. "ntdll.pdb"
        qstring path;               // where it landed, empty when it failed
        qstring error;              // why, when it failed
    };

    // Drain the finished downloads. Main thread only (it hands work back to
    // IDA). Returns the number of results appended to 'out'.
    size_t symsrv_take_completed(std::vector<FetchResult> *out);

    // How many downloads are still running.
    size_t symsrv_pending();

    // Stop accepting new work, ask running fetches to give up, and wait for the
    // threads to finish. Safe to call more than once.
    void symsrv_shutdown();
}
```

`src/common/trace_link.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "common/trace_link.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A "$ " name, like the plugin's other netnodes, cannot collide with a
    // program byte name.
    static const char  TL_NODE[] = "$ ida-ttd trace";
    static const uchar TL_STR    = 'S';   // supstr slots
    static const uchar TL_NUM    = 'N';   // altval slots

    // Slot numbers. A new field takes a new slot and a version bump; changing
    // a slot's meaning requires the version check to reject the old layout.
    enum
    {
        S_TRACE_PATH  = 0,
        S_MODULE_PATH = 1,
        S_MODULE_NAME = 2,
    };
    enum
    {
        N_VERSION     = 0,
        N_MODULE_BASE = 1,
        N_MODULE_SIZE = 2,
        // 1 = 32-bit, 2 = 64-bit, so 0 (altval's missing slot) means unknown.
        N_BITNESS     = 3,
        // 4 held the per-database automatic start answer; the
        // replay_on_open setting replaced it. Not to be reused: old
        // databases still have it.
    };

    static const nodeidx_t TL_VERSION = 1;

    // A supval holds at most MAXSPECSIZE bytes, so a longer path (a deep
    // folder, or a few hundred non-Latin characters in UTF-8) went
    // unstored and the database lost its recording. One that fits keeps its
    // supstr slot, which every build reads; a longer one goes in a blob at
    // the same index (tag TL_BLOB), read first, with the supstr emptied.
    static const uchar TL_BLOB = 'B';

    static void put_str(netnode &nn, nodeidx_t slot, const char *s)
    {
        const size_t n = qstrlen(s);
        nn.delblob(slot, TL_BLOB);
        if ( n + 1 <= MAXSPECSIZE )
        {
            nn.supset(slot, s, n + 1, TL_STR);
            return;
        }
        nn.supset(slot, "", 1, TL_STR);
        nn.setblob(s, n, slot, TL_BLOB);
    }

    static void get_str(netnode &nn, nodeidx_t slot, qstring *out)
    {
        out->qclear();
        bytevec_t b;
        if ( nn.getblob(&b, slot, TL_BLOB) > 0 )
        {
            out->append((const char *)b.begin(), b.size());
            return;
        }
        nn.supstr(out, slot, TL_STR);
    }

    bool trace_link_present()
    {
        netnode nn(TL_NODE);
        if ( nn == BADNODE )
            return false;
        return nn.altval(N_VERSION, TL_NUM) == TL_VERSION;
    }

    bool trace_link_read(TraceLink *out)
    {
        if ( out == nullptr )
            return false;
        netnode nn(TL_NODE);
        if ( nn == BADNODE )
            return false;
        // Refuse an unknown schema rather than return half of it.
        if ( nn.altval(N_VERSION, TL_NUM) != TL_VERSION )
            return false;

        *out = TraceLink();
        get_str(nn, S_TRACE_PATH,  &out->trace_path);
        get_str(nn, S_MODULE_PATH, &out->module_path);
        get_str(nn, S_MODULE_NAME, &out->module_name);
        out->module_base = (ea_t)nn.altval(N_MODULE_BASE, TL_NUM);
        out->module_size = (uint64_t)nn.altval(N_MODULE_SIZE, TL_NUM);

        nodeidx_t b = nn.altval(N_BITNESS, TL_NUM);
        out->bitness = b == 1 ? 32 : b == 2 ? 64 : 0;

        return !out->trace_path.empty();
    }

    void trace_link_write(const TraceLink &link)
    {
        netnode nn(TL_NODE, 0, true);   // create on first write
        nn.altset(N_VERSION, TL_VERSION, TL_NUM);
        put_str(nn, S_TRACE_PATH,  link.trace_path.c_str());
        put_str(nn, S_MODULE_PATH, link.module_path.c_str());
        put_str(nn, S_MODULE_NAME, link.module_name.c_str());
        nn.altset(N_MODULE_BASE, (nodeidx_t)link.module_base, TL_NUM);
        nn.altset(N_MODULE_SIZE, (nodeidx_t)link.module_size, TL_NUM);
        nn.altset(N_BITNESS, link.bitness == 32 ? 1 : link.bitness == 64 ? 2 : 0, TL_NUM);
    }

    void trace_link_set_path(const char *path)
    {
        if ( path == nullptr )
            return;
        netnode nn(TL_NODE, 0, true);
        put_str(nn, S_TRACE_PATH, path);
    }

    // Settings subkey for the start mark. One value per database, so one that
    // fails does not block the others.
    static const char TL_REGKEY[] = "ida-ttd";

    static qstring start_mark_name()
    {
        const char *path = get_path(PATH_TYPE_IDB);
        if ( path == nullptr || path[0] == 0 )
            path = get_path(PATH_TYPE_CMD);
        if ( path == nullptr || path[0] == 0 )
            return qstring();
        qstring name = "starting:";
        name.append(path);
        return name;
    }

    bool trace_link_start_marked()
    {
        qstring name = start_mark_name();
        return !name.empty() && reg_read_int(name.c_str(), 0, TL_REGKEY) != 0;
    }

    void trace_link_mark_start(bool pending)
    {
        qstring name = start_mark_name();
        if ( name.empty() )
            return;
        if ( pending )
            reg_write_int(name.c_str(), 1, TL_REGKEY);
        else
            reg_delete(name.c_str(), TL_REGKEY);
    }
}
```

`src/common/trace_link.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // The record a database created from a recording keeps about that file.
    //
    // The loader runs only when the database is created; later opens go
    // straight to the plugin, so whatever it needs to reconnect the database
    // to its recording is written here.
    struct TraceLink
    {
        qstring  trace_path;            // absolute path of the recording, as it was then
        qstring  module_path;           // main module's full path on the RECORDING machine
        qstring  module_name;           // its base name, matched against module loads
        ea_t     module_base = BADADDR; // recorded load address of the main image
        uint64_t module_size = 0;
        int      bitness = 0;           // 0 unknown, 32, or 64
    };

    // True when this database was created by the trace loader.
    bool trace_link_present();
    // Read the record. False when absent or written by a newer schema.
    bool trace_link_read(TraceLink *out);
    void trace_link_write(const TraceLink &link);
    // Point the record at a different path, when the user re-locates a
    // recording that was moved or renamed.
    void trace_link_set_path(const char *path);

    // Crash guard for the automatic start.
    //
    // Set just before an automatic start and cleared once the session is up.
    // Still set at the next open means that start crashed, so the open skips
    // it; otherwise a database that takes IDA down could never be opened to
    // turn the automatic start off.
    //
    // Kept in IDA's settings, not the database, which may never have been
    // saved.
    bool trace_link_start_marked();
    void trace_link_mark_start(bool pending);
}
```

`src/common/write_scans.h`:

```h
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 OR GPL-2.0-only
//
// Dual-licensed, unlike the rest of ida-ttd: compiled into the Microsoft
// backend, which ships under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE), and into the Sogen backend,
// which is GPL-2.0-only because Sogen is (LICENSES/GPL-2.0-only.txt). Each
// takes it under its own license.
//
// The string and buffer scanners both backends feed: the Microsoft backend
// from its watchpoint replays, the Sogen backend from recorded write events.
// Implements docs/scan-rules.md and is written from that description, not
// ported from another project. The rules follow Sogen's, so a list reads the
// same whichever kind of recording it came from.
//
// Header-only and standard-library-only on purpose: the Sogen backend builds
// without the rest of the plugin.

#pragma once

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstddef>
#include <cstdint>
#include <cstring>
#include <iterator>
#include <map>
#include <set>
#include <string>
#include <tuple>
#include <vector>

namespace idattd::scans
{
    // ---- limits callers see ----------------------------------------------
    inline constexpr size_t kStringMaximum = 4096;      // longest string, in characters
    inline constexpr size_t kStringContext = 512;       // overlap callers give each window
    inline constexpr size_t kScanChunk     = 65536;     // the window callers step by
    inline constexpr size_t kMaximumRegion = 256 * 1024; // longest a region may grow

    // ---- byte tests shared by both scanners --------------------------------
    namespace detail
    {
        inline bool printable(uint8_t b)
        {
            return b >= 0x20 && b <= 0x7E;
        }

        // A UTF-16LE character of the kind both scanners accept: a printable
        // low byte and a zero high byte, both inside [0, size).
        inline bool wide_pair(const uint8_t *p, size_t size, size_t k)
        {
            return k + 1 < size && printable(p[k]) && p[k + 1] == 0;
        }

        // Whether [p, p + n) begins with the 'len' bytes of 'sig'. A prefix
        // only matches when there are at least that many bytes.
        inline bool starts_with(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, const char *sig, size_t len)
        {
            return n >= len && memcmp(p, sig, len) == 0;
        }

        inline bool contains(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, const char *needle)
        {
            const size_t len = strlen(needle);
            if ( n < len )
                return false;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i + len <= n; i++ )
                if ( memcmp(p + i, needle, len) == 0 )
                    return true;
            return false;
        }
    }

    //=======================================================================
    // Strings
    //=======================================================================
    // Every NUL-terminated ASCII or UTF-16LE string seen in the windows of
    // memory the caller offers, keyed by address. A string that grows in
    // place (written piece by piece, each window seeing more) keeps one
    // entry, ending with the longest text and the position of its last
    // extension.
    template <typename Pos>
    class StringScan
    {
    public:
        struct Entry
        {
            Pos         pos;
            bool        wide;
            std::string value;
        };

        bool truncated = false;

        StringScan(size_t minimum, size_t cap = 500000) : m_minimum(minimum), m_cap(cap) {}

        size_t minimum() const { return m_minimum; }

        // One window: 'bytes' at 'address', as memory held them at 'pos'.
        // ASCII strings go in before UTF-16 ones; the order decides which
        // entry an address's later offers land on.
        void inspect(uint64_t address, const std::vector<uint8_t> &bytes, const Pos &pos)
        {
            scan_ascii(address, bytes.data(), bytes.size(), pos);
            scan_wide(address, bytes.data(), bytes.size(), pos);
        }

        // fn(uint64_t address, const Entry &): addresses ascending, then each
        // address's entries in the order they were first added.
        template <typename Fn>
        void for_each(Fn fn) const
        {
            for ( const auto &[address, entries] : m_entries )
                for ( const Entry &e : entries )
                    fn(address, e);
        }

    private:
        size_t m_minimum;
        size_t m_cap;
        size_t m_count = 0;
        std::map<uint64_t, std::vector<Entry>> m_entries;

        // A run of printable bytes counts only when the window shows the NUL
        // after it. A run cut off by the window's end may continue, and the
        // overlapping next window sees it whole.
        void scan_ascii(uint64_t address, const uint8_t *p, size_t size, const Pos &pos)
        {
            size_t i = 0;
            while ( i < size )
            {
                if ( !detail::printable(p[i]) )
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                size_t e = i;
                while ( e < size && detail::printable(p[e]) )
                    e++;
                const size_t len = e - i;
                if ( len >= m_minimum && len <= kStringMaximum && e < size && p[e] == 0 )
                    offer(address + i, pos, false, std::string(reinterpret_cast<const char *>(p + i), len));
                i = e;
            }
        }

        // Every offset is tried, odd ones too, since a wide string need not
        // be aligned. An offset that continues the pair two bytes before it
        // is inside a string, not a start.
        void scan_wide(uint64_t address, const uint8_t *p, size_t size, const Pos &pos)
        {
            std::string text;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i + 1 < size; i++ )
            {
                if ( !detail::wide_pair(p, size, i) )
                    continue;
                if ( i >= 2 && detail::wide_pair(p, size, i - 2) )
                    continue;
                text.clear();
                size_t k = i;
                while ( text.size() < kStringMaximum && detail::wide_pair(p, size, k) )
                {
                    text.push_back(char(p[k]));
                    k += 2;
                }
                if ( text.size() >= m_minimum && k + 1 < size && p[k] == 0 && p[k + 1] == 0 )
                    offer(address + i, pos, true, text);
            }
        }

        void offer(uint64_t address, const Pos &pos, bool wide, const std::string &value)
        {
            auto it = m_entries.find(address);
            if ( it != m_entries.end() )
            {
                // The first entry of the same kind that is this text, or a
                // prefix of it, absorbs the offer.
                for ( Entry &e : it->second )
                {
                    if ( e.wide != wide )
                        continue;
                    if ( e.value == value )
                        return;
                    if ( value.size() > e.value.size() && value.compare(0, e.value.size(), e.value) == 0 )
                    {
                        e.value = value;
                        e.pos   = pos;
                        return;
                    }
                }
            }
            if ( m_count >= m_cap )
            {
                truncated = true;
                return;
            }
            // The address's slot is made only now, so a refused offer leaves
            // nothing for for_each to visit.
            if ( it == m_entries.end() )
                it = m_entries.emplace(address, std::vector<Entry>()).first;
            it->second.push_back(Entry{ pos, wide, value });
            m_count++;
        }
    };

    //=======================================================================
    // Buffers
    //=======================================================================

    template <typename Pos>
    struct FoundBuffer
    {
        uint64_t    address = 0, size = 0;
        Pos         first, last;
        uint64_t    writer_ip = 0, writes = 0;
        std::string kind, preview;
    };

    // Groups the program's writes into regions (bytes written close together
    // in space, and either touching or close together in time) and, as each
    // region is retired, classifies what it held: files, text, code that ran,
    // random-looking data, plain buffers, and the strings and embedded files
    // inside them.
    template <typename Pos>
    class BufferScan
    {
    public:
        bool truncated = false;
        std::vector<FoundBuffer<Pos>> results;

        // 'nearby' is how many clock ticks after a region's last write a
        // write just beyond it still counts as the same burst.
        explicit BufferScan(uint64_t nearby) : m_nearby(nearby) {}

        void ingest(uint64_t address, const uint8_t *bytes, size_t size, uint64_t clock, const Pos &pos, uint64_t ip)
        {
            if ( size == 0 || uint64_t(size) > UINT64_MAX - address )
                return;
            const uint64_t end = address + size;

            auto cand = candidate(address);
            if ( cand != m_regions.end() && cand->first <= end + kGap )
            {
                Region &r = cand->second;
                const uint64_t s = cand->first;
                const uint64_t t = r.end(s);
                const uint64_t lo = std::min(s, address);
                const uint64_t hi = std::max(t, end);
                // Deliberately weaker than overlapping: a write wholly
                // before the region also counts, as in Sogen.
                const bool reaches = address < t;

                if ( reaches && rewrites_executed(s, r, address, bytes, size) )
                {
                    retire(cand);
                }
                else if ( (reaches || clock - r.last_clock <= m_nearby) && hi - lo <= kMaximumRegion )
                {
                    grow(cand, lo, hi, address, bytes, size, clock, pos, ip);
                    return;
                }
                else if ( reaches )
                {
                    retire(cand);
                }
            }
            start_region(address, bytes, size, clock, pos, ip);
        }

        // [address, address + size) ran. Only bytes the program wrote count
        // as code it made, and regions starting above 'address' are not
        // touched.
        void executed(uint64_t address, size_t size)
        {
            const uint64_t end = saturating_end(address, size);
            auto it = m_regions.upper_bound(address);
            while ( it != m_regions.begin() )
            {
                --it;
                const uint64_t s = it->first;
                if ( address - s >= kMaximumRegion )
                    break;
                Region &r = it->second;
                const uint64_t t = r.end(s);
                if ( t <= address )
                    continue;
                const size_t from = size_t(address - s);
                const size_t to   = size_t(std::min(t, end) - s);
                for ( size_t k = from; k < to; k++ )
                    if ( r.known[k] )
                        r.exec[k] = 1;
            }
        }

        // Memory in [address, address + size) was mapped, unmapped or
        // remapped, so what the regions held there is gone. Each region's
        // part in the range is reported now, as it stood, then forgotten.
        void mapping_changed(uint64_t address, uint64_t size)
        {
            if ( size == 0 )
                return;
            const uint64_t end = address > UINT64_MAX - size ? UINT64_MAX : address + size;
            // A region starting more than the longest region ever held below
            // 'address' ends before it. Not kMaximumRegion: a single large
            // write starts a region longer than that.
            auto it = address > m_longest ? m_regions.lower_bound(address - m_longest) : m_regions.begin();
            for ( ; it != m_regions.end() && it->first < end; )
            {
                const uint64_t s = it->first;
                Region &r = it->second;
                const uint64_t t = r.end(s);
                if ( t <= address )
                {
                    ++it;
                    continue;
                }
                const size_t from = size_t(std::max(s, address) - s);
                const size_t to   = size_t(std::min(t, end) - s);
                emit(s, r, from, to);
                bool any = false;
                for ( size_t k = 0; k < r.bytes.size(); k++ )
                {
                    if ( k >= from && k < to )
                    {
                        r.known[k] = 0;
                        r.exec[k]  = 0;
                    }
                    any = any || r.known[k] != 0;
                }
                if ( any )
                {
                    ++it;
                }
                else
                {
                    m_order.erase(order_key(s, r));
                    it = m_regions.erase(it);
                }
            }
        }

        // The end of the recording: every region still open is reported.
        void finish()
        {
            for ( const auto &[s, r] : m_regions )
                emit(s, r, 0, r.bytes.size());
            m_regions.clear();
            m_order.clear();
        }

    private:
        static constexpr uint64_t kGap          = 16;      // how far apart writes may be and still join
        static constexpr size_t   kMaxRegions   = 16384;   // active at once
        static constexpr size_t   kSmallRegion  = 512;     // evicted before longer ones
        static constexpr size_t   kMaxResults   = 20000;
        static constexpr size_t   kMinSegment   = 16;
        static constexpr size_t   kMinText      = 32;
        static constexpr size_t   kMinEntropy   = 256;
        static constexpr size_t   kMinBuffer    = 512;
        static constexpr size_t   kMinAscii     = 16;      // printable bytes, for ascii_string
        static constexpr size_t   kMinWideBytes = 24;      // bytes of pairs, for utf16le_string
        static constexpr size_t   kMaxStrings   = 128;     // of each kind, per segment
        static constexpr size_t   kMaxEmbedded  = 64;      // per segment
        static constexpr size_t   kTextPreview  = 48;
        static constexpr size_t   kWidePreview  = 96;
        static constexpr size_t   kPemWindow    = 128;

        // A byte array that grows at both ends. A region growing downwards
        // (stack pushes, a buffer filled from its end) gains a few bytes at
        // its front at a time; a plain vector moves the whole region for each.
        // Unused room is kept before the first byte instead, so growing the
        // front is amortised constant time per byte, like growing the back.
        class Lane
        {
        public:
            size_t size() const { return m_v.size() - m_head; }
            uint8_t *data() { return m_v.data() + m_head; }
            const uint8_t *data() const { return m_v.data() + m_head; }
            uint8_t &operator[](size_t k) { return m_v[m_head + k]; }
            const uint8_t &operator[](size_t k) const { return m_v[m_head + k]; }
            typename std::vector<uint8_t>::iterator begin() { return m_v.begin() + ptrdiff_t(m_head); }
            typename std::vector<uint8_t>::const_iterator begin() const { return m_v.begin() + ptrdiff_t(m_head); }

            void assign(const uint8_t *first, const uint8_t *last) { m_v.assign(first, last); m_head = 0; }
            void assign(size_t n, uint8_t value) { m_v.assign(n, value); m_head = 0; }

            // Never shrinks below the current size: regions only grow.
            void resize(size_t n, uint8_t value) { m_v.resize(m_head + n, value); }

            // 'n' zero bytes before the first.
            void grow_front(size_t n)
            {
                if ( n <= m_head )
                {
                    m_head -= n;
                    std::fill_n(m_v.begin() + ptrdiff_t(m_head), n, uint8_t(0));
                    return;
                }
                // Room for as much again as the region will hold, capped at
                // the longest a region grows by merging.
                const size_t len   = size();
                const size_t slack = std::min(len + n, kMaximumRegion);
                std::vector<uint8_t> w(slack + n + len, 0);
                std::copy(begin(), m_v.end(), w.begin() + ptrdiff_t(slack + n));
                m_v.swap(w);
                m_head = slack;
            }

        private:
            std::vector<uint8_t> m_v;
            size_t m_head = 0;      // unused bytes before the first
        };

        // One region, stored under its start address. Per-byte flags:
        // 'known' when the program wrote it (not bytes gained by growing
        // over a gap), 'exec' when a known byte later ran.
        struct Region
        {
            Lane                 bytes, known, exec;
            Pos                  first, last;
            uint64_t             last_clock = 0;
            uint64_t             writer_ip = 0;
            uint64_t             writes = 0;

            uint64_t end(uint64_t start) const { return start + bytes.size(); }
        };
        using Regions = std::map<uint64_t, Region>;

        // Eviction order: short regions first, then the one written longest
        // ago, then the lowest start. The std::set stays sorted as regions
        // change, so finding the victim does not walk every region.
        using OrderKey = std::tuple<int, uint64_t, uint64_t>;

        uint64_t           m_nearby;
        uint64_t           m_longest = 0;     // the longest region so far, for mapping_changed
        Regions            m_regions;
        std::set<OrderKey> m_order;

        static OrderKey order_key(uint64_t start, const Region &r)
        {
            return OrderKey(r.bytes.size() < kSmallRegion ? 0 : 1, r.last_clock, start);
        }

        static uint64_t saturating_end(uint64_t address, uint64_t size)
        {
            return address > UINT64_MAX - size ? UINT64_MAX : address + size;
        }

        // The region a write at 'address' may belong to: the one starting at
        // or below it if that ends no more than kGap before it, else the
        // next one up. The caller still checks that it is close enough.
        typename Regions::iterator candidate(uint64_t address)
        {
            auto next = m_regions.upper_bound(address);
            if ( next != m_regions.begin() )
            {
                auto prev = std::prev(next);
                if ( prev->second.end(prev->first) + kGap >= address )
                    return prev;
            }
            return next;
        }

        // Whether the write puts a different value over a byte that already
        // ran (new code over old), so the old code is reported as it was.
        static bool rewrites_executed(uint64_t s, const Region &r, uint64_t address, const uint8_t *bytes, size_t size)
        {
            const uint64_t lo = std::max(s, address);
            const uint64_t hi = std::min(r.end(s), address + size);
            for ( uint64_t a = lo; a < hi; a++ )
            {
                const size_t k = size_t(a - s);
                if ( r.exec[k] && r.bytes[k] != bytes[a - address] )
                    return true;
            }
            return false;
        }

        void grow(typename Regions::iterator it, uint64_t lo, uint64_t hi, uint64_t address,
                  const uint8_t *bytes, size_t size, uint64_t clock, const Pos &pos, uint64_t ip)
        {
            const uint64_t s = it->first;
            m_order.erase(order_key(s, it->second));
            // A region growing downwards changes its key. No other region
            // can start at 'lo': it would have been the candidate.
            Region r = std::move(it->second);
            if ( lo != s )
            {
                m_regions.erase(it);
                const size_t front = size_t(s - lo);
                r.bytes.grow_front(front);
                r.known.grow_front(front);
                r.exec.grow_front(front);
            }
            const size_t length = size_t(hi - lo);
            r.bytes.resize(length, 0);
            r.known.resize(length, 0);
            r.exec.resize(length, 0);
            const size_t at = size_t(address - lo);
            memcpy(r.bytes.data() + at, bytes, size);
            std::fill_n(r.known.begin() + at, size, uint8_t(1));
            std::fill_n(r.exec.begin() + at, size, uint8_t(0));
            r.last_clock = clock;
            r.last       = pos;
            r.writer_ip  = ip;
            r.writes++;
            m_longest = std::max<uint64_t>(m_longest, length);
            m_order.insert(order_key(lo, r));
            if ( lo != s )
                m_regions.emplace(lo, std::move(r));
            else
                it->second = std::move(r);
        }

        void start_region(uint64_t address, const uint8_t *bytes, size_t size, uint64_t clock,
                          const Pos &pos, uint64_t ip)
        {
            auto old = m_regions.find(address);
            if ( old != m_regions.end() )
                retire(old);
            Region r;
            r.bytes.assign(bytes, bytes + size);
            r.known.assign(size, 1);
            r.exec.assign(size, 0);
            r.first      = pos;
            r.last       = pos;
            r.last_clock = clock;
            r.writer_ip  = ip;
            r.writes     = 1;
            m_longest = std::max<uint64_t>(m_longest, size);
            m_order.insert(order_key(address, r));
            m_regions.emplace(address, std::move(r));
            if ( m_regions.size() > kMaxRegions )
            {
                const uint64_t victim = std::get<2>(*m_order.begin());
                retire(m_regions.find(victim));
            }
        }

        // Report a region and forget it.
        void retire(typename Regions::iterator it)
        {
            emit(it->first, it->second, 0, it->second.bytes.size());
            m_order.erase(order_key(it->first, it->second));
            m_regions.erase(it);
        }

        // ---- reporting ------------------------------------------------------

        // Bytes [from, to) of the region starting at 's', one segment (run
        // of known bytes) at a time.
        void emit(uint64_t s, const Region &r, size_t from, size_t to)
        {
            size_t i = from;
            while ( i < to )
            {
                if ( !r.known[i] )
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                size_t e = i;
                while ( e < to && r.known[e] )
                    e++;
                if ( e - i >= kMinSegment )
                    emit_segment(s + i, r, i, e - i);
                i = e;
            }
        }

        void emit_segment(uint64_t address, const Region &r, size_t begin, size_t n)
        {
            const uint8_t *p = r.bytes.data() + begin;
            const bool text = is_text(p, n);

            std::string kind = signature(p, n);
            if ( kind.empty() )
            {
                if ( std::find(r.exec.begin() + begin, r.exec.begin() + begin + n, uint8_t(1))
                     != r.exec.begin() + begin + n )
                    kind = "contains_executed_code";
                else if ( text )
                    kind = "ascii_text";
                else if ( is_wide_text(p, n) )
                    kind = "utf16le_text";
                else if ( n >= kMinEntropy && entropy(p, n) >= 7.5 )
                    kind = "high_entropy_buffer";
                else if ( n >= kMinBuffer )
                    kind = "buffer";
            }
            if ( !kind.empty() )
                record(r, address, p, n, kind, text ? Preview::text : Preview::hex);

            // ASCII strings: runs of printable bytes within the segment. A
            // run that is the whole of a text segment would only repeat it.
            size_t count = 0;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < n && count < kMaxStrings; )
            {
                if ( !detail::printable(p[i]) )
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                size_t e = i;
                while ( e < n && detail::printable(p[e]) )
                    e++;
                if ( e - i >= kMinAscii && !(text && i == 0 && e == n) )
                {
                    record(r, address + i, p + i, e - i, "ascii_string", Preview::text);
                    count++;
                }
                i = e;
            }

            // UTF-16LE strings: the walk skips past each run of pairs, long
            // enough or not, so a run is only examined from its start.
            count = 0;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i + 1 < n && count < kMaxStrings; )
            {
                if ( !detail::wide_pair(p, n, i) || (i >= 2 && detail::wide_pair(p, n, i - 2)) )
                {
                    i++;
                    continue;
                }
                size_t k = i;
                while ( detail::wide_pair(p, n, k) )
                    k += 2;
                if ( k - i >= kMinWideBytes )
                {
                    record(r, address + i, p + i, k - i, "utf16le_string", Preview::wide);
                    count++;
                }
                i = k;
            }

            // Files inside the segment, past its first byte (a file at the
            // start is the segment's own kind). The first-byte test is a
            // quick filter for the signatures looked for here.
            count = 0;
            for ( size_t i = 1; i + 16 < n && count < kMaxEmbedded; i++ )
            {
                const uint8_t b = p[i];
                if ( b != 'M' && b != 0x89 && b != 'G' && b != '%' && b != 'P' && b != 'S' && b != '-' )
                    continue;
                const std::string inner = signature(p + i, n - i);
                if ( inner.empty() || inner == "bmp_image" || inner == "jpeg_image" )
                    continue;
                record(r, address + i, p + i, n - i, inner, Preview::hex);
                count++;
            }
        }

        enum class Preview { text, hex, wide };

        void record(const Region &r, uint64_t address, const uint8_t *p, size_t n,
                    const std::string &kind, Preview style)
        {
            if ( n == 0 )
                return;
            if ( results.size() >= kMaxResults )
            {
                truncated = true;
                return;
            }
            FoundBuffer<Pos> f;
            f.address   = address;
            f.size      = n;
            f.first     = r.first;
            f.last      = r.last;
            f.writer_ip = r.writer_ip;
            f.writes    = r.writes;
            f.kind      = kind;
            f.preview   = preview(p, n, style);
            results.push_back(std::move(f));
        }

        static std::string preview(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, Preview style)
        {
            std::string out;
            if ( style == Preview::wide )
            {
                // The characters' low bytes, as they are.
                const size_t limit = std::min(n, kWidePreview);
                for ( size_t k = 0; k + 1 < limit; k += 2 )
                    out.push_back(char(p[k]));
                return out;
            }
            const size_t limit = std::min(n, kTextPreview);
            static const char hex[] = "0123456789abcdef";
            for ( size_t k = 0; k < limit; k++ )
            {
                if ( style == Preview::text )
                {
                    out.push_back(detail::printable(p[k]) ? char(p[k]) : '.');
                }
                else
                {
                    out.push_back(hex[p[k] >> 4]);
                    out.push_back(hex[p[k] & 0xF]);
                }
            }
            return out;
        }

        // ---- classification ---------------------------------------------------
        // The percentage tests use integers so boundary cases come out the
        // same on every compiler.

        static bool is_text(const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
        {
            if ( n < kMinText )
                return false;
            const size_t printable = size_t(std::count_if(p, p + n, detail::printable));
            return printable * 100 >= n * 90;
        }

        // Pairs are counted at even offsets only, as in aligned UTF-16 text.
        static bool is_wide_text(const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
        {
            if ( n < kMinText )
                return false;
            size_t pairs = 0;
            for ( size_t k = 0; k + 1 < n; k += 2 )
                if ( detail::wide_pair(p, n, k) )
                    pairs++;
            return pairs * 100 >= (n / 2) * 85;
        }

        // Shannon entropy in bits per byte.
        static double entropy(const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
        {
            size_t counts[256] = {};
            for ( size_t k = 0; k < n; k++ )
                counts[p[k]]++;
            double h = 0.0;
            for ( size_t c : counts )
            {
                if ( c == 0 )
                    continue;
                const double q = double(c) / double(n);
                h -= q * std::log2(q);
            }
            return h;
        }

        // The kind of file [p, p + n) begins with; empty when none.
        static std::string signature(const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
        {
            if ( n >= 64 && p[0] == 'M' && p[1] == 'Z' )
            {
                // The PE header the DOS header points at must lie inside.
                const uint32_t e = uint32_t(p[0x3C]) | uint32_t(p[0x3D]) << 8
                                 | uint32_t(p[0x3E]) << 16 | uint32_t(p[0x3F]) << 24;
                if ( e <= n - 4 && memcmp(p + e, "PE\0\0", 4) == 0 )
                    return "pe_image";
            }
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "\x7F" "ELF", 4) )
                return "elf_image";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "\x89" "PNG\r\n\x1A\n", 8) )
                return "png_image";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "\xFF\xD8\xFF", 3) )
                return "jpeg_image";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "GIF8", 4) )
                return "gif_image";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "BM", 2) )
                return "bmp_image";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "%PDF-", 5) )
                return "pdf_document";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "PK\x03\x04", 4) )
                return "zip_archive";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "\x1F\x8B\x08", 3) )
                return "gzip_stream";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "SQLite format 3\0", 16) )
                return "sqlite_database";
            if ( detail::starts_with(p, n, "-----BEGIN ", 11) )
            {
                const size_t window = std::min(n, kPemWindow);
                if ( detail::contains(p, window, "PRIVATE KEY-----") )
                    return "pem_private_key";
                if ( detail::contains(p, window, "PUBLIC KEY-----") )
                    return "pem_public_key";
            }
            return std::string();
        }
    };
}

```

`src/core/abi_convert.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

#include <cstddef>
#include <cstring>

// The conversions between the core's types (core/backend.h) and the C ABI's
// (abi/ida_ttd_backend.h), each written once and used by both sides of the
// boundary: abi_export.cpp turns a C++ backend's answers into ABI structs
// (to_abi), and backend_module.cpp turns a DLL's ABI structs back into core
// types (from_abi). A field added to one direction is then next to its
// partner, rather than in another file.
//
// Where the two directions are not mirror images (a clamp, a default, a
// field one side fills and the other ignores) the difference is the
// historical behavior of that side, kept on purpose and said at the pair.
//
// Header-only and free of ida.lib calls beyond what qstring needs: the MS
// backend, which does not link ida.lib, includes it through abi_export.cpp.

namespace idattd
{
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- strings

    // Into a fixed-size ABI field, cut to fit and always terminated. Not
    // qstrncpy: this is built into a backend that does not link ida.dll.
    inline void copy_str(char *dst, size_t cap, const char *src)
    {
        if ( cap == 0 )
            return;
        size_t n = src != nullptr ? strlen(src) : 0;
        if ( n >= cap )
            n = cap - 1;
        if ( n != 0 )
            memcpy(dst, src, n);
        dst[n] = '\0';
    }

    template <size_t N>
    inline void copy_str(char (&dst)[N], const qstring &src)
    {
        copy_str(dst, N, src.c_str());
    }

    // A fixed-size string field of an ABI struct, read without trusting the
    // NUL: a backend that filled it to the brim must not make the core read
    // past the struct.
    template <size_t N>
    inline qstring fixed_str(const char (&s)[N])
    {
        return qstring(s, strnlen(s, N));
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- positions

    // The core's Position and the ABI's ittd_position are the same two words
    // with the same three sentinels, so the conversion is a copy.
    inline ittd_position to_abi(Position p) { return ittd_position{ p.hi, p.lo }; }
    inline Position from_abi(ittd_position p) { return Position{ p.hi, p.lo }; }

    inline ittd_position_range to_abi(PositionRange r)
    {
        return ittd_position_range{ to_abi(r.first), to_abi(r.last) };
    }
    inline PositionRange from_abi(ittd_position_range r)
    {
        return PositionRange{ from_abi(r.first), from_abi(r.last) };
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- address ranges

    inline ittd_range to_abi(const std::pair<ea_t, ea_t> &r)
    {
        return ittd_range{ (uint64_t)r.first, (uint64_t)r.second };
    }
    inline std::pair<ea_t, ea_t> from_abi(const ittd_range &r)
    {
        return { (ea_t)r.start, (ea_t)r.end };
    }

    inline std::vector<ittd_range> to_abi(const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &ranges)
    {
        std::vector<ittd_range> r;
        r.reserve(ranges.size());
        for ( const auto &p : ranges )
            r.push_back(to_abi(p));
        return r;
    }
    inline std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> from_abi(const ittd_range *ranges, size_t n)
    {
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> r;
        r.reserve(n);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < n; i++ )
            r.push_back(from_abi(ranges[i]));
        return r;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- access kinds

    // A set of AccessKind bits as ITTD_ACCESS_* bits, and back.
    inline uint32_t to_abi_kinds(uint8_t kinds)
    {
        return ((kinds & ACCESS_READ)  ? ITTD_ACCESS_READ  : 0)
             | ((kinds & ACCESS_WRITE) ? ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE : 0)
             | ((kinds & ACCESS_EXEC)  ? ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC  : 0);
    }
    inline uint8_t from_abi_kinds(uint32_t k)
    {
        return (uint8_t)(((k & ITTD_ACCESS_READ)  ? ACCESS_READ  : 0)
                       | ((k & ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE) ? ACCESS_WRITE : 0)
                       | ((k & ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC)  ? ACCESS_EXEC  : 0));
    }

    // One access's kind: a single value each way. Not mirror images: going
    // out, a core kind with several bits set gives the first of read, write,
    // execute (and none gives execute); coming in, anything but exactly
    // read or write is execute.
    inline uint32_t to_abi_kind(uint8_t k)
    {
        return (k & ACCESS_READ) ? ITTD_ACCESS_READ : (k & ACCESS_WRITE) ? ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE : ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC;
    }
    inline uint8_t from_abi_kind(uint32_t k)
    {
        return k == ITTD_ACCESS_READ  ? ACCESS_READ
             : k == ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE ? ACCESS_WRITE : ACCESS_EXEC;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- stop reasons

    inline int to_abi(StopReason r)
    {
        switch ( r )
        {
            case StopReason::Stepped:       return ITTD_STOP_STEPPED;
            case StopReason::Breakpoint:    return ITTD_STOP_BREAKPOINT;
            case StopReason::TraceBoundary: return ITTD_STOP_BOUNDARY;
            default:                        return ITTD_STOP_FAILED;
        }
    }
    inline StopReason stop_from_abi(int stop)
    {
        switch ( stop )
        {
            case ITTD_STOP_STEPPED:    return StopReason::Stepped;
            case ITTD_STOP_BREAKPOINT: return StopReason::Breakpoint;
            case ITTD_STOP_BOUNDARY:   return StopReason::TraceBoundary;
            default:                   return StopReason::Failed;
        }
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- trace info

    // The capability bits are converted on their own: ITTD_CAP_PREPARE comes
    // from prepared(), not from Capabilities, and the core also requires the
    // table entries some bits promise (backend_module.cpp).
    inline uint32_t to_abi(const Capabilities &c)
    {
        uint32_t caps = 0;
        if ( c.access_queries )   caps |= ITTD_CAP_ACCESS_QUERIES;
        if ( c.call_queries )     caps |= ITTD_CAP_CALL_QUERIES;
        if ( c.mapping_changes )  caps |= ITTD_CAP_MAPPING_CHANGES;
        if ( c.syscalls )         caps |= ITTD_CAP_SYSCALLS;
        if ( c.recorded_exports ) caps |= ITTD_CAP_RECORDED_EXPORTS;
        if ( c.batch_regs )       caps |= ITTD_CAP_BATCH_REGS;
        if ( c.reverse_step )     caps |= ITTD_CAP_REVERSE_STEP;
        if ( c.exceptions )       caps |= ITTD_CAP_EXCEPTIONS;
        if ( c.self_modifying )   caps |= ITTD_CAP_SELF_MODIFYING;
        if ( c.fork )             caps |= ITTD_CAP_FORK;
        if ( c.replay_scans )     caps |= ITTD_CAP_REPLAY_SCANS;
        if ( c.cheap_reads )      caps |= ITTD_CAP_CHEAP_READS;
        return caps;
    }
    inline Capabilities caps_from_abi(uint32_t c)
    {
        Capabilities x;
        x.access_queries   = (c & ITTD_CAP_ACCESS_QUERIES) != 0;
        x.call_queries     = (c & ITTD_CAP_CALL_QUERIES) != 0;
        x.mapping_changes  = (c & ITTD_CAP_MAPPING_CHANGES) != 0;
        x.syscalls         = (c & ITTD_CAP_SYSCALLS) != 0;
        x.recorded_exports = (c & ITTD_CAP_RECORDED_EXPORTS) != 0;
        x.batch_regs       = (c & ITTD_CAP_BATCH_REGS) != 0;
        x.reverse_step     = (c & ITTD_CAP_REVERSE_STEP) != 0;
        x.exceptions       = (c & ITTD_CAP_EXCEPTIONS) != 0;
        x.self_modifying   = (c & ITTD_CAP_SELF_MODIFYING) != 0;
        x.fork             = (c & ITTD_CAP_FORK) != 0;
        x.replay_scans     = (c & ITTD_CAP_REPLAY_SCANS) != 0;
        x.cheap_reads      = (c & ITTD_CAP_CHEAP_READS) != 0;
        return x;
    }

    // Everything but 'capabilities', which the caller fills (above).
    inline ittd_trace_info to_abi(const TraceInfo &ti)
    {
        ittd_trace_info x{};
        x.is64        = ti.is64 ? 1 : 0;
        x.fingerprint = ti.fingerprint;
        x.first       = to_abi(ti.first);
        x.last        = to_abi(ti.last);
        copy_str(x.main_module, ti.main_module);
        copy_str(x.backend_name, ti.backend_name);
        return x;
    }
    inline TraceInfo from_abi(const ittd_trace_info &x)
    {
        TraceInfo ti;
        ti.is64         = x.is64 != 0;
        ti.fingerprint  = x.fingerprint;
        ti.first        = from_abi(x.first);
        ti.last         = from_abi(x.last);
        ti.main_module  = fixed_str(x.main_module);
        ti.backend_name = fixed_str(x.backend_name);
        return ti;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- modules, threads, timeline

    inline ittd_module to_abi(const ModuleInfo &m)
    {
        ittd_module x{};
        x.base      = (uint64_t)m.base;
        x.size      = m.size;
        x.loaded    = to_abi(m.loaded);
        x.unloaded  = to_abi(m.unloaded);
        x.machine   = m.machine;
        x.timestamp = m.timestamp;
        x.checksum  = m.checksum;
        copy_str(x.name, m.name);
        copy_str(x.path, m.path);
        return x;
    }
    // The ABI's machine is 32 bits wide; the core keeps the PE header's 16.
    inline ModuleInfo from_abi(const ittd_module &m)
    {
        ModuleInfo mi;
        mi.base      = (ea_t)m.base;
        mi.size      = m.size;
        mi.name      = fixed_str(m.name);
        mi.path      = fixed_str(m.path);
        mi.loaded    = from_abi(m.loaded);
        mi.unloaded  = from_abi(m.unloaded);
        mi.machine   = (uint16_t)m.machine;
        mi.timestamp = m.timestamp;
        mi.checksum  = m.checksum;
        return mi;
    }

    inline ittd_thread to_abi(const ThreadInfo &t)
    {
        ittd_thread x{};
        x.tid         = t.tid;
        x.created     = to_abi(t.created);
        x.exited      = to_abi(t.exited);
        x.teb         = (uint64_t)t.teb;
        x.teb32       = (uint64_t)t.teb32;
        x.stack_base  = (uint64_t)t.stack_base;
        x.stack_limit = (uint64_t)t.stack_limit;
        copy_str(x.name, t.name);
        return x;
    }
    inline ThreadInfo from_abi(const ittd_thread &t)
    {
        ThreadInfo ti;
        ti.tid         = t.tid;
        ti.created     = from_abi(t.created);
        ti.exited      = from_abi(t.exited);
        ti.name        = fixed_str(t.name);
        ti.teb         = (ea_t)t.teb;
        ti.teb32       = (ea_t)t.teb32;
        ti.stack_base  = (ea_t)t.stack_base;
        ti.stack_limit = (ea_t)t.stack_limit;
        return ti;
    }

    inline ittd_trace_event to_abi(const TraceEvent &e)
    {
        ittd_trace_event x{};
        x.pos  = to_abi(e.pos);
        x.kind = e.kind;
        x.tid  = e.tid;
        copy_str(x.text, e.what);
        return x;
    }
    inline TraceEvent from_abi(const ittd_trace_event &e)
    {
        TraceEvent te;
        te.pos  = from_abi(e.pos);
        te.what = fixed_str(e.text);
        te.kind = e.kind;
        te.tid  = e.tid;
        return te;
    }

    inline ittd_symbol to_abi(const ITraceBackend::Symbol &s)
    {
        ittd_symbol x{};
        x.ea        = (uint64_t)s.ea;
        x.is_export = s.is_export ? 1 : 0;
        copy_str(x.name, s.name);
        return x;
    }
    inline ITraceBackend::Symbol from_abi(const ittd_symbol &s)
    {
        ITraceBackend::Symbol sym;
        sym.ea        = (ea_t)s.ea;
        sym.name      = fixed_str(s.name);
        sym.is_export = s.is_export != 0;
        return sym;
    }

    inline ittd_name to_abi_name(const qstring &s)
    {
        ittd_name n{};
        copy_str(n.name, s);
        return n;
    }
    inline qstring from_abi(const ittd_name &n)
    {
        return fixed_str(n.name);
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- breakpoints

    // Both directions read a size of 0 as 1.
    inline ittd_breakpoint to_abi(const Breakpoint &b)
    {
        ittd_breakpoint x{};
        x.addr  = (uint64_t)b.addr;
        x.size  = b.size == 0 ? 1 : b.size;
        x.kinds = to_abi_kinds(b.kinds);
        return x;
    }
    inline Breakpoint from_abi(const ittd_breakpoint &x)
    {
        Breakpoint b;
        b.addr  = (ea_t)x.addr;
        b.size  = x.size == 0 ? 1 : x.size;
        b.kinds = from_abi_kinds(x.kinds);
        return b;
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------- query answers

    // BADADDR becomes ITTD_BADADDR going out; coming in the two addresses are
    // plain casts (the same value where ea_t is 64 bits). The kind is one
    // value each way (to_abi_kind, from_abi_kind).
    inline ittd_access to_abi(const Access &a)
    {
        ittd_access x{};
        x.pos  = to_abi(a.pos);
        x.pc   = a.pc == BADADDR ? ITTD_BADADDR : (uint64_t)a.pc;
        x.addr = a.addr == BADADDR ? ITTD_BADADDR : (uint64_t)a.addr;
        x.size = a.size;
        x.kind = to_abi_kind(a.kind);
        x.tid  = a.tid;
        return x;
    }
    inline Access from_abi(const ittd_access &a)
    {
        Access x;
        x.pos  = from_abi(a.pos);
        x.tid  = a.tid;
        x.pc   = (ea_t)a.pc;
        x.addr = (ea_t)a.addr;
        x.size = a.size;
        x.kind = from_abi_kind(a.kind);
        return x;
    }

    // The site maps BADADDR both ways; the target is a plain cast both ways.
    inline ittd_call to_abi(const CallEvent &e)
    {
        ittd_call x{};
        x.pos       = to_abi(e.pos);
        x.entry_pos = to_abi(e.entry_pos);
        x.ret_pos   = to_abi(e.ret_pos);
        x.site      = e.site == BADADDR ? ITTD_BADADDR : (uint64_t)e.site;
        x.target    = (uint64_t)e.target;
        x.tid       = e.tid;
        x.flags     = e.is_call ? 0 : ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL;
        return x;
    }
    inline CallEvent from_abi(const ittd_call &c)
    {
        CallEvent e;
        e.pos       = from_abi(c.pos);
        e.entry_pos = from_abi(c.entry_pos);
        e.ret_pos   = from_abi(c.ret_pos);
        e.tid       = c.tid;
        e.site      = c.site == ITTD_BADADDR ? BADADDR : (ea_t)c.site;
        e.target    = (ea_t)c.target;
        e.is_call   = (c.flags & ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL) == 0;
        return e;
    }

    // The core keeps targets grouped by site, so the site travels beside the
    // IndirectTarget rather than in it.
    inline ittd_call_target to_abi(ea_t site, const IndirectTarget &t)
    {
        ittd_call_target x{};
        x.site      = (uint64_t)site;
        x.target    = (uint64_t)t.target;
        x.hits      = t.hits;
        x.first_pos = to_abi(t.first);
        x.flags     = t.is_call ? 0 : ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL;
        return x;
    }
    inline IndirectTarget from_abi(const ittd_call_target &c)
    {
        IndirectTarget t;
        t.target  = (ea_t)c.target;
        t.hits    = c.hits;
        t.first   = from_abi(c.first_pos);
        t.is_call = (c.flags & ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL) == 0;
        return t;
    }

    inline ittd_exception to_abi(const ExceptionEvent &e)
    {
        ittd_exception x{};
        x.pos            = to_abi(e.pos);
        x.raise_pos      = to_abi(e.raise_pos);
        x.address        = (uint64_t)e.address;
        x.information[0] = e.information[0];
        x.information[1] = e.information[1];
        x.code           = e.code;
        x.flags          = e.flags;
        x.tid            = e.tid;
        return x;
    }
    inline ExceptionEvent from_abi(const ittd_exception &x)
    {
        ExceptionEvent e;
        e.pos            = from_abi(x.pos);
        e.raise_pos      = from_abi(x.raise_pos);
        e.tid            = x.tid;
        e.code           = x.code;
        e.flags          = x.flags;
        e.address        = (ea_t)x.address;
        e.information[0] = x.information[0];
        e.information[1] = x.information[1];
        return e;
    }

    inline ittd_syscall to_abi(const SyscallEvent &e)
    {
        ittd_syscall x{};
        x.pos    = to_abi(e.pos);
        x.result = e.result;
        x.number = e.number;
        x.tid    = e.tid;
        copy_str(x.name, e.name);
        return x;
    }
    inline SyscallEvent from_abi(const ittd_syscall &x)
    {
        SyscallEvent e;
        e.pos    = from_abi(x.pos);
        e.result = x.result;
        e.number = x.number;
        e.tid    = x.tid;
        e.name   = fixed_str(x.name);
        return e;
    }

    inline ittd_string_hit to_abi(const StringHit &e)
    {
        ittd_string_hit x{};
        x.address = (uint64_t)e.address;
        x.pos     = to_abi(e.pos);
        x.wide    = e.wide ? 1 : 0;
        x.length  = e.length;
        copy_str(x.text, e.text);
        return x;
    }
    inline StringHit from_abi(const ittd_string_hit &x)
    {
        StringHit h;
        h.address = (ea_t)x.address;
        h.pos     = from_abi(x.pos);
        h.wide    = x.wide != 0;
        h.length  = x.length;
        h.text    = fixed_str(x.text);
        return h;
    }

    inline ittd_buffer_hit to_abi(const BufferHit &e)
    {
        ittd_buffer_hit x{};
        x.address   = (uint64_t)e.address;
        x.size      = e.size;
        x.first_pos = to_abi(e.first_pos);
        x.last_pos  = to_abi(e.last_pos);
        x.writer_ip = (uint64_t)e.writer_ip;
        x.writes    = e.writes;
        copy_str(x.kind, e.kind);
        copy_str(x.preview, e.preview);
        return x;
    }
    inline BufferHit from_abi(const ittd_buffer_hit &x)
    {
        BufferHit h;
        h.address   = (ea_t)x.address;
        h.size      = x.size;
        h.first_pos = from_abi(x.first_pos);
        h.last_pos  = from_abi(x.last_pos);
        h.writer_ip = (ea_t)x.writer_ip;
        h.writes    = x.writes;
        h.kind      = fixed_str(x.kind);
        h.preview   = fixed_str(x.preview);
        return h;
    }

    inline ittd_selfmod to_abi(const SelfModHit &e)
    {
        ittd_selfmod x{};
        x.address     = (uint64_t)e.address;
        x.size        = e.size;
        x.write_pos   = to_abi(e.write_pos);
        x.write_ip    = (uint64_t)e.write_ip;
        x.execute_pos = to_abi(e.execute_pos);
        x.executions  = e.executions;
        return x;
    }
    inline SelfModHit from_abi(const ittd_selfmod &x)
    {
        SelfModHit h;
        h.address     = (ea_t)x.address;
        h.size        = x.size;
        h.write_pos   = from_abi(x.write_pos);
        h.write_ip    = (ea_t)x.write_ip;
        h.execute_pos = from_abi(x.execute_pos);
        h.executions  = x.executions;
        return h;
```
