`src/core/backend_module.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A backend DLL, seen through the C++ interface the core uses.
    //
    // A pure translation between the C ABI (abi/ida_ttd_backend.h) and
    // ITraceBackend that adds no behavior: an entry the table leaves NULL
    // becomes a query that did not run, a navigation that Failed, or an empty
    // list.
    //
    // The DLL stays loaded for the life of the process: the table is static
    // and the core keeps the pointer, and unloading from a static destructor
    // would run under the loader lock.
    class BackendModule : public ITraceBackend
    {
    public:
        // Wraps 'api', which the module at 'path' returned for this core's
        // ABI version.
        BackendModule(const ittd_backend_api *api, const qstring &path);
        ~BackendModule() override;

        const char *id() const override;
        const char *display_name() const override;
        bool        can_open(const char *path) const override;
        const char *file_filter() const override;
        // The same module's table: every open() of it is a separate backend.
        std::unique_ptr<ITraceBackend> new_instance() const override
        { return std::make_unique<BackendModule>(m_api, m_path); }

        bool open(const char *path, qstring *errbuf) override;
        void close() override;
        bool is_open() const override { return m_handle != nullptr; }
        const TraceInfo    &info() const override { return m_info; }
        const Capabilities &capabilities() const override { return m_caps; }
        bool prepare(ProgressSink *progress) override;
        bool prepared() const override;

        qstring     format_position(Position p) const override;
        bool        parse_position(const char *text, Position *out) const override;
        const char *position_syntax() const override;

        CursorPtr make_cursor() override;
        std::unique_ptr<INavigator> make_navigator(ITraceCursor *cursor) override;

        std::vector<ModuleInfo> modules() const override;
        std::vector<ThreadInfo> threads() const override;
        std::vector<TraceEvent> timeline() const override;

        QueryResult query_accesses(ea_t lo, ea_t hi, uint8_t kinds, PositionRange when,
                                   std::vector<Access> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_executed(const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &ranges,
                                   std::vector<ea_t> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_calls(const std::vector<ea_t> &targets, PositionRange when,
                                std::vector<CallEvent> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_indirect_targets(const std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &ranges,
                                           bool jumps,
                                           std::map<ea_t, std::vector<IndirectTarget>> *out,
                                           ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_exceptions(std::vector<ExceptionEvent> *out,
                                     ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_syscalls(std::vector<SyscallEvent> *out,
                                   ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_self_modifying(std::vector<SelfModHit> *out,
                                         ProgressSink *progress) override;
        ForkResult  record_fork(const ForkRequest &req, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        bool        can_record() const override;
        ForkResult  record_program(const RecordRequest &req, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_strings(const ReplaySettings &settings, uint32_t min_length,
                                  std::vector<StringHit> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_buffers(const ReplaySettings &settings,
                                  std::vector<BufferHit> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult query_mapping_changes(std::vector<ittd_mapping_change> *out,
                                          std::vector<qstring> *files,
                                          ProgressSink *progress) override;
        Position position_add(Position p, int64_t delta) const override;
        QueryResult query_access_heat(uint32_t page_shift, uint32_t slices,
                                      std::vector<HeatCell> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        Position heat_slice_position(uint32_t slices, uint32_t slice) override;
        QueryResult query_access_heat_window(uint32_t page_shift, uint32_t slices, PositionRange when,
                                             std::vector<HeatCell> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        Position heat_window_slice_position(uint32_t slices, uint32_t slice, PositionRange when) override;
        bool can_window_heat() const override;
        bool query_out_values(const std::vector<OutSlot> &slots,
                              std::vector<std::optional<uint64_t>> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        bool query_register_change(Position at, uint32_t tid, uint32_t reg, uint64_t max_back,
                                   Position *where, bool *found, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        bool query_frame_entry(Position at, uint32_t tid, uint64_t max_back,
                               Position *call_pos, ea_t *entry, ProgressSink *progress = nullptr) override;
        QueryResult query_instructions(PositionRange when, uint32_t tid, size_t max,
                                       std::vector<Access> *out, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult registers_at(const std::vector<Position> &positions,
                                 std::vector<ittd_regs> *out,
                                 ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult visit_positions(const std::vector<Position> &at, const std::vector<Position> *after,
                                    const VisitFn &fn, ProgressSink *progress) override;
        QueryResult read_memory_at(const std::vector<MemAt> &reads, std::vector<uint8_t> *data,
                                   std::vector<uint8_t> *known, ProgressSink *progress) override;

        std::vector<Symbol> module_symbols(ea_t base) override;
        std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> module_functions(ea_t base) override;

        // The file the module was loaded from, for messages.
        const qstring &path() const { return m_path; }
        // The backend's own reason for its last failure on the open trace.
        qstring last_error() const override;
        ReplayBlock last_replay_block() const override { return m_replayBlock; }
        bool replay_env(ReplayEnv *out) override;
        HiveCheck check_registry(const char *dir, qstring *why) override;
        qstring scan_notice() const override;

    private:
        // Keeps what a replay call's status code says the user can fix.
        int note_replay(int rc);

        const ittd_backend_api *m_api = nullptr;
        qstring       m_path;
        ittd_backend *m_handle = nullptr;
        bool          m_prepared = false;
        // The open recording's info set ITTD_CAP_PREPARE and the table has
        // prepare(): only then is prepare() called.
        bool          m_needs_prepare = false;
        TraceInfo     m_info;
        Capabilities  m_caps;
        ReplayBlock   m_replayBlock = ReplayBlock::None;
    };

    // $IDAUSR\ida-ttd, or a folder in it when 'sub' is given: where files the
    // user adds after installing live (the TTD runtime in windbg\, the Sogen
    // backend in backends\, registry hives in registry\). Not in
    // plugins\ida-ttd\, which HCLI replaces on every upgrade, and not under
    // plugins\ at all, since none of it is a plugin.
    qstring user_data_dir(const char *sub = nullptr);

    // Load every backend DLL in $IDAUSR\ida-ttd\backends, then in the user's
    // and the installation's plugins\ida-ttd-backends and
    // plugins\ida-ttd\ida-ttd-backends, and add those that speak this core's
    // ABI version to BackendRegistry. A module that fails to load or speaks
    // another version is named in the output window and skipped. Later calls
    // load nothing more.
    //
    // A backend DLL is loaded once per process and its table is shared by
    // every IDA module that loads it (ida-ttd.dll and ttd-loader.dll), so its
    // log callback is whichever was set last. With 'install_log' (the
    // plugin), every call points every registered module's log at this
    // binary again, so a callback a since-unloaded binary left behind is
    // replaced. The loader passes false and uses attach_backend_log /
    // detach_backend_log around the work it does.
    void load_backend_modules(bool install_log = true);
    // Point every registered module's log at this binary. With
    // 'post_requests' false, lines logged from other threads are only queued,
    // never handed to IDA as a UI request, so nothing of this binary can run
    // after it is unloaded; they are printed by flush_backend_log and by
    // detach_backend_log.
    void attach_backend_log(bool post_requests);
    // Clear every registered module's log callback and print what is queued.
    // Call on the main thread, after the backends' work has finished.
    void detach_backend_log();
    // detach_backend_log for this binary's unloading (the plugin's term), and
    // stop posting requests: if one is still in IDA's queue, which cannot be
    // withdrawn, this binary is pinned in memory so the request does not run
    // unmapped code.
    void backend_log_unloading();
    // Print what backends logged from other threads, when called on the main
    // thread (run_query's wait loop calls it).
    void flush_backend_log();
    // The emulator log's (RecordOptions::log) last 'n' lines, oldest first,
    // into 'out' (NULL: none). Returns how many lines have been logged so
    // far, so a caller can tell whether anything new came. Any thread.
    uint64_t emulator_log_tail(size_t n, qstrvec_t *out);
    // The lines logged since emulator_log_tail or emulator_log_since
    // returned 'seq' (as many as are still kept), oldest first. Returns the
    // count to pass next time. Any thread.
    uint64_t emulator_log_since(uint64_t seq, qstrvec_t *out);
    // Forget the last lines, before work whose own lines are to be shown.
    void clear_emulator_log_tail();
}
```

`src/core/backend_registry.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/backend_registry.h"

namespace idattd
{
    BackendRegistry &BackendRegistry::instance()
    {
        // A function-local static, not a file-scope object: the registrations
        // run during static initialization and would otherwise race the
        // registry's own construction across translation units.
        static BackendRegistry reg;
        return reg;
    }

    void BackendRegistry::add(Factory f)
    {
        if ( f != nullptr )
        {
            m_factories.push_back(f);
            m_dirty = true;
        }
    }

    void BackendRegistry::add_backend(BackendPtr b)
    {
        if ( b )
        {
            m_loaded.push_back(std::move(b));
            m_dirty = true;
        }
    }

    const std::vector<ITraceBackend *> &BackendRegistry::all()
    {
        if ( !m_dirty )
            return m_all;
        // Run any factory not yet run, then list everything, compiled-in
        // backends first so they win the can_open() tie-break. The two
        // vectors own the backends; this list only orders them.
        for ( size_t i = m_compiled.size(); i < m_factories.size(); i++ )
            m_compiled.push_back(m_factories[i]());
        m_all.clear();
        for ( const BackendPtr &b : m_compiled )
            if ( b )
                m_all.push_back(b.get());
        for ( const BackendPtr &b : m_loaded )
            m_all.push_back(b.get());
        m_dirty = false;
        return m_all;
    }

    ITraceBackend *BackendRegistry::for_file(const char *path)
    {
        if ( path == nullptr || path[0] == '\0' )
            return nullptr;
        for ( ITraceBackend *b : all() )
            if ( b->can_open(path) )
                return b;
        return nullptr;
    }

    ITraceBackend *BackendRegistry::by_id(const char *id)
    {
        if ( id == nullptr )
            return nullptr;
        for ( ITraceBackend *b : all() )
            if ( qstrcmp(b->id(), id) == 0 )
                return b;
        return nullptr;
    }

    qstring BackendRegistry::file_filters()
    {
        qstring out;
        for ( ITraceBackend *b : all() )
        {
            const char *f = b->file_filter();
            if ( f == nullptr || f[0] == '\0' )
                continue;
            if ( !out.empty() )
                out.append('|');
            out.append(f);
        }
        return out;
    }
}
```

`src/core/backend_registry.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Which backends are available, and which one a file belongs to.
    //
    // Backends are separate DLLs the core loads at startup from its backend
    // directories (docs/modular-backends.md). Installing one is dropping a
    // file in, and each backend keeps its third-party dependencies and its
    // license to itself.
    //
    // add() is for a backend compiled into the core (none is today), such as
    // a test double.
    class BackendRegistry
    {
    public:
        static BackendRegistry &instance();

        using Factory = BackendPtr (*)();
        void add(Factory f);
        // A backend that already exists: one loaded from a DLL
        // (core/backend_module.h). Kept in the order added, after every
        // compiled-in one.
        void add_backend(BackendPtr b);

        // One instance of every registered backend, created on first use and
        // kept: can_open() and the identity accessors are valid before anything
        // is opened, and the chosen one then has open() called on it.
        const std::vector<ITraceBackend *> &all();

        // The first registered backend that says it handles 'path', or nullptr.
        // Registration order breaks ties, so can_open() should look at the
        // file, not only its extension.
        ITraceBackend *for_file(const char *path);
        ITraceBackend *by_id(const char *id);

        // The File > Open filter, with one entry per backend.
        qstring file_filters();

    private:
        std::vector<Factory>         m_factories;
        std::vector<BackendPtr>      m_compiled;   // owners, one per factory run
        std::vector<BackendPtr>      m_loaded;     // owners, from add_backend()
        std::vector<ITraceBackend *> m_all;        // both, compiled-in first
        bool                         m_dirty = true;
    };

    // Helper for the macro below.
    struct BackendRegistration
    {
        explicit BackendRegistration(BackendRegistry::Factory f)
        { BackendRegistry::instance().add(f); }
    };
}

// Put one of these at file scope in a backend's implementation:
//
//     REGISTER_TTD_BACKEND(MyTestBackend);
//
// 'type' must be default-constructible and derive from ITraceBackend. The
// object is created when the registry is first asked for its backends, not
// here, so a constructor may do real work.
#define REGISTER_TTD_BACKEND(type)                                            \
    namespace                                                                 \
    {                                                                         \
        ::idattd::BackendPtr make_##type() { return std::make_unique<type>(); } \
        const ::idattd::BackendRegistration register_##type{ &make_##type };  \
    }

```

`src/core/diag.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/diag.h"

#include <cstdio>

namespace idattd
{
    static std::mutex g_mtx;
    static std::atomic<bool> g_enabled{ true };

    void diag_set_enabled(bool on)
    {
        g_enabled.store(on);
    }

    static std::wstring log_path(const wchar_t *name)
    {
        wchar_t dir[MAX_PATH] = { 0 };
        DWORD n = GetTempPathW(MAX_PATH, dir);
        if ( n == 0 || n >= MAX_PATH )
            return std::wstring();
        return std::wstring(dir) + name;
    }

    void diag_rotate()
    {
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_mtx);
        std::wstring cur = log_path(L"ida-ttd-diag.log");
        std::wstring old = log_path(L"ida-ttd-diag.prev.log");
        if ( cur.empty() )
            return;
        DeleteFileW(old.c_str());
        MoveFileW(cur.c_str(), old.c_str());
    }

    void diag(const char *fmt, ...)
    {
        if ( !g_enabled.load() )
            return;
        char line[2048];
        va_list va;
        va_start(va, fmt);
        vsnprintf(line, sizeof(line), fmt, va);
        va_end(va);

        SYSTEMTIME st;
        GetLocalTime(&st);
        std::lock_guard<std::mutex> lock(g_mtx);
        std::wstring path = log_path(L"ida-ttd-diag.log");
        FILE *f = path.empty() ? nullptr : _wfopen(path.c_str(), L"a");
        if ( f == nullptr )
            return;
        fprintf(f, "%02u:%02u:%02u.%03u [%5lu] %s\n", st.wHour, st.wMinute, st.wSecond,
                st.wMilliseconds, GetCurrentThreadId(), line);
        fclose(f);
    }

    DiagTimer::DiagTimer(const char *what, uint32_t threshold_ms)
        : m_what(what), m_threshold(threshold_ms), m_t0(GetTickCount64())
    {
    }

    DiagTimer::DiagTimer(const char *what, const qstring &detail, uint32_t threshold_ms)
        : m_what(what), m_detail(detail), m_threshold(threshold_ms), m_t0(GetTickCount64())
    {
    }

    DiagTimer::DiagTimer(const char *what, uint64_t ea, uint64_t size, uint32_t threshold_ms)
        : m_what(what), m_threshold(threshold_ms), m_t0(GetTickCount64()),
          m_range(true), m_ea(ea), m_size(size)
    {
    }

    DiagTimer::~DiagTimer()
    {
        uint64_t ms = GetTickCount64() - m_t0;
        if ( ms < m_threshold )
            return;
        if ( m_range )
            diag("%s %llX+%llX: %llu ms", m_what, m_ea, m_size, ms);
        else
            diag("%s%s%s: %llu ms", m_what, m_detail.empty() ? "" : " ", m_detail.c_str(), ms);
    }
}
```

`src/core/diag.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A timing log for what takes long, in %TEMP%\ida-ttd-diag.log.
    //
    // A frozen IDA cannot be asked what it is doing, but its log can be read
    // from another process. Each line has a timestamp and thread id; slow
    // backend calls and session phases are logged. Nothing is written for a
    // call that finishes quickly.
    void diag(const char *fmt, ...);

    // Start a fresh log, keeping the last one as ida-ttd-diag.prev.log.
    void diag_rotate();

    // Off: nothing more is written (the diagnostics_log setting).
    void diag_set_enabled(bool on);

    // Logs '<what> <detail>: <n> ms' on destruction when the scope took at
    // least 'threshold_ms'. 0 logs always.
    class DiagTimer
    {
    public:
        DiagTimer(const char *what, uint32_t threshold_ms = 200);
        DiagTimer(const char *what, const qstring &detail, uint32_t threshold_ms = 200);
        // '<what> <ea>+<size>', the detail formatted only if the line is
        // written: for timers on every memory read, where building a string
        // each time would cost more than most reads.
        DiagTimer(const char *what, uint64_t ea, uint64_t size, uint32_t threshold_ms = 200);
        ~DiagTimer();

    private:
        const char *m_what;
        qstring     m_detail;
        uint32_t    m_threshold;
        uint64_t    m_t0;
        bool        m_range = false;   // log m_ea+m_size rather than m_detail
        uint64_t    m_ea = 0;
        uint64_t    m_size = 0;
    };
}
```

`src/core/guest_view.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/guest_view.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    GuestRead guest_read(ITraceCursor *cursor)
    {
        // 'known' is kept with the reader and reused: export and .pdata
        // parsing make thousands of small reads. A cursor is used by one
        // thread at a time, and so is this reader.
        return [cursor, known = std::vector<uint8_t>()](uint64_t addr, void *buf, size_t size) mutable -> size_t
        {
            if ( cursor == nullptr || buf == nullptr || size == 0 )
                return 0;
            memset(buf, 0, size);
            known.clear();
            cursor->read_memory((ea_t)addr, buf, size, &known);
            size_t n = 0;
            while ( n < size && n < known.size() && known[n] != 0 )
                n++;
            return n;
        };
    }

    GuestView guest_view(ITraceCursor *cursor)
    {
        GuestView v;
        v.read = guest_read(cursor);
        v.regs = [cursor](ittd_regs *out)
        {
            return cursor != nullptr && cursor->read_registers(out);
        };
        return v;
    }
}

```

`src/core/guest_view.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "abi/ida_ttd_backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class ITraceCursor;

    // Guest memory at one position, as parsers want it: fill buf[0..size)
    // from [addr, addr + size) and return how many leading bytes are real,
    // with no hole. A structure reader tests == size; a string reader scans
    // exactly that far.
    //
    // A function rather than a cursor type, so PE parsing, string reading and
    // argument decoding are written once for every backend.
    using GuestRead = std::function<size_t(uint64_t addr, void *buf, size_t size)>;

    // Memory and registers at one position: what a calling convention reads.
    struct GuestView
    {
        GuestRead read;
        // The registers there; false when the backend cannot produce them.
        std::function<bool(ittd_regs *out)> regs;
    };

    // Through a backend's cursor at its current position. A placeholder byte
    // (mapped, value unknown) counts as a real zero, as structure readers have
    // always been given.
    GuestRead guest_read(ITraceCursor *cursor);
    GuestView guest_view(ITraceCursor *cursor);
}
```

`src/core/position.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "core/position.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    static const ITraceBackend *g_position_backend = nullptr;

    void set_position_backend(const ITraceBackend *backend)
    {
        g_position_backend = backend;
    }

    const char *position_syntax()
    {
        return g_position_backend != nullptr ? g_position_backend->position_syntax()
                                             : hex_position_syntax();
    }

    qstring format_position(Position p)
    {
        if ( !p.is_valid() )
            return qstring();
        return g_position_backend != nullptr ? g_position_backend->format_position(p)
                                             : format_hex_position(p);
    }

    bool parse_position(const char *text, Position *out)
    {
        return g_position_backend != nullptr ? g_position_backend->parse_position(text, out)
                                             : parse_hex_position(text, out);
    }

    const char *hex_position_syntax()
    {
        return "Sequence:Steps in hex";
    }

    qstring format_hex_position(Position p)
    {
        qstring out;
        if ( !p.is_valid() )
            return out;
        out.sprnt("%llX:%llX", (uint64_t)p.hi, (uint64_t)p.lo);
        return out;
    }

    // One hex field, which must be non-empty and entirely hex. strtoull alone
    // would read "zzz" as 0 and send the cursor to the start of the recording
    // rather than saying the input was not a position.
    static bool parse_hex_field(const char *begin, const char *end, uint64_t *out)
    {
        while ( begin < end && qisspace(*begin) )
            begin++;
        while ( end > begin && qisspace(end[-1]) )
            end--;
        if ( begin == end )
            return false;

        uint64_t v = 0;
        for ( const char *c = begin; c < end; c++ )
        {
            int digit;
            if ( *c >= '0' && *c <= '9' )
                digit = *c - '0';
            else if ( *c >= 'a' && *c <= 'f' )
                digit = *c - 'a' + 10;
            else if ( *c >= 'A' && *c <= 'F' )
                digit = *c - 'A' + 10;
            else
                return false;
            if ( v > (UINT64_MAX >> 4) )
                return false;               // would overflow
            v = (v << 4) | (uint64_t)digit;
        }
        *out = v;
        return true;
    }

    bool parse_hex_position(const char *text, Position *out)
    {
        if ( text == nullptr || out == nullptr )
            return false;
        const char *colon = strchr(text, ':');
        if ( colon == nullptr )
            return false;

        uint64_t hi = 0, lo = 0;
        if ( !parse_hex_field(text, colon, &hi)
          || !parse_hex_field(colon + 1, text + qstrlen(text), &lo) )
            return false;

        Position p{ hi, lo };
        // The sentinels are not positions a user can ask to go to.
        if ( p.is_sentinel() )
            return false;
        *out = p;
        return true;
    }
}

```

`src/core/position.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A point in a recording, as the backend that loaded it means it.
    //
    // Two 64-bit words: Microsoft TTD uses (sequence, steps), Sogen a single
    // instruction counter in 'lo' with 'hi' zero. The core never interprets
    // them; it compares them, stores them, and asks the backend to render and
    // parse them.
    //
    // Lexicographic order on (hi, lo) must be the recording's chronology,
    // which both backends satisfy.
    //
    // Two words rather than an opaque handle so a position is cheap to copy
    // (every listing row holds one), trivially comparable, and storable in a
    // netnode blob without a backend call to read it back (bookmarks and the
    // memory map keep thousands).
    struct Position
    {
        uint64_t hi = SENTINEL_WORD;
        uint64_t lo = SENTINEL_WORD;

        constexpr Position() = default;
        constexpr Position(uint64_t h, uint64_t l) : hi(h), lo(l) {}

        constexpr bool operator==(const Position &o) const { return hi == o.hi && lo == o.lo; }
        constexpr bool operator!=(const Position &o) const { return !(*this == o); }
        constexpr bool operator< (const Position &o) const { return hi != o.hi ? hi < o.hi : lo < o.lo; }
        constexpr bool operator> (const Position &o) const { return o < *this; }
        constexpr bool operator<=(const Position &o) const { return !(o < *this); }
        constexpr bool operator>=(const Position &o) const { return !(*this < o); }

        // The three sentinels every backend has to be able to express.
        //
        // 'none' is "no position": a default-constructed Position, and what a
        // query that found nothing returns. 'begin' and 'end' mean "the
        // start/end of the recording, wherever that is"; a seek resolves them.
        // They differ from the first and last recorded positions in
        // TraceInfo. A backend translates all three explicitly and must not
        // assume the bit patterns mean anything to its engine.
        static constexpr Position none()  { return { SENTINEL_WORD, SENTINEL_WORD }; }
        static constexpr Position begin() { return { 0, 0 }; }
        static constexpr Position end()   { return { SENTINEL_WORD, SENTINEL_WORD - 1 }; }

        constexpr bool is_valid() const { return *this != none(); }
        constexpr bool is_sentinel() const
        { return *this == none() || *this == begin() || *this == end(); }

    private:
        // Beyond any real position: Microsoft's sequence ids stop well short of
        // it, and Sogen would need 2^64 instructions to reach it.
        static constexpr uint64_t SENTINEL_WORD = UINT64_MAX;
    };

    class ITraceBackend;

    // Render a position the way the recording's own tooling numbers it, and
    // parse it back, through the running session's backend
    // (set_position_backend): instruction numbers for Sogen, Sequence:Steps
    // for Microsoft. With none set, Microsoft's notation, in which positions
    // stored before backends existed are written.
    //
    // An invalid position formats as "", so a listing column comes out blank
    // rather than FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF.
    qstring     format_position(Position p);
    bool        parse_position(const char *text, Position *out);
    // What to put next to an input box that takes one.
    const char *position_syntax();

    // The backend the three above defer to; nullptr for none. The session
    // sets it when a recording opens and clears it when it closes.
    void set_position_backend(const ITraceBackend *backend);

    // Microsoft TTD's notation, two hex words "Sequence:Steps": the default
    // above, and what its backend answers with.
    qstring     format_hex_position(Position p);
    bool        parse_hex_position(const char *text, Position *out);
    const char *hex_position_syntax();

    // A span of a recording, from 'first' to 'last'. begin() to end() is the
    // whole recording, the default for a query with no range.
    struct PositionRange
    {
        Position first = Position::begin();
        Position last  = Position::end();

        constexpr bool whole_trace() const
        { return first == Position::begin() && last == Position::end(); }
    };
}
```

`src/debugger/apidecode.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "debugger/apidecode.h"
#include "debugger/callconv.h"
#include "debugger/module_registry.h"
#include "analysis/syscalls.h"

namespace idattd
{
    using win32meta::ArgKind;
    using win32meta::AuxKind;
    using win32meta::FuncSig;
    using win32meta::ParamSig;

    namespace
    {
        const size_t kMaxPreview = 32;      // bytes of a buffer shown
        const size_t kX86Align   = 4;
        const size_t kMaxParams  = 32;

        bool    g_tried = false;
        qstring g_error;

        bool ensure_loaded()
        {
            if ( !g_tried )
            {
                g_tried = true;
                std::string err;
                if ( !win32meta::loadIndex({}, err) )
                {
                    g_error = err.c_str();
                    msg("[ida-ttd] API metadata not loaded (%s): calls are decoded from IDA's types only.\n",
                        err.c_str());
                }
            }
            return win32meta::index().loaded();
        }

        bool type_is(const ParamSig &p, const char *name)
        {
            return p.type != nullptr && strcmp(p.type, name) == 0;
        }

        // From ttd-capa's abi.cpp: what one parameter occupies on the x86
        // stack, or 0 when the metadata cannot say (a by-value aggregate, an
        // ambiguous 8-byte scalar), after which no offset can be trusted.
        size_t x86_footprint(const ParamSig &p)
        {
            if ( p.x86Footprint != 0 )
                return (p.x86Footprint + kX86Align - 1) / kX86Align * kX86Align;
            if ( p.kind == ArgKind::StructPtr )
            {
                size_t len = p.type != nullptr ? strlen(p.type) : 0;
                bool by_value = len == 0
                             || (p.type[len - 1] != '*' && !(len >= 2 && p.type[len - 2] == '[' && p.type[len - 1] == ']'));
                if ( by_value )
                    return 0;
            }
            size_t size = 4;
            switch ( p.kind )
            {
                case ArgKind::Double:
                    size = 8;
                    break;
                case ArgKind::Integer:
                case ArgKind::Enum:
                case ArgKind::Bool:
                    if ( p.pointeeSize == 8 )
                    {
                        if ( type_is(p, "UIntPtr") || type_is(p, "IntPtr") )
                            size = 4;
                        else if ( type_is(p, "UInt64") || type_is(p, "Int64") )
                            size = 8;
                        else
                            return 0;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        size = p.pointeeSize >= 1 && p.pointeeSize < 8 ? p.pointeeSize : 4;
                    }
                    break;
                default:
                    break;
            }
            return (size + kX86Align - 1) / kX86Align * kX86Align;
        }

        // Each parameter's byte offset from the first stack argument; false
        // when a footprint is unknown.
        bool x86_offsets(const FuncSig &sig, std::vector<size_t> *offsets)
        {
            size_t footprint[kMaxParams] = { 0 };
            uint8_t max_slot = 0;
            for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
            {
                const ParamSig &p = sig.params[i];
                if ( p.slot >= kMaxParams )
                    return false;
                size_t b = x86_footprint(p);
                if ( b == 0 )
                    return false;
                footprint[p.slot] = b;
                max_slot = std::max(max_slot, p.slot);
            }
            size_t running[kMaxParams] = { 0 }, off = 0;
            for ( uint8_t s = 0; s <= max_slot; s++ )
            {
                running[s] = off;
                off += footprint[s] != 0 ? footprint[s] : kX86Align;
            }
            offsets->resize(sig.paramCount);
            for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
                (*offsets)[i] = running[sig.params[i].slot];
            return true;
        }

        bool read_exact(const GuestView &v, uint64_t addr, void *buf, size_t n)
        {
            return addr != 0 && v.read && v.read(addr, buf, n) == n;
        }

        uint64_t read_uint(const GuestView &v, uint64_t addr, size_t n, bool *ok)
        {
            uint64_t x = 0;
            *ok = n <= 8 && read_exact(v, addr, &x, n);
            return x;
        }

        bool is_pointer_kind(ArgKind k)
        {
            switch ( k )
            {
                case ArgKind::AnsiString: case ArgKind::WideString:
                case ArgKind::AnsiBuffer: case ArgKind::WideBuffer: case ArgKind::ByteBuffer:
                case ArgKind::PtrToInt: case ArgKind::StructPtr: case ArgKind::Guid:
                case ArgKind::Pointer: case ArgKind::PtrToAnsiString: case ArgKind::PtrToWideString:
                case ArgKind::CountedAnsiString: case ArgKind::CountedWideString:
                    return true;
                default:
                    return false;
            }
        }

        qstring hex(uint64_t x)
        {
            qstring s;
            s.sprnt("0x%llX", (unsigned long long)x);
            return s;
        }

        qstring number(uint64_t x)
        {
            qstring s;
            if ( x < 10 )
                s.sprnt("%llu", (unsigned long long)x);
            else
                s = hex(x);
            return s;
        }

        // "NAME|NAME" for a value of a parameter with an enum, or empty.
        qstring enum_text(const ParamSig &p, uint64_t val)
        {
            qstring s;
            if ( !p.hasEnum() )
                return s;
            for ( const std::string &name : win32meta::index().decodeEnum(p.enumIndex, val) )
            {
                if ( !s.empty() )
                    s.append('|');
                s.append(name.c_str());
            }
            return s;
        }

        qstring int_text(const ParamSig &p, uint64_t val)
        {
            qstring s = enum_text(p, val);
            return s.empty() ? number(val) : s;
        }

        uint32_t pointee_width(const ParamSig &p, bool is64)
        {
            return p.pointeeSize >= 1 && p.pointeeSize <= 8 ? p.pointeeSize : (is64 ? 8 : 4);
        }

        // A buffer's length in bytes, from the parameter that holds it.
        uint64_t buffer_bytes(const DecodedCall &c, const ParamSig &p, const GuestView *at_return)
        {
            uint64_t n = 0;
            const size_t unit = p.kind == ArgKind::WideBuffer ? 2 : p.pointeeSize != 0 ? p.pointeeSize : 1;
            if ( p.auxKind == AuxKind::CountConst )
                return (uint64_t)p.auxValue * unit;
            if ( p.auxKind != AuxKind::BytesFromParam && p.auxKind != AuxKind::CountFromParam )
                return 0;
            if ( p.auxValue < 0 || (size_t)p.auxValue >= c.args.size() )
                return 0;
            const ParamSig &len = c.sig->params[p.auxValue];
            n = c.args[p.auxValue].raw;
            // A length passed by pointer (DWORD *lpNumberOfBytesRead): its value,
            // at the return when there is one.
            if ( len.kind == ArgKind::PtrToInt && at_return != nullptr )
            {
                bool ok = false;
                n = read_uint(*at_return, n, len.pointeeSize != 0 ? len.pointeeSize : 4, &ok);
                if ( !ok )
                    return 0;
            }
            else if ( len.kind == ArgKind::PtrToInt )
            {
                return 0;
            }
            return p.auxKind == AuxKind::CountFromParam ? n * unit : n;
        }

        qstring preview_bytes(const GuestView &v, uint64_t addr, uint64_t n, bool wide_text)
        {
            if ( addr == 0 )
                return "NULL";
            qstring s = hex(addr);
            if ( n == 0 )
                return s;
            std::vector<uint8_t> b((size_t)std::min<uint64_t>(n, kMaxPreview));
            size_t got = v.read ? v.read(addr, b.data(), b.size()) : 0;
            if ( got == 0 )
                return s;
            b.resize(got);
            // Text when it reads as text, else hex.
            size_t printable = 0;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < b.size(); i += wide_text ? 2 : 1 )
                printable += b[i] >= 0x20 && b[i] < 0x7F;
            const size_t chars = wide_text ? (b.size() + 1) / 2 : b.size();
            s.cat_sprnt(" [%llu]: ", (unsigned long long)n);
            if ( chars != 0 && printable * 10 >= chars * 9 )
            {
                s.append('"');
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < b.size(); i += wide_text ? 2 : 1 )
                    s.append(b[i] >= 0x20 && b[i] < 0x7F ? (char)b[i] : '.');
                s.append('"');
            }
            else
            {
                for ( uint8_t c : b )
                    s.cat_sprnt("%02X", c);
            }
            if ( n > b.size() )
                s.append("...");
            return s;
        }

        qstring counted_string(const GuestView &v, uint64_t us, bool wide, bool is64)
        {
            if ( us == 0 )
                return "NULL";
            uint16_t len = 0;
            bool ok = false;
            len = (uint16_t)read_uint(v, us, 2, &ok);
            if ( !ok )
                return hex(us);
            uint64_t buf = read_uint(v, us + (is64 ? 8 : 4), is64 ? 8 : 4, &ok);
            if ( !ok || buf == 0 )
                return hex(us);
            std::vector<uint8_t> b(std::min<size_t>(len, 1024));
            if ( !read_exact(v, buf, b.data(), b.size()) )
                return hex(us);
            qstring s("\"");
            if ( wide )
            {
                qstring u8;
                utf16_utf8(&u8, (const wchar16_t *)b.data(), (int)(b.size() / 2));
                s.append(u8);
            }
            else
            {
                s.append((const char *)b.data(), b.size());
            }
            s.append('"');
            return s;
        }

        // How one value reads, as of the view.
        qstring render(const GuestView &v, const DecodedCall &c, const ParamSig &p, uint64_t x,
                       const GuestView *at_return)
        {
            const bool is64 = c.is64;
            if ( is_pointer_kind(p.kind) && x == 0 )
                return "NULL";
            switch ( p.kind )
            {
                case ArgKind::Bool:
                    return (uint32_t)x != 0 ? "TRUE" : "FALSE";
                case ArgKind::Handle:
                    if ( x == ~0ull || (!is64 && x == 0xFFFFFFFFull) )
                        return "-1";
                    return hex(x);
                case ArgKind::Enum:
                    return int_text(p, x);
                case ArgKind::Integer:
                {
                    qstring s = enum_text(p, x);
                    return !s.empty() ? s : number(p.pointeeSize == 4 ? (uint32_t)x : x);
                }
                case ArgKind::AnsiString:
                    return qstring("\"") + read_string_at(v, x) + "\"";
                case ArgKind::WideString:
                    return qstring("L\"") + read_wstring_at(v, x) + "\"";
                case ArgKind::AnsiBuffer:
                case ArgKind::WideBuffer:
                case ArgKind::ByteBuffer:
                    return preview_bytes(v, x, buffer_bytes(c, p, at_return), p.kind == ArgKind::WideBuffer);
                case ArgKind::PtrToInt:
                {
                    bool ok = false;
                    uint64_t val = read_uint(v, x, pointee_width(p, is64), &ok);
                    return ok ? hex(x) + " -> " + int_text(p, val) : hex(x);
                }
                case ArgKind::Guid:
                {
                    uint8_t b[16];
                    if ( !read_exact(v, x, b, sizeof(b)) )
                        return hex(x);
                    qstring s;
                    s.sprnt("{%08X-%04X-%04X-%02X%02X-%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X%02X}",
                            *(uint32_t *)b, *(uint16_t *)(b + 4), *(uint16_t *)(b + 6),
                            b[8], b[9], b[10], b[11], b[12], b[13], b[14], b[15]);
                    return s;
                }
                case ArgKind::PtrToAnsiString:
                case ArgKind::PtrToWideString:
                {
                    bool ok = false;
                    uint64_t str = read_uint(v, x, is64 ? 8 : 4, &ok);
                    if ( !ok || str == 0 )
                        return hex(x);
                    return hex(x) + " -> " + (p.kind == ArgKind::PtrToWideString
                                              ? qstring("L\"") + read_wstring_at(v, str) + "\""
                                              : qstring("\"") + read_string_at(v, str) + "\"");
                }
                case ArgKind::StructPtr:
                    // The one structure worth opening: what a native call names.
                    if ( type_is(p, "OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES*") )
                    {
                        bool ok = false;
                        uint64_t us = read_uint(v, x + (is64 ? 16 : 8), is64 ? 8 : 4, &ok);
                        return ok && us != 0 ? counted_string(v, us, true, is64) : hex(x);
                    }
                    return hex(x);
                case ArgKind::CountedAnsiString:
                    return counted_string(v, x, false, is64);
                case ArgKind::CountedWideString:
                    return counted_string(v, x, true, is64);
                default:
                    return hex(x);
            }
        }

        bool is_native(const char *name)
        {
            return (name[0] == 'N' && name[1] == 't') || (name[0] == 'Z' && name[1] == 'w')
                || strncmp(name, "Rtl", 3) == 0 || strncmp(name, "Ldr", 3) == 0;
        }
    }

    const qstring &api_metadata_error()
    {
        ensure_loaded();
        return g_error;
    }

    const FuncSig *api_signature(const char *name)
    {
        if ( name == nullptr || *name == '\0' || !ensure_loaded() )
            return nullptr;
        qstring n(name);
        // Strip "module!", IDA's import and thunk prefixes, and its "_0"
        // suffix for a second name.
        ssize_t bang = n.rfind('!');
        if ( bang >= 0 )
            n.remove(0, (size_t)bang + 1);
        if ( strncmp(n.c_str(), "__imp_", 6) == 0 )
            n.remove(0, 6);
        if ( strncmp(n.c_str(), "j_", 2) == 0 )
            n.remove(0, 2);
        const FuncSig *sig = win32meta::index().lookup(std::string_view(n.c_str(), n.length()));
        if ( sig == nullptr )
        {
            ssize_t us = n.rfind('_');
            if ( us > 0 && us + 1 < (ssize_t)n.length() && qisdigit(n[us + 1]) )
            {
                n.resize((size_t)us);
                sig = win32meta::index().lookup(std::string_view(n.c_str(), n.length()));
            }
        }
        return sig != nullptr && !sig->unsupported() ? sig : nullptr;
    }

    const FuncSig *api_signature(ModuleRegistry *mods, ea_t func_ea)
    {
        if ( mods != nullptr )
        {
            qstring e = mods->export_name_at(func_ea);
            if ( !e.empty() )
                if ( const FuncSig *s = api_signature(e.c_str()) )
                    return s;
        }
        qstring n;
        if ( get_name(&n, func_ea) > 0 )
            return api_signature(n.c_str());
        return nullptr;
    }

    namespace
    {
        // A type from its C spelling, against the database's type libraries.
        // Silent: a name no library defines is the expected failure.
        bool parse_c_type(const qstring &spelling, tinfo_t *out)
        {
            qstring decl, name;
            decl.sprnt("%s ittd_param;", spelling.c_str());
            tinfo_t t;
            if ( !parse_decl(&t, &name, get_idati(), decl.c_str(), PT_SIL) || t.empty() || !t.is_correct() )
                return false;
            *out = t;
            return true;
        }

        // The metadata's spelling of a type's base name in C. win32json uses
        // the .NET names of the primitive types; phnt already uses C names.
        qstring c_base_name(const qstring &base, bool is64)
        {
            static const struct { const char *meta; const char *c; } names[] =
            {
                { "Void",    "void" },
                { "Byte",    "unsigned __int8" },
                { "SByte",   "signed __int8" },
                { "Char",    "wchar_t" },             // a UTF-16 unit in win32json
                { "Int16",   "__int16" },
                { "UInt16",  "unsigned __int16" },
                { "Int32",   "int" },
                { "UInt32",  "unsigned int" },
                { "Int64",   "__int64" },
                { "UInt64",  "unsigned __int64" },
                { "Single",  "float" },
                { "Double",  "double" },
                { "Boolean", "bool" },
                { "Guid",    "GUID" },
                { "PSTR",    "char *" },
                { "PWSTR",   "wchar_t *" },
                { "PCSTR",   "const char *" },
                { "PCWSTR",  "const wchar_t *" },
                { "VOID",    "void" },
            };
            if ( base == "IntPtr" )
                return is64 ? "__int64" : "int";
            if ( base == "UIntPtr" )
                return is64 ? "unsigned __int64" : "unsigned int";
            for ( const auto &n : names )
                if ( base == n.meta )
                    return n.c;
            return base;
        }

        // A generic stand-in for a type the database does not know.
        tinfo_t generic_param_type(const ParamSig &p, bool is64)
        {
            tinfo_t t;
            switch ( p.kind )
            {
                case ArgKind::Float:
                    t.create_simple_type(BTF_FLOAT);
                    return t;
                case ArgKind::Double:
                    t.create_simple_type(BTF_DOUBLE);
                    return t;
                case ArgKind::Handle:
                case ArgKind::FuncPtr:
                    break;
                case ArgKind::Integer:
                case ArgKind::Enum:
                case ArgKind::Bool:
                case ArgKind::Unknown:
                {
                    // pointeeSize is a scalar's own size (x86_footprint reads
                    // it the same way).
                    switch ( p.pointeeSize )
                    {
                        case 1: t.create_simple_type(BT_INT8  | BTMT_UNSIGNED); return t;
                        case 2: t.create_simple_type(BT_INT16 | BTMT_UNSIGNED); return t;
                        case 4: t.create_simple_type(BT_INT32 | BTMT_UNSIGNED); return t;
                        case 8:
                            if ( is64 || type_is(p, "UInt64") || type_is(p, "Int64") )
                            {
                                t.create_simple_type(BT_INT64 | BTMT_UNSIGNED);
                                return t;
                            }
                            break;
                        default:
                            break;
                    }
                    t.create_simple_type((is64 ? BT_INT64 : BT_INT32) | BTMT_UNSIGNED);
                    return t;
                }
                default:
                    break;
            }
            // Pointers of every kind, handles and function pointers.
            tinfo_t v;
            v.create_simple_type(BTF_VOID);
            t.create_ptr(v);
            return t;
        }

        // One parameter's type: its metadata spelling when the database
        // knows it (array suffixes read as pointers), else, for a pointer to
        // an unknown type, a void pointer of the same depth, else a generic.
        tinfo_t param_type(const ParamSig &p, bool is64)
        {
            qstring spelling(p.type != nullptr ? p.type : "");
            while ( spelling.length() >= 2 && spelling.ends_with("[]") )
            {
                spelling.resize(spelling.length() - 2);
                spelling.append('*');
            }
            size_t stars = 0;
            while ( stars < spelling.length() && spelling[spelling.length() - 1 - stars] == '*' )
                stars++;
            qstring base = spelling.substr(0, spelling.length() - stars);
            base.trim2();
            tinfo_t t;
            if ( !base.empty() )
            {
                qstring c = c_base_name(base, is64);
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < stars; i++ )
                    c.append(i == 0 ? " *" : "*");
                if ( parse_c_type(c, &t) )
                    return t;
                if ( stars != 0 )
                {
                    t.create_simple_type(BTF_VOID);
                    for ( size_t i = 0; i < stars; i++ )
                    {
                        tinfo_t ptr;
                        ptr.create_ptr(t);
                        t = ptr;
                    }
                    return t;
                }
                if ( p.kind == ArgKind::Handle && parse_c_type("HANDLE", &t) )
                    return t;
            }
            return generic_param_type(p, is64);
        }
    }

    bool api_prototype(const FuncSig &sig, bool is64, tinfo_t *out)
    {
        if ( sig.hiddenRetPtr() || sig.unsupported() )
            return false;
        func_type_data_t fd;
        // Every Win32 and native API name begins with a capital; the C
        // runtime functions the hand-written table adds (memset, _stricmp)
        // are __cdecl, which only differs from __stdcall on x86.
        const bool crt = sig.name[0] == '_' || (sig.name[0] >= 'a' && sig.name[0] <= 'z');
        fd.set_cc(is64 ? CM_CC_FASTCALL : crt ? CM_CC_CDECL : CM_CC_STDCALL);
        const bool status = (sig.name[0] == 'N' && sig.name[1] == 't')
                         || (sig.name[0] == 'Z' && sig.name[1] == 'w');
        if ( !status || !parse_c_type("NTSTATUS", &fd.rettype) )
            fd.rettype.create_simple_type(is64 ? BT_INT64 : BT_INT32);
        for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
        {
            const ParamSig &p = sig.params[i];
            funcarg_t a;
            a.name = p.name;
            a.type = param_type(p, is64);
            fd.push_back(a);
        }
        return out->create_func(fd);
    }

    bool api_has_out_params(const win32meta::FuncSig &sig)
    {
        // The same test decode_api_args makes for DecodedArg::out.
        for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
        {
            const ParamSig &p = sig.params[i];
            if ( p.isOut() && is_pointer_kind(p.kind) && !type_is(p, "OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES*") )
                return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    void decode_api_args(const GuestView &v, const FuncSig &sig, bool is64, DecodedCall *out)
    {
        out->sig  = &sig;
        out->is64 = is64;
        out->args.clear();
        ittd_regs r{};
        if ( !v.regs || !v.regs(&r) )
            return;
        std::vector<size_t> offs;
        const bool have_offs = is64 || x86_offsets(sig, &offs);
        out->args.resize(sig.paramCount);
        // The raw values first: a buffer's length can live in a later parameter.
        for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
        {
            const ParamSig &p = sig.params[i];
            DecodedArg &a = out->args[i];
            a.name = p.name;
            // The metadata marks OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES "out"; its name goes in.
            a.out  = p.isOut() && is_pointer_kind(p.kind) && !type_is(p, "OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES*");
            bool ok = true;
            if ( is64 )
            {
                static const int GP[4] = { ITTD_REG_RCX, ITTD_REG_RDX, ITTD_REG_R8, ITTD_REG_R8 + 1 /* R9 */ };
                if ( p.slot < 4 && p.isFloat() )
                    memcpy(&a.raw, r.xmm[p.slot], sizeof(a.raw));     // the low 64 bits of XMMn
                else if ( p.slot < 4 )
                    a.raw = r.gp[GP[p.slot]];
                else
                    a.raw = read_uint(v, r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] + 0x20 + 8 * (uint64_t)(p.slot - 4), 8, &ok);
            }
            else if ( have_offs )
            {
                size_t n = x86_footprint(p) == 8 ? 8 : 4;
                // ESP: a backend's 32-bit context may carry upper bits, and
                // callconv.cpp truncates the same way.
                a.raw = read_uint(v, (uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] + (uint64_t)offs[i], n, &ok);
            }
            else
            {
                ok = false;
            }
            if ( !ok )
                a.text = "?";
        }
        for ( uint8_t i = 0; i < sig.paramCount; i++ )
        {
            DecodedArg &a = out->args[i];
            if ( a.text == "?" )
                continue;
            const ParamSig &p = sig.params[i];
            if ( p.isFloat() )
            {
                if ( p.kind == ArgKind::Float )
                {
                    float f;
                    uint32_t bits = (uint32_t)a.raw;
                    memcpy(&f, &bits, 4);
                    a.text.sprnt("%g", f);
                }
                else
                {
                    double d;
                    memcpy(&d, &a.raw, 8);
                    a.text.sprnt("%g", d);
                }
                continue;
            }
            // An out parameter is only its address until the callee has run.
            a.text = a.out ? (a.raw == 0 ? qstring("NULL") : hex(a.raw)) : render(v, *out, p, a.raw, nullptr);
            if ( a.out && a.raw != 0 && p.kind == ArgKind::PtrToInt )
            {
                bool ok = false;
                uint64_t val = read_uint(v, a.raw, pointee_width(p, is64), &ok);
                if ( ok )
                    a.pointee_before = val;
            }
        }
    }

    std::vector<std::pair<size_t, uint32_t>> api_int_outs(const DecodedCall &call)
    {
        std::vector<std::pair<size_t, uint32_t>> v;
        if ( call.sig == nullptr )
            return v;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < call.args.size() && i < call.sig->paramCount; i++ )
        {
            const ParamSig &p = call.sig->params[i];
            if ( !call.args[i].out || call.args[i].raw == 0 || p.kind != ArgKind::PtrToInt )
                continue;
            uint32_t w = p.pointeeSize == 4 || p.pointeeSize == 8 ? p.pointeeSize : (call.is64 ? 8 : 4);
            v.emplace_back(i, w);
        }
        return v;
    }

    qstring api_args_text(const DecodedCall &call)
    {
        qstring text;
        for ( const DecodedArg &a : call.args )
        {
            if ( !text.empty() )
                text.append(", ");
            text.cat_sprnt("%s=%s", a.name.c_str(), a.text.c_str());
        }
        return text;
    }

    void decode_api_outs(const GuestView &v, DecodedCall *call)
    {
        if ( call->sig == nullptr )
            return;
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < call->args.size() && i < call->sig->paramCount; i++ )
        {
            DecodedArg &a = call->args[i];
            if ( !a.out || a.raw == 0 || a.text == "?" )
                continue;
            const ParamSig &p = call->sig->params[i];
            if ( p.kind == ArgKind::PtrToInt && i < call->out_values.size() && call->out_values[i].has_value() )
            {
                a.text = hex(a.raw) + " -> " + int_text(p, *call->out_values[i]);
                continue;
            }
            if ( !v.read )
                continue;
            a.text = render(v, *call, p, a.raw, &v);
            if ( p.kind == ArgKind::PtrToInt )
            {
                bool ok = false;
                uint64_t val = read_uint(v, a.raw, pointee_width(p, call->is64), &ok);
                if ( ok )
                    a.pointee_after = val;
            }
        }
    }

    qstring decode_api_return(const DecodedCall &call, uint64_t rv)
    {
        qstring s;
        // Nt and Zw calls return an NTSTATUS. Rtl and Ldr ones mostly do, but
        // some return a pointer (RtlAllocateHeap) or a count, and the metadata
        // does not say which. A status written to eax clears rax's upper half,
        // so a value with upper bits set is not one, and truncating it would
        // show a wrong pointer.
        const bool status = call.sig != nullptr && is_native(call.sig->name)
                         && (call.sig->name[0] == 'N' || call.sig->name[0] == 'Z'
                          || !call.is64 || (rv >> 32) == 0);
        if ( status )
        {
            const char *st = ntstatus_name((uint32_t)rv);
            if ( st != nullptr )
                return st;
            s.sprnt("0x%08X", (uint32_t)rv);
            return s;
        }
        if ( !call.is64 )
            rv = (uint32_t)rv;
        s.sprnt("0x%llX", (unsigned long long)rv);
        return s;
    }
}
```

`src/debugger/apidecode.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/guest_view.h"
#include "common/apimeta/win32meta.hpp"

namespace idattd
{
    class ModuleRegistry;

    // API calls decoded from metadata rather than IDA's types: Microsoft's
    // Win32 metadata (win32json) and phnt's native API headers, as indexed by
    // ttd-capa (common/apimeta; the two files in ida-ttd-data). They know what
    // IDA's type libraries do not: flag and enum names, which parameters the
    // callee fills in (read again at the return), and each buffer's length.

    // The signature for a function, by its export or IDA name, or nullptr.
    // The indexes load on first use; without them everything here answers
    // nullptr and callers fall back to IDA's types.
    const win32meta::FuncSig *api_signature(ModuleRegistry *mods, ea_t func_ea);
    const win32meta::FuncSig *api_signature(const char *name);
    // Why the indexes are not loaded, or empty when they are.
    const qstring &api_metadata_error();

    // An IDA prototype built from a signature, for a function the database's
    // type libraries do not know (phnt's ntdll Rtl names, which mssdk lacks).
    // Each parameter keeps its name and gets its metadata type when the
    // database's types know that name (ULONG, HANDLE, UNICODE_STRING *),
    // else a generic integer or pointer of the right size. The metadata has
    // no return types: Nt and Zw calls return NTSTATUS, others a
    // pointer-sized integer. __fastcall on x64, __stdcall on x86 (__cdecl
    // for the C runtime). False for a signature that returns an aggregate
    // through a hidden pointer, whose parameter list would be misleading.
    bool api_prototype(const win32meta::FuncSig &sig, bool is64, tinfo_t *out);

    struct DecodedArg
    {
        qstring  name;
        qstring  text;                  // as shown
        uint64_t raw = 0;               // the argument's own value
        bool     out = false;           // read again at the return
        // An out parameter pointing at an integer: the integer at the call
        // and at the return. Equal values may mean Microsoft TTD lacks the
        // kernel's write (ITraceBackend::query_out_values).
        std::optional<uint64_t> pointee_before, pointee_after;
    };

    struct DecodedCall
    {
        const win32meta::FuncSig *sig = nullptr;
        bool                      is64 = true;
        std::vector<DecodedArg>   args;
        // Values found for integer and handle out parameters, by parameter
        // (ITraceBackend::query_out_values), used instead of reading memory at
        // the return, where Microsoft TTD lacks the kernel's writes.
        std::vector<std::optional<uint64_t>> out_values;
    };

    // The out parameters of a decoded call that point at an integer or a
    // handle: parameter index and the integer's width.
    std::vector<std::pair<size_t, uint32_t>> api_int_outs(const DecodedCall &call);
    // "name=value, ..." of a decoded call.
    qstring api_args_text(const DecodedCall &call);

    // At the call site, before the call: every parameter of 'sig'. 'is64' is
    // the calling convention (x64, or x86 stdcall/cdecl).
    void decode_api_args(const GuestView &v, const win32meta::FuncSig &sig, bool is64, DecodedCall *out);
    // Whether decode_api_args would mark any of sig's arguments 'out' (so
    // decode_api_outs may read memory after the call), from the signature
    // alone.
    bool api_has_out_params(const win32meta::FuncSig &sig);
    // At the return: what the callee wrote through its out parameters.
    void decode_api_outs(const GuestView &v, DecodedCall *call);
    // The return value: an NTSTATUS by name for a native API, else hex.
    qstring decode_api_return(const DecodedCall &call, uint64_t rv);
}
```

`src/debugger/callconv.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "debugger/callconv.h"

namespace idattd
{
    size_t stack_arg_offset(const tinfo_t &func_tinfo, size_t n, size_t first_stack_arg,
                            size_t slot)
    {
        size_t off  = 0;
        size_t mask = slot - 1;
        for ( size_t i = first_stack_arg; i < n; i++ )
        {
            tinfo_t arg = func_tinfo.get_nth_arg((int)i);
            size_t sz = arg.get_size();
            // An unknown size still takes a slot; skipping it shifted every
            // later argument.
            if ( sz == BADSIZE )
                sz = slot;
            if ( sz < slot )
                sz = slot;                       // stack slots are pointer-sized minimum
            off += (sz + mask) & ~mask;
        }
        return off;
    }

    // Read at the call instruction before it executes, so no return address
    // is pushed yet: register arguments are in their registers and stack
    // arguments at SP (+ shadow space on x64, + preceding stack arguments).
    uint64_t get_int_arg(const GuestView &view, const tinfo_t &tinfo, size_t n, bool is64)
    {
        func_type_data_t fd;
        if ( !tinfo.get_func_details(&fd) )
            return 0;
        return get_int_arg(view, fd, n, is64);
    }

    // stack_arg_offset over an unpacked prototype.
    static size_t stack_arg_offset(const func_type_data_t &fd, size_t n, size_t first_stack_arg,
                                   size_t slot)
    {
        size_t off  = 0;
        size_t mask = slot - 1;
        for ( size_t i = first_stack_arg; i < n && i < fd.size(); i++ )
        {
            size_t sz = fd[i].type.get_size();
            if ( sz == BADSIZE )
                sz = slot;          // still a slot, as above
            if ( sz < slot )
                sz = slot;
            off += (sz + mask) & ~mask;
        }
        return off;
    }

    uint64_t get_int_arg(const GuestView &view, const func_type_data_t &fd, size_t n, bool is64)
    {
        ittd_regs r{};
        if ( n >= fd.size() || !view.regs || !view.regs(&r) )
            return 0;

        const tinfo_t &arg = fd[n].type;
        const callcnv_t cc = fd.get_cc();

        // A __usercall prototype says where each argument is. IDA numbers
        // the x86 general registers as ITTD_REG_* does (rax 0 .. r15 15);
        // a stack location is an offset from the first stack argument, which
        // is where the stack pointer points at the call. Anything else (an
        // XMM register, a register pair, a scattered aggregate) reads as 0.
        if ( fd.is_user_cc() )
        {
            const argloc_t &loc = fd[n].argloc;
            const size_t sz = arg.get_size();
            if ( loc.is_reg1() && loc.reg1() >= 0 && loc.reg1() < 16 )
            {
                uint64_t v = r.gp[loc.reg1()] >> (8 * loc.regoff());
                return is64 ? v : (uint32_t)v;
            }
            if ( loc.is_stkoff() )
            {
                uint64_t sp = is64 ? r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] : (uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP];
                uint64_t v = 0;
                view.read(sp + loc.stkoff(), &v, sz != BADSIZE && sz >= 1 && sz <= 8 ? sz : (is64 ? 8 : 4));
                return v;
            }
            return 0;
        }

        if ( is64 )
        {
            if ( n < 4 )
            {
                if ( arg.is_floating() )
                {
                    // The low 64 bits of XMM0..3.
                    uint64_t lo = 0;
                    memcpy(&lo, r.xmm[n], sizeof(lo));
                    return lo;
                }
                const int regs[4] = { ITTD_REG_RCX, ITTD_REG_RDX, ITTD_REG_R8, ITTD_REG_R8 + 1 /* R9 */ };
                return r.gp[regs[n]];
            }
            // Every x64 argument takes one 8-byte slot (anything not 1, 2, 4
            // or 8 bytes goes by reference), so type sizes are not summed.
            // 0x20 is the callee's shadow space.
            size_t off = 0x20 + 8 * (n - 4);
            uint64_t v = 0;
            view.read(r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] + off, &v, sizeof(v));
            return v;
        }

        // A 32-bit target's registers are the low halves.
        size_t first_stack_arg = 0;
        if ( cc == CM_CC_FASTCALL )
        {
            // ECX and EDX go to the first two arguments that fit in 32 bits
            // and are not floating point, in order; every other argument is
            // on the stack in order, each taking its size rounded up to 4.
            // So in fastcall(__int64 a, int b), b is in ECX and a on the
            // stack.
            int regs_used = 0;
            size_t stack_off = 0;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i <= n && i < fd.size(); i++ )
            {
                const size_t isz = fd[i].type.get_size();
                const bool in_reg = regs_used < 2 && !fd[i].type.is_floating()
                                 && isz != BADSIZE && isz <= 4;
                if ( i == n )
                {
                    if ( in_reg )
                        return (uint32_t)r.gp[regs_used == 0 ? ITTD_REG_RCX : ITTD_REG_RDX];
                    uint64_t v = 0;
                    view.read((uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] + stack_off, &v, isz == 8 ? 8 : 4);
                    return v;
                }
                if ( in_reg )
                    regs_used++;
                else
                    stack_off += isz == BADSIZE || isz == 0 ? 4 : (isz + 3) & ~size_t(3);
            }
            return 0;
        }
        else if ( cc == CM_CC_THISCALL )
        {
            if ( n == 0 )
                return (uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RCX];
            first_stack_arg = 1;
        }
        size_t off = stack_arg_offset(fd, n, first_stack_arg, 4);
        size_t sz  = arg.get_size();
        uint64_t v = 0;
        view.read((uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] + off, &v, sz == 8 ? 8 : 4);
        return v;
    }

    uint64_t get_return_value(const GuestView &view, bool is64)
    {
        ittd_regs r{};
        if ( !view.regs || !view.regs(&r) )
            return 0;
        return is64 ? r.gp[ITTD_REG_RAX] : (uint32_t)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RAX];
    }

    static void cat_char(qstring *out, wchar_t c)
    {
        switch ( c )
        {
            case L'\n': out->append("\\n"); break;
            case L'\r': out->append("\\r"); break;
            case L'\t': out->append("\\t"); break;
            default:
                // Other control characters would land raw in a one-line listing.
                if ( c < 0x20 || c == 0x7F )
                    out->cat_sprnt("\\x%02X", (unsigned)c);
                else if ( (c >> 8) == 0 )
                    out->cat_sprnt("%c", (char)(c & 0xFF));
                else
                    out->cat_sprnt("%lc", c);
                break;
        }
    }

    // Both string readers read in chunks: per character, a 260-character
    // string cost 260 engine queries per argument of every traced call.
    static const int kMaxStrChars = 260;

    qstring read_string_at(const GuestView &view, uint64_t addr)
    {
        qstring out;
        char    chunk[64];
        int     done = 0;
        while ( done < kMaxStrChars )
        {
            size_t want = (size_t)(kMaxStrChars - done);
            if ( want > sizeof(chunk) )
                want = sizeof(chunk);
            size_t got = view.read(addr + done, chunk, want);
            if ( got == 0 )
                break;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < got; i++ )
            {
                if ( chunk[i] == '\0' )
                    return out;
                cat_char(&out, (unsigned char)chunk[i]);
            }
            done += (int)got;
        }
        return out;
    }

    qstring read_wstring_at(const GuestView &view, uint64_t addr)
    {
        qstring out;
        wchar_t chunk[64];
        int     done = 0;
        while ( done < kMaxStrChars )
        {
            size_t want = (size_t)(kMaxStrChars - done) * sizeof(wchar_t);
            if ( want > sizeof(chunk) )
                want = sizeof(chunk);
            size_t got = view.read(addr + (uint64_t)done * sizeof(wchar_t), chunk, want);
            size_t nch = got / sizeof(wchar_t);
            if ( nch == 0 )
                break;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < nch; i++ )
            {
                if ( chunk[i] == L'\0' )
                    return out;
                cat_char(&out, chunk[i]);
            }
            done += (int)nch;
        }
        return out;
    }
}
```

`src/debugger/callconv.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/guest_view.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Calling-convention helpers the function tracer uses to read arguments
    // and return values. The view must be at the call site (arguments) or
    // just after the matching return (return values); any backend's cursor
    // gives one (core/guest_view.h).

    // Byte offset of the n-th argument from the first stack argument: the
    // sizes of the stack arguments before it, each rounded up to 'slot'
    // (the stack slot size; only x86, with 4, uses this).
    size_t stack_arg_offset(const tinfo_t &func_tinfo, size_t n, size_t first_stack_arg,
                            size_t slot);

    // Integer / pointer argument n of the function described by 'tinfo', read at
    // the view's position (call site). is64 selects the convention.
    uint64_t get_int_arg(const GuestView &view, const tinfo_t &tinfo, size_t n, bool is64);
    // The same from a prototype already unpacked with get_func_details, so a
    // caller reading many calls of one function unpacks it once. Honors
    // __fastcall and __thiscall on x86, and a __usercall prototype's own
    // argument locations (general registers and the stack).
    uint64_t get_int_arg(const GuestView &view, const func_type_data_t &fd, size_t n, bool is64);

    // Integer return value (RAX / EAX) at the view's position.
    uint64_t get_return_value(const GuestView &view, bool is64);

    // Read a (bounded) NUL-terminated narrow / wide string from guest memory,
    // rendered with escapes for control characters.
    qstring read_string_at(const GuestView &view, uint64_t addr);
    qstring read_wstring_at(const GuestView &view, uint64_t addr);
}
```
