`src/debugger/trace_manager.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/position.h"
#include "core/backend.h"
#include "debugger/event_queue.h"
#include "debugger/module_registry.h"
#include "debugger/memory_reader.h"
#include "debugger/code_analyzer.h"
#include "debugger/kept_functions.h"
#include "debugger/segment_layout.h"
#include "common/strings.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // What the plugin wants done when a trace session begins and ends. This is
    // the only way back out to the plugin, so debugger/ does not depend on
    // plugin/.
    struct SessionHooks
    {
        std::function<void()> on_start;   // a trace is loaded: show the TTD UI
        std::function<void()> on_end;     // the trace is closing: tear it down
    };

    // A fork being prepared.
    //
    // "Fork here" fixes a position. Registers and memory changed there
    // through IDA (registers window, hex view, patching) are kept as the
    // fork's changes and shown instead of the recording's while the cursor
    // stands there; elsewhere the recording is read-only. Recording the fork
    // turns them into a ForkRequest.
    class ForkDraft
    {
    public:
        bool     active = false;
        Position at;
        thid_t   tid = NO_THREAD;           // the thread that runs next
        std::map<int, uint64_t> regs;       // IDA register index, value
        std::map<ea_t, uchar>   bytes;

        // A cursor at 'p' shows the draft's changes.
        bool here(Position p) const { return active && p == at; }
        // 'buffer' holds a read of [ea, ea + size) at the draft's position,
        // which returned 'rc' with '*nbytes' bytes: lay the draft's bytes
        // over it. Returns the read's new drc_t.
        ssize_t overlay_read(size_t *nbytes, ea_t ea, void *buffer, size_t size, ssize_t rc) const;
        // Lay the draft's register values over 'values', a read of its
        // thread's registers at its position.
        void    overlay_registers(regval_t *values) const;
        // The draft's position and changes, as a request to record.
        void    fill_request(ForkRequest *req, bool is64) const;
    };

    // The analysis flags and debugger options a session changes, saved by
    // the constructor and put back by the destructor, so a session that
    // starts and ends any way at all leaves the user's choices as they were.
    class SessionOptions
    {
    public:
        SessionOptions();
        ~SessionOptions();
        SessionOptions(const SessionOptions &) = delete;
        SessionOptions &operator=(const SessionOptions &) = delete;
        // Set the session's values again (a second start without an end).
        void apply() const;

    private:
        uint32 m_savedAf = 0;          // INF_AF before the session
        bool   m_dinfoWasOn = false;   // DOPT_LOAD_DINFO before the session
    };

    // The debugger session: translates IDA debugger events (ev_*) into
    // movement through a recording, register and memory reads, and IDA debug
    // events, through whichever backend reads the recording (core/backend.h;
    // Microsoft TTD for a .run, Sogen for a .sogttd). It owns the backend's
    // playhead cursor and navigator and uses only the interface, so nothing
    // here knows which engine is underneath. One instance lives as long as the
    // plugin.
    class TraceManager
    {
    public:
        struct NamedPosition
        {
            std::string name;
            Position    pos;
        };

        TraceManager() = default;

        void set_session_hooks(SessionHooks h) { m_hooks = std::move(h); }
        bool is_active() const { return (bool)m_cursor; }
        // A movement is replaying the playhead cursor; anything that would use
        // the backend from a message pump during it should wait.
        bool is_navigating() const { return m_navigating; }

        // ---- IDA debugger event handlers (return drc_t in an ssize_t) ------
        ssize_t on_init();
        ssize_t on_term();
        ssize_t on_get_processes(procinfo_vec_t *procs);
        ssize_t on_get_debapp_attrs(debapp_attrs_t *attrs);
        ssize_t on_start_process(const char *path, const char *input_path, qstring *errbuf);
        ssize_t on_get_debug_event(gdecode_t *code, debug_event_t *event, int timeout_ms);
        ssize_t on_read_memory(size_t *nbytes, ea_t ea, void *buffer, size_t size);
        ssize_t on_get_memory_info(meminfo_vec_t *ranges);
        ssize_t on_read_registers(thid_t tid, int clsmask, regval_t *values);
        ssize_t on_rebase_if_required_to(ea_t new_base);
        ssize_t on_resume(debug_event_t *event);
        const qstring &last_resume() const { return m_lastResume; }
        // The recording this session replays, as IDA was given it.
        const qstring &trace_path() const { return m_tracePath; }
        // Counts ev_resume calls, so the UI can tell what a movement did
        // (between a resume and its stop) from what the user did.
        uint64 resume_serial() const { return m_resumeSerial; }
        const std::deque<qstring> &event_log() const { return m_eventLog; }

        ssize_t on_set_backwards(bool backwards);
        ssize_t on_set_resume_mode(thid_t tid, resume_mode_t resmod);
        ssize_t on_update_bpts(int *nbpts, update_bpt_info_t *bpts, int nadd, int ndel);
        ssize_t on_exit_process();

        // What the UI has asked for, carried out by the next ev_resume. One
        // value rather than a flag per kind, so of two requests made before a
        // resume only the later fires.
        enum class Request
        {
            None,               // nothing queued: follow IDA's resume mode
            GotoPosition,       // 'position'
            Step,               // one instruction, in 'forward'
            Run,                // to a breakpoint or the trace edge, in 'forward'
            StepOutBackward,    // rewind out of the current frame
            RunToCursor,        // to 'address', in 'forward'
        };

        // ---- UI helpers ----------------------------------------------------
        // Travel to 'p' at the next resume. Shows a wait box until the stop
        // there is fully processed (end_travel_wait), which can take seconds
        // because a backend may rebuild the state only when it is first read.
        void                       set_next_position(const Position &p);
        void                       end_travel_wait();
        void                       goto_position();
        void                       request_single_step(bool forward);
        void                       request_run(bool forward);
        void                       request_step_out_backward();
        // Run backward until execution reaches 'addr', a user breakpoint or
        // the start of the trace. IDA grays out its own
        // ThreadRunToCursorBackwards for this debugger.
        void                       request_run_to_cursor_backward(ea_t addr);
        // Run forward until execution reaches 'addr', a user breakpoint or the
        // end of the trace. IDA's own ThreadRunToCursor plants a real
        // breakpoint, which intermittently fails on a read-only recording.
        void                       request_run_to_cursor_forward(ea_t addr);
        Position                   current_position() const;
        // The instruction the cursor stands on. Bookmarks record it so the list
        // shows where each mark is without seeking to every row.
        ea_t                       current_pc_ea() const;

        // Re-read [lo, hi) from the recording and re-analyze it.
        //
        // IDA's byte cache keeps the first answer for an address, so a range
        // read before its module was mapped, or before the write that produced
        // it was replayed, stays stale. This drops that answer, rebuilds the
        // range from recorded writes and lets IDA disassemble it again.
        //
        // Returns the number of bytes recovered from recorded writes.
        size_t                     reread_range(ea_t lo, ea_t hi);

        // The modules the recording loaded (see ModuleRegistry). This class
        // only tells the registry when a session begins and ends.
        ModuleRegistry       &modules()       { return m_modules; }
        const ModuleRegistry &modules() const { return m_modules; }

        // Identity of the loaded recording, so something cached in the database
        // against one trace is not shown against another. Zero with no trace.
        uint64_t trace_fingerprint() const;

        // What IDA is told the recorded address space looks like, and the
        // reconstructed memory map behind it.
        SegmentLayout       &layout()       { return m_layout; }
        const SegmentLayout &layout() const { return m_layout; }
        // Shorthands: almost every caller wants the map, not the layout.
        const MemoryMap &memmap() const        { return m_layout.map(); }
        MemoryMap       &memmap_for_update()   { return m_layout.map_for_update(); }
        // Last position of the loaded trace, or Position::none() without one.
        // Its 'hi' word is what a replay progress readout divides by.
        Position                   last_position() const;
        std::vector<NamedPosition> collect_positions() const;

        bool                       is64() const { return m_is64; }

        // The backend reading the open recording, and the playhead cursor.
        // Null with no session.
        ITraceBackend             *backend() const { return m_backend; }
        ITraceCursor              *cursor() const  { return m_cursor.get(); }

        // ---- a fork being prepared (ForkDraft) -------------------------------
        using ForkDraft = idattd::ForkDraft;
        void             begin_fork_draft();
        void             discard_fork_draft() { m_draft = ForkDraft{}; }
        const ForkDraft &fork_draft() const { return m_draft; }
        // The cursor stands at the draft's position.
        bool             at_fork_draft() const;
        // The draft's position and changes, as a request to record.
        void             fill_fork_request(ForkRequest *req) const { m_draft.fill_request(req, m_is64); }
        ssize_t on_write_register(thid_t tid, int regidx, const regval_t *value, qstring *errbuf);
        ssize_t on_write_memory(size_t *nbytes, ea_t ea, const void *buffer, size_t size, qstring *errbuf);

        // Called once per stop (HT_DBG dbg_suspend_process), when the debugger
        // memory cache is valid for the new position: names exports of newly
        // seen modules and disassembles code around RIP.
        void                       on_suspended();

        // Explicit, user-triggered deep analysis (CodeAnalyzer::analyze_whole_function).
        void                       analyze_whole_function();

        // The user's work on functions outside every module, kept across
        // sessions (KeptFunctions).
        KeptFunctions             &kept() { return m_kept; }
        // Apply what was kept to the functions defined since the last call.
        // Only while stopped. True when anything was restored.
        bool                       restore_kept();

        // While positive, the messages a stop shows (an edge of the trace, a
        // navigator's notice) go to the output window rather than a modal
        // box: the script api raises it around each ttd() command.
        void                       quiet_stops(bool on) { m_quietStops += on ? 1 : -1; }

    private:
        void   reset_session_state();
        // Copy the user's work on functions outside every module as IDA shows
        // it (at m_shownAt), before a new memory layout deletes them; the
        // playhead is back at 'here' afterwards. Once per shown position.
        void   capture_kept_at_shown(Position here);
        // Replace the pending request with 'kind' and have IDA resume to carry
        // it out. Warns and does nothing without a session.
        void   queue_request(Request kind, bool forward, ea_t address = BADADDR);

        thid_t current_tid() const;
        ea_t   program_counter() const;

        // What the playhead sees, to tell IDA about the threads and modules
        // that a movement started or ended.
        std::set<uint32_t>                          snapshot_threads() const;
        std::map<std::pair<ea_t, Position>, const ModuleInfo *> snapshot_modules() const;
        void  apply_differences(const std::set<uint32_t> &threads_before,
                                const std::set<uint32_t> &threads_after,
                                const std::map<std::pair<ea_t, Position>, const ModuleInfo *> &mods_before,
                                const std::map<std::pair<ea_t, Position>, const ModuleInfo *> &mods_after);
        bool  is_target_module(const ModuleInfo &m) const;
        void  emit_module_load(const ModuleInfo &m);

        // One movement through the navigator, behind a wait box, recording
        // the boundary it hit and any notice the navigator left. 'move' does
        // the movement and says why it stopped.
        StopReason navigate(bool forward, const std::function<StopReason()> &move);
        void  navigate_to(Position p);
        // How a stop is reported to IDA: a single step, a breakpoint the
        // movement stopped on, or neither (a travel, the trace's edge).
        enum class StopEvent { Step, Breakpoint, Suspended };
        // A movement the UI asked for (a travel, a run) stops suspended; one
        // of IDA's step modes stops as a step, which is what IDA waits for.
        // Either way a breakpoint the movement stopped on is reported as one.
        static StopEvent stop_event(StopReason sr)
        { return sr == StopReason::Breakpoint ? StopEvent::Breakpoint : StopEvent::Suspended; }
        static StopEvent step_event(StopReason sr)
        { return sr == StopReason::Breakpoint ? StopEvent::Breakpoint : StopEvent::Step; }
        // Queue the stop, with the thread and module changes the movement
        // made reported first. Under IDA's step modes any event other than
        // the step ends the step there and leaves the step's own event
        // queued, so during one the changes are held back and reported with
        // the next stop outside a step mode.
        void  emit_stop(StopEvent kind);
        // Report the threads and modules that differ from what IDA was last
        // told, and remember the new state as told.
        void  report_differences();

    private:
        SessionHooks      m_hooks;
        ModuleRegistry    m_modules;
        MemoryReader      m_memory;
        CodeAnalyzer      m_code;
        SegmentLayout     m_layout;
        KeptFunctions     m_kept;

        ITraceBackend              *m_backend = nullptr;
        CursorPtr                   m_cursor;       // the playhead
        // The position whose memory IDA shows: where the last stop was
        // handled (on_suspended). A movement that changes the memory layout
        // copies the user's work from there, not from where it landed.
        Position                    m_shownAt = Position::none();
        int                         m_quietStops = 0;   // quiet_stops()
        // capture_kept_at_shown() has run for m_shownAt.
        bool                        m_shownCaptured = false;
        std::unique_ptr<INavigator> m_nav;          // moves m_cursor
        std::vector<Breakpoint>     m_bpts;         // what IDA has set

        // From the first start of a session to its end (on_term). A failed
        // start keeps it, as the options stay changed until then.
        std::optional<SessionOptions>   m_options;

        EventQueue   m_events;
        bool         m_is64 = false;

        bool          m_isForward = true;
        resume_mode_t m_resumeMode = RESMOD_NONE;
        // What the last ev_resume carried, for the script API's 'state'; it is
        // otherwise invisible which movement IDA asked for.
        qstring       m_lastResume;
        qstring       m_tracePath;
        uint64        m_resumeSerial = 0;
        // The threads and modules IDA has been told about.
        std::set<uint32_t> m_toldThreads;
        std::map<std::pair<ea_t, Position>, const ModuleInfo *> m_toldMods;
        bool          m_stepMode   = false;   // this resume is one of IDA's step modes
        bool          m_travelWait = false;   // set_next_position's wait box is up
        // A movement is in progress. Its wait box pumps messages, so IDA can
        // deliver another ev_resume meanwhile, which must not move the same
        // navigator again.
        bool          m_navigating = false;
        // IDA changed breakpoints during a movement; navigate() hands the new
        // set to the navigator once it ends.
        bool          m_bptsDeferred = false;
        // The last few events handed to IDA, resumes received and breakpoint
        // updates, oldest first, for diagnosing what IDA asked for.
        static constexpr size_t EVENT_LOG_LINES = 48;
        std::deque<qstring> m_eventLog;
        void log_event(const qstring &line);

        // The recording edge a movement ran into, reported once the stop is
        // shown (a modal box inside ev_resume is unsafe).
        enum { BOUNDARY_NONE = 0, BOUNDARY_START, BOUNDARY_END };
        int          m_pendingBoundary = BOUNDARY_NONE;
        qstring      m_pendingNotice;

        pid_t         m_pid = 1;

        // The movement the UI asked for, carried out by the next ev_resume.
        struct PendingRequest
        {
            Request  kind    = Request::None;
            bool     forward = true;
            ea_t     address = BADADDR;      // RunToCursor
            Position position;               // GotoPosition
        };
        PendingRequest m_pending;

        std::string m_targetName; // file name of the analyzed binary (for rebase)
        ForkDraft   m_draft;
    };
}

```

`src/loader/ldr_main.cpp`:

```cpp
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ida-ttd trace loader
//
// Lets IDA open a recording (a Microsoft TTD .run, or anything an installed
// backend reads) as a file, with no copy of the recorded binary on disk. The
// program's PE headers and section bytes are read from the recording, at the
// position where it was mapped, and laid down as IDA segments at the address
// it really occupied.
//
// A separate binary from the plugin: IDA finds loaders (LDSC) under loaders/
// and plugins (PLUGIN) under plugins/, and one file in both places would be
// loaded twice, with two copies of every global.
//
// The loader leaves a database plus a trace_link record naming the
// recording, so the plugin can offer to replay it. It never touches the
// debugger.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#include "common/pch.h"
// idaldr.h's validate_array_count trips C4018/C4267; silenced around the SDK
// include only.
#pragma warning(push)
#pragma warning(disable: 4018 4267)
#include <idaldr.h>
#pragma warning(pop)
#include <lines.hpp>
#include <segregs.hpp>

#include "common/trace_link.h"
#include "common/symbols.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"
#include "core/backend_registry.h"
#include "core/guest_view.h"
#include "analysis/query_runner.h"

using namespace idattd;

// The path accept_file was given, as load_file's fallback (load_file gets no
// file name; the database's input path comes first). IDA calls accept_file
// while building the format list, then load_file, so the last value is right.
static qstring g_accepted_path;

// The backend that reads 'path'. Loads the backend modules on first use,
// without installing a log callback: IDA unloads this DLL after loading, and
// the backend DLLs (shared with the plugin) stay. load_file attaches the log
// only for its own work and detaches it before returning.
static ITraceBackend *backend_for(const char *path)
{
    load_backend_modules(false);
    return BackendRegistry::instance().for_file(path);
}

// Whether a file could be a recording some backend reads, judged without
// loading any backend: accept_file sees every file IDA opens, and loading the
// backend DLLs (Sogen's is large) for each .exe would be slow and would map
// code nobody asked for. The ABI has no way to learn a backend's signature
// before loading it, so the known formats are listed here: Sogen's .sogttd,
// whose header starts "SOGTTD" followed by a version digit and a NUL. A new
// backend's format needs a line here to be opened through File > Open.
static bool may_be_backend_recording(const char *filename, const char *head, size_t n)
{
    if ( n >= 6 && memcmp(head, "SOGTTD", 6) == 0 )
        return true;
    const char *ext = filename != nullptr ? strrchr(filename, '.') : nullptr;
    return ext != nullptr && _stricmp(ext, ".sogttd") == 0;
}

static int idaapi accept_file(
        qstring *fileformatname,
        qstring *processor,
        linput_t *li,
        const char *filename)
{
    // Runs for every file IDA opens, so it must stay cheap. A .run is known
    // by its six magic bytes without loading anything (least of all
    // TTDReplay.dll); anything else whose name or header looks like a known
    // backend format goes to the backends' can_open, which only reads a
    // signature.
    char magic[8] = { 0 };
    qlseek(li, 0, SEEK_SET);
    ssize_t got = qlread(li, magic, sizeof(magic));
    bool is_run = got >= 6 && memcmp(magic, "TTDLog", 6) == 0;

    ITraceBackend *b = nullptr;
    if ( !is_run )
    {
        if ( filename == nullptr || !qfileexist(filename)
          || !may_be_backend_recording(filename, magic, got > 0 ? (size_t)got : 0) )
            return 0;
        b = backend_for(filename);
        if ( b == nullptr )
            return 0;
    }

    if ( filename != nullptr )
        g_accepted_path = filename;

    if ( is_run )
        *fileformatname = "Microsoft TTD trace (.run)";
    else
        fileformatname->sprnt("%s recording", b->display_name());
    *processor      = "metapc";
    // ACCEPT_FIRST puts this above IDA's "Binary file" entry, the only other
    // format that claims a trace.
    return 1 | ACCEPT_FIRST;
}

// Where the trace is: the input file path, or the stashed name when that path
// does not exist (an archive member name, for instance).
static qstring trace_file_path()
{
    char buf[QMAXPATH];
    if ( get_input_file_path(buf, sizeof(buf)) > 0 && qfileexist(buf) )
        return qstring(buf);
    return g_accepted_path;
}

// Permissions and class for one PE section, from its characteristics.
static void section_attrs(uint32_t chars, uint32_t rawsize, uchar *perm, const char **sclass)
{
    uchar p = 0;
    if ( (chars & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE) != 0 ) p |= SEGPERM_EXEC;
    if ( (chars & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ)    != 0 ) p |= SEGPERM_READ;
    if ( (chars & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE)   != 0 ) p |= SEGPERM_WRITE;
    // A section with none of the three is malformed; keep it readable.
    if ( p == 0 )
        p = SEGPERM_READ;
    *perm = p;

    if ( (chars & (IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE)) != 0 )
        *sclass = CLASS_CODE;
    else if ( rawsize == 0 || (chars & IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA) != 0 )
        *sclass = CLASS_BSS;
    else if ( (chars & IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE) == 0 )
        *sclass = CLASS_CONST;
    else
        *sclass = CLASS_DATA;
}

// Copy the bytes of [lo, hi) the recording really has into the database.
// Placeholders (mapped memory with no recorded value) are skipped: zeros would
// claim a value nobody saw, while an unloaded byte shows as what it is.
static size_t fill_from_trace(ITraceCursor *cur, ea_t lo, ea_t hi)
{
    static const size_t PAGE = 0x1000;
    uint8_t buf[PAGE];
    std::vector<uint8_t> known;
    size_t total = 0;

    for ( ea_t a = lo; a < hi; )
    {
        size_t want = (size_t)qmin((uint64_t)PAGE - (a & (PAGE - 1)), (uint64_t)(hi - a));
        memset(buf, 0, want);
        cur->read_memory(a, buf, want, &known);
        // A backend that cannot read memory leaves 'known' as it was.
        if ( known.size() < want )
        {
            a += want;
            continue;
        }
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < want; )
        {
            if ( known[i] != ITTD_KNOWN_YES )
            {
                i++;
                continue;
            }
            size_t j = i;
            while ( j < want && known[j] == ITTD_KNOWN_YES )
                j++;
            mem2base(buf + i, a + i, a + j, -1);   // -1: these bytes have no file offset
            total += j - i;
            i = j;
        }
        a += want;
    }
    return total;
}

// Whether the recording has this address's bytes at the cursor's position.
// Real code is never 64 zero bytes, so a placeholder page does not count.
static bool image_readable_here(ITraceCursor *cur, ea_t ea)
{
    uint8_t b[64] = { 0 };
    std::vector<uint8_t> known;
    cur->read_memory(ea, b, sizeof(b), &known);
    if ( known.size() < sizeof(b) )
        return false;
    for ( size_t i = 0; i < sizeof(b); i++ )
        if ( known[i] == ITTD_KNOWN_YES && b[i] != 0 )
            return true;
    return false;
}

static bool is_exe(const qstring &name)
{
    size_t n = name.length();
    return n > 4 && _stricmp(name.c_str() + n - 4, ".exe") == 0;
}

// The recorded program: the first .exe mapped (only system DLLs come earlier;
// a Sogen recording maps win32u first), else the backend's main module, else
// the first module.
static const ModuleInfo *pick_main_module(ITraceBackend *backend,
                                          const std::vector<ModuleInfo> &mods)
{
    auto when = [](const ModuleInfo &m)
    {
        return m.loaded.is_valid() ? m.loaded : Position::begin();
    };
    const ModuleInfo *best = nullptr;
    for ( const ModuleInfo &m : mods )
        if ( is_exe(m.name) && (best == nullptr || when(m) < when(*best)) )
            best = &m;
    if ( best != nullptr )
        return best;

    const char *named = backend->info().main_module.c_str();
    for ( const ModuleInfo &m : mods )
        if ( named[0] != '\0' && _stricmp(m.name.c_str(), named) == 0 )
            return &m;
    return mods.empty() ? nullptr : &mods.front();
}

// loader_failure() longjmps, so no destructor runs. A recording left open stays
// locked for the session, so fail() releases it first. The handles live here,
// not on load_file's stack, so they are not in a frame the longjmp abandons.
static ITraceBackend *g_backend = nullptr;
static CursorPtr      g_cursor;

static void release_trace()
{
    g_cursor.reset();
    if ( g_backend != nullptr )
        g_backend->close();
    g_backend = nullptr;
    // Nothing of the backend runs on after this, so its log can be taken
    // back and what it queued printed while this DLL is still loaded.
    detach_backend_log();
}

AS_PRINTF(1, 2) static void fail(const char *format, ...)
{
    qstring m;
    va_list va;
    va_start(va, format);
    m.vsprnt(format, va);
    va_end(va);

    release_trace();
    loader_failure("%s", m.c_str());
}

void idaapi load_file(linput_t * /*li*/, ushort neflags, const char *fileformatname)
{
    // The processor owns segment defaults, so it is set before any segment.
    // With SETPROC_LOADER a failure does not return.
    set_processor_type("metapc", SETPROC_LOADER);

    qstring path = trace_file_path();
    if ( path.empty() || !qfileexist(path.c_str()) )
        loader_failure("Cannot find the trace file to load.");

    ITraceBackend *backend = backend_for(path.c_str());
    if ( backend == nullptr )
        loader_failure("No installed backend reads %s.", path.c_str());
    // The backend's diagnostics (index building can take minutes) reach the
    // output window during the load. Lines from other threads are only
    // queued, never posted as UI requests, which could run after IDA unloads
    // this DLL; release_trace() detaches the log and prints them, on every
    // way out (fail() calls it too).
    attach_backend_log(false);
    qstring err;
    if ( !backend->open(path.c_str(), &err) )
        fail("%s", err.c_str());
    g_backend = backend;

    std::vector<ModuleInfo> mods = backend->modules();
    const ModuleInfo *main = pick_main_module(backend, mods);
    if ( main == nullptr )
        fail("The trace records no modules, so there is no image to load.");
    Position mainPos = main->loaded.is_valid() ? main->loaded : backend->info().first;

    ea_t        mainBase = main->base;
    std::string mainPath = main->path.empty() ? main->name.c_str() : main->path.c_str();
    std::string mainName = main->name.c_str();

    // ---- preparation ----------------------------------------------------
    //
    // A Microsoft trace needs its memory index to read the image, and building
    // it is uninterruptible and can take minutes, so ask. Declining still gives
    // correct addresses, names and permissions (no bytes); the plugin builds
    // the index when the replay starts.
    bool haveIndex = backend->prepared();
    if ( !haveIndex && (neflags & NEF_MINI) == 0 )
    {
        int r = ask_yn(ASKBTN_YES,
                       "This trace has no index yet.\n\n"
                       "Building one can take several minutes and cannot be "
                       "interrupted, but without it the recorded program's bytes "
                       "cannot be read.\n\n"
                       "Build the index now?\n"
                       "(No: create the database with the right addresses, names "
                       "and permissions but no code. The index is then built when "
                       "you start the replay.)");
        if ( r == ASKBTN_CANCEL )
            fail("Loading the trace was cancelled.");
        if ( r == ASKBTN_YES )
        {
            // Nothing may longjmp while a wait box or worker is alive;
            // prepare_backend() returns with both gone.
            haveIndex = prepare_backend(backend);
        }
    }

    g_cursor = backend->make_cursor();
    CursorPtr &cur = g_cursor;
    if ( !cur )
        fail("Failed to create a cursor over the trace.");
    cur->seek(mainPos);

    // ---- the recorded image's own headers --------------------------------
    GuestPeInfo pe;
    bool havePe = read_guest_pe_info(guest_read(cur.get()), mainBase, &pe);

    // Bitness from the optional header magic, not the recording machine: a
    // 32-bit program recorded on x64 would otherwise get the wrong register
    // table.
    bool is64 = havePe ? pe.is64 : ((uint64_t)mainBase > 0xFFFFFFFFull);
    if ( !havePe )
    {
        msg("[ida-ttd] could not read %s's PE headers out of the recording; "
            "assuming %d-bit from its load address.\n", mainName.c_str(), is64 ? 64 : 32);
    }

    // Read the image where it was mapped, the right static baseline. But a
    // recording may hold memory only once accessed, and nothing is touched
    // yet when a module appears; if the entry point reads back empty, use the
    // end of the recording, by which time all executed code has been seen.
    if ( havePe && pe.entry_rva != 0 && haveIndex
      && !image_readable_here(cur.get(), mainBase + pe.entry_rva) )
    {
        cur->seek(backend->info().last);
        if ( image_readable_here(cur.get(), mainBase + pe.entry_rva) )
        {
            msg("[ida-ttd] %s is not recorded at the position it was mapped; "
                "reading it from the end of the recording instead.\n",
                mainName.c_str());
        }
        else
        {
            cur->seek(mainPos);      // no better anywhere; keep the baseline
        }
    }

    inf_set_app_bitness(is64 ? 64 : 32);
    // f_PE, not f_LOADER: the PDB plugin and the x86 module gate behavior on
    // it (symbols, MS calling conventions), and the debugger copies it into
    // debugger_t::filetype.
    inf_set_filetype(f_PE);
    inf_set_baseaddr(0);
    inf_set_dll(false);
    set_imagebase(mainBase);
    set_compiler_id(COMP_MS);
    // The Windows SDK type library, as IDA's PE loader would choose. Left alone
    // IDA picked the kernel DDK's (ntddk64_win7), which has no user-mode API,
    // so resolved calls got no prototypes. A recording is always user mode.
    add_til(is64 ? "mssdk64_win10" : "mssdk_win10", ADDTIL_DEFAULT);

    // ---- segments --------------------------------------------------------
    // One flat selector for the whole image.
    sel_t sel      = setup_selector(0);
    // The smaller of the PE's SizeOfImage and the engine's module size: a
    // corrupt or hostile header must not stretch the segments past what the
    // recording mapped.
    uint64_t imageSize = main->size;
    if ( havePe && pe.size_of_image != 0 )
        imageSize = imageSize != 0 ? qmin((uint64_t)pe.size_of_image, (uint64_t)imageSize)
                                   : (uint64_t)pe.size_of_image;
    ea_t  imageEnd = mainBase + (ea_t)imageSize;
    int   nsegs    = 0;

    uint64_t loaded = 0;
    auto add_one = [&](ea_t lo, ea_t hi, const char *name, const char *sclass, uchar perm)
    {
        if ( hi <= lo )
            return;
        size_t got = 0;
        if ( haveIndex && (neflags & NEF_MINI) == 0 )
            got = fill_from_trace(cur.get(), lo, hi);
        loaded += got;

        segment_info_t si;
        si.start_ea = lo;
        si.end_ea   = hi;
        si.set_sel(sel);
        si.set_bitness(is64 ? 2 : 1);
        si.set_align(saRelByte);
        si.set_comb(scPub);
        si.set_perm(perm);
        si.set_name(name);
        si.set_sclass(sclass);
        // SFL_LOADER: the plugin uses it to tell segments that survive the
        // session from debugger segments.
        si.set_loader_segm(true);
        // Sparse only where nothing was loaded; mem2base already made the
        // loaded ranges dense.
        int flags = ADDSEG_NOSREG | ADDSEG_QUIET;
        if ( got == 0 )
            flags |= ADDSEG_SPARSE;
        if ( add_segment_ex(&si, flags) )
            nsegs++;
    };

    if ( havePe && !pe.sections.empty() )
    {
        if ( pe.size_of_headers != 0 )
        {
            // Clamp to the first section, which would otherwise truncate or
            // destroy the header segment on a malformed SizeOfHeaders.
            ea_t hdrEnd = mainBase + pe.size_of_headers;
            ea_t first  = mainBase + pe.sections[0].va;
            if ( hdrEnd > first )
                hdrEnd = first;
            // And to the image, like every section: a hostile SizeOfHeaders
            // with a far first section would cover other modules' memory
            // (and read it page by page from the recording).
            if ( hdrEnd > imageEnd )
                hdrEnd = imageEnd;
            add_one(mainBase, hdrEnd, "HEADER", CLASS_CONST, SEGPERM_READ);
        }

        for ( size_t i = 0; i < pe.sections.size(); i++ )
        {
            const GuestPeSection &s = pe.sections[i];
            uint32_t span = s.vsize != 0 ? s.vsize : s.rawsize;
            if ( span == 0 )
                continue;
            ea_t lo = mainBase + s.va;
            ea_t hi = lo + span;
            if ( lo >= imageEnd )
                continue;
            // Clamp a section running into the next one above it, so
            // segments never overlap. The next by address, not by table
            // order: a malformed image can list them out of order.
            for ( size_t k = 0; k < pe.sections.size(); k++ )
            {
                ea_t next = mainBase + pe.sections[k].va;
                if ( next > lo && hi > next )
                    hi = next;
            }
            if ( hi > imageEnd )
                hi = imageEnd;

            uchar       perm   = 0;
            const char *sclass = CLASS_DATA;
            section_attrs(s.characteristics, s.rawsize, &perm, &sclass);
            add_one(lo, hi, s.name[0] != '\0' ? s.name : ".seg", sclass, perm);
        }
    }
    else
    {
        // No readable section table: one segment over the recorded extent.
        add_one(mainBase, imageEnd, mainName.c_str(), CLASS_CODE,
                SEGPERM_READ | SEGPERM_WRITE | SEGPERM_EXEC);
    }
    set_default_dataseg(sel);

    // ---- entry point ------------------------------------------------------
    if ( havePe && pe.entry_rva != 0 )
    {
        ea_t entry = mainBase + pe.entry_rva;
        inf_set_start_ea(entry);
        inf_set_start_ip(entry);
        inf_set_start_cs(sel);
        add_entry(entry, entry, "start", true);
    }

    // Export names come for free while a cursor is open where the module is
    // mapped; without them the database has no structure until a replay.
    if ( haveIndex && (neflags & NEF_MINI) == 0 )
    {
        size_t named = apply_module_exports(guest_read(cur.get()), mainBase, is64);
        if ( named != 0 )
            msg("[ida-ttd] named %d export(s) of %s from the recording.\n",
                (int)named, mainName.c_str());
    }

    // ---- provenance -------------------------------------------------------
    //
    // The input path becomes the recorded module's path, not the recording's:
    // the title bar shows it, and IDA passes it to ev_start_process, where
    // TraceManager matches its base name against the trace's modules.
    set_root_filename(mainPath.c_str());
    create_filename_cmt();
    add_pgm_cmt("Trace:           %s (%s)", path.c_str(), backend->display_name());
    add_pgm_cmt("Recorded module: %s", mainPath.c_str());
    add_pgm_cmt("Recorded base:   %a, size %08X", mainBase, (uint32)main->size);

    TraceLink link;
    link.trace_path  = path;
    link.module_path = mainPath.c_str();
    link.module_name = mainName.c_str();
    link.module_base = mainBase;
    link.module_size = main->size;
    link.bitness     = is64 ? 64 : 32;
    trace_link_write(link);

    msg("[ida-ttd] loaded %s from %s: %d segment(s) at %a, %d-bit, "
        "0x%llX byte(s) recovered from the recording.\n",
        mainName.c_str(), fileformatname != nullptr ? fileformatname : "a TTD trace",
        nsegs, mainBase, is64 ? 64 : 32, loaded);
    if ( loaded == 0 )
    {
        msg("[ida-ttd] the recording holds no bytes of %s at the position it was "
            "mapped, so the database has its layout but no code. Starting the "
            "replay will serve the bytes as you navigate.\n", mainName.c_str());
    }

    // The plugin opens the recording again when the replay starts.
    release_trace();
}

// The bytes came from recorded memory at their real address, so there are no
// fixups to patch when a segment moves. A null here would tell IDA this loader
// cannot move segments at all.
static int idaapi move_segm(ea_t, ea_t, asize_t, const char *)
{
    return 1;
}

loader_t LDSC =
{
    IDP_INTERFACE_VERSION,
    0,                  // no LDRF_RELOAD: reloading bytes from a recording is meaningless
    accept_file,
    load_file,
    nullptr,            // save_file: a database cannot be written back as a recording
    move_segm,
    nullptr,            // process_archive
};
```

`src/plugin/dllmain.cpp`:

```cpp
// DLL entry point.
#include "common/pch.h"

// The plugin's module handle, for the file name IDA knows it by.
// load_debugger() selects a debugger by its plugin's file name, not by
// debugger_t::name, so switching to this debugger programmatically needs it
// (the SDK's win32 debugger calls load_debugger("win32_stub") while its
// debugger_t::name is "win32").
static HMODULE g_module = nullptr;

// Base name of this DLL without its extension ("ida-ttd"), or empty if it
// cannot be determined. Derived at runtime so a renamed plugin still finds
// itself.
qstring plugin_module_name()
{
    qstring out;
    if ( g_module == nullptr )
        return out;

    char path[QMAXPATH];
    DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameA(g_module, path, (DWORD)sizeof(path));
    if ( n == 0 || n >= sizeof(path) )
        return out;

    const char *base = path;
    for ( const char *p = path; *p != '\0'; p++ )
        if ( *p == '\\' || *p == '/' )
            base = p + 1;

    out = base;
    size_t dot = out.rfind('.');
    if ( dot != qstring::npos )
        out.resize(dot);
    return out;
}

BOOL APIENTRY DllMain( HMODULE hModule,
                       DWORD  ul_reason_for_call,
                       LPVOID lpReserved
                     )
{
    switch (ul_reason_for_call)
    {
    case DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH:
        g_module = hModule;
        break;
    case DLL_THREAD_ATTACH:
    case DLL_THREAD_DETACH:
    case DLL_PROCESS_DETACH:
        break;
    }
    return TRUE;
}
```

`src/plugin/one_shot_timer.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A deferred call onto IDA's UI thread, for work that must not run inside
    // the notification that decided on it.
    //
    // The callback does NOT run from IDA's timer. IDA locks its timer list
    // while a timer callback runs; if the callback pumps the event loop (any
    // wait box or dialog does) and another one-shot timer fires, that timer
    // waits on the same lock to unregister itself, and the main thread
    // deadlocks. This froze IDA when the auto-coverage sweep ran behind a wait
    // box from its timer and the decompiler re-focus timer fired inside it.
    // So the timer only queues an execute_sync(MFF_NOWAIT) request, which IDA
    // runs on a later turn of the UI loop, outside any timer.
    //
    // The callback returns a positive interval to be called again, anything
    // else to stop.
    class OneShotTimer
    {
    public:
        using callback_t = int (idaapi *)(void *ud);

        OneShotTimer() = default;
        ~OneShotTimer() { cancel(); }
        OneShotTimer(const OneShotTimer &) = delete;
        OneShotTimer &operator=(const OneShotTimer &) = delete;

        // Arm, unless already armed or queued: a second request before the
        // first has run is the same request.
        void arm(int interval_ms, callback_t callback, void *ud)
        {
            if ( m_timer != nullptr || m_req != nullptr )
                return;
            m_cb = callback;
            m_ud = ud;
            m_timer = register_timer(interval_ms, on_timer, this);
        }

        void cancel()
        {
            if ( m_timer != nullptr )
            {
                unregister_timer(m_timer);
                m_timer = nullptr;
            }
            if ( m_req != nullptr )
            {
                // Still queued, so still alive: m_req is cleared before the
                // request runs. Disowned first in case it runs regardless.
                m_req->owner = nullptr;
                cancel_exec_request(m_reqId);
                m_req = nullptr;
            }
        }

    private:
        // With MFF_NOWAIT, IDA owns the request and deletes it after running it.
        struct Request : public exec_request_t
        {
            OneShotTimer *owner = nullptr;
            ssize_t idaapi execute() override
            {
                if ( owner != nullptr )
                    owner->run();
                return 0;
            }
        };

        static int idaapi on_timer(void *ud)
        {
            OneShotTimer *t = static_cast<OneShotTimer *>(ud);
            t->m_timer = nullptr;               // IDA frees it once this returns -1
            Request *r = new Request;
            r->owner = t;
            t->m_req = r;
            t->m_reqId = (int)execute_sync(*r, MFF_WRITE | MFF_NOWAIT);
            if ( t->m_reqId < 0 )
            {
                // Not queued, so IDA will neither run nor delete it; left
                // in m_req it would also block every later arm().
                t->m_req   = nullptr;
                t->m_reqId = 0;
                delete r;
            }
            return -1;
        }

        void run()
        {
            m_req = nullptr;
            int again = m_cb(m_ud);
            if ( again > 0 )
                arm(again, m_cb, m_ud);
        }

        qtimer_t   m_timer = nullptr;
        Request   *m_req   = nullptr;
        int        m_reqId = -1;
        callback_t m_cb    = nullptr;
        void      *m_ud    = nullptr;
    };
}
```

`src/plugin/plugin.cpp`:

```cpp
// The plugin's lifetime: the constructor, the destructor, run() and the
// entry point. The rest of Plugin is in the plugin_*.cpp files
// (plugin_internal.h says which holds what).
#include "plugin/plugin_internal.h"
#include "analysis/callsites.h"
#include "common/trace_link.h"
#include "common/symsrv.h"
#include "common/python_eval.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"
#include "plugin/script_api.h"
#include "plugin/settings.h"
#include "debugger/registers.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Put ida-ttd-python\ (beside the plugin; scripts/ida_ttd.py and its
    // siblings) on IDAPython's sys.path, so `import ida_ttd` works. Safe to
    // repeat; a no-op without IDAPython or the folder. True when IDAPython is
    // loaded (so the settings could be read through it).
    static bool register_python_module()
    {
        if ( !python_available() )
            return false;
        HMODULE self = nullptr;
        wchar_t buf[MAX_PATH * 2];
        if ( !GetModuleHandleExW(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS
                               | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                                 reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(&register_python_module), &self)
          || GetModuleFileNameW(self, buf, qnumber(buf)) == 0 )
            return true;
        qstring dir;
        utf16_utf8(&dir, (const wchar16_t *)buf);
        ssize_t slash = dir.rfind('\\');
        if ( slash < 0 )
            return true;
        dir.resize((size_t)slash);
        dir.append("/ida-ttd-python");
        dir.replace("\\", "/");     // a Python string literal without escapes
        if ( !qisdir(dir.c_str()) )
            return true;
        // A quote still needs escaping: a user name can hold one (O'Neil).
        dir.replace("'", "\\'");
        qstring code;
        code.sprnt("import sys\n"
                   "if '%s' not in sys.path:\n"
                   "    sys.path.append('%s')\n", dir.c_str(), dir.c_str());
        qstring err;
        if ( !eval_py(code.c_str(), &err) )
            msg("[ida-ttd] could not put %s on IDAPython's path: %s\n", dir.c_str(), err.c_str());
        return true;
    }

    static int idaapi pdb_poll_cb(void *ud);     // below

    // The live plugin. A request queued with execute_ui_requests can outlive
    // the plugin (the database closes), so each checks its pointer against
    // this first.
    Plugin *g_live_plugin = nullptr;

    Plugin::Plugin()
    {
        g_live_plugin = this;
        // The backend DLLs are not loaded here: the plugin loads in every
        // database, and the Sogen backend links its whole emulator. Every
        // path that needs one (opening a recording, the debugger's init,
        // drv.open, backends, forks) calls load_backend_modules first.
        // Hex-Rays variable and comment edits mark their function for the
        // kept-functions copy, as IDB events do for the rest.
        set_function_edit_hook([](ea_t ea)
        {
            if ( g_live_plugin != nullptr )
                g_live_plugin->manager().kept().note_changed(ea);
        });
        // ttd("...") for scripts (plugin/script_api.h).
        install_script_api(this);
        // An idalib worker gets no ui_ready_to_run; there, IDAPython is
        // already loaded if present at all.
        m_pythonSeen = register_python_module();
        load_settings();

        configure_debugger(m_debugger, inf_is_64bit());
        m_tracer.set_manager(&m_mgr);
        m_tracer.set_64bit(inf_is_64bit());

        // The session's only way back to the plugin, so debugger/ does not
        // depend on plugin/.
        m_mgr.set_session_hooks({
            [this]()
            {
                show_actions();
                // PDB names are applied while a session is paused; the timer
                // runs only then, not in every database for the plugin's life.
                m_pdbTimer.arm(1000, pdb_poll_cb, this);
            },
            [this]()
            {
                hide_actions();
                // The traced functions and recorded calls belong to the closing
                // trace; their positions mean nothing in the next one, and the
                // choosers would travel to them.
                m_tracer.reset();
                coverage_session_ended();
                callsites_session_ended();
                // Their windows travel to positions of this trace too.
                heatmap_session_ended();
                origin_session_ended();
            },
        });

        m_dbgEvents.p = this;
        m_uiEvents.p  = this;
        m_idbEvents.p = this;

        // One context for every TTD handler.
        m_ctx.mgr    = &m_mgr;
        m_ctx.tracer = &m_tracer;
        m_ctx.store  = &m_bookmarks;
        m_ctx.refresh_position = [this]() { update_position_label(); };
        m_ctx.switch_trace     = [this](const qstring &path) { switch_trace(path); };
        m_recordProgram.ctx    = &m_ctx;

        // Icons live as long as the plugin; the actions are registered only
        // while a trace is loaded (show_actions/hide_actions).
        load_icons();
        build_action_table();
        // Pseudocode coverage highlighting, optional: without Hex-Rays the
        // rest works unchanged.
        m_haveDecompiler = init_decompiler();
        hook_event_listener(HT_IDD, this);
        hook_event_listener(HT_DBG, &m_dbgEvents);
        hook_event_listener(HT_UI,  &m_uiEvents);
        hook_event_listener(HT_IDB, &m_idbEvents);
    }

    // PDBs are downloaded and read in the background; their names are applied
    // here a few milliseconds at a time while paused, so no step waits on a
    // PDB. Ticks every 100 ms while there is work, else once a second.
    static int idaapi pdb_poll_cb(void *ud)
    {
        Plugin *p = static_cast<Plugin *>(ud);
        if ( !p->manager().is_active() )
            return -1;                  // armed again at the next session's start
        if ( get_process_state() == DSTATE_SUSP
          && p->manager().modules().advance_pdbs(15) != 0 )
            refresh_idaview_anyway();
        return p->manager().modules().pdbs_pending() ? 100 : 1000;
    }

    Plugin::~Plugin()
    {
        g_live_plugin = nullptr;
        // hide_actions() below rebuilds the TTD menu (with Python calls for
        // its icons) when it unregisters the session's actions; the menu is
        // deleted a few lines later, so that work would be thrown away.
        m_tearingDown = true;
        // First: no symbol download may outlive the plugin, and no script may
        // reach it while it goes away.
        symsrv_shutdown();
        remove_script_api();
        // The Fork manager holds this plugin's action context.
        close_fork_manager();
        m_refocusTimer.cancel();
        m_autoCoverTimer.cancel();
        m_attachTimer.cancel();
        m_switchTimer.cancel();
        m_pdbTimer.cancel();
        m_keptTimer.cancel();
        set_function_edit_hook(nullptr);
        unhook_event_listener(HT_IDB, &m_idbEvents);
        unhook_event_listener(HT_UI,  &m_uiEvents);
        unhook_event_listener(HT_DBG, &m_dbgEvents);
        unhook_event_listener(HT_IDD, this);
        // init() pointed IDA's global 'dbg' at m_debugger, a member; leaving it
        // would hand the kernel a dangling pointer (the listeners that guarded
        // on it are already unhooked).
        if ( ::dbg == &m_debugger )
            ::dbg = nullptr;
        // The backends stay loaded, this DLL does not: their log callback
        // goes, and a log request still in IDA's queue keeps this DLL mapped.
        backend_log_unloading();
        hide_actions();     // toolbar + actions, if a session was still open
        // After hide_actions(), which closes pseudocode views of runtime code;
        // that needs the Hex-Rays hook.
        term_decompiler();
        // The TTD menu outlives sessions but not the plugin.
        delete_menu(SUB_BACKENDS);
        for ( const SubmenuDesc &s : TTD_SUBMENUS )
            delete_menu(s.name);
        delete_menu(TTD_MENU);
        if ( m_menuActionsRegistered )
        {
            unregister_action(actions::INSTALL_RUNTIME);
            unregister_action(actions::INSTALL_SOGEN);
            unregister_action(actions::RECORD_PROGRAM);
            unregister_action(actions::BACKEND_HDR_MS);
            unregister_action(actions::BACKEND_HDR_SOGEN);
            for ( const char *sep : SUBMENU_SEP_ACTIONS )
                unregister_action(sep);
            unregister_action(SUB_BACKENDS_SEP);
            unregister_action(SETTINGS_ACTION);
            m_menuActionsRegistered = false;
        }
        for ( int ic : m_icons )
            if ( ic != -1 )
                free_custom_icon(ic);
    }

    bool idaapi Plugin::run(size_t)
    {
        if ( trace_link_present() && get_process_state() == DSTATE_NOTASK )
        {
            start_trace_session();
            return true;
        }
        info("ida-ttd: open a trace (.run, .sogttd) directly, or select 'TTD trace replayer' "
             "under Debugger > Switch debugger and start with the trace file as "
             "the application.");
        return true;
    }

    // At ui_ready_to_run: IDAPython is loaded by now. The settings are read
    // again only if it was not when the plugin was (they then came from the
    // defaults), so a GUI start reads them once, not twice.
    void Plugin::settings_after_python()
    {
        if ( !m_pythonSeen && register_python_module() )
        {
            m_pythonSeen = true;
            load_settings();
        }
    }
}

//===========================================================================
// Plugin entry point
//===========================================================================
static plugmod_t *idaapi init()
{
    auto *p = new idattd::Plugin();
    dbg = &p->debugger();      // make this plugin's debugger the active one
    return p;
}

plugin_t PLUGIN =
{
    IDP_INTERFACE_VERSION,
    PLUGIN_DBG | PLUGIN_HIDE | PLUGIN_MULTI,
    init,
    nullptr,
    nullptr,
    "Time Travel Debugger (TTD) trace replayer",
    "Loads time travel recordings (Microsoft TTD, Sogen) and lets you navigate them in IDA.",
    "TTD trace replayer",
    nullptr
};
```

`src/plugin/plugin.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"
#include "analysis/tracer.h"
#include "ui/ui.h"
#include "plugin/one_shot_timer.h"
#include "analysis/coverage.h"
#include "ui/decompiler.h"

// Base name of this DLL without its extension, from dllmain.cpp.
qstring plugin_module_name();

namespace idattd
{
    class Plugin;

    // HT_DBG notifications. Resolves export symbols once IDA has created a
    // module's segment.
    struct DbgEventListener : public event_listener_t
    {
        Plugin *p = nullptr;
        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list va) override;
    };

    // HT_UI notifications: the TTD context-menu items, plus UI-ready and
    // widget-closing handling.
    struct UiEventListener : public event_listener_t
    {
        Plugin *p = nullptr;
        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list va) override;
    };

    // HT_IDB notifications: when names change (e.g. IDA applies a downloaded
    // PDB), refresh the call stack so frames show names instead of raw VAs.
    struct IdbEventListener : public event_listener_t
    {
        Plugin *p = nullptr;
        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list va) override;
    };

    // The plugmod_t returned from init(), and the HT_IDD listener for every
    // debugger (ev_*) notification of the plugin's debugger_t.
    class Plugin : public plugmod_t, public event_listener_t
    {
    public:
        Plugin();
        virtual ~Plugin();

        bool    idaapi run(size_t arg) override;
        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list va) override;

        debugger_t     &debugger() { return m_debugger; }
        TraceManager   &manager()  { return m_mgr; }
        const ActionContext *action_context() const { return &m_ctx; }
        FunctionTracer &tracer()   { return m_tracer; }

        // The TTD commands exist only while a trace is loaded, so no TTD
        // shortcut or button is live without one.
        void show_actions();    // register actions, build the TTD toolbar (session start)
        void hide_actions();    // remove the toolbar, unregister actions (session end)
        void reskin_actions();  // (re)apply the codicon icons to the movement actions
        bool actions_visible() const { return m_actionsRegistered; }
        void update_position_label();   // refresh the toolbar's position readout

        // --- keep the decompiler focused across stops --------------------------
        // IDA brings the disassembly to the front on every stop; if the user
        // stepped from the decompiler, it is brought back afterwards.
        void begin_movement();                // ev_resume: note where the user stepped from
        void movement_done();                 // ev_resume carried it out; the stop is known
        void check_stop_decompiles();         // dbg_suspend_process, stepping in pseudocode
        void widget_closing(TWidget *w);      // drop a closed widget pointer
        void reset_step_state()               // a new session: no movement is under way
        { m_stepView = nullptr; m_viewsBefore.clear(); m_renderBefore.clear(); }
        void schedule_after_stop();           // queue the re-focus and view restores

        // Queue a coverage sweep of the function just stopped in, if enabled
        // and not measured before. Deferred to a timer: a sweep pumps the UI
        // behind a wait box, which invites reentrancy inside a debugger
        // notification.
        void schedule_auto_coverage();

        // Restore kept work on functions just defined outside the modules
        // (KeptFunctions), from a timer: the definition is reported inside
        // IDA's notification, where changing the function again is unsafe.
        void schedule_kept_restore();

        // Install the decompiler hook if not installed yet. Cheap, idempotent,
        // and called from several places because Hex-Rays may load after this
        // plugin.
        void try_hook_decompiler();

        // A database created by the loader records its recording. If present,
        // start (or offer) the replay and put a TTD menu action for it, so a
        // declined start is never a dead end. Called once the UI is up.
        void offer_trace_session();
        // Rebuild the whole TTD menu: session items (during a session), then
        // the replay-start items (database made from a recording), then
        // Backends (always). IDA appends to menus and has no reliable
        // "insert before", so every change rebuilds it in order.
        void rebuild_ttd_menu();
        // Wait for the initial analysis to finish, then offer. Starting a
        // session rebases the program and adds segments, which is unsafe while
        // the analysis queue is draining.
        void schedule_trace_offer();
        void switch_trace(const qstring &path);
        // A switch's first half, from the request queue: end the session.
        void switch_exit();
        // At the new session's first stop after a switch: reopen the Fork
        // manager if it was open before.
        void reopen_fork_manager();
        // Start replaying 'path' (a fork of this database's recording). False
        // when the debugger could not be selected.
        // 'quiet' shows no dialog (a script's call: a modal box would hang it).
        bool start_trace_at(const char *path, bool quiet = false);
        // The action body. With 'error' (a script's call) nothing is shown or
        // asked: a failure, or a recording that moved, is returned in it
        // instead of a dialog, which would hang the script. True when the
        // process was started.
        bool start_trace_session(qstring *error = nullptr);
        // Point IDA's debugger at this plugin and the trace, so Debugger >
        // Process options and Start process are correct whether or not the
        // replay starts now. False when the debugger could not be selected.
        // 'quiet' suppresses the popup, for the silent call on database open.
        bool select_trace_debugger(const char *trace_path, bool quiet = false);

        // IDA offers to map a source file whenever it finds line information
        // at the stop; for someone else's build that source is not here and
        // the dialog is noise. The line-info providers are switched off for
        // the session and back on when it ends.
        void suspend_source_debugging();
        void restore_source_debugging();

        void settings_after_python();
        bool can_fork_recording() const
        {
            return m_mgr.backend() != nullptr && m_mgr.backend()->capabilities().fork;
        }
        // The recording can be stepped backwards (both backends today): the
        // backward buttons and menu entries are offered only then.
        bool can_reverse() const
        {
            return m_mgr.backend() != nullptr && m_mgr.backend()->capabilities().reverse_step;
        }

    private:
        void register_actions();
        void unregister_actions();
        void attach_session_menu();
        void restore_native_icons();          // give IDA's movement actions their own icons back
        void load_icons();
        void build_action_table();            // fill m_actions (after load_icons)
        void do_after_stop();                 // timer body: post-stop view work
        static int idaapi refocus_cb(void *ud);
        void do_auto_coverage();              // timer body: sweep the current function
        bool auto_coverage_wanted(ea_t start) const;
        bool auto_indirect_wanted(ea_t start) const;
        bool auto_condmoves_wanted(ea_t start) const;
        static int idaapi autocover_cb(void *ud);
        static int idaapi kept_cb(void *ud);
        static int idaapi attach_cb(void *ud);  // timer body: wait for analysis, then offer

        // One TTD command, as registration, the menu and unregistration need
        // it. m_actions is the only list, so a command cannot be added to one
        // of the three and forgotten in the others.
        struct ActionDesc
        {
            const char       *id       = nullptr;
            const char       *label    = nullptr;
            action_handler_t *handler  = nullptr;
            const char       *shortcut = nullptr;   // nullptr for none
            const char       *tooltip  = nullptr;
            int               icon     = -1;        // -1 for none
            bool              new_group = false;    // separator above this item, in its menu
            bool              on_menu   = true;     // false: toolbar only
            const char       *submenu  = nullptr;   // a TTD_SUBMENUS name, nullptr for the TTD menu
        };

        debugger_t     m_debugger = {};
        TraceManager   m_mgr;
        FunctionTracer m_tracer;
        // Bookmarks belong to the database, so this outlives a session; it is
        // invalidated at session end since the next may be another database.
        BookmarkStore  m_bookmarks;

        DbgEventListener m_dbgEvents;
        UiEventListener  m_uiEvents;
        IdbEventListener m_idbEvents;

        // What every TTD handler reaches the plugin's state through, bound once.
        ActionContext m_ctx;

        // TTD-specific navigation (most stepping is IDA's native actions).
        RunBackHandler         m_runBack;
        StepOutBackHandler     m_stepOutBack;
        RunToCursorBackHandler m_runToCurBack;
        RunToCursorFwdHandler  m_runToCurFwd;
        OpenTimelineHandler    m_timeline;
        PositionCopyHandler    m_posLabel;   // toolbar readout; click copies position
        GotoPositionHandler    m_goto;
        AnalyzeFuncHandler     m_analyzeFunc;
        FullPdbHandler         m_fullPdb;
        // Function-call tracer
        TraceFuncHandler    m_traceFunc;
        TracePatternHandler m_tracePat;
        InstallRuntimeHandler m_installRuntime;
        InstallSogenHandler   m_installSogen;
        RecordProgramHandler  m_recordProgram;
        // Bookmarks + execution coverage
        AddBookmarkHandler   m_addBookmark;
        OpenBookmarksHandler m_bookmarksView;
        CoverageHandler      m_coverage;
        ClearCoverageHandler m_coverageClear;
        // Memory access search + indirect call annotation
        MemSearchHandler          m_memSearch;
        SyscallsHandler           m_syscalls;
        SelfModHandler            m_selfMod;
        ForkHandler               m_fork;
        ForkRecordHandler         m_forkRecord;
        ForkDiscardHandler        m_forkDiscard;
        ForkManagerHandler        m_forkManager;
        ForkOpenHandler           m_forkOpen;
        ForkForgetHandler         m_forkForget;
        RecoverStringsHandler     m_recoverStrings;
        RecoverBuffersHandler     m_recoverBuffers;

        HandlesHandler            m_handles;
        HeatmapHandler            m_heatmap;
        IndirectCallsHandler      m_indirect;
        ClearIndirectCallsHandler m_indirectClear;

        // Every TTD command, in menu order. Built once in the constructor.
        std::vector<ActionDesc> m_actions;

        // SVG icons, loaded once for the plugin's lifetime. The first six go
        // on IDA's own movement actions, in NATIVE_MOVEMENT_ACTIONS order; the
        // rest belong to TTD actions and are set at registration.
        enum Icon
        {
            ICO_CONTINUE = 0,

            ICO_STEP_OVER,
            ICO_STEP_OUT,
            ICO_STEP_INTO_BACK,

            ICO_REV_CONTINUE = ICO_NATIVE_COUNT,
            ICO_STEP_OUT_BACK,

            ICO_ORIGIN,
            ICO_HANDLES,
            ICO_COUNT
        };
        // One array, so the destructor frees them all without a second list
        // to keep in step. -1 means "not loaded".
        std::array<int, ICO_COUNT> m_icons{};

        // True while the actions are registered (a trace is loaded), so
        // registration is never doubled.
        bool m_actionsRegistered = false;
        bool m_pythonSeen = false;      // IDAPython was loaded when the settings were read
        bool m_tearingDown = false;     // in the destructor: no menu rebuilds

        // IDA's own icons for the re-skinned movement actions, captured the
        // first time each action is seen (they register lazily) and restored
        // when the trace unloads: the override is global and would otherwise
        // re-skin the toolbar for every other debugger. Parallel to
        // NATIVE_MOVEMENT_ACTIONS in plugin_actions.cpp.
        int  m_nativeSaved[ICO_NATIVE_COUNT]   = { -1, -1, -1, -1, -1, -1 };
        bool m_nativeSavedOk[ICO_NATIVE_COUNT] = { false, false, false, false, false, false };

        // Decompiler-focus tracking, decided when a movement starts: the view
        // with focus then is where the user stepped from. Watching focus
        // changes cannot work, because IDA's own switches look like the user's.
        TWidget *m_stepView = nullptr;        // pseudocode view the movement started in
        std::vector<TWidget *> m_viewsBefore; // pseudocode views open when it started
        uint64   m_settledResume = 0;         // resume_serial() when the last stop settled
        OneShotTimer m_refocusTimer;          // deferred re-focus
        void settle_stop();                   // the stop is done: the next resume is a new movement
        // Disassembly views and their text/graph mode when the movement
        // started: IDA flips a text view to graph by itself when a stop lands
        // in a function, and that is undone.
        std::vector<std::pair<TWidget *, tcc_renderer_type_t>> m_renderBefore;
        void restore_renderers();
        // IDA's 'batch' flag, set across a stop Hex-Rays cannot decompile so
        // its "Decompilation failure" goes to the output window instead of a
        // dialog per step.
        bool m_quiet      = false;
        bool m_quietOwned = false;      // batch was off, and quiet_ui() turned it on
        bool m_layoutChanged = false;   // since the last after-stop work
        void quiet_ui();
        void unquiet_ui();
        // The position readout only grows within a session, so the toolbar
        // does not shift each time the position gains a digit.
        size_t m_posLabelChars = 0;
        // The sample the position button was last pinned for while stopped.
        qstring m_posPinned;

        // Automatic per-function coverage. Functions whose sweep the user
        // cancelled are remembered for the session only, so the next step
        // does not re-offer it; reopening the trace retries.
        OneShotTimer    m_autoCoverTimer;
        OneShotTimer    m_attachTimer;
        // Switching the replay to another recording: stop, then start it once
        // IDA has finished with the old session.
        qstring         m_switchTo;
        bool            m_switchExitSent = false;
        bool            m_reopenForkManager = false;   // it was open when a switch began
        OneShotTimer    m_switchTimer;
        static int idaapi switch_cb(void *ud);
        OneShotTimer    m_pdbTimer;          // applies downloaded PDBs while paused
        OneShotTimer    m_keptTimer;         // restores kept work (schedule_kept_restore)
        ea_t            m_autoCoverFunc  = BADADDR;   // function the timer will sweep
        std::set<ea_t>  m_autoCoverDeclined;
        bool            m_haveDecompiler = false;
        // Source-info providers turned off here; only these are turned back
        // on, so one the user had disabled stays disabled. The entries are
        // string literals, so storing the pointers is safe.
        std::vector<const char *> m_srcProvidersOff;
        // The Backends actions and menu separators: registered with the
        // plugin, not a session.
        bool m_menuActionsRegistered = false;
        // A failed debugger switch is worth saying once, not on every try.
        bool m_switchReported   = false;
    };
}
```

```cpp
    // Every TTD command, in menu order. Adding one takes a handler member, its
```
