`src/plugin/script_internal.h`:

```h
#pragma once

// What the script_*.cpp files share: the plugin and the drv.* recording
// the commands work on, the helpers more than one file uses, and the
// command rows. Each command file exports its rows (session_commands()
// and so on); script_api.cpp merges them into the table 'help' lists and
// dispatch searches.
#include "plugin/plugin.h"
#include "plugin/script_args.h"
#include "plugin/script_json.h"

#include <span>

namespace idattd
{
    // The plugin the commands work on (script_api.cpp).
    extern Plugin *g_plugin;

    // A recording opened directly through a backend, without a debugger
    // session: what drv.* works on. Exercises a backend and the core's adapter
    // in-process, headless or not.
    //
    // Its own backend instance, never the registry's: that one belongs to the
    // debugger session, whose recording another open would close.
    struct Driver
    {
        BackendPtr     owned;
        ITraceBackend *backend = nullptr;
        CursorPtr      cursor;
        std::unique_ptr<INavigator> nav;
        qstring        path;
        // Counts drv.open calls. A script holding an older handle (a second
        // Recording in Python closed the first) is told so rather than
        // driving the newer recording by mistake.
        uint64_t       handle = 0;

        void close()
        {
            nav.reset();
            cursor.reset();
            if ( backend != nullptr )
                backend->close();
            backend = nullptr;
            owned.reset();
            path.clear();
        }
    };

    // The one drv.* works on (script_drv.cpp).
    extern Driver g_drv;

    inline TraceManager &mgr() { return g_plugin->manager(); }

    // Fail unless a replay session is running (script_session.cpp).
    void need_session();
    // Bytes as hex pairs, "??" where 'known' says the recording does
    // not account for one, as a JSON string (script_drv.cpp).
    qstring bytes_json(const uint8_t *buf, const uint8_t *known, size_t n);
    // The value origin commands' arguments (script_analysis.cpp): a
    // "from=POS" word, removed from the list, and the target at the front.
    bool from_arg(Args *a, Position *p);
    OriginTarget origin_target_arg(const Args &a, const char *cmd);

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ commands

    using Handler = void (*)(const Args &, JObj &);
    struct Command
    {
        const char *name;
        Handler     fn;
        const char *usage;
    };

    // Each file's commands. The order 'help' lists them in is
    // script_api.cpp's.
    std::span<const Command> session_commands();
    std::span<const Command> analysis_commands();
    std::span<const Command> fork_commands();
    std::span<const Command> ui_commands();
    std::span<const Command> drv_commands();
}
```

`src/plugin/script_json.h`:

```h
#pragma once

// The JSON the script interface answers in (script_api.h).
#include "common/pch.h"

#include <vector>

namespace idattd
{
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ JSON
    //
    // Just enough to write answers. Addresses and other 64-bit values go out
    // as "0x..." strings, since a JSON reader that parses into doubles would
    // lose bits.

    // Length of the well-formed UTF-8 sequence at 'p', or 0 when it is not one
    // (a stray continuation byte, an overlong or truncated sequence).
    inline size_t utf8_sequence(const unsigned char *p)
    {
        size_t n;
        if ( (p[0] & 0xE0) == 0xC0 && p[0] >= 0xC2 )
            n = 2;
        else if ( (p[0] & 0xF0) == 0xE0 )
            n = 3;
        else if ( (p[0] & 0xF8) == 0xF0 && p[0] <= 0xF4 )
            n = 4;
        else
            return 0;
        // The NUL terminator is not a continuation byte, so this never reads
        // past the end of the string.
        for ( size_t i = 1; i < n; i++ )
            if ( (p[i] & 0xC0) != 0x80 )
                return 0;
        // Overlong forms, UTF-16 surrogates and code points past U+10FFFF.
        if ( (p[0] == 0xE0 && p[1] < 0xA0) || (p[0] == 0xED && p[1] >= 0xA0)
          || (p[0] == 0xF0 && p[1] < 0x90) || (p[0] == 0xF4 && p[1] >= 0x90) )
            return 0;
        return n;
    }

    inline void json_escape(qstring *out, const char *s)
    {
        out->append('"');
        for ( const unsigned char *p = (const unsigned char *)s; *p != 0; p++ )
        {
            switch ( *p )
            {
                case '"':  out->append("\\\""); break;
                case '\\': out->append("\\\\"); break;
                case '\n': out->append("\\n");  break;
                case '\r': out->append("\\r");  break;
                case '\t': out->append("\\t");  break;
                default:
                    if ( *p < 0x20 )
                    {
                        out->cat_sprnt("\\u%04x", *p);
                    }
                    else if ( *p < 0x80 )
                    {
                        out->append((char)*p);
                    }
                    else if ( size_t n = utf8_sequence(p); n != 0 )
                    {
                        out->append((const char *)p, n);
                        p += n - 1;
                    }
                    else
                    {
                        // Text from a recording need not be UTF-8, and one bad
                        // byte would make the answer unparseable: emit it as
                        // the Latin-1 character.
                        out->cat_sprnt("\\u%04x", *p);
                    }
            }
        }
        out->append('"');
    }

    class JObj
    {
    public:
        JObj &raw(const char *key, const qstring &json)
        {
            sep();
            json_escape(&m_s, key);
            m_s.append(':');
            m_s.append(json);
            return *this;
        }
        JObj &str(const char *key, const char *v)
        {
            qstring j;
            json_escape(&j, v != nullptr ? v : "");
            return raw(key, j);
        }
        JObj &str(const char *key, const qstring &v) { return str(key, v.c_str()); }
        JObj &num(const char *key, int64_t v)
        {
            qstring j;
            j.sprnt("%lld", (long long)v);
            return raw(key, j);
        }
        // A number written as a "0x..." string (JSON numbers lose 64-bit
        // values in many parsers). Its key is listed in the object's "_hex",
        // which is how ida_ttd.py's py() knows to make it an int: a text
        // field that happens to read "0x41" stays text.
        JObj &hex(const char *key, uint64_t v)
        {
            qstring j;
            j.sprnt("\"0x%llX\"", (unsigned long long)v);
            mark_hex(key);
            return raw(key, j);
        }
        // An array of such numbers, listed in "_hex" the same way.
        JObj &hex_list(const char *key, const uint64_t *v, size_t n)
        {
            qstring j = "[";
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < n; i++ )
                j.cat_sprnt("%s\"0x%llX\"", i == 0 ? "" : ",", (unsigned long long)v[i]);
            j.append(']');
            mark_hex(key);
            return raw(key, j);
        }
        JObj &boolean(const char *key, bool v) { return raw(key, qstring(v ? "true" : "false")); }
        qstring done() const
        {
            qstring s = "{";
            s.append(m_s);
            if ( !m_hexKeys.empty() )
            {
                s.append(m_s.empty() ? "\"_hex\":[" : ",\"_hex\":[");
                for ( size_t i = 0; i < m_hexKeys.size(); i++ )
                {
                    if ( i != 0 )
                        s.append(',');
                    json_escape(&s, m_hexKeys[i].c_str());
                }
                s.append(']');
            }
            s.append('}');
            return s;
        }

    private:
        void sep() { if ( !m_s.empty() ) m_s.append(','); }
        void mark_hex(const char *key)
        {
            for ( const qstring &k : m_hexKeys )
                if ( k == key )
                    return;
            m_hexKeys.push_back(key);
        }
        qstring m_s;
        std::vector<qstring> m_hexKeys;
    };

    class JArr
    {
    public:
        void add(const qstring &json)
        {
            if ( !m_s.empty() )
                m_s.append(',');
            m_s.append(json);
            m_n++;
        }
        size_t size() const { return m_n; }
        qstring done() const
        {
            qstring s = "[";
            s.append(m_s);
            s.append(']');
            return s;
        }

    private:
        qstring m_s;
        size_t  m_n = 0;
    };
}
```

`src/plugin/script_session.cpp`:

```cpp
// The script commands on the debugger session: its state, starting,
// waiting, moving and switching, what IDA shows (registers, memory,
// segments), and the plugin's backends and settings.
#include "plugin/script_internal.h"
#include "plugin/settings.h"
#include "core/backend_registry.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ session

    void need_session()
    {
        if ( get_process_state() == DSTATE_NOTASK || !mgr().is_active() )
            fail("no replay session is running; use 'start'");
    }

    // Wait for the debugger to stop again, and say where.
    static void wait_stop(int timeout, JObj &out)
    {
        // WFNE_SILENT: a script has nobody to answer a modal box.
        dbg_event_code_t code = wait_for_next_event(WFNE_SUSP | WFNE_SILENT, timeout);
        out.num("event", code);
        if ( code == DEC_TIMEOUT )
            out.boolean("timed_out", true);
        if ( mgr().is_active() )
        {
            out.str("pos", format_position(mgr().current_position()))
               .hex("pc", mgr().current_pc_ea());
            thid_t tid = get_current_thread();
            out.num("tid", tid);
        }
        out.num("process_state", get_process_state());
    }

    static void cmd_state(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        out.num("process_state", get_process_state()).boolean("session", mgr().is_active())
           .boolean("actions_visible", g_plugin->actions_visible());
        if ( mgr().is_active() )
            out.str("pos", format_position(mgr().current_position())).hex("pc", mgr().current_pc_ea())
               .str("trace", mgr().trace_path());
        out.str("drv_backend", g_drv.backend != nullptr ? g_drv.backend->id() : "")
           .str("last_resume", mgr().last_resume());
        JArr log;
        for ( const qstring &l : mgr().event_log() )
        {
            qstring q;
            json_escape(&q, l.c_str());
            log.add(q);
        }
        out.raw("event_log", log.done());
    }

    static void cmd_start(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        if ( get_process_state() != DSTATE_NOTASK )
            fail("a debugging session is already running");
        // No dialogs from a script: a modal box (the recording moved, the
        // debugger cannot be selected) would hang the caller.
        qstring err;
        a.only(1, { "timeout=" });
        const int timeout = timeout_of(a, 0);
        if ( !g_plugin->start_trace_session(&err) )
            fail("%s", err.c_str());
        wait_stop(timeout, out);
    }

    static void cmd_wait(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        a.only(1, { "timeout=" });
        wait_stop(timeout_of(a, 0), out);
    }

    // switch PATH [TIMEOUT]: end any session and replay PATH in this
    // database, as the Fork manager's switch does but without its timer.
    static void cmd_switch(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        qstring path = a.at(0);
        a.only(2, { "timeout=" });
        const int timeout = timeout_of(a, 1);
        // Before ending anything: a mistyped path must not cost the session.
        if ( !qfileexist(path.c_str()) )
            fail("there is no recording at %s", path.c_str());
        if ( get_process_state() != DSTATE_NOTASK )
        {
            exit_process();
            wait_for_next_event(WFNE_ANY | WFNE_SILENT, 10);
        }
        if ( get_process_state() != DSTATE_NOTASK )
            fail("the running session did not end");
        if ( !g_plugin->start_trace_at(path.c_str(), true) )
            fail("the replay of %s did not start (see the output window)", path.c_str());
        wait_stop(timeout, out);
        out.str("trace", mgr().trace_path());
    }

    // The switch as the Fork manager makes it (timer, then IDA's request
    // queue), returning at once. Poll "state" for the new trace.
    static void cmd_switch_ui(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        g_plugin->switch_trace(a.at(0));
        out.str("queued", a.at(0));
    }

    // One movement of the debugger session, then wait for the stop. Backward
    // movements go the way the TTD toolbar sends them.
    static void cmd_move(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        const qstring &c = a.v[0];
        // runto takes its address first; every movement takes a direction
        // and a timeout, and nothing else.
        a.only(c == "runto" ? 1 : 0, { "back", "backward", "backwards", "timeout=" });
        const bool back = a.back();
        const int timeout = timeout_of(a);
        if ( c == "step" )
            back ? request_step_into_backwards() : request_step_into();
        else if ( c == "over" )
            back ? request_step_over_backwards() : request_step_over();
        else if ( c == "out" )
        {
            if ( back ) { mgr().request_step_out_backward(); wait_stop(timeout, out); return; }
            request_step_until_ret();
        }
        else if ( c == "run" )
        {
            if ( back ) { mgr().request_run(false); wait_stop(timeout, out); return; }
            request_continue_process();
        }
        else if ( c == "runto" )
        {
            ea_t ea = (ea_t)a.u64(0);
            back ? mgr().request_run_to_cursor_backward(ea) : mgr().request_run_to_cursor_forward(ea);
            wait_stop(timeout, out);
            return;
        }
        run_requests();
        wait_stop(timeout, out);
    }

    static void cmd_goto(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        a.only(1, { "timeout=" });
        const int timeout = timeout_of(a);
        mgr().set_next_position(position_arg(a.at(0)));
        request_continue_process();
        run_requests();
        wait_stop(timeout, out);
    }

    static void cmd_regs(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        static const char *names64[] = { "RAX", "RBX", "RCX", "RDX", "RSI", "RDI", "RBP", "RSP",
                                         "R8", "R9", "R10", "R11", "R12", "R13", "R14", "R15",
                                         "RIP", "EFL" };
        static const char *names32[] = { "EAX", "EBX", "ECX", "EDX", "ESI", "EDI", "EBP", "ESP",
                                         "EIP", "EFL" };
        bool is64 = inf_is_64bit();
        JObj regs;
        size_t n = is64 ? qnumber(names64) : qnumber(names32);
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < n; i++ )
        {
            const char *name = is64 ? names64[i] : names32[i];
            uint64 v = 0;
            if ( get_reg_val(name, &v) )
            {
                qstring key = name;
                qstrlwr(key.begin());
                regs.hex(key.c_str(), v);
            }
        }
        out.str("pos", format_position(mgr().current_position())).raw("regs", regs.done());
    }

    static void cmd_read(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        uint64_t ea = a.u64(0), size = a.u64_or(1, 0x40);
        if ( size == 0 || size > 0x10000 )
            fail("read at most 0x10000 bytes");
        std::vector<uint8_t> buf((size_t)size);
        ssize_t got = read_dbg_memory((ea_t)ea, buf.data(), buf.size());
        out.hex("ea", ea).num("got", got)
           .raw("bytes", bytes_json(buf.data(), nullptr, got > 0 ? (size_t)got : 0));
    }

    static void cmd_segments(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        uint64_t max = a.u64_or(0, 400);
        JArr arr;
        for ( int i = 0; i < get_segm_qty() && arr.size() < max; i++ )
        {
            segment_info_t si;
            if ( !get_segment_info_by_num(&si, i, GSI_NAME | GSI_SCLASS) )
                continue;
            JObj o;
            o.str("name", si.get_name()).str("class", si.get_sclass())
             .hex("start", si.start_ea).hex("end", si.end_ea)
             .num("perm", si.get_perm()).boolean("debugger", si.is_debugger_segm());
            arr.add(o.done());
        }
        out.num("count", get_segm_qty()).raw("segments", arr.done());
    }

    static void cmd_stop(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        if ( get_process_state() != DSTATE_NOTASK )
        {
            exit_process();
            wait_for_next_event(WFNE_ANY | WFNE_SILENT, 10);
        }
        out.num("process_state", get_process_state());
    }

    static void cmd_backends(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        load_backend_modules();
        JArr arr;
        for ( ITraceBackend *b : BackendRegistry::instance().all() )
        {
            JObj o;
            BackendModule *m = dynamic_cast<BackendModule *>(b);
            o.str("id", b->id()).str("name", b->display_name()).str("filter", b->file_filter())
             .str("path", m != nullptr ? m->path() : qstring("(built in)"));
            arr.add(o.done());
        }
        out.raw("backends", arr.done());
    }

    // The settings as the plugin holds them (re-read first if
    // ida-config.json changed), so a test can see a change arrive.
    static void cmd_settings(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        reload_settings_if_changed();
        const Settings &s = settings();
        out.boolean("replay_on_open", s.replay_on_open)
           .boolean("symbol_downloads", s.symbol_downloads)
           .str("symbol_server", s.symbol_server)
           .boolean("auto_coverage", s.auto_coverage)
           .boolean("auto_callsites", s.auto_callsites)
           .str("fork_instructions", qstring().sprnt("%llu", (unsigned long long)s.fork_instructions))
           .str("registry_folder", s.registry_folder)
           .boolean("sogen_network", s.sogen_network)
           .str("sogen_checkpoint_interval",
                qstring().sprnt("%llu", (unsigned long long)s.sogen_checkpoint_interval))
           .boolean("sogen_record_reads", s.sogen_record_reads)
           .boolean("sogen_record_writes", s.sogen_record_writes)
           .boolean("sogen_record_executes", s.sogen_record_executes)
           .boolean("sogen_elevated", s.sogen_elevated)
           .boolean("sogen_log", s.sogen_log)
           .boolean("sogen_start_now", s.sogen_start_now)
           .str("sogen_emulation_root", s.sogen_emulation_root)
           .boolean("diagnostics_log", s.diagnostics_log)
           .boolean("memmap_flag_code", s.memmap_flag_code);
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ commands

    static const Command SESSION_COMMANDS[] = {
        { "state",          cmd_state,          "the debugger and session state" },
        { "backends",       cmd_backends,       "the backends loaded, and the folders they came from" },
        { "settings",       cmd_settings,       "the plugin's settings, as it holds them" },
        { "start",          cmd_start,          "[TIMEOUT|timeout=N] start the replay for this database and wait for the first stop" },
        { "wait",           cmd_wait,           "[TIMEOUT|timeout=N] wait for the debugger to stop" },
        { "step",           cmd_move,           "[back] [timeout=N] one instruction" },
        { "over",           cmd_move,           "[back] [timeout=N] step over" },
        { "out",            cmd_move,           "[back] [timeout=N] step out" },
        { "run",            cmd_move,           "[back] [timeout=N] to a breakpoint or the edge of the trace" },
        { "runto",          cmd_move,           "EA [back] [timeout=N] run to an address" },
        { "goto",           cmd_goto,           "POS [timeout=N] travel to a position" },
        { "regs",           cmd_regs,           "the registers IDA shows" },
        { "read",           cmd_read,           "EA [SIZE] debugger memory, as IDA reads it" },
        { "segments",       cmd_segments,       "[MAX] the segments, debugger ones included" },
        { "stop",           cmd_stop,           "end the session" },
        { "switch",         cmd_switch,         "PATH [TIMEOUT|timeout=N] replay another recording (a fork) in this database" },
        { "switch.ui",      cmd_switch_ui,      "PATH replay another recording the way the Fork manager does it (returns at once)" },
    };

    std::span<const Command> session_commands() { return SESSION_COMMANDS; }
}
```

`src/plugin/script_ui.cpp`:

```cpp
// The ui.* script commands: what the plugin's windows ask for (their
// models, a node's action), and the travels they make.
#include "plugin/script_internal.h"
#include "analysis/calltree.h"
#include "analysis/origin.h"
#include "ui/graph_view.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // For the call tree window (scripts/ida_ttd_calltree.py): the tree the
    // TTD menu command last built.
    static void cmd_ui_calltree(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        const qstring &j = call_tree_json();
        if ( j.empty() )
            fail("no call tree has been built");
        out.raw("tree", j);
    }

    // The heatmap's counts, for its window.
    static void cmd_ui_heat(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        const qstring &j = heatmap_json();
        if ( j.empty() )
            fail("no heatmap has been built");
        out.raw("heat", j);
    }

    // The heatmap slice the cursor is in, for the window's marker. Polled,
    // so cheap; "busy" while the replay is moving.
    static void cmd_ui_heatnow(const Args &, JObj &out)
    {
        if ( get_process_state() != DSTATE_SUSP )
        {
            out.boolean("busy", true);
            return;
        }
        out.num("slice", heatmap_current_slice(&mgr()));
    }

    // Count the heatmap again over a span (FROM TO), or over the whole
    // recording (no arguments), and hand the window the new counts.
    static void cmd_ui_heatzoom(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        PositionRange when;
        if ( a.count() >= 2 )
        {
            when.first = position_arg(a.at(0));
            when.last  = position_arg(a.at(1));
        }
        qstring err;
        if ( !build_heatmap(&mgr(), &err, when) )
            fail("%s", err.c_str());
        out.raw("heat", heatmap_json());
    }

    // Travel, then show EA in the hex view, as a double-click in the heatmap does.
    static void cmd_ui_showbytes(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        bool hex = travel_and_show_bytes(&mgr(), position_arg(a.at(0)), (ea_t)a.u64(1));
        out.boolean("hex_view", hex);
    }

    // Travel the way a double-click in a list does: returns at once.
    static void cmd_ui_travel(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        // ui.travel POS [RECORDING]: with the fingerprint of the recording
        // the position came from (a window's data), refused on another one.
        if ( a.count() > 1 && !a.at(1).empty() )
        {
            RecordingStamp made;
            made.fingerprint = a.u64(1);
            if ( !made.current() )
                fail("the position is from another recording than the one being replayed");
            travel_to(&mgr(), position_arg(a.at(0)), made);
        }
        else
        {
            travel_to(&mgr(), position_arg(a.at(0)));
        }
        out.str("queued", a.at(0));
    }

    // The value origin graph, shown as the TTD menu shows it.
    static void cmd_ui_origingraph(const Args &args, JObj &out)
    {
        need_session();
        Args a = args;
        Position from = mgr().current_position();
        from_arg(&a, &from);
        const OriginTarget t = origin_target_arg(a, "ui.origingraph");
        show_origin_graph(&mgr(), t, from);
        out.boolean("shown", graph_is_open("origin"));
    }

    // The graph window's model, and a node's action.
    static void cmd_ui_graph(const Args &a, JObj &out)
    {
        qstring j;
        if ( !graph_json(a.at(0).c_str(), &j) )
            fail("there is no '%s' graph", a.at(0).c_str());
        out.raw("graph", j);
    }

    static void cmd_ui_graphact(const Args &a, JObj &)
    {
        if ( !graph_act(a.at(0).c_str(), (int)a.u64(1), a.count() > 2 ? a.at(2) : qstring()) )
            fail("no such node");
    }

    // ------------------------------------------------------------------ commands

    static const Command UI_COMMANDS[] = {
        { "ui.origingraph", cmd_ui_origingraph, "REG | mem ADDR [SIZE] [from=POS] show the value origin graph" },
        { "ui.graph",       cmd_ui_graph,       "KIND the model of a graph window (forks, origin)" },
        { "ui.graphact",    cmd_ui_graphact,    "KIND NODE ACTION run a graph node's action (NODE in hex, as every number)" },
        { "ui.calltree",    cmd_ui_calltree,    "the call tree last built by the TTD menu (for its window)" },
        { "ui.heat",        cmd_ui_heat,        "the memory heatmap's counts (for its window)" },
        { "ui.heatnow",     cmd_ui_heatnow,     "the heatmap slice the current position is in (-1: outside the span)" },
        { "ui.heatzoom",    cmd_ui_heatzoom,    "[FROM TO] count the heatmap over a span (none: the whole recording)" },
        { "ui.showbytes",   cmd_ui_showbytes,   "POS EA travel there and show EA in the hex view" },
        { "ui.travel",      cmd_ui_travel,      "POS travel there, returning at once (as a double-click does)" },
    };

    std::span<const Command> ui_commands() { return UI_COMMANDS; }
}
```

`src/plugin/settings.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "plugin/settings.h"
#include "common/symsrv.h"
#include "common/python_eval.h"
#include "core/diag.h"

#include <diskio.hpp>
#include <expr.hpp>

namespace idattd
{
    static Settings g_settings;

    const Settings &settings()
    {
        return g_settings;
    }

    RecordOptions recording_options()
    {
        const Settings &s = g_settings;
        RecordOptions o;
        o.network = s.sogen_network;
        o.access_mask = (s.sogen_record_reads ? ITTD_ACCESS_READ : 0u)
                      | (s.sogen_record_writes ? ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE : 0u)
                      | (s.sogen_record_executes ? ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC : 0u);
        // None at all reads as "all" in the ABI; keep the executes then,
        // the least a recording can be stepped through with.
        if ( o.access_mask == 0 )
            o.access_mask = ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC;
        o.checkpoint_interval = s.sogen_checkpoint_interval;
        o.elevated = s.sogen_elevated;
        o.log = s.sogen_log;
        return o;
    }

    // Every key, for ida_ttd_settings.dump().
    static const char ALL_KEYS[] = "replay_on_open symbol_downloads symbol_server auto_coverage auto_callsites "
                                   "fork_instructions registry_folder diagnostics_log memmap_flag_code "
                                   "sogen_network sogen_checkpoint_interval sogen_record_reads "
                                   "sogen_record_writes sogen_record_executes sogen_elevated sogen_log "
                                   "sogen_emulation_root sogen_start_now";

    static bool parse_bool(const qstring &v, bool *out)
    {
        if ( v == "true" )
            *out = true;
        else if ( v == "false" )
            *out = false;
        else
            return false;
        return true;
    }

    // Digits only: strtoull also takes leading blanks and a sign, and turns
    // "-1" into 2^64-1 (for fork_instructions, a fork that runs to the
    // recording's end).
    static bool parse_count(const qstring &value, uint64 *out)
    {
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < value.length(); i++ )
            if ( !qisdigit(value[i]) )
                return false;
        char *end = nullptr;
        errno = 0;
        unsigned long long n = strtoull(value.c_str(), &end, 10);
        if ( value.empty() || end == nullptr || *end != '\0' || errno == ERANGE )
            return false;
        *out = n;
        return true;
    }

    // Apply one "key=value" line from dump(). False for a value the plugin
    // cannot use (it keeps its default); ida-settings already validated it
    // against ida-plugin.json, so this means the two disagree.
    static bool apply(Settings *s, const qstring &key, const qstring &value)
    {
        if ( key == "replay_on_open" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->replay_on_open);
        if ( key == "symbol_downloads" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->symbol_downloads);
        if ( key == "auto_coverage" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->auto_coverage);
        if ( key == "auto_callsites" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->auto_callsites);
        if ( key == "diagnostics_log" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->diagnostics_log);
        if ( key == "memmap_flag_code" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->memmap_flag_code);
        if ( key == "symbol_server" )
        {
            if ( strncmp(value.c_str(), "https://", 8) != 0 && strncmp(value.c_str(), "http://", 7) != 0 )
                return false;
            s->symbol_server = value;
            while ( s->symbol_server.length() > 8 && s->symbol_server.last() == '/' )
                s->symbol_server.remove_last();
            return true;
        }
        if ( key == "fork_instructions" )
            return parse_count(value, &s->fork_instructions);
        if ( key == "sogen_checkpoint_interval" )
            return parse_count(value, &s->sogen_checkpoint_interval);
        if ( key == "sogen_network" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_network);
        if ( key == "sogen_record_reads" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_record_reads);
        if ( key == "sogen_record_writes" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_record_writes);
        if ( key == "sogen_record_executes" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_record_executes);
        if ( key == "sogen_elevated" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_elevated);
        if ( key == "sogen_log" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_log);
        if ( key == "sogen_start_now" )
            return parse_bool(value, &s->sogen_start_now);
        if ( key == "sogen_emulation_root" )
        {
            s->sogen_emulation_root = value;
            while ( !s->sogen_emulation_root.empty()
                 && (s->sogen_emulation_root.last() == '\\' || s->sogen_emulation_root.last() == '/') )
                s->sogen_emulation_root.remove_last();
            return true;
        }
        if ( key == "registry_folder" )
        {
            s->registry_folder = value;
            return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // dump()'s answer, or empty without IDAPython, without ida-settings, or
    // without the module (a build folder copied by hand).
    static qstring read_values()
    {
        qstring text;
        if ( !python_available(true) )
            return text;
        qstring err;
        if ( !eval_py("import ida_ttd_settings\n", &err) )
            return text;
        qstring expr;
        expr.sprnt("ida_ttd_settings.dump('%s')", ALL_KEYS);
        idc_value_t rv;
        if ( eval_py_expr(&rv, expr.c_str(), &err) && rv.vtype == VT_STR )
            text = rv.qstr();
        else if ( !err.empty() )
            msg("[ida-ttd] could not read the plugin's settings (%s); using the defaults.\n", err.c_str());
        return text;
    }

    // ida-config.json's modification time and size when the values were last
    // read. The time has one-second resolution, so two saves within a second
    // could look like none; the size catches most of those (a changed value
    // usually changes the length).
    struct ConfigStamp
    {
        qtime64_t mtime = 0;
        uint64    size  = 0;
        bool operator!=(const ConfigStamp &o) const { return mtime != o.mtime || size != o.size; }
    };
    static ConfigStamp g_configStamp;

    static ConfigStamp config_stamp()
    {
        qstring path = get_user_idadir();
        path.append("\\ida-config.json");
        qstatbuf st;
        ConfigStamp c;
        if ( qstat(path.c_str(), &st) == 0 )
        {
            c.mtime = st.qst_mtime;
            c.size  = (uint64)st.qst_size;
        }
        return c;
    }

    void reload_settings_if_changed()
    {
        if ( config_stamp() != g_configStamp )
            load_settings();
    }

    void load_settings()
    {
        g_configStamp = config_stamp();
        Settings s;
        qstring text = read_values();
        size_t at = 0;
        while ( at < text.length() )
        {
            size_t nl = text.find('\n', at);
            if ( nl == qstring::npos )
                nl = text.length();
            qstring line = text.substr(at, nl);
            at = nl + 1;
            ssize_t eq = line.find('=');
            if ( eq <= 0 )
                continue;
            const bool bad = line[0] == '!';
            qstring key = line.substr(bad ? 1 : 0, eq);
            qstring value = line.substr(eq + 1);
            if ( bad )
                msg("[ida-ttd] setting %s is not valid (%s); using its default.\n",
                    key.c_str(), value.c_str());
            else if ( !apply(&s, key, value) )
                msg("[ida-ttd] setting %s=\"%s\" cannot be used; using its default.\n",
                    key.c_str(), value.c_str());
        }
        g_settings = s;

        symsrv_configure(s.symbol_downloads, s.symbol_server.c_str());
        diag_set_enabled(s.diagnostics_log);
    }
}
```

`src/plugin/settings.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "core/backend.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // The plugin's settings (ida-plugin.json, "settings"). The values come
    // from ida-settings through IDAPython (scripts/ida_ttd_settings.py), read
    // when the plugin loads and again at a stop after ida-config.json changes
    // (reload_settings_if_changed). The defaults here must match
    // ida-plugin.json: they apply without IDAPython or ida-settings.
    struct Settings
    {
        bool     replay_on_open    = true;
        bool     symbol_downloads  = true;
        qstring  symbol_server     = "https://msdl.microsoft.com/download/symbols";
        bool     auto_coverage     = true;      // where the database never set it
        bool     auto_callsites    = false;     // likewise
        uint64   fork_instructions = 1000000;
        qstring  registry_folder;               // empty: none
        qstring  sogen_emulation_root;          // empty: record against this machine's files
        // How Sogen forks and new recordings are made (RecordOptions).
        bool     sogen_network     = false;
        uint64   sogen_checkpoint_interval = 500000;   // 0: Sogen's default
        bool     sogen_record_reads    = true;
        bool     sogen_record_writes   = true;
        bool     sogen_record_executes = true;
        bool     sogen_elevated    = false;
        bool     sogen_log         = false;
        bool     sogen_start_now   = true;      // new recordings start at today's date, not 1970
        bool     diagnostics_log   = true;
        bool     memmap_flag_code  = true;      // highlight executable memory outside modules
    };

    const Settings &settings();

    // The Sogen settings as what a fork or a new recording is made with; the
    // Fork and Record dialogs start from it.
    RecordOptions recording_options();

    // Read the values and pass the relevant ones to lower layers (the symbol
    // downloader, the diagnostics log). Needs ida-ttd-python on sys.path
    // (register_python_module) when IDAPython is present.
    void load_settings();

    // load_settings() again if ida-config.json (where ida-settings keeps the
    // values) changed since the last read. Called on every stop, so a
    // Settings Editor change applies from the next one; costs one stat when
    // nothing changed.
    void reload_settings_if_changed();
}
```

`src/setup/setup_main.cpp`:

```cpp
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// ida-ttd loader setup
//
// Puts the trace loader where IDA looks for loaders. HCLI installs only into
// plugins\ida-ttd\ (no install hook), while IDA finds loaders only in the
// loaders\ folders of $IDAUSR and the IDA directory. So the package carries
// ttd-loader.dll beside this component, which copies it into $IDAUSR\loaders\
// as IDA starts.
//
// A separate plugin because of timing: PLUGIN_FIX plugins load at startup,
// before File > Open or a command-line file, while the main plugin loads with
// a database. From there, a fresh install would not recognize a recording
// until some other database had been opened.
//
// It also shows TTD > Backends while no database is open (the main plugin's
// menu, with the same installers, exists only with a database). The menu is
// removed as a database opens and restored when it closes. Without the GUI or
// the installer script, init() returns nullptr once the loader is in place,
// and nothing stays loaded.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#include "common/pch.h"
#include "common/installer_labels.h"
#include "common/python_eval.h"
#include <diskio.hpp>
#include <expr.hpp>

#include <chrono>
#include <filesystem>
#include <fstream>
#include <iterator>
#include <system_error>
#include <vector>

namespace fs = std::filesystem;

namespace
{
    const wchar_t LOADER_NAME[] = L"ttd-loader.dll";

    fs::path module_dir()
    {
        HMODULE self = nullptr;
        wchar_t buf[MAX_PATH * 2];
        if ( !GetModuleHandleExW(GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_FROM_ADDRESS
                               | GET_MODULE_HANDLE_EX_FLAG_UNCHANGED_REFCOUNT,
                                 reinterpret_cast<LPCWSTR>(&module_dir), &self) )
            return {};
        DWORD n = GetModuleFileNameW(self, buf, qnumber(buf));
        if ( n == 0 || n >= qnumber(buf) )
            return {};
        return fs::path(std::wstring(buf, n)).parent_path();
    }

    fs::path utf8_path(const char *s)
    {
        qwstring w;
        utf8_utf16(&w, s);
        return fs::path(reinterpret_cast<const wchar_t *>(w.c_str()));
    }

    qstring display(const fs::path &p)
    {
        qstring out;
        utf16_utf8(&out, reinterpret_cast<const wchar16_t *>(p.c_str()));
        return out;
    }

    bool read_file(const fs::path &p, std::vector<char> *out)
    {
        std::ifstream f(p, std::ios::binary);
        if ( !f )
            return false;
        out->assign(std::istreambuf_iterator<char>(f), std::istreambuf_iterator<char>());
        return !f.bad();
    }

    // Whether 'installed' is byte-identical to the bundled loader. Content,
    // not timestamp: an upgrade can carry an older file time, and a downgrade
    // is a change too.
    bool same_contents(const fs::path &bundled, const fs::path &installed)
    {
        std::error_code ec;
        if ( !fs::is_regular_file(installed, ec) )
            return false;
        if ( fs::file_size(bundled, ec) != fs::file_size(installed, ec) || ec )
            return false;
        std::vector<char> a, b;
        return read_file(bundled, &a) && read_file(installed, &b) && a == b;
    }

    // Copy 'bundled' over 'target' without a half-written DLL ever sitting in
    // loaders\: stage under a name IDA does not load, then rename into place.
    // A loader mapped by another IDA cannot be replaced but can be renamed, so
    // it is moved aside and deleted on a later start.
    bool install(const fs::path &bundled, const fs::path &target, qstring *err)
    {
        // The process id keeps two IDAs starting at once from writing the
        // same staging file; the name still does not end in .dll.
        const fs::path staged = fs::path(target).concat(L"." + std::to_wstring(GetCurrentProcessId()) + L".new");
        const fs::path aside = fs::path(target).concat(L".old");
        std::error_code ec;
        fs::remove(aside, ec);      // left by an earlier update; fails while still mapped
        if ( !fs::copy_file(bundled, staged, fs::copy_options::overwrite_existing, ec) )
        {
            err->sprnt("could not write %s: %s", display(staged).c_str(), ec.message().c_str());
            return false;
        }
        const DWORD flags = MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING | MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH;
        if ( MoveFileExW(staged.c_str(), target.c_str(), flags) )
            return true;
        if ( MoveFileExW(target.c_str(), aside.c_str(), MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING) )
        {
            if ( MoveFileExW(staged.c_str(), target.c_str(), flags) )
                return true;
            // Put the old loader back rather than leave none.
            DWORD e = GetLastError();
            MoveFileExW(aside.c_str(), target.c_str(), 0);
            SetLastError(e);
        }
        err->sprnt("could not replace %s (error %lu)", display(target).c_str(), GetLastError());
        fs::remove(staged, ec);
        return false;
    }

    // Copy the bundled loader into $IDAUSR\loaders\ when it is not already
    // there as it is. 'dir' is this DLL's folder.
    void install_loader(const fs::path &dir)
    {
        // Only a package install has the loader beside this DLL; elsewhere
        // (a build folder copied into plugins\) there is nothing to do.
        const fs::path bundled = dir / LOADER_NAME;
        std::error_code ec;
        if ( !fs::is_regular_file(bundled, ec) )
            return;

        const fs::path loaders = utf8_path(get_user_idadir()) / L"loaders";
        const fs::path target = loaders / LOADER_NAME;

        // What an install that stopped between copy and rename left behind
        // (LOADER_NAME.<pid>.new), once it is old enough not to be another
        // IDA's install in progress.
        {
            const std::wstring prefix = std::wstring(LOADER_NAME) + L".";
            for ( fs::directory_iterator it(loaders, ec), end; !ec && it != end; it.increment(ec) )
            {
                const std::wstring name = it->path().filename().wstring();
                if ( name.size() <= prefix.size() + 4 || name.compare(0, prefix.size(), prefix) != 0
                  || name.compare(name.size() - 4, 4, L".new") != 0 )
                    continue;
                std::error_code tec;
                const auto age = fs::file_time_type::clock::now() - fs::last_write_time(it->path(), tec);
                if ( !tec && age > std::chrono::hours(1) )
                    fs::remove(it->path(), tec);
            }
            ec.clear();
        }

        // A loader the user put in the IDA directory wins; a second copy would
        // list the format twice in File > Open. A copy this component put in
        // $IDAUSR\loaders\ earlier is removed then, but only one it can tell
        // is a copy (the same bytes as this package's, or as the IDA
        // directory's): never a file it does not know.
        const fs::path ida_copy = utf8_path(idadir(LDR_SUBDIR)) / LOADER_NAME;
        if ( fs::is_regular_file(ida_copy, ec) )
        {
            if ( fs::is_regular_file(target, ec)
              && (same_contents(bundled, target) || same_contents(ida_copy, target)) )
            {
                if ( fs::remove(target, ec) )
                    msg("[ida-ttd] removed %s: the trace loader in %s takes its place.\n",
                        display(target).c_str(), display(ida_copy.parent_path()).c_str());
            }
            return;
        }
        if ( same_contents(bundled, target) )
        {
            fs::remove(fs::path(target).concat(L".old"), ec);
            return;
        }

        const bool update = fs::exists(target, ec);
        fs::create_directories(loaders, ec);
        qstring err;
        if ( install(bundled, target, &err) )
            msg("[ida-ttd] %s the trace loader in %s: File > Open now recognizes "
                ".run and .sogttd recordings. It is not removed when the plugin is "
                "uninstalled; delete it by hand then.%s\n",
                update ? "Updated" : "Installed", display(loaders).c_str(),
                update ? "" : " TTD > Backends installs what opening them needs: "
                              "the TTD runtime for Microsoft recordings, the Sogen "
                              "backend for Sogen ones.");
        else
            msg("[ida-ttd] Could not install the trace loader, so File > Open will not "
                "recognize recordings (%s). Copy %s into %s by hand.\n",
                err.c_str(), display(bundled).c_str(), display(loaders).c_str());
    }

    //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // TTD > Backends while no database is open
    //-----------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Internal names distinct from the main plugin's "TTD" menu, so the two
    // are never confused while both exist. The labels (used in the paths
    // below) match, so the menu looks the same with or without a database.
    const char MENU[]            = "idattd_setup:TTD";
    const char SUBMENU[]         = "idattd_setup:Backends";
    const char ACT_RUNTIME[]     = "idattd_setup:install_runtime";
    const char ACT_SOGEN[]       = "idattd_setup:install_sogen";

    // Runs one function of ida_ttd_runtime (in ida-ttd-python\ beside the main
    // plugin) through IDAPython, like the main plugin's installer actions. With
    // no database open that folder is not on sys.path yet, so the snippet adds
    // it.
    struct installer_t : public action_handler_t
    {
        qstring pydir;          // forward slashes, quotes escaped
        const char *func;       // "install_runtime" or "install_sogen"
        const char *what;       // for the failure message

        installer_t(const char *f, const char *w) : func(f), what(w) {}

        int idaapi activate(action_activation_ctx_t *) override
        {
            if ( !idattd::python_available() )
            {
                warning("Installing %s needs IDAPython, which is not available.", what);
                return 1;
            }
            qstring code;
            code.sprnt("import sys\n"
                       "if '%s' not in sys.path:\n"
                       "    sys.path.append('%s')\n"
                       "import ida_ttd_runtime\n"
                       "ida_ttd_runtime.%s()\n", pydir.c_str(), pydir.c_str(), func);
            qstring err;
            if ( !idattd::eval_py(code.c_str(), &err) )
                warning("Installing %s failed: %s", what, err.c_str());
            return 1;
        }

        action_state_t idaapi update(action_update_ctx_t *) override
        {
            return AST_ENABLE_ALWAYS;
        }
    };

    struct setup_plugin_t : public plugmod_t, public event_listener_t
    {
        installer_t runtime{ "install_runtime", "the TTD runtime" };
        installer_t sogen{ "install_sogen", "the Sogen backend" };
        qtimer_t    timer = nullptr;
        bool        db_open = false;
        bool        shown = false;

        explicit setup_plugin_t(const qstring &pydir)
        {
            runtime.pydir = pydir;
            sogen.pydir = pydir;
            register_action(ACTION_DESC_LITERAL_PLUGMOD(
                ACT_RUNTIME, idattd::INSTALL_RUNTIME_LABEL, &runtime, this, nullptr,
                idattd::INSTALL_RUNTIME_TOOLTIP, -1));
            register_action(ACTION_DESC_LITERAL_PLUGMOD(
                ACT_SOGEN, idattd::INSTALL_SOGEN_LABEL, &sogen, this, nullptr,
                idattd::INSTALL_SOGEN_TOOLTIP, -1));
            ::hook_event_listener(HT_UI, this, this);
            // Not from init(): the menu bar may not exist yet. A command-line
            // file may open before or after this fires; ui_initing_database
            // removes the menu again if after.
            timer = register_timer(0, [](void *ud) -> int
            {
                setup_plugin_t *self = static_cast<setup_plugin_t *>(ud);
                self->timer = nullptr;
                if ( !self->db_open )
                    self->show_menu();
                return -1;
            }, this);
        }

        ~setup_plugin_t() override
        {
            if ( timer != nullptr )
                unregister_timer(timer);
            hide_menu();
            ::unhook_event_listener(HT_UI, this);
        }

        bool idaapi run(size_t) override { return true; }

        void show_menu()
        {
            if ( shown )
                return;
            // No position: appended to the menu bar, like the main plugin's.
            create_menu(MENU, "TTD");
            create_menu(SUBMENU, "Backends", "TTD/");
            attach_action_to_menu("TTD/Backends/", ACT_RUNTIME, SETMENU_APP);
            attach_action_to_menu("TTD/Backends/", ACT_SOGEN, SETMENU_APP);
            shown = true;
        }

        void hide_menu()
        {
            if ( !shown )
                return;
            delete_menu(SUBMENU);
            delete_menu(MENU);
            shown = false;
        }

        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list) override
        {
            switch ( code )
            {
                case ui_initing_database:
                    db_open = true;
                    hide_menu();
                    break;
                case ui_database_closed:
                    db_open = false;
                    show_menu();
                    break;
            }
            return 0;
        }
    };
}

static plugmod_t *idaapi init()
{
    const fs::path dir = module_dir();
    if ( dir.empty() )
        return nullptr;
    install_loader(dir);

    // The menu needs the GUI and the installer script, which the package puts
    // in ida-ttd-python\ one level up.
    if ( !is_idaq() )
        return nullptr;
    std::error_code ec;
    const fs::path pydir = dir.parent_path() / L"ida-ttd-python";
    if ( !fs::is_regular_file(pydir / L"ida_ttd_runtime.py", ec) )
        return nullptr;
    qstring py = display(pydir);
    py.replace("\\", "/");      // a Python string literal without escapes...
    py.replace("'", "\\'");     // ...except a quote (C:/Users/O'Neil)
    return new setup_plugin_t(py);
}

plugin_t PLUGIN =
{
    IDP_INTERFACE_VERSION,
    PLUGIN_FIX | PLUGIN_HIDE | PLUGIN_MULTI,
    init,
    nullptr,
    nullptr,
    "Installs the ida-ttd trace loader",
    nullptr,
    "ida-ttd loader setup",
    nullptr,
};
```

`src/tools/ittd_probe.c`:

```c
/*
 * ittd-probe: load an ida-ttd backend DLL and exercise it against a recording,
 * with no IDA involved.
 *
 *   ittd-probe BACKEND.dll TRACE [EXPORT]
 *
 * Prints what the backend reports and checks the ABI's promises about
 * positions, where a wrong answer is silent in the UI (a register view one
 * instruction off):
 *
 *   - at an access's position, the program counter is the instruction that did
 *     it;
 *   - at a call's pos the PC is the call site, at entry_pos the target, and at
 *     ret_pos it is back in the caller just past the site;
 *   - a forward step moves the position by one.
 *
 * EXPORT (default RtlAllocateHeap) is the function whose calls are listed.
 *
 * Written in C on purpose, to check that abi/ida_ttd_backend.h is plain C.
 */

#include <abi/ida_ttd_backend.h>

#include <windows.h>
#include <psapi.h>
#pragma comment(lib, "psapi.lib")
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static const ittd_backend_api *api;
static ittd_backend *B;

/* Whether the table has entry 'f' and fills it, as the core checks: an entry
 * past the backend's 'size' is not there, whatever the memory beyond holds. */
#define HAS(f) (offsetof(ittd_backend_api, f) + sizeof(api->f) <= api->size && api->f != NULL)
static int failures;
/* The capacity each count-then-fill below was given (clamp_count). */
static size_t n_cap, m_cap, nn_cap, wn_cap;

static double now_ms(void)
{
    static LARGE_INTEGER freq;
    LARGE_INTEGER t;
    if ( freq.QuadPart == 0 )
        QueryPerformanceFrequency(&freq);
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&t);
    return (double)t.QuadPart * 1000.0 / (double)freq.QuadPart;
}

static void check(int ok, const char *what)
{
    printf("  [%s] %s\n", ok ? "ok" : "FAIL", what);
    if ( !ok )
        failures++;
}

static const char *pos_text(ittd_position p)
{
    static char buf[4][64];
    static int k;
    char *b = buf[k++ & 3];
    if ( api->format_position != NULL )
        api->format_position(B, p, b, sizeof(buf[0]));
    else
        snprintf(b, sizeof(buf[0]), "%llx:%llx", (unsigned long long)p.hi, (unsigned long long)p.lo);
    return b;
}

static int is_none(ittd_position p) { return p.hi == UINT64_MAX && p.lo == UINT64_MAX; }

/* The position num/den of the way from a to b. Interpolating 'lo' alone is
   only right when both share 'hi' (Sogen: hi is 0); on a Microsoft recording
   hi is the sequence and lo the steps within it, so a position taken from
   one end's hi and an interpolated lo is not in the middle, and can wrap.
   Interpolates the sequence then, at its first step. */
static ittd_position pos_between(ittd_position a, ittd_position b, uint64_t num, uint64_t den)
{
    ittd_position p = a;
    if ( den == 0 || b.hi < a.hi || (b.hi == a.hi && b.lo <= a.lo) )
        return a;
    if ( b.hi == a.hi )
    {
        p.lo = a.lo + (b.lo - a.lo) / den * num;
        return p;
    }
    p.hi = a.hi + (uint64_t)((double)(b.hi - a.hi) * (double)num / (double)den);
    p.lo = p.hi == a.hi ? a.lo : 0;
    if ( p.hi == b.hi && p.lo > b.lo )
        p.lo = b.lo;
    return p;
}

/* About 'delta' instructions after p, through position_add when the backend
   has it; otherwise p itself. */
static ittd_position pos_plus(ittd_position p, int64_t delta)
{
    ittd_position out = p;
    if ( offsetof(ittd_backend_api, position_add) + sizeof(api->position_add) <= api->size
      && api->position_add != NULL && api->position_add(B, p, delta, &out) == ITTD_OK )
        return out;
    return p;
}

/* A count-then-fill answer must not report more entries than the buffer
   given holds (query_all clamps the same way): loops over the answer would
   read past it. Clamps, and fails a check when it had to. Always 1, so it
   can sit in a condition. */
static int clamp_count(size_t *n, size_t cap)
{
    if ( *n > cap )
    {
        check(0, "a fill reports no more entries than the buffer it was given holds");
        *n = cap;
    }
    return 1;
}

/* visit_positions bench: each visit reads its stack block into its slot
   (phase 0) and the same block just after it (phase 1). */
typedef struct visit_bench
{
    const ittd_mem_read *rd;
    uint8_t *at, *after, *at_known, *after_known;
    volatile long visits, afters;
} visit_bench;

static void visit_bench_fn(void *ud, size_t index, int phase, ittd_read_fn read, void *read_ctx)
{
    visit_bench *vb = (visit_bench *)ud;
    uint8_t *dst = phase == 0 ? vb->at : vb->after;
    uint8_t *kn  = phase == 0 ? vb->at_known : vb->after_known;
    size_t got = read(read_ctx, vb->rd[index].addr, dst + index * 256, 256), k;
    for ( k = 0; k < 256; k++ )
        kn[index * 256 + k] = k < got ? 1 : 0;
    InterlockedIncrement(phase == 0 ? &vb->visits : &vb->afters);
}

static uint64_t rip_at(ittd_cursor *c, ittd_position p)
{
    ittd_regs r;
    static int reported;
    if ( api->cursor_seek(c, p) != ITTD_OK || api->cursor_regs(c, &r) != ITTD_OK
      || (r.have & ITTD_REGS_GP) == 0 )
    {
        if ( !reported++ )
            printf("    (no registers at %s: %s)\n", pos_text(p), api->last_error(B));
        return ITTD_BADADDR;
    }
    return r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP];
}

/* Count-then-fill into a fresh array of 'size'-byte elements. */
static void *query_all(int (*count_fill)(void *buf, size_t cap, size_t *n), size_t size, size_t *n)
{
    void *buf;
    size_t cap;
    *n = 0;
    if ( count_fill(NULL, 0, n) != ITTD_OK )
    {
        *n = 0;         /* callers loop over *n even when the result is NULL */
        return NULL;
    }
    cap = *n;
    buf = calloc(cap ? cap : 1, size);
    if ( buf == NULL || count_fill(buf, cap, n) != ITTD_OK )
    {
        free(buf);
        *n = 0;
        return NULL;
    }
    /* A count that grew between the calls filled only what fit. */
    if ( *n > cap )
        *n = cap;
    return buf;
}

static int f_modules(void *b, size_t cap, size_t *n) { return api->modules(B, (ittd_module *)b, cap, n); }
static int f_threads(void *b, size_t cap, size_t *n) { return api->threads(B, (ittd_thread *)b, cap, n); }
static int f_timeline(void *b, size_t cap, size_t *n) { return api->timeline(B, (ittd_trace_event *)b, cap, n); }

static uint64_t g_symbase;
static int f_symbols(void *b, size_t cap, size_t *n) { return api->module_symbols(B, g_symbase, (ittd_symbol *)b, cap, n); }

/* The emulator's log (ittd_fork_settings::log): counted, and printed with
   ITTD_PROBE_LOG=1. */
static size_t g_log_lines;

static void probe_log(void *ctx, const char *line)
{
    ++*(size_t *)ctx;
    if ( getenv("ITTD_PROBE_LOG") != NULL )
        printf("  | %s\n", line);
}

static long long file_size_of(const char *path)
{
    WIN32_FILE_ATTRIBUTE_DATA a;
    if ( !GetFileAttributesExA(path, GetFileExInfoStandard, &a) )
        return -1;
    return ((long long)a.nFileSizeHigh << 32) | a.nFileSizeLow;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    const char *want = argc > 3 ? argv[3] : "RtlAllocateHeap";
    HMODULE dll;
    ittd_entry_point entry;
    ittd_trace_info info;
    ittd_module *mods;
    ittd_thread *thr;
    ittd_trace_event *tl;
    ittd_cursor *c;
    size_t nmods = 0, nthr = 0, ntl = 0, i;
    uint64_t target = ITTD_BADADDR;
    double t0;

    if ( argc < 3 )
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: ittd-probe BACKEND.dll TRACE [EXPORT]\n");
        return 2;
    }

    dll = LoadLibraryA(argv[1]);
    if ( dll == NULL )
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "could not load %s (error %lu)\n", argv[1], GetLastError());
        return 1;
    }
    entry = (ittd_entry_point)GetProcAddress(dll, ITTD_ENTRY_POINT_NAME);
    api = entry != NULL ? entry(ITTD_ABI_VERSION) : NULL;
    if ( api == NULL )
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "%s does not speak ABI version %u\n", argv[1], ITTD_ABI_VERSION);
        return 1;
    }
    printf("backend: %s (%s), filter \"%s\"\n", api->id(), api->display_name(), api->file_filter());

    /* ---- a new recording ----------------------------------------------------------
       ITTD_PROBE_RECORD=<exe>: record that program from its start into TRACE
       first (record_program), then probe the result. Its hives come from
       ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY, or ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ROOT names an emulation
       root; ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ARGS, ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_MAX (instructions),
       ITTD_PROBE_NET=1 (the real network), ITTD_PROBE_START_TIME (seconds
       since 1970 UTC) and ITTD_PROBE_LOG=1 (print the emulator's log) as
       named. */
    if ( getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD") != NULL )
    {
        ittd_record_request rq;
        ittd_fork_settings rs;
        uint64_t ran = 0;
        int rc;
        if ( !HAS(record_program) || api->record_program == NULL )
        {
            fprintf(stderr, "this backend cannot record\n");
            return 1;
        }
        memset(&rq, 0, sizeof(rq));
        rq.size = sizeof(rq);
        rq.application = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD");
        rq.arguments = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ARGS");
        rq.out_path = argv[2];
        rq.max_instructions = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_MAX") != NULL
                            ? strtoull(getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_MAX"), NULL, 0) : 0;
        /* Seconds since 1970 UTC; unset starts the run at 1970. */
        rq.start_time = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_START_TIME") != NULL
                      ? (int64_t)strtoll(getenv("ITTD_PROBE_START_TIME"), NULL, 0) : 0;
        memset(&rs, 0, sizeof(rs));
        rs.size = sizeof(rs);
        rs.flags = ITTD_FORK_ALLOW_HOST;
        rs.registry_dir = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_FORK_REGISTRY");
        rs.emulation_root = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_RECORD_ROOT");
        rs.network = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_NET") != NULL ? ITTD_NET_LIVE : ITTD_NET_OFFLINE;
        rs.elevated = getenv("ITTD_PROBE_ELEVATED") != NULL ? 1 : 0;
        rs.log = probe_log;
        rs.log_ctx = &g_log_lines;
        /* Without consent, nothing runs against this machine. */
        if ( rs.emulation_root == NULL )
        {
            rs.flags = 0;
            rc = api->record_program(&rq, &rs, NULL, &ran);
            check(rc == ITTD_E_HOST_REPLAY, "record_program against the host needs ITTD_FORK_ALLOW_HOST");
            rs.flags = ITTD_FORK_ALLOW_HOST;
        }
        t0 = now_ms();
        rc = api->record_program(&rq, &rs, NULL, &ran);
        printf("record %s into %s: %s, %llu instruction(s), %zu log line(s), %.1f ms\n", rq.application, rq.out_path,
               rc == ITTD_OK ? "ok" : api->last_error(NULL), (unsigned long long)ran, g_log_lines, now_ms() - t0);
        check(rc == ITTD_OK && ran > 0, "record_program records the program");
        if ( rc != ITTD_OK )
            return 1;
    }

    printf("can_open: %d\n", api->can_open(argv[2]));

    t0 = now_ms();
    B = api->open(argv[2]);
    if ( B == NULL )
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "open failed: %s\n", api->last_error(NULL));
        return 1;
    }
    printf("open: %.1f ms\n", now_ms() - t0);

    api->info(B, &info);
    printf("info: %s, %s, %d-bit, positions %s..%s, fingerprint %016llx, caps 0x%x\n",
           info.backend_name, info.main_module, info.is64 ? 64 : 32,
           pos_text(info.first), pos_text(info.last),
           (unsigned long long)info.fingerprint, info.capabilities);

    /* ---- ITTD_PROBE_PEEK=ADDR,POS: what touched 32 bytes at ADDR, and what
       they hold just before, at and after the position POS (its low part,
       as the probe prints positions), for chasing one address by hand. */
    if ( getenv("ITTD_PROBE_PEEK") != NULL )
    {
        char *end = NULL;
        uint64_t addr = strtoull(getenv("ITTD_PROBE_PEEK"), &end, 16);
        uint64_t lo = end != NULL && *end == ',' ? strtoull(end + 1, NULL, 0) : 0;
        ittd_access acc[64];
        ittd_position_range all;
        size_t na = 0, k;
        int trunc = 0;
        ittd_cursor *pc = api->cursor_open(B);
        /* The accesses in the 200 steps before POS and a few after. */
        all.first = info.first;
        all.last = info.last;
        all.first.lo = lo > 200 ? lo - 200 : 0;
        all.last.lo = lo + 5;
        if ( api->query_accesses(B, addr, addr + 32, ITTD_ACCESS_ALL, all, acc, 64, &na, &trunc, NULL) == ITTD_OK )
        {
            printf("peek %llx: %zu access(es)%s\n", (unsigned long long)addr, na, trunc ? " (first 64)" : "");
            for ( k = 0; k < na && k < 64; k++ )
                printf("  %s  %c %llx +%u by %llx tid %u\n", pos_text(acc[k].pos),
                       acc[k].kind == ITTD_ACCESS_READ ? 'r' : acc[k].kind == ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE ? 'w' : 'x',
                       (unsigned long long)acc[k].addr, acc[k].size, (unsigned long long)acc[k].pc, acc[k].tid);
        }
        for ( k = 0; pc != NULL && k < 3; k++ )
        {
            ittd_position p = info.first;
            uint8_t mem[32], kn[32];
            size_t j;
            double t_read;
            p.lo = lo + k - 1;
            if ( api->cursor_seek(pc, p) != ITTD_OK )
                continue;
            t_read = now_ms();
            if ( api->cursor_read_memory(pc, addr, mem, kn, sizeof(mem), NULL) != ITTD_OK )
                continue;
            printf("  at %s (%.1f ms):", pos_text(p), now_ms() - t_read);
            for ( j = 0; j < sizeof(mem); j++ )
                printf(kn[j] ? " %02x" : " ??", mem[j]);
            printf("\n");
            /* And what reading 0x400 bytes there costs, as IDA asks for after
               a stop (a slow one stalls single-stepping). */
            {
                static uint8_t big[0x400], bigk[0x400];
                size_t got = 0;
                double t1 = now_ms();
                api->cursor_read_memory(pc, addr & ~0xFFFull, big, bigk, sizeof(big), &got);
                printf("    0x400 bytes at %llx: %.1f ms, %zu known\n",
                       (unsigned long long)(addr & ~0xFFFull), now_ms() - t1, got);
            }
        }
        if ( pc != NULL )
            api->cursor_close(pc);
    }

    /* ---- modules, threads, timeline ---------------------------------- */
    mods = (ittd_module *)query_all(f_modules, sizeof(ittd_module), &nmods);
    printf("modules: %zu\n", nmods);
    for ( i = 0; i < nmods && i < 8; i++ )
        printf("  %016llx %8llx machine %04x  %s\n", (unsigned long long)mods[i].base,
               (unsigned long long)mods[i].size, mods[i].machine, mods[i].name);

    thr = (ittd_thread *)query_all(f_threads, sizeof(ittd_thread), &nthr);
    printf("threads: %zu\n", nthr);
    for ( i = 0; i < nthr && i < 6; i++ )
        printf("  tid %u  %s..%s  teb %llx  stack %llx..%llx  %s\n", thr[i].tid,
               pos_text(thr[i].created), pos_text(thr[i].exited),
               (unsigned long long)thr[i].teb, (unsigned long long)thr[i].stack_limit,
               (unsigned long long)thr[i].stack_base, thr[i].name);

    t0 = now_ms();
    tl = (ittd_trace_event *)query_all(f_timeline, sizeof(ittd_trace_event), &ntl);
    printf("timeline: %zu event(s) in %.1f ms\n", ntl, now_ms() - t0);
    for ( i = 0; i < ntl && i < 5; i++ )
        printf("  %s  %s\n", pos_text(tl[i].pos), tl[i].text);

    /* ---- the export whose calls are listed ------------------------------ */
    /* Or an address, for a backend that records no exports (Microsoft TTD). */
    if ( want[0] == '0' && (want[1] == 'x' || want[1] == 'X') )
    {
        target = strtoull(want + 2, NULL, 16);
        printf("calls to the function at %llx\n", (unsigned long long)target);
    }
    for ( i = 0; i < nmods && target == ITTD_BADADDR; i++ )
    {
        size_t ns = 0, k;
        ittd_symbol *syms;
        g_symbase = mods[i].base;
        syms = (ittd_symbol *)query_all(f_symbols, sizeof(ittd_symbol), &ns);
        for ( k = 0; syms != NULL && k < ns; k++ )
            if ( strcmp(syms[k].name, want) == 0 )
            {
                target = syms[k].ea;
                printf("export %s!%s at %llx (%zu exports in the module)\n",
                       mods[i].name, want, (unsigned long long)target, ns);
                break;
            }
        free(syms);
    }

    c = api->cursor_open(B);
    if ( c == NULL )
    {
        fprintf(stderr, "cursor_open failed: %s\n", api->last_error(B));
        return 1;
    }

    /* ---- positions and registers ------------------------------------------ */
    printf("\npositions\n");
    {
        ittd_position mid = pos_between(info.first, info.last, 1, 2), here;
        ittd_regs r;
        uint32_t tid = 0;
        int stop = -1;
        uint8_t bytes[16], known[16];
        size_t nk = 0;

        check(api->cursor_seek(c, mid) == ITTD_OK, "seek to the middle");
        /* The middle may be a sequence's first step (Microsoft: a key frame,
           where the next instruction can be in another sequence): the checks
           below start a few instructions on, where a step is one position. */
        api->nav_step(c, 4, &stop);
        api->cursor_position(c, &mid);
        stop = -1;
        t0 = now_ms();
        check(api->cursor_seek(c, mid) == ITTD_OK, "seek to a position near the middle");
        memset(&r, 0, sizeof(r));
        if ( api->cursor_regs(c, &r) != ITTD_OK )
            printf("  registers: %s\n", api->last_error(B));
        check((r.have & ITTD_REGS_GP) != 0, "registers there");
        printf("  regs at %s: %.1f ms, rip %llx rsp %llx\n", pos_text(mid), now_ms() - t0,
               (unsigned long long)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP], (unsigned long long)r.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP]);
        api->cursor_thread(c, &tid);
        printf("  thread %u\n", tid);

        t0 = now_ms();
        memset(bytes, 0, sizeof(bytes));
        memset(known, 0, sizeof(known));    /* printed below even if the read fails */
        api->cursor_read_memory(c, r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP], bytes, known, sizeof(bytes), &nk);
        printf("  16 bytes at rip, %zu known, %.1f ms:", nk, now_ms() - t0);
        for ( i = 0; i < 16; i++ )
            printf(known[i] ? " %02x" : " ??", bytes[i]);
        printf("\n");
        check(nk > 0, "the instruction at rip is readable");

        /* The access at this position must be done by the instruction at rip. */
        {
            ittd_access acc[8];
            size_t n = 0;
            int trunc = 0;
            ittd_position_range when;
            when.first = mid;
            when.last  = mid;
            /* the position just before an instruction runs, to the one after it */
            when.last.lo = mid.lo + 1;
            api->query_accesses(B, r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP], r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP] + 1, ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC,
                                when, acc, 8, &n, &trunc, NULL);
            check(n >= 1 && acc[0].pc == r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP] && acc[0].pos.lo == mid.lo,
                  "the execute event of the instruction at rip is at this position");
        }

        /* The instruction stream from here starts with the instruction at rip. */
        if ( HAS(query_instructions) )
        {
            ittd_access ins[16];
            ittd_position_range w;
            size_t n = 0;
            int trunc = 0;
            uint32_t tid2 = 0;
            w.first = mid;
            w.last.hi = UINT64_MAX;
            w.last.lo = UINT64_MAX - 1;
            api->cursor_thread(c, &tid2);
            t0 = now_ms();
            api->query_instructions(B, w, tid2, ins, 16, &n, &trunc, NULL);
            printf("  16 instructions from here on thread %u: %zu, %.1f ms\n", tid2, n, now_ms() - t0);
            check(n == 16 && trunc && ins[0].pc == r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP] && ins[0].pos.lo == mid.lo,
                  "the instruction stream starts here, with the instruction at rip");
        }

        api->nav_step(c, 1, &stop);
        api->cursor_position(c, &here);
        printf("  a step from %s", pos_text(mid));
        printf(" lands at %s (stop %d)\n", pos_text(here), stop);
        check(here.hi == mid.hi && here.lo == mid.lo + 1 && stop == ITTD_STOP_STEPPED,
              "a forward step moves one position");
        api->nav_step(c, 0, &stop);
        api->cursor_position(c, &here);
        check(here.lo == mid.lo, "and a backward step moves back");

        /* An execute breakpoint on the instruction a step starts from: the
           step still executes it. IDA sets one there itself when stepping
           from pseudocode; stopping in place read as a breakpoint hit, and
           IDA's statement stepping then ran on to the end of the recording. */
        if ( api->nav_breakpoints != NULL )
        {
            ittd_breakpoint bp;
            memset(&bp, 0, sizeof(bp));
            bp.addr  = r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP];
            bp.size  = 1;
            bp.kinds = ITTD_ACCESS_EXEC;
            api->nav_breakpoints(c, &bp, 1);
            stop = -1;
            api->nav_step(c, 1, &stop);
            api->cursor_position(c, &here);
            api->nav_breakpoints(c, NULL, 0);
            printf("  step from an execute breakpoint on rip: stop %d at %s\n", stop, pos_text(here));
            check(here.lo == mid.lo + 1 && stop == ITTD_STOP_STEPPED,
                  "a step from an instruction with a breakpoint on it moves one position");
            api->cursor_seek(c, mid);
        }

        /* run to the instruction at rip again, from just past it */
        api->nav_step(c, 1, &stop);
        t0 = now_ms();
        api->nav_run_to(c, r.gp[ITTD_REG_RIP], 0, &stop);
        api->cursor_position(c, &here);
        printf("  run back to rip: stop %d at %s, %.1f ms\n", stop, pos_text(here), now_ms() - t0);
        check(here.lo == mid.lo && stop == ITTD_STOP_STEPPED, "running backward to rip lands on this position");

        /* What tracing a register's origin costs: single steps backward, which
           must stay on one thread. ITTD_PROBE_BACKSTEPS=N. */
        if ( getenv("ITTD_PROBE_BACKSTEPS") != NULL )
        {
            unsigned long steps = strtoul(getenv("ITTD_PROBE_BACKSTEPS"), NULL, 0), k, changed = 0;
            uint32_t tid0 = 0, tidk = 0;
            int same_thread = 1;
            ittd_regs prev = r, now_regs;
            api->cursor_thread(c, &tid0);
            t0 = now_ms();
            for ( k = 0; k < steps; k++ )
            {
                if ( api->nav_step(c, 0, &stop) != ITTD_OK || stop != ITTD_STOP_STEPPED )
                    break;
                api->cursor_thread(c, &tidk);
                same_thread &= tidk == tid0;
                api->cursor_regs(c, &now_regs);
                changed += now_regs.gp[ITTD_REG_RAX] != prev.gp[ITTD_REG_RAX];
                prev = now_regs;
            }
            printf("  %lu backward steps: %.3f ms each, rax changed %lu times\n",
                   k, k ? (now_ms() - t0) / (double)k : 0.0, changed);
            check(same_thread, "backward single steps stay on the thread");
            api->cursor_seek(c, mid);

            /* query_register_change against stepping back: the first step
               back where the register differs is the instruction that set it. */
            if ( offsetof(ittd_backend_api, query_register_change) + sizeof(api->query_register_change) <= api->size
              && api->query_register_change != NULL )
            {
                static const uint32_t regs[] = { ITTD_REG_RAX, ITTD_REG_RBX, ITTD_REG_RSI, ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0 };
                size_t q;
                for ( q = 0; q < sizeof(regs) / sizeof(regs[0]); q++ )
                {
                    ittd_position got, first_change;
                    int found = 0, rc;
                    unsigned long s;
                    const uint32_t reg = regs[q];
                    const int xmm = reg >= ITTD_ORIGIN_XMM0;
                    t0 = now_ms();
                    rc = api->query_register_change(B, mid, tid0, reg, 1000000, &got, &found, NULL);
                    printf("  last change of register %u: rc %d, found %d at %s, %.1f ms\n",
                           reg, rc, found, found ? pos_text(got) : "-", now_ms() - t0);
                    first_change.hi = first_change.lo = UINT64_MAX;
                    api->cursor_seek(c, mid);
                    for ( s = 0; s < steps; s++ )
                    {
                        if ( api->nav_step(c, 0, &stop) != ITTD_OK || stop != ITTD_STOP_STEPPED )
                            break;
                        api->cursor_regs(c, &now_regs);
                        if ( xmm ? memcmp(now_regs.xmm[0], r.xmm[0], 16) != 0
                                 : now_regs.gp[reg] != r.gp[reg] )
                        {
                            api->cursor_position(c, &first_change);
                            break;
                        }
                    }
                    api->cursor_seek(c, mid);
                    if ( first_change.hi != UINT64_MAX )
                        check(rc == ITTD_OK && found && got.hi == first_change.hi && got.lo == first_change.lo,
                              "  the register's last change is the one stepping back finds");
                    else
                        printf("  (no change within %lu steps back to compare)\n", steps);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /* ---- calls -------------------------------------------------------------- */
    if ( target != ITTD_BADADDR )
    {
        ittd_position_range all;
        ittd_call *calls;
        size_t n = 0, with_ret = 0, k;
        int trunc = 0;
        all.first.hi = 0; all.first.lo = 0;
        all.last.hi = UINT64_MAX; all.last.lo = UINT64_MAX - 1;

        printf("\ncalls to %s\n", want);
        t0 = now_ms();
        api->query_calls(B, &target, 1, all, NULL, 0, &n, &trunc, NULL);
        n_cap = n;
        calls = (ittd_call *)calloc(n ? n : 1, sizeof(ittd_call));
        api->query_calls(B, &target, 1, all, calls, n, &n, &trunc, NULL);
        clamp_count(&n, n_cap);
        for ( k = 0; k < n; k++ )
            if ( !is_none(calls[k].ret_pos) )
                with_ret++;
        printf("  %zu call(s), %zu with a return, %.1f ms\n", n, with_ret, now_ms() - t0);

        for ( k = 0; k < n && k < 3; k++ )
        {
            ittd_call *e = &calls[k];
            uint64_t at_pos = is_none(e->pos) ? ITTD_BADADDR : rip_at(c, e->pos);
            uint64_t at_entry = rip_at(c, e->entry_pos);
            uint64_t at_ret = is_none(e->ret_pos) ? ITTD_BADADDR : rip_at(c, e->ret_pos);
            ittd_regs r;
            printf("  #%zu tid %u site %llx pos %s entry %s ret %s%s\n", k, e->tid,
                   (unsigned long long)e->site, pos_text(e->pos), pos_text(e->entry_pos),
                   pos_text(e->ret_pos), (e->flags & ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL) ? " (jump)" : "");
            int is_call = (e->flags & ITTD_CALL_F_NOT_CALL) == 0;
            if ( !is_none(e->pos) )
                check(at_pos == e->site, "  rip at pos is the call site");
            check(at_entry == e->target, "  rip at entry_pos is the target");
            /* At the callee's first instruction, the frame was entered by this
               very call. */
            if ( k == 0 && !is_none(e->pos) && is_call && HAS(query_frame_entry) )
            {
                ittd_position fc;
                uint64_t fe = 0;
                int rc = api->query_frame_entry(B, e->entry_pos, e->tid, 0x10000, &fc, &fe);
                printf("    frame entry from entry_pos: rc %d, call at %s, entry %llx\n",
                       rc, pos_text(fc), (unsigned long long)fe);
                check(rc == ITTD_OK && fc.lo == e->pos.lo && fe == e->target,
                      "  the frame at entry_pos was entered by this call");
                /* The cancellable entry answers the same. */
                if ( HAS(query_frame_entry_progress) )
                {
                    ittd_position fc2;
                    uint64_t fe2 = 0;
                    int rc2 = api->query_frame_entry_progress(B, e->entry_pos, e->tid, 0x10000, &fc2, &fe2, NULL);
                    check(rc2 == rc && fc2.hi == fc.hi && fc2.lo == fc.lo && fe2 == fe,
                          "  query_frame_entry_progress answers as query_frame_entry");
                }
            }
            /* A write breakpoint on the slot the call pushes its return address
               into stops at the call, run forward from just before it. */
            if ( k == 0 && !is_none(e->pos) && is_call && e->pos.lo > 0 && api->nav_breakpoints != NULL )
            {
                ittd_regs rr;
                ittd_breakpoint bp;
                ittd_position before = e->pos, landed;
                int stop = -1;
                memset(&bp, 0, sizeof(bp));
                api->cursor_seek(c, e->pos);
                if ( api->cursor_regs(c, &rr) == ITTD_OK )
                {
                    bp.addr  = rr.gp[ITTD_REG_RSP] - 8;
                    bp.size  = 8;
                    bp.kinds = ITTD_ACCESS_WRITE;
                    before.lo = e->pos.lo - 1;
                    api->cursor_seek(c, before);
                    api->nav_breakpoints(c, &bp, 1);
                    api->nav_run(c, 1, &stop);
                    api->cursor_position(c, &landed);
                    api->nav_breakpoints(c, NULL, 0);
                    printf("    write breakpoint on [rsp-8, rsp): stop %d at %s\n", stop, pos_text(landed));
```
