`src/ui/decompiler.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "ui/decompiler.h"
#include "analysis/coverage.h"
#include "analysis/callsites.h"

// hexrays.hpp is the one SDK header that warns at this project's level
// (narrowing and a signed/unsigned compare, in inline code the plugin never
// calls). Silence it around the include only, so the plugin's own code stays
// held to a clean build.
#pragma warning(push)
#pragma warning(disable: 4018)  // signed/unsigned mismatch
#pragma warning(disable: 4244)  // conversion, possible loss of data
#pragma warning(disable: 4267)  // size_t -> int, possible loss of data
#include <hexrays.hpp>
#pragma warning(pop)

namespace idattd
{
    static bool g_hooked           = false;
    static bool g_reported_missing = false;
    static void (*g_edit_hook)(ea_t) = nullptr;

    void set_function_edit_hook(void (*hook)(ea_t func_ea))
    {
        g_edit_hook = hook;
    }

    // What a paint reads changes only with an item's color or comment, so
    // the stop-time repaint is skipped for a view painted since the last
    // such change. Any writer counts (a sweep, an annotation, the user, a
    // script): the database's own events bump the generation, rather than
    // each of the plugin's writers remembering to.
    static uint64_t g_paint_generation = 1;
    // The generation each function's text was last painted at. Keyed by the
    // cfunc_t: regenerated text is painted on hxe_func_printed and recorded
    // again, so a stale entry is never trusted for new text.
    static std::map<const cfunc_t *, uint64_t> g_painted_at;

    struct PaintInputsListener : public event_listener_t
    {
        ssize_t idaapi on_event(ssize_t code, va_list) override
        {
            if ( code == idb_event::item_color_changed || code == idb_event::cmt_changed )
                g_paint_generation++;
            return 0;
        }
    };
    static PaintInputsListener g_paint_inputs;

    // Every address a pseudocode line was decompiled from.
    //
    // Generated pseudocode carries invisible COLOR_ADDR tags holding ctree
    // anchors (indices into cfunc_t::treeitems, each of which knows its
    // address); hxe_func_printed documents this. get_line_item() is no
    // substitute: it answers for one column, and column zero is indentation,
    // which belongs to no item.
    //
    // All anchors, not just the first: one line holds many items (statement,
    // assigned variable, call, arguments) from different instructions. In
    // "v11 = v7(...)" the first anchor is the assignment, while the call's
    // annotation is on the call instruction a few bytes earlier.
    //
    // 'items', when given, receives the items themselves.
    static void line_addresses(const cfunc_t *cf, const char *line,
                               std::vector<ea_t> &out,
                               std::vector<const citem_t *> *items = nullptr)
    {
        out.clear();
        if ( items != nullptr )
            items->clear();
        // Caps a pathological line, since this runs on every repaint.
        static const size_t kMaxPerLine = 32;

        for ( const char *p = line; p[0] != '\0' && out.size() < kMaxPerLine; )
        {
            if ( p[0] != COLOR_ON || p[1] != (char)COLOR_ADDR )
            {
                p++;
                continue;
            }
            // COLOR_ON, the tag byte, then COLOR_ADDR_SIZE hex digits, with no
            // closing COLOR_OFF. A truncated tag ends the scan.
            uval_t v  = 0;
            bool   ok = true;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < COLOR_ADDR_SIZE; i++ )
            {
                char c = p[2 + i];
                int  d;
                if ( c >= '0' && c <= '9' )      d = c - '0';
                else if ( c >= 'A' && c <= 'F' ) d = c - 'A' + 10;
                else if ( c >= 'a' && c <= 'f' ) d = c - 'a' + 10;
                else { ok = false; break; }
                v = (v << 4) | (uval_t)d;
            }
            if ( !ok )
                break;
            p += 2 + COLOR_ADDR_SIZE;

            ctree_anchor_t anc;
            anc.value = v;
            if ( !anc.is_citem_anchor() )
                continue;                   // a local variable, not a statement
            int idx = anc.get_index();
            if ( idx < 0 || (size_t)idx >= cf->treeitems.size() )
                continue;
            const citem_t *it = cf->treeitems[idx];
            if ( it == nullptr || it->ea == BADADDR )
                continue;
            if ( items != nullptr )
                items->push_back(it);
            // Colors and comments live on item heads, and an item's address
            // need not be one.
            ea_t ea = it->ea;
            ea_t head = get_item_head(ea);
            if ( head != BADADDR )
                ea = head;
            if ( std::find(out.begin(), out.end(), ea) == out.end() )
                out.push_back(ea);
        }
    }

    // Marks a line that already carries the plugin's note, so repainting the
    // same text does not append it again.
    static const char TTD_CMT_MARK[] = "// TTD: ";

    // Whether 'joined' (notes separated by "; ") already holds 'note' as a
    // whole entry. A substring test would drop "-> foo" next to
    // "-> foo_impl". A note may itself contain "; " (a flattened
    // multi-target note), so it is matched as one unit at entry boundaries
    // rather than by splitting.
    static bool has_note(const qstring &joined, const char *note)
    {
        const size_t n = strlen(note);
        if ( n == 0 )
            return true;
        for ( size_t at = joined.find(note); at != qstring::npos; at = joined.find(note, at + 1) )
        {
            const bool starts = at == 0 || (at >= 2 && joined[at - 2] == ';' && joined[at - 1] == ' ');
            const size_t end = at + n;
            const bool ends = end == joined.length()
                           || (end + 1 < joined.length() && joined[end] == ';' && joined[end + 1] == ' ');
            if ( starts && ends )
                return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // The text of the function's lines that show a note already, without
    // color tags, one per line. From 9.5 Hex-Rays prints a call
    // instruction's repeatable comment itself, the annotation's note
    // included; before, it printed none. It puts the comment wherever its own
    // map of instructions to statements says, which is often not a line
    // naming the call: a neighbouring statement, or a comment line of its own
    // above it. So what it shows is matched by text, over the whole function,
    // and those notes are not added a second time. Notes the plugin appended
    // in an earlier paint are in it too, which keeps a repaint from adding
    // one again on an earlier line naming the same call.
    static qstring notes_already_shown(const cfunc_t *cf)
    {
        qstring shown, text;
        for ( const simpleline_t &sl : cf->sv )
        {
            // Cheap first: the note's prefix survives the color tags whole.
            if ( strstr(sl.line.c_str(), "TTD: ") == nullptr )
                continue;
            tag_remove(&text, sl.line.c_str());
            shown.append(text);
            shown.append('\n');
        }
        return shown;
    }

    // Whether 'shown' holds the note whose first line is 'note' as a whole
    // note: "calls a!foo" must not count as shown because of "calls a!foo_impl".
    static bool note_shown(const qstring &shown, const qstring &note)
    {
        if ( note.empty() || shown.empty() )
            return false;
        for ( const char *at = strstr(shown.c_str(), note.c_str()); at != nullptr;
              at = strstr(at + 1, note.c_str()) )
        {
            const char end = at[note.length()];
            if ( end == '\0' || end == '\n' || end == ' ' || end == ';' )
                return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // Show the annotation an indirect call site carries on its pseudocode line,
    // unless the function's text shows it already (notes_already_shown).
    static void append_ttd_comments(simpleline_t &sl, const std::vector<ea_t> &eas,
                                    std::set<ea_t> &already, const qstring &shown)
    {
        // Painted by an earlier pass (every open or refresh of a cached view
        // paints again). Its call sites still count as annotated; otherwise
        // the next line naming the same call (an argument on its own line)
        // would take the note too, one line further down per repaint.
        if ( strstr(sl.line.c_str(), TTD_CMT_MARK) != nullptr )
        {
            already.insert(eas.begin(), eas.end());
            return;
        }

        // A line with two indirect calls shows both notes; identical notes
        // are shown once.
        qstring joined;
        for ( ea_t ea : eas )
        {
            // A call with one argument per line names the same instruction on
            // each of those lines; the note goes on the first only.
            if ( already.find(ea) != already.end() )
                continue;

            // The flag first: most anchors have no comment, and this runs
            // for every line on every repaint.
            qstring full;
            if ( !has_cmt(get_flags(ea)) || get_cmt(&full, ea, true) <= 0 || full.empty() )
                continue;
            // Only the annotation's note, which follows the user's own text
            // when the site has some.
            qstring cmt = ttd_call_note(full);
            if ( cmt.empty() )
                continue;
            if ( note_shown(shown, qstring(cmt.c_str(), strcspn(cmt.c_str(), "\r\n"))) )
            {
                already.insert(ea);
                continue;                          // Hex-Rays prints it
            }

            qstring flat;
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < cmt.length(); i++ )
            {
                char c = cmt[i];
                if ( c == '\n' || c == '\r' )
                {
                    // A newline inside a simpleline_t corrupts the view, so a
                    // multi-target note is flattened: collapse the run of line
                    // breaks and the indentation after it.
                    if ( !flat.empty() && !flat.ends_with("; ") )
                        flat.append("; ");
                    while ( i + 1 < cmt.length() && (cmt[i + 1] == ' ' || cmt[i + 1] == '\n'
                                                  || cmt[i + 1] == '\r' || cmt[i + 1] == '\t') )
                        i++;
                    continue;
                }
                flat.append(c);
            }
            const char *body = flat.c_str() + 5;   // past the "TTD: " prefix
            already.insert(ea);
            if ( has_note(joined, body) )
                continue;                          // same note twice on one line
            if ( !joined.empty() )
                joined.append("; ");
            joined.append(body);
        }
        if ( joined.empty() )
            return;

        // Not the automatic comment color: too dim on a coverage color.
        sl.line.append("  ");
        sl.line.append(SCOLOR_ON);
        sl.line.append(SCOLOR_REGCMT);
        sl.line.append(TTD_CMT_MARK);
        sl.line.append(joined);
        sl.line.append(SCOLOR_OFF);
        sl.line.append(SCOLOR_REGCMT);
    }

    // The if statement a conditional move at 'ea' became, when 'it' is part
    // of one, else nullptr. Hex-Rays can write one CMOVcc as a whole if:
    // the condition and the assignment in the body are then both items of
    // that instruction, and the condition has its address. '*in_branch' says
    // whether 'it' is in the then or else branch (the assignment the move
    // makes, which only happens when the condition holds) rather than the
    // condition itself (which always runs).
    static const cinsn_t *cmov_if_of(const cfunc_t *cf, const citem_t *it, ea_t ea, bool *in_branch)
    {
        *in_branch = false;
        if ( it->op == cit_if && ((const cinsn_t *)it)->cif->expr.ea == ea )
            return (const cinsn_t *)it;
        const citem_t *child = it;
        for ( const citem_t *p = cf->body.find_parent_of(child);
              p != nullptr;
              child = p, p = cf->body.find_parent_of(p) )
        {
            if ( p->op != cit_if )
                continue;
            const cinsn_t *ifs = (const cinsn_t *)p;
            const cif_t *ci = ifs->cif;
            if ( ci->expr.ea != ea )
                continue;                   // another if, around this one
            *in_branch = child == ci->ithen || child == ci->ielse;
            return ifs;
        }
        return nullptr;
    }

    // Whether a line is the body of an if made from a conditional move that
    // never moved in this recording ('untaken'): the instruction ran, so
    // coverage holds it, but what the line says never happened.
    static bool in_untaken_branch(const cfunc_t *cf, const std::vector<const citem_t *> &items,
                                  const std::set<ea_t> &untaken)
    {
        for ( const citem_t *it : items )
        {
            if ( untaken.count(it->ea) == 0 )
                continue;
            bool in_branch = false;
            if ( cmov_if_of(cf, it, it->ea, &in_branch) != nullptr && in_branch )
                return true;
        }
        return false;
    }

    // On a coverage color, dim gray text (Hex-Rays' argument names) in the
    // normal text color, so it stays readable.
    static void brighten_dim_text(qstring &line)
    {
        for ( size_t i = 0; i + 1 < line.length(); i++ )
        {
            if ( (line[i] == COLOR_ON || line[i] == COLOR_OFF) && line[i + 1] == COLOR_AUTOCMT )
                line[i + 1] = COLOR_DEFAULT;
            else if ( line[i] == COLOR_ON && line[i + 1] == COLOR_ADDR )
                i += 1 + COLOR_ADDR_SIZE;   // skip an address tag's digits
        }
    }

    // Paint one function's pseudocode from the colors already in the database.
    // A line is covered when an address it came from carries one of the
    // plugin's coverage colors, and takes that color, so a database
    // highlighted in two shades reads the same here as in the disassembly.
    // The exception is the body of an if made from a conditional move that
    // never moved (in_untaken_branch), which is left unpainted.
    //
    // True when a line lost its coverage color: its text was brightened in
    // place (brighten_dim_text), and only regenerating it brings back the
    // dim argument names.
    static bool paint(cfunc_t *cf)
    {
        if ( cf == nullptr )
            return false;
        bool uncovered = false;
        // Both sets once per paint: each is a netnode walk.
        std::set<bgcolor_t> previous, only_here;
        std::set<bgcolor_t> ours = coverage_colors(&previous, &only_here);
        std::vector<ea_t>   eas;              // reused; no per-line allocation
        // Call sites whose note is already placed (see append_ttd_comments).
        std::set<ea_t>      annotated;
        // The function's conditional moves that never moved, and so the
        // lines' items, needed only when there are some.
        std::set<ea_t> untaken;
        func_entry_info_t fi;
        if ( get_func_entry_info(&fi, cf->entry_ea) )
            untaken = untaken_conditional_moves(fi.start_ea, fi.end_ea);
        std::vector<const citem_t *> items;
        const qstring shown = notes_already_shown(cf);

        for ( size_t i = 0; i < cf->sv.size(); i++ )
        {
            simpleline_t &sl = cf->sv[i];

            // Clear only the plugin's colors first: a line no longer covered
            // (sweep cleared, shade changed) loses a stale highlight, and a
            // color set by something else is left alone.
            const bool was_ours = ours.find(sl.bgcolor) != ours.end();
            if ( was_ours )
                sl.bgcolor = DEFCOLOR;

            line_addresses(cf, sl.line.c_str(), eas, untaken.empty() ? nullptr : &items);
            if ( eas.empty() )
                continue;
            if ( !untaken.empty() && in_untaken_branch(cf, items, untaken) )
            {
                if ( was_ours )
                    uncovered = true;
                append_ttd_comments(sl, eas, annotated, shown);
                continue;
            }

            // Covered if any instruction it came from ran. Where they differ,
            // a difference wins: ran only in this recording first, then only
            // in the other one (a fork's parent, or a fork), then in both.
            int rank = 0;
            for ( ea_t ea : eas )
            {
                bgcolor_t c = get_item_color(ea);
                if ( c == DEFCOLOR || ours.find(c) == ours.end() )
                    continue;
                // "Both" ranks with plain coverage: lowest.
                const int r = only_here.count(c) != 0 ? 3 : previous.count(c) != 0 ? 2 : 1;
                if ( r > rank )
                {
                    rank = r;
                    sl.bgcolor = c;
                }
                if ( rank == 3 )
                    break;
            }
            if ( sl.bgcolor != DEFCOLOR )
                brighten_dim_text(sl.line);
            else if ( was_ours )
                uncovered = true;

            append_ttd_comments(sl, eas, annotated, shown);
        }
        // A function printed and dropped again would leave its entry behind;
        // the map only needs the open views, so an overgrown one is reset.
        if ( g_painted_at.size() > 256 )
            g_painted_at.clear();
        g_painted_at[cf] = g_paint_generation;
        return uncovered;
    }

    static ssize_t idaapi hx_callback(void *, hexrays_event_t ev, va_list va)
    {
        switch ( ev )
        {
            case hxe_func_printed:
                // The text has just been generated; sv may be colored now.
                paint(va_arg(va, cfunc_t *));
                break;

            // Variable edits: the view's function changed.
            case lxe_lvar_name_changed:
            case lxe_lvar_type_changed:
            case lxe_lvar_cmt_changed:
            case lxe_lvar_mapping_changed:
            {
                vdui_t *vu = va_arg(va, vdui_t *);
                if ( g_edit_hook != nullptr && vu != nullptr && vu->cfunc != nullptr )
                    g_edit_hook(vu->cfunc->entry_ea);
                break;
            }
            case hxe_cmt_changed:
            {
                cfunc_t *cf = va_arg(va, cfunc_t *);
                if ( g_edit_hook != nullptr && cf != nullptr )
                    g_edit_hook(cf->entry_ea);
                break;
            }

            case hxe_open_pseudocode:
            case hxe_refresh_pseudocode:
            {
                // A cached decompilation was printed before the function was
                // highlighted, and raises no hxe_func_printed: paint it here.
                vdui_t *vu = va_arg(va, vdui_t *);
                if ( vu != nullptr && vu->cfunc != nullptr )
                    paint(vu->cfunc);
                break;
            }

            default:
                break;
        }
        return 0;
    }

    // Cheap, and called repeatedly on purpose. Hex-Rays is itself a plugin, and
    // while this plugmod is being constructed init_hexrays_plugin() can still
    // report no decompiler. Like the SDK samples, this is retried at each
    // point of use: session start and every stop.
    bool init_decompiler()
    {
        if ( g_hooked )
            return true;
        if ( !init_hexrays_plugin() )
        {
            // Say so once: silence would look like broken painting.
            if ( !g_reported_missing )
            {
                g_reported_missing = true;
                msg("[ida-ttd] no decompiler available yet: pseudocode will not be "
                    "highlighted. (Retried at every stop; this is only said once.)\n");
            }
            return false;
        }
        g_hooked = install_hexrays_callback(hx_callback, nullptr);
        if ( g_hooked )
            hook_event_listener(HT_IDB, &g_paint_inputs, nullptr);
        msg("[ida-ttd] decompiler found: pseudocode %s follow the execution "
            "highlight.\n", g_hooked ? "will" : "could NOT be hooked to");
        return g_hooked;
    }

    void term_decompiler()
    {
        if ( g_hooked )
        {
            remove_hexrays_callback(hx_callback, nullptr);
            unhook_event_listener(HT_IDB, &g_paint_inputs);
            g_painted_at.clear();
            g_hooked = false;
        }
    }

    void pseudocode_paint_inputs_changed()
    {
        g_paint_generation++;
    }

    void refresh_pseudocode_views()
    {
        if ( !g_hooked )
            return;
        // Ask IDA for the open views rather than remember those seen opening:
        // a view that predates the hook was never seen, and needs the repaint
        // most.
        std::vector<TWidget *> views;
        list_pseudocode_views(views);
        for ( TWidget *w : views )
        {
            vdui_t *vu = get_widget_vdui(w);
            if ( vu == nullptr || vu->cfunc == nullptr )
                continue;
            // Nothing a paint reads has changed since this text was painted
            // (most stops: the highlight was already there).
            auto done = g_painted_at.find(vu->cfunc);
            if ( done != g_painted_at.end() && done->second == g_paint_generation )
                continue;

            // Repaint the text the view already shows, then redraw the widget.
            // A decompiler refresh only regenerates the text, so the highlight
            // did not appear until something else redrew the window; and only
            // colors and notes changed, so regenerating would be wasted work.
            // A line that lost its highlight (coverage cleared) keeps the
            // brightened text: regenerate the text then, which paints it
            // again from scratch (hxe_func_printed), no decompiling.
            if ( paint(vu->cfunc) )
                vu->refresh_ctext(false);
            refresh_custom_viewer(vu->ct);
        }
    }

    // Pseudocode windows are titled Pseudocode-A onwards.
    void list_pseudocode_views(std::vector<TWidget *> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        for ( char c = 'A'; c <= 'Z'; c++ )
        {
            char title[16];
            qsnprintf(title, sizeof(title), "Pseudocode-%c", c);
            TWidget *w = find_widget(title);
            if ( w != nullptr && get_widget_type(w) == BWN_PSEUDOCODE )
                out.push_back(w);
        }
    }

    ea_t pseudocode_function(TWidget *view)
    {
        if ( !g_hooked || view == nullptr )
            return BADADDR;
        vdui_t *vu = get_widget_vdui(view);
        if ( vu == nullptr || vu->cfunc == nullptr )
            return BADADDR;
        return vu->cfunc->entry_ea;
    }

    bool can_decompile(ea_t func_ea)
    {
        if ( !g_hooked )
            return false;
        hexrays_failure_t hf;
        return decompile_function(func_ea, &hf, DECOMP_NO_WAIT) != nullptr;
    }

    // Put the caret of a pseudocode view on line 'line', column 'x'.
    //
    // The place comes from the view's own: a pseudocode view's position is a
    // hexrays_place_t, larger than simpleline_place_t, and Hex-Rays reads the
    // rest of it (the function among other things). Jumping with a
    // simpleline_place_t made IDA store that smaller object as the view's
    // position, and Hex-Rays then read past its end: decompilations of
    // "<garbage>: bad input ranges" on every step from pseudocode, crashes,
    // and a database whose saved window position crashed IDA on reopening.
    static void jump_to_line(TWidget *ct, int line, int x)
    {
        const place_t *cur = get_custom_viewer_place(ct, false, nullptr, nullptr);
        if ( cur == nullptr )
            return;
        void *ud = get_viewer_user_data(ct);
        place_t *pl = cur->makeplace(ud, (uval_t)line, 0);
        if ( pl == nullptr )
            return;
        jumpto(ct, pl, x, 0);
        // Whether makeplace() handed over a new object or a static one
        // depends on the class.
        int flags = 0;
        if ( get_place_class(&flags, nullptr, pl->id()) != nullptr
          && (flags & PCF_MAKEPLACE_ALLOCATES) != 0 )
        {
            delete pl;
        }
    }

    // The statement the caret goes to for the instruction at 'ea'.
    //
    // The candidates are the items made from exactly that instruction.
    // Without any (most instructions: an item records one address, while a
    // statement is built from several), they are the statements Hex-Rays'
    // own map of instructions to statements gives (eamap), which is what it
    // follows the instruction pointer by. A function's first instruction maps
    // there to the body, so the caret starts on the first statement rather
    // than the declaration.
    //
    // A conditional move Hex-Rays wrote as a whole if is both the condition's
    // line and the body's: the body when the condition holds now, so a step
    // shows the branch actually taken, and the condition when it does not.
    // Otherwise the first statement among them: for code setting up a call's
    // argument, the call, not the argument's line.
    static const citem_t *caret_statement(cfunc_t *cf, ea_t ea)
    {
        std::vector<const citem_t *> cand;
        for ( const citem_t *it : cf->treeitems )
            if ( it != nullptr && it->ea == ea )
                cand.push_back(it);
        if ( cand.empty() )
        {
            eamap_t &em = cf->get_eamap();
            eamap_iterator_t p = eamap_find(&em, ea);
            if ( p != eamap_end(&em) )
                for ( const cinsn_t *s : eamap_second(p) )
                    if ( s != nullptr )
                        cand.push_back(s);
        }
        if ( cand.empty() )
            return nullptr;

        regval_t efl;
        bool holds = false;
        if ( get_reg_val("EFL", &efl) && conditional_move_at(ea, efl.ival, &holds) )
        {
            const cinsn_t *ifs  = nullptr;
            const citem_t *body = nullptr;
            for ( const citem_t *it : cand )
            {
                bool in_branch = false;
                const cinsn_t *f = cmov_if_of(cf, it, ea, &in_branch);
                if ( f == nullptr )
                    continue;
                ifs = f;
                if ( in_branch && body == nullptr )
                    body = it;
            }
            if ( ifs != nullptr )
            {
                const citem_t *s = holds && body != nullptr ? body : ifs;
                while ( s != nullptr && s->is_expr() )
                    s = cf->body.find_parent_of(s);
                return s;
            }
        }

        const citem_t *best = nullptr;
        for ( const citem_t *it : cand )
            if ( best == nullptr || (best->is_expr() && !it->is_expr()) )
                best = it;
        while ( best != nullptr && best->is_expr() )
            best = cf->body.find_parent_of(best);
        return best;
    }

    bool show_in_pseudocode(TWidget *view, ea_t ea)
    {
        if ( !g_hooked || view == nullptr )
            return false;
        vdui_t *vu = get_widget_vdui(view);
        func_entry_info_t fi;
        if ( vu == nullptr || !get_func_entry_info(&fi, ea) )
            return false;

        // Decompile first and switch only on success. open_pseudocode() does
        // both, but picks the window itself (the wrong one) and shows a
        // failure dialog on every step.
        if ( vu->cfunc == nullptr || vu->cfunc->entry_ea != fi.start_ea )
        {
            hexrays_failure_t hf;
            cfuncptr_t cf = decompile_function(fi.start_ea, &hf, DECOMP_NO_WAIT);
            if ( cf == nullptr )
                return false;
            vu->switch_to(cf, false);
        }

        const citem_t *best = caret_statement(vu->cfunc, ea);
        int x = 0;
        int y = 0;
        if ( best != nullptr && vu->cfunc->find_item_coords(best, &x, &y) )
            jump_to_line(vu->ct, y, x);
        return true;
    }

    void redecompile_pseudocode_views()
    {
        if ( !g_hooked )
            return;
        std::vector<TWidget *> views;
        list_pseudocode_views(views);
        for ( TWidget *w : views )
        {
            vdui_t *vu = get_widget_vdui(w);
            if ( vu != nullptr && vu->cfunc != nullptr )
            {
                mark_cfunc_dirty(vu->cfunc->entry_ea, false);
                vu->refresh_view(true);
            }
        }
    }

    void close_volatile_pseudocode_views()
    {
        if ( !g_hooked )
            return;
        int closed = 0;
        std::vector<TWidget *> views;
        list_pseudocode_views(views);
        for ( TWidget *w : views )
        {
            vdui_t *vu = get_widget_vdui(w);
            if ( vu == nullptr || vu->cfunc == nullptr )
                continue;

            // Keep views backed by a loader segment. Written so the answer is
            // the same whether or not the debugger segments are torn down yet:
            // ephemeral and vanished segments both fail to survive.
            segment_info_t si;
            if ( get_segment_info(&si, vu->cfunc->entry_ea) && !si.is_ephemeral_segm() )
                continue;

            // No WCLS_SAVE: keep it out of the saved desktop.
            close_widget(w, WCLS_CLOSE_LATER);
            closed++;
        }
        if ( closed != 0 )
            msg("[ida-ttd] closed %d pseudocode view(s) of runtime-allocated code: "
                "those bytes exist only while a trace is loaded, and a view left "
                "open on them fails to decompile when the database is reopened.\n",
                closed);
    }
}
```

`src/ui/decompiler.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // Pseudocode coverage highlighting.
    //
    // Many IDA installs have no Hex-Rays, so everything here is a no-op when
    // init_decompiler() reports it absent.
    //
    // Nothing new is stored: coverage is already a per-instruction color in
    // the database, and a pseudocode line takes the color of the addresses it
    // came from.
    bool init_decompiler();     // true when Hex-Rays is present and hooked
    void term_decompiler();

    // Called with the function's entry when the user renames, retypes or
    // comments a variable, or comments the pseudocode: edits Hex-Rays keeps
    // itself, with no IDB event. Null to stop.
    void set_function_edit_hook(void (*hook)(ea_t func_ea));

    // Decompile every open pseudocode view again: types changed under it.
    void redecompile_pseudocode_views();

    // Repaint every open pseudocode view in place and redraw it. Call after a
    // coverage sweep or an annotation pass changes what the database says.
    void refresh_pseudocode_views();

    // Something a paint reads changed without an IDB event (the conditional
    // moves found never to have moved), so the next refresh repaints even a
    // view painted since the last color change.
    void pseudocode_paint_inputs_changed();

    // Close, without saving to the desktop, pseudocode views of code that
    // exists only while a trace is loaded. Called at session end: runtime
    // allocated code has no segment afterwards, and a view restored from the
    // desktop would fail with "cannot convert to microcode" on every touch.
    void close_volatile_pseudocode_views();

    // Every open pseudocode view. Asks IDA by window title rather than
    // remembering what was seen opening: IDA's source-level debugging opens
    // views without Hex-Rays reporting them.
    void list_pseudocode_views(std::vector<TWidget *> &out);

    // The entry of the function a pseudocode view shows; BADADDR when the
    // widget is not a pseudocode view or shows nothing.
    ea_t pseudocode_function(TWidget *view);

    // Whether the function starting at func_ea decompiles. Silent: a failure
    // shows no dialog. Successes are cached by Hex-Rays, so asking again is cheap.
    bool can_decompile(ea_t func_ea);

    // Show the function containing ea in this pseudocode view, caret on the
    // statement holding ea, without opening another window. False when the function cannot be
    // decompiled; the view is then left as it was.
    bool show_in_pseudocode(TWidget *view, ea_t ea);
}
```

`src/ui/graph_view.cpp`:

```cpp
// The plugin's graph window: the models it draws, handed to IDAPython as
// JSON, and the actions it sends back.
#include "ui/graph_view.h"
#include "common/python_eval.h"

#include <expr.hpp>

namespace idattd
{
    namespace
    {
        std::map<qstring, GraphModel> g_models;

        void json_field(qstring *out, const char *name, const qstring &value)
        {
            out->cat_sprnt("\"%s\":", name);
            json_str(out, value.c_str());
        }

        // Kinds are plugin-chosen words; this keeps anything else out of the
        // Python snippet.
        bool plain(const char *kind)
        {
            if ( kind == nullptr || *kind == '\0' )
                return false;
            for ( const char *p = kind; *p != '\0'; p++ )
                if ( !qisalnum((uchar)*p) && *p != '_' )
                    return false;
            return true;
        }

        // The window's code is scripts/ida_ttd_graph.py.
        bool run_python(const char *call)
        {
            qstring err;
            if ( run_python_window("ida_ttd_graph", call, &err) )
                return true;
            msg("[ida-ttd] the graph window failed: %s\n", err.c_str());
            return false;
        }
    }

    bool run_python_window(const char *module, const char *call, qstring *err)
    {
        if ( !python_available() )
        {
            *err = "no IDAPython";
            return false;
        }
        // fresh_module reloads the module when its file changed, so a
        // reinstall's version takes over, as when this code was a string run
        // on every call, without compiling it again on every show.
        qstring code;
        code.sprnt("import ida_ttd_qt\nida_ttd_qt.fresh_module('%s').%s\n", module, call);
        return eval_py(code.c_str(), err);
    }


    bool graph_window_available()
    {
        return python_available();
    }

    TWidget *graph_widget(const char *kind)
    {
        auto it = g_models.find(kind);
        return it != g_models.end() ? find_widget(it->second.title.c_str()) : nullptr;
    }

    bool graph_is_open(const char *kind)
    {
        return graph_widget(kind) != nullptr;
    }

    bool show_graph(const char *kind, GraphModel &&model)
    {
        if ( !plain(kind) )
            return false;
        const bool open = graph_is_open(kind);
        g_models[kind] = std::move(model);
        qstring call;
        call.sprnt("show('%s', %s)", kind, open ? "False" : "True");
        return run_python(call.c_str());
    }

    void refresh_graph(const char *kind, GraphModel &&model)
    {
        if ( !plain(kind) || !graph_is_open(kind) )
            return;
        // Redrawn only when what the window shows changed. The Fork manager
        // is refreshed at every stop, and a redraw re-runs the window's
        // script, lays the graph out again and drops the selection; with
        // the same model the node ids also stay what a pending click names.
        qstring before;
        const bool had = graph_json(kind, &before);
        g_models[kind] = std::move(model);
        qstring after;
        if ( had && graph_json(kind, &after) && after == before )
            return;
        qstring call;
        call.sprnt("show('%s', False)", kind);
        run_python(call.c_str());
    }

    void close_graph(const char *kind)
    {
        TWidget *w = graph_widget(kind);
        if ( w != nullptr )
            close_widget(w, 0);
    }

    void forget_graph(const char *kind)
    {
        close_graph(kind);
        g_models.erase(kind);
    }

    bool graph_json(const char *kind, qstring *out)
    {
        auto it = g_models.find(kind);
        if ( it == g_models.end() )
            return false;
        const GraphModel &m = it->second;
        qstring &j = *out;
        j = "{";
        json_field(&j, "title", m.title);
        j.append(',');
        json_field(&j, "status", m.status);
        j.cat_sprnt(",\"arrows_up\":%s,\"nodes\":[", m.arrows_up ? "true" : "false");
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < m.nodes.size(); i++ )
        {
            const GraphNode &n = m.nodes[i];
            if ( i != 0 )
                j.append(',');
            j.cat_sprnt("{\"id\":%d,", (int)i);
            json_field(&j, "title", n.title);
            j.append(',');
            json_field(&j, "code", n.code);
            j.append(',');
            json_field(&j, "badge", n.badge);
            j.append(',');
            json_field(&j, "tooltip", n.tooltip);
            j.cat_sprnt(",\"dashed\":%s,\"emphasis\":%s,\"lines\":[",
                        n.dashed ? "true" : "false", n.emphasis ? "true" : "false");
            for ( size_t k = 0; k < n.lines.size(); k++ )
            {
                if ( k != 0 )
                    j.append(',');
                json_str(&j, n.lines[k].c_str());
            }
            j.append("],\"menu\":[");
            for ( size_t k = 0; k < n.menu.size(); k++ )
            {
                if ( k != 0 )
                    j.append(',');
                j.append('[');
                json_str(&j, n.menu[k].first.c_str());
                j.append(',');
                json_str(&j, n.menu[k].second.c_str());
                j.append(']');
            }
            j.append("]}");
        }
        j.append("],\"edges\":[");
        for ( size_t i = 0; i < m.edges.size(); i++ )
        {
            const GraphEdge &e = m.edges[i];
            if ( i != 0 )
                j.append(',');
            j.cat_sprnt("{\"src\":%d,\"dst\":%d,\"dashed\":%s,", e.src, e.dst, e.dashed ? "true" : "false");
            json_field(&j, "label", e.label);
            j.append('}');
        }
        j.append("]}");
        return true;
    }

    bool graph_act(const char *kind, int node, const qstring &action)
    {
        auto it = g_models.find(kind);
        if ( it == g_models.end() || node < 0 || node >= (int)it->second.nodes.size() || !it->second.act )
            return false;
        // A copy: the action may replace the model (a fork switch redraws).
        auto act = it->second.act;
        act(node, action);
        return true;
    }
}
```

`src/ui/graph_view.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "common/json_str.h"

namespace idattd
{
    // A graph drawn by the plugin's own graph window
    // (scripts/ida_ttd_graph.py), styled and panned and zoomed like IDA's
    // graphs. The plugin builds the model; IDAPython fetches it with
    // ttd("ui.graph KIND") and sends node actions back with
    // ttd("ui.graphact KIND NODE ACTION"). One window per kind ("forks",
    // "origin").
    //
    // Not IDA's graph viewer: there a plugin node gets only a background
    // color and one block of text, and custom drawing means building against
    // IDA's exact Qt.

    struct GraphNode
    {
        qstring title;                  // first line
        qstring code;                   // an instruction, colored as IDA colors one
        qvector<qstring> lines;         // comment lines
        qstring badge;                  // the node's kind, a comment after the title
        bool    dashed = false;         // a dashed frame: something missing
        bool    emphasis = false;       // IDA's highlight color: where the graph starts
        qstring tooltip;
        // Context menu: (label, action) pairs; an empty pair is a separator.
        // The first is what a double-click does.
        std::vector<std::pair<qstring, qstring>> menu;
    };

    struct GraphEdge
    {
        int     src = -1;
        int     dst = -1;
        qstring label;
        bool    dashed = false;
    };

    struct GraphModel
    {
        qstring title;                  // the window's
        qstring status;                 // the line under the graph
        // Arrowheads at each edge's top end: flow goes up (a value's sources
        // below it) rather than down (a recording's forks).
        bool    arrows_up = false;
        std::vector<GraphNode> nodes;
        std::vector<GraphEdge> edges;
        // A node's action from its menu or a double-click. Runs on the main
        // thread, from the window's event handler.
        std::function<void(int node, const qstring &action)> act;
    };

    // Whether IDAPython (and so the graph window) is there.
    bool graph_window_available();
    // Keep 'model' as the graph of 'kind' and show its window, or bring it
    // up to date if it is open. False when the window could not be opened.
    bool show_graph(const char *kind, GraphModel &&model);
    // Only when its window is open: the model replaced and the window redrawn.
    void refresh_graph(const char *kind, GraphModel &&model);
    bool graph_is_open(const char *kind);
    void close_graph(const char *kind);
    // Close the window and drop the model, so the window's commands find no
    // graph (one whose positions belong to a recording no longer open).
    void forget_graph(const char *kind);
    // TWidget of the window, or nullptr.
    TWidget *graph_widget(const char *kind);

    // For the script commands the window uses.
    bool graph_json(const char *kind, qstring *out);
    bool graph_act(const char *kind, int node, const qstring &action);

    // Run 'call' (say "show()") on the PySide window module 'module'
    // (scripts/<module>.py, in ida-ttd-python/ beside the plugin), reloaded
    // first if its file changed. False, with IDAPython's error in 'err',
    // when IDAPython is absent or the call raised.
    bool run_python_window(const char *module, const char *call, qstring *err);
}

```

`src/ui/names.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "ui/names.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"

namespace idattd
{
    qstring func_display_name(ea_t ea)
    {
        qstring name;
        get_func_name(&name, ea);
        if ( name.empty() )
            get_name(&name, ea);
        qstring dem;
        if ( !name.empty() && demangle_name(&dem, name.c_str(), 0) > 0 && !dem.empty() )
            return dem;
        if ( name.empty() )
            name.sprnt("0x%llX", (uint64_t)ea);
        return name;
    }

    qstring func_offset_name(ea_t ea)
    {
        qstring s;
        ea_t fs = get_func_start(ea);
        if ( fs == BADADDR )
            s.sprnt("0x%llX", (uint64_t)ea);
        else if ( fs == ea )
            s = func_display_name(fs);
        else
            s.sprnt("%s+0x%llX", func_display_name(fs).c_str(), (uint64_t)(ea - fs));
        return s;
    }

    // How far below an address a name may sit and still be taken to belong to
    // it, when there is no exception table to settle the question.
    static const ea_t MAX_NAME_OFFSET = 0x1000;

    // "name+0x10". Callers pass an anchor at or below the address; for one
    // above it the offset is dropped rather than rendered backwards.
    static qstring name_with_offset(const qstring &name, ea_t ea, ea_t anchor)
    {
        qstring out = name;
        if ( ea > anchor )
            out.cat_sprnt("+0x%llX", (uint64_t)(ea - anchor));
        return out;
    }

    qstring describe_address(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea)
    {
        qstring out;
        if ( ea == BADADDR )
            return out;

        qstring mod = mgr != nullptr ? mgr->modules().name_at(ea) : qstring();
        auto qualify = [&mod](const qstring &what)
        {
            qstring r;
            if ( mod.empty() )
                r = what;
            else
                r.sprnt("%s!%s", mod.c_str(), what.c_str());
            return r;
        };

        // 1. Inside a function IDA has defined: let IDA name it. A function's
        //    chunks can sit anywhere, even below its entry, so an offset from
        //    the entry could come out negative. GNCN_REQFUNC answers only for
        //    an address really in a function, so no unrelated name is borrowed.
        qstring nice;
        if ( get_nice_colored_name(&nice, ea, GNCN_NOSEG | GNCN_NOCOLOR | GNCN_REQFUNC) > 0
          && !nice.empty() )
        {
            return qualify(nice);
        }

        func_entry_info_t fi;
        if ( get_func_entry_info(&fi, ea) )
        {
            // In a function IDA had no name for: name the function (no offset
            // when the address sits below the entry).
            qstring fn = func_display_name(fi.start_ea);
            if ( !fn.empty() )
                return qualify(name_with_offset(fn, ea, fi.start_ea));
        }

        // 2. The module's exception table knows where the function starts,
        //    symbols or not; a name before that start belongs to another one.
        ea_t fnstart = BADADDR, fnend = BADADDR;
        bool have_fn = mgr != nullptr && mgr->modules().function_range_at(ea, fnstart, fnend);

        // 3. The nearest name at or below the address. get_nlist_idx returns
        //    the closest match, which can be above it, so step back.
        size_t idx = get_nlist_idx(ea);
        size_t n   = get_nlist_size();
        while ( idx < n && get_nlist_ea(idx) > ea )
        {
            if ( idx == 0 )
            {
                idx = n;    // nothing at or below
                break;
            }
            idx--;
        }
        if ( idx < n )
        {
            ea_t at = get_nlist_ea(idx);
            const char *nm = get_nlist_name(idx);
            bool usable = nm != nullptr && at <= ea;
            // Inside the real function or, with no exception table, close
            // enough to be plausible.
            if ( usable )
                usable = have_fn ? at >= fnstart : (ea - at <= MAX_NAME_OFFSET);
            if ( usable )
                return qualify(name_with_offset(qstring(nm), ea, at));
        }

        // 4. No name inside the function, but its start is known: name it as
        //    IDA names an unnamed function, to match the disassembly.
        if ( have_fn )
        {
            qstring what;
            what.sprnt("sub_%llX", (uint64_t)fnstart);
            return qualify(name_with_offset(what, ea, fnstart));
        }

        // 5. Relative to the module: unambiguous even without symbols.
        ea_t lo = 0, hi = 0;
        if ( mgr != nullptr && mgr->modules().range_at(ea, lo, hi) && !mod.empty() )
        {
            out.sprnt("%s+0x%llX", mod.c_str(), (uint64_t)(ea - lo));
            return out;
        }
        out.sprnt("0x%llX", (uint64_t)ea);
        return out;
    }
}
```

`src/ui/names.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class TraceManager;

    // A function's display name, demangled when possible. Falls back to any
    // plain name at the address (an export or a PDB symbol for a function IDA
    // has not defined), then to the bare address, so a column is never blank.
    qstring func_display_name(ea_t ea);

    // "name+0x12" from the function IDA has defined around an address, the
    // name alone at its entry, else the address in hex.
    qstring func_offset_name(ea_t ea);

    // "module!symbol+offset" for an address, as honestly as the database allows.
    //
    // The nearest name is misleading in a system DLL: without a PDB only
    // exports are named, and allocating code is usually an internal helper,
    // so the nearest name can be an unrelated function tens of KB away.
    //
    // So the enclosing function comes first (IDA's, else the module's
    // exception table, which knows every x64 function start), and a name is
    // used only inside it. Failing that, the address is given relative to the
    // module: less informative, never wrong.
    qstring describe_address(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea);
}
```

`src/ui/query_view.cpp`:

```cpp
// What run_query shows while a query runs: IDA's wait box, or the recording
// window. Moved out of analysis/query_runner.cpp, which keeps the worker,
// the sink and the GIL.
#include "ui/query_view.h"
#include "ui/graph_view.h"
#include "core/backend_module.h"

namespace idattd
{
    namespace
    {
        // A running time to the second: "45 s", "3 min 07 s", "2 h 05 min 09 s".
        qstring clock_text(uint64 ms)
        {
            const unsigned long long s = ms / 1000;
            qstring t;
            if ( s >= 3600 )
                t.sprnt("%llu h %02llu min %02llu s", s / 3600, s / 60 % 60, s % 60);
            else if ( s >= 60 )
                t.sprnt("%llu min %02llu s", s / 60, s % 60);
            else
                t.sprnt("%llu s", s);
            return t;
        }

        // The longest log line the wait box shows whole: it grows with its
        // text. The recording window scrolls instead, and shows lines whole.
        const size_t LOG_LINE_CHARS = 110;

        // A log line as both show it: tabs as spaces, no surrounding blanks.
        qstring tidy_log_line(qstring l)
        {
            l.replace("\t", "    ");
            l.trim2();
            return l;
        }

        // Control characters as spaces, for the recording window: the log
        // carries the guest's console output, color escapes and all.
        void blank_controls(qstring *s)
        {
            for ( size_t i = 0; i < s->length(); i++ )
            {
                const uchar c = (uchar)(*s)[i];
                if ( (c < 0x20 && c != '\n') || c == 0x7F )
                    (*s)[i] = ' ';
            }
        }

        // ida_ttd_qt.<fn>(args...) as a Python expression, each argument a
        // string literal (json_str writes one Python reads as well).
        qstring py_call(const char *fn, std::initializer_list<const char *> args)
        {
            qstring expr;
            expr.sprnt("ida_ttd_qt.%s(", fn);
            bool first = true;
            for ( const char *a : args )
            {
                if ( !first )
                    expr.append(", ");
                first = false;
                json_str(&expr, a);
            }
            return expr;
        }
    }

    QueryProgressView::QueryProgressView(const char *what, bool cancellable, const QueryShow *show)
        : m_what(what), m_cancellable(cancellable), m_show(show), m_started(GetTickCount64())
    {
        // A recording gets the recording window, when there is Qt to show
        // it; everything else, and a recording without it, IDA's wait box.
        if ( show == nullptr || show->log_lines == 0 || !cancellable )
        {
            open_wait_box();
            return;
        }
        extlang_object_t py = find_extlang_by_name("Python");
        qstring err;
        if ( py == nullptr || py->eval_snippet == nullptr || py->eval_expr == nullptr
          || !py->eval_snippet("import ida_ttd_qt\n", &err) )
        {
            open_wait_box();
            return;
        }
        qstring expr = py_call("recording_window_open", { show->title != nullptr ? show->title : what, what });
        expr.append(show->pausable ? ", True)" : ", False)");
        idc_value_t rv;
        if ( !py->eval_expr(&rv, BADADDR, expr.c_str(), &err) || rv.vtype != VT_LONG || rv.num == 0 )
        {
            if ( !err.empty() )
                msg("[ida-ttd] the recording window did not open (%s); using a wait box.\n", err.c_str());
            open_wait_box();
            return;
        }
        m_py.emplace(py);
        m_windowed = true;
        m_winSeq   = emulator_log_tail(0, nullptr);
    }

    QueryProgressView::~QueryProgressView()
    {
        close();
    }

    void QueryProgressView::open_wait_box()
    {
        show_wait_box("%s", wait_text(0, false, 0).c_str());
    }

    void QueryProgressView::close()
    {
        if ( m_closed )
            return;
        m_closed = true;
        if ( !m_windowed )
        {
            hide_wait_box();
        }
        else if ( m_py )
        {
            qstring err;
            (*m_py)->eval_snippet("ida_ttd_qt.recording_window_close()\n", &err);
            m_py.reset();
        }
    }

    QueryProgressView::Ask QueryProgressView::poll(uint32_t percent, bool holding)
    {
        if ( m_closed )
            return ASK_NONE;
        return m_windowed ? poll_window(holding) : poll_wait_box(percent);
    }

    // The window is driven from here ten times a second: update() also runs
    // Qt's events, since this loop is all that runs while the recording does.
    QueryProgressView::Ask QueryProgressView::poll_window(bool holding)
    {
        const ULONGLONG t = GetTickCount64();
        qstrvec_t fresh;
        m_winSeq = emulator_log_since(m_winSeq, &fresh);
        qstring lines;
        for ( const qstring &l : fresh )
        {
            if ( !lines.empty() )
                lines.append('\n');
            lines.append(tidy_log_line(l));
        }
        blank_controls(&lines);
        const uint64 ran = t - m_started - m_pausedMs - (m_paused ? t - m_pausedAt : 0);
        qstring status;
        if ( m_cancelled )
            status = "Stopping: finishing the recording...";
        else if ( m_paused )
            status.sprnt(holding ? "Paused after %s" : "Pausing after %s...", clock_text(ran).c_str());
        else
            status.sprnt("Running for %s", clock_text(ran).c_str());

        // No percentage: a recording runs until the program exits, so the
        // backend's progress (the share of an instruction limit, if any)
        // says little about how far along it is.
        // "stop", "pause", "resume", "" or "gone" (see the Python side).
        qstring asked("gone");
        if ( m_py )
        {
            qstring expr = py_call("recording_window_update", { status.c_str(), lines.c_str() });
            expr.append(')');
            idc_value_t rv;
            qstring err;
            if ( (*m_py)->eval_expr(&rv, BADADDR, expr.c_str(), &err) && rv.vtype == VT_STR )
            {
                asked = rv.qstr();
            }
            else
            {
                msg("[ida-ttd] the recording window failed (%s); stopping the recording.\n", err.c_str());
                m_py.reset();
            }
        }

        if ( m_cancelled )
            return ASK_NONE;
        if ( asked == "stop" || asked == "gone" )
        {
            m_cancelled = true;
            return ASK_STOP;
        }
        if ( asked == "pause" && !m_paused )
        {
            m_paused   = true;
            m_pausedAt = t;
            return ASK_PAUSE;
        }
        if ( asked == "resume" && m_paused )
        {
            m_paused    = false;
            m_pausedMs += t - m_pausedAt;
            return ASK_RESUME;
        }
        return ASK_NONE;
    }

    QueryProgressView::Ask QueryProgressView::poll_wait_box(uint32_t percent)
    {
        // user_cancelled() is also what pumps the UI, without which the wait
        // box never appears (it shows only after a grace period while
        // messages run). So it is called every time, and its answer is
        // ignored for a box without Cancel (HIDECANCEL offers no way to ask,
        // so it reports false anyway).
        const bool asked = user_cancelled();
        if ( m_cancelled )
            return ASK_NONE;
        if ( m_cancellable && asked )
        {
            m_cancelled = true;
            replace_wait_box("HIDECANCEL\nStopping...");
            return ASK_STOP;
        }
        // Recordings (the ones with a title) show no percentage, as in the
        // recording window; scans over a recording do.
        const QueryShow *show = m_show;
        const uint32_t now = show != nullptr && show->title != nullptr ? 0 : percent;
        const ULONGLONG t = GetTickCount64();
        const uint64 secs = show != nullptr && show->elapsed ? (t - m_started) / 1000 : 0;
        const uint64_t seq = show != nullptr && show->log_lines != 0 ? emulator_log_tail(0, nullptr) : 0;
        // New log lines repaint at most four times a second: a busy log
        // would otherwise repaint at every poll.
        if ( now != m_shown || secs != m_shownSecs || (seq != m_shownSeq && t - m_paintedAt >= 250) )
        {
            replace_wait_box("%s", wait_text(now, true, t - m_started).c_str());
            m_shown     = now;
            m_shownSecs = secs;
            m_shownSeq  = seq;
            m_paintedAt = t;
        }
        return ASK_NONE;
    }

    // The wait box's text: the first line as before, then what 'show' asks
    // for. The percentage is left out while it is 0 for work that shows its
    // time instead (a recording without a limit never reports one).
    qstring QueryProgressView::wait_text(uint32_t percent, bool painted, uint64 elapsed_ms) const
    {
        qstring t;
        t.sprnt("%s%s%s...", m_cancellable ? "" : "HIDECANCEL\n", m_what.c_str(),
                m_cancellable ? " (Cancel to stop)" : "");
        const QueryShow *show = m_show;
        if ( painted && (show == nullptr || percent != 0) )
            t.cat_sprnt(" %u%%", percent);
        if ( show == nullptr )
            return t;
        if ( show->elapsed )
            t.cat_sprnt("\nRunning for %s", clock_text(elapsed_ms).c_str());
        if ( show->log_lines != 0 )
        {
            qstrvec_t lines;
            emulator_log_tail(show->log_lines, &lines);
            t.append("\n\nSogen's log");
            if ( lines.empty() )
                t.append("\n(nothing yet)");
            for ( const qstring &raw : lines )
            {
                qstring l = tidy_log_line(raw);
                if ( l.length() > LOG_LINE_CHARS )
                {
                    l.resize(LOG_LINE_CHARS - 3);
                    l.append("...");
                }
                t.append('\n');
                t.append(l);
            }
        }
        return t;
    }
}
```

`src/ui/query_view.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"
#include "analysis/query_runner.h"

#include <expr.hpp>

namespace idattd
{
    // What run_query shows while a query's worker runs: IDA's wait box, or
    // for a recording the recording window (scripts/ida_ttd_qt.py, the
    // recording_window_* functions: Sogen's log in a scrolling box, the
    // running time, Pause and Stop), when IDAPython's Qt is there to show it.
    //
    // run_query (analysis/query_runner.cpp) owns the worker, the sink and the
    // GIL; this owns everything the user sees and turns their clicks into
    // requests. Main thread only.
    class QueryProgressView
    {
    public:
        // What the user asked for since the last poll().
        enum Ask
        {
            ASK_NONE,
            ASK_STOP,       // Cancel, Stop, or the window closed: end the query
            ASK_PAUSE,
            ASK_RESUME,
        };

        // Shows the wait box or the recording window at once.
        QueryProgressView(const char *what, bool cancellable, const QueryShow *show);
        ~QueryProgressView();

        // One turn of the wait loop: repaint what changed (the percentage,
        // the running time, new log lines) and pump the UI. 'percent' is the
        // backend's progress; 'holding' says a pause has taken effect.
        Ask poll(uint32_t percent, bool holding);

        // Take the box or window down. Also done by the destructor.
        void close();

    private:
        void open_wait_box();
        Ask  poll_window(bool holding);
        Ask  poll_wait_box(uint32_t percent);
        qstring wait_text(uint32_t percent, bool painted, uint64 elapsed_ms) const;

        qstring          m_what;
        bool             m_cancellable;
        const QueryShow *m_show;
        ULONGLONG        m_started;
        bool             m_windowed  = false;
        bool             m_closed    = false;
        // Stop was asked for: the status says so and no more is asked.
        bool             m_cancelled = false;
        // The recording window: the Python it runs in, the log lines it has,
        // and the time spent paused, which the running time leaves out.
        std::optional<extlang_object_t> m_py;
        uint64_t         m_winSeq    = 0;
        bool             m_paused    = false;
        ULONGLONG        m_pausedAt  = 0;
        ULONGLONG        m_pausedMs  = 0;
        // The wait box: what it shows now.
        uint32_t         m_shown     = 101;     // out of range, so the first poll repaints
        uint64           m_shownSecs = 0;
        uint64_t         m_shownSeq  = 0;
        ULONGLONG        m_paintedAt = 0;
    };
}
```

`src/ui/scope.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "ui/scope.h"
#include "debugger/trace_manager.h"

namespace idattd
{
    ea_t scope_anchor(TraceManager *mgr, action_activation_ctx_t *ctx)
    {
        ea_t view = ctx != nullptr && ctx->cur_ea != BADADDR ? ctx->cur_ea
                                                            : get_screen_ea();
        func_entry_info_t fi;
        if ( view != BADADDR && get_func_entry_info(&fi, view) )
            return view;

        if ( mgr != nullptr && mgr->is_active() )
        {
            ea_t pc = mgr->current_pc_ea();
            if ( pc != BADADDR )
                return pc;
        }
        return view;
    }

    void scope_items(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea, qstrvec_t *out)
    {
        if ( out == nullptr )
            return;
        out->clear();

        qstring where;
        func_entry_info_t fi;
        if ( get_func_entry_info(&fi, ea) )
        {
            qstring fn;
            if ( get_func_name(&fn, fi.start_ea) > 0 && !fn.empty() )
                where.sprnt("Function %s", fn.c_str());
        }
        if ( where.empty() )
            where.sprnt("Function containing 0x%llX", (uint64_t)ea);

        qstring mod = mgr != nullptr ? mgr->modules().name_at(ea) : qstring();
        qstring modline;
        if ( !mod.empty() )
            modline.sprnt("Module %s", mod.c_str());
        else
            modline.sprnt("Module containing 0x%llX", (uint64_t)ea);

        out->push_back(where);
        out->push_back(modline);
        out->push_back("All loaded modules");
    }

    bool scope_ranges(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea, int scope, const char *what,
                      std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out)
    {
        out.clear();
        if ( mgr == nullptr )
            return false;

        switch ( scope )
        {
            case SCOPE_FUNCTION:
            {
                func_entry_info_t fi;
                if ( !get_func_entry_info(&fi, ea) )
                {
                    warning("There is no defined function at 0x%llX.\n\n"
                            "Define one first, or %s the whole module instead.",
                            (uint64_t)ea, what);
                    return false;
                }
                out.push_back({ fi.start_ea, fi.end_ea });
                return true;
            }

            case SCOPE_MODULE:
            {
                ea_t lo = 0, hi = 0;
                if ( !mgr->modules().range_at(ea, lo, hi) )
                {
                    warning("0x%llX is not inside a module loaded by the trace.\n\n"
                            "Dynamically allocated code has no module to %s; use "
                            "the function scope there.", (uint64_t)ea, what);
                    return false;
                }
                out.push_back({ lo, hi });
                return true;
            }

            default:
                out = mgr->modules().ranges();
                return true;
        }
    }
}
```

`src/ui/scope.h`:

```h
#pragma once

#include "common/pch.h"

namespace idattd
{
    class TraceManager;

    // How much of the database a whole-trace pass looks at. The values are the
    // indices of scope_items()' radio items, as an ask_form()
    // "<~S~cope:b:0:40::>" field yields them.
    enum Scope
    {
        SCOPE_FUNCTION = 0,     // the function under the cursor
        SCOPE_MODULE,           // the module under the cursor
        SCOPE_ALL_MODULES,
    };

    // Where a "current function" or "current module" scope is measured from.
    // The view wins when it points at a function (a deliberate right-click);
    // otherwise the replay position does, since IDA's view does not always
    // follow a travel and a stale address would fail with "no function there".
    ea_t scope_anchor(TraceManager *mgr, action_activation_ctx_t *ctx);

    // The radio items for a scope field around 'ea', in Scope order. They name
    // the function and module, showing which address scope_anchor() picked.
    void scope_items(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea, qstrvec_t *out);

    // Turn a scope choice around 'ea' into the [lo, hi) ranges it means.
    // False, after a warning, when 'ea' has no defined function or is in no
    // module (dynamically allocated code). 'what' names the pass in the
    // warning, e.g. "measure".
    bool scope_ranges(TraceManager *mgr, ea_t ea, int scope, const char *what,
                      std::vector<std::pair<ea_t, ea_t>> &out);
}
```
